findings.highlight: two, separated, become a pair of ones
findings.evidenceJa: 二人から一人が去り、一人と一人が残されてしまった
findings.explanation: The source says that one person leaves from the existing pair, after which two isolated individuals are left behind. The English turns that into the two simply separating into a pair of ones, obscuring both the departure and who remains.
findings.japanese:
二人から一人が去り、
一人と一人が残されてしまった日にも。
findings.todokanai: Falling on the day when two, separated, become a pair of ones.

findings.highlight: "She" is gone now. And only "she and I" remain.
findings.evidenceJa: 『あいつ』は去った。そして、『俺とあの娘』だけが残った。
findings.explanation: The Japanese pointedly gives Kazusa and Setsuna different marked labels: 'that one' leaves, while 'the girl and I' remain. Todokanai TL renders both women as the identical quoted 'she,' erasing the hierarchy and making the quotation marks meaningless.
findings.japanese:
『あいつ』は去った。
そして、『俺とあの娘』だけが残った。
findings.todokanai: "She" is gone now. And only "she and I" remain.

findings.highlight: I can't bring myself to turn around
findings.evidenceJa: 戻すことすらしない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he does not even turn his gaze back to her. “Can't bring myself to” changes deliberate nonresponse into emotional inability, weakening the self-accusation that continues into the following lines.
findings.japanese:
空を見上げた視線を、
声の主に戻すことすらしない。
findings.todokanai: Fixing my gaze toward the sky, I can't bring myself to turn around for the person calling out to me.

findings.highlight: I can't even bring myself to apologize
findings.evidenceJa: 謝ることすらしない
findings.explanation: Again, the source says he does not even apologize; it does not say that he is unable to. The mistranslation softens the cold behavior Haruki is deliberately condemning in himself.
findings.japanese:
そして、そんな突き放した態度を、
謝ることすらしない。
findings.todokanai: I can't even bring myself to apologize for being so callous to her.

findings.highlight: It wouldn't be right not to see my despicable actions to their very end.
findings.evidenceJa: 一度、最低の裏切りをしてしまった相手だから。もう、ずっと最低を貫かなくちゃならないから。
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats 最低 and turns his first betrayal into a self-imposed obligation to remain the worst. Todokanai TL replaces that repeated identity with plural 'despicable actions' and invents the moralizing claim that abandoning them 'wouldn't be right.'
findings.japanese:
一度、最低の裏切りをしてしまった相手だから。
もう、ずっと最低を貫かなくちゃならないから。
findings.todokanai: I've already committed the most despicable act of betrayal against her, after all. It wouldn't be right not to see my despicable actions to their very end.

findings.highlight: a gentle and warm sensation
findings.evidenceJa: 柔らかさと温かさ
findings.explanation: 柔らかさ is physical softness felt against Haruki's back, paired with warmth. “Gentle” turns the tactile detail into an abstract emotional quality.
findings.japanese: 背中に感じる柔らかさと温かさ。
findings.todokanai: Against my back, I feel a gentle and warm sensation.

findings.highlight: and if it's just causing you to suffer more
findings.evidenceJa: あのコを裏切ってしまうって、辛く感じるなら
findings.explanation: The second condition is specifically whether he finds the prospect of betraying her painful. The English invents a separate third condition about the embrace causing additional suffering.
findings.japanese:
「こうされることが嫌なら…
あのコを裏切ってしまうって、辛く感じるなら…」
findings.todokanai: "If you don't want this… if you think this means betraying her, and if it's just causing you to suffer more…"

findings.highlight: you'll come to accept me
findings.evidenceJa: あなたがわたしを受け入れてるって
findings.explanation: 受け入れてる describes the acceptance Setsuna might read into Haruki's present failure to reject her. “You'll come to accept me” moves that acceptance into the future. The separate scope of 悲しさのあまり is genuinely ambiguous and is not claimed as an error here.
findings.japanese:
「悲しさのあまり、あなたがわたしを受け入れてるって、
最低の思い込み、しちゃうよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I'll end up making the worst possible assumptionーthat, overwhelmed by sadness, you'll come to accept me, you know that?"

findings.highlight: "she" is the only thing on my mind right now
findings.evidenceJa: そんな瞬間も、俺の頭の中を占めているのが、『あいつ』のことしかないって事実に。
findings.explanation: The quoted 『あいつ』 deliberately recalls Haruki's marked designation of Kazusa at line 20. Rendering it as generic quoted 'she' removes the echo and the contrast with Setsuna, even as Setsuna is holding him.
findings.japanese:
そんな瞬間も、俺の頭の中を占めているのが、
『あいつ』のことしかないって事実に。
findings.todokanai: Even at this very moment… I can't deny the truth that "she" is the only thing on my mind right now.

findings.highlight: leaving us there in its wake
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちを、そこに置き去りにしてくれる
findings.explanation: The snow spreads a white world before them and leaves them stranded there inside it. An expanding world cannot leave them “in its wake”; the image is defective English and reverses the spatial relation.
findings.japanese:
ただ白く、綺麗なだけの世界を目の前に広げ、
俺たちを、そこに置き去りにしてくれる。
findings.todokanai: A white world abundant only in beauty expands before our eyes, leaving us there in its wake.

findings.highlight: forgotten emotions it had been hiding
findings.evidenceJa: そうやって隠していた事実を、忘れていた想いを
findings.explanation: The source distinguishes facts concealed by the snow from feelings Haruki had forgotten. The English makes the snow the thing that had also been hiding the forgotten emotions, collapsing the contrast.
findings.japanese:
一度解けたら、そうやって隠していた事実を、
忘れていた想いを、もう一度白日の下にさらす。
findings.todokanai: Once it melts, all of the hidden truths and forgotten emotions it had been hiding will once again be brought into daylight for all to see.

findings.highlight: It's not like we're going for the fine arts or something
findings.evidenceJa: 本人たちは芸術のつもりか何だか知らねえけどさ
findings.explanation: Takeya says he does not know whether the music students themselves think what they are doing is art. The English changes the subject to “we” and turns his sneer at their self-conception into a statement about his own group.
findings.japanese:
「空気読んでねぇよなぁ。
本人たちは芸術のつもりか何だか知らねえけどさ」
findings.todokanai: "They're not seeing the big picture. It's not like we're going for the fine arts or something, y'know?"

findings.highlight: derail the conversation
findings.evidenceJa: いつの間に振りほどいた
findings.explanation: 振りほどいた means that Fujishiro physically shook off Takeya's grip. Nothing here means derailing a conversation.
findings.japanese:
「ああっ！？
いつの間に振りほどいた！？」
findings.todokanai: "Ahh!? When did you manage to derail the conversation!?"

findings.highlight: put a white flag on your grave
findings.evidenceJa: 草葉の陰から白旗くらいは振っててやる
findings.explanation: Fujishiro jokes that from beyond the grave he will at least wave a white flag of surrender. The translation instead puts the flag on Takeya's grave, reversing both whose grave is imagined and what happens to the flag.
findings.japanese:
「頑張ってくれ飯塚。成功を祈ってるぞ。
草葉の陰から白旗くらいは振っててやるからな」
findings.todokanai: "Hang in there, Iizuka. I'll be praying for your success. And I'll be sure to put a white flag on your grave!"

findings.highlight: Speak of the devil
findings.evidenceJa: 言ってる側から説教だし
findings.explanation: Takeya means “and you're lecturing me even as you say that.” “Speak of the devil” is the wrong English idiom: nobody has just appeared after being mentioned.
findings.japanese: 「言ってる側から説教だし」
findings.todokanai: "Speak of the devil, here it comes again…"

findings.highlight: as if to say she wouldn't allow anyone to get in her way
findings.evidenceJa: 誰が止めることができようか反語
findings.explanation: Takeya grandly asks who could stop her passion and then literally says “rhetorical question,” reading out the grammatical device as part of his evasive joke. The translation invents a claim about her refusing to be stopped and deletes the joke.
findings.japanese:
「自分の奥底にある想いを精一杯表現したいって情熱を
誰が止めることができようか反語…」
findings.todokanai: "The burning passion deep inside of her was just dying to burst out, as if to say she wouldn't allow anyone to get in her way…"

findings.highlight: was subject to her influence
findings.evidenceJa: その煽りを食らった
findings.explanation: 煽りを食らう means to suffer the adverse fallout from something. The neutral phrase “was subject to her influence” removes the consequence that destroyed the club.
findings.japanese: その煽りを食らったのが我らが軽音楽同好会。
findings.todokanai: Consequently, our light music club was subject to her influence.

findings.highlight: Every year, someone is nominated to be club president in order to gather volunteers in the three months leading up to the school festival.
findings.evidenceJa: 毎年、学園祭の三ヶ月前に集まる有志によって、脈々と受け継がれるこの適当な呼称を持つ当会
findings.explanation: The source says volunteers gather three months before the festival and perpetuate this loosely named organization from year to year. It says nothing about nominating a president to recruit them; that procedure is invented.
findings.japanese:
毎年、学園祭の三ヶ月前に集まる有志によって、
脈々と受け継がれるこの適当な呼称を持つ当会は、
今年は我がそこそこの友、飯塚武也によって旗揚げされた。
findings.todokanai: Every year, someone is nominated to be club president in order to gather volunteers in the three months leading up to the school festival. This year, it happened to be none other than my dearest friend, Iizuka Takeya.

findings.highlight: persuade and manipulate members who were not satisfied with her
findings.evidenceJa: 全員を自由自在に操ろうと画策していた
findings.explanation: She used any means necessary to win over the members who opposed her, then plotted to control everyone. The English makes only the dissatisfied members the object of both persuasion and manipulation.
findings.japanese:
彼女の加入を快く思わないメンバーを、
なりふり構わない手段で懐柔して、
全員を自由自在に操ろうと画策していた。
findings.todokanai: She did everything in her power to persuade and manipulate members who were not satisfied with her.

findings.highlight: the word "persuade" is definitely an understatement
findings.evidenceJa: 『懐柔』という言葉がぴったり来るくらいに柔らかそうだった
findings.explanation: The joke pivots from 懐柔, “to win someone over,” to the literal 柔, “soft”: whatever Tomo used on Haruki looked very soft indeed. Calling “persuade” an understatement neither conveys the physical insinuation nor forms an English joke.
findings.japanese:
…まさに『懐柔』という言葉が
ぴったり来るくらいに柔らかそうだった。
findings.todokanai: …Yeah, the word "persuade" is definitely an understatement.

findings.highlight: pull ourselves together somehow
findings.evidenceJa: 何が何でも形にしないと
findings.explanation: 形にする means they must produce a workable performance at any cost. “Pull ourselves together” means recover composure, not assemble the band or get the show into presentable form.
findings.japanese:
「もうエントリーは済んでるし、
プログラムも入稿寸前だし、
…何が何でも形にしないと」
findings.todokanai: "We've already signed up to perform at the festival, and the program has to be submitted shortly… We have to pull ourselves together somehow."

findings.highlight: another ten times
findings.evidenceJa: 残り１０回を切った
findings.explanation: They have fewer than ten uses of the room left, not another ten.
findings.japanese:
あと一月半…
ここで練習できるのも残り１０回を切ったところで、
事態は綺麗に無垢にまっさらに白紙に戻ってきた。
findings.todokanai: Only a month and a half left… Since we can only practice here another ten times, the situation really has devolved into a pure blank slate.

findings.highlight: if I had her popularity, good looks, and silver tongue
findings.evidenceJa: その人気と外見と媚び慣れた態度があれば
findings.explanation: Haruki is considering what the club could have achieved with Tomo and those assets at its disposal. The English instead imagines Haruki personally possessing her popularity, appearance, and manner.
findings.japanese:
それでも、その人気と外見と媚び慣れた態度があれば、
俺の目的は、結構な確率で達成されたんだろうけどな。
findings.todokanai: But even so, if I had her popularity, good looks, and silver tongue, I could probably achieve my goals rather easily as well.

findings.highlight: out of anyone else's sight
findings.evidenceJa: 誰も聞いていないのをいいことに
findings.explanation: Haruki takes advantage of nobody listening and sighs extravagantly. The translation changes an auditory circumstance into being outside everyone else's sight.
findings.japanese:
俺、峰城大付３年Ｅ組北原春希は、
誰も聞いていないのをいいことに、盛大なため息をついた。
findings.todokanai: I, Kitahara Haruki, of Houjou High School's Class 3-E, could only let out a deep sigh, out of anyone else's sight.

findings.highlight: since our high school is merely affiliated with and shares the university's name
findings.evidenceJa: まさに“付属した祭”
findings.explanation: The quoted phrase calls the school festival itself an “attached festival,” extending the joke in the school's 付属 designation to the event's subordinate scale. The English replaces the wordplay with an invented explanation about sharing the university's name.
findings.japanese:
近隣どころか県外からも多くの人が押し寄せる
峰城大祭に比べ、そりゃ悲しいほどの規模の差を誇る
まさに“付属した祭”なのは仕方のないところ。
findings.todokanai: The university's festival gets swarmed every year not only by local visitors but also by those from outside the prefecture. As such, it's a given that our own festival is pitifully small in comparison, since our high school is merely affiliated with and shares the university's name.

findings.highlight: cunningly placed signboards within the university
findings.evidenceJa: 向こうの看板イベントにあざといまでに便乗し
findings.explanation: 看板イベント means the university festival's flagship event. The high-school contest shamelessly piggybacks on it; there are no cunningly placed signboards.
findings.japanese:
中でも向こうの看板イベントにあざといまでに便乗し、
ある意味本家以上に“内輪で”盛り上がるのが、
この『ミス峰城大付属』。
findings.todokanai: Among other things, there are some cunningly placed signboards within the university, and in a sense, the enthusiasm surrounding the Miss Houjou High contest is greater than anything on the university campus. For us, anyway.

findings.highlight: We had to consider public criticism, the decisions made by staff
findings.evidenceJa: 世間の批判とかも考慮した職員側の判断もあり
findings.explanation: The staff made the decision after considering possible public criticism. The English makes the students the ones obliged to consider criticism and treats the staff's decision as a separate item on their list.
findings.japanese:
けれど、大学ほど自治権を認められていないしがない付属。
色々と世間の批判とかも考慮した職員側の判断もあり、
ミスコンの正式開催が理事会で通ることはなかった。
findings.todokanai: However, merely being affiliated with the university, we are not allowed to have the kind of autonomy which they hold. We had to consider public criticism, the decisions made by staff, and the fact that the school directors never formally approved the holding of our beauty pageant.

findings.highlight: the organizers of the school festival executive committee
findings.evidenceJa: 付属祭実行委員会を二段構えで組織して
findings.explanation: The upperclassmen organized the festival committee as a two-tier structure so the unauthorized contest could operate underneath the official body. The translation omits that mechanism and reduces them to generic committee organizers.
findings.japanese:
しかし、地下で燻っているような先輩諸兄では…
彼らは、付属祭実行委員会を二段構えで組織して、
めでたく『ミス峰城大付属』は裏開催される運びとなった。
findings.todokanai: And so, those upperclassmen that smoldered underground… they, the organizers of the school festival executive committee, opened up Miss Houjou High behind the scenes.

findings.highlight: a failure in the making
findings.evidenceJa: すでに付属祭の裏目玉として定着した趣がある
findings.explanation: The source says the unofficial contest has already become established as the festival's hidden attraction. The translation calls it a coming failure, reversing its status.
findings.japanese:
そんな華々しくない、学生側の自主規制と
学園側の黙認によって成り立っているイベントは、
すでに付属祭の裏目玉として定着した趣がある。
findings.todokanai: Given that it was hardly anything spectacular, the students' regulations and the campus' tacit consent had clued in that it was a failure in the making.

findings.highlight: In the late autumn The neighboring student does Not a single thing
findings.evidenceJa: 秋深し　隣はなにも　しない人
findings.explanation: This is a comic rewrite of the famous haiku 秋深き／隣は何を／する人ぞ: Haruki changes the wondering “What is my neighbor doing?” into “my neighbor does nothing.” The literal English leaves the allusion and the act of parody entirely invisible.
findings.japanese: 秋深し　隣はなにも　しない人
findings.todokanai: In the late autumn The neighboring student does Not a single thing

findings.highlight: sent a letter yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: それなら昨日通しといた
findings.explanation: Haruki says he got the rugby stall approved yesterday, then compiled the handover notes and gave them to the club president. No letter was sent.
findings.japanese:
「それなら昨日通しといた。
申し送り事項は全部まとめて部長に渡したから」
findings.todokanai: "I already sent a letter yesterday. Explaining all the details to the club president."

findings.highlight: I'm pretty sure saying this right now, seems really inexcusable
findings.evidenceJa: 今さらこんなこと言うの、本当に申し訳ないって思うんですけど
findings.explanation: The comma splits the subject from its verb and leaves “I'm pretty sure” without a coherent complement. This is not grammatical English.
findings.japanese:
「その、今さらこんなこと言うの、
本当に申し訳ないって思うんですけど…」
findings.todokanai: "Listen, I'm pretty sure saying this right now, seems really inexcusable…"

findings.highlight: I'm going to have to withdraw from the contest
findings.evidenceJa: 今年は辞退って訳には
findings.explanation: Setsuna tentatively asks whether withdrawing this year might be possible, trailing off before completing the request. The translation turns that hesitant question into a definite announcement that she must withdraw.
findings.japanese: 「わたし、今年は辞退って訳には…」
findings.todokanai: "This year, I'm going to have to withdraw from the contest…"

findings.highlight: make the request to the printing shop this coming Monday
findings.evidenceJa: 週明けで印刷所押さえといて
findings.explanation: Haruki tells her to secure or book the printer for the beginning of the week. The English instead tells her to wait until Monday and then make an unspecified request.
findings.japanese:
「それは今夜中にやっとくから。
もう週明けで印刷所押さえといて」
findings.todokanai: "It'll be finished tonight. You can make the request to the printing shop this coming Monday."

findings.highlight: Be sure to bring it tomorrow morning
findings.evidenceJa: 明日の午前中までに打ち出しといて
findings.explanation: She asks Haruki to print the material out by tomorrow morning. “Bring it” omits the required action.
findings.japanese:
「ありがと、恩に着る！
明日の午前中までに打ち出しといて」
findings.todokanai: "Thank you, I'm in your debt! Be sure to bring it tomorrow morning."

findings.highlight: Once I've worked out the details
findings.evidenceJa: 委細了解してるから
findings.explanation: Haruki says he already understands all the particulars. The English changes that completed understanding into something he has yet to work out.
findings.japanese:
「委細了解してるから。
…ごめん、また話の腰を折った」
findings.todokanai: "Once I've worked out the details… Sorry, I got distracted again."

findings.highlight: personally, or by proxy
findings.evidenceJa: 自薦・他薦を問わず
findings.explanation: 自薦・他薦 means self-nomination or nomination by someone else. “By proxy” means another person acts on the entrant's behalf, which is not the rule being described.
findings.japanese:
「エントリー条件には『自薦・他薦を問わず』とあるけど、
もちろん本人の合意が大前提だ。
小木曽が嫌だったら、エントリーは取り消す」
findings.todokanai: "The entry requirements state that people can enter 'personally, or by proxy,' but only with consent, of course. If you don't like it, Ogiso, we can revoke your entry."

findings.highlight: The way you can persuade someone just by turning your back to them.
findings.evidenceJa: その、背中で語る様に
findings.explanation: Chikashi says Haruki's dejected back speaks for itself; Haruki immediately asks whether he looks that crushed. The English invents a power to persuade people by turning his back.
findings.japanese:
「俺…お前を尊敬するわ。
その、背中で語る様に」
findings.todokanai: "I… seriously respect you, man. The way you can persuade someone just by turning your back to them."

findings.highlight: who's been in the class next to mine for the past two years
findings.evidenceJa: 二つ隣のクラスの同級生
findings.explanation: Takeya is a classmate in the class two over from Haruki's, not someone who has spent the past two years in the adjacent class.
findings.japanese:
そこで何の準備もせずに佇んでいたのは、
軽音楽同好会の部長と、二つ隣のクラスの同級生と、
腐れ縁の親友の一人だった。
findings.todokanai: This person loitering around without preparing for anything right nowーthe president of the Light Music Club, a student from the same grade who's been in the class next to mine for the past two yearsーis an inseparable friend of mine.

findings.highlight: one should never rely on Takeya to try to mend friendships destroyed over a woman
findings.evidenceJa: 友情が修復することは、経験上最初からアテにしていないはずの武也
findings.explanation: Takeya himself knows from experience not to expect friendships broken over a woman to repair themselves, so he searches for replacements. The translation instead says other people cannot rely on Takeya to repair them.
findings.japanese:
女がらみで崩壊した友情が修復することは、
経験上最初からアテにしていないはずの武也は、
どうやら新メンバーを探して奔走していたようだけど…
findings.todokanai: Speaking from experience, one should never rely on Takeya to try to mend friendships destroyed over a woman. However, there he was, running around trying to find new members…

findings.highlight: for reasons beyond my control
findings.evidenceJa: 主にどうしようもある理由で
findings.explanation: The joke says the poor result is mainly due to reasons that could be helped—Takeya's absurd standards. “Beyond my control” reverses that point and changes whose control is at issue.
findings.japanese:
まぁ、主にどうしようもある理由で
結果は芳しくないようだった。
findings.todokanai: Though, for reasons beyond my control, it seems it was pointless after all.

findings.highlight: Areyouevenaman!?
findings.evidenceJa: 潔っ
findings.explanation: Haruki starts an oddly clipped form of 潔い in reaction to how quickly Takeya gives up, prompting Takeya to question the pronunciation. Nothing in the source asks whether Takeya is a man.
findings.todokanai: "Areyouevenaman!?"

findings.highlight: Maybe I've just been discouraged by these long past two days.
findings.evidenceJa: 『最初から無理だったんだよ』って結論を出すのに、二日は長すぎたかもしれない
findings.explanation: Takeya says two days may already have been too long to reach the conclusion that it was impossible from the start. He does not say that two discouraging days caused his mood.
findings.japanese:
「『最初から無理だったんだよ』って結論を出すのに、
二日は長すぎたかもしれないな」
findings.todokanai: "The only conclusion I'm drawing is that it was hopeless from the start. Maybe I've just been discouraged by these long past two days."

findings.highlight: I've told you this before, Takeya
findings.evidenceJa: 前から言おうと思ってたんだけどな武也
findings.explanation: Haruki claims he has merely been meaning to say this for a while; Takeya's next line punctures the pose by saying Haruki has told him clearly many times. The English has Haruki concede that at once, destroying the retort.
findings.japanese:
「前から言おうと思ってたんだけどな武也…
今日こそはハッキリ言わせてもらうぞ」
findings.todokanai: "I've told you this before, Takeya… so I'll spell it out clearly for you today."

findings.highlight: I'm only participating in what I want to do.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ適当に参加してるだけだし
findings.explanation: Haruki minimizes his role as casual, halfhearted participation. He is not saying that he selectively participates only in activities he wants.
findings.japanese:
「俺は別に…
ただ適当に参加してるだけだし」
findings.todokanai: "I don't really mind… I'm only participating in what I want to do."

findings.highlight: That's also… something I do of my own volition.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなことは………自分の意志でやってることだし
findings.explanation: Haruki begins to deny Takeya's description—“That's not…”—but cannot complete it and retreats to saying he acts voluntarily. “That's also” removes the failed denial that the narration explicitly comments on.
findings.japanese:
「そんなことは………
自分の意志でやってることだし」
findings.todokanai: "That's also… something I do of my own volition."

findings.highlight: the festival committee, the executive committee
findings.evidenceJa: 学園祭の表実行委員に、裏実行委員に
findings.explanation: Takeya contrasts the official festival committee with its underground counterpart. The English turns them into two generic committee names and loses the overt/covert joke.
findings.japanese:
「ウチらの手伝いだけじゃなく、
学園祭の表実行委員に、裏実行委員に、Ｗｅｂ担当に、
クラス委員と図書委員と…しかも全部ヘルプで」
findings.todokanai: "You're not only helping us, you're also doing things for the festival committee, the executive committee, being the admin of the school web page, being the class representative, even on the library committee… besides the fact that you're just lending a hand."

findings.highlight: he was being run ragged by girls
findings.evidenceJa: 女の子関係で便利に使い倒されることは
findings.explanation: Haruki says Takeya works him mercilessly whenever girls are involved, with roughly the frequency of eating and sleeping. The English makes Takeya the person being run ragged by the girls.
findings.japanese:
まぁ確かに女の子関係で便利に使い倒されることは、
それこそ人間の三大欲求の残り二つの頻度くらいに
発生する事態ではある訳だけど。
findings.todokanai: It's true that he was being run ragged by girls at about the same frequency as the other two primal urges.

findings.highlight: he wasn't like the people that had come and gone
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで色々とはっちゃけた人間じゃなくて
findings.explanation: Haruki says that until a year ago Takeya was not this uninhibited and over-the-top. The source contains no comparison with people who came and went.
findings.japanese:
それに、一年前までは、
ここまで色々とはっちゃけた人間じゃなくて…
findings.todokanai: And besides, up until last year, he wasn't like the people that had come and gone…

findings.highlight: That piano accompanied me many times, until I finally got into shape. And when it was pleased with my form, it accompanied my music.
findings.evidenceJa: 何度も何度もつっかえて、ようやく形になって、一人悦に入っていたとき、その伴奏は自然にやってきた
findings.explanation: Haruki is the one who repeatedly stumbles, finally gets the piece into shape, and sits alone enjoying his success when the accompaniment arrives. The English makes the piano accompany him throughout and then makes the piano pleased with his form.
findings.japanese:
何度も何度もつっかえて、ようやく形になって、
一人悦に入っていたとき、その伴奏は自然にやってきた。
findings.todokanai: That piano accompanied me many times, until I finally got into shape. And when it was pleased with my form, it accompanied my music.

findings.highlight: would pull pranks on me, guide me, and even show me my weaknesses
findings.evidenceJa: イタズラしているようにも、俺を導いてくれてるようにも、腕の違いを見せつけてるようにも聞こえる
findings.explanation: Haruki offers three alternative impressions of the sound: teasing him, guiding him, or showing off the gap in their ability. The English asserts that it does all three and changes the skill gap into exposing Haruki's weaknesses.
findings.japanese:
俺の音にイタズラしているようにも、
俺を導いてくれてるようにも、
腕の違いを見せつけてるようにも聞こえる、不思議な音。
findings.todokanai: It was a mysterious sound that would pull pranks on me, guide me, and even show me my weaknesses simply through hearing it.

findings.highlight: He doesn't always play the piano.
findings.evidenceJa: たまにピアノじゃないときもあるんだよな
findings.explanation: The neighboring performer has not been identified by number or gender. Japanese supplies no “he”; the scene is deliberately withholding who is playing.
findings.japanese:
「たまにピアノじゃないときもあるんだよな。
ベースだったり、ドラムだったり…」
findings.todokanai: "He doesn't always play the piano. Sometimes it's the bass, or the drums…"

findings.highlight: he caught me off guard
findings.evidenceJa: 先週はいきなりサックスが重なってきて
findings.explanation: The source only says a saxophone suddenly joined in. It does not identify a male performer.
findings.japanese: 先週はいきなりサックスが重なってきてビビったっけ。
findings.todokanai: Though last week, he caught me off guard by suddenly playing the saxophone.

findings.highlight: Seems like he's alone.
findings.evidenceJa: どれも一人でやってる感じ
findings.explanation: Haruki says each performance sounds solo, while the following narration preserves as a hypothesis whether one person plays every instrument. “He's alone” prematurely fixes both a single identity and male gender.
findings.japanese:
「さあ？
でも合わせてるの聞いたことないな。
どれも一人でやってる感じ」
findings.todokanai: "Who knows? I've never heard 'them' play together. Seems like he's alone."

findings.highlight: he intervenes when I'm alone
findings.evidenceJa: こっちが一人の時を狙って介入してくる
findings.explanation: The Japanese continues to omit the performer's identity and gender. The English repeatedly supplies a male subject.
findings.japanese:
だからこそ、こっちが一人の時を狙って介入してくる。
どうやら、よほどの暇人らしい。
findings.todokanai: Which is precisely why he intervenes when I'm alone. Seems like he has a lot of spare time.

findings.highlight: he's never missed a note
findings.evidenceJa: 向こうがミスってるのを聞いたことがない
findings.explanation: 向こう means the performer or performance on the other side; it does not establish a man.
findings.japanese:
どんな楽器でも、どんな曲でも、
向こうがミスってるのを聞いたことがない。
findings.todokanai: No matter what instrument or song, he's never missed a note.

findings.highlight: Perhaps he's had a lot of practice.
findings.evidenceJa: 練習時間が有り余ってる
findings.explanation: Haruki speculates that the unknown performer has an excess of time available to practice, continuing his “idle person” joke. The English changes available time into completed practice and again invents male gender.
findings.japanese:
…やっぱり、練習時間が有り余ってる、
よっぽどの暇人なのかも。
findings.todokanai: …Perhaps he's had a lot of practice. He certainly does seem to have a lot of spare time.

findings.highlight: There's an annex opposite of us connected by two sections where there's an extra-large third music room.
findings.evidenceJa: 向かいの新館に、こっち二つを繋げたくらいの、特大の第三
findings.explanation: The third music room is in the new building opposite and is roughly as large as Music Rooms One and Two combined. The English invents an annex physically connected by two sections.
findings.japanese:
峰城大付の音楽室は、こっちの本館に第一と第二、
向かいの新館に、こっち二つを繋げたくらいの、
特大の第三と、全部で三つも用意されている。
findings.todokanai: Houjou High School has three music rooms. Music Room 1 and 2 are here in the main building. There's an annex opposite of us connected by two sections where there's an extra-large third music room.

findings.highlight: the music students' classes, the eighth class of each grade
findings.evidenceJa: 学年８クラス中１クラスしかない音楽科専用
findings.explanation: The music course occupies one of each grade's eight classes. It is not “the eighth class” of each grade.
findings.japanese:
けれどそのうちの第二と第三は、
学年８クラス中１クラスしかない音楽科専用で、
他の部活や同好会は、狭い第一音楽室を分け合うしかない。
findings.todokanai: However, all the clubs have to share the cramped Music Room 1. Unlike the other two, which are reserved only for the music students' classes, the eighth class of each grade.

findings.highlight: We also have to think of the school's interests as well
findings.evidenceJa: 学校側も相当に力を入れてるしで
findings.explanation: The school itself invests heavily in students who plan to make a living in music. The line does not say that Haruki and the regular-course students must consider the school's interests.
findings.japanese:
まぁ、将来音楽で飯を食う野望を秘めた奴らの巣窟だし、
学校側も相当に力を入れてるしで、仕方ないんだけど。
findings.todokanai: It goes without saying that it's a haven for people who have hopes of getting into a music career. We also have to think of the school's interests as well, so there's nothing we can really do.

findings.highlight: Especially since I'm in third year already, things have gotten pretty tough.
findings.evidenceJa: 特に今年の三年はかなりレベル高いって話だし
findings.explanation: Takeya says this year's third-year music students are reputedly exceptionally skilled. The English makes the problem Takeya's own third-year status and omits their high level.
findings.japanese:
「ま、それを差し引いても望み薄だな。
特に今年の三年はかなりレベル高いって話だし」
findings.todokanai: "Well, that aside, my chances were pretty slim to begin with. Especially since I'm in third year already, things have gotten pretty tough."

findings.highlight: Maybe he's doing secret special training?
findings.evidenceJa: 秘密特訓でもしてるんか
findings.explanation: Takeya speculates about the still-unidentified person or people in the room. The Japanese does not establish a male performer.
findings.japanese:
「…えらく人見知りだな。
秘密特訓でもしてるんか？」
findings.todokanai: "…That's pretty shy. Maybe he's doing secret special training?"

findings.highlight: with him trying to hide behind the Iron Curtain
findings.evidenceJa: こうして鉄のカーテンを引かれると
findings.explanation: The passive construction says that an Iron Curtain has been drawn against Haruki, without identifying who drew it. “Him” is unsupported.
findings.japanese:
お隣さんに興味がないって言ったら嘘になる。
しかもこうして鉄のカーテンを引かれると余計にだ。
findings.todokanai: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't curious. Even more so with him trying to hide behind the Iron Curtain like he is.

findings.highlight: his piano playing
findings.evidenceJa: 素人耳には、完璧にしか聞こえないピアノ
findings.explanation: Haruki evaluates the instruments while the performer's identity remains hidden. The repeated masculine possessive is not in the source.
findings.japanese:
素人耳には、完璧にしか聞こえないピアノ。
それより少しは落ちるけど、きっちり合わせてくる
ベース、ドラム、サックス。
findings.todokanai: To an amateur such as myself, his piano playing is perfect. And although not as perfect, his bass, drums, and saxophone all hold up well.

findings.highlight: If he really is doing this all by himself
findings.evidenceJa: もし一人でやってるとしたら
findings.explanation: The source explicitly keeps it hypothetical whether a single person plays everything and supplies no gender. The English needlessly identifies that hypothetical person as male.
findings.japanese:
もし一人でやってるとしたら、ありえない多芸多才。
天才芸術家とは違うかもしれないけど、
天才芸人であることは間違いない。
findings.todokanai: If he really is doing this all by himself, he's impossibly multi-talented. Maybe not a prodigy of an artist, but certainly an amazing performer.

findings.highlight: at his home in Nishiyama
findings.evidenceJa: 西山宅でちっとも病気じゃない和司を説教してたら
findings.explanation: 西山宅 is Nishiyama's home; Nishiyama is the absent student's surname. The English turns it into a place where Kazuji's home is located.
findings.japanese:
自己満足的に熱いセッションをこなし、
西山宅でちっとも病気じゃない和司を説教してたら、
いつの間にか秋の夕暮れは赤みを消していた。
findings.todokanai: Having finished that heated session feeling satisfied with myself, and after lecturing Kazuji for not being sick in even the slightest at his home in Nishiyama, the red of the autumn evening sky had faded away before I could realize it.

findings.highlight: Despite already clearing two-thirds of your requirements
findings.evidenceJa: ３分の２は通るってのに
findings.explanation: Haruki says roughly two-thirds of applicants get the internal university recommendation. He does not say Io has personally completed two-thirds of a set of requirements.
findings.japanese:
「ああ…
そういえば、上への推薦ヤバいんだっけ？
３分の２は通るってのに」
findings.todokanai: "I see… Speaking of which, I heard you're having trouble getting a recommendation for university. Despite already clearing two-thirds of your requirements, no less."

findings.highlight: since I exceed her in both grades and grace
findings.evidenceJa: 成績や細かさで優位に立てるおかげで
findings.explanation: 細かさ is Haruki's greater fussiness, precision, or talent for picking at details—not “grace.” That mildly unflattering advantage helps him avoid feeling awkward around Io as a girl.
findings.japanese:
…なんだけど、成績や細かさで優位に立てるおかげで、
異性としての苦手意識を感じさせない貴重な友人の一人。
findings.todokanai: …Despite that, she's become an important friend of mine. Although, since I exceed her in both grades and grace, I'm not terribly conscious of the fact that she's of the opposite sex.

findings.highlight: I only look quiet
findings.evidenceJa: 比較対象のせいで朴念仁に見られるだけだ
findings.explanation: 朴念仁 here is a romantically oblivious blockhead, not a quiet person. Haruki's usual defense is that comparison with Takeya merely makes him look sexless or dense.
findings.japanese:
『比較対象のせいで朴念仁に見られるだけだ』
という、いつもなら絶対に口をついて出る弁解は、
諸般の事情を鑑みて自粛しておいた。
findings.todokanai: Usually I'd justify myself by saying, "I only look quiet because of who you keep comparing me to," but due to various circumstances, I decided to hold it in.

findings.highlight: she's way up there
findings.evidenceJa: 思いっきり身持ち固いよ
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna is extremely guarded and respectable in relations with men. “Way up there” suggests status or unattainability while dropping the specific reason a beginner could not break down her defenses.
findings.japanese:
「それに思いっきり身持ち固いよ？
初心者に崩せる相手じゃないと思うけどなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "And she's way up there, you know? I don't think she's someone a beginner like you could handle."

findings.highlight: Takeya's carefree attitude has gotten him into some bad luck there.
findings.evidenceJa: 武也のいい加減な口車に乗って貧乏くじ
findings.explanation: Io says Haruki has once again drawn the short straw by falling for Takeya's irresponsible sales pitch. The English makes Takeya the victim of the bad luck.
findings.japanese:
「また武也のいい加減な口車に乗って貧乏くじ。
そろそろ学習すればいいのに」
findings.todokanai: "Takeya's carefree attitude has gotten him into some bad luck there. He should've learned his lesson already."

findings.highlight: I don't really feel it's irrational or pointless
findings.evidenceJa: そんな理不尽とやるせなさも感じないではないけど
findings.explanation: Haruki does feel the unfairness and frustration; he says he is not without those feelings. The translation negates them. It then misassigns “beyond control” to the work rather than his compulsive responsibility and meddling.
findings.japanese:
そんな理不尽とやるせなさも感じないではないけど、
それよりも湧き上がる無駄な責任感と節介癖は、
どうやら自分でも制御不能な域に達してるようで。
findings.todokanai: I don't really feel it's irrational or pointless, but even with my burning sense of responsibility and nosy tendencies, it seems that this too, is far beyond my capabilities.

findings.highlight: this is the moment where everything goes back to square one
findings.evidenceJa: 学園祭実行委員代理補佐としての目が、ふと素に帰ってしまう瞬間
findings.explanation: This is a moment when Haruki's committee-assistant perspective drops away and he suddenly returns to his unguarded personal self. Nothing goes back to square one.
findings.japanese:
そんな、学園祭実行委員代理補佐としての目が、
ふと素に帰ってしまう瞬間がある。
findings.todokanai: From the eyes of a school festival committee assistant, this is the moment where everything goes back to square one.

findings.highlight: It was a wordless remark, after all.
findings.evidenceJa: どう見ても呆れてるというか
findings.explanation: Haruki corrects himself: her look is not resentful; by any reading she is exasperated with him. The English invents a “wordless remark” and omits the actual correction.
findings.japanese:
…という意図の目つきじゃないけどな、あれは。
どう見ても呆れてるというか。
findings.todokanai: …Then again, maybe that's not what she intended. It was a wordless remark, after all.

findings.highlight: In the late autumn What goes around comes around Compassion's your call
findings.evidenceJa: 秋深し　情けは人の　ためならず
findings.explanation: This is the second parody of Basho's 秋深き／隣は何を／する人ぞ in the scene, so it should visibly recall the earlier altered haiku while splicing in the proverb 情けは人のためならず. The English neither preserves that paired literary callback nor has source support for the added phrase “Compassion's your call.”
findings.japanese: 秋深し　情けは人の　ためならず
findings.todokanai: In the late autumn What goes around comes around Compassion's your call

findings.highlight: He's here today too.
findings.evidenceJa: 今日もいた
findings.explanation: Haruki is relieved that the still-unidentified neighboring performer is present. The Japanese supplies neither name nor gender; “he” prejudges the reveal.
findings.japanese:
「…よかった。
今日もいた」
findings.todokanai: "…Good. He's here today too."

findings.highlight: a proper fine arts student
findings.evidenceJa: 単なる文章好きの文系学生
findings.explanation: Haruki describes himself as an ordinary humanities student who likes writing or literature. 文系 does not mean a fine-arts student, and “proper” is invented.
findings.japanese:
女を口説く環境作りに余念のないあいつと違って、
俺は単なる文章好きの文系学生だったから、
最初はコードの存在すら知らなかった。
findings.todokanai: While he was busy flirting with girls, I was busy being a proper fine arts student who simply enjoyed literature. Because of that, I didn't even know what chords were at first.

findings.highlight: there'd be various things that might perplex you
findings.evidenceJa: 様々な観点から総合的に評価して首を捻る程度
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even now, a comprehensive evaluation from various angles would leave him tilting his head over whether he has improved. The English transfers the perplexity to an unspecified “you” and loses the negative self-assessment.
findings.japanese:
ま、今でもそんなに上達してるかと問われれば、
様々な観点から総合的に評価して首を捻る程度だけど。
findings.todokanai: Though if you asked me right now if my playing had improved at all, there'd be various things that might perplex you.

findings.highlight: My low skill level would probably have just caused them trouble.
findings.evidenceJa: 迷惑をかけたという程には相手にされてなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says they paid so little attention to him that he did not even rise to the level of causing them trouble. The English states the opposite: that his low skill probably did burden them.
findings.japanese:
そんな適当な仲間にも、俺は全然ついていけなくて。
…迷惑をかけたという程には相手にされてなかったけど。
findings.todokanai: And I just couldn't keep up with them… My low skill level would probably have just caused them trouble.

findings.highlight: the song that I've perfected
findings.evidenceJa: 最初にトチらずに弾けるようになった曲
findings.explanation: It was the first song Haruki learned to play without making a mistake. “Perfected” greatly overstates his explicitly modest guitar ability.
findings.japanese:
俺が一番最初に練習して、
最初にトチらずに弾けるようになった曲。
findings.todokanai: This is the song I first began practicing with. And it is the song that I've perfected.

findings.highlight: getting on the bandwagon
findings.evidenceJa: ミーハーかつマイナー
findings.explanation: Takeya's label is the comic contradiction “trendy and obscure.” The English keeps only the trendy half and deletes the deliberately incompatible “minor.”
findings.japanese:
武也には『ミーハーかつマイナー』と笑われたけど、
好きなものは好きなんだから仕方ない。
findings.todokanai: Takeya laughed it off as me "getting on the bandwagon," but I can't help but like it.

findings.highlight: common for karaoke or TV programs to feature this universally beloved song
findings.evidenceJa: カラオケや有線でもある程度定番化されてて
findings.explanation: 有線 is wired music or cable radio, not television. The source calls the song a modestly, quietly loved seasonal standard; “universally beloved” also inflates its deliberately understated status.
findings.japanese:
今や、カラオケや有線でもある程度定番化されてて、
これからの季節、リクエストが徐々に増えていく、
地味に愛されてる曲。
findings.todokanai: Even now it's common for karaoke or TV programs to feature this universally beloved song, and requests for it only increase during the coming season.

findings.highlight: An artist with extraordinary abilities at the time, topping charts even in the U.S., and attaining fame worldwide.
findings.evidenceJa: 今や全米チャートにでさえ顔を出す国際的アーティストは、その頃からやっぱり実力が並外れてた
findings.explanation: Rina appears on American charts now; the retrospective point is that her ability was already extraordinary back then. The English grammar places the international chart success “at the time” of the old festival.
findings.japanese:
最優秀賞は緒方理奈。
今や全米チャートにでさえ顔を出す国際的アーティストは、
その頃からやっぱり実力が並外れてた。
findings.todokanai: The top prize had gone to Ogata Rina. An artist with extraordinary abilities at the time, topping charts even in the U.S., and attaining fame worldwide.

findings.highlight: despite knowing I was a bad singer
findings.evidenceJa: キーが合わないのを承知の上で、裏声で歌いまくり
findings.explanation: Haruki knew the song's key did not suit his voice and therefore sang it repeatedly in falsetto. The source does not call him a bad singer.
findings.japanese:
その番組を見てからしばらくは、
キーが合わないのを承知の上で、裏声で歌いまくり、
家族やクラスメートのひんしゅくを買いまくった。
findings.todokanai: After watching that show, despite knowing I was a bad singer, I kept singing the song in falsetto, bearing all the frowns from my classmates and family.

findings.highlight: despite it not really fitting the guitar
findings.evidenceJa: ギターを弾くだなんて似合わないことを始めたときも
findings.explanation: Playing guitar is what seemed out of character for Haruki. The English makes the song seem ill-suited to the instrument instead.
findings.japanese:
だから、ギターを弾くだなんて似合わないことを
始めたときも、やっぱり皆のひんしゅく覚悟で、
最初に挑む曲は決まっていた。
findings.todokanai: Which was why when I started, despite it not really fitting the guitar, and expecting everyone to frown upon it, this was the song I had decided to take on.

findings.highlight: I figure she'd get suspicious if someone had sprinted up to the rooftop and was gasping for air for no good reason.
findings.evidenceJa: そっちの方が怪しいと思うんだけど
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that a person who sprints to the roof for no reason would be the more suspicious party. The English instead makes Setsuna suspicious of that person, reversing who is making the judgment and losing his dry retort to her question.
findings.japanese:
何の理由もなく、
息も絶え絶えに屋上に駆け上がってくる人間がいたら、
そっちの方が怪しいと思うんだけど。
findings.todokanai: I figure she'd get suspicious if someone had sprinted up to the rooftop and was gasping for air for no good reason.

findings.highlight: A group as fantastic as this sounds too good to be true, doesn't it?
findings.evidenceJa: こんな幸せな締め方、ないんじゃないのか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether there could be any happier way to bring this moment—and what he has decided will be his final performance—to a close. The English invents a fantastic group and evaluates it as too good to be true, deleting the idea of an emotionally satisfying ending.
findings.japanese:
しかも最後の最後に綺麗なボーカルまでついて、
こんな幸せな締め方、ないんじゃないのか？
findings.todokanai: And right at the last minute, a beautiful singer appears. A group as fantastic as this sounds too good to be true, doesn't it?

findings.highlight: Don't just casually say that! You're making me feel uneasy here!
findings.evidenceJa: さり気なく一文字すり替えるなよ
findings.explanation: Chikashi has asked whether Haruki has an ate—a lead or prospect—and Haruki answers saa, “who knows,” changing a single sound. Chikashi explicitly protests that one-character substitution. The English retains only generic anxiety and erases the joke it is reacting to.
findings.japanese:
「さり気なく一文字すり替えるなよ！
思いっきり不安になるじゃないか！」
findings.todokanai: "Don't just casually say that! You're making me feel uneasy here!"

findings.highlight: I didn't think she would come all the way here to seriously respond to my crazy invitation.
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで真剣に反応するとは思いもしなかった
findings.explanation: ここまで measures the degree of Setsuna's seriousness: Haruki never expected her to take his outrageous invitation this seriously. The English misreads it spatially as her coming “all the way here.”
findings.japanese:
俺の、あまりに突拍子もない誘いに、
ここまで真剣に反応するとは思いもしなかった。
findings.todokanai: I didn't think she would come all the way here to seriously respond to my crazy invitation.

findings.highlight: I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしなんかにやれるのか、今のわたしがやってもいいことなのか、そもそも、わたしはやりたいのか
findings.explanation: Setsuna separates three questions: whether she is capable, whether the person she currently is has the right or standing to do it, and whether she wants to. The English turns the second question into another question of ability, erasing the normative self-doubt that later makes her “two-to-one” reversal meaningful.
findings.japanese:
「わたしなんかにやれるのか、
今のわたしがやってもいいことなのか、
そもそも、わたしはやりたいのか」
findings.todokanai: "I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it."

findings.highlight: I'll lend you my shoulder as well. If it's only for crying anyway…
findings.evidenceJa: なんなら胸貸してやってもいいぞ。…泣くだけなら
findings.explanation: Chikashi offers Haruki his chest, then hastily limits the offer to crying. That bodily intimacy is why Haruki immediately calls the suggestion disgusting. Replacing chest with the conventional English shoulder removes the comic setup while leaving both the qualification and Haruki's reaction stranded.
findings.japanese:
「なんなら胸貸してやってもいいぞ。
…泣くだけなら」
findings.todokanai: "I'll lend you my shoulder as well. If it's only for crying anyway…"

findings.highlight: Past Minami-Suetsugu Station, the entertainment district for the students; the second closest station to school, Suetsugu-chou Station, shows an unchanging scenery.
findings.evidenceJa: 学校から二番目に近い末次町駅前は、学生たちの歓楽街を最寄り駅の南末次に譲り
findings.explanation: Suetsugucho is the second-closest station to school; the nearest station, Minami-Suetsugu, has taken the student entertainment district for itself. The English makes Minami-Suetsugu something the narration moves past, obscures which station owns the district, and leaves the sentence structurally broken.
findings.japanese:
学校から二番目に近い末次町駅前は、
学生たちの歓楽街を最寄り駅の南末次に譲り、
来るたび代わり映えのしない光景を映し出している。
findings.todokanai: Past Minami-Suetsugu Station, the entertainment district for the students; the second closest station to school, Suetsugu-chou Station, shows an unchanging scenery.

findings.highlight: The diligent, braided girl who does her best to tend to the grocery store front.
findings.evidenceJa: スーパーの店先で、一生懸命品出しに励む三つ編みの少女
findings.explanation: This deliberately repeats the earlier image of the braided girl diligently stocking goods at the supermarket entrance, now revealing that background figure as Setsuna. “Tend to the grocery store front” changes the action and weakens the repeated wording that performs the reveal.
findings.japanese:
スーパーの店先で、
一生懸命品出しに励む三つ編みの少女。
findings.todokanai: The diligent, braided girl who does her best to tend to the grocery store front.

findings.highlight: Looks like she went to get some leftover food from the grocery store… How thrifty of her.
findings.evidenceJa: どうやらスーパーの残り物を貰ってきたらしい。………なんという生活感
findings.explanation: Setsuna appears to have been given the supermarket's leftovers; Haruki is struck by her vivid air of ordinary domestic life. The English turns receiving leftovers into going to obtain them and replaces domestic lived-in texture with a judgment that she is thrifty.
findings.japanese:
どうやらスーパーの残り物を貰ってきたらしい。
………なんという生活感。
findings.todokanai: Looks like she went to get some leftover food from the grocery store… How thrifty of her.

findings.highlight: I was a bit taken aback when I first talked to you, Kitahara-kun.
findings.evidenceJa: 初めて北原くんとお話ししたときのこと、ちょっと引っかかってたんだ
findings.explanation: Something about their first conversation had continued to nag at or puzzle Setsuna, leading into the remarks she now quotes. “Was taken aback” makes it a momentary surprise during the conversation and loses the lingering question that motivates this exchange.
findings.japanese:
「初めて北原くんとお話ししたときのこと、
ちょっと引っかかってたんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I was a bit taken aback when I first talked to you, Kitahara-kun."

findings.highlight: I find myself not altogether disliking the look of this particular braided and bespectacled girl before me.
findings.evidenceJa: 今、目の前にいるこの三つ編み眼鏡少女は、思いっきりアリだと思ってしまえる
findings.explanation: After saying braided girls with glasses are not especially his type, Haruki concedes that the girl before him is emphatically ari—absolutely a yes. The English replaces that strong attraction with the evasive and much weaker “not altogether disliking.”
findings.japanese:
やはりというか、さすがというか、
今、目の前にいるこの三つ編み眼鏡少女は、
思いっきりアリだと思ってしまえる。
findings.todokanai: But as cliche as it may sound, I find myself not altogether disliking the look of this particular braided and bespectacled girl before me.

findings.highlight: the beautiful face behind those glasses felt out of place, to say the least.
findings.evidenceJa: その眼鏡の奥の素顔は、細かいことを気にする俺にとって、格好のチェック対象だった
findings.explanation: Her bare face behind the glasses became an ideal object of scrutiny for detail-obsessed Haruki, explaining how he eventually recognized her disguise. The English invents “beautiful,” says the face felt out of place, and deletes the observational habit that causes the recognition.
findings.japanese:
その眼鏡の奥の素顔は、
細かいことを気にする俺にとって、
格好のチェック対象だった。
findings.todokanai: And for someone like me who paid attention to small details, the beautiful face behind those glasses felt out of place, to say the least.

findings.highlight: Even though I've been here like this for a year now.
findings.evidenceJa: それこそ一年の頃からずっと
findings.explanation: Setsuna has used this disguise ever since her first year at school, not merely for one year. As a third-year student, the English shortens the history of her double life by roughly half.
findings.japanese:
「今のわたしの正体が見破られたの、今日が初めて。
それこそ一年の頃からずっと、だったのに」
findings.todokanai: "Today's the first time anyone's managed to recognize me like this. Even though I've been here like this for a year now."

findings.highlight: After all, Ogiso has resolved to talk about it with a nobody like me…
findings.evidenceJa: 小木曽が、他の誰にでもないこの俺に、大きな覚悟を持って話してくれるんだから
findings.explanation: Haruki is struck that Setsuna has resolved to tell this to him and no one else—to me, of all people. The English replaces that exclusive act of trust with unsupported self-abasement, calling him “a nobody.”
findings.japanese:
小木曽が、他の誰にでもないこの俺に、
大きな覚悟を持って話してくれるんだから…
findings.todokanai: After all, Ogiso has resolved to talk about it with a nobody like me…

findings.highlight: I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…
findings.evidenceJa: 後はそのイメージを守るために見栄に見栄を重ねて
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she piled one act of keeping up appearances upon another to preserve the image. “Did so many things” deletes the accumulating pretense that trapped her inside the school persona.
findings.japanese:
「そうなると、
後はそのイメージを守るために見栄に見栄を重ねて…」
findings.todokanai: "When that happened, I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…"

findings.highlight: Having heard her somewhat lackluster confession
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで微妙な打ち明け話をされると
findings.explanation: 微妙 describes a confession awkwardly poised between grave and trivial, which is why Haruki cannot decide whether to press or retreat. “Lackluster” instead dismisses Setsuna's confession as dull or unimpressive.
findings.japanese:
なにしろ、ここまで微妙な打ち明け話をされると、
押していいのか引くべきなのか判断できない。
findings.todokanai: Having heard her somewhat lackluster confession, I'm on the fence about whether I should push onward or pull back.

findings.highlight: Ogiso gives me a cheerful look, making me wonder whether she'd noticed I was hesitating just now.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなふうに逡巡してる隙に、小木曽は正体がバレてスッキリしてしまったのか、結構晴れ晴れとした顔で立ち上がる
findings.explanation: While Haruki hesitates, Setsuna stands looking relieved—perhaps because having her identity exposed has cleared the air. The English invents her noticing his hesitation and makes that the focus of her expression.
findings.japanese:
そんなふうに逡巡してる隙に、
小木曽は正体がバレてスッキリしてしまったのか、
結構晴れ晴れとした顔で立ち上がる。
findings.todokanai: Ogiso gives me a cheerful look, making me wonder whether she'd noticed I was hesitating just now.

findings.highlight: My mom makes dinner three times a week.
findings.evidenceJa: お母さんも週三でパートなの
findings.explanation: Setsuna says her mother also works part-time three days a week. The English turns the mother's employment schedule into a dinner rota.
findings.japanese:
「お母さんも週三でパートなの。
それにそろそろ弟がお腹空かせて帰ってくる頃だし」
findings.todokanai: "My mom makes dinner three times a week. Also, my hungry younger brother is coming home soon."

findings.highlight: You shouldn't easily believe in cool-headed people who take advantage of others' weaknesses, or selfish people who don't consider others' circumstances.
findings.evidenceJa: 人の弱みに付け込む冷徹さと、人の事情を考えない卑劣さを持つ人間を、そんなに簡単に信じていいわけがないって
findings.explanation: Haruki condemns himself as one person possessing both the coldness to exploit weakness and the baseness to ignore another's circumstances. The English generalizes this into advice about two kinds of “people,” softens 冷徹 into “cool-headed,” and turns 卑劣 into ordinary selfishness.
findings.japanese:
人の弱みに付け込む冷徹さと、
人の事情を考えない卑劣さを持つ人間を、
そんなに簡単に信じていいわけがないって。
findings.todokanai: You shouldn't easily believe in cool-headed people who take advantage of others' weaknesses, or selfish people who don't consider others' circumstances.

findings.highlight: being a business district that doesn't sleep, even in the dead of night.
findings.evidenceJa: 深夜遅くまで眠らない繁華街、南末次
findings.explanation: Minami-Suetsugu is a nightlife or entertainment district that stays awake late into the night. Calling it a business district gives the rendezvous the wrong urban setting and atmosphere.
findings.japanese:
末次町とは違い、
深夜遅くまで眠らない繁華街、南末次。
findings.todokanai: Minami-Suetsugu is different from Suetsugu-chou, being a business district that doesn't sleep, even in the dead of night.

findings.highlight: Just the two of us, in the night of the business district…
findings.evidenceJa: 夜の繁華街。二人きりの待ち合わせ
findings.explanation: The repeated setup is a nighttime rendezvous for two in an entertainment district, with the suggestive associations that creates. “The night of the business district” is both the wrong setting and defective English.
findings.japanese:
夜の繁華街。
二人きりの待ち合わせ。
findings.todokanai: Just the two of us, in the night of the business district…

findings.highlight: next will be the usual ones, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 次はいつもの定番を流してみようかな
findings.explanation: Setsuna muses that she will put on her usual standards next. The English converts her self-directed decision into a confirmation question to Haruki, weakening the scene's joke that she controls the entire karaoke session without consulting him.
findings.japanese:
「ええと…とりあえず新曲一通り行ったから、
次はいつもの定番を流してみようかな」
findings.todokanai: "Umm… since we went through the new songs for the time being, next will be the usual ones, right?"

findings.highlight: The business district. The two of us alone, in the middle of the night.
findings.evidenceJa: 夜の繁華街。二人きりの待ち合わせ
findings.explanation: The narration repeats its deliberately suggestive “nighttime entertainment district; a rendezvous for two” setup immediately before the karaoke punchline. The English again substitutes a business district and changes a rendezvous into generic physical solitude.
findings.japanese:
夜の繁華街。
二人きりの待ち合わせ。
findings.todokanai: The business district. The two of us alone, in the middle of the night.

findings.highlight: Did I disappoint you?
findings.evidenceJa: 退いた？
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether this side of her has put Haruki off or made him recoil. “Disappoint” makes her worry that she failed an expectation rather than that her intensity repelled him.
findings.todokanai: "…Did I disappoint you?"

findings.highlight: It's such a waste if you can't even get through ten songs in two hours, you know?
findings.evidenceJa: ２時間で１０曲歌えなかったりすると悔しいでしょ
findings.explanation: Setsuna says it is frustrating or galling not to manage ten songs in two hours; Haruki immediately repeats those emotional words in disbelief. “A waste” changes the emotion into an efficiency judgment and weakens his reaction.
findings.japanese: ２時間で１０曲歌えなかったりすると悔しいでしょ？」
findings.todokanai: It's such a waste if you can't even get through ten songs in two hours, you know?"

findings.highlight: And if you start singing right after the previous song ends, you can fit in about five more.
findings.evidenceJa: 歌い終わってすぐに演奏ストップすれば、さらに５曲くらい稼げるし
findings.explanation: Setsuna stops the accompaniment as soon as she finishes singing, skipping each remaining instrumental outro to squeeze in five more songs. The English instead has her start singing after a song has already ended, which is ordinary karaoke sequencing and loses the obsessive trick.
findings.japanese:
「その点、一人なら２時間あれば３０曲は歌えるし。
歌い終わってすぐに演奏ストップすれば、
さらに５曲くらい稼げるし」
findings.todokanai: "On that note, one person can sing 30 songs in two hours. And if you start singing right after the previous song ends, you can fit in about five more."

findings.highlight: when I heard a song I'm good at… not to mention it being my favorite song
findings.evidenceJa: 自分のレパートリーの…しかも一番のお気に入りが流れてきちゃったら
findings.explanation: The song was part of Setsuna's repertoire and, moreover, her favorite. レパートリー does not assert that she is especially good at it; the English invents a skill claim where she is explaining irresistible familiarity and attachment.
findings.japanese:
「だから、自分のレパートリーの…
しかも一番のお気に入りが流れてきちゃったら、
我慢なんかしてられる訳、ないの」
findings.todokanai: "That's why, when I heard a song I'm good at… not to mention it being my favorite song, there was no way I could hold it in."

findings.highlight: So that's… the reason.
findings.evidenceJa: あれは………ガチか
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes that her rooftop performance was genuine—the real thing, not a momentary lapse. The English replaces that assessment with a generic causal conclusion.
findings.japanese: あれは………ガチか。
findings.todokanai: So that's… the reason.

findings.highlight: Ogiso puts on a delighted, enchanting face.
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に嬉しそうな恍惚の表情を浮かべた
findings.explanation: Setsuna's expression is rapt or ecstatic as she relives singing with them. “Enchanting” describes how attractive her face is to an observer, redirecting her inward musical ecstasy into conventional feminine allure.
findings.japanese:
あの時のことを思い出すべく目を閉じた小木曽は、
本当に嬉しそうな恍惚の表情を浮かべた。
findings.todokanai: After closing her eyes to remember that moment, Ogiso puts on a delighted, enchanting face.

findings.highlight: I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしなんかにやれるのか、今のわたしがやってもいいことなのか、そもそも、わたしはやりたいのか
findings.explanation: The earlier three-part question is repeated here: ability, whether the person she currently is has the right to do it, and desire. The English again collapses the normative second question into ability, damaging the exact repetition on which Setsuna now bases her two-to-one vote.
findings.japanese:
「わたしなんかにやれるのか、
今のわたしがやってもいいことなのか、
そもそも、わたしはやりたいのか」
findings.todokanai: "I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it."

findings.highlight: I thought I couldn't do it. I thought I couldn't do it the way I am now.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしなんかにできないと思った。今のわたしがやってもいいこととも思えなかった
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly answers two different questions: she thought she could not do it, and she thought it was not something the present version of herself was entitled or fit to do. The English repeats inability twice, erasing one of the two votes she is about to overrule with desire.
findings.japanese:
「わたしなんかにできないと思った。
今のわたしがやってもいいこととも思えなかった」
findings.todokanai: "I thought I couldn't do it. I thought I couldn't do it the way I am now."

findings.highlight: as if to cover up various important things about herself.
findings.evidenceJa: 今決まった、色々と重要な事実を覆い隠すかのように
findings.explanation: Setsuna's playful gesture seems designed to cover the various important facts just decided—above all her reversal and participation—not biographical facts about herself. The English attaches the modifier to the wrong subject matter.
findings.japanese:
ほんの一瞬、ぺろりと舌を出した小木曽は、
今決まった、色々と重要な事実を覆い隠すかのように、
マイクを取り、立ち上がった。
findings.todokanai: Ogiso sticks out her tongue for an instant, taking the microphone and standing up, as if to cover up various important things about herself.

findings.highlight: Despite my face burning… I really am breaking out in a cold sweat.
findings.evidenceJa: 顔は火照ってるのに出るのは…やっぱり熱い汗
findings.explanation: Earlier Haruki called it cold sweat despite his flushed face. After Setsuna joins and tells him he now knows everything about her, the narration corrects itself: this time it is, after all, hot sweat. Todokanai TL says cold sweat again, reversing the emotional and verbal payoff.
findings.japanese: …顔は火照ってるのに出るのは…やっぱり熱い汗。
findings.todokanai: …Despite my face burning… I really am breaking out in a cold sweat.

findings.highlight: you know I enjoy cleaning up others' messes
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の仕切り癖を知ってて俺に振るお前が悪い
findings.explanation: Haruki blames Takeya for handing him the task despite knowing his compulsive habit of taking charge and organizing things. The English recasts that executive compulsion as enjoying the cleanup of other people's messes, changing both the trait and his attitude toward it.
findings.japanese: 「俺の仕切り癖を知ってて俺に振るお前が悪い！」
findings.todokanai: "It's your fault for throwing it my way when you know I enjoy cleaning up others' messes!"

findings.highlight: I simply don't want to leave any regrets on the stage…
findings.evidenceJa: ただ純粋に、ステージに穴を開けたくなくて
findings.explanation: Haruki's stated practical motive is not wanting an empty hole in the festival stage program. The English turns that staffing obligation into the sentimental abstraction of leaving regrets onstage.
findings.japanese:
「何度も言うけど、そう言うんじゃないから。
ただ純粋に、ステージに穴を開けたくなくて。
…お前の言うとおり、学園最後の思い出作りだし」
findings.todokanai: "I've told you many times already, that's not how it is. I simply don't want to leave any regrets on the stage… I want to create fond memories of the last of my school days, just like you said."

findings.highlight: there's the old saying
findings.evidenceJa: 恋する漢は百万馬力なのかもしれないけど
findings.explanation: Takeya tentatively improvises that a man in love may have extraordinary power. Todokanai TL converts the remark into an established ‘old saying,’ adding authority and quotation structure absent from the Japanese and changing the comic beat. Rendering the hyperbole as ‘the strength of a million horses’ is not itself treated as erroneous.
findings.japanese:
「いや、まぁ…
恋する漢は百万馬力なのかもしれないけど」
findings.todokanai: "Well… there's the old saying, 'A man in love has the strength of a million horses.'"

findings.highlight: I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…
findings.evidenceJa: 後はそのイメージを守るために見栄に見栄を重ねて
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats Setsuna's exact admission that she piled one act of keeping up appearances upon another, now recognizing the same trap in his own lie. The generic “did so many things” again deletes the accumulating pretense and weakens the explicit self-comparison.
findings.japanese:
『そうなると、
後はそのイメージを守るために見栄に見栄を重ねて…』
findings.todokanai: "When that happened, I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…"

findings.highlight: In order to get others interested in me, I'm leaving misunderstandings as they are, and slowly driving myself into a corner.
findings.evidenceJa: 相手に気に入られたくて、いい顔して、向こうの勘違いをそのまま放置して、どんどん追い込まれていって
findings.explanation: The pattern is wanting to be liked, putting on an agreeable face, leaving the other person's misunderstanding intact, and becoming trapped. The English turns being liked into attracting interest and omits the crucial performance of showing a pleasing face—the behavior Haruki has just recognized in both Setsuna and himself.
findings.japanese:
相手に気に入られたくて、いい顔して、
向こうの勘違いをそのまま放置して、
どんどん追い込まれていって。
findings.todokanai: In order to get others interested in me, I'm leaving misunderstandings as they are, and slowly driving myself into a corner.

findings.highlight: was in desperate need of such abilities.
findings.evidenceJa: その実力は、喉から食指のついた手が出てくるほどで
findings.explanation: Haruki deliberately crashes together 喉から手が出る, wanting something so badly a hand emerges from one's throat, and 食指が動く, one's index finger twitching with appetite. The generic “desperate need” preserves only the conclusion and deletes the grotesque mixed-idiom joke.
findings.japanese:
ギターしかいない俺たち軽音楽同好会にとって、
その実力は、喉から食指のついた手が出てくるほどで。
findings.todokanai: Our Light Music Club, which currently only has guitarists, was in desperate need of such abilities.

findings.highlight: my first impression of his crowd was right on the mark.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺のその第一印象は、まるっきり正鵠を得ていたことを痛感させられた
findings.explanation: After speaking with Matsukawa, Haruki finds his first impression of that individual—nervous-looking and difficult—exactly correct. “His crowd” invents a collective referent and misdirects the evaluation from Matsukawa to the music students generally.
findings.japanese:
…で、ちょっと話してみただけで、俺のその第一印象は、
まるっきり正鵠を得ていたことを痛感させられた。
findings.todokanai: …And after talking with him for a little bit, my first impression of his crowd was right on the mark.

findings.highlight: They'd give unpleasant looks
findings.evidenceJa: 気まずそうに目をそらしたり
findings.explanation: The music students awkwardly avert their eyes when the room is mentioned, behavior that suggests concealed knowledge. The English has them give unpleasant looks instead, reversing the direction of the gaze and changing discomfort into hostility.
findings.japanese:
なんだか、やけに触れたくない話題のようで、
気まずそうに目をそらしたり、
関わり合いになるのを恐れたり。
findings.todokanai: It seemed like they didn't want to touch the subject. They'd give unpleasant looks, and would try not to get involved.

findings.highlight: A piano that echoes… and nobody knows anything…
findings.evidenceJa: 誰も使っていないはずの音楽室。鳴り響くピアノ。そして、口を閉ざす生徒たち
findings.explanation: Haruki's school-mystery montage ends with students who close their mouths—an image of deliberate silence after their averted eyes. “Nobody knows anything” turns that suspicious refusal to speak into simple ignorance.
findings.japanese:
誰も使っていないはずの音楽室。
鳴り響くピアノ。
そして、口を閉ざす生徒たち。
findings.todokanai: No one should even be using that music room. A piano that echoes… and nobody knows anything…

findings.highlight: Listen and shudder!
findings.evidenceJa: 聞いて驚け
findings.explanation: Haruki says “Listen and be amazed,” setting up Kazusa's reply that she will not listen and therefore will not be amazed. “Shudder” supplies the wrong reaction and turns his boast into something ominous.
findings.japanese:
「聞いて驚け。
なんとあの…」
findings.todokanai: "Listen and shudder! It turns out she's…"

findings.highlight: In the end, I'd also slept through my usual practice time.
findings.evidenceJa: 結局、いつもの練習時間まで居座ってしまった
findings.explanation: It is just past five, and Haruki realizes he has ended up lingering in the classroom until his usual practice time. The English says he slept through the practice period, falsely implying that the time has already passed and that he missed it.
findings.japanese:
時計を見ると、何だかんだでもう５時を過ぎてる。
結局、いつもの練習時間まで居座ってしまった。
findings.todokanai: Looking at the time, it seems like it's just past five. In the end, I'd also slept through my usual practice time.

findings.highlight: a sound that was casual, profound, elegant, and stubborn
findings.evidenceJa: 軽快で、重厚で、流麗で、頑強な音
findings.explanation: Haruki describes the playing as brisk, weighty, fluid, and robust. “Casual” and especially “stubborn” are not musical equivalents for 軽快 and 頑強, so the English distorts the four-part description of the pianist's sound at the moment he encounters the instrument itself.
findings.japanese:
ほんのついさっきまで、いつものように、
軽快で、重厚で、流麗で、頑強な音を奏でてたのか。
findings.todokanai: Just a moment ago, as usual, he was playing with a sound that was casual, profound, elegant, and stubborn.

findings.highlight: my chance at almost catching the owner of Music Room 2
findings.evidenceJa: 『第二音楽室の主』の尻尾を掴むチャンス
findings.explanation: Haruki says he squandered a chance to catch the pianist's tail—that is, to get a lead on the person's identity. The English turns the missed chance for a clue into having almost caught the person outright.
findings.japanese:
とどめに『第二音楽室の主』の尻尾を掴むチャンスを、
自らのポカで棒に振ってしまった。
findings.todokanai: And wasting my chance at almost catching the owner of Music Room 2, through my own blunder.

findings.highlight: that fine thread
findings.evidenceJa: たった一つの蜘蛛の糸を掴み取った
findings.explanation: The source pointedly calls his last hope 蜘蛛の糸, “the spider's thread,” invoking Akutagawa's story and its single thread of salvation. “That fine thread” removes the title phrase and therefore the literary image that organizes Haruki's sudden reversal from failure to hope.
findings.japanese:
だけど、そのポカの果て。
最後の最後の最後に、
たった一つの蜘蛛の糸を掴み取った。
findings.todokanai: But, at the end of that blunder, right at the end of it all, I'd grabbed that fine thread.

findings.highlight: I'll catch you next time
findings.evidenceJa: 今度こそ、会える。会ってみせる
findings.explanation: Haruki resolves that next time he will meet the pianist—he will make the meeting happen. “Catch you” changes the desired encounter into capturing or apprehending the person, extending the previous clue metaphor into an action the Japanese does not state.
findings.japanese:
「今度こそ、会える。
会ってみせる」
findings.todokanai: "I'll catch you next time. I'll make sure of it."

findings.highlight: a complacent human being who was wary and securely locked the door during practice time. Yet he forgot to lock the door and window
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の練習中には厳重に鍵をかけるくせに、帰るときには施錠どころか窓を閉めることすら忘れる、用心深いくせに無頓着な人間
findings.explanation: Haruki constructs a paradoxical person: extremely cautious during practice, yet so careless on leaving that they forget not merely to lock up but even to close the window. “Complacent” is the wrong trait, and the English changes failure to close the window into failure to lock a window, blunting both the physical clue and the cautious/careless contrast.
findings.japanese:
自分の練習中には厳重に鍵をかけるくせに、
帰るときには施錠どころか窓を閉めることすら忘れる、
用心深いくせに無頓着な人間、だ。
findings.todokanai: He was just a complacent human being who was wary and securely locked the door during practice time. Yet he forgot to lock the door and window when heading home.

findings.highlight: people say 'fool around while you're still young,' right?
findings.evidenceJa: 『若いうちの馬鹿は買ってでもしろ』って言うだろ？
findings.explanation: Haruki has deliberately corrupted the fixed proverb 若いうちの苦労は買ってでもせよ, replacing youthful hardship with youthful stupidity, so that Takeya agrees before Haruki springs the correction. The English supplies an ordinary-sounding maxim instead of a visibly mangled proverb, leaving “No they don't” without the source joke's mechanism.
findings.japanese:
「それに…
『若いうちの馬鹿は買ってでもしろ』って言うだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "Besides, people say 'fool around while you're still young,' right?"

findings.highlight: move along the rain gutter between classrooms, and then jump to new footing at the other classroom
findings.evidenceJa: まずは教室と教室の間にある雨どいに移り、そこを新たな足場として向こうの教室の窓に飛び移る
findings.explanation: The plan is to transfer onto the rain gutter, use it as the new foothold, and then cross to the other classroom's window. The English instead has Haruki move along the gutter and treats the other classroom as the new footing, reversing the staging of the dangerous crossing.
findings.japanese:
まずは教室と教室の間にある雨どいに移り、
そこを新たな足場として向こうの教室の窓に飛び移る。
findings.todokanai: For starters, I should move along the rain gutter between classrooms, and then jump to new footing at the other classroom.

findings.highlight: my body would smash into the wall
findings.evidenceJa: もし手が離れたら全身ズルむけだな
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines the rough wall stripping the skin from his whole body if his hands slip. The English replaces that specific, tactile consequence with simply smashing into the wall, losing the payoff to his observation that the surface is rough.
findings.japanese:
いくら命綱があっても、
もし手が離れたら全身ズルむけだな…
findings.todokanai: Even if I have a lifeline, should I lose my grip, my body would smash into the wall…

findings.highlight: control my breath, and reach for the window
findings.evidenceJa: 息を整える間もなく、隣の教室の窓に手を伸ばす
findings.explanation: Haruki reaches for the next window without even pausing to steady his breathing. The English says that he controls his breath before reaching, reversing the haste that follows the gutter's alarming creak.
findings.japanese:
雨どいに全身を預けたときの嫌な軋み音を
聞かなかったことにするため、
息を整える間もなく、隣の教室の窓に手を伸ばす。
findings.todokanai: As soon as I put my entire body weight on the rain gutter, I hear a disturbing, creaking sound. I do my best to ignore it, control my breath, and reach for the window of the next classroom.

findings.highlight: Sensitive, with a small face
findings.evidenceJa: 線が細く、顔も小さく
findings.explanation: 線が細い describes the pianist's slight, slender build. “Sensitive” is not a physical description and invents a personality judgment just as Haruki is visually assembling the unknown pianist's identity.
findings.japanese:
線が細く、顔も小さく、
何より、その横顔の白さ。
findings.todokanai: Sensitive, with a small face, and most importantly, the paleness of the face from the side.

findings.highlight: wiping away all those minor details, what absolutely enthralls me is that strong melody
findings.evidenceJa: それらのか細いイメージを一掃する、俺の耳を叩く力強い旋律
findings.explanation: The powerful melody striking Haruki's ears sweeps away the preceding impression of physical slightness and fragility. The English demotes those visual impressions to “minor details” and invents enthrallment, breaking the deliberate contrast between the small figure and the force of her playing.
findings.japanese:
けれど、それらのか細いイメージを一掃する、
俺の耳を叩く力強い旋律。
findings.todokanai: However, wiping away all those minor details, what absolutely enthralls me is that strong melody ringing in my ears.

findings.highlight: may or may not be a violation of the school rules
findings.evidenceJa: いくつの校則を違反しているか定かでない行為
findings.explanation: There is no doubt that Haruki is violating school rules; the joke is that he cannot tell how many. The English changes uncertainty about the number of violations into uncertainty about whether any violation occurred at all.
findings.japanese:
俺の、いくつの校則を違反しているか定かでない行為は、
とうとう、校内で然るべき責任を持つ人たちの
知ることとなり。
findings.todokanai: My actions, which may or may not be a violation of the school rules, are found out by the school staff.

findings.highlight: is none other than my neighboring student
findings.evidenceJa: 放課後のお隣さんの、これが正体
findings.explanation: Kazusa is revealed as Haruki's “neighbor after school”—the unknown pianist in the room next door. The next line then identifies her as his neighbor during class, joining the two meanings of 隣 that the scene has kept separate. Calling her merely a neighboring student collapses the first half of that paired reveal into the classroom relation.
findings.japanese:
『第二音楽室の主』。
放課後のお隣さんの、これが正体。
findings.todokanai: The owner of Music Room 2… is none other than my neighboring student.

findings.highlight: It's too late to regret it now.
findings.evidenceJa: 今さらシンパシーを感じても遅すぎるってのに。
findings.explanation: シンパシー, belatedly feeling sympathy or kinship with Kazusa, becomes generic regret.
findings.japanese: 今さらシンパシーを感じても遅すぎるってのに。
findings.todokanai: It's too late to regret it now.

findings.highlight: Touma isn't all too opposed to the idea of just forgetting about what happened
findings.evidenceJa: 全部帳消しにしてもいいような気もしないでもなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that Kazusa's present expression almost makes him feel that he could let everything be wiped clean. The English transfers that willingness to Kazusa, making her the person who may be ready to forget what happened.
findings.japanese:
なんとなく、今の冬馬の表情で、
全部帳消しにしてもいいような気もしないでもなかった。
findings.todokanai: Judging by her expression, I get the feeling Touma isn't all too opposed to the idea of just forgetting about what happened.

findings.highlight: any chance of explaining myself in a cool-headed manner is out the window
findings.evidenceJa: 真面目と自己弁護するには虚しすぎる
findings.explanation: After admitting how much he enjoyed Setsuna's touch, Haruki says it would be too hollow to defend his reaction as mere earnestness or propriety. The English instead says he has lost the ability to explain himself cool-headedly, replacing the moral self-indictment with a claim about composure.
findings.japanese:
思わず小木曽の手の届かない頭上へと両手を掲げ、
至福の感触を放棄してしまう俺は、
真面目と自己弁護するには虚しすぎる。
findings.todokanai: I instinctively raise my hands above my head so Ogiso can't reach them, relinquishing myself of the blissful sensation of her hands. With that, any chance of explaining myself in a cool-headed manner is out the window.

findings.highlight: I'd never seen her until last year
findings.evidenceJa: 去年まで全然見かけなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says he had never seen Kazusa through the end of last year, consistent with her move into the regular curriculum this year. The English says he first saw her last year, shifting the timeline by a year.
findings.japanese:
「でも、ま、
道理で去年まで全然見かけなかったわけだ」
findings.todokanai: "Well, in that case, it's no wonder I'd never seen her until last year."

findings.highlight: were without a doubt from that 21
findings.evidenceJa: 全２１人中何番目くらいだったんだろう
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders what rank, among the twenty-one girls, Takeya's attempted introductions would have occupied. The English merely says those girls were among the twenty-one, deleting the ranking punchline and replacing the question with a certainty.
findings.japanese:
今まで俺に紹介してくれようとした女の子たちは、
全２１人中何番目くらいだったんだろう…
findings.todokanai: All the girls he's been trying to introduce me to were without a doubt from that 21…

findings.highlight: a model student ever since she enrolled in the music program
findings.evidenceJa: 音楽科始まって以来の優等生
