findings.explanation: The claim is that Kazusa was an outstanding student in the history of the music program—since the program itself began—not merely that she behaved as a model student from the date of her own enrollment. The same phrase is translated correctly at ref 240, making the local error especially clear.
findings.japanese:
「冬馬かずさはな…
入学当時、音楽科始まって以来の優等生だったんだとよ」
findings.todokanai: "Touma Kazusa, you see… was a model student ever since she enrolled in the music program."

findings.highlight: At first, the music teachers had all praised Touma. When compared to Touma, her classmates all appeared to be inexperienced amateurs.
findings.evidenceJa:
当初、音楽科の教師たちはこぞって冬馬を持ち上げ、
クラスメートたちは彼女と比較され、
その未熟さを幾度となくこき下ろされたらしい。
findings.explanation: Teachers repeatedly disparaging the other students as immature by comparison is reduced to classmates merely appearing inexperienced.
findings.japanese:
当初、音楽科の教師たちはこぞって冬馬を持ち上げ、
クラスメートたちは彼女と比較され、
その未熟さを幾度となくこき下ろされたらしい。
findings.todokanai: At first, the music teachers had all praised Touma. When compared to Touma, her classmates all appeared to be inexperienced amateurs.

findings.highlight: grit their teeth while taking all the jobs others wouldn't want to do
findings.evidenceJa: 他人の嫌がる仕事を黙らずにやる
findings.explanation: Haruki characterizes the class representative's role as doing the work others hate without keeping quiet about it—a pointed description of his own competent but vocal interventionism. 'Grit their teeth' implies silent endurance and reverses the 黙らず qualification.
findings.japanese:
他人の嫌がる仕事を黙らずにやるのが
クラス委員の仕事じゃなかったのか？
findings.todokanai: Isn't it the representative's job to grit their teeth while taking all the jobs others wouldn't want to do?

findings.highlight: She might refuse, despite getting along with you
findings.evidenceJa: 仲間とつるむのに拒否反応があるかもしれない
findings.explanation: Takeya warns that Kazusa may have an aversive reaction to associating with a group at all. The English presupposes that she already gets along with Haruki and merely may refuse his request, changing both the social diagnosis and the warning.
findings.japanese:
「難しいぞ、あのコは。
仲間とつるむのに拒否反応があるかもしれない」
findings.todokanai: "She's going to be a difficult one, that girl. She might refuse, despite getting along with you."

findings.highlight: On top of that, it's because… she's the one who played that beautiful melody…
findings.evidenceJa: しかも、その音を奏でてたのが…だったのなら…
findings.explanation: Haruki's suspended counterfactual—if the person producing that sound was...—is completed and supplied with the unsupported phrase 'beautiful melody.'
findings.japanese: しかも、その音を奏でてたのが…だったのなら…
findings.todokanai: On top of that, it's because… she's the one who played that beautiful melody…

findings.highlight: there are also times when you should really take a step back
findings.evidenceJa: お前は気を使ってるつもりで、実は一歩も退かなかったりする
findings.explanation: Takeya's point is not generic advice to step back: Haruki believes he is being considerate while in fact sometimes refusing to yield even a single step. The English deletes that gap between Haruki's self-image and behavior, immediately relevant to the confrontation that follows.
findings.japanese:
「あと、いつもみたいな説教もやめとけ。
お前は気を使ってるつもりで、
実は一歩も退かなかったりすることがあるからな」
findings.todokanai: "Also, don't go off lecturing like you always do. I know you mean well, but there are also times when you should really take a step back."

findings.highlight: I can hear nothing off-key. I can't clearly hear every note
findings.evidenceJa: 音が跳んでるところが見つからない。あまり聴く機会はないけど、プロと区別がつかない
findings.explanation: Haruki's amateur ears cannot find any skipped notes, and although he rarely has occasion to hear professionals, he cannot distinguish Kazusa from one. The English changes missing notes into bad intonation and misreads his limited exposure to professionals as an inability to hear every note.
findings.japanese:
素人耳では、音が跳んでるところが見つからない。
あまり聴く機会はないけど、プロと区別がつかない。
…まぁ、だからこそ素人なんだけど。
findings.todokanai: Being the amateur I am, I can hear nothing off-key. I can't clearly hear every note, but I can't tell her apart from a professional… Well, I guess that's what makes me an amateur.

findings.highlight: if I keep on rambling anyway
findings.evidenceJa: 俺がしつこく話しかけても気にするな
findings.explanation: Haruki tells Kazusa not to mind when he persistently approaches and talks to her, claiming the future right to keep initiating contact despite her silence. 'Rambling' instead describes the manner or length of speech within a conversation and loses the relationship-forming persistence.
findings.japanese:
「だから冬馬も、
俺がしつこく話しかけても気にするな」
findings.todokanai: "So please don't hold it against me if I keep on rambling anyway, Touma."

findings.highlight: I know all about how you've spent the past two years
findings.evidenceJa: 二年間、冬馬がどんな思いで過ごしてきたか
findings.explanation: Haruki provocatively claims to know what feelings Kazusa has lived with for two years. The English makes this sound like factual knowledge of how she spent the period, suppressing the invasive psychological certainty that angers her.
findings.japanese:
「だからさ、今の俺には全部わかってるんだ。
二年間、冬馬がどんな思いで過ごしてきたかってこと」
findings.todokanai: "Like I said, I understand everything now. I know all about how you've spent the past two years."

findings.highlight: I think you should try to get along with everyone
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬は、皆に歩み寄るべきだったと思う
findings.explanation: Haruki judges that Kazusa should have met the others halfway during the preceding two years. The English turns that retrospective judgment into mild present-tense advice to get along with everyone, reducing both its severity and its relevance to the history he is prosecuting.
findings.japanese:
「だけどさ、厳しいこと言ってるかもしれないけど、
それでも冬馬は、皆に歩み寄るべきだったと思うんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Still, you know… although this may sound quite painful, I think you should try to get along with everyone."

findings.highlight: I'm not sure if people our age would understand such a line of thought
findings.evidenceJa: 俺らの歳でこんな悟ったようなこと言ってもしょうがない
findings.explanation: Haruki undercuts himself, saying there is little point in someone their age talking as though he were enlightened. The English instead suggests that their peers may be unable to understand his insight, reversing self-mockery into intellectual superiority.
findings.japanese:
「そんな生き方の方が今よりよっぽど楽しいと思うけどな。
いや、まぁ俺らの歳でこんな悟ったようなこと言っても
しょうがないとは思うんだけど」
findings.todokanai: "I think living that way is a lot better in comparison. No, I guess I'm not sure if people our age would understand such a line of thought."

findings.highlight: you and us guitarists
findings.evidenceJa: 小木曽以外にはギターしかいない
findings.explanation: Haruki admits that besides Setsuna there is only a guitar—that is, Haruki himself—in the club. The plural 'us guitarists' invents at least one additional guitarist and obscures how radically incomplete the band remains.
findings.japanese:
「だからその…
キーボードがいるみたいに嘘ついてたこと。
本当は、小木曽以外にはギターしかいないのに」
findings.todokanai: "Well, you know… at me for lying that we had a keyboardist. There really isn't anyone else other than you and us guitarists."

findings.highlight: that miracle of a session on that day was only made possible
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬のピアノと小木曽の歌声が合わさったとき、あの日の奇跡のセッションが、やっと完成する
findings.explanation: Haruki looks forward: when Kazusa's piano and Setsuna's voice come together, the miraculous session from that day will finally become complete. The English converts this goal into a past causal statement about what had already made the earlier session possible, erasing the imagined completion of the trio.
findings.japanese:
俺のギターはともかく、
冬馬のピアノと小木曽の歌声が合わさったとき、
あの日の奇跡のセッションが、やっと完成するんだから。
findings.todokanai: Putting aside my performance, that miracle of a session on that day was only made possible by both Touma's piano and Ogiso's singing.

findings.highlight: it most likely had something to do with my attitude
findings.evidenceJa: 純粋に、俺の態度に対してのものだった
findings.explanation: Although Haruki still does not know why, he concludes that Kazusa's anger was directed purely at his attitude. The English reduces that explicit deduction to weak probability, weakening the premise for his plan to have someone else negotiate.
findings.japanese:
あいつが怒っているのは、
原因がさっぱりわからないというのは置いておくとして、
純粋に、俺の態度に対してのものだった。
findings.todokanai: As for why she got mad, I still don't have a clue, but it most likely had something to do with my attitude.

findings.highlight: shameless enough to tangle her up just a little bit
findings.evidenceJa: 比較的身勝手な理屈をこねるくらいには、ちょっとだけ恥知らず
findings.explanation: Haruki's narration calibrates its own moral judgment: he is shameless enough to construct a relatively selfish argument. The English invents the action of 'tangling her up' and deletes the comic self-correction over how selfish and shameless he is.
findings.japanese:
…けれど、
比較的身勝手な理屈をこねるくらいには、
ちょっとだけ恥知らずだったりする。
findings.todokanai: …However, I am shameless enough to tangle her up just a little bit.

findings.highlight: isn't it only natural for us two to know about each other
findings.evidenceJa: お互いのこと知っておくべきなのは当然だよね
findings.explanation: Setsuna throws Haruki's claim about future bandmates back at him to demand why he knows Kazusa so well; お互い refers to Haruki and Kazusa. In direct English, 'us two' refers to Setsuna and Haruki, misdirecting the retort to the people currently speaking.
findings.japanese:
「これから一緒にやっていく仲間なんだから、
お互いのこと知っておくべきなのは当然だよね？」
findings.todokanai: "We'll be doing this together, so isn't it only natural for us two to know about each other?"

findings.highlight: even a little amount of practice should be enough if you do it seriously
findings.evidenceJa: 短い期間でも本気で練習すればこれくらいできる
findings.explanation: Kazusa says this much is achievable through serious practice even over a short period. The English says only a small amount of practice is needed, contradicting the ten-hours-a-day standard she has just invoked and changing her accusation about Haruki's lack of effort.
findings.japanese:
「短い期間でも本気で練習すればこれくらいできる。
あんた偉そうなこと言ってるけど努力不足」
findings.todokanai: "To learn this, even a little amount of practice should be enough if you do it seriously. You act all high and mighty, but you don't try hard enough."

findings.highlight: help her have a more positive outlook on life
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女がそれで前向きになってくれるなら
findings.explanation: Setsuna means that the disclosure may make Kazusa more positive or receptive toward the present proposal. The English inflates that bounded hope into reforming Kazusa's entire outlook on life, changing Setsuna's immediate motive into a global judgment of her.
findings.japanese:
「うん…
彼女がそれで前向きになってくれるなら」
findings.todokanai: "Yup… If that's what would help her have a more positive outlook on life."

findings.highlight: I really want to get to know her after all you told me
findings.evidenceJa: 早くあの人と友達になりたいな
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly says she wants to become Kazusa's friend soon. The English weakens friendship to getting acquainted and invents 'after all you told me' as the cause, altering both the intimacy and urgency of her aim.
findings.japanese:
「その代わり…
絶対に、冬馬さんをわたしの前に連れてくること。
わたし、早くあの人と友達になりたいな」
findings.todokanai: "In return… I want you to get Touma-san to meet me. I really want to get to know her after all you told me."

findings.highlight: when I first heard her singing on the rooftop
findings.evidenceJa: 最初に屋上で歌ってるとこ見たとき
findings.explanation: Haruki says that when he first saw Setsuna singing on the rooftop, she struck him as someone who makes a picture. The English changes seeing to hearing, making the ensuing visual judgment 'picture perfect' lose its perceptual basis; ref 650 makes the same substitution.
findings.japanese:
「けど、本質はそんなとこじゃないんだ。
最初に屋上で歌ってるとこ見たときに感じたんだけど、
えっと、陳腐な言い方すれば『絵になる』って言うか」
findings.todokanai: "Still, that isn't really the main point here. I truly felt it when I first heard her singing on the rooftop… Well, what was that cliche phrase again? 'Picture perfect'?"

findings.highlight: I have to give up the negotiations in Music Room 2
findings.evidenceJa: 第二音楽室でのやり取りは割愛する
findings.explanation: The narrator says he will omit recounting the exchange in Music Room 2. The English says he gives up the negotiations themselves, even though the next line separately reports that the persuasion failed.
findings.japanese: まぁ、第二音楽室でのやり取りは割愛するとして。
findings.todokanai: Well, it pains me to admit it, but for now I have to give up the negotiations in Music Room 2.

findings.highlight: beautiful people are really persuasive when they're angry
findings.evidenceJa: 綺麗な人が怒ると迫力ある
findings.explanation: Setsuna says beautiful people have intimidating force or presence when angry, explaining how Kazusa drove the men away. 'Persuasive' makes the men seem convinced by an argument rather than cowed by her anger.
findings.japanese:
「しかも、みんなあっさり追い払っちゃうし。
やっぱり綺麗な人が怒ると迫力あるよねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "On top of that, you drove everyone away real quick. I guess beautiful people are really persuasive when they're angry."

findings.highlight: I don't care.
findings.evidenceJa: 知らないって
findings.explanation: Kazusa says 'I don't know,' denying Setsuna's assertion that she already understands Haruki. The English turns denial of knowledge into a declaration of indifference, changing both her stance and the setup for the repeated correction at ref 737.
findings.japanese: 「知らないって」
findings.todokanai: "I don't care."

findings.highlight: I told you, I don't care.
findings.evidenceJa: だから知らないって言ってる
findings.explanation: Kazusa repeats 'I'm telling you, I don't know,' as Setsuna presses her supposed knowledge of Haruki. Repeating 'I don't care' instead sustains the wrong emotional posture and breaks the scene's insistence on whether Kazusa knows him.
findings.japanese: 「だから知らないって言ってる」
findings.todokanai: "I told you, I don't care."

findings.highlight: You've really bought into that idiot
findings.evidenceJa: 随分と、あの馬鹿を買ってるんだな
findings.explanation: 買ってる means Setsuna values or thinks highly of Haruki. 'Bought into' instead suggests that she has accepted his pitch or been taken in by him, changing Kazusa's observation about Setsuna's esteem into skepticism about Haruki's influence.
findings.japanese: 「随分と、あの馬鹿を買ってるんだな」
findings.todokanai: "You've really bought into that idiot, huh."

findings.highlight: He kept on speaking so highly about you
findings.evidenceJa: あなたののろけ話、散々聞かされて
findings.explanation: Setsuna provocatively calls Haruki's extensive talk about Kazusa のろけ話—lovestruck or romantic boasting about her. Generic praise removes the romantic framing that makes Kazusa angry and that Haruki belatedly realizes sounded compromising.
findings.japanese:
「だぁって、わたしも怒れて来ちゃったもん。
あなたののろけ話、散々聞かされて」
findings.todokanai: "I mean, I got really angry too. He kept on speaking so highly about you."

findings.highlight: Part of the reason was probably for my sake
findings.evidenceJa: 多分、半分以上は俺のために
findings.explanation: Haruki estimates that more than half of Setsuna's ready action was probably for his sake. 'Part of the reason' removes that explicit majority and materially weakens his recognition of how strongly she is acting for him.
findings.japanese:
そして、あっさり動いてくれたから。
多分、半分以上は俺のために。
findings.todokanai: In the end, she took immediate action. Part of the reason was probably for my sake.

findings.highlight: I just dug my own grave
findings.evidenceJa: 捨てたカードが全部手札に戻ってきてしまった
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines every card he discarded as a defense returning to his hand as Setsuna quotes his own praise back at him. The generic grave idiom deletes the extended card-play logic and the joke that his supposedly discarded statements have become live evidence.
findings.japanese: 捨てたカードが全部手札に戻ってきてしまった…
findings.todokanai: Damn, I just dug my own grave…

findings.highlight: I'm not quite satisfied with the reason
findings.evidenceJa: 理由はいまいち釈然としない
findings.explanation: Haruki says the reason still is not entirely clear to him. The English says he is dissatisfied with it, changing his continuing obliviousness into a judgment that Setsuna's anger is inadequately justified.
findings.japanese: 「理由はいまいち釈然としないけど…」
findings.todokanai: "Though I'm not quite satisfied with the reason…"

findings.highlight: I made it within five minutes
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は５分くらい平気だけど
findings.explanation: Haruki says he personally does not mind Setsuna being about five minutes late, then asks whether Kazusa has anything to say. The English instead boasts that Haruki arrived within five minutes, changing who is being evaluated and removing his contrast with Kazusa's strict punctuality.
findings.japanese:
「俺は５分くらい平気だけど…
冬馬、そっちは何か言うことはないのか？」
findings.todokanai: "I made it within five minutes but… Touma, don't you have anything to say to her?"

findings.highlight: when the topic shifts to Ogiso
findings.evidenceJa: 相手が小木曽だと、途端に萎縮する
findings.explanation: Kazusa shrinks or becomes intimidated when the person she is dealing with is Setsuna. The English says her attitude changes when Setsuna becomes the topic, misidentifying direct interpersonal pressure as a conversational subject change.
findings.japanese:
相手が小木曽だと、
途端に萎縮するんだよな…何故だ？
findings.todokanai: Her attitude suddenly changes when the topic shifts to Ogiso… But seriously, why?

findings.highlight: 40 minutes had passed.
findings.evidenceJa: 今から４０分ほど前
findings.explanation: The narration jumps back to approximately forty minutes before the present scene. 'Forty minutes had passed' states elapsed forward time instead, reversing the flashback marker.
findings.japanese: 今から４０分ほど前。
findings.todokanai: 40 minutes had passed.

findings.highlight: where the slightest thing will tick off Touma
findings.evidenceJa: 軽い気持ちで面倒くさがっている冬馬を本気で怒らせて
findings.explanation: Haruki intends to push Kazusa, who is dismissing the request as a casual nuisance, into becoming genuinely angry so the contest ends either in her joining or never speaking to him again. The English makes her anger an accidental response to 'the slightest thing,' deleting his deliberate brinkmanship.
findings.japanese:
軽い気持ちで面倒くさがっている冬馬を本気で怒らせて、
仲間になってもらうか、二度と口聞いてもらえなくなるか、
そんなギリギリの勝負をすることで。
findings.todokanai: We're down to the wire, where the slightest thing will tick off Touma, and either she'll become our ally, or she'll never talk to us again.

findings.highlight: It's because she followed the instructions in the book carefully that she was able to make something like this in practice
findings.evidenceJa: 教科書にあることがマスターできてこそ、応用が効果的に利くようになる
findings.explanation: Haruki gives a general principle: only after mastering the textbook fundamentals can one apply variations effectively, and that is where future rates of improvement diverge. The English invents a direct causal account of this meal and reduces his characteristically pedantic theory to having followed instructions carefully.
findings.japanese:
教科書にあることがマスターできてこそ、
応用が効果的に利くようになる。
つまり、ここからの上達の速さに差が出るってことで。
findings.todokanai: It's because she followed the instructions in the book carefully that she was able to make something like this in practice. She'll only get better from now on.

findings.highlight: In other words, their relationship was predestined to be turbulent because of this.
findings.evidenceJa:
つまり、二人の間には、
そんな前提条件のところから齟齬があるんだろうな。
findings.explanation: A mismatch between Setsuna and Kazusa beginning at their basic premises becomes a relationship predestined to be turbulent.
findings.japanese:
つまり、二人の間には、
そんな前提条件のところから齟齬があるんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: In other words, their relationship was predestined to be turbulent because of this.

findings.highlight: she was the one waiting for this topic to be brought up
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬のその反応を熱望していたはずの小木曽
findings.explanation: Setsuna had been longing for exactly this reaction from Kazusa—her voice finally heating up and engaging seriously—yet interrupts it. The English says she merely wanted the topic introduced, replacing the desired emotional engagement with a topical milestone.
findings.japanese:
そこに冷水を浴びせたのは、
冬馬のその反応を熱望していたはずの小木曽だった。
findings.todokanai: Ogiso puts out the flames with cold water, even though she was the one waiting for this topic to be brought up.

findings.highlight: her sulky attitude is a completely different matter, given her family's history
findings.evidenceJa: ひねくれてみせたところで、本家にはとっくにネタが上がってたりして
findings.explanation: Haruki jokes that even when he tries acting contrary, the original master of contrariness—Kazusa—has already seen through his material. The English introduces an unexplained family history and no longer expresses either his imitation or her having his number.
findings.japanese:
でも、ひねくれてみせたところで、
本家にはとっくにネタが上がってたりして。
findings.todokanai: Though her sulky attitude is a completely different matter, given her family's history.

findings.highlight: You avoid competition, you make sure no one's left behind and that everyone makes it to the end together. You don't oppose anyone, always smiling quietly.
findings.evidenceJa: 決して人とは争わず、いつも静かに笑ってる
findings.explanation: Kazusa's escalating parallel description culminates in an unmistakable adaptation of the cadence and wording of Miyazawa Kenji's Ame ni mo Makezu. The English conveys the component traits as ordinary explanatory prose but does not recreate or signal the literary echo that structures the characterization.
findings.japanese:
「非競争主義、脱落者ゼロ、一緒にゴール。
決して人とは争わず、いつも静かに笑ってる」
findings.todokanai: "You avoid competition, you make sure no one's left behind and that everyone makes it to the end together. You don't oppose anyone, always smiling quietly."

findings.highlight: that's the kind of person I've always striven to be
findings.evidenceJa: 将来的にはそういう人になりたい
findings.explanation: Haruki says that this is indeed the kind of person he would like to become in the future. The English claims it has always been his active program, reversing future aspiration into established lifelong striving immediately after Kazusa's literary caricature.
findings.japanese:
それにしても容赦のない…
確かに、将来的にはそういう人になりたいけどさぁ。
findings.todokanai: Her words are merciless… but it's true, that's the kind of person I've always striven to be.

findings.highlight: Don't try to break my train of thought.
findings.evidenceJa: そうやって足下を切り崩そうとしないの
findings.explanation: Setsuna's observation that Kazusa knows Haruki well undermines the footing of Kazusa's argument, and Kazusa tells her not to chip away at it that way. The English instead complains of an interrupted train of thought, losing Setsuna's successful counterattack and Kazusa's defensive recognition of it.
findings.japanese:
「今はあたしの話なんかしてないから。
そうやって足下を切り崩そうとしないの」
findings.todokanai: "We're not talking about me right now. Don't try to break my train of thought."

findings.highlight: Maybe you shouldn't go?
findings.evidenceJa: 行かない方がいいかしら
findings.explanation: Setsuna's mother wonders whether she herself—or the family—had better not attend, because she could not bear watching Setsuna embarrass herself. The English addresses Setsuna and advises her not to participate, changing whose prospective attendance is under discussion.
findings.japanese:
「…行かない方がいいかしら？
娘が全校生徒の前で大恥かくのは見るに忍びないし…」
findings.todokanai: "…Maybe you shouldn't go? I don't want my daughter to make a complete fool of herself in front of all the students…"

findings.highlight: although I look back at the road behind, I'm unable to see that brilliant face
findings.evidenceJa: 元来た道を振り返り、俺にその整った顔を見せず
findings.explanation: Kazusa stops beside Haruki and turns back toward the road they came from, withholding her face from him. The English makes Haruki the one who looks back and merely fails to see her face, reversing the physical action and deleting Kazusa's deliberate concealment.
findings.japanese:
俺の隣を歩く歩調は、いつの間にか止まり、
元来た道を振り返り、俺にその整った顔を見せず。
findings.todokanai: She had stopped walking by my side at some point, and although I look back at the road behind, I'm unable to see that brilliant face.

findings.highlight: because I experienced that kind of drama at home in the past as well
findings.evidenceJa: 俺も、あのホームドラマにあてられていたから
findings.explanation: Haruki keeps talking because he too has been emotionally affected by the Ogiso family's home-drama-like warmth they just witnessed. The English says he continues because he experienced comparable family drama in the past, replacing the immediate emotional cause with biography.
findings.japanese:
それでも話し続けてしまうのは、
俺も、あのホームドラマにあてられていたからで。
findings.todokanai: Even so, I continue my story, because I experienced that kind of drama at home in the past as well.

findings.highlight: You're bold, Kitahara. Did you plan to convince me with your tepid attitude…? You're getting ahead of yourself.
findings.evidenceJa: 潔いな北原。そんなぬるい根性であたしを口説こうとしてたわけ？…５年早いね
findings.explanation: Kazusa sarcastically notes how readily Haruki had conceded failure, mocks the weak resolve with which he meant to win her over, and says he is five years too early. 'Bold' reverses the first evaluation, while 'getting ahead of yourself' removes the pointed five-year measure and its superiority joke.
findings.japanese:
「潔いな北原。
そんなぬるい根性であたしを口説こうとしてたわけ？
…５年早いね」
findings.todokanai: "You're bold, Kitahara. Did you plan to convince me with your tepid attitude…? You're getting ahead of yourself."

findings.highlight: which was very close to being disbanded
findings.evidenceJa: 一度空中分解した軽音楽同好会
findings.explanation: The club had actually fallen apart once and has now recovered the bare minimum form. The English says it merely came close to disbanding, softening an accomplished prior collapse into an averted possibility.
findings.japanese:
一度空中分解した軽音楽同好会は、
最低限の、本当に最低限の体裁を取り戻し、
いよいよ最後の学園祭へと突き進んでいく。
findings.todokanai: But at last, the Light Music Club, which was very close to being disbanded, has now managed to regain its form at the bare minimum and is finally pushing toward its final school festival.

findings.highlight: a singer who can only sing
findings.evidenceJa: 専任ボーカル
findings.explanation: 専任 means dedicated or specialist. The line identifies the band's instrumentation problem—a dedicated vocalist, two guitarists, and a keyboardist—not a vocalist whose abilities are limited to singing.
findings.japanese:
「確かに四人いれば普通バンドは組めるけど、
それが専任ボーカルとギター二人とキーボードとなれば
全然話は別」
findings.todokanai: "Certainly, we could form a normal band with four people, but it's a different story with a singer who can only sing, two guitarists, and a keyboardist."

findings.highlight: In the majority, right?
findings.evidenceJa: メジャー指向だよねぇ
findings.explanation: メジャー指向 describes mainstream or major-label-oriented tastes. 'In the majority' is not a viable reading and leaves the proposition unintelligible.
findings.japanese: 「メジャー指向だよねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "In the majority, right?"

findings.highlight: We absolutely don't have enough people in the sound department.
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対的にパートが足りないのよ
findings.explanation: パート means musical parts here. Kazusa says their instrumentation is missing essential parts, not that a nonexistent sound department is understaffed.
findings.japanese:
「今のメンバー構成なら、
誰かがやらなくちゃならない事なの。
絶対的にパートが足りないのよ」
findings.todokanai: "With our current numbers, someone has to take on that role. We absolutely don't have enough people in the sound department."

findings.highlight: I'd like to at least finish one song before the week is done.
findings.evidenceJa: とにかくまずはドラム。少なくとも１曲目は今週中に欲しい。
findings.explanation: Kazusa specifically wants the programmed drum part for at least the first song by the end of the week. The translation turns that assignment into the much broader task of finishing an entire song.
findings.japanese:
「とにかくまずはドラム。
少なくとも１曲目は今週中に欲しい。できる？
ま、できなくてもやってもらうんだけど」
findings.todokanai: "Anyway, drums first. I'd like to at least finish one song before the week is done. Can you do it? Well, do it even if you can't."

findings.highlight: You can sing the melody to the song, right?
findings.evidenceJa: キーは原曲のまんまで行けるんだよね？
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks whether Setsuna can perform the song in its original key. The translation substitutes the unrelated question of whether she can sing its melody.
findings.japanese:
「キーは原曲のまんまで行けるんだよね？
発声練習する？」
findings.todokanai: "You can sing the melody to the song, right? Want to do voice training?"

findings.highlight: you could just stop complaining and show us something real
findings.evidenceJa: 文句を言わせない実力と、現実的なビジョンを示せば良かったのに
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that, if Takeya objected, he should have demonstrated unanswerable competence and a realistic vision. The translation replaces those two standards with an instruction to stop complaining and vaguely show 'something real.'
findings.japanese:
「不満があるならさ、文句を言わせない実力と、
現実的なビジョンを示せば良かったのに。
そしたら喜んで従ったよ？　『部長代理』」
findings.todokanai: "If you don't like it, you could just stop complaining and show us something real. Then I'll be happy to oblige, Mister Vice President."

findings.highlight: But in return, I want you to promise me something.
findings.evidenceJa: その代わり、信じさせてもらうからな
findings.explanation: Haruki is declaring that in exchange he will trust Kazusa to take care of everything that remains. He is not asking Kazusa to make a promise; the translation changes both the speech act and who assumes the trust.
findings.japanese:
「ああ約束する。
もう学園祭まではギターのことしか考えない。
その代わり、信じさせてもらうからな」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, I promise. I won't think about anything else but the guitar until the school festival. But in return, I want you to promise me something."

findings.highlight: we've regained that teacher-student relationship
findings.evidenceJa: あの時の主従関係を取り戻した
findings.explanation: 主従関係 is a master-servant relationship. Recasting it as teacher-student deletes Haruki's comic political-status metaphor and the self-abasing dependence he has just accepted.
findings.japanese:
今日やっと、あの時の主従関係を取り戻した。
だからもう、心配することはやめよう。
findings.todokanai: And today, finally, we've regained that teacher-student relationship, so there's no more need to worry now.

findings.highlight: our usual unenergetic conversation
findings.evidenceJa: いつもよりちょっと元気のない会話
findings.explanation: The conversation is a little less lively than usual. The translation instead characterizes their conversations as habitually lifeless, reversing the explicit comparison and changing the relationship baseline.
findings.japanese:
いつものように、真っ暗な道を三人で歩き、
駅で一人減って電車に乗り込んだ俺たちは、
いつもよりちょっと元気のない会話を交わした。
findings.todokanai: After the three of us walked down the dark streets together, and after the two of us got on the train, we engaged in our usual unenergetic conversation.

findings.highlight: The guitar head laid on top of me when I woke up on the floor last night.
findings.evidenceJa: ギターがベッドの上で毛布にくるまれてた
findings.explanation: The guitar was on the bed, wrapped in a blanket, while Haruki woke on the floor. The translation invents a guitar head lying on Haruki and loses the visual joke about how Kazusa treated him versus the instrument.
findings.japanese:
昨夜、俺が床の上で目覚めたとき、
ギターがベッドの上で毛布にくるまれてたっけ。
findings.todokanai: The guitar head laid on top of me when I woke up on the floor last night.

findings.highlight: There are days when I don't have to play at all
findings.evidenceJa: 一日中弾かなくてもいい日がこんなにあるなんて
findings.explanation: Kazusa marvels that there are so many days when she does not have to play all day long. The translation says there are days when she does not have to play at all, reversing the scope of the relief.
findings.japanese:
「ほんと、今は天国。
一日中弾かなくてもいい日がこんなにあるなんて」
findings.todokanai: "It's really paradise right now. There are days when I don't have to play at all…"

findings.highlight: when someone wants to change the subject
findings.evidenceJa: その転調に合わせられるくらいには、俺の人生、練習は重ねてきたつもりだ
findings.explanation: 転調 literally means musical modulation and is applied to Kazusa's conversational change of key; 合わせる sustains the musical metaphor while also meaning to adapt or play along. The translation conveys only a topic change and drops the recreatable music joke.
findings.japanese:
その転調に合わせられるくらいには、
俺の人生、練習は重ねてきたつもりだ。
findings.todokanai: I've gained enough experience throughout my life to know when to play along when someone wants to change the subject.

findings.highlight: we took a step forward with our preparations for the performance, but we're still short on time
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっとだけ前進しそうだった俺のステージは、最終的には『時間切れ』という無難な結論になった
findings.explanation: Haruki's own 'stage'—both his chance to join the rehearsal and his relational opening—seemed about to advance but ended when time literally ran out at the station. The translation turns this into general progress on festival preparations plus an ongoing lack of time.
findings.japanese:
結局、ちょっとだけ前進しそうだった俺のステージは、
最終的には『時間切れ』という無難な結論になった。
findings.todokanai: In the end, it seems like we took a step forward with our preparations for the performance, but we're still short on time.

findings.highlight: I thought that I wouldn't be capable of making such an impossible assumption
findings.evidenceJa: そういう、あり得ない仮定しか、想像できなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki could imagine only the impossible hypothesis that Kazusa was inviting him home. The translation says he thought himself incapable of making that hypothesis, reversing the construction.
findings.japanese:
そういう、あり得ない仮定しか、
想像できなかったけど…
findings.todokanai: I thought that I wouldn't be capable of making such an impossible assumption, but…

findings.highlight: I saw a white room around 40 square meters large.
findings.evidenceJa: そこにはピアノを始め、沢山の楽器が転がっていた
findings.explanation: The line explicitly reveals a piano and many other instruments scattered through the room. The translation omits the entire clause, deleting the content that establishes it as a private music studio.
findings.japanese:
冬馬がその地下室の電源をつけると、
二十畳くらいの広めの白い部屋があり、
そこにはピアノを始め、沢山の楽器が転がっていた。
findings.todokanai: And when Touma turned on the lights, I saw a white room around 40 square meters large.

findings.highlight: a microphone dangling from the ceiling of a small room, closed off by glass windows
findings.evidenceJa: 部屋の天井からぶら下がっている高そうなマイクと、部屋の奥にある、ガラスで仕切られた狭い部屋
findings.explanation: The source names two separate features: an expensive microphone hanging from the main room's ceiling and a narrow glass-partitioned room at the back. The translation collapses them into a microphone hanging inside the glass room.
findings.japanese:
けれど何よりも俺の目を点にしたのは、
部屋の天井からぶら下がっている高そうなマイクと、
部屋の奥にある、ガラスで仕切られた狭い部屋。
findings.todokanai: But what caught my eye the most was a microphone dangling from the ceiling of a small room, closed off by glass windows.

findings.highlight: In fact, perhaps I've been pushing my luck all day today, and it's simply that she has grown more tolerant to it.
findings.evidenceJa:
そもそも、今までと同じように、
実は今でも踏み込むだけ踏み込んでて、
ただ向こうの許容範囲が広がっただけかもしれないけど。
findings.explanation: 今までと同じように becomes 'all day today,' narrowing a recurring pattern to one day.
findings.japanese:
そもそも、今までと同じように、
実は今でも踏み込むだけ踏み込んでて、
ただ向こうの許容範囲が広がっただけかもしれないけど。
findings.todokanai: In fact, perhaps I've been pushing my luck all day today, and it's simply that she has grown more tolerant to it.

findings.highlight: the vivid image of what lies underneath is still fresh in my…
findings.evidenceJa: その制服に包まれた内部をつぶさにイメージできる今の状態では
findings.explanation: Haruki says that, although Kazusa looks as usual, he can now picture in detail what the uniform contains. The English terminates at 'my…' and never supplies the grammatical or semantic completion before the next speaker.
findings.japanese:
しかし、いつもと全く同じ外見でも、
その制服に包まれた内部をつぶさにイメージできる
今の状態では…
findings.todokanai: But even with her usual school uniform, the vivid image of what lies underneath is still fresh in my…

findings.highlight: the incredibly sociable attitude
findings.evidenceJa: 今までの小木曽とは違いすぎるあけすけな態度
findings.explanation: あけすけ describes Setsuna's startlingly open, unguarded display of favoritism, not mere sociability. The translation changes the nature of the behavioral shift driving the surrounding rumors.
findings.japanese:
今までの小木曽とは違いすぎるあけすけな態度に、
周囲がついていけてない。
findings.todokanai: Our surroundings can't keep up with the incredibly sociable attitude that Ogiso had never shown before.

findings.highlight: With a lot of sugar.
findings.evidenceJa: 一番量の多いやつで
findings.explanation: Kazusa orders the largest available cafe au lait, not one with extra sugar. Her large sugar intake is revealed separately afterward, so this substitution also damages the timing of that character joke.
findings.japanese:
「カフェオレ。
一番量の多いやつで」
findings.todokanai: "Cafe au lait. With a lot of sugar."

findings.highlight: just how little faith did I have in us, anyway?
findings.evidenceJa: どれだけ信用がなかったんだ俺
findings.explanation: Haruki is delighted that Setsuna is so overwhelmingly happy for him, then realizes how little confidence she must have had in him—or how little credibility he had. The translation makes Haruki the one who lacked faith in the group.
findings.japanese:
これがまた、俺の予想を遥かに越えた勢いで、
こんなに心から喜んでくれることが本当に嬉しくて。
…というか、どれだけ信用がなかったんだ俺。
findings.todokanai: From the bottom of my heart, I feel so happy that we've completely blown past all my predictions… Come to think of it, just how little faith did I have in us, anyway?

findings.highlight: He worked hard all by himself
findings.evidenceJa: たった一人でずっと頑張って、ちゃんと期待した通りの結果を出したんだね
findings.explanation: Setsuna is praising Haruki directly: 'You worked hard all by yourself.' The translation shifts the address into third-person narration even though Haruki is present and being spoken to.
findings.japanese:
「たった一人でずっと頑張って、
ちゃんと期待した通りの結果を出したんだね、凄いよ」
findings.todokanai: "He worked hard all by himself, and he managed to produce just the result we were hoping for! Amazing!"

findings.highlight: Touma completely takes over the conversation, noticing that I have absolutely no idea how to explain myself.
findings.evidenceJa: どうやって言い訳しようか、それもどっちに言い訳しようか逡巡した隙に、冬馬があっさり流してくれてしまった
findings.explanation: Haruki hesitates over how to explain himself and, crucially, which of the two girls he owes an explanation to; Kazusa simply lets the matter pass. The translation deletes the two-sided dilemma and invents Kazusa noticing it and taking over.
findings.japanese:
どうやって言い訳しようか、
それもどっちに言い訳しようか逡巡した隙に、
冬馬があっさり流してくれてしまった。
findings.todokanai: Touma completely takes over the conversation, noticing that I have absolutely no idea how to explain myself.

findings.highlight: Is she complimenting me?
findings.evidenceJa: 庇ってくれた、のか？
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether Kazusa covered for or protected him by concealing the private tutoring. He is not asking whether she complimented him.
findings.japanese: 庇ってくれた、のか？
findings.todokanai: Is she complimenting me?

findings.highlight: evening hasn't settled in yet
findings.evidenceJa: それでも夕方のまま留まっている時間
findings.explanation: Despite shortening days, it is still lingering in evening at a little after five. The translation says evening has not arrived, reversing the scene's temporal image.
findings.japanese:
時計を見ても、まだ５時をちょっと過ぎたところ。
日に日に短くなっていく昼が、
それでも夕方のまま留まっている時間。
findings.todokanai: I look at my watch… It's a little past 5 o'clock. Even though daytime is shorter in this season, evening hasn't settled in yet.

findings.highlight: Our first rehearsal will be this Saturday and Sunday
findings.evidenceJa: この土日が第一の勝負どころだから
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls the weekend their first critical juncture or decisive push. It cannot be their first rehearsal: the script has already shown repeated rehearsals and a completed first song.
findings.japanese:
「この土日が第一の勝負どころだから、
今週末は泊まり込みで合宿ね」
findings.todokanai: "Our first rehearsal will be this Saturday and Sunday, so you'll all be staying over this weekend."

findings.highlight: whether or not we can get permission for her to stay over
findings.evidenceJa: 外泊を許可できる環境かどうか、そこに尽きるんです
findings.explanation: Haruki says the sole issue is whether the environment is safe and suitable enough for the parents to permit an overnight stay. The translation makes his criterion circular—whether permission itself can be obtained—and removes the safety argument.
findings.japanese:
「お母さん、
一生懸命かどうかはこの際問題じゃないんです。
外泊を許可できる環境かどうか、そこに尽きるんです」
findings.todokanai: "Ma'am, it's not a matter of us doing our best. It's just a matter of whether or not we can get permission for her to stay over."

findings.highlight: Start off with a strong emphasis on reason, then make an appeal to human sympathy leaving no room for any remaining opposition.
findings.evidenceJa: これぞ北原式論破術
findings.explanation: The translation omits the punchline that names this maneuver 'the Kitahara school of winning arguments.' That mock-branding is the self-parodic payoff to Haruki's description of his own technique.
findings.japanese:
最初に正論であることを強調しておきながら、
最後は人情話で誤魔化しつつ押し切る。
これぞ北原式論破術。
findings.todokanai: Start off with a strong emphasis on reason, then make an appeal to human sympathy leaving no room for any remaining opposition.

findings.highlight: that's the only thing he's good at
findings.evidenceJa: セコい詭弁に関してだけは、あたしたちは、北原の足下にも及ばない
findings.explanation: Kazusa limits the comparison: only when it comes to cheap sophistry are she and Setsuna nowhere near Haruki. The translation invents the broader insult that sophistry is the only thing Haruki is good at.
findings.japanese:
「セコい詭弁に関してだけは、
あたしたちは、北原の足下にも及ばない。
…安心して任せればいい」
findings.todokanai: "We can't hold a candle to Kitahara when it comes to sophistry, that's the only thing he's good at… Don't worry and just leave it to him."

findings.highlight: Just as I had carefully planned
findings.evidenceJa: 自分的には予定調和ながらも
findings.explanation: 予定調和 means the group's shock at the mansion is predictable or foreordained from Haruki's perspective. It does not mean he carefully planned that reaction; the translation invents personal agency.
findings.japanese:
自分的には予定調和ながらも、
冬馬家の豪華さに衝撃を受けるところから、
俺たちの合宿は幕を開けた。
findings.todokanai: Just as I had carefully planned, our stay started off with everyone being taken aback by the Touma household's extravagance.

findings.highlight: After giving it some more thought
findings.evidenceJa: 持ち時間を考えると
findings.explanation: 持ち時間 is the band's allotted stage time. They need more than one song to fill their slot, not because Kazusa has simply given the matter more thought.
findings.japanese:
「持ち時間を考えると、
レパートリー１曲じゃ全然足りないし。
あと２曲、最低でも１曲は」
findings.todokanai: "After giving it some more thought, one song isn't enough for our repertoire. We should have two more songs if possible, or at the very least one more."

findings.highlight: is not laughing anymore
findings.evidenceJa: さっきまで笑ってたカラスがもう笑顔
findings.explanation: The line moves from Kazusa laughing a moment ago to smiling now. Todokanai TL reverses that into her no longer laughing and drops the smile, changing the visible emotional progression. The Japanese also plays on a proverb about a crow's rapidly changing mood, but an English translation may recreate rather than literally retain that culturally specific verbal mechanism.
findings.japanese: さっきまで笑ってたカラスがもう笑顔…
findings.todokanai: The raven that was laughing is not laughing anymore…

findings.highlight: Even though I was busy with class rep work and always headed straight home to study in the past
findings.evidenceJa: 委員長の霍乱と言われようが、帰宅部の冷や水と言われようが
findings.explanation: Haruki adapts two stock expressions—鬼の霍乱 and 年寄りの冷や水—to his roles as class rep and homecoming-club member. The translation invents a history of being busy and going home to study, eliminating both parallel jokes.
findings.japanese:
委員長の霍乱と言われようが、
帰宅部の冷や水と言われようが、
楽しむことだけは絶対に忘れたくない。
findings.todokanai: Even though I was busy with class rep work and always headed straight home to study in the past, I won't forget to have fun this time.

findings.highlight: "My fingers are numb…"
findings.evidenceJa: 「指がつった…」
findings.explanation: 指がつった means Haruki's fingers cramped, not that they went numb.
findings.japanese: 「指がつった…」
findings.todokanai: "My fingers are numb…"

findings.highlight: Despite feeling quite awful last night
findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜の段階でも余裕で壊滅中だった俺は、ちょっとばかり目眩がしたけど
findings.explanation: What was still 'devastated' the previous night was Haruki's ability to play the new song; the prospect of full-band practice makes him dizzy. The translation treats 壊滅中 as a physical illness he was suffering last night.
findings.japanese:
昨夜の段階でも余裕で壊滅中だった俺は、
ちょっとばかり目眩がしたけど、師の命令には逆らえず、
１曲目よりもかなり早い段階で全体練習が始まった。
findings.todokanai: Despite feeling quite awful last night and still feeling kind of dizzy, I can't disobey my master. We started band practice far earlier than we did for the first song.

findings.highlight: only you have nothing more to show
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬にだけは何の見せ場もないだろ？
findings.explanation: Haruki argues that Kazusa alone lacks a showcase or spotlight moment in the arrangement. 'Nothing more to show' instead implies that she has exhausted what she can demonstrate, distorting both the music proposal and its flattering motive.
findings.japanese:
「だって考えてもみろよ。
小木曽はボーカルだし、俺もソロが入る。
けど、冬馬にだけは何の見せ場もないだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "I mean, just think about it. Ogiso's the singer, and I'm also doing solos. But only you have nothing more to show, right?"

findings.highlight: I'm pridefully proclaiming this as my own personal wish
findings.evidenceJa: それは自分から望んだことだって胸を張ってるけど
findings.explanation: The omitted subject is Kazusa: she proudly maintains that being forgotten and remaining an ordinary-course underachiever is what she chose. Haruki realizes that state is only a hollow by-product of her stubbornness elsewhere. The translation makes Haruki the one proclaiming a personal wish.
findings.japanese:
それは自分から望んだことだって胸を張ってるけど、
そんなのは、別のことで意地を張ってしまったときの
虚しい副産物にしか過ぎないってわかってしまった。
findings.todokanai: Although I'm pridefully proclaiming this as my own personal wish, when I honestly think about it… it's really nothing more than the by-product of my stubbornness regarding a different matter.

findings.highlight: "Of course not…! I don't overreact that much."
findings.evidenceJa:
「やだなぁもう…！
わたし、そんなに思い込み激しくないよぉ」
findings.explanation: 思い込み激しくない becomes 'I don't overreact that much,' shifting from jumping to conclusions to emotional reaction.
findings.japanese:
「やだなぁもう…！
わたし、そんなに思い込み激しくないよぉ」
findings.todokanai: "Of course not…! I don't overreact that much."

findings.highlight: I can't chase after her
findings.evidenceJa: 追い越すことも、止めることも、そして責めることもできず、ただ同じ速度で、小木曽の後を追いかけるだけ
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot overtake Setsuna, stop her, or reproach her; all he can do is follow at the same pace. The translation says he cannot chase her and immediately says he does follow her, replacing the first action and creating a contradiction.
findings.japanese:
わからないから、追い越すことも、止めることも、
そして責めることもできず、ただ同じ速度で、
小木曽の後を追いかけるだけ。
findings.todokanai: After all, I have no idea what she's thinking, I can't chase after her, stop her, or even counter her. I can only keep the same pace, following after Ogiso.

findings.highlight: She must have taken my ambiguous response as a negative one, and decided to ignore me.
findings.evidenceJa: 訳がわからないが故の曖昧な反応を、きっちり“悪”だと糾弾する
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly condemns Haruki's ambiguous reaction, born of incomprehension, as morally 'bad.' The translation turns that accusation into her private interpretation of his response and invents a decision to ignore him.
findings.japanese:
俺の、訳がわからないが故の曖昧な反応を、
きっちり“悪”だと糾弾する。
findings.todokanai: She must have taken my ambiguous response as a negative one, and decided to ignore me.

findings.highlight: I have absolutely no idea what could resolve this problem.
findings.evidenceJa: その心当たりも解決方法も、今の俺はまるっきり持ち合わせていない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he possesses neither a clue to the cause nor a way to fix it. The translation omits the first half of that information state, which is central to why he cannot respond to Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
そして、その心当たりも解決方法も、
今の俺はまるっきり持ち合わせていないって、こと。
findings.todokanai: And I have absolutely no idea what could resolve this problem.

findings.highlight: the unexpected attitude and reply
findings.evidenceJa: 予想通りの言葉と態度と、予想外のタイミング
findings.explanation: Setsuna's words and manner are exactly what Haruki expected; only the timing is unexpected. The translation reverses the sentence's explicit expected/unexpected contrast.
findings.japanese:
予想通りの言葉と態度と、予想外のタイミングに、
思わず声と口調が上ずってしまう。
findings.todokanai: My voice inadvertently rises at the unexpected attitude and reply.

findings.highlight: I don't want you to feel bad.
findings.evidenceJa: モヤモヤした気持ちでいるのは嫌だから
findings.explanation: Haruki says he does not want to remain in a state of unresolved unease even for an hour. The translation changes the experiencer to Setsuna and recasts his motive as protecting her feelings.
findings.japanese:
「たとえ１時間でも、
モヤモヤした気持ちでいるのは嫌だから」
findings.todokanai: "Even if it's only an hour, I don't want you to feel bad."

findings.highlight: She told me everything…
findings.evidenceJa: そしたらバレてるって
findings.explanation: Kazusa told Haruki that Setsuna had already figured out the secret. She did not disclose 'everything' to him; the translation falsely makes Kazusa the source of Setsuna's private history or feelings.
findings.japanese:
「さっき、小木曽のこと冬馬に相談した。
そしたらバレてるって…」
findings.todokanai: "I spoke with Touma about you a while ago. She told me everything…"

findings.highlight: "The closer you are to everyone, the easier it becomes to feel left out, even if it's just over small things… Kitahara-kun, did you know that?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「みんなとの距離が近ければ近いほど、
ちょっとしたことで、徹底的に仲間外れになるんだよ…
北原くん、そういうの知ってるかな？」
findings.explanation: 徹底的に仲間外れになる is weakened from being completely ostracized to feeling left out.
findings.japanese:
「みんなとの距離が近ければ近いほど、
ちょっとしたことで、徹底的に仲間外れになるんだよ…
北原くん、そういうの知ってるかな？」
findings.todokanai: "The closer you are to everyone, the easier it becomes to feel left out, even if it's just over small things… Kitahara-kun, did you know that?"

findings.highlight: they were close friends who'd stayed over at her house just a week prior to that
findings.evidenceJa: しかもそれが先週自分の家に泊まってた親友とかもう
findings.explanation: The compressed singular それ and 親友 indicate that a member of the exclusion side had been Setsuna's close friend and had stayed at her house the week before. The translation pluralizes the relationship and claims that all of 'they' were close friends who had stayed over.
findings.japanese:
小木曽から一つ一つのエピソードを聞くたびに、
少しずつ胃に重いモノが溜まってくるようだった。
しかもそれが先週自分の家に泊まってた親友とかもう…
findings.todokanai: Every single one of Ogiso's stories I hear gradually makes me feel more and more sick to the stomach. What's worse is the fact that they were close friends who'd stayed over at her house just a week prior to that.

findings.highlight: would it really be alright for me to ask Ogiso about it?
findings.evidenceJa: それでいいのか小木曽と問い質したくもなる
findings.explanation: Haruki wants to press Setsuna on whether reverting to her vulnerable former self because of him is really all right. The translation instead makes him wonder whether he has permission to ask her, reversing the modal relation.
findings.japanese:
光栄と言えばこの上なく光栄なんだけど、
それでいいのか小木曽と問い質したくもなる。
findings.todokanai: It's actually an honor among honors that I've managed to do this, but would it really be alright for me to ask Ogiso about it?

findings.highlight: From now on, you 'should' call me Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: 『雪菜“が”いいからね』
findings.explanation: Setsuna has changed the earlier 雪菜でいい, 'Setsuna is fine,' to 雪菜がいい, 'Setsuna is the one I want.' The narration explicitly calls the one-particle change a power-up, but the translation repeats the same instruction and emphasizes 'should,' so the grammatical escalation no longer exists.
findings.japanese: 『雪菜“が”いいからね』
findings.todokanai: "From now on, you 'should' call me Setsuna."

findings.highlight: Everyone I got along with in my class… Until the summer holidays, anyway.
findings.evidenceJa: 仲のいいクラスだったんだよ………夏休みまではね
findings.explanation: Setsuna says theirs was a close-knit class until summer vacation. The translation misparses the class as 'everyone I got along with' and leaves the social setup as a fragment.
findings.japanese:
「中学のときはみんなそう呼んでた。
男子だって女子だって。
仲のいいクラスだったんだよ………夏休みまではね」
findings.todokanai: "Everyone called me that in middle school, both boys and girls. Everyone I got along with in my class… Until the summer holidays, anyway."

findings.highlight: everything that I just did in front of Setsuna would be…
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちの正面からやってきた雪菜の、あの行動の意味は…
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders what Setsuna's conspicuous behavior as she approached the two of them would mean if Kazusa had been listening since the shoe lockers. The English assigns the behavior to Haruki instead and replaces that specific question with everything he did in front of Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
だって、そうじゃないとすると、
俺たちの正面からやってきた雪菜の、
あの行動の意味は…
findings.todokanai: Because if it isn't, everything that I just did in front of Setsuna would be…

findings.highlight: I'm just a simple commoner, after all…
findings.evidenceJa: 庶民派、だからな…
findings.explanation: The elided subject is the princess in the immediately preceding exchange—Setsuna is down-to-earth enough to accept such a cheap tribute. The English makes Haruki call himself a commoner and breaks the improvised princess, knight, and tribute metaphor.
findings.japanese: 「庶民派、だからな…」
findings.todokanai: "I'm just a simple commoner, after all…"

findings.highlight: I'd just like to get better at playing before then.
findings.evidenceJa: それまでに、ちゃんと弾けるようになってたらな
findings.explanation: Haruki says they can go if he has learned to play properly by then, using that condition to evade Setsuna's suggestion that the three visit his couples-only haunted house. The English turns the conditional answer into a general wish, leaving the next line's self-congratulation about a clever segue without its actual verbal mechanism.
findings.japanese: 「それまでに、ちゃんと弾けるようになってたらな」
findings.todokanai: "I'd just like to get better at playing before then."

findings.highlight: You can stop pretending.
findings.evidenceJa: セコい真似するな
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Haruki's maneuver petty: after establishing first-name terms with Setsuna, he tries to restore distance by presenting the apples as being from “Ogiso.” She accepts only after he corrects the donor to “Setsuna.” “Stop pretending” does not identify the cheap naming maneuver and obscures the new relationship rule being enforced.
findings.japanese: 「セコい真似するな」
findings.todokanai: "You can stop pretending."

findings.highlight: Usually, she'd get annoyed by this point from talking back and being dismissive of him, but today, she's being unusually humble.
findings.evidenceJa: いつもなら、そろそろいい加減うざくなってきて、噛みつくかシカトするはずの冬馬が、今日に限っては妙に腰が低い。
findings.explanation: Normally, once Suwa's lecture became sufficiently irritating, Kazusa would snap back at him or ignore him. The English makes talking back and dismissiveness sound like causes of her annoyance and leaves the sentence grammatically confused, obscuring the contrast with today's unusual humility.
findings.japanese:
いつもなら、そろそろいい加減うざくなってきて、
噛みつくかシカトするはずの冬馬が、
今日に限っては妙に腰が低い。
findings.todokanai: Usually, she'd get annoyed by this point from talking back and being dismissive of him, but today, she's being unusually humble.

findings.highlight: The way she's saying "I'm sorry" is completely different too. Even if it's only natural to accuse her of not doing it in good faith, she's honestly bowing her head
findings.evidenceJa: 『すいません』も、いつも同様、誠意がこもっていないのはまぁ当然としても、横向いたり睨んだりせず、普通に俯いている。
findings.explanation: Kazusa's apology is as insincere as usual; what has changed is that she simply looks down instead of turning away or glaring. The English says her way of apologizing is completely different, recasts the narrator's observation as an accusation, and calls her lowered gaze an honest bow.
findings.japanese:
『すいません』も、いつも同様、
誠意がこもっていないのはまぁ当然としても、
横向いたり睨んだりせず、普通に俯いている。
findings.todokanai: The way she's saying "I'm sorry" is completely different too. Even if it's only natural to accuse her of not doing it in good faith, she's honestly bowing her head, without even looking to the side or scowling.

findings.highlight: I'm not too late to cover up for Touma's outburst.
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬の豹変についていけなかった自分を、今からでも遅くはないって必死に勇気づける。
findings.explanation: Having failed to keep up with Kazusa's sudden transformation and departure, Haruki desperately tells himself that it is not too late to go after her. The English invents a plan to cover up her outburst, changing his immediate motive from following her to concealing misconduct.
findings.japanese:
冬馬の豹変についていけなかった自分を、
今からでも遅くはないって必死に勇気づける。
findings.todokanai: Even though I've failed already, I desperately try to convince myself that I'm not too late to cover up for Touma's outburst.

findings.evidenceJa: っ…っ…っぁ…
findings.explanation: Kazusa is audibly breathing or moaning in distress; that sound is the abnormality Haruki notices after entering the dark house, and the later narration explicitly refers back to her pained breathing. The English replaces the vocalization with silent ellipses and removes the sensory cue that alerts him.
findings.japanese: 「っ…っ…っぁ…」

findings.highlight: It'll be Sunday after three days.
findings.evidenceJa: 三日後は土曜だ。
findings.explanation: Three days later is Saturday, the day of the performance. The English says Sunday, moving the doctor's recovery window past the decisive event and changing the deadline calculation.
findings.japanese:
三日後は土曜だ。
その頃やっと熱が下がったとしても、もう…
findings.todokanai: It'll be Sunday after three days. Even if she does recover by then…

findings.highlight: coming up with excuses and apologies to her for some reason.
findings.evidenceJa: 次から次へと自分を責める思いが湧き上がり、何て言うか、どうやって謝るかしか考えられない。
findings.explanation: Self-reproach wells up one thought after another until Haruki can think only about how to apologize. The English adds excuse-making to a passage defined by his inability to do anything but blame himself, materially changing his response to Kazusa's collapse.
findings.japanese:
そんな不謹慎な考えと同時に、
次から次へと自分を責める思いが湧き上がり、
何て言うか、どうやって謝るかしか考えられない。
findings.todokanai: With those inappropriate thoughts in mind, I find myself feeling guilty, and coming up with excuses and apologies to her for some reason.

findings.highlight: What beats me up the most inside is the notebook that lies beside Touma right now as she's sleeping in the living room.
findings.evidenceJa:
中でも俺を一番打ちのめしたのは、
リビングで倒れてた冬馬の傍らに落ちていたノート。
findings.explanation: The notebook was found beside Kazusa where she had collapsed in the living room, while the English describes it as lying beside her “right now” as she sleeps.
findings.japanese:
中でも俺を一番打ちのめしたのは、
リビングで倒れてた冬馬の傍らに落ちていたノート。
findings.todokanai: What beats me up the most inside is the notebook that lies beside Touma right now as she's sleeping in the living room.

findings.highlight: That's my answer to you asking why.
findings.evidenceJa: だったら何で？　というわけだ。
findings.explanation: After excluding the keyboard, guitar, and old pop songs as sources of the growing buzz, Haruki asks, “Then why? That's the question,” before identifying Setsuna as the secret weapon. The English calls the line an answer to a question Setsuna never asked, reversing its rhetorical function.
findings.japanese:
「だったら何で？　というわけだ。
わかった？　秘密兵器のボーカルさん？」
findings.todokanai: "That's my answer to you asking why. Got it, Miss Secret-weapon-singer?"

findings.highlight: Her breath is still very warm, and occasionally unsteady.
findings.evidenceJa: 相変わらず吐く息は熱そうで、時々ふらついて
findings.explanation: Kazusa's exhaled breath still seems hot, and Kazusa herself sometimes staggers or sways. The English makes her breath occasionally unsteady, transferring a visible sign of bodily weakness onto the wrong subject.
findings.japanese:
相変わらず吐く息は熱そうで、時々ふらついて、
とても回復しているとは思えない状況のままだけど。
findings.todokanai: Her breath is still very warm, and occasionally unsteady. I can't imagine her getting better soon considering that.

findings.highlight: Whatever nostalgic, sophisticated or convenient motive we had, no one has any idea what it was right now.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな、今となっては懐かしい、詭弁もいいところだった動機なんか、もう誰もが忘れてる。
findings.explanation: The old motives are now nostalgic but were blatant sophistries or pretexts, and everyone has forgotten them. The English mistranslates 詭弁 as the positive “sophisticated,” distributes incompatible labels as alternative motives, and turns forgetting them into the defective claim that nobody knows what a single motive was “right now.”
findings.japanese:
そんな、今となっては懐かしい、
詭弁もいいところだった動機なんか、
もう誰もが忘れてる。
findings.todokanai: Whatever nostalgic, sophisticated or convenient motive we had, no one has any idea what it was right now.

findings.highlight: kind of scary… It's become so absurd.
findings.evidenceJa: でも、その迷走こそが楽しくて、嬉しくて、尊くて…こんなにも、無茶をするようになってしまった。
findings.explanation: Their very lack of direction has become fun, joyful, and precious, which is why they have come to push themselves this recklessly. The English replaces “precious” with “scary” and makes the situation itself absurd, reversing the passage's affirmation of their shared, irrational effort.
findings.japanese:
でも、その迷走こそが楽しくて、嬉しくて、尊くて…
こんなにも、無茶をするようになってしまった。
findings.todokanai: But going off track in itself is fun, enjoyable, and kind of scary… It's become so absurd.

findings.highlight: there's no point crying over spilled milk.
findings.evidenceJa: 悔やんでも悔やみきれない。
findings.explanation: Haruki says the mistake is so frustrating that he cannot regret it enough. The English uses an idiom counseling resignation because regret is pointless, reversing the intensity and direction of his reaction.
findings.japanese: まぁ要するに、悔やんでも悔やみきれない。
findings.todokanai: Well, there's no point crying over spilled milk.

findings.highlight: The patient whom I diligently cared for ended up pouring cold water on my moment of self-satisfaction.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の自己満足にきっちり水を差したのは、俺が一時間ごとに水差しで水を与えていた病人だった。
findings.explanation: The line repeats water in two senses: Kazusa pours cold water on Haruki's self-satisfaction, and she is literally the patient he has been giving water from a pitcher every hour. The English keeps only the idiomatic half and replaces the concrete water-pitcher wording with generic diligent care, breaking the engineered repetition.
findings.japanese:
俺の自己満足にきっちり水を差したのは、
俺が一時間ごとに水差しで水を与えていた病人だった。
findings.todokanai: The patient whom I diligently cared for ended up pouring cold water on my moment of self-satisfaction.

findings.highlight: holding her hands up and apologizing so exaggeratedly
findings.evidenceJa: なぜ、反則を誤魔化すヒールレスラーみたいに、わざわざ大げさに両手を挙げて否定するんだろう？
findings.explanation: Kazusa raises both hands in exaggerated denial, like a heel wrestler pretending not to have committed a foul, after claiming she was not holding Haruki's sleeve. The English calls the gesture an apology, changing the physical gag and the purpose of her display.
findings.japanese:
なぜ、反則を誤魔化すヒールレスラーみたいに、
わざわざ大げさに両手を挙げて否定するんだろう？
findings.todokanai: Why is she holding her hands up and apologizing so exaggeratedly as if she were a heel wrestler trying to gloss over the fact that they just played dirty?

findings.highlight: She's been living alone for three years now
findings.evidenceJa: 毎日毎日、三年間ずっと一人だった奴が。
findings.explanation: Haruki dismisses the thought that Kazusa fears being alone because she has been alone every day for all three years, a statement about her sustained isolation. The English narrows this to living by herself at home and removes the broader social history that makes her present dependence difficult for him to recognize.
findings.japanese:
…そんな訳ないよな。
毎日毎日、三年間ずっと一人だった奴が。
findings.todokanai: …No, there's no way. She's been living alone for three years now, after all.

findings.highlight: We're done for if she's only going to get better by the latter two days, though I suppose we were already done for for quite some time…
findings.evidenceJa: 後ろ二つだったらもう致命的というボーダーにはとっくに来てるんだけどな…
findings.explanation: They have already reached the point at which either of the latter two recovery times—the day after tomorrow or next week—would be fatal to the performance plan. The English says they have already been doomed for quite some time, converting a threshold and conditional forecast into a settled past result.
findings.japanese:
後ろ二つだったらもう致命的というボーダーには
とっくに来てるんだけどな…
findings.todokanai: We're done for if she's only going to get better by the latter two days, though I suppose we were already done for for quite some time…

findings.highlight: Haruki's been slacking off for two whole days.
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬が回復したとしても、春希が２日もロスした。
findings.explanation: Takeya says that even if Kazusa recovers, Haruki has lost two days of practice. Haruki spent those days nursing her; “slacking off” invents idleness and moral blame where the source states only lost time.
findings.japanese:
「冬馬が回復したとしても、春希が２日もロスした。
本当に弾けるようになってるのか、あいつ？」
findings.todokanai: "Even if Touma gets better, Haruki's been slacking off for two whole days. Will he really be able to play?"

findings.highlight: There's not all that much to see, either…
findings.evidenceJa: 見せもんじゃねえってのに。…少なくとも今日は
findings.explanation: Takeya protests that Setsuna is not a sideshow or spectacle—at least not today—as boys gather to watch her rehearsal. The English instead says there is not much worth seeing, changing his defense of her into a disparaging evaluation of the attraction.
findings.japanese:
「見せもんじゃねえってのに。
…少なくとも今日は」
findings.todokanai: "There's not all that much to see, either… Not today, anyway."

findings.highlight: while we were doing the laundry.
findings.evidenceJa: 一緒に洗い物をしながら、冬馬家の色々な事情を事細かに話してくれた。
findings.explanation: Shibata tells Haruki the Touma household's circumstances while the two wash dishes together. The English changes the domestic action to doing laundry, giving the conversation a different physical setting and degree of intrusion into Kazusa's personal effects.
findings.japanese:
やっぱり『近所の話し好きなおばさん』の中身通り、
一緒に洗い物をしながら、冬馬家の色々な事情を
事細かに話してくれた。
findings.todokanai: Being the chatty neighborhood lady that she is, she explained the Touma family's circumstances to me while we were doing the laundry.

findings.highlight: Stories like these with discord in mutual feelings usually happen due to someone's misunderstanding.
findings.evidenceJa:
こういう、お互いの思いがすれ違う話ってのは、
大抵、双方の言ってる意味が、
結構大きく食い違ってたりする。
findings.explanation: The source says that in stories of crossed feelings, what the two sides mean by their words often differs greatly; “someone's misunderstanding” collapses that mutual semantic mismatch into a generic one-sided error.
findings.japanese:
こういう、お互いの思いがすれ違う話ってのは、
大抵、双方の言ってる意味が、
結構大きく食い違ってたりする。
findings.todokanai: Stories like these with discord in mutual feelings usually happen due to someone's misunderstanding.

findings.highlight: couldn't stand feeling so helpless.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ…どうしようもなく気に入らなかったんだ。それだけだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa does not claim that she felt helpless; she says that, regardless of whether she was unhappy or her mother was objectively wrong, she simply could not stand it. The English misreads どうしようもなく as the content of her feeling and invents helplessness, weakening her deliberately nonjudicial statement of visceral rejection.
findings.japanese:
「ただ…どうしようもなく気に入らなかったんだ。
それだけだ」
findings.todokanai: "I just… couldn't stand feeling so helpless. That's all."

findings.highlight: you play beautifully
findings.evidenceJa: ピアノが上手くて綺麗な事以外は、普っ通～の人間だな
findings.explanation: Haruki says that aside from being good at piano and beautiful, Kazusa is an utterly ordinary person. The English makes both attributes describe her piano playing and deletes the direct acknowledgment of her beauty, which is precisely the embarrassing affirmation he disguises inside a backhanded insult.
findings.japanese:
「ピアノが上手くて綺麗な事以外は、
普っ通～の人間だな」
findings.todokanai: "You are a terrific pianist and you play beautifully, but under all that, you're just an ordinary person!"

findings.highlight: "Then that just makes you a proper scumbag, doesn't it? You've been troubling someone as miserable as I am, after all."
findings.evidenceJa:
「じゃあ、北原は筋金入りのクズだね。
そんなあたしにここまで迷惑かけるんだから」
findings.explanation: “Someone as miserable as I am” invents self-description; そんなあたし refers back to Kazusa as the troublesome person Haruki has just criticized.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ、北原は筋金入りのクズだね。
そんなあたしにここまで迷惑かけるんだから」
findings.todokanai: "Then that just makes you a proper scumbag, doesn't it? You've been troubling someone as miserable as I am, after all."

findings.highlight: Everybody thinks that such problems bother only them, and sometimes they see them as life-or-death situations. But if they could look at their problems objectively, they'd realize it's no big deal.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな、誰もが持ってる『自分だけの事情』って、本人的には生きるか死ぬかの問題だと思ってても、端から見ると、実は大したことなかったりして。
findings.explanation: Haruki says everyone has personal circumstances of their own; to the person involved they may feel like life or death, while to an outsider they may sometimes look less momentous. The English invents the claim that people think their problems bother only themselves and changes the outside observer into the sufferer achieving objectivity, altering the perspective of his generalization.
findings.japanese:
そんな、誰もが持ってる『自分だけの事情』って、
本人的には生きるか死ぬかの問題だと思ってても、
端から見ると、実は大したことなかったりして。
findings.todokanai: Everybody thinks that such problems bother only them, and sometimes they see them as life-or-death situations. But if they could look at their problems objectively, they'd realize it's no big deal.

findings.highlight: They won't pay for our performance.
findings.evidenceJa: お金も出してない。
findings.explanation: The festival audience has paid no admission money and therefore owes the band neither attention nor patience. The English says the audience will not pay the performers, assigning the money to the wrong transaction and obscuring Haruki's argument about winning over casual nonpaying spectators.
findings.japanese:
お金も出してない。暇じゃないかもしれない。
ましてや音楽なんか好きでも何でもなく、
ただ人数合わせで動員かけられてるだけかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: They won't pay for our performance. They might come for something else. Worst case scenario, they might come just because they're told to fill the hall, and might have no interest in music in the first place.

findings.highlight: Or an amateurish band's honest performance?
findings.evidenceJa: それとも、コミックバンドのパフォーマンス？
findings.explanation: Haruki contrasts authentic sound with the performance of a comic or novelty band as two ways to make indifferent festivalgoers turn their heads. The English replaces the deliberate comic-band strategy with an amateurish but honest performance, changing both the genre and the opposition he is proposing.
findings.japanese:
そんな奴らを振り向かせられるのは本物の音？
それとも、コミックバンドのパフォーマンス？
findings.todokanai: What can attract such people? The real deal? Or an amateurish band's honest performance?

findings.highlight: Why aren't they answering my calls…?
findings.evidenceJa: どうして来ないのかな。電話、してくれないのかな。
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks why they have not come and why they will not call her. The English makes her complain that they are not answering calls she placed, reversing who is expected to initiate contact and weakening the vulnerable expectation that Haruki will reach out.
findings.japanese:
「…どうして来ないのかな。
電話、してくれないのかな。
もう、本番は明日なのに」
findings.todokanai: "Why aren't they coming…? Why aren't they answering my calls…? Our performance is tomorrow…"

findings.highlight: you are a retro maid today.
findings.evidenceJa: 今日の雪菜はレトロな女給さんなの。
findings.explanation: Setsuna is dressed as a retro 女給, the waitress role at the center of the class's Taisho-romance cafe conceit. Calling her a maid substitutes a different service role and modern pop-cultural costume, erasing the period register that structures the subsequent waitress performance.
findings.japanese:
「ダメ！　時間切れ！
今日の雪菜はレトロな女給さんなの。
これも引き受けたからにはしっかりやらないと！」
findings.todokanai: "Nope! Time's up! Setsuna, you are a retro maid today. You agreed to do this as well, so do your best!"

findings.highlight: since last week.
findings.evidenceJa: 道理で今週から始まった雪菜の『定時連絡』がなかった訳だ。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's scheduled check-ins began this week, not last week. The English lengthens an explicitly new routine and changes the timeline of their newly established closeness.
findings.japanese:
道理で今週から始まった
雪菜の『定時連絡』がなかった訳だ。
findings.todokanai: So that's why I didn't get any periodic updates from Setsuna, the ones she'd started giving me since last week.

findings.highlight: Haruki's here…
findings.evidenceJa: 実行委員だ…
findings.explanation: Io identifies Haruki with the executive committee role as he disperses the line; the joke is that classmates treat this one former committee member as the institution itself, then inflate him into the committee chairman. The English supplies only his name and removes the public-role identification that sets up the following misunderstanding.
findings.japanese: 「実行委員だ…」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki's here…"

findings.highlight: I won't have any trouble with you two by my side!
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対に、みんなの足だけは引っ張らないように…
findings.explanation: Setsuna vows to work hard so that she will absolutely not hold the others back. The English instead says that the other two being beside her will prevent her from having trouble, reversing responsibility and deleting the anxious determination that prompts Haruki to intervene.
findings.japanese:
「わたしも頑張る…頑張るから！
絶対に、みんなの足だけは引っ張らないように…」
findings.todokanai: "I will do my best, definitely! I won't have any trouble with you two by my side!"

findings.highlight: "…Your instructions are so specific. I wonder when you'll find the time to apologize."
findings.evidenceJa: 「…本当に謝る気があるのか疑わしい具体的な指示だね」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki's concrete practice instructions make her doubt whether he sincerely intends to apologize; the English turns that into wondering when he will find time to apologize.
findings.japanese: 「…本当に謝る気があるのか疑わしい具体的な指示だね」
findings.todokanai: "…Your instructions are so specific. I wonder when you'll find the time to apologize."

findings.highlight: feel free to hide with my profile.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなに恥ずかしいんだったら、もっと俺の陰に隠れてくれていいから
findings.explanation: Haruki tells Setsuna that, if she is so embarrassed, she can hide farther behind him or in his shadow. “Hide with my profile” is defective English and obscures the physical invitation that she immediately answers by clutching his chest and clinging to him.
findings.japanese:
「そんなに恥ずかしいんだったら、
もっと俺の陰に隠れてくれていいから」
findings.todokanai: "If it's that embarrassing for you, feel free to hide with my profile."

findings.highlight: Being stuck in such a tight space
findings.evidenceJa: その、少し余裕のある空間は、車内の人々の奇異の視線を、あからさまに意識させてくれる。
findings.explanation: The carriage has a little spare room, which makes the other passengers' strange looks conspicuous rather than masking them in a crowd. The English calls the space tight, reversing the physical fact that explains why every gaze is so easy to feel.
findings.japanese:
その、少し余裕のある空間は、
車内の人々の奇異の視線を、
あからさまに意識させてくれる。
findings.todokanai: Being stuck in such a tight space, I can't help but feel conscious of all the looks the other people in the train are giving us.

findings.highlight: I'll have even more trouble looking her in the eyes…
findings.evidenceJa: とにかくこれで、今まで以上に雪菜に頭が上がらなくなってしまった。
findings.explanation: 頭が上がらない means Haruki is even more indebted to, outmatched by, or unable to take a superior position toward Setsuna after her recovery. The English reads the image literally as difficulty making eye contact and changes the relationship judgment into embarrassment.
findings.japanese:
とにかくこれで、
今まで以上に雪菜に頭が上がらなくなってしまった。
findings.todokanai: After this, I'm sure that I'll have even more trouble looking her in the eyes…

findings.highlight: The modern-era Touma doesn't seem to be familiar with Taisho-era waitresses.
findings.evidenceJa:
大正時代の女給さんとのスキンシップに、
現代っ子である冬馬は慣れていないようだった。
findings.explanation: The joke is that modern Kazusa is unused to physical affection from a Taisho-era waitress; the English merely says she is unfamiliar with Taisho-era waitresses and omits the skinship.
findings.japanese:
大正時代の女給さんとのスキンシップに、
現代っ子である冬馬は慣れていないようだった。
findings.todokanai: The modern-era Touma doesn't seem to be familiar with Taisho-era waitresses.

findings.highlight: "Touma composed thisーour third song. I didn't think we'd make it, in all honesty, and I already gave up halfway…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「冬馬が作ってたんだ。３曲目。
時間的に無理かなって思って、
半分諦めてたんたけど…」
findings.explanation: “I already gave up halfway” changes 半分諦めてた, being half resigned to failure, into giving up at a temporal halfway point.
findings.japanese:
「冬馬が作ってたんだ。３曲目。
時間的に無理かなって思って、
半分諦めてたんたけど…」
findings.todokanai: "Touma composed thisーour third song. I didn't think we'd make it, in all honesty, and I already gave up halfway…"

findings.highlight: "I couldn't care less about this song, but you know, Kitahara insisted on playing it no matter what…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「あたしは別にどっちでも良かったんだけど、
北原がどうしても演りたいって…」
findings.explanation: “I couldn't care less about this song” is harsher than どっちでも良かった, Kazusa's claim that she was fine whether they performed it or not.
findings.japanese:
「あたしは別にどっちでも良かったんだけど、
北原がどうしても演りたいって…」
findings.todokanai: "I couldn't care less about this song, but you know, Kitahara insisted on playing it no matter what…"

findings.highlight: Kitahara's going out in his uniform
findings.evidenceJa: だって北原は私服なんだろ？
findings.explanation: Kazusa protests that Haruki gets to perform in ordinary clothes while she has been put in a revealing costume. 私服 is explicitly non-uniform clothing; the English reverses the visual fact and damages the basis of her complaint that the arrangement is unfair.
findings.japanese:
「だって北原は私服なんだろ？
そんなの不公平だ！」
findings.todokanai: "I mean, Kitahara's going out in his uniform, isn't he? It's not fair!"

findings.highlight: Those costumes look so good on you I can hardly resist!
findings.evidenceJa: もう二人とも似合い過ぎててヤバい。どうすりゃいいんだ俺！
findings.explanation: Haruki is overwhelmed and blurts that the outfits suit them so absurdly well that he does not know what to do with himself. “I can hardly resist” invents an object and a sexualized threat of losing control, changing the joke from verbal incoherence to predatory implication.
findings.japanese:
「駄目だこれ…凄ぇ、凄ぇよ…マジスッゲー！
もう二人とも似合い過ぎててヤバい。
どうすりゃいいんだ俺！」
findings.todokanai: "Oh, this is dangerous… Awesome… So awesome… You two look so freakin' awesome! Those costumes look so good on you I can hardly resist!"

findings.highlight: they seem to hate her so much
findings.evidenceJa: 相当嫌ってるらしいからなぁお互い
findings.explanation: Takeya says Kazusa and the music students apparently hate each other. The English makes the hostility one-sided, with the students hating Kazusa, removing her reciprocal antagonism from his explanation of why some have come to watch her fail.
findings.japanese:
「相当嫌ってるらしいからなぁお互い。
笑い者にしたくてしょうがないんじゃないか？」
findings.todokanai: "Then again, they seem to hate her so much. Maybe they're just here hoping to make fun of her?"

findings.highlight: Word has spread even throughout the university
findings.evidenceJa: 大学からもかなり流れてきてたって
findings.explanation: Haruki says that quite a lot of people had flowed over from the neighboring university. The English turns the movement of university students into the spread of information, contradicting the scene's repeated visual accounting of who is entering the high-school grounds.
findings.japanese:
「だからさっきからそう言ってるだろ。
大学からもかなり流れてきてたって」
findings.todokanai: "Just like I said earlier, see? Word has spread even throughout the university."

findings.highlight: I've ever seen her excited even once
findings.evidenceJa: テンション上がってハイになってる冬馬なんてのは、出会って半年の間、お目に掛かったことない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he has never seen Kazusa become visibly amped up or giddy with excitement during the six months he has known her. The English broadens that specific high-energy state into never having seen her excited at all, making her emotional range markedly flatter than the Japanese does.
findings.japanese:
とはいえ、
テンション上がってハイになってる冬馬なんてのは、
出会って半年の間、お目に掛かったことないけどな。
findings.todokanai: That said, it's not like I've ever seen her excited even once in the whole half a year I've known her.
