findings.highlight: Even if she makes a careless slip-up now, I'm sure she won't get nervous over it
findings.evidenceJa: 今の雪菜なら、うっかりミスはあっても、緊張で失敗することはあり得ない
findings.explanation: Haruki believes that Setsuna might make an ordinary careless mistake, but she can no longer fail because of stage fright. The English instead says a mistake will not make her nervous, reversing the direction between anxiety and failure and weakening the point of her recovery from the previous day.
findings.japanese:
今の雪菜なら、うっかりミスはあっても、
緊張で失敗することはあり得ないって信じられる。
そんな、強い瞳を俺たちに見せてくれる。
findings.todokanai: Even if she makes a careless slip-up now, I'm sure she won't get nervous over it. I can see her strong determination shining through her eyes.

findings.highlight: even under the dazzling spotlight of the stage
findings.evidenceJa: そんな強い光を受けても
findings.explanation: The “strong light” Kazusa receives is the strength shining in Setsuna's eyes in the immediately preceding narration. Todokanai TL invents a literal stage spotlight, breaking the exchange of looks in which Setsuna's recovered resolve meets Kazusa's calm, fearless expression.
findings.japanese:
で、そんな強い光を受けても、
冬馬の淡々として、それでいて不敵な面構えは、
やっぱり崩れるはずもなかった。
findings.todokanai: And even under the dazzling spotlight of the stage, Touma's detached yet fearless expression shows no sign of breaking for even a second.

findings.highlight: the president, who broke up the club right before the festival
findings.evidenceJa: 同好会を一度は崩壊させた部長
findings.explanation: Kazusa identifies Takeya as the president who once allowed the club to collapse; the last-minute timing belongs to Haruki's subsequent re-formation of it. The English moves “right before the festival” onto Takeya's earlier breakup, inventing a chronology the sentence deliberately assigns to the other culprit.
findings.japanese:
「こんな準備不足で上手く演れるわけがない。
これは全て、同好会を一度は崩壊させた部長と、
時間がないのにやっつけで再結成した北原の責任だ」
findings.todokanai: "There's no way this will end well with our lack of practice. The responsibility is all on the president, who broke up the club right before the festival, and Kitahara who insisted on reforming the club on such short notice."

findings.highlight: if the three of them are this close right now… it's only going to get worse for them
findings.evidenceJa: あんなにどうしようもなくなっちゃったら、これからが辛いよね、あの三人
findings.explanation: Io does not simply say that increasing closeness will make things worse. She sees the three as already having become hopelessly or helplessly entangled and predicts that what lies ahead will be painful. The English normalizes her diagnosis into ordinary intimacy escalating, weakening the scene's explicit foreboding about an unclassifiable bond.
findings.japanese:
「でもさ…
あんなにどうしようもなくなっちゃったら、
これからが辛いよね、あの三人」
findings.todokanai: "But… if the three of them are this close right now… it's only going to get worse for them from now on."

findings.highlight: she half-heartedly accepted because she wanted even more attention
findings.evidenceJa: 本人も軽い気持ちで目立とうと思って
findings.explanation: The imagined audience thinks Setsuna herself chose, on a lighthearted impulse, to stand out. “Half-heartedly accepted” instead makes her a reluctant recipient of the invitation, while “even more attention” invents a comparative degree of vanity. Both the agency and the supposed motive are changed.
findings.japanese:
ただ、人気があるだけで選ばれて、
本人も軽い気持ちで目立とうと思って、
そんな利害の一致しかないと思ってた人も多いはずだ。
findings.todokanai: Most of them probably thought we chose her because of her popularity, and she half-heartedly accepted because she wanted even more attention.

findings.highlight: That's why she can keep watching over us the entire time
findings.evidenceJa: 力加減を必要としない電子楽器は、彼女には物足りないのか、指先を全然見ずに、常に俺たちへと目配りを忘れない
findings.explanation: Haruki speculates that an electronic keyboard, requiring less control of force than a piano, may be insufficiently demanding for Kazusa; she therefore never needs to look at her fingertips and can continually monitor the others. The English reduces this characterizing excess of skill to a generic property of the instrument that simply enables her attention.
findings.japanese:
ピアノの時みたいに力加減を必要としない
電子楽器は、彼女には物足りないのか、
指先を全然見ずに、常に俺たちへと目配りを忘れない。
findings.todokanai: Unlike a piano, an electronic synthesizer doesn't require delicate adjustment of force to play. That's why she can keep watching over us the entire time.

findings.highlight: And the fact they're quiet means that they're earnestly listening to Setsuna's singing as well.
findings.evidenceJa:
というか、皆が聴き入ってるってことはつまり、
雪菜の歌を、もう完全に『聴けるレベル』だって、
認識したってこと。
findings.explanation: Haruki concludes that the audience has fully recognized Setsuna's singing as worth listening to; the English reports only that they are listening earnestly.
findings.japanese:
というか、皆が聴き入ってるってことはつまり、
雪菜の歌を、もう完全に『聴けるレベル』だって、
認識したってこと。
findings.todokanai: And the fact they're quiet means that they're earnestly listening to Setsuna's singing as well.

findings.highlight: I really am the most unreliable member of this band
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が一番心配されてるんだろうな
findings.explanation: Haruki infers from Kazusa's gaze that he is the member everyone is most worried about. The English converts that relational observation into the narrator objectively declaring himself the most unreliable member, changing who makes the judgment and flattening the comic self-awareness of being watched.
findings.japanese:
…やっぱりこのユニットの中では、
俺が一番心配されてるんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: …I really am the most unreliable member of this band of ours, huh?

findings.highlight: In any case, my mind's drifting off to focus on the solo in our second song, but my intuition is still handling this perfectly in spite of myself.
findings.evidenceJa:
何しろ思いはもう２曲目のソロパートに飛んでいってて、
俺のくせに今は流してる感覚が強かったりする。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is already thinking about the second-song solo and feels he is letting the present part flow on autopilot; the English attributes perfect handling to his intuition.
findings.japanese:
何しろ思いはもう２曲目のソロパートに飛んでいってて、
俺のくせに今は流してる感覚が強かったりする。
findings.todokanai: In any case, my mind's drifting off to focus on the solo in our second song, but my intuition is still handling this perfectly in spite of myself.

findings.highlight: a suggestive wink
findings.evidenceJa: 意味ありげな目配せを送る
findings.explanation: Haruki sends Kazusa a meaningful look to cue their rehearsed stunt. A wink is not stated, and “suggestive” adds an English sexual or conspiratorial coloration beyond the functional exchange of glances that the narration repeatedly describes.
findings.japanese:
ずっと俺の手元を注目してた冬馬に、
意味ありげな目配せを送る。
findings.todokanai: I give a suggestive wink to Touma, who's been looking at my fingers all along.

findings.highlight: composed enough to wink back at me
findings.evidenceJa: 俺と目配せで会話できるほど余裕を持っていた
findings.explanation: Kazusa has enough spare capacity while playing a secondary instrument to conduct an actual exchange with Haruki through eye contact. “Wink back” again invents a single gesture and discards the sustained nonverbal conversation used to demonstrate both her technical ease and their coordination.
findings.japanese:
専門じゃないサックスを吹く間でも、
俺と目配せで会話できるほど余裕を持っていた。
findings.todokanai: Despite playing the saxophone, which is not her specialty, she's still composed enough to wink back at me.

findings.highlight: I guess, yeah.
findings.evidenceJa: なんだかなぁ
findings.explanation: Kazusa's なんだかなぁ expresses dubious exasperation—roughly, she still does not know what to make of this ridiculous success. “I guess, yeah” turns it into mild agreement with Haruki's triumph, reversing the cool resistance maintained throughout their glance exchange.
findings.japanese: 『なんだかなぁ』
findings.todokanai: "I guess, yeah."

findings.highlight: "Don't talk to me right now. I'm basking in the afterglow."
findings.evidenceJa:
「話しかけるな。
余韻に浸れない」
findings.explanation: Chiaki says talking to her prevents her from soaking in the afterglow; the English states simply that she is basking in it.
findings.japanese:
「話しかけるな。
余韻に浸れない」
findings.todokanai: "Don't talk to me right now. I'm basking in the afterglow."

findings.highlight: everyone would have been quiet after our performance
findings.evidenceJa: 外したら、あとずっと静まっちゃいそうで
findings.explanation: Setsuna feared that if their old opening number failed to land, the audience would remain subdued for everything that followed. The English moves the silence to after the entire performance, removing the risk attached to opening their set with this particular song.
findings.japanese:
「本当は、最初にこの曲を持ってくるのって、
結構勇気がいったんですよ。古い曲だし…
外したら、あとずっと静まっちゃいそうで」
findings.todokanai: "To tell you the truth, when we first thought of using this song, it took a lot of courage to decide on it because it's a pretty old song… If we'd messed up, everyone would have been quiet after our performance."

findings.highlight: "Standing here and singing in front of everyone… I've never been this nervous in my entire life."
findings.evidenceJa:
「こういうところに立って歌うの、
ホント生まれて初めてなので凄く緊張してました」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says this is her first time singing in a place like this and that she was very nervous; the English replaces the first-time fact with a lifetime superlative about nervousness.
findings.japanese:
「こういうところに立って歌うの、
ホント生まれて初めてなので凄く緊張してました」
findings.todokanai: "Standing here and singing in front of everyone… I've never been this nervous in my entire life."

findings.highlight: more than good enough for this
findings.evidenceJa: 余裕あるじゃん、雪菜
findings.explanation: Haruki observes that Setsuna has composure to spare: she is relaxed enough onstage to improvise this speech. The English instead praises her general ability, losing the immediate evidence that her stage fright has vanished.
findings.japanese: 余裕あるじゃん、雪菜…
findings.todokanai: You're actually more than good enough for this, Setsuna…

findings.highlight: was the head of the festival committee
findings.evidenceJa: 学園祭実行委員とか、クラス委員とか色々なお仕事を兼任してるので
findings.explanation: Setsuna lists festival-committee work, class-representative work, and Haruki's other concurrent jobs. The Japanese never calls him head of the festival committee; the English invents a leadership post and shifts the ongoing accumulation of duties into the past.
findings.japanese:
「北原くんは、学園祭実行委員とか、
クラス委員とか色々なお仕事を兼任してるので、
お世話になった方も多いと思います」
findings.todokanai: "In the past, Kitahara-kun was the head of the festival committee and he was also a class representative. He's been involved with a lot of things at school, so I'm sure he's had many opportunities to help you all out with all sorts of things."

findings.highlight: supporting us through his two-faced nature
findings.evidenceJa: 陰ひなたから支えてくれる
findings.explanation: 陰ひなたなく/陰ひなたから支える means supporting someone both publicly and behind the scenes. Todokanai TL reads the light-and-shadow idiom as duplicity, making Setsuna call dependable Haruki two-faced in the middle of praising him.
findings.japanese:
「普段と同様、いつもわたしたちメンバーを、
陰ひなたから支えてくれる、
とても頼りがいのある人です」
findings.todokanai: "And just as he's done for many of you, he was the one driving us on and supporting us through his two-faced nature. He's someone that we could always depend on."

findings.highlight: When she joined our group, we were amazed by just how skilled she was
findings.evidenceJa: わたしたちのユニットに参加してくれたのが不思議なくらい実力がずば抜けてて
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Kazusa is so far beyond them that it is almost strange she agreed to join their band at all. The English merely says her skill amazed them after she joined, deleting the affectionate self-deprecation about how absurdly overqualified she is.
findings.japanese:
「わたしたちのユニットに参加してくれたのが
不思議なくらい実力がずば抜けてて、
何度助けられたか、もう数えきれません」
findings.todokanai: "When she joined our group, we were amazed by just how skilled she was. I can't even tell you how many times she's helped us already!"

findings.highlight: I was told to delete the bass programming and do the keyboard instead
findings.evidenceJa: ベース外してキーボード入れろって
findings.explanation: Takeya is reporting Haruki's audacious arrangement instruction: take the bass out of Sound of Destiny and put the keyboard in. The English turns it into something Takeya himself was ordered to do to programmed audio, inventing both the performer and the implementation.
findings.japanese:
「で、『ＳＯＵＮＤ　ＯＦ　ＤＥＳＴＩＮＹ』は、
ベース外してキーボード入れろって…」
findings.todokanai: "And for Sound of Destiny, I was told to delete the bass programming and do the keyboard instead…"

findings.highlight: she went along with it so easily
findings.evidenceJa: それでも簡単にやっちゃうところが
findings.explanation: Io's complaint is that Kazusa can execute the technically absurd arrangement with ease. “Went along with it” makes the feat one of willing compliance instead of effortless musical ability, breaking the punch line to their exchange about her detestable genius.
findings.japanese:
「それでも簡単にやっちゃうところが、
思いっきり嫌味なんだけどなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "But the fact that she went along with it so easily is what makes it so detestable."

findings.highlight: couldn't care less what anyone thinks of her
findings.evidenceJa: 自らが好むと好まざるとに関わらず
findings.explanation: Kazusa draws the room's eyes whether she likes it or not. Todokanai TL changes involuntary visibility into an assertion that she does not care what anyone thinks, replacing the scene's external dynamic with a much harder claim about her attitude.
findings.japanese:
ステージの上の黒いピエロは、
自らが好むと好まざるとに関わらず、
会場の目を次々と自分に向けさせていた。
findings.todokanai: The audience's full attention is now on the clown dressed in black on top of the stage, who couldn't care less what anyone thinks of her.

findings.highlight: she just thinks it'd be cuter if I made a fool of myself
findings.evidenceJa: 馬鹿な弟子ほど可愛いの法則なのか
findings.explanation: Haruki jokingly invokes a proverb-like rule that the more foolish the pupil, the dearer the pupil becomes. The English instead says Kazusa wants him to make a fool of himself, changing her indulgent attachment to her hopeless student into a desire to see him embarrassed.
findings.japanese:
…のに、全然効きやしない。
俺の師匠は、本当に弟子のことを信用してないのか、
それとも、馬鹿な弟子ほど可愛いの法則なのか。
findings.todokanai: But it's not really reassuring. Looks like my master really can't trust her disciple, or she just thinks it'd be cuter if I made a fool of myself.

findings.highlight: our performance is pretty shallow
findings.evidenceJa: まともに評価なんかできるわけない俺たちのステージ
findings.explanation: Haruki says their stage cannot be evaluated fairly because the understaffed band is using a backing track and repeatedly deploying crowd-pleasing cheat moves. Todokanai TL converts that refusal of fair comparison into Haruki judging the performance itself shallow.
findings.japanese:
人が足りないから、オケも使ってる。
受けを狙って、反則技を何度も繰り出してる。
まともに評価なんかできるわけない俺たちのステージ。
findings.todokanai: Since we're short on people, we're using pre-recorded segmentsーa rather underhanded method. As a whole, our performance is pretty shallow.

findings.highlight: there were a few hiccups in the singing
findings.evidenceJa: 適当だったり声詰まらせたりして
findings.explanation: The preceding line identifies both Kazusa's bass and Setsuna's vocals. Haruki then says Kazusa was playing roughly and Setsuna's voice was catching; Todokanai TL retains only the vocal hiccups, omitting Kazusa's part of the deliberately paired underperformance.
findings.japanese:
二人とも、視線が泳いでたり、
適当だったり声詰まらせたりして、
じっくり聴いてみれば結構酷いものになってるはずだ。
findings.todokanai: With the way both of their gazes were wandering, and how there were a few hiccups in the singing, it would probably sound pretty bad to anyone listening closely.

findings.highlight: That cold expression
findings.evidenceJa: その凛とした表情
findings.explanation: 凛とした describes Kazusa's dignified, resolute bearing as she wordlessly tells Haruki to trust Setsuna. Calling it cold changes supportive confidence into emotional distance at the point where the three musicians coordinate without speech.
findings.japanese: その凛とした表情が俺に言葉以外で告げてくる。
findings.todokanai: That cold expression tells me everything I need to know.

findings.highlight: we gave the audience one last awkward bow and left the stage
findings.evidenceJa: ぎこちない挨拶で別れた
findings.explanation: Thirty minutes earlier, the three band members awkwardly said goodbye to one another, concealing their embarrassment after clearing out. Todokanai TL invents a final bow to the audience and repeats their departure from the stage, erasing the private post-performance parting.
findings.japanese:
なんだか照れくささを隠すように、
ぎこちない挨拶で別れたのが３０分前。
findings.todokanai: As if hiding our embarrassment, we gave the audience one last awkward bow and left the stage. All that, just some half an hour ago.

findings.highlight: say, "Welcome" just for them
findings.evidenceJa: 『お帰りなさいませ』とか言ってくれる
findings.explanation: お帰りなさいませ is the marked maid-cafe welcome-home formula, which is why the dazzling singer immediately serving classmates has such charge. The generic “Welcome” removes the roleplay register and the cultural joke rather than translating it.
findings.japanese:
さっきまでステージの上で輝いていた雪菜のままで、
目の前で『お帰りなさいませ』とか言ってくれる訳で。
findings.todokanai: I'd bet everyone would want to hear her say, "Welcome" just for them, right after her dazzling performance on the stage.

findings.highlight: if my brain were working properly
findings.evidenceJa: 脳に知れたら絶対に放送禁止だ
findings.explanation: Haruki personifies his brain as a censor: if it found out he was saying something this painfully earnest, it would ban the line from broadcast. Todokanai TL replaces that joke with the ordinary claim that he would not speak this way while thinking clearly.
findings.japanese:
だって、こんな痛い台詞、
脳に知れたら絶対に放送禁止だ。
findings.todokanai: Because I know full well I'd never say something as embarrassing as this if my brain were working properly.

findings.highlight: I'm just a 'person,'
findings.evidenceJa: あいつは“花”で、あたしは“奴”か
findings.explanation: Kazusa explicitly contrasts Haruki's elevated metaphor for Setsuna, “flower,” with the rough 奴 he used for Kazusa. “Person” is neutral English and erases the entire lexical contrast she has noticed between how he casts the two women.
findings.japanese: 『あいつは“花”で、あたしは“奴”か…』
findings.todokanai: "So she's a 'flower,' and I'm just a 'person,' huh…?"

findings.highlight: There's no way I wasn't happy
findings.evidenceJa: 嬉しくないわけないだろ
findings.explanation: Kazusa insists there is no way she is not happy to be with Haruki and Setsuna. The English abruptly puts the final and most vulnerable admission in the past, making it possible to read her happiness as something already over rather than an ongoing feeling she is struggling to voice.
findings.japanese:
『………嫌なわけないだろ。
楽しくないわけないだろ。
嬉しくないわけないだろ』
findings.todokanai: "…There's no way I wouldn't like it. There's no way it wouldn't be fun. There's no way I wasn't happy."

findings.highlight: I can't believe it
findings.evidenceJa: そんなのってないよ
findings.explanation: Watching Kazusa kiss the sleeping Haruki, Setsuna protests that this is not fair or that Kazusa cannot do such a thing. “I can't believe it” reduces her first response to surprise, removing the accusation and sense of violated relationship rules in the scene's final line.
findings.japanese: 「そんなのってないよ…冬馬さん」
findings.todokanai: "I can't believe it… Touma-san…"

findings.highlight: some boundaries I crossed in our conversation that I shouldn't have
findings.evidenceJa: もっと踏み込んだ話題があったはずだけど
findings.explanation: Half-awake, Haruki senses that there had been a deeper, more intimate subject in his conversation with Kazusa. Todokanai TL invents both a boundary violation and his judgment that he should not have crossed it, moralizing a simple failure to recall what they discussed.
findings.japanese:
もっと踏み込んだ話題があったはずだけど、
起き抜けの思考が追いついていかない。
findings.todokanai: I feel like there were some boundaries I crossed in our conversation that I shouldn't have, but having just woken up, I can't remember what it was for the life of me.

findings.highlight: Not having to ask the reason why, I gently put the coat over her shoulders.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺はなんとか理由を聞くことなく、
その肩に、ゆっくりコートをかけていく。
findings.explanation: Haruki somehow manages not to ask why Setsuna has turned her unguarded back to him; “not having to ask” removes his active restraint.
findings.japanese:
俺はなんとか理由を聞くことなく、
その肩に、ゆっくりコートをかけていく。
findings.todokanai: Not having to ask the reason why, I gently put the coat over her shoulders.

findings.highlight: nothing can really stop you
findings.evidenceJa: 一線を越えちゃったら二度とやめられなくなりそう
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that once she crosses the line into performing, she feels as though she may never be able to quit. The English turns her potentially addictive exhilaration into the external claim that nothing can stop her.
findings.japanese:
「人前で歌うのって、ものすごく緊張するけど、
一線を越えちゃったら二度とやめられなくなりそう」
findings.todokanai: "The thought of having to sing in front of other people is really scary, but once you cross that line, nothing can really stop you."

findings.highlight: I didn't even wave to them!
findings.evidenceJa: 振りつけとか全然やらなかったね
findings.explanation: Setsuna realizes they did no choreography or dance movements at all. The English substitutes a single missed wave to the audience, changing a reflection on their whole stage presentation into a trivial greeting gesture.
findings.japanese: 「…そういえば振りつけとか全然やらなかったね」
findings.todokanai: "…Come to think of it, I didn't even wave to them!"

findings.highlight: I can see Touma just refusing the idea flat out
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬にはけんもほろろに断られたけどな
findings.explanation: Haruki notes that Kazusa has already rejected his suggestion out of hand. Todokanai TL turns the completed exchange into his prediction of how she would respond, obscuring that he has already asked her about performing again.
findings.japanese: 冬馬にはけんもほろろに断られたけどな…
findings.todokanai: I can see Touma just refusing the idea flat out, though…

findings.highlight: public policy
findings.evidenceJa: 今のところ政経のつもりだけど
findings.explanation: Haruki says he currently intends to enter political science and economics, the 政経 course or faculty. “Public policy” is a different academic field and breaks the department comparison Setsuna immediately begins.
findings.japanese: 「え？　いや、今のところ政経のつもりだけど…」
findings.todokanai: "Eh? No, right now I'm thinking along the lines of public policy…"

findings.highlight: You won't take English?
findings.evidenceJa: 英文行かない？
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether Haruki will join the English Literature department, so they can align their university paths. “Take English” sounds like choosing a class and does not name the degree program under discussion.
findings.japanese: 「むぅ…英文行かない？」
findings.todokanai: "Hmm… You won't take English?"

findings.highlight: I know that for a fact
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対的に
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is bad at English only relatively; Setsuna replies that she is bad at politics and economics absolutely. “I know that for a fact” removes the explicit relative/absolute pair on which their teasing exchange is built.
findings.japanese: 「わたしだって政治も経済も苦手だよ。絶対的に」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I'm bad at politics and economics too. I know that for a fact."

findings.highlight: I just couldn't get over my crush
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の心を掴みきれてなかったわたしが悪い
findings.explanation: Setsuna blames herself for failing to grasp her own heart completely and therefore failing to anticipate that she would approach Haruki instead of remaining passive. Todokanai TL says she could not get over a crush she already understood, reversing the line's crucial distinction between self-discovery and failed suppression.
findings.japanese:
「仕方がないか…
自分の心を掴みきれてなかった
わたしが悪いんだもんね」
findings.todokanai: "But I guess I can't help myself… I just couldn't get over my crush, so it's all my own fault, right?"

findings.highlight: has no real reason to resist
findings.evidenceJa: 抵抗なんかするわけがなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki narrates that there was no possibility Setsuna would resist the kiss she had invited. The English instead invents his rationale that she has no reason to resist, changing observed certainty about her response into his judgment about what she is entitled or expected to do.
findings.japanese: 雪菜は…抵抗なんかするわけがなかった。
findings.todokanai: And Setsuna… has no real reason to resist.

findings.highlight: And then, I force myself onto Setsuna once more
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の方が雪菜に押しつけていた
findings.explanation: After Setsuna finally pulls her lips away when Haruki's arms loosen, he realizes retrospectively that he had been the one pressing the kiss onto her. Todokanai TL invents a new second advance after the separation—“once more”—materially changing the physical sequence and sexual agency.
findings.japanese: …俺の方が雪菜に押しつけていた。
findings.todokanai: …And then, I force myself onto Setsuna once more.

findings.highlight: While I, on the other hand… I feel as if I could die in peace over the unimaginably pleasant sensation.
findings.evidenceJa:
そして俺の方は…
あまりにも想像を絶する快感に、
果ててしまいそうになっていた。
findings.explanation: 果ててしまいそう carries a sexual and bodily sense of reaching an endpoint or climax; “die in peace” turns it into a comic death idiom.
findings.japanese:
そして俺の方は…
あまりにも想像を絶する快感に、
果ててしまいそうになっていた。
findings.todokanai: While I, on the other hand… I feel as if I could die in peace over the unimaginably pleasant sensation.

findings.highlight: I guess she's hoping that I've stayed the same as I've always been
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女が望む限りは、いつも通りの俺でいようって
findings.explanation: Haruki resolves that, for as long as Kazusa wants it, he will remain his usual self even after the special day. The English makes Kazusa the person hoping that Haruki has remained unchanged, deleting his deliberate decision and reversing whose mental act the narration reports.
findings.japanese:
彼女が望む限りは、いつも通りの俺でいようって。
特別な日をまたいでも、変わらない俺でいようって。
findings.todokanai: I guess she's hoping that I've stayed the same as I've always been. That I haven't changed even after that special day…

findings.highlight: she's finally opened the proverbial Heavenly Rock Cave
findings.evidenceJa: 天の岩戸が、今やっと開いてくれた
findings.explanation: The Amaterasu image is of the Heavenly Rock Door or barrier finally opening, with the opening itself as the grammatical subject. The English has Kazusa actively open a cave, muddying both the movement and the culturally recognizable image; the corresponding Coda reuse later loses it altogether.
findings.japanese:
その思いが通じたのかわからないけど…
とにかく、天の岩戸が、今やっと開いてくれた。
findings.todokanai: I have no idea how she interpreted my reply, but for now, I'm just glad she's finally opened the proverbial Heavenly Rock Cave.

findings.highlight: Rather, nothing will change if I hear her opinion. I can't let my current feelings be swayed by anything other than my own will right now.
findings.evidenceJa:
というより、聞いてどうにかなるようじゃ駄目だから。
今の俺の思いを、自分の意志以外で曲げてしまっては
絶対に駄目だから。
findings.explanation: Haruki's resolve that it would be unacceptable for what he is about to hear to change anything becomes the factual prediction that nothing will change.
findings.japanese:
というより、聞いてどうにかなるようじゃ駄目だから。
今の俺の思いを、自分の意志以外で曲げてしまっては
絶対に駄目だから。
findings.todokanai: Rather, nothing will change if I hear her opinion. I can't let my current feelings be swayed by anything other than my own will right now.

findings.highlight: I perfected my poker-face a long time ago, so there's no need to worry
findings.evidenceJa: 昔からそう見えないのは認めるけど
findings.explanation: Haruki only admits that he has never looked nervous, despite actually being nervous. The English invents a deliberately perfected poker face and an assurance that there is no need to worry, turning an observation about appearances into trained concealment.
findings.japanese: …ま、昔からそう見えないのは認めるけど。
findings.todokanai: …Well, I perfected my poker-face a long time ago, so there's no need to worry.

findings.highlight: With a majority of over 60%
findings.evidenceJa: ６割近くの４０２票
findings.explanation: The source says 402 of 683 votes was nearly sixty percent. It is approximately 58.9 percent, so 'over 60%' reverses the explicit threshold.
findings.japanese:
全有効投票数、６８３票のうち、
実に６割近くの４０２票を獲得しての、
あまりにも箔をつけ過ぎな堂々の三連覇。
findings.todokanai: Out of all the valid votes, 683 in total, 402 went to her. With a majority of over 60%, Setsuna won spectacularly for the third time in a row, uncontested.

findings.highlight: I said I don't care about it at all. You can celebrate it yourself
findings.evidenceJa: だからあたしを祝ったってしょうがないだろ。自分で勝手に祝杯でも上げてろ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says there is no point congratulating her and tells Haruki to raise his own celebratory toast instead. The English repeats a declaration of indifference, deleting the self-effacing redirection of the celebration and making her more dismissive.
findings.japanese:
「だからあたしを祝ったってしょうがないだろ。
自分で勝手に祝杯でも上げてろ…」
findings.todokanai: "I said I don't care about it at all. You can celebrate it yourself…"

findings.highlight: Touma came into my view before I knew it
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬は、いつの間にか視界に納めてた
findings.explanation: The object carried over from the preceding line is Haruki's nod: Kazusa had brought it into her field of vision and was watching him. The English reverses the perceiver and says Kazusa entered Haruki's view.
findings.japanese: 冬馬は、いつの間にか視界に納めてた。
findings.todokanai: Touma came into my view before I knew it.

findings.highlight: But I've finally said it.
findings.evidenceJa: でも、とうとう来てしまったって気持ちばかりだ。
findings.explanation: Haruki feels that the long-awaited moment has finally arrived; the English says only that Kazusa finally said it.
findings.japanese: でも、とうとう来てしまったって気持ちばかりだ。
findings.todokanai: But I've finally said it.

findings.highlight: Your two friends would be leaving you out, spending more time with each other
findings.evidenceJa: 二人の友達を、片方だけひいきしたみたいで
findings.explanation: Haruki worries that inviting Setsuna alone would make it look as though he were favoring one of his two friends. The English instead makes the two friends exclude Kazusa by spending time with each other, reversing who performs the socially questionable action.
findings.japanese: 「…二人の友達を、片方だけひいきしたみたいで」
findings.todokanai: "…Your two friends would be leaving you out, spending more time with each other…"

findings.highlight: All that means nothing to me
findings.evidenceJa: そんなの、なにもない
findings.explanation: Kazusa answers Haruki's proposed reason for separating their friendships by saying there is no such reason, then reminds him she has said so before. 'All that means nothing to me' turns her acceptance of continued association into emotional dismissal.
findings.japanese:
「そんなの、なにもない。
だって、前にも言っただろ？」
findings.todokanai: "All that means nothing to me. I told you before, didn't I?"

findings.highlight: From now on, our bonds will deepen and become stronger, without a doubt.
findings.evidenceJa:
これから絆を深く、
そして強くしていかなくちゃならないんだから。
findings.explanation: Haruki frames strengthening the bond among the three as an obligation; the English predicts that the friendship will naturally grow.
findings.japanese:
これから絆を深く、
そして強くしていかなくちゃならないんだから。
findings.todokanai: From now on, our bonds will deepen and become stronger, without a doubt.

findings.highlight: It's important for a musician to make sure the audience is paying attention to her
findings.evidenceJa: 人に見られることを意識するってのは、演奏家にとって大切なこと
findings.explanation: Youko says it is important for a performer to remain conscious of being watched. The English instead says a musician must make the audience pay attention, reversing the direction of awareness and turning stage consciousness into audience capture.
findings.japanese:
「何よ、いいじゃない。
人に見られることを意識するってのは、
演奏家にとって大切なことでしょう？」
findings.todokanai: "What's the matter? It's fine, isn't it? It's important for a musician to make sure the audience is paying attention to her, you know?"

findings.highlight: the way you tried to show off just how dazzling you were
findings.evidenceJa: いちいちカッコつけたり、艶っぽさを見せつけたり
findings.explanation: Youko accuses Kazusa of posing and deliberately flaunting her sensuality while intensely aware of being watched. 'Dazzling' deletes the explicitly erotic 艶っぽさ and weakens the mother's recognition that Kazusa performed toward Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「人の目をバリバリに意識して、
いちいちカッコつけたり、艶っぽさを見せつけたり」
findings.todokanai: "The way you were mad conscious about how you were being looked at, and the way you tried to show off just how dazzling you were."

findings.highlight: "But if you have both the will and ability, Kazusa, I can raise you to become a pro overseas. It's okay if you don't resign yourself fully, and I don't mind if you'd be doing it to forget about that boy, either."
findings.evidenceJa:
「逆に、かずさにその気と能力があるなら、
向こうであなたをプロに育ててもいい。
大した覚悟がなくても、男を忘れるためでも構わない」
findings.explanation: Youko says Kazusa can keep living even without summoning much resolve, while the English advises her not to resign herself fully.
findings.japanese:
「逆に、かずさにその気と能力があるなら、
向こうであなたをプロに育ててもいい。
大した覚悟がなくても、男を忘れるためでも構わない」
findings.todokanai: "But if you have both the will and ability, Kazusa, I can raise you to become a pro overseas. It's okay if you don't resign yourself fully, and I don't mind if you'd be doing it to forget about that boy, either."

findings.highlight: being deceived by Kitahara's stupidity
findings.evidenceJa: 小木曽が北原の馬鹿に騙されて
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Setsuna was fooled by the idiot Kitahara and carelessly joined the club. The English makes Haruki's abstract stupidity the agent that deceived her, producing a nonsensical relation and removing Kazusa's direct insult.
findings.japanese:
「小木曽が北原の馬鹿に騙されて、
のこのこ同好会に入るから悪いんだぞ」
findings.todokanai: "It's all your fault for being deceived by Kitahara's stupidity and carelessly joining the club, Ogiso."

findings.highlight: so passionate about your own values
findings.evidenceJa: 二人揃って、思い込みの激しさはそっくりだな
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki and Setsuna are alike in how intensely they jump to conclusions or commit to assumptions. The English recasts this shared cognitive flaw as passion about personal values, changing her diagnosis of why they suit each other.
findings.japanese:
「二人揃って、思い込みの激しさはそっくりだな。
…ある意味、お似合いかも」
findings.todokanai: "The two of you are really so passionate about your own values, huh. …In a way, I guess the two of you might really be a good match…"

findings.highlight: a hypocrite who only cares about his own image
findings.evidenceJa: やせ我慢の偽善者
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Haruki a self-denying hypocrite who stubbornly endures and puts on a brave face. The English invents concern for his public image, replacing the compulsive self-restraint that defines his behavior with vanity.
findings.japanese:
「しつこくて、ウザくて、価値観の押しつけばかりで、
強引で、独りよがりで、やせ我慢の偽善者なところとか」
findings.todokanai: "He's persistent, annoying, forces his own values on others, brazen, self-righteous, and a hypocrite who only cares about his own image…"

findings.highlight: You won't be able to have him for yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬さんのものじゃ、なくしちゃったんだよ
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she took Haruki and made him no longer Kazusa's, explicitly framing her act as theft from a prior claim. The English changes this to Kazusa's future inability to have him, weakening Setsuna's confession of guilt and the presupposed emotional ownership.
findings.japanese:
「わたし…春希くん取っちゃったんだよ？
冬馬さんのものじゃ、なくしちゃったんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I've taken Haruki-kun away, you know? You won't be able to have him for yourself, Touma-san, you know?"

findings.highlight: "Then, I'll tell you one last thing as a friend… Kitahara's not a good match for you at all, Ogiso."
findings.evidenceJa:
「じゃあ、もう一度友人として言ってやる。
…小木曽に北原なんて似合わない」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether they can become friends once again; the English says one last time.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ、もう一度友人として言ってやる。
…小木曽に北原なんて似合わない」
findings.todokanai: "Then, I'll tell you one last thing as a friend… Kitahara's not a good match for you at all, Ogiso."

findings.highlight: "I've accepted both of my friends' promises. Anything more would be a pain, so I'll give you my blessing as well."
findings.evidenceJa:
「あたしは、あたしの友達二人の約束を認める。
それと、あとがめんどくさいから祝福してやる」
findings.explanation: One shared commitment or promise involving her two friends is pluralized into both friends' separate promises.
findings.japanese:
「あたしは、あたしの友達二人の約束を認める。
それと、あとがめんどくさいから祝福してやる」
findings.todokanai: "I've accepted both of my friends' promises. Anything more would be a pain, so I'll give you my blessing as well."

findings.highlight: Having to worry about the likes of Kitahara is just irritating too
findings.evidenceJa: 北原ごときに心配されるのもむかつく
findings.explanation: Kazusa is irritated at being worried about by someone like Haruki. The English reverses the concern and says Kazusa has to worry about Haruki, changing who is vulnerable and who is caring.
findings.japanese:
「だから、この話はおしまいだ。
…北原ごときに心配されるのもむかつく。
今まで通り…全部、今まで通りにしてやるよ」
findings.todokanai: "That's why this conversation is finished. Having to worry about the likes of Kitahara is just irritating too. Let's just carry on with everything… carry on like we've always done up until now."

findings.highlight: think back fondly on it in the following four months of our gray lives
findings.evidenceJa: 残る灰色だけの四か月に、思いを馳せざるを得なくなる
findings.explanation: With the festival over, the third-years are forced to turn their thoughts toward the four gray months that remain. The English instead has them spend those months reminiscing fondly about the festival, reversing the temporal direction and replacing dread of the future with nostalgia for the past.
findings.japanese:
学園生活最後の煌めきだった学園祭も終わり、
俺たち三年は、残る灰色だけの四か月に、
思いを馳せざるを得なくなる。
findings.todokanai: The school festival, the final bright event in our school life, has ended. All that we third-years can do now is to think back fondly on it in the following four months of our gray lives.

findings.highlight: the leftover number of students would be in the triple digits
findings.evidenceJa: 残るは三桁を切る
findings.explanation: 三桁を切る means the remaining group falls below three digits—fewer than one hundred. The English says it remains in the triple digits, the opposite side of the stated threshold.
findings.japanese:
その中でも、他の大学に推薦の決まった強者や負け組、
就職を決めた社会人組を除くと、残るは三桁を切る。
findings.todokanai: This includes the ones who decided on other universities, be it because they're overachievers or underachievers, and the ones who have decided to go into employment. Take them away, and the leftover number of students would be in the triple digits.

findings.highlight: I see no reason for society to have to support another leech
findings.evidenceJa: 事情もない社会的弱者を生み出すつもりはないぞ
findings.explanation: Haruki says that, although Kazusa's family could support one NEET, he has no intention of creating a socially vulnerable person with no extenuating circumstances. The English invents society as her supporter and has Haruki call her a leech, making his intervention substantially more contemptuous and moralizing.
findings.japanese:
「確かにお前ん家の財力なら
ニートの一人くらい余裕だろうけど、俺はそんな、
事情もない社会的弱者を生み出すつもりはないぞ」
findings.todokanai: "With how rich your family is, you could probably get by just fine, even as a jobless NEET. Be that as it may, though, I see no reason for society to have to support another leech."

findings.highlight: In this day and age…?
findings.evidenceJa: この年代で
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks whether a hot-spring trip is suitable at their age. The English asks whether it is suitable in the present historical era, changing the object of her surprise.
findings.japanese: 「この年代で…？」
findings.todokanai: "In this day and age…?"

findings.highlight: I don't exactly have any complaints
findings.evidenceJa: 問題がないわけじゃない
findings.explanation: Haruki concedes that the plan is not without problems. The English says he does not really have complaints, reversing the concession from acknowledged difficulties to near-approval.
findings.japanese: そりゃ、確かに問題がないわけじゃないけど…
findings.todokanai: Well, it's true that I don't exactly have any complaints…

findings.highlight: we're a couple that people wouldn't deem acceptable
findings.evidenceJa: 自他共に認める、認められないカップル
findings.explanation: Haruki's deliberate paradox is that they are, by their own and everyone else's admission, an 'unacceptable' or impossible-to-acknowledge couple. The English keeps only outsiders refusing approval and deletes the repeated 認める／認められない architecture and the couple's own recognition.
findings.japanese:
…俺たちは、自他共に認める、
認められないカップルなんだって。
findings.todokanai: I realize that we're a couple that people wouldn't deem acceptable.

findings.highlight: Since my subjects today were the same as hers
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日は、同じ教科だったから
findings.explanation: Haruki says yesterday's exam was in the same subject as Setsuna's, which at least let him study for himself while helping her. The English changes yesterday to today and singular subject to plural subjects.
findings.japanese:
昨日は、同じ教科だったから、
まだこっちも試験勉強できる分マシだった。
findings.todokanai: Since my subjects today were the same as hers, I figured I'd be able to get some studying in for myself as well.

findings.highlight: less than 30 minutes into the exam
findings.evidenceJa: ３０分過ぎた時点で
findings.explanation: Haruki considers the answer-sheet switch once thirty minutes have already passed. The English places the thought before the thirty-minute point, reversing the explicit timing.
findings.japanese:
今日の試験も、もういっそのこと３０分過ぎた時点で
隣の席と答案用紙をすり替えるトリックを使おうかと
本気で悩んだ。
findings.todokanai: Even today, less than 30 minutes into the exam, I was seriously considering sneakily switching answer sheets with the person next to me.

findings.highlight: I'm going on a trip with someone
findings.evidenceJa: 誰と旅行に行く
findings.explanation: Takeya's death-flag joke depends on Setsuna letting slip who she is traveling with—Haruki—so that he would decorate Haruki's desk with memorial flowers. The English quote discloses only that she is traveling with someone, removing the identifying information that would trigger the threat and making the punchline causally incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「…もしも『誰と旅行に行く』かを
彼女が誰かにポロリと漏らしたら、
お前の席に花だけは飾っておいてやるからな」
findings.todokanai: "If she carelessly spreads the news and blurts out, 'I'm going on a trip with someone,' I'll make sure to put some flowers on your desk, at the very least."

findings.highlight: Io's holding back from saying something
findings.evidenceJa: どこかやり切れなさみたいなものが見え隠れしてて
findings.explanation: Io's tone intermittently reveals helpless frustration or an unbearable, unresolved feeling. The English instead says she is withholding an unspoken message, replacing an emotional quality with a conversational intention.
findings.japanese:
そういうことよりも、依緒の口調には、
どこかやり切れなさみたいなものが見え隠れしてて、
なんだか、心がざわつく。
findings.todokanai: That aside, though, I can tell from her tone of voice that Io's holding back from saying something, and that's what really bothers me.

findings.highlight: not to pass this around to anyone
findings.evidenceJa: 誰にでも回してる訳じゃないぞ
findings.explanation: Takeya says he does not circulate the file to just anyone—Chiaki is a selective recipient—and then reminds her of their promise. The English instead orders Chiaki not to pass the file to anyone, reversing the subject and changing a statement of his discretion into a restriction on her behavior.
findings.japanese:
「言っとくけど、誰にでも回してる訳じゃないぞ。
約束、忘れてないだろうな？」
findings.todokanai: "I don't think I need to remind you not to pass this around to anyone, right? And I don't need to remind you about our promise either, do I?"

findings.highlight: I took on a sort of elder-sister role for the club
findings.evidenceJa: 最初は長女役だけのつもりだった
findings.explanation: Chiaki initially intended to play only the eldest-daughter role in the production. The English turns the dramatic role into the informal social role of being an elder sister to the club, obscuring the acting context and why no castmate could match her.
findings.japanese:
「最初は長女役だけのつもりだったんだけどね。
結局、あたしに合わせられるコが一人もいなくて」
findings.todokanai: "At first, I took on a sort of elder-sister role for the club, you know? But eventually, it became obvious that not a single person could match my level."

findings.highlight: in the past, when I was sure I really loved the piano despite who I was
findings.evidenceJa: こんなあたしでも、きっと昔は、ピアノが大好きだったんじゃないかなってことを
findings.explanation: Kazusa wants to remember or recognize that even someone like her must surely have loved the piano once. The English produces a malformed past clause in which she was already certain then, erasing her present, tentative reconstruction of a lost feeling.
findings.japanese:
「ううん…
こんなあたしでも、きっと昔は、
ピアノが大好きだったんじゃないかなってことを」
findings.todokanai: "No… in the past, when I was sure I really loved the piano despite who I was."

findings.highlight: Somehow, I guess it's all working out
findings.evidenceJa: なんだか、どうでもよくなってきてるのかな
findings.explanation: After saying she once hated her mother, Kazusa wonders whether she is beginning not to care anymore. The English says the situation is working out, replacing emotional detachment or exhaustion with optimistic resolution.
findings.japanese:
「はは…あんなに嫌ってたはずなのにな。
なんだか、どうでもよくなってきてるのかな」
findings.todokanai: "Haha… Even though I hated her so much. Somehow, I guess it's all working out."

findings.highlight: an overbearing girl who easily misunderstands everything
findings.evidenceJa: 思い込みの激しい痛いコ
findings.explanation: Setsuna protests that they are making her sound like a painfully or embarrassingly deluded girl who commits intensely to assumptions. 'Overbearing' instead characterizes her as domineering toward other people, importing a different interpersonal fault.
findings.japanese:
「ふ、二人とも、馬鹿にしないでよ！
わたしのこと、思い込みの激しい痛いコみたいに言って」
findings.todokanai: "S-Stop making fun of me, you two! You're making me sound like an overbearing girl who easily misunderstands everything."

findings.highlight: my whole world is flipped upside down in an instant
findings.evidenceJa: 一瞬のうちにうやむやになってしまった
findings.explanation: Kazusa's interruption causes the preceding dispute or question to become muddled and left unresolved in an instant. The English invents Haruki's whole world being overturned and never states that the conversation has been dropped.
findings.japanese: そして、一瞬のうちにうやむやになってしまった。
findings.todokanai: And my whole world is flipped upside down in an instant.

findings.highlight: "…The Kanto region will have very cloudy skies during the day, and snowfall is expected during the night, primarily in the mountain range. Up next are the forecasts for each region in the country…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「続いて北関東地方、日中から雲が多く、
夜には山間部を中心に雪となるでしょう。
では各地のお天気です…」
findings.explanation: A broader Northern Kanto destination is narrowed in English.
findings.japanese:
「続いて北関東地方、日中から雲が多く、
夜には山間部を中心に雪となるでしょう。
では各地のお天気です…」
findings.todokanai: "…The Kanto region will have very cloudy skies during the day, and snowfall is expected during the night, primarily in the mountain range. Up next are the forecasts for each region in the country…"

findings.highlight: Haruki-kun really leaves nothing to chance
findings.evidenceJa: 転ばぬ先の春希くん
findings.explanation: Setsuna substitutes Haruki's name into 転ばぬ先の杖, 'a cane before a fall,' making him the preventative implement who is always prepared. The generic compliment about leaving nothing to chance deletes the proverb substitution and the joke's image.
findings.japanese: 「さすが、転ばぬ先の春希くん、だね」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki-kun really leaves nothing to chance, huh?"

findings.highlight: close out the year-end party with a toast
findings.evidenceJa: 忘年会で言うところの『一本締め』の時間
findings.explanation: 一本締め is the ceremonial rhythmic hand-clap used to close a gathering, not a toast. The English replaces the named closing action with a different drinking ritual.
findings.japanese:
テーブルに並べられたご馳走は既に底をつき、
忘年会で言うところの『一本締め』の時間になった。
findings.todokanai: The feast that had been laid out on the table is already finished, and it's time for everyone to close out the year-end party with a toast.

findings.highlight: "That's just… terribly convenient for you. Utterly selfish and self-centered. You're completely disregarding your friend's and your boyfriend's personal thoughts on the matter. Can't you see how unbelievably egoistic that is?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「それってさ…勝手で、身勝手で、手前勝手で、
相手のこと…恋人のことすら何も考えてない、
信じられない自己中じゃないか…」
findings.explanation: A singular other person—even one's lover—is split into a friend and a boyfriend with separate thoughts.
findings.japanese:
「それってさ…勝手で、身勝手で、手前勝手で、
相手のこと…恋人のことすら何も考えてない、
信じられない自己中じゃないか…」
findings.todokanai: "That's just… terribly convenient for you. Utterly selfish and self-centered. You're completely disregarding your friend's and your boyfriend's personal thoughts on the matter. Can't you see how unbelievably egoistic that is?"

findings.highlight: Pretending that just drinking and messing around like this is some kind of huge event
findings.evidenceJa: とんでもない大イベントみたいに錯覚して
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she finds herself under the illusion that merely drinking and fooling around is some tremendous event. The English makes her knowingly pretend it is important, changing an involuntary emotional experience into conscious playacting.
findings.japanese:
「こんなふうに、ふざけて酒飲むだけのことが、
なんだかとんでもない大イベントみたいに錯覚して…」
findings.todokanai: "Pretending that just drinking and messing around like this is some kind of huge event…"

findings.highlight: Even though it's common sense, it doesn't even occur to me because of the situation I'm in.
findings.evidenceJa:
とか、そういう些細な問題を云々するのは、
今の状況に頭がついていかなかったせいで。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is dwelling on a trivial issue because his mind cannot catch up with the situation; the English says common sense does not occur to him.
findings.japanese:
とか、そういう些細な問題を云々するのは、
今の状況に頭がついていかなかったせいで。
findings.todokanai: Even though it's common sense, it doesn't even occur to me because of the situation I'm in.

findings.highlight: I kept teasing her earlier, remember?
findings.evidenceJa: さっき雪菜をからかったろ
findings.explanation: Kazusa reminds Haruki that he teased Setsuna earlier and explains that Setsuna has apparently held a grudge. The English makes Kazusa claim she herself kept teasing Setsuna, reversing responsibility for the prank that motivates the bath retaliation.
findings.japanese:
「さっき雪菜をからかったろ？
…ずっと根に持ってたみたいなんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I kept teasing her earlier, remember? …I imagine she was holding a grudge over that."

findings.highlight: that would mean carrying Setsuna with only a towel on?
findings.evidenceJa: 湯船の中で、ちゃんとマナー通りタオルを取ってる雪菜を
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks of Setsuna in the bath having properly removed her towel in accordance with bathing etiquette. The English says she has only a towel on, reversing the physical fact on which his embarrassment and the joke depend.
findings.japanese:
湯船の中で、ちゃんとマナー通り
タオルを取ってる雪菜を？
findings.todokanai: If I were to stick to proper bathing etiquette, that would mean carrying Setsuna with only a towel on?

findings.highlight: "That's fine. It would be an accident if it happened, so I can't blame you for sneaking a peek."
findings.evidenceJa:
「大丈夫だよ。
その時は事故なんだから、見られても平気だって」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says accidental exposure would not bother her, while the English reframes it as not blaming Haruki for sneaking a peek.
findings.japanese:
「大丈夫だよ。
その時は事故なんだから、見られても平気だって」
findings.todokanai: "That's fine. It would be an accident if it happened, so I can't blame you for sneaking a peek."

findings.highlight: trying her best to encourage everyone not to fall asleep
findings.evidenceJa: 必死に起きて、みんなに頑張って話し掛けていた
findings.explanation: Setsuna had desperately kept herself awake and continued making an effort to talk to everyone. The English invents a goal of keeping the others awake, transferring her struggle with her own exhaustion into responsibility for their alertness.
findings.japanese:
雪菜は、さっきまで必死に起きて、
みんなに頑張って話し掛けていた。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna was eagerly talking to us, trying her best to encourage everyone not to fall asleep until a moment ago.

findings.highlight: We weren't able to fully enjoy the trip until the very end
findings.evidenceJa: 最後の最後まで、頑張ってはしゃぎ続けることができなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says they could not keep making the effort to act excited and merry right to the end; their dwindling speech reveals the strain after the celebration. The English says only that they failed to enjoy the trip fully, erasing the attempted performance of cheerfulness.
findings.japanese:
最後の最後まで、頑張ってはしゃぎ続けることが
できなかったから。
findings.todokanai: We weren't able to fully enjoy the trip until the very end.

findings.highlight: Nonetheless, it seems like she's really hurt by my words, and that's making me seem awful as a result.
findings.evidenceJa:
そのくせ、俺の言葉に本気で傷ついているように
見えるのが、相当にタチ悪い。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls it perversely troublesome that Kazusa looks genuinely hurt, while the English says her reaction makes him seem awful.
findings.japanese:
そのくせ、俺の言葉に本気で傷ついているように
見えるのが、相当にタチ悪い。
findings.todokanai: Nonetheless, it seems like she's really hurt by my words, and that's making me seem awful as a result.

findings.highlight: I was never really expecting any gratitude in return anyway
findings.evidenceJa: 感謝なんて、本当はして欲しくない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he genuinely does not want Kazusa to thank him. The English says only that he did not expect thanks, changing a deliberate refusal rooted in how he understands his actions into a prediction about what he would receive.
findings.japanese:
「それにさ
感謝なんて、本当はして欲しくない」
findings.todokanai: "Not to mention… I was never really expecting any gratitude in return anyway."

findings.highlight: I hope Touma can accept this as a reward for her efforts
findings.evidenceJa: そんな言葉は、自覚してる努力の対価として受け取りたい
findings.explanation: Haruki says he wants to receive words of thanks as compensation only for effort he himself consciously recognizes as effort. The English reverses both roles, making Kazusa receive Haruki's words as a reward for her own efforts.
findings.japanese: そんな言葉は、自覚してる努力の対価として受け取りたい。
findings.todokanai: I hope Touma can accept this as a reward for her efforts.

findings.highlight: Before she could notice, I pinned Setsuna from behind
findings.evidenceJa: 気づいたとき、俺は雪菜を背中から羽交い締めに
findings.explanation: Haruki says that when he himself realized what he was doing, he had already seized Setsuna from behind strongly enough to resemble a restraining hold. The English makes the temporal marker about Setsuna failing to notice, reversing whose realization structures the sudden loss of control.
findings.japanese: 気づいたとき、俺は雪菜を背中から羽交い締めに…
findings.todokanai: Before she could notice, I pinned Setsuna from behind…

findings.highlight: As I run my hands across her coat, I recall the feeling of her smooth skin that I felt from touching her back in the bath.
findings.evidenceJa:
コート越しに、雪菜の背中に触れるだけで、
あの、露天風呂で感じたつるつるの肌を思い出す。
findings.explanation: Simply touching Setsuna's back through her coat becomes running hands across the coat and explicitly touching her bare back in the bath memory.
findings.japanese:
コート越しに、雪菜の背中に触れるだけで、
あの、露天風呂で感じたつるつるの肌を思い出す。
findings.todokanai: As I run my hands across her coat, I recall the feeling of her smooth skin that I felt from touching her back in the bath.

findings.highlight: My hand that was touching her back shifts forward, reaching into her coat and touching her breasts…
findings.evidenceJa:
背中をまさぐっていた手は、いつの間にか前に回り、
コートの中へと差し込まれ、雪菜の、二つのふくらみに…
findings.explanation: A hand moves from her back to the front, slips inside the coat, and approaches her breasts; the English states that it is already touching them.
findings.japanese:
背中をまさぐっていた手は、いつの間にか前に回り、
コートの中へと差し込まれ、雪菜の、二つのふくらみに…
findings.todokanai: My hand that was touching her back shifts forward, reaching into her coat and touching her breasts…

findings.highlight: I'm shamelessly forcing myself onto her like this
findings.evidenceJa: 悪びれずに先を促すなんて
findings.explanation: After Setsuna breaks free, Haruki condemns himself for shamelessly prompting or urging her to let him continue. The English says he is presently forcing himself on her, replacing a coercive verbal request with an ongoing physical assault and materially changing the consent choreography.
findings.japanese:
それどころか、悪びれずに先を促すなんて、
今日の俺は、本当にどうかしてる。
findings.todokanai: What's moreーI'm shamelessly forcing myself onto her like this… I must be completely out of my mind today.

findings.highlight: I would give up after only three days
findings.evidenceJa: たった三日、顔を見なくなっただけで、無意識のうちに途中下車するなんて思わなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says he never expected that a mere three days without seeing Kazusa would make him get off the train unconsciously. The translation invents a separate act of 'giving up,' obscuring that the unscheduled stop itself betrays his resolve to stay away.
findings.japanese:
たった三日、顔を見なくなっただけで、
無意識のうちに途中下車するなんて思わなかった。
findings.todokanai: I didn't expect that I would give up after only three days of not seeing her face, but I got off the train midway without realizing it.

findings.highlight: after being warned by the staff
findings.evidenceJa: なんとか係の人に言付けて、ほっとして戻ったところに
findings.explanation: Setsuna manages to leave a message or request with the staff and returns relieved. The staff do not warn her; the translation invents a reprimand and reverses the interaction.
findings.japanese:
なんとか係の人に言付けて、
ほっとして戻ったところに、今度は今の朝食談義。
findings.todokanai: She finally quieted down after being warned by the staff, but now she's going on about breakfast.

findings.highlight: her accurate sense of rhythm
findings.evidenceJa: ミスのない正確な指さばき
findings.explanation: Haruki and Setsuna can recognize her flawless, precise fingering or handwork. The translation substitutes rhythm, a different musical faculty, in a passage explicitly listing the limited technical features they can assess.
findings.japanese:
疾走するスピード感とか、叩きつける強さとか、
ミスのない正確な指さばきとか、
そういうわかりやすい観点でしか見れない。
findings.todokanai: We can only understand the simple things, like her blistering pace, the force at which she strikes each key, and her accurate sense of rhythm.

findings.highlight: my eyes that were completely fixed on the stage… had become embarrassingly swollen and red
findings.evidenceJa: 拍手をするためにようやく離した手と、そして、最後までステージを凝視し続けた目は…恥ずかしながら、赤く腫れ上がっていた
findings.explanation: The coordinated subject makes both the hands they finally unclasped and the eyes that stared at the stage red and swollen—the former from gripping each other, the latter from crying. The English applies the result only to Haruki's eyes and deletes half of the physical parallel.
findings.japanese:
拍手をするためにようやく離した手と、
そして、最後までステージを凝視し続けた目は…
恥ずかしながら、赤く腫れ上がっていた。
findings.todokanai: By the time we finally let go of each other's hands to applaud, my eyes that were completely fixed on the stage… had become embarrassingly swollen and red.

findings.highlight: Eventually, Touma met us with a noticeably cool expression.
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬は、えらくすっきりとした顔で迎えてくれた。
findings.explanation: Kazusa's remarkably refreshed or cleared expression becomes a 'cool expression.'
findings.japanese: 冬馬は、えらくすっきりとした顔で迎えてくれた。
findings.todokanai: Eventually, Touma met us with a noticeably cool expression.

findings.highlight: along with the lonely atmosphere she's brought about recently, Touma looks like she's drawing a line
findings.evidenceJa: その仕草や言葉は、最近の、目に見えないけど、寂しげな雰囲気を醸し出してたあの冬馬とは、一線を画してるようにも見えて
findings.explanation: Kazusa's present gestures and words seem to mark a clear break from the recently lonely Kazusa. The translation instead folds that lonely atmosphere into her present demeanor and leaves 'drawing a line' without the source's comparison, obscuring the apparent change Haruki is evaluating.
findings.japanese:
その仕草や言葉は、最近の、目に見えないけど、
寂しげな雰囲気を醸し出してたあの冬馬とは、
一線を画してるようにも見えて…
findings.todokanai: Through her demeanor and speech, along with the lonely atmosphere she's brought about recently, Touma looks like she's drawing a line…

findings.highlight: Is she cutting us off again?
findings.evidenceJa: 吹っ切ったのか？
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether Kazusa has finally gotten over or put the trouble behind her. 'Cutting us off' makes her newly withdraw from them, reversing the direction of the change he is considering.
findings.japanese:
…吹っ切ったのか？
というか、ただの俺の空回りだったのか？
findings.todokanai: Is she cutting us off again? Was I wrong in thinking that she had opened up to begin with?

findings.highlight: I am absolutely not allowed to hesitate with for even a moment
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっとでも退かれたらおしまいな
findings.explanation: Haruki fears the overbearing gift will be fatal if Setsuna recoils from it even slightly. The translation makes Haruki the one who must not hesitate, reversing the experiencer and replacing his fear of her reaction with resolve about his own conduct.
findings.japanese:
…なんともやっちゃった感漂う、
ちょっとでも退かれたらおしまいな、
痛い誕生日プレゼント。
findings.todokanai: …I feel like I've really done it now. It's an embarrassingly overbearing birthday present that I am absolutely not allowed to hesitate with for even a moment.

findings.highlight: She might be taking a nap right about now, completely exhausted after doing some intense training in the basement.
findings.evidenceJa:
今ごろ、必死で地下に籠もり猛特訓してたり、
力尽きてうたた寝してたりするかもしれないのに。
findings.explanation: Two alternative possibilities—Kazusa training fiercely in the basement or collapsing into a nap—are combined into a nap caused by training.
findings.japanese:
今ごろ、必死で地下に籠もり猛特訓してたり、
力尽きてうたた寝してたりするかもしれないのに。
findings.todokanai: She might be taking a nap right about now, completely exhausted after doing some intense training in the basement.

findings.highlight: her teacher is not even allowing her to go home, and is subjecting her to strict lessons
findings.evidenceJa: ずっと家に帰らず、件の先生のもとに泊まり込んで、厳しいレッスン三昧の日々を送っているかもしれない
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines Kazusa perhaps staying with the teacher instead of going home and immersing herself in strict lessons. The source does not say the teacher forbids her to leave or subjects her to the training; the English invents coercive agency.
findings.japanese:
あるいは、ずっと家に帰らず、
件の先生のもとに泊まり込んで、
厳しいレッスン三昧の日々を送っているかもしれないのに。
findings.todokanai: Or maybe her teacher is not even allowing her to go home, and is subjecting her to strict lessons every day.

findings.highlight: how stubborn I am
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の逆恨み
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes his own 逆恨み—misdirected or unjustified resentment—against Kazusa. Calling it stubbornness deletes the moral self-indictment and the contrast with Kazusa's justification.
findings.japanese:
そうやって考えれば考えるほど、
実は冬馬の正当性と、俺の逆恨みが
クローズアップされていく。
findings.todokanai: The more I think about it, the more I realize how stubborn I am and how justified Touma's actions are.

findings.highlight: It looks like she got held up a bit.
findings.evidenceJa: なんとか引っかかったみたいね
findings.explanation: Youko says Kazusa appears to have barely passed or been selected—she 'managed to make the cut.' The translation misreads 引っかかった as being delayed, breaking the result being disclosed before Haruki asks whether she passed.
findings.japanese:
「なんとか引っかかったみたいね。
昨夜電話がかかってきて、今から帰るって」
findings.todokanai: "It looks like she got held up a bit. She told me over the phone last night that she would be coming back soon."

findings.highlight: Always keeping me at arm's length, but never letting me reach you.
findings.evidenceJa: 手が届かないくせに、ずっと近くにいろなんて
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki became unattainable yet demanded that she remain close, turning proximity itself into torture. The English instead makes Haruki actively keep her at arm's length and then redundantly refuse access, changing the accusation's causal structure.
findings.japanese:
「手が届かないくせに、ずっと近くにいろなんて、
そんな拷問を思いついたのもお前だろ！」
findings.todokanai: "Always keeping me at arm's length, but never letting me reach you. Wasn't that torture your idea!?"

findings.highlight: finding out each other's misunderstandings
findings.evidenceJa: そんな悲しい突っ込みどころを見つけたところで
findings.explanation: Haruki has found a bitterly ironic point to call out: Kazusa too could not be honest with him because she was trying to be sincere toward Setsuna. This is not the discovery of mutual misunderstandings; that phrase erases the specific parallel in guilt immediately preceding the irreparable crack.
findings.japanese:
…そんな悲しい突っ込みどころを見つけたところで、
俺たちの間に穿たれた亀裂は、
もう、どうしようもない。
findings.todokanai: …Even after finding out each other's misunderstandings, the crack between us is already too wide to mend.

findings.highlight: after parting with her
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女を離してしまったあの場所
findings.explanation: Haruki identifies the place where he let Kazusa go, with しまった marking regret over his own completed action. 'Parting with her' turns this into a neutral or mutual separation and removes the agency central to his guilt.
findings.japanese:
そんな中、俺はあの場所で…
彼女を離してしまったあの場所で動けないまま。
findings.todokanai: Amidst that snow, I stood in place… I couldn't move after parting with her.

findings.highlight: my throat was dry
findings.evidenceJa: 喉を枯らしてた
findings.explanation: Haruki had cried himself hoarse or worn his voice out. A dry throat is a different physical condition and removes the evidence that he had been crying out, not merely silently weeping.
findings.japanese:
次に覚えてるのは、自分のベッドで震えてたこと。
顔を涙でくしゃくしゃにして、喉を枯らしてたこと。
findings.todokanai: The next thing I remember, I was shivering in my bed. My face was a tearful mess and my throat was dry.

findings.highlight: so I just brought the essentials
findings.evidenceJa: 大事取ってただけで
findings.explanation: Haruki says he stayed home an extra day as a precaution because there were no important classes. 大事を取る means to play it safe or take precautions; nothing in the line concerns bringing essential belongings.
findings.japanese:
「もともと昨日には熱は下がってた。
もう大した授業もないから、大事取ってただけで」
findings.todokanai: "My fever had already gone down yesterday in the first place. There won't be any more important classes either, so I just brought the essentials."

findings.highlight: cars can crash into it too
findings.evidenceJa: 車はぶつけるし
findings.explanation: Haruki recalls that he crashed the car on their snowy trip. The English makes a generic claim that cars can collide with snow, losing his agency and the callback to the actual accident.
findings.japanese: 「それに…車はぶつけるし」
findings.todokanai: "Besides that… cars can crash into it too."

findings.highlight: I was prepared for an accident back then. But even still, it wasn't a good feeling.
findings.evidenceJa: 遭難を覚悟したな。あ、それでいい印象なかったのか
findings.explanation: Haruki thought they might be stranded or lost, then realizes aloud that this is why he had no good impression of snow. The translation changes the danger to an accident and deletes the causal self-correction.
findings.japanese:
「あの時俺、遭難を覚悟したな。
あ、それでいい印象なかったのか」
findings.todokanai: "I was prepared for an accident back then. But even still, it wasn't a good feeling."

findings.highlight: A pianist nearing the end of her career
findings.evidenceJa: ピアニストの端くれ
findings.explanation: 端くれ means a humble or minor member of a profession—roughly 'some kind of pianist'—not a performer nearing retirement. The translation invents a late-career fact about Youko.
findings.japanese:
「うん、冬馬曜子。
ピアニストの端くれにして、あたしの元師匠にして、
超放任主義の母親失格者」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, Touma Youko. A pianist nearing the end of her career, and my former teacher. A non-intervening failure of a mother figure."

findings.highlight: regained her interest in me
findings.evidenceJa: あたしを連れて行く気になったんだって
findings.explanation: After seeing the school-festival performance, Youko decided that she wanted to take Kazusa with her. The translation reduces that concrete decision, which triggers the move to Vienna, to a vague renewal of interest.
findings.japanese:
「あの学園祭のライブを見てさ…
あたしを連れて行く気になったんだって」
findings.todokanai: "She watched our performance during the school festival… and regained her interest in me."

findings.highlight: She just selfishly shouldered what was supposed to be mine to bear.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつの片棒を担いでる俺に
findings.explanation: Haruki indicts himself as Kazusa's accomplice—literally, someone helping carry her end of the pole—in sustaining the strong facade. The English makes Kazusa shoulder Haruki's burden and calls her selfish, reversing both subject and moral judgment.
findings.japanese: あいつの片棒を担いでる俺に。
findings.todokanai: She just selfishly shouldered what was supposed to be mine to bear.

findings.highlight: "…Thank you. That's why I'm really glad to have you as a friend, Io."
findings.evidenceJa:
「…ありがとう。
だから、依緒とは友達でいられたんだろうな」
findings.explanation: Setsuna's conclusion that this is probably why she could remain friends with Io becomes generic gladness to have Io as a friend.
findings.japanese:
「…ありがとう。
だから、依緒とは友達でいられたんだろうな」
findings.todokanai: "…Thank you. That's why I'm really glad to have you as a friend, Io."

findings.highlight: why you've been so down lately
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜がそんなふうになった理由
findings.explanation: そんなふう refers to the immediately preceding account of Setsuna becoming a friend who keeps part of herself behind walls. Io says Setsuna still has not explained why she became that way; the translation substitutes a recent low mood and changes the topic of the conversation.
findings.japanese:
「結局、雪菜がそんなふうになった理由は、
まだ話してもらってないけど」
findings.todokanai: "That said, Setsuna, you still haven't told me why you've been so down lately."

findings.highlight: He completely ignored your feelings
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜の気持ちも知らずに先走って
findings.explanation: Io says Haruki rushed ahead without knowing Setsuna's feelings. 'Ignored' means he knew them and willfully disregarded them, materially increasing his culpability and changing the information state on which he acted.
findings.japanese:
「春希が悪いんだから。
あいつが、雪菜の気持ちも知らずに先走って…」
findings.todokanai: "It's all Haruki's fault. He completely ignored your feelings and acted rashly, Setsuna…"

findings.highlight: I already know what it is she's hiding.
findings.evidenceJa: 隠してることがわかっちゃったんだ
findings.explanation: Setsuna realized that Kazusa was hiding something. The Japanese does not say she already knows the concealed content; the translation upgrades detection of concealment into certainty about exactly what is hidden.
findings.japanese:
「かずさ…すごくうまく隠してた。
…でも、隠してることがわかっちゃったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Kazusa… has been really good at hiding it. But I already know what it is she's hiding."

findings.highlight: upon this once-in-a-lifetime stage
findings.evidenceJa: 本日、一度目の舞台上
findings.explanation: Haruki calls this his first appearance onstage today, foreshadowing the later figurative or relational 'stage.' The translation changes the count into 'once in a lifetime,' inventing a different temporal claim and losing the day's structural repetition.
findings.japanese: 本日、一度目の舞台上。
findings.todokanai: Today, upon this once-in-a-lifetime stage.

findings.highlight: with the same honors
findings.evidenceJa: 以下同文
findings.explanation: 以下同文 is the certificate formula meaning that the remainder is the same as stated above. It does not award 'the same honors'; the translation invents an academic distinction during the graduation-certificate recitation.
findings.japanese:
「卒業証書。
３年Ｅ組北原春希。
…以下同文」
findings.todokanai: "I hereby bestow the graduation certificate to Kitahara Haruki from Class 3-E, with the same honors."

findings.highlight: prepared some unfitting lines in my script or my speech
findings.evidenceJa: 文章や台詞に乗せるのかもしれないけど
findings.explanation: Haruki is imagining how an uncharacteristic line might be assigned to prose narration or dialogue if his youth were a movie, drama, or novel. The English makes him prepare a literal script or graduation speech, collapsing the surrounding metafictional comparison into an event in the scene.
findings.japanese:
ここで式を台無しにするような、らしくない言葉を、
文章や台詞に乗せるのかもしれないけど…
findings.todokanai: I imagine I might've prepared some unfitting lines in my script or my speech that would probably have ruined the ceremony, but…

findings.highlight: how I played White Album with the two of you
findings.evidenceJa: お前たちと歌った『ＷＨＩＴＥ　ＡＬＢＵＭ』
findings.explanation: Kazusa names White Album as the song she sang with Haruki and Setsuna, a shared trio memory. The translation changes that collective singing into Kazusa playing the song, weakening both the factual callback and the three-way act she promises to remember.
findings.japanese:
「お前たちと歌った
『ＷＨＩＴＥ　ＡＬＢＵＭ』のこと」
findings.todokanai: "I'll remember how I played White Album with the two of you."

findings.highlight: hiding under a light pole
findings.evidenceJa: 灯台の下に隠れてた
findings.explanation: The phrasing clearly modifies 灯台下暗し, the proverb that what is nearest is hardest to see: after searching the world, Haruki finds Kazusa directly below his own building. Literalizing 灯台 as a light pole creates a nonexistent object in the scene and erases the distance joke.
findings.japanese: 灯台の下に隠れてた、卑怯な愛しいひとを。
findings.todokanai: My beloved coward, hiding under a light pole.

findings.highlight: at just about the same time and volume
findings.evidenceJa: まったく同じタイミングと、音の高さで
findings.explanation: The siren is heard at exactly the same time and pitch, the physical clue that Kazusa is nearby and hearing the same ambulance. The translation changes exact timing to approximation and pitch to volume, corrupting both parts of the acoustic match.
findings.japanese:
俺の部屋で聞こえてたのと、
まったく同じタイミングと、音の高さで。
findings.todokanai: And at just about the same time and volume, I heard the same sound in my room.

findings.evidenceJa: とうとう、断りもなく、その膨らみに直接触れる
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly touches Kazusa's breast directly and without asking or permission. The translation preserves the touch but omits 断りもなく, materially sanitizing how his own narration characterizes the action.

ブラを無理やりたくし上げて、

findings.explanation: Haruki deliberately uses 犯す, the transgressive verb 'violate' or 'rape,' in response to Kazusa calling him a beast. The translation replaces that intentionally ugly combat/predation register with romantic possession and even shifts the ongoing act to 'about to.'
findings.japanese:

白い胸の先端に、今度こそ激しく舌を這わせ、

本当は、そこの場所を特定するためにも、
正しいことをしているはずなんだけど。

findings.explanation: Kazusa is already crying with a face on the verge of tears; she suddenly smiles and then cries again. The source's deliberate repeated paradox moves through crying, smiling, and renewed crying. 'Only then' falsely says the tears begin after the smile and removes the repetition.
findings.japanese:
泣きそうな顔で泣いていたかずさが、
ふっと微笑んで、そして泣いた。

１１時だよ」
findings.todokanai: "You should at least try to take a guess before asking someone. It's 11 o'clock already."

findings.highlight: With her excellent grades and ideal learning mindset, I have no idea why she ended up coming to prep school when all she needs is just a recommendation from her homeroom teacher, however.

そんなふうに成績優秀かつ授業態度も理想的、

findings.explanation: Haruki values this job in both respects developed around the line: it supplies a punishing amount of work and enough pay to exceed his rent. The English instead assigns the two sides of appreciation to Haruki and the company, obscuring why both workload and compensation make the job useful to him.

findings.evidenceJa: 本当の心が透けて見えるくらいに、寂しい笑顔で笑ってた。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's lonely smile is transparent enough that her own true feelings show through it. The English makes Setsuna's smile see through Haruki's heart, reversing whose inner state is exposed and who perceives it.
findings.japanese:
俺のために、俺の目の前でいつでも笑ってた。
本当の心が透けて見えるくらいに、
寂しい笑顔で笑ってた。
findings.todokanai: She continued to force herself to smile for me. I felt as if she could see straight through my heart with her lonesome smile.

findings.highlight: In the past week, I've steadily tried to exert my brain completely, working myself to exhaustion
findings.evidenceJa: 徐々に、徐々に頭の中を切り替えて、何も考えずに眠れるようになって一週間。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he gradually shifted his mind and has now been able to sleep without thinking for one week. The English instead describes a week of ongoing attempts to exhaust his brain, changing both the achieved state and the span measured from it.
findings.japanese:
徐々に、徐々に頭の中を切り替えて、
何も考えずに眠れるようになって一週間。
findings.todokanai: In the past week, I've steadily tried to exert my brain completely, working myself to exhaustion so that I wouldn't have time to think about it.

findings.highlight: That hurt, man.
findings.evidenceJa: た、武也…お前、酷いぞそれ
findings.explanation: Haruki protests that Takeya's mangled “fish eyes” expression is awful; Takeya misreads him as complaining about the light tap and answers accordingly. “That hurt” makes Haruki explicitly complain about physical pain and removes the misunderstanding that motivates his grammatical correction.
findings.japanese:
「げほっ、げほぉっ…
た、武也…お前、酷いぞそれ」
findings.todokanai: "Kgh, agh… T-Takeya… That hurt, man."

findings.highlight: Public Policy Department
findings.evidenceJa: 俺と同じ政経で
findings.explanation: Haruki and Takeya were both in Political Science and Economics through their second year. The English substitutes Public Policy, repeating an institutional error that alters the campus and transfer context.
findings.japanese:
二年まで、やっぱり俺と同じ政経で、
俺が転部した時には相当やり合った。
findings.todokanai: We were together in the Public Policy Department up until our second year, and we ended up fighting when he discovered that I changed departments.

findings.highlight: And yet his lack of patience doesn't win him any fights in the end.
findings.evidenceJa: それでも、結局根負けしたのはこいつの方で。
findings.explanation: The source says Takeya was ultimately the one who yielded after repeatedly confronting Haruki; the English says his impatience does not win him any fights.
findings.japanese: それでも、結局根負けしたのはこいつの方で。
findings.todokanai: And yet his lack of patience doesn't win him any fights in the end.

findings.highlight: I realize now that I have no memory of any situation in which an unknown girl abruptly appeared and glared at me with such hostility up until this point.
findings.evidenceJa:
今みたいに、会ったこともない女のコに、
いきなり敵意むき出しで睨みつけられる場合には、
何の参考にもならないと言うことを、思い知らされた。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his maxim about anger being easier than tears offers no guidance in this new case, while the English says he has no memory of such a case.
findings.japanese:
今みたいに、会ったこともない女のコに、
いきなり敵意むき出しで睨みつけられる場合には、
何の参考にもならないと言うことを、思い知らされた。
findings.todokanai: I realize now that I have no memory of any situation in which an unknown girl abruptly appeared and glared at me with such hostility up until this point.

findings.highlight: Do you even realize how depressing you sound?
findings.evidenceJa: 一発でもっとタチ悪いことしてきたってわかるわよ？
findings.explanation: Seeing Haruki look relieved while agreeing with her dating joke, Mari says that reaction tells her at a glance he has done something even worse. The English replaces her inference about serious misconduct with a comment that he sounds depressing, breaking the two-step reading of his expressions.
findings.japanese:
「…ほっとした顔で肯定しないの。
一発でもっとタチ悪いことしてきたってわかるわよ？」
findings.todokanai: "…Don't put on that happy face and nod in agreement. Do you even realize how depressing you sound?"

findings.highlight: my weakness was exposed to me twice, and both times I was told, "Everyone has moments like that."
findings.evidenceJa: 二度も心の中をぐるぐるに掻き回された俺としては、『みっともなくもなるさ』と開き直るしかなかったり。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his heart was churned up twice within twenty hours, leaving him only able to defiantly admit that of course he has become unsightly. The English invents other people exposing his weakness and twice telling him “Everyone has moments like that,” dialogue and events absent from the source.
findings.japanese:
けど、たった２０時間のうちに、
二度も心の中をぐるぐるに掻き回された俺としては、
『みっともなくもなるさ』と開き直るしかなかったり。
findings.todokanai: But within twenty hours, my weakness was exposed to me twice, and both times I was told, "Everyone has moments like that."

findings.highlight: All the people around me are "experienced adults," so I can continue to be myself in peace…
findings.evidenceJa:
周りは皆、『わかった大人』ばかり。
安心して、人の中で一人でいられる…
findings.explanation: Haruki values being able to remain alone among people, while “continue to be myself in peace” removes the social isolation inside company.
findings.japanese:
周りは皆、『わかった大人』ばかり。
安心して、人の中で一人でいられる…
findings.todokanai: All the people around me are "experienced adults," so I can continue to be myself in peace…
