findings.highlight: If they don't know anything, I can easily keep my distance.
findings.evidenceJa:
何もわかっていないのなら、
きちんと人との距離を取れ。
findings.explanation: Haruki's internal imperative tells Koharu to keep a proper distance if she knows nothing; the English turns that into his own ability to keep distance from unspecified people.
findings.japanese:
何もわかっていないのなら、
きちんと人との距離を取れ。
findings.todokanai: If they don't know anything, I can easily keep my distance.

findings.highlight: She never forgets to ask how I'm doing when she attends my class
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の授業いつも出てくれてたし、挨拶は欠かさないし、毎回居残ってまで質問してくれたし
findings.explanation: Haruki says Mihoko always attended his classes, always greeted him, and stayed behind every time to ask questions. The English replaces regular attendance with her asking how he is whenever she happens to attend, inventing a personal check-in and weakening the evidence for her ideal conduct as a student.
findings.japanese:
「矢田さん、教え子としては理想のコだったんだ。
俺の授業いつも出てくれてたし、挨拶は欠かさないし、
毎回居残ってまで質問してくれたし…」
findings.todokanai: "As a student, Yada-san is an ideal girl. She never forgets to ask how I'm doing when she attends my class, greets me politely, and she also stays late to ask me questions…"

findings.highlight: I'm partially to blame as well, after all.
findings.evidenceJa: そこはちゃんとする。俺も責任持つからさ…
findings.explanation: Takeya promises that they will handle the matter properly and that he too will take responsibility for ensuring Mihoko is satisfied. The English changes this forward-looking commitment into an admission that Takeya is partly to blame for what happened.
findings.japanese:
「わかった、わかったから。
とにかく、相手のコが納得すればいいんだろ？
そこはちゃんとする。俺も責任持つからさ…」
findings.todokanai: "Okay, we got it. So all we need to do is to help that girl accept it, right? We'll take care of it. I'm partially to blame as well, after all."

findings.highlight: do something that could make a really desirable guy fall for you
findings.evidenceJa: 誰もが認めるいい男に惚れるとかそういうの
findings.explanation: Takeya asks why Io cannot react like an ordinary woman by falling for a universally recognized good man—implicitly himself. The English instead tells her to make such a man fall for her, reversing who experiences the attraction and blunting his self-serving romantic hint.
findings.japanese:
「おい依緒、
お前もうちょっと普通の女の反応とかないのかよ？
誰もが認めるいい男に惚れるとかそういうの」
findings.todokanai: "Oi, Io, why can't you react more like a normal woman would? Like, do something that could make a really desirable guy fall for you, you know?"

findings.highlight: dumped more than a thousand times
findings.evidenceJa: 大学三年間で三桁を超える彼女に振られる
findings.explanation: Io says Takeya has been rejected by a three-digit number of women—more than one hundred—during university. The English raises that claim to more than one thousand, changing the joke's explicit scale by an order of magnitude.
findings.japanese:
「大学三年間で三桁を超える彼女に振られるのと
どっちが哀れかよく考えてからにしてよね」
findings.todokanai: "Compared to a guy who's been dumped more than a thousand times in the past three years, I wonder which is more pathetic."

findings.highlight: It's about time they got back together.
findings.evidenceJa: いい加減、お互い許し合えばいいのに
findings.explanation: Io says that after three years Haruki and Setsuna should finally forgive each other. The English turns forgiveness into getting back together, asserting a specific romantic reunion rather than the interpersonal resolution that forms the parallel contrast with Takeya's proposal to separate.
findings.japanese:
「だってさぁ…もう三年だよ？
どうしてずっと引きずったままなんだよ？
いい加減、お互い許し合えばいいのに」
findings.todokanai: "But still… it's been three years, right? Why does it have to drag on like this? It's about time they got back together."

findings.highlight: But I'll take that back if you're still here when I come back.
findings.evidenceJa: すれ違いになるといけないから、今言っとくわね
findings.explanation: Mari says goodbye now because she and Haruki may miss or pass each other while she is out buying food. The English invents a threat to retract her “good work” if he is still there when she returns, reversing a practical farewell into disciplinary pressure.
findings.japanese:
「そうね、早く帰った方がいいわ。お疲れさま。
…すれ違いになるといけないから、今言っとくわね」
findings.todokanai: "That's good, it's better if you go home early. Good work today… But I'll take that back if you're still here when I come back."

findings.highlight: going to their seminars and working with their social media
findings.evidenceJa: 新聞サークルとか、マスコミ就職のためのゼミとかに積極的に参加した。
findings.explanation: Haruki actively joined a newspaper club and seminars aimed at employment in mass media, separate activities he used to consume his private time. The English folds the seminars into the newspaper club and invents social-media work, deleting the explicit employment preparation.
findings.japanese:
自分の学部と無関係の講義を受けまくった。
新聞サークルとか、マスコミ就職のための
ゼミとかに積極的に参加した。
findings.todokanai: I participated in lectures that had nothing to do with my specialization. I'm also very active in the newspaper club, going to their seminars and working with their social media.

findings.highlight: I can only give up on Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: だから俺はもう、雪菜に呆れられるしかない。
findings.explanation: Haruki believes his only remaining course is to make Setsuna become disgusted with him, hate him, and finally reject him. The English instead says Haruki must give up on Setsuna, reversing who is supposed to relinquish whom in his self-punishing plan.
findings.japanese:
だから俺はもう、雪菜に呆れられるしかない。
嫌われてしまわなくちゃならない。
憎まれるべき人間だ。
findings.todokanai: That's why I can only give up on Setsuna. To become a person she hates and detests.

findings.highlight: fly freely like she used to
findings.evidenceJa: あいつみたいに、飛び立って欲しかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki wants Setsuna to fly free like “that person,” a deliberately withheld referent that the article's final reveal resolves as Kazusa. The English makes Setsuna fly as she herself used to, erasing the cross-character comparison and breaking the script's delayed referent.
findings.japanese:
あいつみたいに、飛び立って欲しかった。
俺みたいな人間に、囚われて欲しくなかった。
findings.todokanai: Instead of being chained down by a person such as myself, I wish she could fly freely like she used to.

findings.highlight: I'll finally be able to recover from this deep slump I've been stuck in for the longest time
findings.evidenceJa: 立ち直るのにとても長い時間がかかるくらい、深く落ち込むことができるんだろう
findings.explanation: If Setsuna is finally freed, Haruki thinks he will then permit himself to sink into a depression so deep that recovery will take a very long time. The English says that moment will let him recover from a long-standing slump, reversing anticipated collapse into recovery.
findings.japanese:
その時、俺はようやく
立ち直るのにとても長い時間がかかるくらい、
深く落ち込むことができるんだろうって、思う。
findings.todokanai: That's when I'll finally be able to recover from this deep slump I've been stuck in for the longest time, or so I hope.

findings.highlight: I try to escape into reality
findings.evidenceJa: ありとあらゆる方法を駆使して逃げてる現実と、無意識のうちに向き合ってしまっていた。
findings.explanation: The reality Haruki uses every possible method to flee is what he has unconsciously found himself facing again. The English makes reality his refuge—something he escapes into—reversing the direction of his avoidance at the climax of the work-as-escape passage.
findings.japanese:
夢に見るのも辛くて、
ありとあらゆる方法を駆使して逃げてる現実と、
無意識のうちに向き合ってしまっていた。
findings.todokanai: Dreaming about it is too painful, so I try to escape into reality, but before I realize it, I'm unconsciously thinking about it again.

findings.highlight: The fact that you're only ever on campus in the morning…
findings.evidenceJa: 朝でないと大学いないじゃないかお前...
findings.explanation: Haruki answers that he had to come in the morning because Chiaki is never at the university otherwise. The English leaves only an unfinished noun phrase and never states the reason he came early, obscuring his direct reply to her question.
findings.japanese: 「朝でないと大学いないじゃないかお前...」
findings.todokanai: "The fact that you're only ever on campus in the morning…"

findings.highlight: merely a joke from him ended up coming true
findings.evidenceJa: 嘘から出た誠だったみたいで。
findings.explanation: Chiaki's earlier claim that Haruki had been appointed her tutor appears to have started as a lie and subsequently become true. The English instead says a joke from the professor came true, assigning the original statement to the wrong person and changing Chiaki's history of bluffing him.
findings.japanese: と言うか、嘘から出た誠だったみたいで。
findings.todokanai: Perhaps it's better to say that a lot of what initially came out as merely a joke from him ended up coming true after all.

findings.highlight: Given that I'm in charge of you now
findings.evidenceJa: 所属してんだから来て当然だろ？
findings.explanation: Haruki says Chiaki should attend the seminar because she belongs to it. The English says attendance is obvious because Haruki is now in charge of her, replacing her institutional obligation with authority arising from their new tutoring arrangement.
findings.japanese: 「所属してんだから来て当然だろ？」
findings.todokanai: "Given that I'm in charge of you now, isn't that obvious?"

findings.highlight: I was able to remember the faces of everyone within my year
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は一週間で同学年の奴ら全員に顔を覚えられ
findings.explanation: Because Chiaki dragged the new transfer around, every student in Haruki's year learned and remembered his face within a week. The English reverses that social result and says Haruki learned everyone else's faces.
findings.japanese:
けれど、こいつのこの仕打ちが原因で、
俺は一週間で同学年の奴ら全員に顔を覚えられ...
findings.todokanai: Then again, thanks to these splurges of hers, I was able to remember the faces of everyone within my year in a mere week…

findings.highlight: I wasn't joking, you know?
findings.evidenceJa: ネタにし切れてないよ？
findings.explanation: After Haruki tries to turn Chiaki's painfully accurate warning into a jab at her, she points out that he has not fully managed to make his response into a joke. The English instead says Chiaki herself was not joking, losing her observation that his attempted deflection still exposes genuine hurt.
findings.japanese: 「ネタにし切れてないよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I wasn't joking, you know?"

findings.highlight: without fear of reservation
findings.evidenceJa: 見返りが来ることを恐れずに世話を焼けることが、俺にとってはありがたかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki is grateful that he can care for Chiaki without fearing any reciprocal return—especially the stronger feelings his kindness has elicited from other women. “Without fear of reservation” is defective and fails to state what he fears coming back, obscuring the central reason this friendship feels safe.
findings.japanese:
見返りが来ることを恐れずに世話を焼けることが、
俺にとってはありがたかった。
findings.todokanai: I'm grateful to have someone whose business I can butt into without fear of reservation like this.

findings.highlight: I can't stand this girl.
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱ苦手だ、この女。
findings.explanation: After Chiaki's sexual teasing, Haruki corrects himself back to saying she is difficult for him to handle. The English says he cannot stand her, changing affectionate exasperation inside a friendship he has just called irreplaceable into outright dislike.
findings.japanese: やっぱ苦手だ、この女。
findings.todokanai: I can't stand this girl.

findings.highlight: Should I joke about how her motivation always seems to be in the wrong place, or respect her ability to calmly do these things I've never even thought of?
findings.evidenceJa:
相変わらず目の付け所がエッジと言うか、
俺が思いつかないことを平然とやってのけると言うか。
findings.explanation: Haruki describes Chiaki's edgy choice of focus and ability to do what he would never conceive; the English changes the first trait to misplaced motivation and invents a joke-versus-respect choice.
findings.japanese:
相変わらず目の付け所がエッジと言うか、
俺が思いつかないことを平然とやってのけると言うか。
findings.todokanai: Should I joke about how her motivation always seems to be in the wrong place, or respect her ability to calmly do these things I've never even thought of?

findings.highlight: Your mistress, then?
findings.evidenceJa: 春希のワケあり女？
findings.explanation: Chiaki revises “girlfriend” to a woman with some complicated or compromising connection to Haruki. The English specifies a mistress, inventing an illicit sexual relationship rather than preserving the deliberately vague suspicion.
findings.japanese: 「春希のワケあり女？」
findings.todokanai: "Your mistress, then?"

findings.highlight: "The truth is… I got into a little mess with one of her friends. She got pretty upset over it."
findings.evidenceJa:
「実は...彼女の友達に、ちょっと悪いことして。
それで彼女を怒らせてて」
findings.explanation: Haruki admits he did something a little bad to Koharu's friend; “got into a little mess with” weakens his agency and wrongdoing into a mutual situation.
findings.japanese:
「実は...彼女の友達に、ちょっと悪いことして。
それで彼女を怒らせてて」
findings.todokanai: "The truth is… I got into a little mess with one of her friends. She got pretty upset over it."

findings.highlight: you pervert! Pedophile! Criminal!
findings.evidenceJa: よっ、色男。年下殺し。犯罪者
findings.explanation: Chiaki jokingly escalates from “ladies' man” to “killer of younger girls” to “criminal” after summarizing the failed communication. The English replaces the first two teasing labels with “pervert” and “pedophile,” inventing a direct accusation of sexual deviance and child abuse that the source does not make.
findings.japanese:
「届かない想いに、伝わらない言葉に、
そして、わかってくれない大人...
よっ、色男。年下殺し。犯罪者」
findings.todokanai: "Feelings that couldn't be conveyed, words that were never said, and an adult who just wouldn't understand… Well, how's it going, you pervert! Pedophile! Criminal!"

findings.highlight: There's no way it'd go that smoothly.
findings.evidenceJa: そこまで甘える訳にいくかよ。
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks he cannot impose on or depend on Chiaki to that extent; “There's no way it'd go that smoothly” changes reluctance to accept help into doubt about success.
findings.japanese: そこまで甘える訳にいくかよ。
findings.todokanai: There's no way it'd go that smoothly.

findings.highlight: "This is the dilemma he's struggling with. Despite still holding on to his kind and caring attitude, he can't bear accepting others' gratitude."
findings.evidenceJa:
「だから、いつもジレンマを抱えてる。
人にとても優しくしてしまうのに、
人から優しくしてもらうのが耐えられない」
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot bear receiving kindness from others, but the English narrows this to accepting gratitude.
findings.japanese:
「だから、いつもジレンマを抱えてる。
人にとても優しくしてしまうのに、
人から優しくしてもらうのが耐えられない」
findings.todokanai: "This is the dilemma he's struggling with. Despite still holding on to his kind and caring attitude, he can't bear accepting others' gratitude."

findings.highlight: "No, I should be the one saying that. Because after this, you still need to go through this difficult conversation with your friend."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ううん、おあいこ。
だって、あなたもこれから、
友達に辛い話をしなくちゃならないんだから」
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she and Koharu are even because Koharu must now tell her friend something painful; “I should be the one saying that” loses the reciprocal balance.
findings.japanese:
「ううん、おあいこ。
だって、あなたもこれから、
友達に辛い話をしなくちゃならないんだから」
findings.todokanai: "No, I should be the one saying that. Because after this, you still need to go through this difficult conversation with your friend."

findings.highlight: around Nishiguchi
findings.evidenceJa: 春希のマンション、西口の方だよね？
findings.explanation: Chiaki says Haruki's apartment is on the west-exit side of the station. The English treats 西口, “west exit,” as a proper place name, “Nishiguchi,” so the direction she remembers becomes a nonexistent named location.
findings.japanese:
「さ、じゃあ行こか。
確か春希のマンション、西口の方だよね？」
findings.todokanai: "Then let's get going. Your apartment's around Nishiguchi, right, Haruki?"

findings.highlight: …Well, before all that, we should focus on whether or not she'll actually graduate.
findings.evidenceJa:
...まぁ、そもそも卒業どころか進級すら怪しいからこそ、
今ここにいる訳だけど。
findings.explanation: Chiaki may not even advance to the next year, let alone graduate; the English mentions only the more distant graduation risk.
findings.japanese:
...まぁ、そもそも卒業どころか進級すら怪しいからこそ、
今ここにいる訳だけど。
findings.todokanai: …Well, before all that, we should focus on whether or not she'll actually graduate.

findings.highlight: I might have been very dedicated.
findings.evidenceJa: あんなに練習したけれど。あんなにしごかれもしたけれど。
findings.explanation: Haruki remembers both practicing intensely and being drilled or put through severe training, preserving Kazusa's role in teaching him. The English turns the second experience into Haruki's own dedication, deleting the other person's forceful coaching from his reason the guitar still carries memories.
findings.japanese:
あんなに練習したけれど。
あんなにしごかれもしたけれど。
findings.todokanai: I might have practiced very hard. I might have been very dedicated.

findings.highlight: "I feel kind of bad if you're saying you did that because of me…"
findings.evidenceJa: 「あたしのせいにされても困るんだけどなぁ」
findings.explanation: Chiaki objects to Haruki making her his excuse for rejecting the call, while the English says she feels bad if he did it because of her.
findings.japanese: 「あたしのせいにされても困るんだけどなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "I feel kind of bad if you're saying you did that because of me…"

findings.highlight: "No, no, you can't look. The first person I have to show this to is…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「駄目、駄目、見ちゃ駄目。
だって、わたしが最初に伝えたいのは...」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she wants to be the first to tell someone the news, but the English says the first person she has to show the magazine to.
findings.japanese:
「駄目、駄目、見ちゃ駄目。
だって、わたしが最初に伝えたいのは...」
findings.todokanai: "No, no, you can't look. The first person I have to show this to is…"

findings.highlight: whether it has emotions passionately poured into it
findings.evidenceJa: 一生懸命、想いを込めずに発した言葉でも、文字通りの意味しか相手に伝わらずに済む。
findings.explanation: Haruki chooses text so that even words he works hard to produce without putting his feelings into them will communicate only their literal meaning. The English says the alternative is a message with emotions passionately poured into it, reversing his deliberate emotional suppression.
findings.japanese:
それなら、まるで当たり障りのない内容でも、
一生懸命、想いを込めずに発した言葉でも、
文字通りの意味しか相手に伝わらずに済む。
findings.todokanai: This way, regardless of whether the message is completely banal or whether it has emotions passionately poured into it, only the most literal meaning of its words will reach the recipient.

findings.highlight: I'm twisting the memories I have back from high school
findings.evidenceJa: 付属時代の思い出が様々に形を変え、今になって伝わってくる事実から逃げ。
findings.explanation: Haruki runs from high-school memories returning in various changed forms and from facts only now reaching him. The English makes Haruki actively twist those memories himself, assigning agency for their changing forms to him rather than describing what he avoids.
findings.japanese:
付属時代の思い出が様々に形を変え、
今になって伝わってくる事実から逃げ。
findings.todokanai: I'm twisting the memories I have back from high school, running away from the truth of what things have become now.

findings.highlight: You'll help out, won't you, Kitahara?
findings.evidenceJa: 北原にも手伝ってもらったでしょ？
findings.explanation: The editor reminds Haruki that he already helped them with the Kaiou Graph. The translation changes completed past assistance into a request or expectation that he will help in the future.
findings.japanese:
「だから今週発売の開桜グラフ。
北原にも手伝ってもらったでしょ？」
findings.todokanai: "As I've said, it's about the Kaiou Graph we're releasing this week. You'll help out, won't you, Kitahara?"

findings.highlight: There's serious talent behind those looks too.
findings.evidenceJa: 話題性も抜群だ
findings.explanation: 話題性 is newsworthiness or publicity value. The line says the proposed subject is exceptionally marketable as a topic, not that her looks conceal serious artistic talent.
findings.japanese:
「それだけじゃないぞ。話題性も抜群だ。
こりゃ、クラシック界で久々に来たかなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "And that's not all. There's serious talent behind those looks too. It's been a while since someone shook up the classical music world like this."

findings.highlight: a second-year grad student
findings.evidenceJa: 大卒二年目
findings.explanation: 大卒二年目 means someone in the second year after graduating from university. Haruki is a second-year member of the workforce, not a graduate student.
findings.japanese: 「大卒二年目を二年生って言うんならな…」
findings.todokanai: "I guess if you count a second-year grad student as a 'second-year'…"

findings.highlight: "Hold on, Kitahara… What's this about you leaving in the morning? You didn't tell me about this."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ちょっと北原…
朝帰りって何よ？
私聞いてないわよ？」
findings.explanation: 朝帰り is an all-night absence followed by returning home in the morning, not merely leaving somewhere in the morning.
findings.japanese:
「ちょっと北原…
朝帰りって何よ？
私聞いてないわよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Hold on, Kitahara… What's this about you leaving in the morning? You didn't tell me about this."

findings.highlight: Broke his hip, I heard?
findings.evidenceJa: 腰やっちゃったんだって？
findings.explanation: 腰をやる means injuring one's lower back or waist. Nothing says the branch manager broke his hip.
findings.japanese:
「腰やっちゃったんだって？
ま、あの歳じゃなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Broke his hip, I heard? Well, he is at that age after all…"

findings.highlight: "Don't use those puppy eyes on me. I agreed to help only for today."
findings.evidenceJa:
「そこであからさまにほっとされても困る。
俺、今日一日だけのヘルプって約束なんだから」
findings.explanation: An openly relieved expression becomes 'puppy-dog eyes.'
findings.japanese:
「そこであからさまにほっとされても困る。
俺、今日一日だけのヘルプって約束なんだから」
findings.todokanai: "Don't use those puppy eyes on me. I agreed to help only for today."

findings.highlight: this slightly cowardly acting manager
findings.evidenceJa: 少しばかり弱腰な幹部候補
findings.explanation: He is a somewhat timid candidate for management, not the acting manager. The translation changes both his disposition and his employment status.
findings.japanese:
店長を除けば最古参で、しかも俺より二つ年上なのに、
何故か俺に敬語を使う、少しばかり弱腰な幹部候補。
findings.todokanai: The branch manager aside, he's the one with the most experience here, not to mention he's two years older than me. Despite all that, though, this slightly cowardly acting manager still speaks so politely to me.

findings.highlight: Aren't you a full-fledged employee? You want to live up to that role, don't you?
findings.evidenceJa: 準社員なんだろ？　正式採用目指してるんだろ？
findings.explanation: Satou is a quasi-employee or associate employee aiming for formal hire. The translation calls him already full-fledged and replaces his concrete goal of formal employment with the vague wish to live up to his present role.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあビシッと言えよ。
準社員なんだろ？　正式採用目指してるんだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "Then just be strict with them. Aren't you a full-fledged employee? You want to live up to that role, don't you?"

findings.highlight: It's not like I can really give a statement saying her training's over right now.
findings.evidenceJa: 『もうおしまい』とか、一方的に言われることはなくなった
findings.explanation: Haruki notes that Koharu has stopped unilaterally telling him that their interaction is over. The translation instead makes Haruki unable to declare her training over, reversing speaker and action.
findings.japanese:
さすがに『もうおしまい』とか、
一方的に言われることはなくなった。
findings.todokanai: It's not like I can really give a statement saying her training's over right now.

findings.highlight: I should at least look at the scheduled shifts before leaving her by herself…
findings.evidenceJa: 今月のシフト表を見てしまった後だと
findings.explanation: Haruki has already seen the month's understaffed roster, which makes abandoning the store difficult. The translation turns that prior knowledge into an intention to inspect the schedule before leaving Koharu alone.
findings.japanese:
かと言って、このままこの店を放置するのも、
今月のシフト表を見てしまった後だと…
findings.todokanai: But even so, I should at least look at the scheduled shifts before leaving her by herself…

findings.highlight: it wasn't until two hours later that I could get my hands on the evening shift schedule.
findings.evidenceJa: 夜シフトのメンバーが揃ったのは、さらに２時間が経過した後
findings.explanation: The evening-shift staff finally assembled two hours later. The translation substitutes Haruki obtaining a schedule, an event that does not happen here.
findings.japanese:
結局、夜シフトのメンバーが揃ったのは、
さらに２時間が経過した後だった。
findings.todokanai: In the end, it wasn't until two hours later that I could get my hands on the evening shift schedule.

findings.highlight: I can feel a sharp sting in her words.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の言葉に刺はなかったけど
findings.explanation: The source explicitly says her words contained no barb, while adding that they did not feel rounded or warm either. The translation directly reverses the first half of that calibrated judgment.
findings.japanese:
彼女の言葉に刺はなかったけど、
だからといって丸みを感じられたかというと…
findings.todokanai: I can feel a sharp sting in her words. Nevertheless, these two continue to stare daggers at me.

findings.highlight: They've long since mastered this strategy of mine…
findings.evidenceJa: こっちが向こうの声にならない言葉を理解でき過ぎることが、どうやら向こうにも当てはまってる
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes that the same excessive ability he has to understand their unspoken words also applies in reverse: they understand his. The translation invents a deliberate strategy that the others have mastered and loses the mutual recognition.
findings.japanese:
こっちが向こうの声にならない言葉を
理解でき過ぎることが、
どうやら向こうにも当てはまってるようだった…
findings.todokanai: During times like these, silence speaks louder than words. They've long since mastered this strategy of mine…

findings.highlight: There's nothing to forgive you for, so I won't forgive you
findings.evidenceJa: 三年間『許す理由がないから許しあえない』どこかの二人
findings.explanation: The Japanese describes two people unable to forgive each other for three years because they lack even a reason or occasion to forgive, a reciprocal paradox contrasted with Haruki and Koharu's easy reconciliation. The translation turns it into a unilateral 'I won't forgive you' and locates the damage only inside Haruki.
findings.japanese:
三年間『許す理由がないから許しあえない』
どこかの二人を嘲笑うかのように、
和解の瞬間は実にあっさりとやってきた。
findings.todokanai: As if to mock the "There's nothing to forgive you for, so I won't forgive you" situation that's been tearing at me for three years, my reconciliation with this girl came in a mere instant.

findings.highlight: what she said coincided perfectly with the thoughts going through my mind.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女に告げられたその言葉は、しごく自然な流れだったのにもかかわらず
findings.explanation: Koharu's words followed perfectly naturally from the conversation, yet Haruki was too preoccupied to identify their referent calmly. The translation instead claims that her words matched Haruki's thoughts.
findings.japanese:
彼女に告げられたその言葉は、
しごく自然な流れだったのにもかかわらず。
findings.todokanai: Although what she said coincided perfectly with the thoughts going through my mind.

findings.highlight: seem too mundane for this scenery.
findings.evidenceJa: 『三年ぶり』とか『懐かしいな』とか言うには、あまりにも日常の風景
findings.explanation: The scenery is too close to Haruki's everyday life to feel like a place that warrants saying 'three years' or 'nostalgic.' The translation reverses the relation and calls the words too mundane for the scenery.
findings.japanese:
『三年ぶり』とか『懐かしいな』とか言うには、
あまりにも日常の風景。
findings.todokanai: Words like, "It's been three years", or "It really takes me back" seem too mundane for this scenery.

findings.highlight: with a surprised expression
findings.evidenceJa: 憮然と立っていた
findings.explanation: Koharu is standing there sullen or displeased, not surprised. Her expression establishes the confrontational tone of the reunion.
findings.japanese:
きっと会ってしまうだろうと思っていた人物が、
予想通り、俺の目の前に憮然と立っていた。
findings.todokanai: A certain someone who I was sure I'd be meeting here eventually was standing right in front of me with a surprised expression, just as I expected.

findings.highlight: abandoning your position as my trainer
findings.evidenceJa: 突き放した教え方
findings.explanation: Koharu criticizes Haruki's detached, deliberately sink-or-swim way of teaching her. She does not accuse him of abandoning the trainer position.
findings.japanese:
「酷いこと言ったりとか、突き放した教え方したりとか、
そもそもわたしのバイト先に突然現れたりとか、
そういうこと謝るつもりなのかなって」
findings.todokanai: "I was just wondering if you were looking to apologize, is all. For saying mean things to me, for abandoning your position as my trainer, or maybe for showing up at my workplace in the first place."

findings.highlight: get hired as our substitute teacher
findings.evidenceJa: 教育実習
findings.explanation: 教育実習 is student teaching or a teaching practicum. Haruki is discussing returning as a trainee teacher, not being hired as a substitute teacher.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ、今日は一体何の用なんです？
わたしのクラスに『偶然』教育実習にでも来ましたか？」
findings.todokanai: "So, what business do you have with me today? Did you just coincidentally get hired as our substitute teacher or something?"

findings.highlight: Do I really get this irritating when I talk to someone…?
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が二人いると、こんなにもウザいのか
findings.explanation: Haruki's joke is that having two copies of himself—him and Mini-Haruki Koharu—is this irritating. The translation deletes the mirrored-character premise and turns it into a generic observation about how he talks.
findings.japanese:
俺が二人いると、
こんなにもウザいのか…
findings.todokanai: Do I really get this irritating when I talk to someone…?

findings.highlight: even if I try to dodge it little by little
findings.evidenceJa: 例え順を追って振られても、受け入れる準備なんかできるわけもない話題
findings.explanation: Haruki says he could not be prepared to accept this topic even if the teacher introduced it carefully, step by step. The translation instead makes Haruki the agent who tries to dodge it gradually.
findings.japanese:
けど今度は、例え順を追って振られても、
受け入れる準備なんかできるわけもない話題で。
findings.todokanai: But this time, even if I try to dodge it little by little, it's still too sensitive of a topic for me to have been prepared for.

findings.highlight: Remembering to lock up is pretty impressive.
findings.evidenceJa: 教室の戸締まりとかも、よくやった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that he often used to handle locking up classrooms. The translation changes this recollection of his own past conduct into praise for Koharu remembering to lock up now.
findings.japanese:
「教室の戸締まりとかも、よくやった。
結構忘れてく奴ら多いんだよな」
findings.todokanai: "Remembering to lock up is pretty impressive. Most people forget all about it."

findings.highlight: whether my feelings for this girl
findings.evidenceJa: 杉浦小春のこと、温かいとか冷たいとか、今まで考えたこともなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says he had never considered whether Koharu herself was a warm or cold person. The translation changes the object to whether his own feelings for her are passionate or indifferent, introducing a romantic question absent from the line.
findings.japanese:
そういえば…
このコ…杉浦小春のこと、温かいとか冷たいとか、
今まで考えたこともなかったっけ。
findings.todokanai: Now that I think of it… whether my feelings for this girlーSugiura Koharuーare of passion or indifference is something I haven't really thought about until now.

findings.highlight: our conversation ended there as she no longer had any more cards to play.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の断り方も、不自然なくらいに自然で、どこにもカドが立たないまま、するっと会話が成り立つ
findings.explanation: The point is that their exchange has become almost unnaturally natural: it proceeds smoothly, without sharp edges or friction. The translation invents an adversarial card game in which Koharu runs out of moves and misses the new ease between them.
findings.japanese:
だからだろうか。
彼女の断り方も、不自然なくらいに自然で、
どこにもカドが立たないまま、するっと会話が成り立つ。
findings.todokanai: And for that reason, her refusal of my courtesy sounds unnaturally natural, and our conversation ended there as she no longer had any more cards to play.

findings.highlight: hailing her as an unbelievable prodigy, an unmatched model student, and an elegant and refined lady.
findings.evidenceJa: ありもしない天才で優等生でお嬢様だった冬馬
findings.explanation: Haruki says everyone praises a prodigy, model-student, fine-young-lady Touma who never existed. Reading ありもしない as intensifying 'unbelievable' erases his critique that this public Kazusa is a fabricated persona.
findings.japanese:
誰もが、ありもしない天才で優等生でお嬢様だった
冬馬を絶賛してた。
findings.todokanai: Everyone holds nothing but admiration and praise for Touma, hailing her as an unbelievable prodigy, an unmatched model student, and an elegant and refined lady.

findings.highlight: Poking fun at each other is what friends do
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっとした残酷な友情
findings.explanation: Haruki calls it 'a little cruel friendship,' an oxymoronic phrase whose 残酷 is explicitly picked up by the next line. The translation deletes cruelty, changes the proposition to ordinary teasing, and strands the reply's verbal callback.
findings.japanese:
「あっははは…意地になんないでよ春希。
ちょっとした残酷な友情じゃんか～」
findings.todokanai: "Ahahaha… No need to be like that, Haruki. Poking fun at each other is what friends do, isn't it?"

findings.highlight: An unfamiliar voice.
findings.evidenceJa: 聞き慣れない音
findings.explanation: Haruki wakes to an unfamiliar sound, not an unfamiliar voice. Izumi's voice is familiar to him, and the surrounding sequence deliberately lists an unfamiliar ceiling, sound, and posture.
findings.japanese:
見慣れない天井。
聞き慣れない音。
そして、取り慣れない姿勢。
findings.todokanai: An unfamiliar ceiling. An unfamiliar voice. And an unfamiliar sleeping position.

findings.highlight: The possibility never crossed my mind.
findings.evidenceJa: その可能性に思い至らない訳じゃなかった
findings.explanation: The double negative says it was not that the possibility failed to occur to Haruki: he did consider it. The translation states the exact opposite.
findings.japanese: その可能性に思い至らない訳じゃなかった。
findings.todokanai: The possibility never crossed my mind.

findings.highlight: That's why this single point that will never be a line will never be the thing that connects us.
findings.evidenceJa:
だから点は線にならず、
やっぱり俺たちは、繋がらないままだった。
findings.explanation: Points that had not formed a line are rendered as points that never formed one.
findings.japanese:
だから点は線にならず、
やっぱり俺たちは、繋がらないままだった。
findings.todokanai: That's why this single point that will never be a line will never be the thing that connects us.

findings.highlight: You slept through all three periods!
findings.evidenceJa: この三限寝太郎
findings.explanation: 三限寝太郎 is a high-confidence parody of 三年寝太郎, the folkloric 'Three-Year Sleeper,' replacing 'year' with the university term for class period after Haruki sleeps through three classes. The translation conveys the bare event but deletes the recreatable allusive nickname.
findings.japanese:
「起きろ！
この三限寝太郎！」
findings.todokanai: "Wake up! You slept through all three periods!"

findings.highlight: they ended up unable to break away from those old facades
findings.evidenceJa: 最初は反動とか反抗とか反応待ちとかだったのに、いつの間にかライフワークに近くなってるような
findings.explanation: Takeya's conduct began as rebound, rebellion, and waiting for Io's reaction, then gradually became almost his life's work. The translation reduces the motives to jealousy and makes both people trapped in facades, deleting the progression of Takeya's behavior.
findings.japanese:
最初は反動とか反抗とか反応待ちとかだったのに、
いつの間にかライフワークに近くなってるような。
findings.todokanai: At first it was just his attempt to make her jealous and gain a reaction, but they ended up unable to break away from those old facades, no matter how many years it's been.

findings.highlight: I don't want him to cover for me either.
findings.evidenceJa: フォローもしてないけど
findings.explanation: Haruki admits that he has not followed up with or supported Setsuna. The translation instead says he does not want Takeya to cover for him, reversing both subject and relationship action.
findings.japanese: …フォローもしてないけど。
findings.todokanai: …I don't want him to cover for me either.

findings.highlight: If she were only upset because the article's worth less than the paper it's printed on, she probably wouldn't be having such an obviously irritated expression on her face right now.
findings.evidenceJa:
ただ単に記事がヘタクソでムカついてるだけなら、
こんなに心の底から悔しそうな顔するはずがない。
findings.explanation: A frustrated or rueful expression becomes irritation.
findings.japanese:
ただ単に記事がヘタクソでムカついてるだけなら、
こんなに心の底から悔しそうな顔するはずがない。
findings.todokanai: If she were only upset because the article's worth less than the paper it's printed on, she probably wouldn't be having such an obviously irritated expression on her face right now.

findings.highlight: I was completely incapable of thinking about her. Rather, I didn't want to think about her.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつのことを思ってなんて、全然なかった。逆だった。あいつのことを思いたくなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says his decision was not made out of consideration for Kazusa at all; the truth was the opposite—he did not want to think about her. The translation turns the first clause into cognitive incapacity and obscures the explicit contrast between altruistic consideration and avoidance.
findings.japanese:
あいつのことを思ってなんて、全然なかった。
逆だった。あいつのことを思いたくなかった。
findings.todokanai: I was completely incapable of thinking about her. Rather, I didn't want to think about her.

findings.highlight: I let my awful self that hurt the one I love get in the way of what I wanted to do…
findings.evidenceJa: 好きな人を傷つけて傷ついた最低な自分を、自分のやりたかった事にまで持ち込む
findings.explanation: Haruki indicts the awful self who was wounded by having wounded someone he loved, and for carrying that resulting self into the work he wanted to do. The translation omits his own hurt and flattens the reflexive emotional chain driving the sentence.
findings.japanese:
好きな人を傷つけて傷ついた最低な自分を、
自分のやりたかった事にまで持ち込むなんて。
findings.todokanai: To think I let my awful self that hurt the one I love get in the way of what I wanted to do…

findings.highlight: I'm actually not sure if I should be teaching you stuff like this.
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっと裏技っぽい操作だし…おいおい教えていければいいかなって
findings.explanation: Haruki says the operation is a little like a trick or workaround, so he thought he could teach it gradually or in due course. The translation instead says he is unsure whether he should teach it at all, changing the rationale behind Koharu's accusation that he withheld instruction.
findings.japanese:
「ちょっと裏技っぽい操作だし…
おいおい教えていければいいかなって」
findings.todokanai: "This technique's a bit of a cheat, so… I'm actually not sure if I should be teaching you stuff like this."

findings.highlight: whose reassuring message of "Just got up" let us breathe a sigh of relief.
findings.evidenceJa: 遅番のもう一人は、さっき電話で『今起きた』との頼もしい言葉を聞くことができた
findings.explanation: The absent evening-shift worker has only just woken up; 実に頼もしい is sarcastic. The translation takes the irony literally and invents relief, when the message actually confirms that staffing help is not arriving.
findings.japanese:
遅番のもう一人は、さっき電話で『今起きた』との
頼もしい言葉を聞くことができた。
findings.todokanai: We also got in touch with the other evening shift worker, whose reassuring message of "Just got up" let us breathe a sigh of relief.

findings.highlight: You even got incredibly popular over what happened with the Light Music Club.
findings.evidenceJa: 軽音楽同好会とか、色々出し抜いてくれた
findings.explanation: Tomo accuses Setsuna of outmaneuvering or upstaging her in several matters, including the Light Music Club. The translation changes Setsuna's action against Tomo into the unrelated fact of becoming popular.
findings.japanese:
「っ！
付属の頃のことは綺麗さっぱりですか？
軽音楽同好会とか、色々出し抜いてくれたくせに」
findings.todokanai: "…! Did you forget all about what happened back in high school? You even got incredibly popular over what happened with the Light Music Club."

findings.highlight: it wasn't an event I wanted to participate in anyway.
findings.evidenceJa: 元々わたしなんかが出られるイベントじゃない
findings.explanation: Setsuna says it was never an event someone like her could or should enter, expressing self-effacement or a sense of ineligibility. The translation substitutes lack of desire and removes the characterization driving her concession.
findings.japanese:
「それは…
元々わたしなんかが出られるイベントじゃないから」
findings.todokanai: "That's because… it wasn't an event I wanted to participate in anyway."

findings.highlight: I'll explain once we get away from these guys.
findings.evidenceJa: こいつらから逃げたきゃ話合わせて
findings.explanation: Shouko whispers, 'If you want to get away from these guys, play along.' The translation replaces the instruction Setsuna must follow with a promise that Shouko will explain later.
findings.japanese: 「こいつらから逃げたきゃ話合わせて」
findings.todokanai: "I'll explain once we get away from these guys."

findings.highlight: Economics Department, third year.
findings.evidenceJa: 商学部三年
findings.explanation: 商学部 is the faculty or department of commerce/business, not economics. The line gives Shouko's fabricated academic affiliation as a concrete identifying fact.
findings.japanese:
「長瀬晶子。商学部三年。
初めまして、小木曽雪菜さん」
findings.todokanai: "I'm Nagase Shouko. Economics Department, third year. Nice to meet you, Ogiso Setsuna-san."

findings.highlight: Parents being on some board of directors
findings.evidenceJa: 親が院長
findings.explanation: The partygoer's boast is that a parent is a hospital director or head physician. The translation changes that concrete status into parents sitting on an unspecified board of directors.
findings.japanese:
「ミス峰城ちゃんの言う通り、
自慢話ばっかりでうんざりしちゃって。
やれ親が院長だとか、フェラーリ何台持ってるとか」
findings.todokanai: "Just like that little Miss Houjou said, nobody could stop bragging about themselves. Parents being on some board of directors, owning however many Ferraris or whatever."

findings.highlight: An obnoxious meddler.
findings.evidenceJa: 救いがたいお人好し
findings.explanation: Koharu calls Haruki an incorrigibly good-natured soft touch or do-gooder after watching him help strangers and people he dislikes. 'Obnoxious meddler' deletes the altruistic judgment and turns the line into simple condemnation.
findings.japanese:
関係ない人間にまでお節介を焼き、
自分の嫌っている人間までも助けようとする、
救いがたいお人好し。
findings.todokanai: Worrying about complete strangers, and even going so far as to help out someone you hate. An obnoxious meddler.

findings.highlight: shouldn't I be able to understand just what it is that you want to do?
findings.evidenceJa: わたしが今、先輩にどうして欲しいのか、理解できる
findings.explanation: Koharu says Haruki should be able to understand what she wants him to do now. The translation makes Koharu the one understanding what Haruki wants to do, reversing both the knower and the person whose desire is at issue.
findings.japanese:
「だったら…
わたしが今、先輩にどうして欲しいのか、
理解できるんじゃないでしょうか？」
findings.todokanai: "Then if that's the case… shouldn't I be able to understand just what it is that you want to do?"

findings.highlight: I don't want to know someone I can't understand.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分にとって、わからない人でいて欲しくない
findings.explanation: Koharu does not want Haruki to remain someone she cannot understand. The translation instead says she does not want to know an incomprehensible person, nearly reversing her motive to become closer and understand him.
findings.japanese:
「先輩のことを知るためです。
自分にとって、わからない人でいて欲しくないから」
findings.todokanai: "Because I want to know more about you. I don't want to know someone I can't understand."

findings.highlight: her determination to get the truth out of me
findings.evidenceJa: そんな彼女の真意を問い質そうという思い
findings.explanation: This is Haruki's impulse to question Shouko about her true intention. The translation reverses subject and object, making Shouko determined to extract the truth from Haruki.
findings.japanese:
そんな彼女の真意を問い質そうという思いも、
これ以上干渉されたくないという迷いも、
全て、着信音にかき消された。
findings.todokanai: Be it her determination to get the truth out of me or my uncertain desire to stop her from prying, both dispersed with the arrival of my phone call.

findings.highlight: I love you too, but she's the only one for me!
findings.evidenceJa: お前のことも愛してる。けれど一番はあいつ
findings.explanation: The man says he loves Shouko too, but the other woman is number one. Calling the other woman 'the only one' contradicts the simultaneous love the first clause asserts and destroys the ranking on which Shouko's close-second joke depends.
findings.japanese:
「そしたら、『お前のことも愛してる。
けれど一番はあいつなんだ』だってさ～」
findings.todokanai: "And then he was all like, 'I love you too, but she's the only one for me!' seriously!"

findings.highlight: My eyes get a little fuzzy after a couple of drops slip in…
findings.evidenceJa: さっきから何滴か目に入ったせいで妙にしみる…
findings.explanation: Sweat getting into Haruki's eyes and stinging is rendered as his eyes becoming fuzzy.
findings.japanese: さっきから何滴か目に入ったせいで妙にしみる…
findings.todokanai: My eyes get a little fuzzy after a couple of drops slip in…

findings.highlight: Maybe the irritated tone in my voice as I said her name put her off or something, but after "Sugiura" makes her comment, she puts on her usual glare.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺の、負の感情をぶつけるときの
呼びにくさに配慮したのか、
“杉浦”は、そう言って、やっぱり睨みつけた。
findings.explanation: The narration's joke about dropping the honorific making Sugiura's name easier to say when venting negative emotion is replaced by a guess that Haruki's irritated tone put her off.
findings.japanese:
俺の、負の感情をぶつけるときの
呼びにくさに配慮したのか、
“杉浦”は、そう言って、やっぱり睨みつけた。
findings.todokanai: Maybe the irritated tone in my voice as I said her name put her off or something, but after "Sugiura" makes her comment, she puts on her usual glare.

findings.highlight: sounds rather convenient, although not exactly manly either, no?
findings.evidenceJa: 便利な男っぽくない？
findings.explanation: The question means, 'Doesn't that sound like a convenient/useful man?' The translation misparses っぽくない as a separate negative judgment about manliness and invents a contrast absent from the line.
findings.japanese:
「面倒見のいい人…？
なんかそういうのって、便利な男っぽくない？」
findings.todokanai: "Someone who likes to look out for other people…? Someone like that sounds rather convenient, although not exactly manly either, no?"

findings.highlight: Setsuna definitely made her way out of that party earlier.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は間違いなく、例のパーティには出てた
findings.explanation: Haruki concludes that Setsuna definitely attended or was present at the party. The translation says she made her way out of it, changing the fact that the witness has just established.
findings.japanese:
…てことは、雪菜は間違いなく、
例のパーティには出てたってことになる。
findings.todokanai: …Which means Setsuna definitely made her way out of that party earlier.

findings.highlight: Having seen yet another part of my past involving someone else
findings.evidenceJa: またしても別人の俺に遭遇した
findings.explanation: Koharu has once again encountered a different version of Haruki—the decisive, commanding Haruki he had concealed. The translation makes this merely another part of his past involving someone else, deleting the recurring multiplicity of Haruki's personas.
findings.japanese:
杉浦は、またしても別人の俺に遭遇したせいか、
なんだか戸惑ってるみたいだった。
findings.todokanai: Having seen yet another part of my past involving someone else, Sugiura seems to have fallen into a bit of a daze.

findings.highlight: For prioritizing what I requested and not giving me any more trouble.
findings.evidenceJa: 単にこっちのスピード重視のためだけに、余計な心配を掛けてしまったことを
findings.explanation: Haruki is apologizing inwardly for causing the manager needless worry solely because Haruki prioritized speed. The translation instead thanks or credits the manager for prioritizing the request and not causing Haruki trouble.
findings.japanese:
単にこっちのスピード重視のためだけに、
余計な心配を掛けてしまったことを。
findings.todokanai: For prioritizing what I requested and not giving me any more trouble.

findings.highlight: I have some past connections with a few of the girls, after all.
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと女の子の方にも裏取ったし
findings.explanation: Takeya says he properly corroborated the story with the women as well. The translation substitutes the fact that he has prior connections with some of them and loses the verification that makes his report credible.
findings.japanese:
「多分な。ちゃんと女の子の方にも裏取ったし。
…千佳が混ざってたのは地味にショックだったけど」
findings.todokanai: "Probably. I have some past connections with a few of the girls, after all. …Hearing Chika was there was quite a shock, though."

findings.highlight: Slipped away from that crazy high-class party
findings.evidenceJa: 付属出身者たちよりも更にブルジョアな連中とのパーティにうつつを抜かして
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines Setsuna losing herself in or being carried away by a party with people even more bourgeois than the University High alumni. The translation says she slipped away from the party, reversing her involvement in it.
findings.japanese:
自分は付属出身者たちよりも更にブルジョアな連中との
パーティにうつつを抜かして、友達と偶然会ったら、
今度は日付が変わるまで飲んで…
findings.todokanai: Slipped away from that crazy high-class party, ran into a friend, and is now drinking with her all the way past midnight…

findings.highlight: she left me a tiny sliver of a chance to hang on to.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつは俺に、可能性を残そうとしてたんだろう
findings.explanation: The antecedent is Takeya, who has just ended the call after urging Haruki to use this opportunity to speak to Setsuna. The translation assigns Takeya's attempt to preserve that possibility to an unidentified woman.
findings.japanese:
そんなふうに、ほとんどない可能性だってわかってて、
あいつは俺に、可能性を残そうとしてたんだろう。
findings.todokanai: Precisely because she knows how unlikely it is, she left me a tiny sliver of a chance to hang on to.

findings.highlight: apart from places like Onjuku, you'd hardly see another soul on the streets this late at night.
findings.evidenceJa: この御宿でなければ、もうアウトと言ってもいいくらいの時間帯
findings.explanation: Haruki says that if this were anywhere other than Onjuku, it would already be too late to catch the last train. The translation changes the transport fact into an observation about whether streets elsewhere would be deserted.
findings.japanese:
それどころか、この御宿でなければ、
もうアウトと言ってもいいくらいの時間帯。
findings.todokanai: Not to mention that, apart from places like Onjuku, you'd hardly see another soul on the streets this late at night.

findings.highlight: And yet, unable to make the same mental progress as her, I can only repeat my tired acts of sarcasm to Sugiura like I did before.
findings.evidenceJa:
なのに、そんな彼女の進歩に合わせられず、
まるでちょっと前の杉浦みたいな憎まれ口しか叩けない俺。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he can only produce spiteful remarks like the Sugiura of moments ago; the translation compares his present sarcasm toward Sugiura with his own former behavior.
findings.japanese:
なのに、そんな彼女の進歩に合わせられず、
まるでちょっと前の杉浦みたいな憎まれ口しか叩けない俺。
findings.todokanai: And yet, unable to make the same mental progress as her, I can only repeat my tired acts of sarcasm to Sugiura like I did before.

findings.highlight: She couldn't just stay exasperated in the face of all the troubles plaguing her mind. She couldn't just brush it all off saying, "This is just stupid."
findings.evidenceJa: そんな苦悩を、呆れることなんかできない。『馬鹿だな』って、言ってやれない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he cannot respond to Setsuna's anguish with exasperation or tell her she is foolish. The translation makes Setsuna herself unable to stay exasperated or dismiss her own troubles, reversing the experiencer and speaker.
findings.japanese:
そんな苦悩を、呆れることなんかできない。
『馬鹿だな』って、言ってやれない。
findings.todokanai: She couldn't just stay exasperated in the face of all the troubles plaguing her mind. She couldn't just brush it all off saying, "This is just stupid."

findings.highlight: stab at her heart.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜の温かくて愚かな気持ちが、心を抉る
findings.explanation: Setsuna's warm, foolish feelings gouge Haruki's heart in his narration. The translation makes those feelings wound Setsuna's own heart, reversing the emotional impact at the center of his self-indictment.
findings.japanese: 雪菜の温かくて愚かな気持ちが、心を抉る。
findings.todokanai: That caused Setsuna's own tender but foolish feelings to stab at her heart.

findings.highlight: Let go, already…
findings.evidenceJa: 早く、ふってよ
findings.explanation: ふって here means 'dump me' or 'reject me.' Setsuna is asking Haruki to end their suspended relationship, not asking him to release a physical hold.
findings.japanese: 「早く、ふってよ」
findings.todokanai: "Let go, already…"

findings.highlight: we need to start finalizing everything
findings.evidenceJa: 実はそろそろ出ないといけない時間
findings.explanation: Kazusa says it is nearly time for them to leave, despite still having time before the performance. The English instead says it is time to finalize everything, replacing an immediate physical departure with an unspecified production task.
findings.japanese:
「本番まではまだ少し余裕あるけど、
実はそろそろ出ないといけない時間」
findings.todokanai: "We still have some time before the live performance, but it's getting to the point where we need to start finalizing everything."

findings.highlight: applying to our department formally next year
findings.evidenceJa: 来年ウチ受けるって言ってる以上
findings.explanation: Mari says Haruki intends to apply to their company next year, so she is training him now. The English changes the target to their department, materially altering his employment plan and her reason for mentoring him.
findings.japanese:
「来年ウチ受けるって言ってる以上、
今のうちから鍛えておかないと」
findings.todokanai: "He said he'd be applying to our department formally next year, so I'm using this as an opportunity to prepare him."

findings.highlight: dub some voices over it
findings.evidenceJa: 諏訪までダビングしろとか言ってきたし
findings.explanation: Suwa asked for a duplicate or dub copy of the festival recording. The English says he asked to record voices over it, inventing a creative voice-dubbing task rather than copying the video.
findings.japanese:
「例の『開桜グラフ』が出てからお前らで５組目だよ。
諏訪までダビングしろとか言ってきたし」
findings.todokanai: "You're already the fifth bunch to come to me after that Kaiou Graph article. Suwa even told me to dub some voices over it."

findings.highlight: looking at others from a distance as if he were a complete stranger
findings.evidenceJa: 他人事みたいに自分を遠くから見てて
findings.explanation: Koharu says Haruki steps back and watches himself from afar as though his own life were someone else's affair. The English instead has him watch other people from a distance, deleting the self-alienation at the center of her diagnosis.
findings.japanese:
「一歩退いて、他人事みたいに自分を遠くから見てて、
人の心が近づくのを極端に恐れる、冷血動物だよ」
findings.todokanai: "He's always removed, looking at others from a distance as if he were a complete stranger, absolutely terrified of getting close… A cold-blooded animal…"

findings.highlight: Is the person I saw in the music room back then…
findings.evidenceJa: あの時の、音楽室の、あいつだよ
findings.explanation: Koharu concludes that the person on the recording is the same Haruki she saw in the music room. The English leaves an unfinished question and never states the recognition that reconciles his apparently different selves.
findings.japanese: 「あの時の、音楽室の、あいつだよ…」
findings.todokanai: "Is the person I saw in the music room back then…"

findings.highlight: almost the whole day
findings.evidenceJa: 丸一日以上
findings.explanation: The manuscript had not advanced a line for more than a full day before being completed in one hour. “Almost the whole day” reverses the boundary and weakens the deliberate more-than-a-day versus one-hour contrast.
findings.japanese:
丸一日以上、机の前で唸っても、
一行も進まなかった原稿が、
たったの一時間で仕上がってしまった。
findings.todokanai: I finally finished the manuscript that had me groaning in front of my desk because of how I've been incapable of progressing with it for almost the whole day, and it took me only an hour.

findings.highlight: I remembered everythingーhow she never opened her heart to anyone, her status as a prodigy of the music program, how she struggled with the regular curriculum, how she was usually irritable but mellowed out eventually, and how she was frank, yet not so honest after all…
findings.evidenceJa:
誰にも心を開かなかった、音楽科の天才にして、
普通科の落ちこぼれが、怒ったり、黄昏れたり、
素直になったり、素直じゃなかったり…
findings.explanation: The source lists Kazusa getting angry, brooding, becoming honest, and being dishonest; the English turns part of that sequence into a stable irritable personality that later mellowed.
findings.japanese:
誰にも心を開かなかった、音楽科の天才にして、
普通科の落ちこぼれが、怒ったり、黄昏れたり、
素直になったり、素直じゃなかったり…
findings.todokanai: I remembered everythingーhow she never opened her heart to anyone, her status as a prodigy of the music program, how she struggled with the regular curriculum, how she was usually irritable but mellowed out eventually, and how she was frank, yet not so honest after all…

findings.highlight: I have no intention of worrying
findings.evidenceJa: 考えるのも億劫になってきた
findings.explanation: Haruki has become too exhausted even to think about his guilt and satisfaction. The English makes this a deliberate refusal or lack of intention to worry, replacing depletion with volitional avoidance.
findings.japanese:
けどもう、そんな罪悪感も満足感も、
考えるのも億劫になってきた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, I have no intention of worrying about either my guilt or my satisfaction.

findings.highlight: Do I really have to say it?
findings.evidenceJa: 言ってもいいのか？
findings.explanation: Mari asks whether she may say what she is about to say, seeking permission to cross a personal boundary. The English asks whether she is obligated to say it, reversing permission into reluctant compulsion.
findings.japanese: 「言ってもいいのか？」
findings.todokanai: "Do I really have to say it?"

findings.highlight: Trying to exhaust yourself on a mental level
findings.evidenceJa: 精神的自滅願望がある
findings.explanation: Mari diagnoses Haruki as seeming to possess a wish for psychological self-destruction, concealed by his extreme conventionality. The English reduces this to trying to tire himself mentally, removing the ruinous desire that gives her intervention its force.
findings.japanese:
「精神的自滅願望がある…ような気がする。
けど、過剰なまでの常識人としての資質が、
そういうとこを覆い隠してる」
findings.todokanai: "Trying to exhaust yourself on a mental level… is what I think you're doing. But deep down, your values and morals as a human being overshadow it."

findings.highlight: "So basically… I'm looking to mentally suffocate myself, but because of my naturally serious and careful personality, I'm incapable of actually pulling the trigger?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「要するに…心の中では破滅を望んでるけど、
元々が真面目だからなかなか踏み切れない、と」
findings.explanation: Haruki's inward wish for ruin becomes an effort to mentally suffocate himself.
findings.japanese:
「要するに…心の中では破滅を望んでるけど、
元々が真面目だからなかなか踏み切れない、と」
findings.todokanai: "So basically… I'm looking to mentally suffocate myself, but because of my naturally serious and careful personality, I'm incapable of actually pulling the trigger?"

findings.highlight: didn't really end up being the main issue
findings.evidenceJa: 障害にすらならなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says Kazusa's current circumstances were not even an obstacle for him. The English merely says they were not the main issue, leaving them as a possible secondary obstacle and weakening his correction of Mari's simple account.
findings.japanese:
いや、そもそもあいつの今の境遇なんか、
俺にとって障害にすらならなかった。
findings.todokanai: You could even say that her current circumstances didn't really end up being the main issue for me here.

findings.highlight: It doesn't seem like she realizes that herself, either.
findings.evidenceJa: その時はまだ、自分でも意識してなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that at the time he himself had not yet realized he had found two important keywords in Mari's speech. The English assigns the lack of realization to Mari, reversing whose latent insight the narration tracks.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんの言葉の中に、
二つ気になるキーワードを見つけたことを、
その時はまだ、自分でも意識してなかった。
findings.todokanai: Mari-san's words just now carried two important bits of information. It doesn't seem like she realizes that herself, either.

findings.highlight: "Of course not. I'll gratefully accept it… Though I don't really see myself treasuring it that much."
findings.evidenceJa:
「まさか。
ありがたく頂きますよ。
…あまり何度も見たりはしないですが」
findings.explanation: Haruki says he will not look at the souvenir many times; the English says he will not treasure it very much.
findings.japanese:
「まさか。
ありがたく頂きますよ。
…あまり何度も見たりはしないですが」
findings.todokanai: "Of course not. I'll gratefully accept it… Though I don't really see myself treasuring it that much."

findings.highlight: now and then
findings.evidenceJa: 時々どころか、いつも妙に人間くさい
findings.explanation: Haruki says Mari is strangely human not merely sometimes but always. The English says she shows a human side only now and then, reversing the explicit frequency correction and weakening his affectionate reassessment of her.
findings.japanese:
ただのバイトに、こんな熱い説教をかましたり、
本当に何というか、仕事魔人のくせに、
時々どころか、いつも妙に人間くさい人で…
findings.todokanai: To think she'd give such a passionate talk to a part-timer. How should I put it? Despite her workaholic nature, she still does show a certain human side of her now and then…

findings.highlight: above all, loud
findings.evidenceJa: 熱くて青くて…響く言葉
findings.explanation: Mari leaves him with words that are passionate, youthful or green, and resonant—words that continue to echo in him. The English calls them loud, turning emotional resonance into simple volume.
findings.japanese:
最後に、多分今ごろもの凄く後悔しているであろう、
熱くて青くて…響く言葉を伝えてくれた。
findings.todokanai: At the last moment, she says something she's probably regretting right about now. Passionate, full of youth, and above all, loud.

findings.highlight: graduate this year
findings.evidenceJa: 進級はなんとかなりそうだけど
findings.explanation: Haruki says two more sessions should finish the paper and allow Chiaki to advance to the next year, then asks what she will do as a fourth-year student. The English says she can graduate this year, contradicting the immediately stated next-year status.
findings.japanese:
「レポートはあと２回くらいで終わりそうだから、
進級はなんとかなりそうだけど...
和泉、お前四年になったらどうするつもりなんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "From the looks of it, we can finish up the paper in just two more sessions, so you should be able to graduate this year… Still, Izumi, how do you even plan to get through the fourth year?"

findings.highlight: Even two days ago… no, even if she were to have brought this out last night, I probably wouldn't have been able to understand her then either.
findings.evidenceJa:
そんな二日前...
いや、昨夜までの俺を持ち出されても、
こいつの言いたいことなんか理解できるはずもない。
findings.explanation: The temporal perspective around confronting the self from two days ago or last night is rearranged into Chiaki bringing something out last night.
findings.japanese:
そんな二日前...
いや、昨夜までの俺を持ち出されても、
こいつの言いたいことなんか理解できるはずもない。
findings.todokanai: Even two days ago… no, even if she were to have brought this out last night, I probably wouldn't have been able to understand her then either.

findings.highlight: made the organizer give you everyone's contact information
findings.evidenceJa: 幹事さんは全員に連絡取らされるし
findings.explanation: Koharu says Haruki made the organizer contact everyone while searching for Setsuna. The English instead says the organizer gave Haruki everyone's contact information, changing both the action and direction of information flow.
findings.japanese:
「パーティ会場のお店の人は脅されるし、
幹事さんは全員に連絡取らされるし、
挙げ句の果てにお友達まで巻き込んで...」
findings.todokanai: "Not only did you threaten the manager at where the party was hosted, but you also made the organizer give you everyone's contact information, and you even dragged your friend into it at the end…"

findings.highlight: I don't think I do
findings.evidenceJa: 自分でもそう思いますけど
findings.explanation: Koharu agrees that she herself thinks she is meddling, but says she could not remain silent this time. The English makes her deny that self-assessment, reversing the concession that frames her intervention.
findings.japanese:
「自分でもそう思いますけど...
今度ばかりは黙っていられなかったんです」
findings.todokanai: "I don't think I do, but… It's just that I can't stay quiet this time."

findings.highlight: regret your decision so much
findings.evidenceJa: そんなに未練たらたらでいながら
findings.explanation: Koharu says Haruki remains full of lingering attachment to Setsuna. The English recasts that attachment as regret over a decision, supplying a specific past choice and losing the ongoing love that motivates her demand not to give up.
findings.japanese:
「そんなに未練たらたらでいながら、
彼女のこと諦めるなんて納得できません！
今別れてしまったら、絶対に駄目です！」
findings.todokanai: "Since you regret your decision so much, I won't allow you to leave her! I definitely won't allow you two to break up now!"

findings.highlight: it would only cause us more pain and confusion over time
findings.evidenceJa: 余計に辛すぎて、どうしたらいいかわかりません
findings.explanation: Koharu projects herself into Setsuna's position and says she personally would find it unbearably painful and would not know what to do. The English turns this into a mutual long-term prognosis about “us,” changing a direct empathetic self-test into relationship forecasting.
findings.japanese:
「しかも相手が、本当は自分のことを
まだ好きでいてくれるなんて知ってたら、
余計に辛すぎて、どうしたらいいかわかりません」
findings.todokanai: "Especially if I knew that that person still liked me and that it would only cause us more pain and confusion over time."

findings.highlight: I'd probably lose my temper
findings.evidenceJa: おそらく他人が同じ事を言ったら、もの凄い勢いで噛みつくんだろうな
findings.explanation: Haruki observes that if anyone else said the same thing, Koharu would snap furiously at that person. The English makes Haruki himself the one who would lose his temper, erasing his characterization of Koharu's selective response to him.
findings.japanese:
おそらく他人が同じ事を言ったら、
もの凄い勢いで噛みつくんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: If someone else were to tell me the same thing, I'd probably lose my temper and argue back.

findings.highlight: If you keep doing that, you could cause some serious misunderstandings!
findings.evidenceJa: ついこの間、致命的な行き違いを誘発したばかりだろ
findings.explanation: Haruki reminds Chiaki that this exact prank just recently caused a disastrous misunderstanding. The English changes the concrete past consequence into a hypothetical future risk, deleting the callback to the phone incident.
findings.japanese:
「っ...くだらないイタズラはやめんか！
ついこの間、致命的な行き違いを誘発したばかりだろ」
findings.todokanai: "Ugh… Don't play stupid pranks like that! If you keep doing that, you could cause some serious misunderstandings!"

findings.highlight: I've been telling you that I forgot about the original deadline
findings.evidenceJa: 今までそう言ってきたせいで、とっくに締め切り過ぎてて今度が最終期限
findings.explanation: Haruki explains that because the procrastinating excuse has kept being used, Chiaki's deadline passed long ago and the new one is final. The English has Haruki claim that he repeatedly told Takeya he forgot his own deadline, breaking the concealed-subject joke sustained by the following narration.
findings.japanese:
「今までそう言ってきたせいで、
とっくに締め切り過ぎてて今度が最終期限なんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "I've been telling you that I forgot about the original deadline and missed it, so this is my final chance."

findings.highlight: called Mermaid
findings.evidenceJa: 駅前の『半魚人』という
findings.explanation: The establishment is explicitly named 『半魚人』, literally a merman or half-fish person. “Mermaid” changes the named venue's creature and gendered image rather than preserving or neutrally representing the proper name; the exact release spelling remains an editorial naming decision.
findings.japanese:
「一時間だけ飲むつもりならお薦めの場所があるぞ。
駅前の『半魚人』という...」
findings.todokanai: "If you only want to drink for an hour, I know just the spot. There's this place called Mermaid right in front of the station…"

findings.highlight: isn't she here for the same reason
findings.evidenceJa: 和泉が今、この場所を去ろうとするのも、結局、あいつらとまるで同じ理由
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes Chiaki is leaving for the same reason Takeya and Io tried to come: concern for him. The English asks whether she is here for that reason, replacing the self-sacrificing departure that prompts his realization with her presence.
findings.japanese:
和泉が今、この場所を去ろうとするのも、
結局、あいつらとまるで同じ理由なんじゃないかって...
findings.todokanai: And that's why Izumi has to leave, but isn't she here for the same reason…?

findings.highlight: I'd really like that person.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなあたしのワガママを、一生懸命頑張って叶えてくれる人が好き。大好き
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she likes—loves—the person who works hard to grant her selfish wishes, escalating a present declaration in Haruki's face. The English turns it into a hypothetical preference, “I'd really like that person,” weakening the scene's deliberate apparent confession.
findings.japanese:
「そんなあたしのワガママを、
一生懸命頑張って叶えてくれる人が好き。大好き」
findings.todokanai: "Someone who'd do everything in his power to grant my selfish little wishes. I'd really like that person."

findings.highlight: treat myself to a crappy reward
findings.evidenceJa: 自分をも巻き込んだ嫌がらせの賜物か
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether the repeated curry is the fruit of harassment or spite that also catches himself in it. The English calls it a bad reward he gives himself, reversing self-directed collateral punishment into self-treatment.
findings.japanese:
これもレパートリーのなさによるものか、
自分をも巻き込んだ嫌がらせの賜物か。
findings.todokanai: I wonder if it's because my cooking repertoire is limited or if I just want to treat myself to a crappy reward.

findings.highlight: she read the atmosphere
findings.evidenceJa: 空気を読んだ...というか読み過ぎた武也が
findings.explanation: Takeya reads—or overreads—the atmosphere and immediately elbows Io. The English initially assigns the social perception to Io and only then says Takeya elbowed her, losing the narrator's comic correction about Takeya's excessive vigilance.
findings.japanese:
空気を読んだ...というか読み過ぎた武也が、
即座に依緒を肘でつつく。
findings.todokanai: And she read the atmosphere… Or rather, she got promptly elbowed by the overreacting Takeya who was sitting next to her.

findings.highlight: making you remember all that was a mistake
findings.evidenceJa: とお前に思わせたことがそもそも失敗
findings.explanation: Takeya says the original failure was making Haruki think changing departments without consulting them was Haruki's own wrongdoing. The English says merely reminding him of the event was a mistake, deleting Takeya's attempt to lift Haruki's blame.
findings.japanese: 「...とお前に思わせたことがそもそも失敗なわけ」
findings.todokanai: "…Well, making you remember all that was a mistake to begin with."

findings.highlight: Here, Rokku.
findings.evidenceJa: ほれ、ロック
findings.explanation: In the drinking sequence, ロック refers to a drink served on the rocks. The English transliterates it as the apparent name “Rokku,” producing a meaningless address and obscuring the friends' casual coordination over drinks and snacks.
findings.japanese: 「...ほれ、ロック」
findings.todokanai: "…Here, Rokku."

findings.highlight: "Make sure the AC is on stronger. While you're at it, set the humidifier to its maximum."
findings.evidenceJa:
「その代わりエアコンだけは強くしといて。
ついでに加湿器があると最高」
findings.explanation: A humidifier that would be ideal if present becomes an existing humidifier to set to maximum.
findings.japanese:
「その代わりエアコンだけは強くしといて。
ついでに加湿器があると最高」
findings.todokanai: "Make sure the AC is on stronger. While you're at it, set the humidifier to its maximum."

findings.highlight: hasn't changed at all since the old days
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たち三人の強さは、昔から結構トントンだった
findings.explanation: Haruki says the three friends' alcohol tolerances had always been roughly equal. The English instead says their tolerance has not changed over time, losing the three-way equality that the next line says a fourth person would disrupt.
findings.japanese: 俺たち三人の強さは、昔から結構トントンだった。
findings.todokanai: Between the three of us, our alcohol tolerance hasn't changed at all since the old days.

findings.highlight: both of us are eagerly waiting for the other
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は依緒が口火を切るのを、依緒は自分が口火を切るのを
findings.explanation: Haruki waits for Io to break the silence, while Io also waits for herself to do so; both know Io must begin. The English turns this into each waiting for the other, reversing the asymmetrical pressure that leads directly to Io speaking.
findings.japanese:
俺は依緒が口火を切るのを、
依緒は自分が口火を切るのを、
きっと、今か今かと待っていた。
findings.todokanai: I'm sure the both of us are eagerly waiting for the other to get the ball rolling.

findings.highlight: During the past few days, so many people checked up on me, I can't afford to stay depressed any longer.
findings.evidenceJa:
ここ数日で、色んな人たちの介入を受けて、
深く思い悩む暇もなかった。
findings.explanation: Having had no time to brood deeply becomes being unable to afford staying depressed any longer.
findings.japanese:
ここ数日で、色んな人たちの介入を受けて、
深く思い悩む暇もなかった。
findings.todokanai: During the past few days, so many people checked up on me, I can't afford to stay depressed any longer.

findings.highlight: It's 3 AM… Wednesday.
findings.evidenceJa: 今はもう、夜中の３時。...つまり水曜２７時
findings.explanation: The source deliberately renames 3 a.m. as Wednesday 27:00, extending the prior day into the special shared hour that motivates Haruki's renewed contact with Setsuna. The English reduces this to ordinary Wednesday and deletes the scene's organizing time motif.
findings.japanese:
今はもう、夜中の３時。
...つまり水曜２７時。
findings.todokanai: It's 3 AM… Wednesday.

findings.highlight: This is completely irrelevant
findings.evidenceJa: なんて当たり障りのない
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines his friends calling the message bland, safe, or noncommittal. The English calls it completely irrelevant, replacing criticism of his emotional caution with a claim that its content has no relevance.
findings.japanese:
『なんて当たり障りのない』とか、
『もっと伝えるべき事があるだろ』とか、
『お前こそ中学生か』とか。
findings.todokanai: Things like "This is completely irrelevant", or "There are more important things you should tell her", or "Are you a middle schooler or something?"

findings.highlight: You're biting the hand that's feeding you.
findings.evidenceJa: それって逆恨みだよ
findings.explanation: Sayuri tells Mihoko that she is directing unjustified resentment at Koharu. The English accuses her of betraying a benefactor, inventing a dependence or favor relationship rather than identifying misplaced blame.
findings.japanese:
「いい加減にしときなよ矢田。
それって逆恨みだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Stop being unreasonable, Yada. You're biting the hand that's feeding you."

findings.highlight: I have the morning shift at Goodies with Sugiura on Saturday and Sunday.
findings.evidenceJa: 今週土曜日は、杉浦がグッディーズの早番。日曜も同様
findings.explanation: Haruki's schedule calculation says Sugiura has the early Goodies shift on both Saturday and Sunday. The English says Haruki has those shifts with her, assigning him work he is merely considering visiting around.
findings.japanese:
毎週金曜日は、開桜社のバイト。
今週土曜日は、杉浦がグッディーズの早番。
日曜も同様。
findings.todokanai: I have part-time work at Kaiou Graph tonight. And I have the morning shift at Goodies with Sugiura on Saturday and Sunday.

findings.highlight: They've been rushing me on this since yesterday!
findings.evidenceJa: こっちは本当は昨日がデッドだった
findings.explanation: Hamada admits his real deadline was yesterday. The English instead says other people have been rushing him since yesterday, deleting the fact that his assignment is already overdue.
findings.japanese:
「何ぃ？　お前上司に向かって生意気だぞ！
こっちは本当は昨日がデッドだったんだからな！」
findings.todokanai: "What's that? Is that the kind of attitude you should have when talking to your superior!? They've been rushing me on this since yesterday!"

findings.highlight: a speech that could lead to a huge misunderstanding
findings.evidenceJa: 勘違いも甚だしい発言だったかも
findings.explanation: Mari regrets that her encouragement may itself have been founded on a severe misunderstanding of Haruki. The English says her speech might cause someone else to misunderstand, reversing whether misunderstanding produced or resulted from the statement.
findings.japanese:
「その、偉そうだった上に、
勘違いも甚だしい発言だったかもと、
その後反省しきりで...」
findings.todokanai: "About… me acting all high and mighty, and making a speech that could lead to a huge misunderstanding. I thought about that afterward…"

findings.highlight: it feels very awkward to talk about it
findings.evidenceJa: なんとなく言わずにはおれなかった
findings.explanation: Mari says several things overlapped with her own experience, so she somehow could not help saying the advice. The English says the overlap made it awkward to talk, reversing an irresistible impulse to speak into reluctance.
findings.japanese:
「ちょっと色々オーバーラップするところがあって、
なんとなく言わずにはおれなかったというか...」
findings.todokanai: "Since there are so many coincidences overlapping, it feels very awkward to talk about it…"

findings.highlight: what does she mean?
findings.evidenceJa: まだって何だ
findings.explanation: After thinking he cannot ask such an intrusive question “yet,” Haruki catches and questions his own use of “yet.” The English makes him wonder what Mari means, assigning his revealing self-correction to her.
findings.japanese: ...まだって何だ。
findings.todokanai: …But what does she mean?

findings.highlight: the gentle winter sun finally came to melt it once and for all
findings.evidenceJa: そこにまた、冬の優しい日射しが降り注いでくれたから
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines gentle winter sunlight falling again on snow that thawed and then refroze harder; the line does not say it has now melted. The English declares it melted once and for all, converting tentative renewed warmth into completed permanent healing.
findings.japanese:
解けかけた雪が夜に凍結し、
前よりも固く凍りついてしまったけれど、
そこにまた、冬の優しい日射しが降り注いでくれたから？
findings.todokanai: Is it because the terrible cold of night revitalized the snow which was on the verge of finally melting, forming ice even colder than before, but then the gentle winter sun finally came to melt it once and for all?

findings.highlight: I've moved on already.
findings.evidenceJa: もう終わったことだって言いましたよね
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats that the relationship or event is over, a claim the surrounding chapter distinguishes from its emotional aftermath. “I've moved on” asserts inner resolution that his narration and continued pain explicitly do not support.
findings.japanese:
「いいですよ、そんなに気を使わなくて。
もう終わったことだって言いましたよね」
findings.todokanai: "It's fine, don't worry about it. Like I said before, I've moved on already."

findings.highlight: thinking about making this amazing burger
findings.evidenceJa: 超絶バーガー頼むこともある
findings.explanation: Mari says she sometimes splurges by ordering the Superlative Burger, whose drawback is how long it takes to arrive. The English says she is thinking of making an amazing burger and that cooking it takes too long, changing takeout or service into home preparation.
findings.japanese:
「最近はちょっと贅沢に
超絶バーガー頼むこともあるけど、
あれ、出てくるのに時間かかるのが難点ね」
findings.todokanai: "I was thinking about making this amazing burger lately, but the problem with making it is that it would take too much time…"

findings.highlight: She's swaying left and right.
findings.evidenceJa: 左右にブレてきたわね
findings.explanation: At the batting center, Sawako says Mari's hits are beginning to scatter left and right, evidence that she is nearing her limit. The English says Mari's body is swaying, replacing declining batting accuracy with physical instability.
findings.japanese:
「左右にブレてきたわね。
そろそろ限界じゃない？」
findings.todokanai: "She's swaying left and right. Are you at your limit already?"

findings.highlight: "She's a good person. Even though I hate to admit it. She's a very cute woman. Just a little stubborn. So promise not to abandon her?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「あいつ、いい奴なのよ。むかつくけど。
可愛い女なのよ。やってられないけど。
だから、捨てないでやってね？」
findings.explanation: Sawako's “I can't stand it” aside becomes “just a little stubborn,” changing her affectionate complaint into a trait assigned to Mari.
findings.japanese:
「あいつ、いい奴なのよ。むかつくけど。
可愛い女なのよ。やってられないけど。
だから、捨てないでやってね？」
findings.todokanai: "She's a good person. Even though I hate to admit it. She's a very cute woman. Just a little stubborn. So promise not to abandon her?"

findings.highlight: shows that she's interested in this topic
findings.evidenceJa: あからさまに面白くなさそうな表情
findings.explanation: Sawako listens with an openly displeased or unamused expression and seems unwilling to accept Haruki's account. The English says her face shows interest, reversing the affect that motivates her argumentative refusal.
findings.japanese:
雨宮さんは、あからさまに面白くなさそうな表情で、
俺の話す事実を受け入れがたそうに聞いている。
findings.todokanai: Amamiya-san's expression shows that she's interested in this topic, but she doesn't seem to believe what I'm telling her.

findings.highlight: Mari chose you
findings.evidenceJa: その上で麻理はあなたを選ぶと思う
findings.explanation: Sawako says she thinks Mari would choose Haruki even after taking age and character into account. The English makes that hypothetical judgment a completed past choice, prematurely confirming the romance Haruki is denying.
findings.japanese:
「もちろんその通りよ。
その上で麻理はあなたを選ぶと思うんだけどなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Well, of course, that's exactly right. But I still think Mari chose you because she sees more in you beyond that."

findings.highlight: given the fact that she's walking alone
findings.evidenceJa: 足取りとか見てると、ちっとも酔ってるようには見えない
findings.explanation: Haruki judges from Mari's gait that she does not look drunk at all. The English says this is because she is walking alone, replacing the observed steadiness of her steps with an irrelevant social fact.
findings.japanese:
足取りとか見てると、
ちっとも酔ってるようには見えないけどな。
findings.todokanai: But given the fact that she's walking alone, I wouldn't be able to tell if she's drunk at all.

findings.highlight: we'll probably feel really awkward if she still remembers
findings.evidenceJa: 今度は今日のことを思い出して、気まずい思いを抱えてそうだ
