findings.explanation: Haruki predicts that when sober Mari next sees him, she will remember today's behavior and carry embarrassment. The English turns this into mutual awkwardness conditional on whether she remembers, changing both subject and certainty.
findings.japanese:
これでまた素面の時に顔を合わせたら、
今度は今日のことを思い出して、
気まずい思いを抱えてそうだ。
findings.todokanai: At this rate, when we see each other next time, we'll probably feel really awkward if she still remembers what happened today.

findings.highlight: I couldn't understand the hidden messages
findings.evidenceJa: 親友同士の認識の溝は埋まらず
findings.explanation: The unresolved gap is between the two best friends' interpretations of which woman became carried away. The English instead says Haruki failed to understand hidden messages, relocating the disagreement into his private comprehension.
findings.japanese: 結局、親友同士の認識の溝は埋まらずか。
findings.todokanai: As a result, I couldn't understand the hidden messages between these two best friends after all.

findings.highlight: 30 minutes away from the station
findings.evidenceJa: 始発まであと３０分
findings.explanation: Haruki says there are about thirty minutes until the first train. The English says they are thirty minutes away from the station, turning a waiting time into travel distance and obscuring why Mari chooses a taxi.
findings.japanese: 「始発まであと３０分くらいありますけど？」
findings.todokanai: "Aren't we still 30 minutes away from the station?"

findings.highlight: Suzuki sent me a text earlier
findings.evidenceJa: さっき鈴木にメール入れたら、元気な泣き言が返ってきた
findings.explanation: Mari says she texted Suzuki and received an energetic complaint in reply. The English says Suzuki initiated the earlier text, reversing who contacted whom as Mari decides to return and help the office.
findings.japanese:
「さっき鈴木にメール入れたら、
元気な泣き言が返ってきたからね」
findings.todokanai: "Suzuki sent me a text earlier, she's practically crying for me to come back and help."

findings.highlight: You don't really think of it as anything special yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が偉いわけじゃないのに、自慢するのって、おかしいよね
findings.explanation: Setsuna calls it odd for her to boast because she herself is not the person whose achievement makes Haruki admirable. The English says Haruki does not regard his own behavior as special, transferring her self-effacing concern to his self-evaluation.
findings.japanese:
『なんてね。
自分が偉いわけじゃないのに、
自慢するのって、おかしいよね…』
findings.todokanai: "Just kidding. You don't really think of it as anything special yourself, so me being proud sounds kinda weird, doesn't it…?"

findings.highlight: I'll text you again after your paper's done.
findings.evidenceJa: レポート終わったらまたメールしてね
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks Haruki to email her once the paper is finished. The English says she will text him again afterward, reversing who is expected to initiate the completion report and weakening her request for continued contact.
findings.japanese:
『それじゃ、頑張って。
レポート終わったらまたメールしてね』
findings.todokanai: "Anyway, I'll be cheering you on. I'll text you again after your paper's done."

findings.highlight: "I think both suit you just fine."
findings.evidenceJa: 「どっちも充足するっちゃぁするだろ」
findings.explanation: Haruki says the toilet could satisfy either proposed urge, while the English says both options suit Chiaki.
findings.japanese: 「どっちも充足するっちゃぁするだろ」
findings.todokanai: "I think both suit you just fine."

findings.highlight: Are you that interested in me?
findings.evidenceJa: 惚れた弱みって言うか
findings.explanation: Chiaki explicitly teases that Haruki's knowledge of her may be the weakness of having fallen in love. The English reduces this to mere interest, removing the romantic proposition Haruki is being baited to confront.
findings.japanese:
「やだな～もう。
どこまであたしのことわかっちゃってんのよ春希～。
もうなんての？　惚れた弱みって言うか？」
findings.todokanai: "Oh, come on～! You know so much about me already, Haruki～ What's this? Are you that interested in me?"

findings.highlight: report the progress of my paper
findings.evidenceJa: レポートの顛末は、日付が変わる前に伝えないと
findings.explanation: Haruki must report how Chiaki's paper turned out before midnight because Setsuna is waiting for news. The English calls it his paper, erasing the very reason he has lied about still working and obscuring the betrayal he recognizes in the next lines.
findings.japanese:
『あまり遅くまで待つな』って
前のメールに書いてしまった以上、
レポートの顛末は、日付が変わる前に伝えないと。
findings.todokanai: Since I told her to not stay up too late, I should at least report the progress of my paper to her before the date changes.

findings.highlight: Every time we get together, they start arguing
findings.evidenceJa: 親同士がさ、あたしの目の前で、顔を合わせるたびキッツい喧嘩をしてた時は
findings.explanation: Chiaki recalls the period when her parents fought whenever they met and says she also sympathized with this side—her mother. The English makes the fights present and recurring whenever “we” meet, then says she sometimes feels sorry for both parents, changing time and referent.
findings.japanese:
「親同士がさ、あたしの目の前で、
顔を合わせるたびキッツい喧嘩をしてた時は、
そりゃ、嫌な気分だったけど、こっち側に同情もしてた」
findings.todokanai: "Every time we get together, they start arguing like crazy right in front of my eyes. It does get annoying, but sometimes I actually feel sorry for them."

findings.highlight: When will I finally be able to put those broken fragments of my memories back together again, I wonder…?
findings.evidenceJa:
あの時に散らばってしまった想いの欠片、
いつか拾い集めること、できるんだろうか…
findings.explanation: Fragments of feelings scattered three years ago become fragments of memories.
findings.japanese:
あの時に散らばってしまった想いの欠片、
いつか拾い集めること、できるんだろうか…
findings.todokanai: When will I finally be able to put those broken fragments of my memories back together again, I wonder…?

findings.highlight: felt utterly superficial
findings.evidenceJa: 『貴重な無駄だったね』という一言を、俺はいつか、実感することができるのかな
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether he will someday be able to feel the truth of Chiaki's smiling description, “a valuable waste.” The English declares her words utterly superficial, inventing a dismissive judgment that reverses his tentative hope of understanding them.
findings.japanese:
別れ際、あいつがにっこりと笑って言った
『貴重な無駄だったね』という一言を、
俺はいつか、実感することができるのかな。
findings.todokanai: Her cheerful parting words of "what a valuable waste of time that was" felt utterly superficial. I wonder if I'll ever be able to feel the same way?

findings.highlight: You sent me a text yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日着信くれたでしょ
findings.explanation: Chiaki returns a call her mother placed yesterday; 着信 denotes the incoming or missed call. The English says her mother sent a text, changing the communication event as their relationship begins to soften.
findings.japanese:
「あ、母さん？
昨日着信くれたでしょ？　何？」
findings.todokanai: "Hey, Mom? You sent me a text yesterday, right? What's up?"

findings.highlight: "Ah, my brother yelled at me just now. I guess it's a bad idea to light a few celebratory firecrackers when it's already past midnight."
findings.evidenceJa:
『あ、今、弟に怒鳴られちゃった。
０時過ぎにクラッカーはまずかったみたい』
findings.explanation: A celebratory party popper becomes several firecrackers.
findings.japanese:
『あ、今、弟に怒鳴られちゃった。
０時過ぎにクラッカーはまずかったみたい』
findings.todokanai: "Ah, my brother yelled at me just now. I guess it's a bad idea to light a few celebratory firecrackers when it's already past midnight."

findings.highlight: I don't have an answer to that question
findings.evidenceJa: 質問に対する返答がまだ
findings.explanation: Drunk Setsuna tells “Professor” Haruki that his response to her question is still missing. The English says she herself lacks an answer, reversing who owes whom a reply in their flirtatious exchange about his winter plans.
findings.japanese:
『せんせ～
質問に対する返答がまだで～す』
findings.todokanai: "Sorry, Professor～! I don't have an answer to that question yeeet～"

findings.highlight: "…Still, I know you'll just see through others' requests to the very end no matter what I say, won't you, Haruki-kun?"
findings.evidenceJa:
『…なんて言っても、
頼まれたらやめられないのが春希くんだよね』
findings.explanation: Haruki being unable to refuse when asked becomes always seeing requests through to completion.
findings.japanese:
『…なんて言っても、
頼まれたらやめられないのが春希くんだよね』
findings.todokanai: "…Still, I know you'll just see through others' requests to the very end no matter what I say, won't you, Haruki-kun?"

findings.highlight: thinking I'd be super curious about it
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が見たら、絶対にちくんとすることを、しっかり残しておく
findings.explanation: Haruki notices Setsuna deliberately left in words guaranteed to prick or sting him when he read them. The English says she wanted to make him curious, replacing the slight poison and newly returning candor that the next lines explicitly analyze.
findings.japanese:
俺が見たら、絶対にちくんとすることを、
しっかり残しておくのはなんでなんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: She probably kept them there on purpose, thinking I'd be super curious about it or something.

findings.highlight: letting her go off on her own
findings.evidenceJa: バイト三日目でもうフル参戦ってのは、負担だった
findings.explanation: Haruki worries that making Koharu participate at full capacity on only her third day was too heavy a burden. The English says she was sent off to work on her own, inventing isolation rather than the intensity of full participation.
findings.japanese:
…やっぱりバイト三日目でもうフル参戦ってのは、
負担だったんじゃないだろうか？
findings.todokanai: …Was letting her go off on her own on only the third day too much for her to handle after all?

findings.highlight: "The way you put it sounds awfully disrespectful toward me… Not that I would disagree, though."
findings.evidenceJa:
「そういう言い方、
わたしに対して失礼だと思います。
…あえて指摘しませんけど」
findings.explanation: Koharu says she will refrain from pointing out Haruki's disrespect, while the English says she does not disagree with his rejection.
findings.japanese:
「そういう言い方、
わたしに対して失礼だと思います。
…あえて指摘しませんけど」
findings.todokanai: "The way you put it sounds awfully disrespectful toward me… Not that I would disagree, though."

findings.highlight: Just when I thought she'd become a bit more modest.
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっとは素直になったと思ったのに。
findings.explanation: Haruki thought Koharu had become more honest or straightforward; the English says more modest.
findings.japanese: ちょっとは素直になったと思ったのに。
findings.todokanai: Just when I thought she'd become a bit more modest.

findings.highlight: stop coming after New Year's
findings.evidenceJa: 今年いっぱいで終わるかも
findings.explanation: Haruki says the short-term job may end by the close of the current year. The English says he may stop only after New Year's, shifting the endpoint across the holiday boundary central to Setsuna's question about visiting.
findings.japanese:
『それに、このバイトは短期だし、
もしかしたら、今年いっぱいで終わるかも』
findings.todokanai: "Also, this is a short-term job, and I might even stop coming after New Year's."

findings.highlight: I'm done for.
findings.evidenceJa: 語るに落ちた
findings.explanation: Haruki corrects the phrase to 語るに落ちた, meaning that someone's own speech inadvertently reveals the truth. The English glosses it as being “done for,” failing precisely where the scene pauses to correct Satou's Japanese and then reuses the phrase.
findings.japanese: 「語るに落ちた、だ」
findings.todokanai: "You mean to say that I'm done for."

findings.highlight: we reconciled almost immediately
findings.evidenceJa: すっかり全員の認識が統一されてしまっていた
findings.explanation: By the time Haruki notices the staff eavesdropping, everyone's understanding has consolidated around the same mistaken conclusion that he and Koharu are involved. The English says Haruki and Koharu reconciled, inventing resolution instead of the collective misunderstanding driving the rest of the scene.
findings.japanese:
ドア越しに聞き耳を立てているスタッフが多すぎて、
店の回転に支障が出かけていると気づいた時には、
すっかり全員の認識が統一されてしまっていた。
findings.todokanai: But when we realized that the number of people pressing their ears on the other side of the door was enough to be a serious detriment to the restaurant, we reconciled almost immediately.

findings.highlight: she just choked herself
findings.evidenceJa: 『自分に絞れ』という意思表示にも取れます
findings.explanation: Satou says Mari's denial can be read as signaling that Haruki should narrow his choice to her alone. The English's “choked herself” is unrelated and deletes the romantic interpretation that prompts Haruki's Japanese-language rebuke.
findings.japanese: 「『自分に絞れ』という意思表示にも取れますが」
findings.todokanai: "I think she just choked herself with what she said there…"

findings.highlight: The last of my seminars also ended today.
findings.evidenceJa: 今日はこのままゼミの打ち上げ
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is going straight on to the seminar wrap party today, while the fourth-years and M2 students still have no holiday. The English says only that his last seminars ended, deleting the party that structures the chapter's parallel meetings.
findings.japanese:
『今日はこのままゼミの打ち上げ。
とは言っても四年やＭ２の先輩たちには、
クリスマスも正月もないんだろうけど』
findings.todokanai: "The last of my seminars also ended today. Even so, our upperclassmen from fourth year and M2 still don't get to enjoy Christmas or New Year's."

findings.highlight: skiing in Hokkaido or Okinawa
findings.evidenceJa: 北海道でスキーとか、逆に沖縄とか
findings.explanation: Haruki proposes skiing in Hokkaido or, conversely, going to Okinawa. The English grammatically makes both Hokkaido and Okinawa skiing destinations, erasing the deliberate warm-versus-cold travel contrast and creating the false Okinawa activity.
findings.japanese:
『雪菜は冬休み、どこか行く？
北海道でスキーとか、逆に沖縄とか。
それとも思い切って海外？』
findings.todokanai: "Where are you planning to go during winter break, Setsuna? Are you going skiing in Hokkaido or Okinawa? Maybe going overseas?"

findings.highlight: I can't walk right back out after coming in here.
findings.evidenceJa: お店に入ってすぐに出てきても駄目
findings.explanation: Setsuna says a parfait should not come out immediately after entering the warm shop; it should arrive after her body has warmed. The English says Setsuna herself cannot leave immediately, changing the timing of the dessert into the timing of her departure.
findings.japanese:
「ん～、やっぱりおいし。
お店に入ってすぐに出てきても駄目なんだよね。
だいぶ体があったまった頃に出てきてもらわないと」
findings.todokanai: "Mmm～ but this is so delicious! I can't walk right back out after coming in here. I have to let my body warm up first before I leave."

findings.highlight: if you know anyone that suits me, please introduce them to me
findings.evidenceJa: 手当たり次第コナかけてる
findings.explanation: Chiaki claims she is indiscriminately flirting with every available prospect to find a man by Christmas. The English instead asks Setsuna to introduce a suitable person, replacing active scattershot seduction with passive matchmaking.
findings.japanese:
「あたしはさぁ、もう大変よぉ。
クリスマス合わせで新しい男見つけようって、
手当たり次第コナかけてるんだけどさぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I'm just doing terrible here. I'd like to find a new man during the Christmas holidays, so if you know anyone that suits me, please introduce them to me."

findings.highlight: She never attended any of the seminars, even when her papers were due, but Izumi suddenly decided to attend the party all of a sudden, forcing me to make all sorts of adjustments.
findings.evidenceJa:
今までゼミの行事を、課題提出含め全部スルーしてきた
和泉が、初めて打ち上げに参加してもいいってんで、
結構方々に調整で走り回ったんだけどなぁ。
findings.explanation: Chiaki skipped seminar events, including assignment submission, while the English says she never attended seminars even when papers were due.
findings.japanese:
今までゼミの行事を、課題提出含め全部スルーしてきた
和泉が、初めて打ち上げに参加してもいいってんで、
結構方々に調整で走り回ったんだけどなぁ。
findings.todokanai: She never attended any of the seminars, even when her papers were due, but Izumi suddenly decided to attend the party all of a sudden, forcing me to make all sorts of adjustments.

findings.highlight: …As bad as I may feel about saying this, it seems that I'm the only one capable of taming her.
findings.evidenceJa:
...言い方は悪いけど、
俺にだけは懐いてくれてると思ったんだけどな。
findings.explanation: Haruki thought Chiaki had become tame or attached only toward him; the English asserts he alone is capable of taming her.
findings.japanese:
...言い方は悪いけど、
俺にだけは懐いてくれてると思ったんだけどな。
findings.todokanai: …As bad as I may feel about saying this, it seems that I'm the only one capable of taming her.

findings.highlight: your imagination is way too rich
findings.evidenceJa: 逆だよ...感受性が豊かだったんだ
findings.explanation: Setsuna answers that the opposite was true: he was richly sensitive, which is why neither wound heals. The English tells Chiaki that her imagination is rich, assigning the quality to the wrong person and severing the causal link to Haruki's lasting guilt.
findings.japanese: 「逆だよ...感受性が豊かだったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "It's the opposite… and your imagination is way too rich."

findings.highlight: I got into a little trouble
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっと中てられてた、というか、ものすごく濃い特訓してた
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she was overwhelmed or affected by Setsuna and, more precisely, underwent an extraordinarily intense training session in studying her. The English calls this getting into trouble and learning a hard lesson, losing both her intoxication by Setsuna and her actress-observer metaphor.
findings.japanese:
「...ごめん。
ちょっと中てられてた、というか、
ものすごく濃い特訓してた」
findings.todokanai: "…I'm sorry. I got into a little trouble… Well, specifically, I learned a pretty hard lesson."

findings.highlight: There's no way our relationship wouldn't be shaken by words like that.
findings.evidenceJa: 別に、そんな言葉に動揺するような関係じゃない
findings.explanation: Haruki insists theirs is not the kind of relationship in which “I want to be alone with you” should unsettle him. The English says there is no way it would not unsettle their relationship, reversing the denial that his subsequent agitation exposes.
findings.japanese:
『二人きりになりたい』って...
別に、そんな言葉に動揺するような関係じゃない。
findings.todokanai: "The two of us, alone," huh… There's no way our relationship wouldn't be shaken by words like that.

findings.highlight: You haven't spoken to the professor for a while
findings.evidenceJa: 教授とだって、まともに話したことない
findings.explanation: Haruki says Chiaki has never properly spoken with the professor. The English says only that she has not done so for a while, inventing a prior working relationship and weakening his argument that she finally needs to appear.
findings.japanese:
「教授とだって、まともに話したことないだろ？
あと一年以上付き合うんだからさ、
そろそろ顔出しといた方がいいんじゃないか？」
findings.todokanai: "You haven't spoken to the professor for a while either, right? You still have to bear with him for another year, so shouldn't you at least show up?"

findings.highlight: incapable of finding a retort
findings.evidenceJa: 和泉のその決断を、引き留めることなんかできない
findings.explanation: Because his motive is guilty, Haruki cannot ask Chiaki not to go home or hold her back. The English says he cannot find a verbal retort, replacing a relinquished attempt to keep her with argumentative defeat.
findings.japanese:
そんな後ろめたい理由だからこそ、
和泉のその決断を、引き留めることなんかできない。
findings.todokanai: It's because I'm feeling this guilt that I'm incapable of finding a retort against Izumi's decision.

findings.highlight: Despite having put aside the gloomy atmosphere
findings.evidenceJa: なんとなく湿っぽい雰囲気に後ろ髪を引かれつつ
findings.explanation: The damp emotional atmosphere makes both characters reluctant to part, so they keep holding the silent phones to their ears. The English says they have put that atmosphere aside, reversing the feeling that physically prolongs the ended conversation.
findings.japanese:
なんとなく湿っぽい雰囲気に後ろ髪を引かれつつ、
俺たちは、会話の終わった受話器を耳に当て続け...
findings.todokanai: Despite having put aside the gloomy atmosphere between us somehow, we continue holding our phones to our ears despite having ended our conversation.

findings.highlight: I just want to enjoy myself
findings.evidenceJa: 楽に、なりたいだけなの
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she no longer wants to keep striving; she only wants relief, to be released from the burden. The English makes this a wish to enjoy herself, trivializing the exhaustion that immediately makes Haruki ask who denied her any ease.
findings.japanese:
『ただ、もう頑張りたくないだけ。
楽に、なりたいだけなの』
findings.todokanai: "It's just that I don't want to work so hard anymore. I just want to enjoy myself, that's all."

findings.highlight: a woman who's above my own league
findings.evidenceJa: あれと同等以上の女を演じなきゃならない
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she now has to perform a woman equal or superior to “that”—Setsuna as the model she has just intensely studied—for the demanding Haruki. The English makes the woman above Chiaki's league, obscuring the acting task and its specific comparator.
findings.japanese:
「あれと同等以上の女を演じなきゃならないなんて、
なんてハードルの高い男だろうねぇ、春希くん」
findings.todokanai: "Making me act like a woman who's above my own league… You're setting the bar awfully high, Haruki-kun."

findings.highlight: Izumi is complaining as she continues drinking
findings.evidenceJa: 和泉は飲んで騒ぐだけ
findings.explanation: Haruki describes their standard unfair gathering: he makes snacks and prepares drinks while Chiaki only drinks and makes merry or noise. The English says she is complaining and that he sponsors the food, changing both her action and his hands-on caretaking.
findings.japanese:
俺がつまみを作り、酒を用意して、
和泉は飲んで騒ぐだけの、不公平な宴席。
findings.todokanai: An unfair drinking party where Izumi is complaining as she continues drinking despite me being the one who's sponsoring all the snacks and drinks.

findings.highlight: an area far to the north
findings.evidenceJa: 北陸地方の民話
findings.explanation: The paper concerns folklore from the named Hokuriku region. The English replaces Hokuriku with a generic area “far to the north,” geographically mislocating or de-specifying the research topic and breaking the earlier correct rendering of the same phrase.
findings.japanese:
北陸地方の民話なんていう、
かなり資料を探すのも大変そうな、
しかも地味な研究をしていた学生時代。
findings.todokanai: It was about a folktale from an area far to the north. Just looking for information on that kind of subject is extremely difficult, and it's also a very uncommon theme for a student to work on.

findings.highlight: slow-witted
findings.evidenceJa: 怠惰で要領良くて人間として軽い和泉
findings.explanation: Haruki calls present Chiaki lazy, efficient or adept at getting by, and frivolous. The English calls her slow-witted, reversing 要領が良い and making his question about when her savvy lightness formed into doubt that she could write the paper.
findings.japanese:
今の、怠惰で要領良くて人間として軽い和泉は、
いつ形づくられたんだろうって、
失礼な疑問が頭に浮かぶのは当然だと思う。
findings.todokanai: It's only natural for me to rudely wonder how someone as lazy and slow-witted as Izumi would ever be able to complete such a paper.

findings.highlight: Her grip is stronger than it usually is
findings.evidenceJa: いつもの力強さ...って言うか、俺の照れと躊躇を誘発しないための気遣いがない
findings.explanation: This touch lacks Chiaki's usual forcefulness—the rough play that normally spares Haruki embarrassment by keeping contact unserious. The English says her grip is stronger, reversing the tactile change that makes the gentle contact more intimate.
findings.japanese:
いつもの力強さ...って言うか、
俺の照れと躊躇を誘発しないための気遣いがない。
findings.todokanai: Her grip is stronger than it usually is… perhaps she's just not bothering to make sure I'm not embarrassed or hesitant this time.

findings.highlight: both the liquor and the hot sweat are rushing out of my body
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は、酒だけじゃない、熱い汗を噴き出させ
findings.explanation: Overcome by Chiaki's unexpected sensuality, Haruki breaks into hot sweat caused by more than alcohol alone. The English says liquor itself rushes out of his body alongside sweat, producing impossible physiology and obscuring arousal as the additional cause.
findings.japanese:
そんな、和泉とは思えない『色』にあてられて、
俺は、酒だけじゃない、熱い汗を噴き出させ...
findings.todokanai: I never thought this kind of "seductiveness" would be coming from Izumi, both the liquor and the hot sweat are rushing out of my body…

findings.highlight: I can't resist my reflexive answers to her questions.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分に反動が返ってくることは避けようがない
findings.explanation: Even if Haruki keeps his heart hidden, he cannot avoid the emotional backlash rebounding onto himself. The English turns this into an inability to resist reflexive verbal answers, changing the cost of concealment from inward pain to conversational impulsiveness.
findings.japanese:
心の中をいくら隠し通しても、
自分に反動が返ってくることは避けようがない。
findings.todokanai: No matter how hard I try to hide my feelings within my heart, I can't resist my reflexive answers to her questions.

findings.highlight: heading toward Aikawa
findings.evidenceJa: 有川行き
findings.explanation: The destination is Arikawa: the same corpus renders 有川 as “Arikawa” and the related school name 東有川 as “Higashi-Arikawa.” “Aikawa” is a local inconsistent reading of the place name in the station announcement.
findings.japanese:
「６番線、有川行きが参ります。
ご注意ください」
findings.todokanai: "Your attention please. The train on Line 6 heading toward Aikawa will arrive shortly."

findings.highlight: Is someone plagiarizing our stories?
findings.evidenceJa: こっちが追ってたネタを抜かれたのか
findings.explanation: Hamada asks whether another publication has scooped them on a story they were pursuing. The English asks whether someone is plagiarizing their stories, substituting copying for being beaten to publication and misidentifying the suspected professional failure.
findings.japanese:
「なんだ？
こっちが追ってたネタを抜かれたのか？」
findings.todokanai: "What is it? Is someone plagiarizing our stories?"

findings.highlight: Whichever it is, let's just stay calm.
findings.evidenceJa: どっちにしろ、穏やかじゃないですね
findings.explanation: Matsuoka says that either possibility would be alarming or no peaceful matter. The English turns this assessment of danger into an instruction to remain calm, reversing the line's speech act and emotional direction.
findings.japanese: 「どっちにしろ、穏やかじゃないですね」
findings.todokanai: "Whichever it is, let's just stay calm."

findings.highlight: I haven't done something like delivering tea for a while, so I'm not sure if I can even do it properly… I'm a little ashamed, since this really is something a part-time student should be doing in the first place.
findings.evidenceJa:
久々に、お茶くみなどというバイトらしい仕事を与えられ、
ちょっとばかり手元のおぼつかない自分が恥ずかしい。
…もう一つの方のバイトじゃ本業なのに。
findings.explanation: Tea service is jokingly called Haruki's main duty at his other part-time job, while the English says it is what a part-time student should do in the first place.
findings.japanese:
久々に、お茶くみなどというバイトらしい仕事を与えられ、
ちょっとばかり手元のおぼつかない自分が恥ずかしい。
…もう一つの方のバイトじゃ本業なのに。
findings.todokanai: I haven't done something like delivering tea for a while, so I'm not sure if I can even do it properly… I'm a little ashamed, since this really is something a part-time student should be doing in the first place.

findings.highlight: If it's really that big, they must be discussing something important in there.
findings.evidenceJa: 『一大事』の中に『大いなる』という意はとっくに入ってるじゃないか
findings.explanation: Haruki catches his own redundant phrasing: 一大事 already contains the sense of something major, so adding 大いなる was needless. The English invents a literal inference that a big matter must be important and deletes the self-editing language joke entirely.
findings.japanese:
『一大事』の中に『大いなる』という意は
とっくに入ってるじゃないか。
findings.todokanai: If it's really that big, they must be discussing something important in there.

findings.highlight: She's handling herself extraordinarily well for a new pianist.
findings.evidenceJa: 新人ピアニストにしては破格の扱いだけどね
findings.explanation: Mari says Kazusa has received exceptional editorial treatment for a new pianist, referring to the cover feature. The English makes the claim about Kazusa conducting herself extraordinarily well, shifting the subject from the magazine's treatment to her behavior.
findings.japanese:
「新人ピアニストにしては破格の扱いだけどね。
でもまぁいいんじゃない？
見栄えという意味じゃダントツだったのよ」
findings.todokanai: "She's handling herself extraordinarily well for a new pianist. Pretty nice, don't you think? Not to mention the fact that she looks great in the first place."

findings.highlight: "Well, I celebrated too, but rather than eating snacks in the conference room, we went drinking at a hostess club all night."
findings.evidenceJa:
「確かに祝ってくれたけど、
会議室でお菓子で乾杯じゃなくて、
朝までキャバクラで乾杯だった…」
findings.explanation: Hamada says his seniors celebrated him at a hostess club until morning, while the English says he himself celebrated.
findings.japanese:
「確かに祝ってくれたけど、
会議室でお菓子で乾杯じゃなくて、
朝までキャバクラで乾杯だった…」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I celebrated too, but rather than eating snacks in the conference room, we went drinking at a hostess club all night."

findings.highlight: She must have felt very irritated back then, too.
findings.evidenceJa: あの時も、やっぱり相手には退かれてたっけ
findings.explanation: Recalling the earlier graduation celebration, Haruki notes that the other person was put off and backed away then as well. The English says she was irritated, replacing physical or emotional recoil with annoyance and weakening the callback to Haruki's awkward intensity.
findings.japanese: あの時も、やっぱり相手には退かれてたっけ。
findings.todokanai: She must have felt very irritated back then, too.

findings.highlight: it's not like I can find myself making any excuses, either
findings.evidenceJa: 言い訳をせずにはいられなくしてくれる
findings.explanation: Mari's caretaking makes Haruki feel so uncomfortable that he cannot help making excuses. The English says he cannot bring himself to make excuses, reversing the explicit double-negative and his characteristic defensive compulsion.
findings.japanese:
俺を、いつもいたたまれない気分にさせてくれる。
言い訳をせずにはいられなくしてくれる。
findings.todokanai: It makes me extremely shameful. But it's not like I can find myself making any excuses, either.

findings.highlight: what would come after if I were to share this with them
findings.evidenceJa: もう少し後付けの問題というか
findings.explanation: Haruki says the difficulty is not his family circumstances or friendships themselves but a more subsequent or later-added complication: the article's connection to Kazusa. The English instead invents future consequences that would follow sharing the article, assigning the problem to disclosure.
findings.japanese:
「つまりですね…
俺の家庭環境や交友関係がどうとかじゃなくて、
もう少し後付けの問題というか…」
findings.todokanai: "How do I say this… the problem I have isn't really about the relationships I have with my family or my friends, but rather what would come after if I were to share this with them…"

findings.highlight: laughing at myself after realizing how lame I must look to others
findings.evidenceJa: そのすれ違いが、なんだかおかしくて、自分でも嫌味だなぁと思ってしまう笑み
findings.explanation: Haruki finds the mismatch between Mari's mistaken concern and his real circumstances funny, and a smile he recognizes as rather sardonic keeps welling up. The English makes him laugh at how lame he appears to other people, replacing both the cause and the nature of his self-judgment.
findings.japanese:
そのすれ違いが、なんだかおかしくて、
自分でも嫌味だなぁと思ってしまう笑みが、
後から後から湧き出て止まらない。
findings.todokanai: As we keep talking, I notice that I'm feeling strange. I just started laughing at myself after realizing how lame I must look to others, and I can't stop myself.

findings.highlight: "Mari-san… you're actually quite passionate, aren't you? The way you let things slip out like that might be your only fault."
findings.evidenceJa:
「麻理さんは…熱いひとですね。
ちょっと外し気味なのが玉に瑕ですが」
findings.explanation: Haruki says Mari's passion tends to miss the mark slightly, translated as her letting things slip out.
findings.japanese:
「麻理さんは…熱いひとですね。
ちょっと外し気味なのが玉に瑕ですが」
findings.todokanai: "Mari-san… you're actually quite passionate, aren't you? The way you let things slip out like that might be your only fault."

findings.highlight: "Well, go on home now, Kitahara."
findings.evidenceJa: 「じゃ、じゃあ帰ろうか、北原」
findings.explanation: Mari proposes that the two of them go home, while the English tells Haruki to go home.
findings.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあ帰ろうか、北原」
findings.todokanai: "Well, go on home now, Kitahara."

findings.highlight: I didn't want you to get the magazine before I did, Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜に先に手に入れて欲しくなかったから。俺から直接、雪菜に手渡したかったから
findings.explanation: Haruki did not want Setsuna to obtain a copy first, before he could personally give one to her. The English compares her acquisition with his own, even though he already has the magazine, obscuring that the entire secrecy was meant to preserve his direct gift.
findings.japanese:
『だって、雪菜に先に手に入れて欲しくなかったから。
俺から直接、雪菜に手渡したかったから』
findings.todokanai: "I didn't want you to get the magazine before I did, Setsuna. I wanted to give it to you myself."

findings.highlight: It's just that I've been stubborn and incapable of honestly expressing such desires on my own.
findings.evidenceJa:
ただ、その欲求を口に出して言えるほど、
自分の身勝手に忠実になれなかっただけ。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he could not be faithful enough to his own selfishness to voice the desire, translated as stubborn inability to express it honestly.
findings.japanese:
ただ、その欲求を口に出して言えるほど、
自分の身勝手に忠実になれなかっただけ。
findings.todokanai: It's just that I've been stubborn and incapable of honestly expressing such desires on my own.

findings.highlight: incapable of conclusively expressing my sincerity to her
findings.evidenceJa: ずっと結論のでない『誠実』に、結局、何の結論も出せないまま
findings.explanation: After three years, Haruki still cannot reach any conclusion about what 'sincerity' itself requires. The English turns this unresolved moral problem into an inability to express his sincerity to Setsuna, falsely presupposing that he already possesses the answer and merely cannot communicate it.
findings.japanese:
三年経っても、ずっと結論のでない『誠実』に、
結局、何の結論も出せないまま、だけど。
findings.todokanai: In the end, though, I'm still as incapable of conclusively expressing my sincerity to her as I've ever been, even after three years.

findings.highlight: I'm working the evening shift so that I can match your arrival
findings.evidenceJa: わたしに合わせるよう遅番にしろって言ったから、夜は閉店までいると思います
findings.explanation: Koharu tells the person on the phone that she arranged for Haruki's shift to be made a late one matching hers, so he should remain until closing. The English makes Koharu herself take an evening shift to match the listener's arrival, reversing whose schedule she manipulated and concealing the setup.
findings.japanese:
「わたしに合わせるよう遅番にしろって言ったから、
夜は閉店までいると思います」
findings.todokanai: "I'm working the evening shift so that I can match your arrival, so I intend to stay until the closing hours tonight."

findings.highlight: "My family's planning to have a Christmas party on the 25th. My mom's gonna make fried chicken in the morning, and we're all having flavored champagne as usual."
findings.evidenceJa:
『うち、クリスマスパーティは２５日なの。
朝からお母さんと一緒にチキン焼いて、
相変わらずジュースのシャンペンで乾杯して』
findings.explanation: Setsuna and her mother bake or roast the chicken together and toast with nonalcoholic champagne-like juice; the English makes her mother fry it alone and calls the drink flavored champagne.
findings.japanese:
『うち、クリスマスパーティは２５日なの。
朝からお母さんと一緒にチキン焼いて、
相変わらずジュースのシャンペンで乾杯して』
findings.todokanai: "My family's planning to have a Christmas party on the 25th. My mom's gonna make fried chicken in the morning, and we're all having flavored champagne as usual."

findings.highlight: "Mom has been telling Takahiro for a while now that it's about time he brought home his girlfriend, but it doesn't seem like that'll be happening this year."
findings.evidenceJa:
『お母さんは孝宏に
そろそろ彼女連れてきたらって言ってるけど、
どうやら今年もそんな気配はなさそう』
findings.explanation: Setsuna's mother urges Takahiro to bring a girlfriend sometime, without presupposing one exists; the English says 'his girlfriend.'
findings.japanese:
『お母さんは孝宏に
そろそろ彼女連れてきたらって言ってるけど、
どうやら今年もそんな気配はなさそう』
findings.todokanai: "Mom has been telling Takahiro for a while now that it's about time he brought home his girlfriend, but it doesn't seem like that'll be happening this year."

findings.highlight: it's not like Setsuna to be compromising
findings.evidenceJa: 駆け引きのできるような彼女じゃない
findings.explanation: Haruki concludes that Setsuna is incapable of strategic maneuvering or romantic game-playing, so the opening in her argument is probably innocent. The English says she is not compromising, nearly the opposite trait: refusal to compromise rather than inability to scheme.
findings.japanese:
…気づいてないんだろうなぁ。
駆け引きのできるような彼女じゃないしな。
findings.todokanai: …She probably isn't aware of it. After all, it's not like Setsuna to be compromising.

findings.highlight: When a lump of good intentions like her is mad at me
findings.evidenceJa: そんな善意の塊に腹を立ててもしょうがない
findings.explanation: Haruki says there is no point in his getting angry at someone who is nothing but good intentions. The English makes Koharu the one angry at him, reversing whose anger he is reasoning away.
findings.japanese:
…けど、何しろ裏も下心も他意もまるっきりないから、
そんな善意の塊に腹を立ててもしょうがないんだよな。
findings.todokanai: But it's not like she has any ulterior motive. When a lump of good intentions like her is mad at me, there's not much I can do about it.

findings.highlight: I'm shocked by how perfectly synced their sighs were just now.
findings.evidenceJa:
こういう時の呆れたような視線だけ、
息ぴったりでシンクロしやがって。
findings.explanation: Takeya and Io synchronize their exasperated looks, translated as synchronized sighs.
findings.japanese:
こういう時の呆れたような視線だけ、
息ぴったりでシンクロしやがって。
findings.todokanai: I'm shocked by how perfectly synced their sighs were just now.

findings.highlight: Glancing inside my wallet, I bid farewell to the thousand yen bills that I'd been saving for situations like these.
findings.evidenceJa:
財布を覗くと、
こういう時に限って千円札が潤沢なのがやるせない。
findings.explanation: Haruki is frustrated that his wallet happens to be flush with thousand-yen notes at this moment; the English says he had saved them for situations like this.
findings.japanese:
財布を覗くと、
こういう時に限って千円札が潤沢なのがやるせない。
findings.todokanai: Glancing inside my wallet, I bid farewell to the thousand yen bills that I'd been saving for situations like these.

findings.highlight: only going to be aired once and only on a single day
findings.evidenceJa: １日１回しか上映しないのか
findings.explanation: Haruki asks why the supposedly top film is screened only once per day. The English says it will be shown only once on a single day, changing the revival's ongoing daily schedule into a one-off event.
findings.japanese:
「なんだよ、１日１回しか上映しないのか。
今年の邦画ナンバーワンじゃなかったのかよ」
findings.todokanai: "Wait, what? So this is only going to be aired once and only on a single day? It's the number one Japanese film of the year, is it not?"

findings.highlight: Not only did she buy the magazine that published my first article, she also held a celebration for its release, and always finds plenty of work for me to do, so isn't it normal to pay her back?
findings.evidenceJa:
俺の初仕事の載った雑誌を買ってくれたお礼とか、
打ち上げに連れて行ってくれたお礼とか、
今まで仕事を叩き込んでくれたお礼とか。
findings.explanation: Mari drilled professional work into Haruki, rendered as finding plenty of work for him.
findings.japanese:
俺の初仕事の載った雑誌を買ってくれたお礼とか、
打ち上げに連れて行ってくれたお礼とか、
今まで仕事を叩き込んでくれたお礼とか。
findings.todokanai: Not only did she buy the magazine that published my first article, she also held a celebration for its release, and always finds plenty of work for me to do, so isn't it normal to pay her back?

findings.highlight: Like jumping into a freshwater spri… no, I initially planned to leap into Arumi's waters
findings.evidenceJa: 清水の舞台…じゃなくて、有海の海に飛び込んだつもりで
findings.explanation: Takeya begins the proverb about taking the plunge from Kiyomizu's stage, then comically corrects it to diving into Arumi's sea to suit the bay setting. The English misreads 清水 as fresh water, changes the self-correction into a prior plan, and leaves both the proverb and the proper-name pun incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「畜生わかったよ！　清水の舞台…じゃなくて、
有海の海に飛び込んだつもりで、
思い切って３万６千円でＯＫ！」
findings.todokanai: "Damn it… fine! Like jumping into a freshwater spri… no, I initially planned to leap into Arumi's waters, but I'm okay with selling it to you for 36,000 yen!"

findings.highlight: one of those restaurants that adds things to your bill without you being aware of it
findings.evidenceJa: まるで注文の多い料理店のように、徐々に俺を食い物にしていった
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly invokes Miyazawa's The Restaurant of Many Orders: Takeya's tickets impose one condition after another until they figuratively devour him, as the restaurant intends to devour its guests. The English invents a restaurant billing scam and erases the named literary mechanism.
findings.japanese:
武也が売りつけた『映画のチケット』は、
まるで注文の多い料理店のように、
徐々に俺を食い物にしていった。
findings.todokanai: Takeya's movie ticket deal makes me feel like I was just in one of those restaurants that adds things to your bill without you being aware of it, gradually prying your money away.

findings.highlight: After being viciously caught off guard
findings.evidenceJa: 悪質なマルチに引っかかった後の虚無感
findings.explanation: Haruki compares the spreading financial trap to the emptiness after being taken in by a malicious multilevel-marketing or pyramid scheme. The English reduces this explicit scam analogy to being caught off guard, losing the escalation from literary restaurant to predatory sales scheme.
findings.japanese:
悪質なマルチに引っかかった後の虚無感が、
じわじわと俺の全身を支配していく。
findings.todokanai: After being viciously caught off guard, I feel a sense of emptiness slowly taking over my entire body.

findings.highlight: I'll never fall for such a thing again
findings.evidenceJa: 今度こそ迂闊に生返事だけはしないぞと誓いつつ
findings.explanation: Haruki vows that this time he will not carelessly give another vague, halfhearted assent—the behavior that lets others maneuver him into obligations. The English makes him vow not to fall for a scam again, changing a recurring interpersonal habit into generic gullibility.
findings.japanese:
それでも、
今度こそ迂闊に生返事だけはしないぞと誓いつつ、
ぐったりと、人の減ってきた店内を眺める。
findings.todokanai: Thus, as I swear to myself that I'll never fall for such a thing again, still staggering, I realize that the number of customers in the restaurant has decreased.

findings.highlight: Well, if that's the case, then we're no different.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなの、お互いの定番過ぎて絞り込めないだろ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks which previous occasion Koharu means by his not being honest, then jokes that this is such a standard pattern between them that he cannot narrow it down. The English says only that the two are no different, deleting the frequency joke and his attempt to identify the incident.
findings.japanese:
前に素直じゃなかったのはいつのことだよ？
…そんなの、お互いの定番過ぎて絞り込めないだろ。
findings.todokanai: Was I not honest before? …Well, if that's the case, then we're no different.

findings.highlight: She also really insisted that I should absolutely not tell anyone.
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対に押し込めって、強く言い聞かせておいたよ
findings.explanation: Io says she extracted the meeting date from Setsuna and then firmly told Setsuna to press the opportunity through at all costs. The English makes Setsuna instruct Io not to tell anyone, reversing both speaker and content and contradicting Io's active coordination of the plan.
findings.japanese:
「さっき、何とか雪菜に吐かせた。
絶対に押し込めって、強く言い聞かせておいたよ」
findings.todokanai: "I got it out of Setsuna a little while ago, somehow. She also really insisted that I should absolutely not tell anyone."

findings.highlight: "Still, there's just no way. This is Haruki we're talking about. How could that dense brick make girls do so much for him…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「けど、まさか。
相手は春希だぞ？
あの堅物にそこまでズブズブにハマる女の子が…」
findings.explanation: Takeya doubts that a girl could fall so hopelessly deeply for a stiff man like Haruki; the English asks how Haruki could make girls do so much for him.
findings.japanese:
「けど、まさか。
相手は春希だぞ？
あの堅物にそこまでズブズブにハマる女の子が…」
findings.todokanai: "Still, there's just no way. This is Haruki we're talking about. How could that dense brick make girls do so much for him…"

findings.highlight: My hands are on my knees, I'm deeply bending forward, and I'm panting heavily.
findings.evidenceJa:
膝に手を当てて、がっくりと俯き、
盛大にため息をつく。
findings.explanation: Haruki bends down and releases a huge sigh, translated as panting heavily.
findings.japanese:
膝に手を当てて、がっくりと俯き、
盛大にため息をつく。
findings.todokanai: My hands are on my knees, I'm deeply bending forward, and I'm panting heavily.

findings.highlight: I sprinted into the train when it arrived and the seat kept making creaking sounds due to my impatient fidgeting. Just waiting for ten minutes felt like several hours.
findings.evidenceJa:
ようやく来た電車に飛び乗り、
ガラガラの座席にイライラしながら腰掛け、
ほんの１０分を数時間のように感じ。
findings.explanation: Haruki irritably sits among nearly empty seats; the English invents a creaking seat caused by fidgeting.
findings.japanese:
ようやく来た電車に飛び乗り、
ガラガラの座席にイライラしながら腰掛け、
ほんの１０分を数時間のように感じ。
findings.todokanai: I sprinted into the train when it arrived and the seat kept making creaking sounds due to my impatient fidgeting. Just waiting for ten minutes felt like several hours.

findings.highlight: I hadn't even thought of my cell phone until now
findings.evidenceJa: さっきから、何度も無視され続けてる携帯を、最後の望みとばかりにリダイヤルする
findings.explanation: Haruki has already called repeatedly and been ignored; he redials yet again as his last hope. The English says the phone had not occurred to him until now, erasing the repeated unanswered attempts that establish Koharu's deliberate silence.
findings.japanese:
さっきから、何度も無視され続けてる携帯を、
最後の望みとばかりにリダイヤルする。
findings.todokanai: I hadn't even thought of my cell phone until now, as it's my final hope. I press the redial button.

findings.highlight: Sugiura is trying her best to explain it in a very simple and logical manner, but it turns into a mystery
findings.evidenceJa: いつも、筋が通ってるかは別として、相手にわかりやすく論理的に話そうとする杉浦の、まるっきり謎かけみたいな感情的な吐露
findings.explanation: The point is a contrast: Koharu normally tries to speak logically and plainly, whether or not her logic is sound, but this particular emotional outpouring is entirely like a riddle. The English says she is trying to explain this outpouring logically now and somehow it turns mysterious, losing the marked departure from her normal voice.
findings.japanese:
いつも、筋が通ってるかは別として、
相手にわかりやすく論理的に話そうとする杉浦の、
まるっきり謎かけみたいな感情的な吐露。
findings.todokanai: Ignoring whether or not it made sense, Sugiura is trying her best to explain it in a very simple and logical manner, but it turns into a mystery when she expresses her feelings.

findings.highlight: For a while, I walked with my head hung low since I couldn't find my way around Minegaya anyway.
findings.evidenceJa:
しばらく、ずっと俯いて歩いてたから、
ここが峰ヶ谷のどの辺りなのかもよくわからない。
findings.explanation: Haruki does not know where he is because he walked looking down; the English says he looked down because he could not navigate Minegaya.
findings.japanese:
しばらく、ずっと俯いて歩いてたから、
ここが峰ヶ谷のどの辺りなのかもよくわからない。
findings.todokanai: For a while, I walked with my head hung low since I couldn't find my way around Minegaya anyway.

findings.highlight: "You do know that the last train might have already left, right?"
findings.evidenceJa: 「終電、なくなってること知ってますよね？」
findings.explanation: Koharu knows the last train is already gone; the English says it might have left.
findings.japanese: 「終電、なくなってること知ってますよね？」
findings.todokanai: "You do know that the last train might have already left, right?"

findings.highlight: It's as if we're walking on a curved plank that's barely the width of a foot, like we're always trying to get back to where we began…
findings.evidenceJa:
足の幅ほどしかない平均台の上を蛇行してるみたいに、
すぐに振り出しに戻ってしまいそうな…
findings.explanation: The pair weave along a balance beam only a foot wide and may return to the starting point; the English invents a curved plank and makes returning sound intentional.
findings.japanese:
足の幅ほどしかない平均台の上を蛇行してるみたいに、
すぐに振り出しに戻ってしまいそうな…
findings.todokanai: It's as if we're walking on a curved plank that's barely the width of a foot, like we're always trying to get back to where we began…

findings.highlight: The wound on Setsuna's chest is still open and has yet to be healed.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜の裸の胸に刻まれた、まだ塞がらずに化膿していたその傷
findings.explanation: Haruki remembers the wound carved into Setsuna's bare chest, still unclosed and suppurating. The English omits both the naked visual that makes the memory intimate and the infection that makes it graphic, then redundantly says open and unhealed instead of conveying its severity.
findings.japanese:
雪菜の裸の胸に刻まれた、
まだ塞がらずに化膿していたその傷を。
findings.todokanai: The wound on Setsuna's chest is still open and has yet to be healed.

findings.highlight: "Besides, after having dinner near the sea, it'll be very late, so what am I even saying…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「それに有海で夕食だと帰り遅くなるし、
何言ってんだろうな、俺」
findings.explanation: Dinner in the proper-name location Arumi becomes dinner 'near the sea.'
findings.japanese:
「それに有海で夕食だと帰り遅くなるし、
何言ってんだろうな、俺」
findings.todokanai: "Besides, after having dinner near the sea, it'll be very late, so what am I even saying…"

findings.highlight: "Aa-ah, you're all covered in snow. Bend down a little, Haruki-kun."
findings.evidenceJa:
「あ～あ、なんか湯気出てるよ。
ほら、ちょっと屈んで、春希くん」
findings.explanation: Takeya jokes that steam seems to rise from Haruki, while the English merely says he is covered in snow.
findings.japanese:
「あ～あ、なんか湯気出てるよ。
ほら、ちょっと屈んで、春希くん」
findings.todokanai: "Aa-ah, you're all covered in snow. Bend down a little, Haruki-kun."

findings.highlight: Regardless of whether or not her attitude is merely a facade, I have no choice but to accept her currently cheerful and carefree state as being authentic.
findings.evidenceJa:
その態度が、嘘だろうと本物だろうと、
俺の中の公式設定で『明るく屈託のない雪菜』を
受け入れるしかない。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls the bright, carefree Setsuna an 'official setting'; the English states that her present manner is the real her.
findings.japanese:
その態度が、嘘だろうと本物だろうと、
俺の中の公式設定で『明るく屈託のない雪菜』を
受け入れるしかない。
findings.todokanai: Regardless of whether or not her attitude is merely a facade, I have no choice but to accept her currently cheerful and carefree state as being authentic.

findings.highlight: she didn't even bring so much as a drink with her
findings.evidenceJa: 実際には飲み物にすら手を付けてなかったり
findings.explanation: Setsuna had a drink but had not touched even it, evidence that her distress left her unable to eat or drink. The English says she did not bring a drink, replacing the symptom with an irrelevant fact about what she carried.
findings.japanese:
『映画館と言えばポップコーンだよね』って言ってたのに、
実際には飲み物にすら手を付けてなかったりとか。
findings.todokanai: Despite having made a comment about not forgetting popcorn when going to the cinema, she didn't even bring so much as a drink with her when we went inside.

findings.highlight: the music department wanted to have a feature article done
findings.evidenceJa: 急遽、音楽誌の方でも特集を組むことになった
findings.explanation: A music magazine has abruptly decided to run its own feature. The English invents a generic music department, obscuring that Haruki is discussing a second publication and the concrete editorial assignment created by Kazusa's newsworthiness.
findings.japanese:
「先月の開桜グラフに載ってた冬馬が凄い反響でさ。
急遽、音楽誌の方でも特集を組むことになったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "The bit about Touma in last month's Kaiou Graph made some pretty big waves. It wasn't long until the music department wanted to have a feature article done on her."

findings.highlight: "Said person's quite sharp, you see. They immediately found out that I used to go to school with Touma and came to talk to me right after."
findings.evidenceJa:
「その人がかなりの切れ者でさ、
冬馬と俺が同級生だってすぐに見抜いて、
俺に振ってきた」
findings.explanation: Mari recognized that Haruki attended Kazusa's old school and consequently put him on the biographical portion; the English says only that she found out and spoke to him.
findings.japanese:
「その人がかなりの切れ者でさ、
冬馬と俺が同級生だってすぐに見抜いて、
俺に振ってきた」
findings.todokanai: "Said person's quite sharp, you see. They immediately found out that I used to go to school with Touma and came to talk to me right after."

findings.highlight: It might look like I'm not putting much thought into it
findings.evidenceJa: 突き放してるように見せかけて、実は、慎重に、慎重に言葉を選び。
findings.explanation: Haruki is deliberately making it look as though he is pushing Setsuna away while in fact selecting each word with extreme care. The English turns the apparent cold rejection into apparent thoughtlessness, erasing the manipulative strategy governing the entire exchange.
findings.japanese:
突き放してるように見せかけて、
実は、慎重に、慎重に言葉を選び。
findings.todokanai: It might look like I'm not putting much thought into it, but I'm choosing my words very, very carefully.

findings.highlight: I might ruin the mood if I tried doing something like that myself, but the couples around us don't seem embarrassed at all, paying no mind to our stares.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺にしてみればムードが削がれる気がするんだけど、
でも、どの彼も彼女も堂々としたもので、
俺や雪菜の視線なんか意に介してないようだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki resents couples whose public behavior spoils the atmosphere; the English instead says his own attempt would spoil it.
findings.japanese:
俺にしてみればムードが削がれる気がするんだけど、
でも、どの彼も彼女も堂々としたもので、
俺や雪菜の視線なんか意に介してないようだった。
findings.todokanai: I might ruin the mood if I tried doing something like that myself, but the couples around us don't seem embarrassed at all, paying no mind to our stares.

findings.highlight: After all, it happened to trigger a switch that reawakened memories long pastーmy switch, and likely her own as well.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺と、そして多分、自分自身も、
思い出に引き込むスイッチを押すために。
findings.explanation: Setsuna deliberately draws both of them into a shared memory; the English says the topic simply happened to trigger it.
findings.japanese:
俺と、そして多分、自分自身も、
思い出に引き込むスイッチを押すために。
findings.todokanai: After all, it happened to trigger a switch that reawakened memories long pastーmy switch, and likely her own as well.

findings.highlight: This is something that I can't just laugh off
findings.evidenceJa: それは、流さないといけない。特に、切り返すことだけは絶対にできない質問。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he has to let the question pass, especially because he absolutely cannot turn it back on Setsuna. The English says he cannot laugh it off, reversing his intended response before correctly translating the prohibition on asking it in return.
findings.japanese:
それは、流さないといけない。
特に、切り返すことだけは絶対にできない質問。
findings.todokanai: This is something that I can't just laugh off. More importantly, it's a question that I absolutely cannot ask her in return.

findings.highlight: There was the snow that hid the long-departed airplane during the tiny period of time when I had all traces of Setsuna's existence erased from my heart.
findings.evidenceJa:
ほんの一瞬だけ、
雪菜の存在を自分の中から消し去ったとき、
飛んでいく飛行機を覆い隠してくれた雪。
findings.explanation: Haruki looks for the plane currently flying away; the English calls it long departed.
findings.japanese:
ほんの一瞬だけ、
雪菜の存在を自分の中から消し去ったとき、
飛んでいく飛行機を覆い隠してくれた雪。
findings.todokanai: There was the snow that hid the long-departed airplane during the tiny period of time when I had all traces of Setsuna's existence erased from my heart.

findings.highlight: What we'll be forgetting is the day when the three of us came together
findings.evidenceJa: なかったことになるのは、俺たちが三人になる、その日から
findings.explanation: Haruki proposes erasing everything from the day the trio came into being onward, retaining only his earlier history with Setsuna, as the following narration explains. The English erases only that single day, losing the scope of his counterfactual two-person history.
findings.japanese:
「違うよ。
なかったことになるのは、
俺たちが三人になる、その日から」
findings.todokanai: "No. What we'll be forgetting is the day when the three of us came together."

findings.highlight: I send Setsuna even deeper into a trance with my passion-filled kiss
findings.evidenceJa: さっきより激しく、三年前よりもっと激しく、雪菜以上に切羽詰まった、情欲まみれのキス。
findings.explanation: The kiss is more intense than moments ago, more intense than three years ago, and Haruki is even more desperate than Setsuna, steeped in lust. The English invents an effect on Setsuna—sending her into a deeper trance—and deletes the comparison that exposes Haruki's own greater desperation.
findings.japanese:
さっきより激しく、三年前よりもっと激しく、
雪菜以上に切羽詰まった、情欲まみれのキス。
findings.todokanai: More intensely than just moments before, and much more intensely than I did three years ago, I send Setsuna even deeper into a trance with my passion-filled kiss.

findings.highlight: I want to smile and take comfort in knowing that the path I chose was the right one
findings.evidenceJa: 朝を迎えたとき、自分の選んだ道が正しかったって、心の底から安心して、微笑んでもらえるように。
findings.explanation: Haruki resolves to be gentle so that, when morning comes, Setsuna can feel relief from the bottom of her heart and smile, believing the path she chose was right. The English assigns the reassurance and smile to Haruki himself, reversing the object of his concern.
findings.japanese:
朝を迎えたとき、自分の選んだ道が正しかったって、
心の底から安心して、微笑んでもらえるように。
findings.todokanai: Once morning comes, I want to smile and take comfort in knowing that the path I chose was the right one.

findings.highlight: "The isolated and overly emotional Kazusa followed in the footsteps of the wild and equally emotional Youko, and chose not to restrict herself to Japan's musical world."
findings.evidenceJa:
『孤高で激情家のかずさは、
奔放で激情家の曜子同様、
日本の音楽界に収まりきらなかった』
findings.explanation: Kazusa and Youko did not fit within Japan's music world; the English says Kazusa chose not to restrict herself to it.
findings.japanese:
『孤高で激情家のかずさは、
奔放で激情家の曜子同様、
日本の音楽界に収まりきらなかった』
findings.todokanai: "The isolated and overly emotional Kazusa followed in the footsteps of the wild and equally emotional Youko, and chose not to restrict herself to Japan's musical world."

findings.highlight: Her swollen eyes are, without a doubt, a result of a particular thing that was left on the side of the bed.
findings.evidenceJa:
きっと、泣き腫らした目が、
ベッドの脇に置かれた『それ』に注がれてた。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's swollen eyes are fixed on the magazine, while the English says the magazine caused the swelling.
findings.japanese:
きっと、泣き腫らした目が、
ベッドの脇に置かれた『それ』に注がれてた。
findings.todokanai: Her swollen eyes are, without a doubt, a result of a particular thing that was left on the side of the bed.

findings.highlight: "Sorry… I forgot to close it."
findings.evidenceJa: 「ごめん…しまい忘れてた」
findings.explanation: Haruki forgot to put the magazine away; the English says he forgot to close it.
findings.japanese: 「ごめん…しまい忘れてた」
findings.todokanai: "Sorry… I forgot to close it."

findings.highlight: All memories fade away with time
findings.evidenceJa: どんな想いだって、いつか自然に消えてくよ
findings.explanation: Haruki claims that any feelings will eventually fade naturally. The English instead claims that all memories fade, which is precisely the proposition Setsuna later rejects: she distinguishes his continuing love from memories that cannot simply be erased.
findings.japanese:
「三年も経ったんだ…
どんな想いだって、いつか自然に消えてくよ」
findings.todokanai: "It's been three years already… All memories fade away with time."

findings.highlight: is now simply continuing to pile up
findings.evidenceJa: さっきまで街中に降り積もっていた雪は、今はただ、積もっているだけだった。
findings.explanation: The snow that had been falling and accumulating has stopped; now it merely lies accumulated. The English says it is continuing to pile up, reversing the change in weather at the emotional break and disrupting the chapter's snow progression.
findings.japanese:
さっきまで街中に降り積もっていた雪は、
今はただ、積もっているだけだった。
findings.todokanai: The snow that was piling up on the streets a while ago is now simply continuing to pile up.

findings.highlight: The next train for Line 3
findings.evidenceJa: ３番線、次の電車は０時５５分到着予定です。
findings.explanation: The announcement says the next train at platform 3 is due at 12:55. 番線 denotes a station platform or track, not a numbered railway line; the English gives passengers the wrong transport information.
findings.japanese:
「３番線、次の電車は０時５５分到着予定です。
本日の最終電車となります。
お乗り遅れのないようお願いします」
findings.todokanai: "The next train for Line 3 is scheduled to arrive at 12:55 AM. This will be the final train of the day. Please take care not to miss it."

findings.highlight: I don't want to think about coming to any kind of conclusion about all this, so I should have just stopped thinking about it altogether, but…
findings.evidenceJa:
考えたくない結論に辿り着くのが嫌で、
何も考えないようにしてたはずなのに。
findings.explanation: Haruki had been trying not to think because he feared the conclusion; the English recasts this as what he should have done.
findings.japanese:
考えたくない結論に辿り着くのが嫌で、
何も考えないようにしてたはずなのに。
findings.todokanai: I don't want to think about coming to any kind of conclusion about all this, so I should have just stopped thinking about it altogether, but…

findings.highlight: kept calling me several times per hour until morning came
findings.evidenceJa: 朝まで、依緒と武也からのコールが一時間おきくらいに数件続いてる。
findings.explanation: Several calls from Io and Takeya continued at roughly one-hour intervals until morning. The English says they called several times every hour, multiplying the stated frequency and materially exaggerating their barrage.
findings.japanese:
…その電話があってから後、
朝まで、依緒と武也からのコールが
一時間おきくらいに数件続いてる。
findings.todokanai: …After that, Io and Takeya kept calling me several times per hour until morning came.

findings.highlight: Mari-san's weird changes in her attitude really perplex me sometimes, and I still can't understand her completely to this day
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんの、その妙に言い訳がましい態度の意味は、今の俺には、よく意味がわからなかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki does not understand, at this moment, why Mari is acting strangely defensive—as though making excuses—after volunteering that her traveling companion is not a man. The English turns that specific romantic tell into a timeless general claim that Mari's changing moods sometimes perplex him, erasing both the excuse-like behavior and its immediate cause.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんの、その妙に言い訳がましい態度の意味は、
今の俺には、よく意味がわからなかった。
findings.todokanai: Mari-san's weird changes in her attitude really perplex me sometimes, and I still can't understand her completely to this day.

findings.highlight: The moment I finally manage to keep up with the conversation, a name appears that makes my head go completely blank once again…
findings.evidenceJa:
やっと普通に声が出るようになってきたところに、
また頭を真っ白にしてくれる名字がこぼれ出た…
findings.explanation: Haruki had only just regained an ordinary speaking voice when Touma's surname blanks his mind again; the English says he had managed to keep up with the conversation.
findings.japanese:
やっと普通に声が出るようになってきたところに、
また頭を真っ白にしてくれる名字がこぼれ出た…
findings.todokanai: The moment I finally manage to keep up with the conversation, a name appears that makes my head go completely blank once again…

findings.highlight: You're pretty naive, aren't you, Kitahara?
findings.evidenceJa: 北原って結構ナイーブだよな。傷つきやすくて、自分で自分を責めてばかりで
findings.explanation: ナイーブ is immediately glossed by Mari as emotionally sensitive: Haruki is easily hurt and constantly blames himself. 'Naive' instead calls him inexperienced or gullible, assigning a different character flaw and breaking the explanatory relation to her next sentence.
findings.japanese:
「北原って結構ナイーブだよな。
傷つきやすくて、自分で自分を責めてばかりで」
findings.todokanai: "You're pretty naive, aren't you, Kitahara? You're quite fragile, and you always seem to only put the blame on yourself."

findings.highlight: Because there was nobody you could ask for forgiveness afterward
findings.evidenceJa: 誰も、自分を叱ってくれないから。…叱った後、許してくれないから
findings.explanation: Mari asks whether Haruki sinks further because no one will scold him—and, after scolding him, forgive him. The English changes this into Haruki having nobody from whom he can request forgiveness, weakening Mari's insight that he wants punishment administered by someone who will then absolve him.
findings.japanese:
「だから余計落ち込むのか？
誰も、自分を叱ってくれないから。
…叱った後、許してくれないから」
findings.todokanai: "Is that why you got so depressed? Because there was nobody to reprimand you for it? Because there was nobody you could ask for forgiveness afterward…?"

findings.highlight: "I've always been in love with Touma Kazusaーeven now."
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺、冬馬かずさのこと、今でも好きだったんです」
findings.explanation: Haruki confesses that he discovered he was still in love with Kazusa; 'I've always been in love' makes the continuity more absolute.
findings.japanese: 「俺、冬馬かずさのこと、今でも好きだったんです」
findings.todokanai: "I've always been in love with Touma Kazusaーeven now."

findings.highlight: "Well, I don't mean anything bad by all that. Perhaps it's better to say you're a bit too composed, too argumentative, and too conscious of things sometimes?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「ま、悪い意味じゃないよ。
落ち着きすぎてるって言うか、
理屈っぽいって言うか、醒めてるって言うか」
findings.explanation: Mari calls Haruki overcomposed, argumentative, and emotionally detached or cynical; the English renders the last trait as overly conscious.
findings.japanese:
「ま、悪い意味じゃないよ。
落ち着きすぎてるって言うか、
理屈っぽいって言うか、醒めてるって言うか」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I don't mean anything bad by all that. Perhaps it's better to say you're a bit too composed, too argumentative, and too conscious of things sometimes?"

findings.highlight: …I hope she's aware that it's hard for anybody to give a proper response to that kind of excuse before she uses it.
findings.evidenceJa:
…このネタを使われると、
人のことが言えなくなってしまうので勘弁して欲しい。
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot criticize Chiaki over family estrangement because he is in no position to talk; the English says it is hard for anybody to give a response.
findings.japanese:
…このネタを使われると、
人のことが言えなくなってしまうので勘弁して欲しい。
findings.todokanai: …I hope she's aware that it's hard for anybody to give a proper response to that kind of excuse before she uses it.

findings.highlight: It's just that as far as Izumi is concerned, I know that even if I try to complain, she'll shrug me off with a "Well, whatever" and just do whatever she wants to anyway.
findings.evidenceJa:
ただ、和泉の場合、嘘のはずの脅し文句を
『ま、いっかぁ』程度の割り切りで
実行したりしそうだからしょうがないんだ。
findings.explanation: Chiaki might turn what should be a bluff into reality with a casual shrug; the English says she ignores complaints and does whatever she wants.
findings.japanese:
ただ、和泉の場合、嘘のはずの脅し文句を
『ま、いっかぁ』程度の割り切りで
実行したりしそうだからしょうがないんだ。
findings.todokanai: It's just that as far as Izumi is concerned, I know that even if I try to complain, she'll shrug me off with a "Well, whatever" and just do whatever she wants to anyway.

findings.highlight: I neither hoped for nor approved this
findings.evidenceJa: 望まないまま、許されないまま…それでも俺の生活は、徐々に元へと戻っていく。
findings.explanation: Haruki's life is returning to normal while he still does not want that recovery and still has not been forgiven. The English assigns both verbs to Haruki—he neither hoped for nor approved it—erasing the externally unresolved fact that Setsuna has not forgiven him.
findings.japanese:
望まないまま、許されないまま…
それでも俺の生活は、徐々に元へと戻っていく。
findings.todokanai: I neither hoped for nor approved this… but my life's gradually getting back on track.

findings.highlight: Even so, my stomach, which had started to whine in the middle of it all, is now brazenly accepting chunks of cheese and dough.
findings.evidenceJa:
それでも、途中で音を上げるかと思っていた俺の胃は、
なかなか図太くチーズとパイの塊を受け入れた。
findings.explanation: Haruki expected his stomach to give up midway, but it did not; the English says it had already begun whining.
findings.japanese:
それでも、途中で音を上げるかと思っていた俺の胃は、
なかなか図太くチーズとパイの塊を受け入れた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, my stomach, which had started to whine in the middle of it all, is now brazenly accepting chunks of cheese and dough.

findings.highlight: I've made it kind of a habit
findings.evidenceJa: さすがに外泊を繰り返してたせいで先立つものが…
findings.explanation: Chiaki admits that repeatedly staying away from home has depleted the money she needs, explaining her attempt to shift more of the pizza bill onto Haruki. The English says the sleepovers have simply become a habit, deleting the financial setup and making the bargaining exchange incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「い、いや～、
さすがに外泊を繰り返してたせいで先立つものが…」
findings.todokanai: "Y-You know～ it's just that I've been sleeping over at other places for quite some time now, so I've made it kind of a habit…"

findings.highlight: "That's for the sponsor. It's the sole condition for him to provide his support."
findings.evidenceJa:
「それはスポンサーに譲れ。
資金提供の絶対条件だ」
findings.explanation: Haruki calls himself the sponsor and makes surrendering the last slice his funding condition; the English refers to the sponsor as 'him,' implying a third person.
findings.japanese:
「それはスポンサーに譲れ。
資金提供の絶対条件だ」
findings.todokanai: "That's for the sponsor. It's the sole condition for him to provide his support."

findings.highlight: I can take control of you by using that information
findings.evidenceJa: こっちは逆にそういうの全部コントロールして、相手に逆の意図を誤解させるように仕向けるの
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she controls all of those signals in herself and thereby makes the other person misread her as having the opposite intention. The English says she uses observed information to control the opponent, replacing her actorly command of her own presentation—the skill demonstrated throughout the scene—with generic mind control.
findings.japanese:
「それだけじゃないよ。
こっちは逆にそういうの全部コントロールして、
相手に逆の意図を誤解させるように仕向けるの」
findings.todokanai: "And that's not all. I can take control of you by using that information and mislead you to think and act the way I want you to."

findings.highlight: The pointless conversation goes on and on, while our eyes never leave the cards.
findings.evidenceJa:
そのギリギリの駆け引きは、
お互い、カードから目を離さないまま行われた。
findings.explanation: Their exchange is described as a razor-edge piece of maneuvering; the English calls it a pointless conversation.
findings.japanese:
そのギリギリの駆け引きは、
お互い、カードから目を離さないまま行われた。
findings.todokanai: The pointless conversation goes on and on, while our eyes never leave the cards.

findings.highlight: Do you think it will backfire on me eventually?
findings.evidenceJa: あたしはまだ、ミイラ取りのままでいられてると思う？
findings.explanation: Chiaki invokes ミイラ取りがミイラになる: the mummy hunter becomes a mummy, or the person who set out to capture someone becomes captured herself. She asks whether Haruki thinks she is still merely the hunter—whether she has avoided falling for her own subject. The English reduces this present identity question to a vague possibility that something may backfire eventually.
findings.japanese:
「ね、春希…
あたしはまだ、ミイラ取りのままでいられてると思う？」
findings.todokanai: "Hey, Haruki… Do you think it will backfire on me eventually?"

findings.highlight: I'm able to properly let my feelings out
findings.evidenceJa: けれど、ちゃんと相手には伝わったから。
findings.explanation: Haruki consoles himself that, despite failing to say the crucial words himself, the intended meaning properly reached the other person. The English says only that he was able to let his feelings out, replacing successful reception by Chiaki with successful self-expression.
findings.japanese: けれど、ちゃんと相手には伝わったから。
findings.todokanai: Even so, I'm able to properly let my feelings out.

findings.highlight: "That's impossible… I have confidence in that myself."
findings.evidenceJa:
「あるわけないだろそんなこと…
それがわかる程度には関わった自信はある」
findings.explanation: Haruki echoes Chiaki's earlier formulation that he is confident he has been involved with her enough to know she is no wicked woman; the English reduces this to confidence in himself.
findings.japanese:
「あるわけないだろそんなこと…
それがわかる程度には関わった自信はある」
findings.todokanai: "That's impossible… I have confidence in that myself."

findings.highlight: That beautiful feeling of yours
findings.evidenceJa: 物語にしても遜色のない、あんたたちの綺麗な想いを知ってるよ？
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she knows the beautiful feelings belonging to all of 'you'—あんたたち, the people in Haruki's story—feelings worthy of a story. The English reduces this explicitly plural emotional structure to one beautiful feeling belonging to Haruki alone.
findings.japanese:
「物語にしても遜色のない、
あんたたちの綺麗な想いを知ってるよ？」
findings.todokanai: "That beautiful feeling of yours that's on par with any of the world's many stories, you know what I mean?"

findings.highlight: Happy New Year
findings.evidenceJa: 『良いお年を』
findings.explanation: Before the year ends, 良いお年を wishes someone a good coming year. 'Happy New Year' is the greeting used after the new year has arrived, so the English places Koharu's earlier farewell on the wrong side of the holiday.
findings.japanese: 『良いお年を』
findings.todokanai: "Happy New Year."

findings.highlight: The architect who had set up the moat around my schedule last week to be filled in
findings.evidenceJa: 先週のバイトの時に埋められていた外堀の、現場監督がそこにいた…
findings.explanation: Haruki extends 外堀を埋める, the idiom for removing someone's alternatives or laying the groundwork around them: the 'site foreman' who had filled in his outer moat last week is standing there. The English mechanically combines an architect, a moat, a schedule, and a future passive construction into a sentence with no coherent image or proposition.
findings.japanese:
先週のバイトの時に埋められていた外堀の、
現場監督がそこにいた…
findings.todokanai: The architect who had set up the moat around my schedule last week to be filled in is right here…

findings.highlight: It's just that my original intent was to give up on this little bit of rehabilitation once Sugiura caught me.
findings.evidenceJa:
ただ、杉浦に捕まった時点で、
本来はこのリハビリは諦めるべきだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he ought to have abandoned this rehabilitation once Koharu caught him; the English makes that his original intent.
findings.japanese:
ただ、杉浦に捕まった時点で、
本来はこのリハビリは諦めるべきだった。
findings.todokanai: It's just that my original intent was to give up on this little bit of rehabilitation once Sugiura caught me.

findings.highlight: "I take it that everything you've ordered is to your liking? In that case, please enjoy your meal."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ご注文の品、以上でよろしいでしょうか？
では、ごゆっくりどうぞ」
findings.explanation: Koharu confirms whether that is the customer's full order; the English asks whether everything ordered is to the customer's liking.
findings.japanese:
「ご注文の品、以上でよろしいでしょうか？
では、ごゆっくりどうぞ」
findings.todokanai: "I take it that everything you've ordered is to your liking? In that case, please enjoy your meal."

findings.highlight: She grew distant from others because of me… Those around her accidentally got dragged into this mess
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女のことでねじくれてさ…俺の近くにいる人たちまで無差別に巻き込んで
findings.explanation: Haruki says that he became twisted over Setsuna and indiscriminately dragged even the people around himself into it. The English makes Setsuna grow distant from others and makes people around her get dragged in accidentally, reversing the damaged person's agency, the affected social circle, and Haruki's self-accusation.
findings.japanese:
「彼女のことでねじくれてさ…
俺の近くにいる人たちまで無差別に巻き込んで」
findings.todokanai: "She grew distant from others because of me… Those around her accidentally got dragged into this mess thanks to me."

findings.highlight: an important junior of mine
findings.evidenceJa: 大事な教え子
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Mihoko an important pupil he taught. The English calls her his junior, erasing the tutor–student relationship on which his responsibility, her use of 'Sensei,' and Koharu's position as the pupil's friend all depend.
findings.japanese:
「昔なじみや、大学の友達や、バイト先の同僚や、
それに…大事な教え子とか、さ」
findings.todokanai: "Close friends from the past, friends from university, fellow part-timers, and also… an important junior of mine."

findings.highlight: The best friend of an important former student of mine, who's also a colleague from work.
findings.evidenceJa:
大事な教え子の親友で、
バイト先の同僚で。
findings.explanation: Koharu is the best friend of Haruki's important pupil; the English calls the pupil a former student.
findings.japanese:
大事な教え子の親友で、
バイト先の同僚で。
findings.todokanai: The best friend of an important former student of mine, who's also a colleague from work.

findings.highlight: making me choke up a bit too
findings.evidenceJa: 杉浦がそのとき放った恨みの声は、ほんの少しだけ鼻にかかっていた。
findings.explanation: Koharu's resentful voice is slightly nasal, revealing that she herself is near tears. The English instead makes Haruki choke up, moving the emotional leak from Koharu to him and suppressing her personal investment in the exchange.
findings.japanese:
そんな大事な杉浦がそのとき放った恨みの声は、
ほんの少しだけ鼻にかかっていた。
findings.todokanai: Sugiura, who's so important to me, started voicing her resentment, making me choke up a bit too.

findings.highlight: Sugiura was completely in line with what everyone else had told her. I understand that she's only just now starting to form her own opinion
findings.evidenceJa: その時の杉浦が、一般論に混ぜて、ほんの少しだけ個別論にまで踏み込んでいることも、ちゃんとわかってた。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he understood that, back then, Koharu had mixed a small, personally specific appeal into what she framed as general principles. The English invents other people's prior opinions and says Koharu is only now beginning to form her own, reversing both the time and the nature of her earlier confession.
findings.japanese:
その時の杉浦が、一般論に混ぜて、
ほんの少しだけ個別論にまで踏み込んでいることも、
ちゃんとわかってた。
findings.todokanai: Back then, Sugiura was completely in line with what everyone else had told her. I understand that she's only just now starting to form her own opinion.

findings.highlight: As usual, she's quite straightforward.
findings.evidenceJa: 相変わらず、なんて前向きな。
findings.explanation: Koharu is extraordinarily positive and forward-looking; the English calls her straightforward.
findings.japanese: 相変わらず、なんて前向きな。
findings.todokanai: As usual, she's quite straightforward.

findings.highlight: I've got this feeling for the first time since I was born, so I can't let it go to waste now.
findings.evidenceJa:
せっかくこの世に生を受けた今の感情を、
そのまま止めてしまうなんてことはしたくない。
findings.explanation: Haruki's newly born feeling becomes a feeling he has had for the first time since he himself was born.
findings.japanese:
せっかくこの世に生を受けた今の感情を、
そのまま止めてしまうなんてことはしたくない。
findings.todokanai: I've got this feeling for the first time since I was born, so I can't let it go to waste now.

findings.highlight: where I used to work
findings.evidenceJa: そこが元から俺のバイト先だったってだけ
findings.explanation: Haruki says the place Koharu chose had already been his part-time workplace. The English says it was where he used to work, falsely implying that he no longer works there during a scene in which he has just taken a kitchen shift.
findings.japanese:
「杉浦が卒業旅行のためにバイトを始めたら、
そこが元から俺のバイト先だったってだけ。
…それ以外の理由はないよ」
findings.todokanai: "Sugiura's working part-time to fund her graduation trip, and that place just happened to be where I used to work… That's all there is to it."

findings.highlight: I was afraid of letting others get too close to me
findings.evidenceJa: 自分に向けられる好意が怖かったから。…特に、距離が近ければ近いほど
findings.explanation: Haruki was afraid of affection directed at him, especially when it came from someone already close to him. The English changes this into fear of allowing closeness itself, obscuring why Mihoko's existing trust and romantic interest—not mere intimacy—triggered his cruelty.
findings.japanese:
「あの時の俺はさ、
自分に向けられる好意が怖かったから。
…特に、距離が近ければ近いほど」
findings.todokanai: "At that time, I was afraid of letting others get too close to me. …The closer we were, the stronger my fear became."

findings.highlight: the two girls for whom I harbored equally sincere affections
findings.evidenceJa: 俺に好意を向けてくれた女の子と、俺が好意を抱いた女の子たちと
findings.explanation: The source names the girl who showed Haruki affection and the girl or girls toward whom he felt affection; it does not say those feelings were equal. The English explicitly invents 'equally sincere' love for two girls, imposing a balance on the central triangle that the Japanese carefully does not assert.
findings.japanese:
俺に好意を向けてくれた女の子と、
俺が好意を抱いた女の子たちと、
馬鹿みたいに楽しかった学園祭のステージと。
findings.todokanai: Of the girl who delivered her affections to me, of the two girls for whom I harbored equally sincere affections for, and the performance during the school festival, where the three of us together enjoyed ourselves like fools.

findings.highlight: I don't think I'd ever understand how painful that must be
findings.evidenceJa: 学校を休むほどのショックを受けた繊細な心に、どれほど強い鞭を打ったのか、俺にはわからない。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he cannot know how savagely he lashed with a whip at a delicate heart already shocked enough to miss school. The English turns this self-indicting violent agency into a passive inability to understand Mihoko's pain.
findings.japanese:
学校を休むほどのショックを受けた繊細な心に、
どれほど強い鞭を打ったのか、俺にはわからない。
findings.todokanai: Something shocking enough to make her stop going to school… I don't think I'd ever understand how painful that must be.

findings.highlight: Apologizing to her would simply be making excuses
findings.evidenceJa: 謝りたかったなんて、とんだ詭弁。
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes that claiming he wanted to apologize was sophistry: his true purpose in arranging the meeting was to tell Mihoko why he rejected her and reject her clearly again. The English says an apology would itself be excuse-making, obscuring the distinction between his stated pretext and actual motive.
findings.japanese: 謝りたかったなんて、とんだ詭弁。
findings.todokanai: Apologizing to her would simply be making excuses.

findings.highlight: But that would mean openly rejecting Takeya's invitation.
findings.evidenceJa:
けれど、つまりそれって、
武也の誘いと思いっきりバッティングしてるってこと。
findings.explanation: The concert directly conflicts in time with Takeya's invitation; the English says attending would openly reject Takeya.
findings.japanese:
けれど、つまりそれって、
武也の誘いと思いっきりバッティングしてるってこと。
