findings.todokanai: And in order to answer those desires, Setsuna's body has been preparing for it for all these years…

findings.highlight: "Ah, ah… ahh～! Ii, uaah… ah… more, more…! Do it as if you were putting… three years' worth of emotions into it!"
findings.evidenceJa:
「あ、あ…っ、あ～っ！
ひ、い、ぅぁ…ぁ…もっと、もっと、ぉ…
三年分の強さで…抱きしめなくちゃならないんだよ」
findings.explanation: A release of physical strength is generalized into emotional release.
findings.japanese:
「あ、あ…っ、あ～っ！
ひ、い、ぅぁ…ぁ…もっと、もっと、ぉ…
三年分の強さで…抱きしめなくちゃならないんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, ah… ahh～! Ii, uaah… ah… more, more…! Do it as if you were putting… three years' worth of emotions into it!"

findings.highlight: if only you… sooner, sooner
findings.evidenceJa: もっと、もっと早く
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks for the current motion to become faster and faster. 'If only you… sooner' instead reads as regret that Haruki did not act at an earlier time.
findings.japanese:
「あああんっ、あっ、あ～っ！
そ、それを、それを…
もっと、もっと早く…うあぁぁぁぁんっ」
findings.todokanai: "Aaaaaahn, aah, aaaah～! I-If, if only you… sooner, sooner… aaaahnn…"

findings.highlight: sadistic desires
findings.evidenceJa: 支配欲
findings.explanation: Haruki names a desire to possess or control Setsuna among his conflicting impulses. The translation turns that into sadism, adding pleasure in cruelty that the source does not assert.
findings.japanese:
体の快感と、心の痛みと、
支配欲と、罪悪感とが、
俺の中で混ざりあい、ますます雪菜を離せなくなる。
findings.todokanai: Carnal pleasures, heartache, sadistic desires, and guilt all swirl around inside me, gradually making me unable to let go of Setsuna.

findings.highlight: no one else would ever think of laying eyes on her
findings.evidenceJa: 俺以外の誰もが、もう手も触れられなくなるくらいに
findings.explanation: Haruki wants to mark Setsuna so completely that no one else could touch her. The translation changes physical touch and possession to merely looking at her.
findings.japanese:
雪菜を、汚したい。
俺以外の誰もが、もう手も触れられなくなるくらいに。
findings.todokanai: I want to… defile her. To the point where no one else would ever think of laying eyes on her.

findings.highlight: stain her with my color
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜に、染められたい
findings.explanation: Haruki wants Setsuna to color or stain him so completely that nobody else can move his heart. The translation reverses the direction and makes him stain Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
雪菜に、染められたい。
もう、俺が誰にも心を動かされることのないくらいに。
findings.todokanai: I want to… stain her with my color. To the point where no one else would ever make my heart race again.

findings.highlight: We both took our clothes off and entered the bathroom together, and I had initially planned to pass Setsuna the body wash.
findings.evidenceJa:
服を脱いで、一緒に浴室に入り、
雪菜にボディーソープを渡したはずだった。
findings.explanation: Passing body wash to Haruki becomes planning how to use it.
findings.japanese:
服を脱いで、一緒に浴室に入り、
雪菜にボディーソープを渡したはずだった。
findings.todokanai: We both took our clothes off and entered the bathroom together, and I had initially planned to pass Setsuna the body wash.

findings.highlight: she begins to move in an up-and-down rhythm
findings.evidenceJa: ぬめりを伴って上下に律動する
findings.explanation: Haruki's penis moves rhythmically in the slippery cleft of Setsuna's buttocks. The source does not make Setsuna initiate the up-and-down movement, as the translation does.
findings.japanese:
雪菜のお尻の割れ目に俺のものが挟み込まれ、

findings.evidenceJa: 強引に抱きしめ唇を重ねると
findings.explanation: Once the door closes, Haruki forcefully embraces and kisses Setsuna; she then closes her eyes and yields. The translation makes Setsuna initiate the forceful embrace and kiss.
findings.japanese:
ドアを閉めた途端、強引に抱きしめ唇を重ねると、
あっという間に甘い吐息とともに目を閉じて、
ゆっくりと俺に身を委ねてきた。
findings.todokanai: Before the door even closed, she forcefully hugged me and pressed her lips against mine. Shutting her eyes as she let out her sweet breath after a few moments, she slowly surrendered herself to me.

findings.highlight: placed on a one-week curfew
findings.evidenceJa: 一週間、雪菜は外出禁止令を食らってた
findings.explanation: Setsuna was forbidden to go out for one week. A curfew would still permit daytime outings and changes the father's concrete punishment, which the following exchange explains in detail.
findings.japanese: 先週一週間、雪菜は外出禁止令を食らってた…
findings.todokanai: Setsuna had been placed on a one-week curfew since last week…

findings.highlight: had all three of her meals there
findings.evidenceJa: 三食振舞ってくれた
findings.explanation: Setsuna came in the morning and cooked or served Haruki all three meals before shifting into night mode. The translation says she ate all three meals there, reversing the domestic action and its beneficiary.
findings.japanese:
ところが先週末、
雪菜は朝から俺の部屋に来て三食振舞ってくれた挙げ句、
帰るよう諭す俺の前で『夜モード』になってしまった。
findings.todokanai: Nonetheless, Setsuna had arrived at my place early in the morning last weekend, had all three of her meals there, and would go into her "night mode" whenever I attempted to remonstrate her to return home.

findings.highlight: While we'd spent only ten seconds discussing our escape plan, it took us more than ten minutes to settle… a certain something else.
findings.evidenceJa:
脱走計画の打ち合わせが１０秒で、
それ以外の『突き合わせ』が１０分以上だった。
findings.explanation: The 打ち合わせ versus 突き合わせ wordplay is replaced with settling an unspecified something else.
findings.japanese:
脱走計画の打ち合わせが１０秒で、
それ以外の『突き合わせ』が１０分以上だった。
findings.todokanai: While we'd spent only ten seconds discussing our escape plan, it took us more than ten minutes to settle… a certain something else.

findings.highlight: I don't want the others seeing me do this.
findings.evidenceJa: 人には、見せられないんだ
findings.explanation: Haruki says the gift itself is something he cannot show other people, setting up its age, price, and meaning. The translation says people cannot see him perform the act of giving it, changing the secrecy mechanism and suspense object.
findings.japanese: 「人には、見せられないんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I don't want the others seeing me do this."

findings.highlight: If I start looking for another route now
findings.evidenceJa: 今から乗り継ぎだから
findings.explanation: Setsuna is waiting for the connecting bus and still has a transfer or connection ahead, which may make her later. The translation says she is looking for an alternate route, inventing rerouting rather than an ordinary connection.
findings.japanese:
「そっか…こっちは今、連絡バス待ち。
今から乗り継ぎだから、わたしの方が遅くなるかな…」
findings.todokanai: "Is that so… I'm still waiting for my bus. If I start looking for another route now, I might be late…"

findings.highlight: here in Paris
findings.evidenceJa: パリがもう凄い雪でさ
findings.explanation: Haruki has reached the Strasbourg station and says Paris had extremely heavy snow, explaining his delayed arrival. 'Here in Paris' wrongly leaves him in Paris immediately before he takes a taxi to the Strasbourg hotel.
findings.japanese:
「パリがもう凄い雪でさ、
今日中に着かないかと思ったよ」
findings.todokanai: "It's snowing really hard here in Paris. I didn't think I'd make it by today."

findings.highlight: Through my determination… I was able to catch up just in time.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の決心に、時間がついてきてくれた
findings.explanation: Haruki personifies time as having caught up with or cooperated with his decision, letting the proposal plan come together. The translation says his determination enabled him to catch up to time, reversing the sentence's agent and poetic relation.
findings.japanese: …俺の決心に、時間がついてきてくれた。
findings.todokanai: Through my determination… I was able to catch up just in time.

findings.highlight: I know I've been working hard.
findings.evidenceJa: はい…疲れました
findings.explanation: Haruki silently answers Hamada's formulaic 'thanks for your hard work' with 'Yes… I'm tired,' turning the workplace greeting literal. The translation makes him congratulate himself for working hard and loses the sarcastic call-and-response.
findings.japanese: はい…疲れました。
findings.todokanai: Yes… I know I've been working hard.

findings.highlight: will be sent to you in an attached file
findings.evidenceJa: 添付ファイルで送ってあるから
findings.explanation: Hamada says the detailed attachment has already been sent to Haruki's computer email address and orders him to review it. The translation makes the sending future, changing whether the work materials are already available.
findings.japanese:
『詳細はＰＣのメアドに添付ファイルで送ってあるから、
そっちをしっかり見ておくように。
とりあえずこちらは概要だけ』
findings.todokanai: "The detailed information will be sent to you in an attached file via email. I just want to summarize the most important points."

findings.highlight: I just simply don't want to believe it.
findings.evidenceJa: 当たり前の思い込み
findings.explanation: Haruki explains that he merely held the natural assumption that nobody but Setsuna could call his name in this foreign place. The translation replaces that mistaken premise with a conscious refusal to believe what he hears.
findings.japanese: そんな当たり前の思い込みがあっただけで。
findings.todokanai: I just simply don't want to believe it.

findings.highlight: would take approximately two hours
findings.evidenceJa: 特急で２時間半
findings.explanation: Haruki's stunned geographical calculation gives the Paris-to-Strasbourg express journey as roughly two and a half hours. The translation cuts the stated travel time to roughly two hours.
findings.japanese:
ここはフランス北東部の都市、ストラスブール。
パリから特急で２時間半くらい。
findings.todokanai: This is Strasbourg, a city located in the northeast of France. Taking a trip from Paris to here, even on an express train, would take approximately two hours.

findings.highlight: she went to the same school as you
findings.evidenceJa: 北原の同級生だった
findings.explanation: Hamada recalls that Kazusa was Haruki's classmate, a same-cohort relationship. The translation only says she attended the same school, weakening the precise past connection at the reveal.
findings.japanese:
『なにしろ取材対象は、
日本人ピアニストの冬馬かずさ。
確か北原の同級生だったよな？』
findings.todokanai: "Because the person you're interviewing is the Japanese pianist, Touma Kazusa. I recall she went to the same school as you, didn't she?"

findings.highlight: under the impression that I'm here to help on a rainy day
findings.evidenceJa: ただ『地獄に仏』とばかりに、早く制服に着替えるよう、更衣室を指差してくれるかもしれない。
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines the short-staffed restaurant welcoming his unexpected arrival like a Buddha appearing in hell—that is, as a godsend in desperate circumstances. The English invents helping on a rainy day, an unrelated situation that obscures why the staff would immediately send him to change into uniform.
findings.japanese:
唐突に訪れた俺のことを奇異に思わず、
ただ『地獄に仏』とばかりに、早く制服に着替えるよう、
更衣室を指差してくれるかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: My abrupt visit might instinctively strike them as unusual, but they'd probably direct me to the changing room and put me into uniform under the impression that I'm here to help on a rainy day.

findings.highlight: In terms of your mental state, that is!
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩はよくてもわたしがよくないんです！精神衛生上！
findings.explanation: Koharu says that even if Haruki is content to leave, she is not, because abandoning him would be bad for her own peace of mind. The English instead comments on Haruki's mental state, removing Koharu's explicit reason for chasing and caring for him.
findings.japanese:
「先輩はよくてもわたしがよくないんです！
精神衛生上！」
findings.todokanai: "You might think you're alright, but to me, you're not! In terms of your mental state, that is!"

findings.highlight: I'd have to tell her everything
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女は全てを知ろうとするだろう。
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts that Koharu would actively try to learn everything in exchange for giving him comfort. The English turns that into an obligation for Haruki to tell her everything, changing Koharu's interventionist agency.
findings.japanese:
けれど俺が心の安らぎを得るのと引き替えに、
彼女は全てを知ろうとするだろう。
findings.todokanai: In exchange for getting peace of mind, however, I'd have to tell her everything.

findings.highlight: She was desperately chasing after me… and in the end, she caught up to me.
findings.evidenceJa: 必死で、俺を追いかけてきてくれ…追いかけてきた。
findings.explanation: Haruki begins to think Koharu 'came after me for my sake' and then corrects himself to the neutral 'came after me'; the English changes this to chased and caught up.
findings.japanese: 必死で、俺を追いかけてきてくれ…追いかけてきた。
findings.todokanai: She was desperately chasing after me… and in the end, she caught up to me.

findings.highlight: That feels like a rip-off
findings.evidenceJa: アオムシで鯨を釣りやがって…
findings.explanation: Haruki jokes that the manager has caught a whale with a caterpillar: by forgiving one short absence, he has secured Koharu's labor beyond April. Calling this merely a rip-off deletes both sides of the deliberately absurd bait-versus-catch image and the joke about the manager's enormous return.
findings.japanese: アオムシで鯨を釣りやがって…
findings.todokanai: That feels like a rip-off…

findings.highlight: she's not a fan of warm beverages
findings.evidenceJa: 甘党じゃない代わりに猫舌だったか。
findings.explanation: 猫舌 means that Koharu is sensitive to food or drink being too hot, as her blowing on the canned coffee demonstrates. The English instead says she dislikes warm beverages, inventing a preference and missing the physical trait behind the beat.
findings.japanese: 甘党じゃない代わりに猫舌だったか。
findings.todokanai: It seems she's not a fan of warm beverages despite lacking a sweet tooth.

findings.highlight: you seem to be so serious all the time
findings.evidenceJa: 杉浦は…どんな時にでもまっすぐ来るよな。いい意味でも、悪い意味でも
findings.explanation: Haruki says Koharu always comes at things straight, for better or worse. She answers that Haruki is always twisted or contrary. The English makes her merely serious and, in the next line, him depressed, destroying the paired straight-versus-crooked characterization on which the exchange turns.
findings.japanese:
「杉浦は…どんな時にでもまっすぐ来るよな。
いい意味でも、悪い意味でも」
findings.todokanai: "You know… for better or worse, you seem to be so serious all the time, Sugiura."

findings.highlight: unhindered by the usual possibility of me giving a light retort and potentially causing the conversation to go nowhere
findings.evidenceJa: いつもみたいに軽く切り返せずに会話を詰まらせてしまう俺を、自分が話し続けることにより受け止めてくれてた。
findings.explanation: Haruki is the one unable to make his usual light rejoinders, so he lets the conversation stall; Koharu carries and accepts him by continuing to speak herself. The English says his usual rejoinders might cause the conversation to fail and portrays Koharu as simply unhindered, reversing the immediate conversational mechanics and obscuring her tact.
findings.japanese:
いつもみたいに軽く切り返せずに
会話を詰まらせてしまう俺を、
自分が話し続けることにより受け止めてくれてた。
findings.todokanai: She continues talking about her own life without stopping, unhindered by the usual possibility of me giving a light retort and potentially causing the conversation to go nowhere because of it.

findings.highlight: She went from directly intervening to influencing from the sidelines
findings.evidenceJa: 介入し続けるお節介から、介入しないことで焼くお節介に。
findings.explanation: Haruki contrasts her former meddling by continual intervention with a new kind of meddling expressed precisely by not intervening. 'Influencing from the sidelines' removes the paradoxical non-intervention and therefore the evidence of how Koharu's care has matured.
findings.japanese:
介入し続けるお節介から、
介入しないことで焼くお節介に。
findings.todokanai: She went from directly intervening to influencing from the sidelines.

findings.highlight: So it's not that "she's become a companion for me to talk to," but rather "she wants to be a companion for me to talk to," is it…
findings.evidenceJa: 『話し相手になってあげる』じゃなくて『話し相手になってもらう』か…
findings.explanation: Haruki notices that Koharu said not 'I'll be your conversation partner' but 'I'll have you be mine': she frames the company as something she receives from him, making her need reciprocal rather than patronizing. Both English clauses make Koharu the companion for Haruki, so the explicitly quoted grammatical distinction disappears.
findings.japanese:
『話し相手になってあげる』じゃなくて
『話し相手になってもらう』か…
findings.todokanai: So it's not that "she's become a companion for me to talk to," but rather "she wants to be a companion for me to talk to," is it…

findings.highlight: I can't force you two to date each other
findings.evidenceJa: 付き合えないのはしょうがないけれど、それでも先輩は彼女の憧れだったんです
findings.explanation: Koharu accepts that Haruki cannot date Mihoko, then reminds him that he was still the person Mihoko admired. The English changes this into Koharu's inability to force them together, relocating the constraint from Haruki's relationship decision to Koharu's influence.
findings.japanese:
「付き合えないのはしょうがないけれど、
それでも先輩は彼女の憧れだったんです」
findings.todokanai: "I can't force you two to date each other, but she still looks up to you."

findings.highlight: I want her to properly accept that
findings.evidenceJa: そのことはちゃんと受け止めて欲しいし、友達に戻って欲しいと思ってる
findings.explanation: Koharu wants Haruki, the person she is addressing, to acknowledge what Mihoko's admiration meant and to become her friend again. The English says Mihoko should accept it, reversing who Koharu is asking to face the emotional fact.
findings.japanese:
「そのことはちゃんと受け止めて欲しいし、
友達に戻って欲しいと思ってる」
findings.todokanai: "I want her to properly accept that and for the two of you to go back to being friends again."

findings.highlight: even more reliable as well
findings.evidenceJa: いつもの何倍も魅力的に…そして、いつも通りの頼もしい存在に映った。
findings.explanation: Koharu appears many times more attractive than usual yet as reliable as ever. The English makes both qualities increase, deleting the point that her new attractiveness coexists with the familiar dependability Haruki already trusted.
findings.japanese:
彼女は、いつもの何倍も魅力的に…
そして、いつも通りの頼もしい存在に映った。
findings.todokanai: She appears to be even much more attractive than usual… and even more reliable as well.

findings.highlight: hold onto it without offering any resistance
findings.evidenceJa: 杉浦の差し出した手を、何のてらいもなく握ることしかできなかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki takes Koharu's offered hand without self-consciousness or affected hesitation. The English says he offers no resistance, recasting his simple active acceptance as passive submission and changing the agency of the intimate gesture.
findings.japanese:
だから、杉浦の差し出した手を、
何のてらいもなく握ることしかできなかった。
findings.todokanai: That's why when Sugiura offered her hand, I couldn't do anything but hold onto it without offering any resistance.

findings.highlight: I've been telling the others about these things
findings.evidenceJa: わたしがあることないこと発信してるからこそ、みんながあなたに親しみ持ってくれてるんだけどなぁ。
findings.explanation: Nakagawa cheerfully admits to spreading both true and made-up stories about Koharu, claiming that this rumor mill is why the staff feel close to her. The English reduces this to telling them unspecified 'things,' deleting the self-incriminating comic characterization and the actual means by which familiarity was manufactured.
findings.japanese:
「わたしがあることないこと発信してるからこそ、
みんながあなたに親しみ持ってくれてるんだけどなぁ。
ちょっとは感謝してくれたって…」
findings.todokanai: "It's because I've been telling the others about these things that everyone's able to feel familiar with you. You could at least be a little grateful for that…"

findings.highlight: I don't plan to get along with everyone in my workplace
findings.evidenceJa: わたしは別に仕事で馴れ合いするつもりないですから
findings.explanation: Koharu says she has no intention of turning work into cozy social fraternization or an in-group clique. The English makes her say she does not intend to get along with anyone, changing a rigidly professional stance into broad antisocial hostility that the surrounding staff relationships contradict.
findings.japanese: 「わたしは別に仕事で馴れ合いするつもりないですから」
findings.todokanai: "I don't plan to get along with everyone in my workplace."

findings.highlight: pitying someone is also a form of affection
findings.evidenceJa: 人としての尊敬だって愛だけどね？憐れみだって恋だけどね？
findings.explanation: Nakagawa traps Koharu by insisting first that respect is 愛 and then, more provocatively, that pity is 恋—the specifically romantic word Koharu is trying to disavow. Rendering the second term as generic affection removes the escalation into romantic feeling and weakens the reason Koharu immediately retreats.
findings.japanese:
「人としての尊敬だって愛だけどね？
憐れみだって恋だけどね？」
findings.todokanai: "Respecting someone as a person is also a form of love, right? And pitying someone is also a form of affection, is it not?"

findings.highlight: If Senpai wants to talk about it, I'll be there
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩が言いたくなったら話してくれるはずです。それも約束しましたから
findings.explanation: Koharu says that when Haruki wants to speak, he is supposed to tell her, and that this too was part of their promise. The English substitutes the generic assurance that she will be there, erasing Haruki's promised future act of confiding in her—the new intimacy that alarms Takeya.
findings.japanese:
「先輩が言いたくなったら話してくれるはずです。
それも約束しましたから」
findings.todokanai: "If Senpai wants to talk about it, I'll be there. That's the promise we made."

findings.highlight: Even so, despite the fact that it invites the suspicion of those around her, she seems to continue making this mistake without any hesitation… No, I wouldn't call it a mistake.
findings.evidenceJa:
それでもこのコは、そういう周囲に勘繰られることを
まるで躊躇せずにやらかして…いや、してくれる。
findings.explanation: Haruki corrects 'she goes and does it' to the benefactive 'she does it for me'; the English corrects 'mistake' to 'not a mistake.'
findings.japanese:
それでもこのコは、そういう周囲に勘繰られることを
まるで躊躇せずにやらかして…いや、してくれる。
findings.todokanai: Even so, despite the fact that it invites the suspicion of those around her, she seems to continue making this mistake without any hesitation… No, I wouldn't call it a mistake.

findings.highlight: and continue spending time together after that?
findings.evidenceJa: 俺なんかと二人きりで新年を迎えて…って、続けるつもりだったのに。
findings.explanation: Haruki had intended to continue his unspoken question: 'Are you all right spending New Year's alone with someone like me…?' The English instead says Koharu wants to keep spending time with him after the shrine visit, inventing a further romantic plan that the Japanese neither states nor implies.
findings.japanese:
俺なんかと二人きりで新年を迎えて…
って、続けるつもりだったのに。
findings.todokanai: She wants to welcome the new year alone with someone like me… and continue spending time together after that?

findings.highlight: she went out of her way to make sure everyone around me did
findings.evidenceJa: 別に俺にだけ聞こえるように言うなら良かったんだけど、周りの人間にまる聞こえだったのはなぁ。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he would not have minded Koharu's skeptical remark if only he could hear it, but unfortunately everyone around them heard it too. The English invents deliberate public humiliation by claiming she intentionally made sure the crowd heard.
findings.japanese:
…別に俺にだけ聞こえるように言うなら良かったんだけど、
周りの人間にまる聞こえだったのはなぁ。
findings.todokanai: …I wouldn't have minded it if I was the only one who heard it, but I think she went out of her way to make sure everyone around me did.

findings.highlight: I told her about how the two of us had gone along with Sugiura's plan and arrived at what seemed to be a final chance for the two of us.
findings.evidenceJa:
杉浦の計略にまんまと引っかかることにより、
俺たち二人に最後のチャンスが巡ってきたことも。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his falling completely for Koharu's scheme brought the couple one last chance; the English says both Haruki and Setsuna went along with the scheme.
findings.japanese:
杉浦の計略にまんまと引っかかることにより、
俺たち二人に最後のチャンスが巡ってきたことも。
findings.todokanai: I told her about how the two of us had gone along with Sugiura's plan and arrived at what seemed to be a final chance for the two of us.

findings.highlight: the spider's thread that bound our hands together snapped
findings.evidenceJa: 手元からぷつんと蜘蛛の糸が切れてしまったことも。
findings.explanation: The image invokes Akutagawa's The Spider's Thread: the last slender means of salvation snaps just as Haruki's pretense is exposed. The source does not describe a thread binding Haruki's and Setsuna's hands together; that invented romantic tether misconstrues the allusion's rescue-and-fall logic.
findings.japanese:
…結局、俺の方はただの“フリ”だったってことがバレて、
手元からぷつんと蜘蛛の糸が切れてしまったことも。
findings.todokanai: …And I told her about how the spider's thread that bound our hands together snapped at the very moment I was caught in the act of being insincere.

findings.highlight: But that's just what I have to do
findings.evidenceJa: でもそれが、自分のしてきたことだから…
findings.explanation: Haruki says that this tangled history is nevertheless what he himself has done—the accumulated consequence of his choices. The English turns that retrospective ownership into a statement about what he must do next, replacing self-accounting with future obligation just before Koharu rejects his framing.
findings.japanese: 「でもそれが、自分のしてきたことだから…」
findings.todokanai: "But that's just what I have to do…"

findings.highlight: unable to leave her alone or approach her
findings.evidenceJa: 突き放すことも引き寄せることもできず、彼女の３０センチ前で同じように突っ立ってるだけで。
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot push the sobbing Koharu away or pull her toward him, so he remains frozen thirty centimeters in front of her. The English replaces those two opposed acts of physical contact with leaving her alone versus merely approaching, suppressing the intimacy and the precise paralysis of the scene.
findings.japanese:
そして俺は、突っ立ったまま、我慢もせず泣く杉浦を、
突き放すことも引き寄せることもできず、
彼女の３０センチ前で同じように突っ立ってるだけで。
findings.todokanai: And I could only remain in place about 30 centimeters away from her, unable to leave her alone or approach her as she could no longer hold back her tears.

findings.highlight: I'm really not pushing myself too hard
findings.evidenceJa: 別に自虐とかじゃないぞ。本当にそう思ってる
findings.explanation: Haruki assures Setsuna that his wish for them to avoid further regret is not self-deprecation and that he sincerely means it. The English instead denies overexerting himself, an unrelated claim that removes the tonal clarification from his carefully drafted New Year's message.
findings.japanese:
『…別に自虐とかじゃないぞ。
本当にそう思ってる』
findings.todokanai: "…I'm really not pushing myself too hard, you know. I really mean that."

findings.highlight: doesn't pay any mind to the noise surrounding her, much like she did in the past
findings.evidenceJa: それでも杉浦は、もう以前のように、周囲の声を気にしなくなってしまった。
findings.explanation: Koharu no longer worries about other people's comments the way she did before; her behavior has changed. The English says her present disregard is much like her past behavior, reversing the before-and-after contrast and erasing Haruki's observation that her boundaries around him have shifted.
findings.japanese:
それでも杉浦は、もう以前のように、
周囲の声を気にしなくなってしまった。
findings.todokanai: But Sugiura doesn't pay any mind to the noise surrounding her, much like she did in the past.

findings.highlight: With an expression so sullen it's hard for me to watch, Sugiura stares at her food and pokes at it without even taking so much as a bite.
findings.evidenceJa:
杉浦は、こっちがいたたまれなくなるくらい
寂しそうな表情で、目の前の料理をつついては、
そのまま口に運ばずにぼうっと見つめてる。
findings.explanation: Koharu's expression is painfully lonely; the English calls it sullen, which can suggest resentment.
findings.japanese:
杉浦は、こっちがいたたまれなくなるくらい
寂しそうな表情で、目の前の料理をつついては、
そのまま口に運ばずにぼうっと見つめてる。
findings.todokanai: With an expression so sullen it's hard for me to watch, Sugiura stares at her food and pokes at it without even taking so much as a bite.

findings.highlight: the absolute lack of emotion she showed
findings.evidenceJa: 『成功祈ってます』に込められた感情が、何も見えてこなかった戸惑いのせいで。
findings.explanation: Haruki is unsettled because he cannot discern what emotion Koharu has put into 'I hope it works out.' The English asserts that she showed absolutely no emotion, replacing his fear of an unreadable feeling with emotional blankness and foreclosing the jealousy he is afraid to name.
findings.japanese:
『成功祈ってます』に込められた感情が、
何も見えてこなかった戸惑いのせいで。
findings.todokanai: Because I was so thrown off by the absolute lack of emotion she showed when she said, "I pray for your success."

findings.highlight: Your chance has finally come… after all
findings.evidenceJa: 今、そんな話することないじゃないですか。せっかく………なのに
findings.explanation: Koharu objects that they need not discuss Mihoko now, trailing off over the fact that she and Haruki finally have this time together. The English assigns the unfinished せっかく to Haruki's chance with Setsuna, making Koharu encourage the very romantic development whose interruption of their dinner has just distressed her.
findings.japanese:
「今、そんな話することないじゃないですか。
せっかく………なのに」
findings.todokanai: "Right now is not the time for this, is it? Your chance has finally come… after all."

findings.highlight: What a coincidence
findings.evidenceJa: 偶然…じゃ
findings.explanation: Haruki begins to say that their meeting is not a coincidence, prompting Setsuna to answer that it is only half a coincidence because she predicted his arrival time. The English makes him affirm that it is a coincidence, contradicting her immediate qualification and reversing his recognition that she partly waited for him.
findings.japanese: 「偶然…じゃ」
findings.todokanai: "…What a coincidence."

findings.highlight: "If only I'd studied hard and acquired a recommendation like you did… My parents have been really bugging me about how I can't retake my entrance exams. All our savings got eaten up by my sister, after all."
findings.evidenceJa:
「やっぱお前みたいに頑張って推薦取っとけば…
ウチ一浪までって親に釘刺されてるんだよなぁ。
貯金は全部姉ちゃんが食い潰しちゃってるし」
findings.explanation: Takahiro says his parents permit no more than one additional year as a ronin applicant; the English says he cannot retake the entrance exams at all.
findings.japanese:
「やっぱお前みたいに頑張って推薦取っとけば…
ウチ一浪までって親に釘刺されてるんだよなぁ。
貯金は全部姉ちゃんが食い潰しちゃってるし」
findings.todokanai: "If only I'd studied hard and acquired a recommendation like you did… My parents have been really bugging me about how I can't retake my entrance exams. All our savings got eaten up by my sister, after all."

findings.highlight: the man I wanted to hug the most
findings.evidenceJa: 今アンケート取ったら抱かれたい男ナンバー１！
findings.explanation: 抱かれたい男 is the stock ranking of the man women most want to be held by or sleep with, and Nakagawa bawdily declares Haruki number one as she clings to him. 'Wanted to hug' sanitizes the sexual joke into innocent affection and weakens the deliberately unprofessional welcome.
findings.japanese:
「うおおお北原さ～ん愛してる～。
今アンケート取ったら抱かれたい男ナンバー１！」
findings.todokanai: "Ooohhh, Kitahara-san～! I love you～! You would be the man I wanted to hug the most if I had to take a questionnaire right now!"

findings.highlight: My usual pace would be faster
findings.evidenceJa: いつもは俺を早足で置いてこうとするし、何かしら俺の穴を見つけては説教を始めるのに。
findings.explanation: Ordinarily Koharu walks fast enough to try to leave Haruki behind while lecturing him. The English assigns the faster usual pace to Haruki, reversing who drives their physical rhythm and obscuring why her slow, trailing walk signals that something is wrong.
findings.japanese:
いつもは俺を早足で置いてこうとするし、
何かしら俺の穴を見つけては説教を始めるのに。
findings.todokanai: My usual pace would be faster, and she would start lecturing me the very moment she found any openings she could exploit.

findings.highlight: You two, why don't you say something!?
findings.evidenceJa: お前ら言いくるめられようとしてるだろ！？
findings.explanation: Haruki accuses Satou and Nakagawa of being on the verge of letting Koharu talk them around. The English merely asks them to speak, deleting the joke that their silence is already capitulation to her neatly prepared argument and obscuring why Haruki alone continues resisting.
findings.japanese: 「お前ら言いくるめられようとしてるだろ！？」
findings.todokanai: "You two, why don't you say something!?"

findings.highlight: Something suddenly clicked somewhere in my mind
findings.evidenceJa: 頭のどこかで、一つの鍵が外れそうになっていた。
findings.explanation: At first, a lock in Haruki's mind is only about to come undone as he suspects the missing former class representative is Koharu; at line 60 he finally hears the lock release when Takahiro names Mihoko instead, and line 61 says the sound came from a slightly shifted location. The English makes something fully click already here and then click again at line 60, collapsing the suspense and the deliberately repeated lock mechanism.
findings.japanese: 頭のどこかで、一つの鍵が外れそうになっていた。
findings.todokanai: Something suddenly clicked somewhere in my mind.

findings.highlight: she's aiming for a private university
findings.evidenceJa: 美穂子、成績いいし、それに私立だから、少しくらいは融通利くと思うし
findings.explanation: Koharu says Mihoko has good grades and that their high school is private, so the school may have some administrative latitude about her attendance and graduation. The English instead says Mihoko is aiming for a private university, which provides no reason for the high school to accommodate her and misidentifies the relevant institution.
findings.japanese:
「あ、いえ、多分そんなことは…
美穂子、成績いいし、それに私立だから、
少しくらいは融通利くと思うし」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, no, I don't think that will be the case… Mihoko has good grades and she's aiming for a private university, after all, so I imagine there'll be room to accommodate her."

findings.highlight: he ran away all of a sudden, so I panicked and chased after him
findings.evidenceJa: あの人も意地張って逃げるもんだから、わたしも頭に来ちゃって、制服のまま店の外に出て、駅前追いかけてさぁ
findings.explanation: Koharu explains that Haruki stubbornly fled and that this made her angry enough to run after him in uniform. The English changes stubbornness into suddenness and her anger into panic, materially rewriting the confrontational, meddlesome impulse she is trying to explain to Mihoko.
findings.japanese:
「…うん。で、あの人も意地張って逃げるもんだから、
わたしも頭に来ちゃって、制服のまま店の外に出て、
駅前追いかけてさぁ」
findings.todokanai: "…Right. Well, he ran away all of a sudden, so I panicked and chased after him while still in my uniform, all the way to the front of the station."

findings.highlight: This is what it takes to be honest to absolutely everyone
findings.evidenceJa: そっかぁ…『誰に対しての誠実』って、こういうことか。ほんと、わたしもまだまだだね
findings.explanation: Koharu realizes that the question is 'honesty toward whom': full disclosure may be honest toward Mihoko but betray Haruki. The English turns this conflict between incompatible loyalties into the impossible ideal of being honest to everyone, losing the ethical distinction that leads her to choose silence.
findings.japanese:
「そっかぁ…『誰に対しての誠実』って、こういうことか。
ほんと、わたしもまだまだだね」
findings.todokanai: "I see… This is what it takes to be honest to absolutely everyone. I guess I still have a long way to go."

findings.highlight: if you keep that sour face up
findings.evidenceJa: これ以上杉浦が辛い顔してたら、俺が直接矢田さんと話そうとするかもしれない
findings.explanation: Haruki threatens to intervene if Koharu continues looking pained or distressed. 'Sour face' suggests irritation or bad temper, changing the suffering that motivates his offer and miscoloring her emotional state after the fight.
findings.japanese:
「だからさ…これ以上杉浦が辛い顔してたら、
俺が直接矢田さんと話そうとするかもしれない」
findings.todokanai: "That's why… if you keep that sour face up, Sugiura, I may have to go talk to Yada-san myself."

findings.highlight: I couldn't stand the thought of not having you by my side
findings.evidenceJa: それでも俺、あのときは杉浦が必要だった。君がいなくちゃダメだった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that at that time he needed Koharu and could not have managed without her. The English changes practical and emotional dependence during his collapse into an aversion to the thought of her absence beside him, a more possessive romantic declaration than the source supports.
findings.japanese:
「それでも俺、あのときは杉浦が必要だった。
君がいなくちゃダメだった」
findings.todokanai: "Even so, I needed you back then, Sugiura. I couldn't stand the thought of not having you by my side."

findings.highlight: the proof of her own nobility
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の情けなさが露見した瞬間には、自分が手に入れた優位を、嬉しそうに笑う。
findings.explanation: When Haruki's helplessness is exposed, Koharu happily smiles at the advantage or upper hand she has gained by being needed. The English calls this proof of her nobility, turning a teasingly unequal relational position into moral virtue and obscuring what makes her laugh.
findings.japanese:
それでも杉浦は、
俺の情けなさが露見した瞬間には、
自分が手に入れた優位を、嬉しそうに笑う。
findings.todokanai: The moment she saw the pathetic side of me, as well as the proof of her own nobility, Sugiura smiled happily.

findings.highlight: She hasn't forgiven me, and I haven't even attempted to gain her approval
findings.evidenceJa: 許してもらってないのに。認めてもらおうとしてすらいなかったのに。
findings.explanation: The immediate issue is Haruki's sudden use of 小春 at line 186: he has not received permission for first-name address and had not even tried to ask. The English turns 許す into forgiving a wrongdoing, obscuring the social boundary whose crossing prompts Koharu to answer with 春希先輩.
findings.japanese:
許してもらってないのに。
認めてもらおうとしてすらいなかったのに。
findings.todokanai: She hasn't forgiven me, and I haven't even attempted to gain her approval.

findings.highlight: if we want to overcome this together
findings.evidenceJa: だから、一緒に踏み越えれば…
findings.explanation: After they exchange first names, Haruki thinks that if they cross the boundary together, neither has to retreat alone from the breach in formality. The English makes this a generic wish to overcome their troubles together, deleting the linguistic and relational line they have just stepped across.
findings.japanese: だから、一緒に踏み越えれば…
findings.todokanai: That's why, if we want to overcome this together…

findings.highlight: My fault…? I see… So it is my fault
findings.evidenceJa: 逆ギレ…？そっか…逆ギレしてるんだ、わたし…？
findings.explanation: Koharu repeats Ako's term 逆ギレ—lashing out when accused or angrily turning blame back—and dazedly recognizes that this is how her laughter looks. The English instead makes her accept that the whole situation is her fault, replacing her stunned recognition of her own emotional behavior with a direct confession of culpability.
findings.japanese:
「逆ギレ…？
そっか…逆ギレしてるんだ、わたし…？」
findings.todokanai: "My fault…? I see… So it is my fault…"

findings.highlight: so I just couldn't resist answering your call
findings.evidenceJa: 電話で雑談するの、本当に久しぶりだから勝手が掴めなくて
findings.explanation: Haruki apologizes for being boring because it has been so long since he made casual telephone conversation that he cannot get the hang of it. The English says the long interval made him unable to resist answering, an unrelated impulse that neither explains his poor storytelling nor answers Koharu's complaint.
findings.japanese:
「つまんなくて悪かったな。
電話で雑談するの、本当に久しぶりだから
勝手が掴めなくて」
findings.todokanai: "Sorry if I'm boring you. It's been a long time since I've had a casual conversation on the phone, so I just couldn't resist answering your call."

findings.highlight: I'm feeling quite famished because of that
findings.evidenceJa: 勉強もさっきからやってたって。おかげでお腹がたぷたぷになっちゃった
findings.explanation: Io says they have been studying there and, as a result of repeatedly refilling drinks, her stomach is now sloshing full. The English says studying has made her hungry, reversing fullness into hunger and destroying Haruki's next joke that their stated activity and its actual result do not match.
findings.japanese:
「勉強もさっきからやってたって。
おかげでお腹がたぷたぷになっちゃった」
findings.todokanai: "We've been studying for quite a while earlier. I'm feeling quite famished because of that."

findings.highlight: They just wouldn't stop going on and on
findings.evidenceJa: 悪いっ、遅くなった！なかなか話が切り上げられなくて…
findings.explanation: Haruki apologizes because he himself could not find a way to cut the conversation short. The English blames Takeya and Io for refusing to stop talking, exculpating Haruki from the delay that left Koharu waiting and changes the reason for his apology.
findings.japanese:
「悪いっ、遅くなった！
なかなか話が切り上げられなくて…」
findings.todokanai: "Sorry for being late! They just wouldn't stop going on and on during our conversation…"

findings.highlight: It felt unnatural when we parted our lips and stopped kissing, so I closed the distance again
findings.evidenceJa: 別れ際にキスをしない方が不自然なことになり、本当にさり気なく、唇を寄せるようになる。
findings.explanation: Kissing at the moment they part has already become so customary that not doing it would feel unnatural, and they now bring their lips together casually. The English instead describes separating during one kiss and immediately resuming it, erasing the evidence that a repeated clandestine goodbye ritual has developed between meetings.
findings.japanese:
別れ際にキスをしない方が不自然なことになり、
本当にさり気なく、唇を寄せるようになる。
findings.todokanai: It felt unnatural when we parted our lips and stopped kissing, so I closed the distance again without thinking.

findings.highlight: guiding her tongue to the back of my throat
findings.evidenceJa: 本能のままに小春の唾液を搾り取って、自分の喉の奥まで舌を伝って運び込んだりしない。
findings.explanation: Haruki describes extracting Koharu's saliva and using his own tongue to carry it to the back of his throat. The English instead guides Koharu's tongue itself to the back of his throat, inventing a substantially different physical action in an otherwise explicit, sequential description.
findings.japanese:
その熱い口中を蹂躙したり、
本能のままに小春の唾液を搾り取って、
自分の喉の奥まで舌を伝って運び込んだりしない。
findings.todokanai: I wouldn't be imposing myself upon her warm mouth and guiding her tongue to the back of my throat as if on instinct to indulge in her saliva like this.

findings.highlight: She even spread the rumor to other schools
findings.evidenceJa: あいつらなんか大喜びでさ…交流試合やってた他校の連中にまでメール流してんの。
findings.explanation: The subject is Matsui and the other former club members: they are delighted by Koharu's disgrace and are circulating the email even to players at other schools. The English switches from that hostile group to a singular 'she,' obscuring the coordinated retaliation that explains why the rumor has spread so far.
findings.japanese:
「あいつらなんか大喜びでさ…
交流試合やってた他校の連中にまでメール流してんの。
副キャプテン、あっちの男子にも人気あったし」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, her whole group seems overjoyed… She even spread the rumor to other schools who participated in the interleague match. The vice-captain was popular with the boys there too, after all."

findings.highlight: always right before midnight
findings.evidenceJa: 必ず日付が変わる時間に掛かってくる。
findings.explanation: Koharu always calls at the time the date changes—that is, at midnight. The English relocates every call to before midnight, contradicting the immediately stated 00:15 time during a thirty-minute call and breaking the precisely described ritual around which Haruki now structures his studying.
findings.japanese:
要するに、毎日３０分。
必ず日付が変わる時間に掛かってくる。
findings.todokanai: More precisely, for 30 minutes every day. And always right before midnight.

findings.highlight: before she decided to take matters into her own hands
findings.evidenceJa: 小春は、俺がこうして太鼓判を押す前から、俺を救うためにあいつらを頼ってた。
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes that Koharu had already relied on Takeya and Io to save him before he now gave them his personal seal of approval. The English invents a later decision by Koharu to 'take matters into her own hands,' replacing the actual temporal contrast and weakening Haruki's recognition that her judgment of his friends preceded his endorsement.
findings.japanese:
小春は、俺がこうして太鼓判を押す前から、
俺を救うためにあいつらを頼ってた。
findings.todokanai: Koharu had sought out those two for help in order to save me before she decided to take matters into her own hands.

findings.highlight: spoken through clenched teeth
findings.evidenceJa: 一字一句、互いに噛みしめながら紡いでいく不器用な会話。
findings.explanation: The two awkwardly weave the conversation while each carefully weighs and absorbs every single word. 'Spoken through clenched teeth' conventionally signals anger or hostility, imposing the opposite emotional register on an exchange defined by tenderness, hesitation, and mutual self-denial.
findings.japanese:
昔の長電話みたいに自然と言葉が湧いてくることのない、
一字一句、互いに噛みしめながら紡いでいく不器用な会話。
findings.todokanai: Unlike my long telephone conversations three years ago where words came out naturally, now every word and phrase is awkward, and spoken through clenched teeth.

findings.highlight: "Whatever. In any case, I'll be studying from now until Monday morning. I don't think I'll be able to forgive myself in more ways than one otherwise."
findings.evidenceJa:
「何とでも言え。
とにかく今から月曜の朝までずっと勉強。
でなけりゃ各方面に申し訳が立たん」
findings.explanation: Haruki says he otherwise could not answer to or face the various people concerned; the English says he could not forgive himself 'in more ways than one.'
findings.japanese:
「何とでも言え。
とにかく今から月曜の朝までずっと勉強。
でなけりゃ各方面に申し訳が立たん」
findings.todokanai: "Whatever. In any case, I'll be studying from now until Monday morning. I don't think I'll be able to forgive myself in more ways than one otherwise."

findings.highlight: many far more appropriate methods that she could have opted for
findings.evidenceJa: こんな目立つところで武也に見とがめられるより、よっぽど上手い方法なんかいくらでも考えついたのに。
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that, had Koharu phoned him, he could have devised any number of better ways to meet than letting Takeya spot her in such a conspicuous place. The English makes those alternatives Koharu's responsibility, converting his instinct to manage and conceal their meeting into criticism of her poor choice.
findings.japanese:
こんな目立つところで武也に見とがめられるより、
よっぽど上手い方法なんかいくらでも考えついたのに。
findings.todokanai: And to think there were many far more appropriate methods that she could have opted for rather than appearing here in such a conspicuous place and having Takeya notice her.

findings.highlight: Her eyes widen in surprise
findings.evidenceJa: 目を見開いたり、戸惑ったり、迷いを見せたりはしなかった。
findings.explanation: Koharu does not widen her eyes, become confused, or show hesitation when Haruki warns that going farther means they cannot stop. The English explicitly makes her eyes widen in surprise before retaining only the absence of hesitation, erasing the striking composure with which she receives the sexual warning.
findings.japanese:
目を見開いたり、戸惑ったり、
迷いを見せたりはしなかった。
findings.todokanai: Her eyes widen in surprise, but they show no hesitation.

findings.highlight: I can't really understand the true meaning behind her words
findings.evidenceJa: 相変わらず言葉の真意はきつかったけど、その声の柔らかさが、俺を安心させてくれる。
findings.explanation: Haruki understands that the real import of Koharu's words is as cutting as ever, but the softness of her voice reassures him that she is not angry. The English instead says he cannot understand what she means, replacing the deliberate contrast between harsh content and gentle delivery with interpretive uncertainty.
findings.japanese:
相変わらず言葉の真意はきつかったけど、
その声の柔らかさが、俺を安心させてくれる。
findings.todokanai: I can't really understand the true meaning behind her words, as usual, but her soothing, soft voice does put me at ease.

findings.highlight: the clothes she took off
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が脱がせた小春の服を拾い集め、洗面所に持ち込み、ぬるま湯と液体洗剤で押し洗い。
findings.explanation: Haruki gathers the clothes he stripped off Koharu during sex, then hand-washes them in lukewarm water and liquid detergent. The English says Koharu took the clothes off herself and also changes the lukewarm water to hot water, rewriting two concrete details in the immediate post-sex sequence.
findings.japanese:
浴室からちゃんとシャワーを使う音が聞こえてきたのを
確認してから、俺が脱がせた小春の服を拾い集め、
洗面所に持ち込み、ぬるま湯と液体洗剤で押し洗い。
findings.todokanai: After I had confirmed that Koharu had turned on the shower, I gathered the clothes she took off, brought them to the bathroom, and washed them with hot water and detergent.

findings.highlight: It's alright for me to misunderstand, now, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 誤解だって思っていいんだな？
findings.explanation: Haruki asks himself whether he is allowed to assume Koharu's marriage talk really is only a misunderstanding. The English says he is allowed to misunderstand her, reversing the proposition precisely as she continues asking conspicuously intimate questions about his future wife.
findings.japanese: …誤解だって思っていいんだな？
findings.todokanai: …It's alright for me to misunderstand, now, right?

findings.highlight: I expose Koharu's fair skin
findings.evidenceJa: 小春の白い肌に辿り着かずに
findings.explanation: Even after peeling back layer after layer, Haruki still has not reached Koharu's bare skin, which is what drives his mounting impatience. The translation says he exposes her skin, reversing the scene's physical progress.
findings.japanese:
めくっても、めくっても…
小春の白い肌に辿り着かずに、
じわじわと焦燥感に駆られる。
findings.todokanai: Layer by layer… I expose Koharu's fair skin spurred by my increasing impatience.

findings.highlight: torn off the last of her buttons and tossed her blazer aside
findings.evidenceJa: ボタンを外し、上着を脱ぎ捨てていく
findings.explanation: After Koharu urges him to undress too, Haruki tears open his own buttons and throws off his own outerwear. The translation assigns both garments and actions to Koharu, changing who is being undressed.
findings.japanese:
小春に言われるまでもなく、
引きちぎるようにボタンを外し、
上着を脱ぎ捨てていく。
findings.todokanai: Before Koharu could say anything, I'd already torn off the last of her buttons and tossed her blazer aside.

findings.highlight: a bitch that belongs to you alone
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩だけのビッチなんですから
findings.explanation: Koharu misunderstands the loanword ビッチ as though it could mean a sexually exclusive woman, which is why Haruki immediately says that her sentence makes no sense. English 'your bitch' is an ordinary, coherent expression, so the translation removes the mistake that creates the joke and makes Haruki's response inexplicable.
findings.japanese:
「…本当ですから。
わたし、先輩だけのビッチなんですから！」
findings.todokanai: "…Because it's true. I… I've become a bitch that belongs to you alone, Senpai!"

findings.highlight: she desperately tries to close her legs
findings.evidenceJa: 楽な方向へ逃げようと、一生懸命にぴんと張られる
findings.explanation: Koharu's legs are already open around Haruki and stretch rigidly toward whatever position may hurt less. The translation says she is trying to close them and escape him, reversing the described movement.
findings.japanese:
俺を挟み込むように開かれた両脚は、
必死で楽な方向へ逃げようと、
一生懸命にぴんと張られる。
findings.todokanai: As if trying to escape from me, she desperately tries to close her legs which I'd pried open.

findings.highlight: "I'll only show this perverted side of mine to you, Senpai… only to you, okay?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「先輩にだけ…
先輩にだけ、ですからね？
こんなかっこわるいわたし、見せるのは」
findings.explanation: かっこわるい俺 is Haruki's uncool or undignified self, while 'perverted side' moralizes and sexualizes the self-description.
findings.japanese:

わたし、心から幸せでした」
findings.todokanai: "…Thank you very much. For the past three days… and this past hour. I am truly happy."

findings.highlight: I don't think she'd go out of her way to verify them
findings.evidenceJa: 疑問があっても、無理やり抑え込んでしまうだろう
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts that even if Setsuna has doubts, she will forcibly suppress them. The translation merely says she will not take the trouble to verify them, losing the active self-suppression central to his exploitation of her trust.
findings.japanese:
このメールを見て、
きっと雪菜は納得してしまうだろう。
疑問があっても、無理やり抑え込んでしまうだろう。
findings.todokanai: I'm sure Setsuna will be convinced with this text. Even if she had doubts, I don't think she'd go out of her way to verify them.

findings.highlight: There's been no new text from Setsuna since the day before yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 受信簿に、一昨日の雪菜からのメールはない
findings.explanation: Haruki observes that Setsuna's specific message from the day before yesterday is absent from his inbox. The translation instead says she has sent nothing since that day, changing the clue he is checking.
findings.japanese: やっぱり受信簿に、一昨日の雪菜からのメールはない。
findings.todokanai: There's been no new text from Setsuna since the day before yesterday, as I thought.

findings.highlight: can't get a grip when his childhood friend is involved
findings.evidenceJa: 幼なじみ相手じゃ立たない男
findings.explanation: Takeya crudely apologizes for being a man who cannot get an erection for his childhood friend. 'Can't get a grip' removes the explicit sexual joke and turns the punch line into a vague failure of composure.
findings.japanese:
「どうせお前らが想像するように、
色っぽい話なんかカケラも出てこなかったよ。
ああ悪かったなぁ幼なじみ相手じゃ立たない男でよ！」
findings.todokanai: "It's not like we talked about anything hot between us, just like you and her parents would expect. Yeah, sorry for being a guy who can't get a grip when his childhood friend is involved!"

findings.highlight: Neither Setsuna-chan nor Takahiro actually said anything
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜ちゃんにも孝宏にも何も話してない
findings.explanation: Io and Takeya have told neither Setsuna nor Takahiro that the university student involved with Koharu is Haruki. The translation makes Setsuna and Takahiro the people who said nothing.
findings.japanese:
「雪菜ちゃんにも孝宏にも何も話してない。
…そのコの相手の大学生ってのが、
あろうことかお前だなんてことは」
findings.todokanai: "Neither Setsuna-chan nor Takahiro actually said anything. …But to think that her university student boyfriend happens to be you of all people."

findings.highlight: which caused a critical crack in the relationship between Setsuna and me
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜との間に決定的な亀裂が生まれることを
findings.explanation: Haruki says that he feared deeper involvement in Koharu's circumstances would create a decisive rift with Setsuna. The translation states that his involvement already caused the rift, changing both timing and the motive for his hesitation.
findings.japanese:
俺が、小春と身体を重ねるだけでなく、
小春の事情にまで深く介入することで、
雪菜との間に決定的な亀裂が生まれることを…
findings.todokanai: Not only have I shared a physical relationship with Koharu, I ended up getting even more deeply involved with her, which caused a critical crack in the relationship between Setsuna and me…

findings.highlight: I absolutely can't run away right now
findings.evidenceJa: 今は絶対に、逃がしちゃいけない
findings.explanation: Haruki resolves that he absolutely must not let Koharu get away now. The translation changes the transitive 逃がす into intransitive 逃げる and makes the resolution about Haruki not running away himself.
findings.japanese:
今は絶対に、逃がしちゃいけない。
…周りにいる優しい人たちが、教えてくれたから。
findings.todokanai: I absolutely can't run away right now. …That's what the kind people around me have taught me.

findings.highlight: if the other party doesn't accept it
findings.evidenceJa: 相手が変わってくれなかったら何の意味もない
findings.explanation: Haruki says that deciding unilaterally that one has paid the price is meaningless unless the other person changes. The translation instead requires the other person to accept the sacrifice, replacing a change in their state or behavior with approval.
findings.japanese:
「自分一人が落とし前をつけたって思ってても、
相手が変わってくれなかったら何の意味もない」
findings.todokanai: "Even if you think of paying the price alone, it will be meaningless if the other party doesn't accept it."

findings.highlight: I wonder if Yada-san ever said something like that
findings.evidenceJa: 矢田さんは言ってくれないのかな
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders hopefully whether Yada might say that she still loves Koharu. The English past-tense 'ever said' turns that possibility of future reconciliation into a question about an already completed utterance.
findings.japanese:
そんなふうに、
矢田さんは言ってくれないのかな？
findings.todokanai: I wonder if Yada-san ever said something like that?

findings.highlight: I'm… not someone annoying
findings.evidenceJa: わたし…ウザがってなんかいません
findings.explanation: Koharu says that she does not find Haruki annoying. The translation instead has her defend herself as not being an annoying person, reversing the experiencer and object of the feeling.
findings.japanese: 「わたし…ウザがってなんかいません…っ」
findings.todokanai: "I'm… not someone annoying…!"

findings.highlight: She still looked happy though…
findings.evidenceJa: もみくちゃに『してもらった』か…
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats Koharu's pointed benefactive phrasing, してもらった, after she says her friends roughed her up affectionately; the English replaces that linguistic observation with the invented sentence 'She still looked happy though.'
findings.japanese: もみくちゃに『してもらった』か…
findings.todokanai: She still looked happy though…

findings.highlight: about 90% of it is impossible for this year
findings.evidenceJa: 今年は９割方無理だぞ
findings.explanation: The source says it is roughly ninety percent likely to be impossible this year. The translation makes ninety percent a portion of the task that is impossible, changing probability into quantity.
findings.japanese:
「………キツいぞ？
て言うか今年は９割方無理だぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "…It'll be very demanding, you know? Rather, I think about 90% of it is impossible for this year."

findings.highlight: It was Senpai who showed interest
findings.evidenceJa: 興味は先輩の方なんですか
findings.explanation: Koharu asks whether the coworkers' interest is actually directed at Haruki rather than at her. The translation instead makes Haruki the person who showed interest, reversing the joke's subject and object.
findings.japanese: 「興味は先輩の方なんですか…」
findings.todokanai: "It was Senpai who showed interest…"

findings.highlight: it's my responsibility to get to the bottom of this
findings.evidenceJa: 元を正せば俺の責任であることも棚に上げて
findings.explanation: Haruki admits that he shelves the fact that, at root, the situation is his responsibility while repeatedly pressing Koharu to change her mind. The translation instead defines his responsibility as getting to the bottom of the matter, replacing culpability with a duty to investigate or solve it.
findings.japanese:
そんなふうに俺は、
元を正せば俺の責任であることも棚に上げて、
何度も小春の翻意を促した。
findings.todokanai: I continue to ignore the fact that it's my responsibility to get to the bottom of this and insist on pressing Koharu to change her mind.

findings.highlight: She really has done a good job at maintaining her study ethic. Among Seisen's past exam questions, this is one of the more difficult ones…
findings.evidenceJa:
本当に、高いレベルを保ってる。
これって、青泉の過去問の中でも
かなり難しい部類に入るはずなのに…
findings.explanation: The source discusses academic level or ability, while the English leans toward study habits or ethic.
findings.japanese:
本当に、高いレベルを保ってる。
これって、青泉の過去問の中でも
かなり難しい部類に入るはずなのに…
findings.todokanai: She really has done a good job at maintaining her study ethic. Among Seisen's past exam questions, this is one of the more difficult ones…

findings.highlight: Mihoko refused to go to school
findings.evidenceJa: 美穂子が進学しないって言い出した理由
findings.explanation: 進学しない means Mihoko says she will not advance to higher education. The translation turns that future educational decision into refusal to attend school, changing the unresolved problem being discussed.
findings.japanese:
「その、解決できてない問題…
美穂子が進学しないって言い出した理由について、です」
findings.todokanai: "Um, about that problem that couldn't be solved…? I want to tell you the reason why Mihoko refused to go to school."

findings.highlight: Mihoko's isolating herself more desperately than she has up until now
findings.evidenceJa: だから、美穂子にとって今までよりも深刻なんです
findings.explanation: Koharu says the matter is more serious for Mihoko than before because Koharu hurt her. The translation invents intensified self-isolation as Mihoko's specific behavior, exceeding both the source and the approved note's attribution of this causal account to Koharu.
findings.japanese:
「わたしが、美穂子のこと傷つけちゃったんです。
だから、美穂子にとって今までよりも深刻なんです」
findings.todokanai: "I ended up hurting Mihoko. That's why Mihoko's isolating herself more desperately than she has up until now…"

findings.highlight: her heart and soul should be heavily wounded
findings.evidenceJa: 心も身体も、ボロボロに傷つけられたはずなのに
findings.explanation: The source explicitly pairs mind/heart with body. 'Heart and soul' duplicates the psychological half and erases bodily injury from Haruki's guilt after the sexual relationship.
findings.japanese:
それなのに…
心も身体も、ボロボロに傷つけられたはずなのに…
findings.todokanai: And yet… even though her heart and soul should be heavily wounded by all that…

findings.highlight: I really hope my body manages to suppress such a temptation
findings.evidenceJa: その衝動を抑えなくちゃならない方の身にもなってくれ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks for sympathy for the person who has to suppress the urge to embrace her. The translation makes suppression something he hopes his body will manage, removing his deliberate restraint and the complaint directed at the sleeping Koharu.
findings.japanese:
…抱きしめたくて、
その衝動を抑えなくちゃならない方の身にもなってくれ。
findings.todokanai: …I want to hug her, though I really hope my body manages to suppress such a temptation.

findings.highlight: with the same honors
findings.evidenceJa: 以下同文
findings.explanation: 以下同文 means the remaining certificate wording is the same as the preceding text, the formula being privately imitated in Haruki's room. 'The same honors' invents an honor and breaks the repeated graduation-certificate joke.
findings.japanese:
「卒業証書。
３年Ａ組清水早百合。
…以下同文」
findings.todokanai: "I hereby bestow the graduation certificate to Shimizu Sayuri from Class 3-A, with the same honors."

findings.highlight: if you got chosen without warning
findings.evidenceJa: 断り切れなかったときにも恥をかかずに済むように
findings.explanation: Koharu drafted the speech in case she could not completely refuse the selection. The translation makes her already selected without warning, replacing a contingency about failed refusal with a surprise appointment.
findings.japanese:
「小春のことだから、必死で原稿は作っただろ？
断り切れなかったときにも恥をかかずに済むように」
findings.todokanai: "Knowing you, Koharu, you've desperately prepared the speech already, right? So you wouldn't embarrass yourself if you got chosen without warning."

findings.highlight: whether I would be delivering a message or sending one
findings.evidenceJa: 送られてるのか送ってるのか
findings.explanation: The source contrasts being sent off/receiving the valedictory message with sending it herself. Both English verbs are outgoing, erasing the active-passive reciprocity specifically identified in the approved critical note.
findings.japanese:
「それに、送られてるのか送ってるのか、
よくわからなくなっちゃって…」
findings.todokanai: "And I didn't even know whether I would be delivering a message or sending one…"

findings.highlight: I am truly honored and grateful to be able to speak
findings.evidenceJa: 多数の方々のご臨席を賜り、このように盛大な卒業式を開いて下さったことに、卒業生を代表して感謝申し上げます
findings.explanation: The formal speech thanks the many attendees for their presence and for holding the grand ceremony. The translation instead expresses the speaker's honor and gratitude for being allowed to speak, replacing the object and function of the ceremonial thanks.
findings.japanese:
「本日は、多数の方々のご臨席を賜り、
このように盛大な卒業式を開いて下さったことに、
卒業生を代表して感謝申し上げます」
findings.todokanai: "As the representative for all graduating students, I am truly honored and grateful to be able to speak during this great graduation ceremony today."

findings.highlight: all of my trusted relationships
findings.evidenceJa: わたしの信じる友情
findings.explanation: Koharu vows to preserve the friendship she believes in, singular and focused on Mihoko. The translation generalizes the climax of her private letter into all of her trusted relationships.
findings.japanese:
『わたしたちの人生は、ずっと続いていくんだから、
ずっと諦めずに、わたしの信じる友情を、
これからも大切にしていくって誓います』
findings.todokanai: "Because our lives still go on, I will never give up, and I promise to treasure all of my trusted relationships all the more."

findings.highlight: pushes herself past her limits and tries to get a hold of herself
findings.evidenceJa: 強いようで、自分をしっかり持っているようでいて
findings.explanation: The source says Koharu appears strong and self-possessed but actually always wavers. The English changes those apparent traits into effort and overexertion, altering Haruki's concise characterization.
findings.japanese:
強いようで、自分をしっかり持っているようでいて、
実は、いつも迷い、揺れている…
findings.todokanai: She always pushes herself past her limits and tries to get a hold of herself, but the truth is, she's always doubtful and hesitant…

findings.highlight: go to prep school so that you perform better during the second wave of admissions
findings.evidenceJa: 予備校探すか二次募集にでも備えてな
findings.explanation: The source offers alternatives: find a prep school, or prepare for secondary recruitment, then suggests applying to Seisen literature. The translation makes prep school a means of improving in the second wave and says to join the department, changing both the options and the applicant's current status.
findings.japanese:
「あんたは予備校探すか二次募集にでも備えてな。
そうだ、青泉の文芸なんてどう？
あんたの愛しの女の子も受けるらしいよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I think you should go to prep school so that you perform better during the second wave of admissions. That's right, how about you join Seisen's Literature Department? Isn't the girl you like going there as well?"

findings.highlight: "Your work never pays off, Class Rep. You are quite popular with the underclassmen, though."
findings.evidenceJa:
「報われないねぇ委員長。
あんた結構人気あったのに、下級生とかに」
findings.explanation: 報われない is unrequited or unrewarded, while the English steers toward work not paying off.
findings.japanese:
「報われないねぇ委員長。
あんた結構人気あったのに、下級生とかに」
findings.todokanai: "Your work never pays off, Class Rep. You are quite popular with the underclassmen, though."

findings.highlight: I even changed my way of life because of it
findings.evidenceJa: わたしの人生変えといて何言ってるのこのコたちって
findings.explanation: Setsuna's old friends changed her life and then acted as though the rupture were nothing. The translation makes Setsuna the agent who changed her own way of life, weakening the accusation at the center of her anecdote.
findings.japanese:
「わたしも最初『何それ？』って思ったよ。
もう六年以上も、ずっと心から離れることはなかったのに。
…わたしの人生変えといて何言ってるのこのコたちって」
findings.todokanai: "At first, I was like, 'What the heck?' I've been holding on to it for more than six years. …I even changed my way of life because of it, so what is wrong with them?"

findings.highlight: I've tried my best to make up with them
findings.evidenceJa: 仲直りしようと頑張ったかって聞かれると、ちょっと弱いけどね
findings.explanation: Setsuna admits her case is weak if asked whether she worked to reconcile. The English states the opposite—that she tried her best—and attributes failure to insufficient strength, reversing her accountability.
findings.japanese:
「ここまで…六年かかった。本当に長かった。
…その間、仲直りしようと頑張ったかって聞かれると、
ちょっと弱いけどね」
findings.todokanai: "It's been six years since then. It's been a really long time. …I've tried my best to make up with them within that period, but I wasn't strong enough for that."

findings.highlight: heavily sympathizing with what happened to her
findings.evidenceJa: 自分と重ね合わせてるのかな
findings.explanation: Setsuna thinks Takeya and Io may be overlaying their own experiences onto Koharu, as she is. Generic sympathy erases the self-projection that links their intervention to their own history and guilt.
findings.japanese:
「二人とも、わたしと同じで、
自分と重ね合わせてるのかなって思ったんだけど…」
findings.todokanai: "I thought those two were heavily sympathizing with what happened to her, much like I was…"

findings.highlight: Koharu involved herself to protect me
findings.evidenceJa: 小春は、俺を庇おうとして巻き込まれたんだ
findings.explanation: Haruki says Koharu was dragged into the consequences while trying to protect him. The translation makes her actively involve herself, shifting culpability toward Koharu in the very sentence where Haruki assumes it.
findings.japanese:
「全部、俺が引き起こしたことなんだ。
彼女…小春は、俺を庇おうとして巻き込まれたんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Everything happened because of me. She… Koharu involved herself to protect me."

findings.highlight: Setsuna's been running away from her own situation as well
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜からして自分のこと棚に上げてる
findings.explanation: Haruki notes that Setsuna knowingly sets her own case aside while accusing him. The English says she is running away from her situation and condemns him because she knows the feeling, replacing both the rhetorical maneuver and her stated motive.
findings.japanese:
だって、雪菜からして自分のこと棚に上げてる。
そのことを十分わかってて俺を責めてる。
findings.todokanai: After all, Setsuna's been running away from her own situation as well. She's condemning me exactly because she knows how it feels to do that.

findings.highlight: what she's lost
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が失うもの
findings.explanation: Setsuna weighs helping Koharu even against what she herself will lose. The translation changes that future cost of her choice into a past loss, erasing the active sacrifice occurring in this scene.
findings.japanese:
………それこそ、
自分が失うものと秤に掛けてでも。
findings.todokanai: …And that's even after she's placed what she's lost on the scale.

findings.highlight: I won't see her look upset again
findings.evidenceJa: もう、辛い目になんか遭わせない
findings.explanation: Haruki vows not to let Koharu undergo painful experiences again. The English only says he will not see her look upset, reducing prevention of harm to avoidance of a visible expression.
findings.japanese:
「もう潰させない。
もう、辛い目になんか遭わせない。
…俺が、なんとかしてみせる」
findings.todokanai: "I won't let her collapse anymore. I won't see her look upset again. …I'll do something about this."

findings.highlight: he just couldn't believe that you'd do all those absurd things
findings.evidenceJa: あんな理不尽なことされるコじゃない
findings.explanation: Takahiro said Koharu was not a girl who should have such unreasonable things done to her. The translation makes her the person who did absurd things, reversing victim and actor in his defense of her.
findings.japanese:
「本人、すごく言葉を選んでたけどね。
あんな理不尽なことされるコじゃないって、
自分の力不足が悔しかったって、嘆いてた」
findings.todokanai: "My brother really chose his words carefully, you know. He said he just couldn't believe that you'd do all those absurd things and expressed his frustration that he wasn't capable enough to help you."

findings.highlight: But I did do all those things
findings.evidenceJa: されるコですよ、わたし
findings.explanation: Koharu replies that she is a girl deserving to have those things done to her, continuing her self-punitive acceptance of victimization. The translation repeats the prior reversal and has her confess to perpetrating the acts instead.
findings.japanese:
「………されるコですよ、わたし。
あんなに力になってくれた小木曽まで裏切ったんだから」
findings.todokanai: "…But I did do all those things. I even betrayed Ogiso despite the fact that he stood up for me so much."

findings.highlight: We proceeded with our arrangement to prepare for the exam, though we had to force ourselves through the final spurt
findings.evidenceJa: 計画的に受験対策を進め、それでいて最後に無理してスパートまでかけて
findings.explanation: The source credits Koharu with systematically proceeding through exam preparation and then forcing a final spurt. The English changes the subject to 'we,' sharing her achievement and exertion with Haruki immediately before her result.
findings.japanese:
計画的に受験対策を進め、
それでいて最後に無理してスパートまでかけて、
他のライバル達を余裕でぶっちぎっていった。
findings.todokanai: We proceeded with our arrangement to prepare for the exam, though we had to force ourselves through the final spurt so that she could surpass her other rivals with ease.

findings.highlight: her tears today are for a different reason
findings.evidenceJa: 今日の涙は別格だ
findings.explanation: 別格 says today's tears are in a class apart from her familiar tears, elevating their significance because her effort has been rewarded. The translation makes only their reason different, losing the narrator's explicit scale correction.
findings.japanese: しかも、今日の涙は別格だ。
findings.todokanai: And her tears today are for a different reason at that.

findings.highlight: Even though I was with Setsuna just a while ago… Even though we're still supposed to be thinking about one another…
findings.evidenceJa:
さっきまで雪菜と一緒にいたのに。
ずっと、お互いのことを想っていたのに。
findings.explanation: A statement that Haruki and Setsuna had been mutually thinking of one another risks becoming what they were merely supposed to do.
findings.japanese:
さっきまで雪菜と一緒にいたのに。
ずっと、お互いのことを想っていたのに。
findings.todokanai: Even though I was with Setsuna just a while ago… Even though we're still supposed to be thinking about one another…

findings.highlight: only has one bar left remaining
findings.evidenceJa: とうとう電池が一目盛り減ってしまった
findings.explanation: The fully charged battery has decreased by one notch after the long wait. The translation says only one bar remains, reversing a small consumption into near depletion and falsifying the scene's material measure of waiting.
findings.japanese:
電車の中も、タクシーの中も、
ずっと無駄にライトを使い続けて、
とうとう電池が一目盛り減ってしまった。
findings.todokanai: After pointlessly keeping the brightness on within not only the train but also the taxi, my battery has depleted to the point where it only has one bar left remaining.

findings.highlight: even as she showed no resistance to it
findings.evidenceJa: 和泉に何の断りもなく快感を貪っていた
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes that he indulged without asking Izumi. The translation replaces absence of permission with an inferred absence of resistance, precisely collapsing the distinction the approved source note says must be preserved despite later consent.
findings.japanese:
やっと、自分のしでかしたことの重大さに気づき、
和泉に何の断りもなく快感を貪っていた唇を引き離す。
findings.todokanai: Finally realizing the severity of my action, I pull away from Izumi's lips after indulging in the pleasure of said action, even as she showed no resistance to it.

findings.highlight: succumbed to the darkness yet again
findings.evidenceJa: 俺だけが、暗闇を抜けてしまった
findings.explanation: Haruki says he alone has escaped through the darkness, and experiences that relief as a new, unfair sin. The translation says he succumbed to darkness, reversing the movement that makes being rescued itself culpable.
findings.japanese:
俺だけが、暗闇を抜けてしまった。
また、新しい罪を犯した。
findings.todokanai: I alone succumbed to the darkness yet again. And I've committed a new sin once more.

findings.highlight: because she's acting as though she can't resist at all
findings.evidenceJa: 和泉が抵抗できないように、全力で押さえ込んでいるようにしか見えない
findings.explanation: The source says the position only looks as though Haruki is pinning Izumi down so she cannot resist. The English invents her acting unable to resist and makes that performance Haruki's motive, adding resistance roleplay not present in the scene.
findings.japanese:
和泉が抵抗できないように、
全力で押さえ込んでいるようにしか見えないけど。
findings.todokanai: It looks like I'm using all my strength to force Izumi down because she's acting as though she can't resist at all.

findings.highlight: something becoming uncomfortably bigger
findings.evidenceJa: お互いが膨らんでいることを嫌でも意識させる
findings.explanation: The cloth contact makes them unavoidably aware that both are swelling/aroused. The translation reduces this to one unspecified thing growing and adds discomfort, erasing Izumi's mutual bodily response.
findings.japanese:
その足は、付け根に行くほど柔らかさを増していき、
両脚が繋がったところの布越しの感触が、

findings.evidenceJa: けど、少しだ。あの頃に比べれば全然余裕で日々を普通に過ごしてる。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his present depression is only slight; compared with his earlier collapse, he now has ample emotional room to live normally. The English attaches 'only a little' to his recovery and says he is only slightly better, reversing the degree of improvement he is trying to reassure Mari about.
findings.japanese:
けど、少しだ。
あの頃に比べれば全然余裕で日々を普通に過ごしてる。
findings.todokanai: Though only a little better. Compared to that time, I'm living out my days quite normally.

findings.highlight: if you look at it from a different angle, it doesn't seem like there's any issue
findings.evidenceJa: あいつに甘やかされすぎてそうなってしまった側面もないとは言えないけど。
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot deny that Chiaki's excessive pampering partly caused him to become so unable to function without her. The English instead says that viewed differently there was no issue, erasing his recognition that her cure also intensified the dependency he is now struggling to outgrow.
findings.japanese:
…まぁ、あいつに甘やかされすぎて
そうなってしまった側面もないとは言えないけど。
findings.todokanai: …Well, I might've relied on her too much, but if you look at it from a different angle, it doesn't seem like there's any issue.

findings.highlight: two to three texts a day
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜からは、２、３日ペースで、疎遠とも親密とも言えない距離を守ってのメールが届く。
findings.explanation: Setsuna sends a carefully distanced message once every two or three days. The English says she sends two or three messages every day, multiplying the contact frequency by roughly an order of magnitude and destroying the fragile interval Haruki is monitoring.
findings.japanese:
雪菜からは、２、３日ペースで、
疎遠とも親密とも言えない距離を守ってのメールが届く。
findings.todokanai: As for Setsuna, she'll send me two to three texts a day, and the texts she sends don't feel like we're very distant, but they don't suggest that we're very close either.

findings.highlight: The content of her texts is also unchanged, never talking about how estranged or intimate we are and using polite language inconsistently.
findings.evidenceJa:
内容も相変わらず、疎遠とも親密とも言えない、
丁寧語があったりなかったりの、揺れた文面のまま。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's messages themselves maintain a tone neither distant nor intimate, wavering in and out of polite language; the English says their content never discusses estrangement or intimacy.
findings.japanese:
内容も相変わらず、疎遠とも親密とも言えない、
丁寧語があったりなかったりの、揺れた文面のまま。
findings.todokanai: The content of her texts is also unchanged, never talking about how estranged or intimate we are and using polite language inconsistently.

findings.highlight: From you and another one of my closest friends
findings.evidenceJa: お前とは別の、大切な大切な友達に。
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that he has already been protected enough by a very, very dear friend other than Takeya—Chiaki. The English says Takeya and another friend both protected him, adding Takeya to the immediate claim and weakening the pointed contrast that explains why Haruki dismisses Takeya's warning.
findings.japanese:
俺は十分守ってもらってるから大丈夫だよ。
お前とは別の、大切な大切な友達に。
findings.todokanai: I'm fine now, I've already received enough protection. From you and another one of my closest friends.

findings.highlight: the element of romance in the story gradually increases
findings.evidenceJa: 物語は徐々に伝奇色を強めていき
findings.explanation: The story increasingly takes on the color of 伝奇: occult, supernatural legend and mystery, as the inhuman murders, demon bloodline, and heroine's identity emerge. The English calls this an increasing element of romance, misidentifying the genre movement that organizes the play and its source allusion.
findings.japanese:
そして物語は徐々に伝奇色を強めていき、
やがて意外な犯人像と、
意外な彼女の正体についても描かれる。
findings.todokanai: And the element of romance in the story gradually increases as the unexpected murderer is revealed along with the surprising twist of the girl's true identity.

findings.highlight: wearing a shortcut sailor uniform
findings.evidenceJa: セーラー服にショートカットの、言葉遣いと行動が乱暴な少女
findings.explanation: The second heroine is a rough-spoken, rough-acting girl in a sailor uniform with short-cropped hair. The English attaches 'shortcut' to the uniform, producing a nonexistent garment and omitting the visible hairstyle that helps distinguish Chiaki's second transformation.
findings.japanese:
第二部では主人公が交代し、
セーラー服にショートカットの、
言葉遣いと行動が乱暴な少女が舞台に現れた。
findings.todokanai: The main character changed for the second act, and a brazen girl in words and mannerisms wearing a shortcut sailor uniform appeared on the stage.

findings.highlight: the younger cousin had a quarrel with someone
findings.evidenceJa: 喧嘩相手でもある従兄の青年の夢を辿り、犯人の居場所を突き止めていく
findings.explanation: The heroine follows the dreams of her male cousin—who is also her habitual quarrel partner—to locate the culprit. The English says the cousin quarreled with some third party, changing the central pair's relationship and obscuring whose investigation the suspense plot follows.
findings.japanese:
喧嘩相手でもある従兄の青年の夢を辿り、
犯人の居場所を突き止めていくサスペンスストーリー。
findings.todokanai: This is a suspense story describing how the younger cousin had a quarrel with someone, and through his dreams, arrived at the culprit's whereabouts.

findings.highlight: I don't even mind if I have to stay at home all the time
findings.evidenceJa: だから本当は、ずっとこの家にいてくれたらいいなって、そう思う
findings.explanation: The fourth heroine tells her brother that being with him is fun and privately wishes he would stay in this house forever. The English says she herself does not mind having to stay home, reversing the person whose continued presence she desires.
findings.japanese:
「わたし、お兄ちゃんといるとすごく楽しいんだ。
だから本当は、ずっとこの家にいてくれたらいいなって、
そう思う」
findings.todokanai: "I'm happy as long as I can be with you, onii-chan. To tell you the truth, I don't even mind if I have to stay at home all the time."

findings.highlight: the pond's size
findings.evidenceJa: 部屋の間取りや、流し台が、今までのセットより少し大きめに作ってある。
findings.explanation: The room layout and kitchen sink are built slightly larger than in the previous sets. The English turns the sink into a pond, making nonsense of the domestic interior and concealing the deliberate scale manipulation explained in the next line.
findings.japanese:
例えばこの四女の舞台…
部屋の間取りや、流し台が、
今までのセットより少し大きめに作ってある。
findings.todokanai: For example, during her act for the youngest daughter… The room and the pond's size seem slightly bigger than before.

findings.highlight: make the youngest heroine seem more natural
findings.evidenceJa: 四女の華奢さを際だたせるための、演出の妙。
findings.explanation: The oversized domestic set is a piece of stagecraft designed to accentuate the fourth heroine's slight, delicate build. The English says it makes her seem 'more natural' and merely makes the play interesting, removing the exact visual illusion Haruki is admiring.
findings.japanese:
それはきっと、第四の主人公である
四女の華奢さを際だたせるための、演出の妙。
