findings.todokanai: All that to make the youngest heroine seem more natural, the way they set the stage is also part of the reason why the play is so interesting.

findings.highlight: even louder and longer than the cheers after our performance
findings.evidenceJa: その大きさと長さは、俺たちの演奏が終わったときの、雪菜とかずさに向けられた声援にだって引けを取ってない。
findings.explanation: The applause is no less loud or long than the cheers Setsuna and Kazusa received after the trio's performance. The English says it is even louder and longer, turning parity—the astonishing claim Haruki makes—into superiority.
findings.japanese:
その大きさと長さは、俺たちの演奏が終わったときの、
雪菜とかずさに向けられた声援にだって引けを取ってない。
findings.todokanai: It's even louder and longer than the cheers after our performance, it's just like the cheer Setsuna and Kazusa received.

findings.highlight: their starring member plus president
findings.evidenceJa: 演出兼座長と、脚本兼主演女優のコンビが有名
findings.explanation: The troupe is famous for a pair consisting of its director/troupe leader and its playwright/leading actress. The English turns the first person's production roles into 'starring member plus president,' changing the division of artistic labor that defines the troupe.
findings.japanese:
「メンバー数は他と比べて圧倒的に少ないけど、
演出兼座長と、脚本兼主演女優のコンビが有名…らしい」
findings.todokanai: "The number of members they have is much less than any other club's, but they have the combination of their starring member plus president, along with their scripter plus leading actress… or so it seems."

findings.highlight: In the first segment of that DVD, during the credits section of that amazing play that took place three years ago.
findings.evidenceJa:
あのＤＶＤの１トラック目。
絶賛の嵐の中幕を閉じた、
三年前の舞台の中で。
findings.explanation: The Japanese says the performance ended amid great acclaim; the English describes the credits section ending.
findings.japanese:
あのＤＶＤの１トラック目。
絶賛の嵐の中幕を閉じた、
三年前の舞台の中で。
findings.todokanai: In the first segment of that DVD, during the credits section of that amazing play that took place three years ago.

findings.highlight: when he's still trying to memorize his lines
findings.evidenceJa: ホン読みの段階でそこまで求めなくても
findings.explanation: This is the script-reading or table-read stage, when another member argues that Chiaki need not demand so much yet. The English invents an actor who is still memorizing lines, replacing the production stage that motivates the objection.
findings.japanese: 「ホン読みの段階でそこまで求めなくても…」
findings.todokanai: "Please don't be so harsh when he's still trying to memorize his lines…"

findings.highlight: He didn't use any emotion
findings.evidenceJa: 読み込んでこなかったの丸わかり
findings.explanation: Chiaki says it is obvious the actor did not study or read the part deeply enough and therefore does not understand the character. The English changes her diagnosis to a lack of emotion, losing the exact standard by which the obsessive actress judges him unfit.
findings.japanese:
「駄目。あいつ“彼”を全然わかってない。
読み込んでこなかったの丸わかり。
…今度の舞台もあたし一人でやる」
findings.todokanai: "No, that person doesn't understand 'him' at all. He didn't use any emotion. …I might as well solo this play as well."

findings.highlight: because you're terrible at picking people
findings.evidenceJa: 座長が顔で選ぶからでしょ
findings.explanation: Chiaki says the problem is that the troupe leader chooses recruits by their faces—because they are good-looking. The English reduces this to generic bad judgment and removes both the joke and the stated reason the male actors lack substance.
findings.japanese:
「座長が顔で選ぶからでしょ。
もうちょっと骨のある奴連れてきてよ」
findings.todokanai: "Isn't that because you're terrible at picking people, President? Why don't you find someone more useful?"

findings.highlight: this should still be "the usual Chiaki."
findings.evidenceJa: ただの『いつもと違う千晶』だったのに
findings.explanation: Without the preceding hour's revelation, Haruki could have dismissed what he saw as merely 'Chiaki acting different from usual.' The English calls it the usual Chiaki, reversing the contrast on which his attempt to normalize her behavior depends.
findings.japanese:
…さっきまでの一時間さえなければ、
ただの『いつもと違う千晶』だったのに。
findings.todokanai: …If it wasn't for what I've seen in the last hour, this should still be "the usual Chiaki."

findings.highlight: The way she's seeing right through me is very painful
findings.evidenceJa: なんて、穿った見方をするのが辛い
findings.explanation: What hurts Haruki is having to take such a cynical, suspicious interpretation of Chiaki's words. The English instead says Chiaki is seeing through him, reversing the perceiver and replacing his guilt about mistrusting her with exposure anxiety.
findings.japanese: なんて、穿った見方をするのが辛い。
findings.todokanai: The way she's seeing right through me is very painful.

findings.highlight: it was actually you putting on a one-man-show again
findings.evidenceJa: 実は、一芝居打っていたのはこいつじゃなくて…
findings.explanation: Haruki desperately entertains the possibility that the person who staged the deception was not Chiaki, before the thought is interrupted. The English says it actually was her putting on another show, reversing the explicit negation and destroying the momentary hope that her present emotion might be genuine.
findings.japanese:
もしかしたら、今まで俺の見たもの全てが幻で、
実は、一芝居打っていたのはこいつじゃなくて…
findings.todokanai: Don't tell me that what I just saw was simply an illusion, that it was actually you putting on a one-man-show again…

findings.highlight: you should confirm it again
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱ再確認したわ
findings.explanation: Takeya says that what he has just seen has reconfirmed his own judgment about Haruki and Chiaki. The English turns this into advice that Haruki should perform another confirmation, changing both subject and speech act.
findings.japanese: 「春希…やっぱ再確認したわ」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki… you should confirm it again."

findings.highlight: the woman in my arms whom I'm supposed to understand very well
findings.evidenceJa: 俺のよき理解者だったはずの女
findings.explanation: Chiaki was supposed to be the woman who understood Haruki well; he now finds her incomprehensible, which makes Takeya's warning suddenly persuasive. The English says Haruki was supposed to understand her, reversing the relationship whose collapse terrifies him.
findings.japanese:
武也の言葉がするりと納得できるくらい、
今、腕の中にいる、俺のよき理解者だったはずの女が
まるで理解できない。
findings.todokanai: I'm suddenly incapable of understanding the woman in my arms whom I'm supposed to understand very well whatsoever, as if I've immediately accepted Takeya's words.

findings.highlight: Yuutsuru
findings.evidenceJa: 『夕鶴』
findings.explanation: Chiaki names Junji Kinoshita's canonical play The Twilight Crane, whose crane-wife story immediately structures the following transformation image. Leaving the title as an unexplained romanization prevents an English reader from recognizing the work or the deliberate allusion.
findings.japanese:
「…『夕鶴』。
中学のとき、これで市の最優秀賞取ったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "…Yuutsuru. It won first place in a competition when I was still in middle school."

findings.highlight: took the form of a human girl
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の女の姿を解いてしまった
findings.explanation: Like the crane wife in The Twilight Crane, Chiaki seems to shed or undo her human woman's form and reveal what lies beneath. The English says the crane assumed human form, reversing the transformation at the precise point Haruki sees the familiar Chiaki disappear.
findings.japanese:
あの日助けた鶴が、
人間の女の姿を解いてしまったように。
findings.todokanai: The crane that was saved that day took the form of a human girl.

findings.highlight: you also have yourself to blame for not realizing it
findings.evidenceJa: 気づかなかった自分を責めても仕方ないよ
findings.explanation: Chiaki says Haruki may blame her for deceiving him, but there is no point blaming himself for failing to notice. The English tells him that he also has himself to blame, reversing her coldly consoling logic and making her assign guilt she explicitly dismisses.
findings.japanese:
「騙したあたしを責めるのはともかく、
気づかなかった自分を責めても仕方ないよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I can't question the fact that I'm at fault for deceiving you, but you also have yourself to blame for not realizing it as well, you know?"

findings.highlight: In this situation so treacherous it's sending chills up my spine, Chiaki's words, demeanor and breaths envelop me in warmth as usual.
findings.evidenceJa:
寒気がするほどの空々しい状況なのに、
やっぱり千晶の言葉と態度と息遣いは、
いつも通り、優しく俺を包み込む。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls the situation hollow and farcical; the English calls it treacherous.
findings.japanese:
寒気がするほどの空々しい状況なのに、
やっぱり千晶の言葉と態度と息遣いは、
いつも通り、優しく俺を包み込む。
findings.todokanai: In this situation so treacherous it's sending chills up my spine, Chiaki's words, demeanor and breaths envelop me in warmth as usual.

findings.highlight: "You commute by train, Haruki, while I commute by bike. You take work at school seriously, while I skip classes all the time. You do your best at studying, while I do my best at after-school activities."
findings.evidenceJa:
「電車通学の春希と、自転車通学のあたし。
学校行事を仕切る春希と、ことごとくサボるあたし。
授業中に頑張る春希と、放課後にしか出てこないあたし」
findings.explanation: Chiaki says the real version of her appeared only after school; the English says she did her best at after-school activities.
findings.japanese:
「電車通学の春希と、自転車通学のあたし。
学校行事を仕切る春希と、ことごとくサボるあたし。
授業中に頑張る春希と、放課後にしか出てこないあたし」
findings.todokanai: "You commute by train, Haruki, while I commute by bike. You take work at school seriously, while I skip classes all the time. You do your best at studying, while I do my best at after-school activities."

findings.highlight: because our performance came directly after yours ended
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の舞台が終わった直後だったから、感傷的になってたんだろ
findings.explanation: Haruki suggests Chiaki became sentimental because her own stage performance had just ended. The English invents a sequence in which the trio's performance came after hers and makes that scheduling relation the cause, replacing his simple explanation of her emotional susceptibility.
findings.japanese:
「自分の舞台が終わった直後だったから、
感傷的になってたんだろ…」
findings.todokanai: "It's natural that you'd feel sad because our performance came directly after yours ended, right..?"

findings.highlight: make both of them feel attracted to you
findings.evidenceJa: 三人をまとめる…そして二人を引っかき回すあんたの力
findings.explanation: Chiaki credits Haruki's power both to bind the trio together and to throw the two women into turmoil, the destructive contradiction that made the stage compelling. The English turns the second force into merely making both women attracted to him, flattening her diagnosis of the trio's drama.
findings.japanese:
「あのステージがあそこまでみんなを惹きつけたのは、
演奏はたどたどしくても、三人をまとめる…
そして二人を引っかき回すあんたの力だったんだって」
findings.todokanai: "Despite the fact that your performance was rather awkward, it was as fascinating as it was because the three of you came together… As well as the fact that you've managed to make both of them feel attracted to you."

findings.highlight: a mysterious close friend who does things mindlessly
findings.evidenceJa: 気のおけない謎の親友
findings.explanation: 気のおけない describes a close friend around whom one need not be guarded or reserved. The English treats it as mindlessness, replacing the ease and intimacy of one of Chiaki's carefully constructed roles with an unrelated behavioral defect.
findings.japanese:
あるときは友達以上恋人未満のゼミ仲間。
あるときは気のおけない謎の親友
findings.todokanai: She's someone from my seminars who's at times more than a friend, but not quite a girlfriend. Other times, she's a mysterious close friend who does things mindlessly.

findings.highlight: made my feelings toward you even clearer
findings.evidenceJa: あんたの呪いの言葉が、あたしの引き出しをまた満たしてくれる
findings.explanation: Chiaki says Haruki's anguished words are filling her drawers—her store or repertoire of material—as an actress. The English says they clarify her feelings, erasing the horrifying double register in which genuine love and predatory artistic collection remain inseparable.
findings.japanese:
「あぁ…愛しい。
あんたの呪いの言葉が、
あたしの引き出しをまた満たしてくれる」
findings.todokanai: "Ahh… I'm loving this. Your accursed words made my feelings toward you even clearer."

findings.highlight: There's no one else who loves you as much as I do
findings.evidenceJa: あたしほどあんたをわかってる人間は他にいないよ
findings.explanation: Chiaki claims that no other human being understands Haruki as well as she does. The English repeats that nobody loves him as much, losing the uniquely disturbing claim validated by how thoroughly she has studied, imitated, and manipulated him.
findings.japanese:
「ううん、真剣。
あたし、春希のこと愛してる。
あたしほどあんたをわかってる人間は他にいないよ？」
findings.todokanai: "No, I'm serious. I really do love you, Haruki. There's no one else who loves you as much as I do in this world, you know?"

findings.highlight: I've returned to the state I was in the day before yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 一昨日、寝る前に届いた雪菜のメールを、まだ開けないままの自分がここにいる
findings.explanation: Haruki says Setsuna's message arrived before he went to sleep the day before yesterday and remains unopened now. The English says he has returned to an earlier state in which he could not read it before sleep, obscuring the continuing deliberate silence that he is confessing.
findings.japanese:
だから、一昨日、寝る前に届いた雪菜のメールを、
まだ開けないままの自分がここにいる。
findings.todokanai: That's why I've returned to the state I was in the day before yesterday, back when I was unable to bring myself to read Setsuna's text before I fell asleep.

findings.highlight: performed in high school back when I was in my fourth year
findings.evidenceJa: 例の付属祭でやった『雨月山の鬼』…四年の時あれ見て
findings.explanation: Uehara saw Chiaki's play at the affiliated high school's festival while he himself was a fourth-year university student. The English places his 'fourth year' in high school, producing a nonexistent school year and blurring the joke that he is now a seventh-year university student.
findings.japanese:
「例の付属祭でやった『雨月山の鬼』…
四年の時あれ見て思いっきり引き込まれてね。
彼女が大学に進学してくれたときは歓喜したよ」
findings.todokanai: "I was deeply fascinated when I watched The Demon of Mt. Uzuki being performed in high school back when I was in my fourth year. I must admit I was really delighted when I heard she was enrolling at this university."

findings.highlight: an up-and-coming company
findings.evidenceJa: 新進座のオーディションで内定出ててね
findings.explanation: 新進座 is the company name, Shinshinza, and Chiaki had already received an offer through its audition. The English treats the name as the adjective 'up-and-coming,' directly conflicting with the next line's description of it as a huge, top-tier company.
findings.japanese:
「当時、新進座のオーディションで内定出ててね。
危ないところだった」
findings.todokanai: "She refused the unofficial offer of an up-and-coming company after an audition. It was a close call."

findings.highlight: she got approval from those concerned
findings.evidenceJa: 関係者にもらったって言ってたけどな
findings.explanation: Uehara says Chiaki claimed to have received the audio source from someone involved. The English says she received approval, pre-empting the separate licensing discussion and breaking Takeya's immediate realization that he was the insider who supplied the recording.
findings.japanese: 「関係者にもらったって言ってたけどな」
findings.todokanai: "I heard she got approval from those concerned."

findings.highlight: I was the first one, you know
findings.evidenceJa: あたし、初めてだったんだよ？
findings.explanation: Chiaki tells Io that it was her own first time, then stresses that she gave Haruki everything he asked of her. The English says Chiaki was 'the first one,' which reads as a claim about being Haruki's first partner and reverses the vulnerable evidence she adduces for loving him.
findings.japanese:
「言っとくけどね、あたし、初めてだったんだよ？
あいつに求められたこと、何でもしてあげたんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "For the record, I was the first one, you know? I managed to give him everything he so desired, didn't I?"

findings.highlight: You were lying only to get close to him
findings.evidenceJa: 最初から騙すつもりで春希に近づいたんだよね
findings.explanation: Io says Chiaki approached Haruki from the beginning with the intention of deceiving him. The English says she lied in order to get close, reversing means and end and weakening Io's accusation that the intimacy itself was planned as part of the deception.
findings.japanese:
「だってあんた、好きだから騙した訳じゃないよね？
最初から騙すつもりで春希に近づいたんだよね？」
findings.todokanai: "After all, you didn't lie to him because you loved him, right? You were lying only to get close to him right from the start, weren't you?"

findings.highlight: the sigh that escapes my mouth does nothing but rise gently into the sky
findings.evidenceJa: そのため息をつく口は、結構端が上がっていたりしてた
findings.explanation: While cursing providence for drawing them together, Haruki admits that the corners of his mouth were often raised in a smile. The English makes the sigh itself rise into the sky, erasing the bodily evidence that he secretly enjoyed the supposedly unwanted bond.
findings.japanese:
俺はその天の采配を神に呪いつつ、
けれどそのため息をつく口は、
結構端が上がっていたりしてた。
findings.todokanai: I curse whatever powers above may be that are responsible for this, but the sigh that escapes my mouth does nothing but rise gently into the sky.

findings.highlight: "Oh dear, oh dear～ You're really naive, aren't you, Haruki? It's not like I said I'd dump you or anything～"
findings.evidenceJa:
「やっだな～も～。
本当にナイーブなんだから春希は。
別にふってないってのに～」
findings.explanation: ナイーブ means emotionally sensitive or delicate here; the English false friend 'naive' makes Chiaki call Haruki gullible.
findings.japanese:
「やっだな～も～。
本当にナイーブなんだから春希は。
別にふってないってのに～」
findings.todokanai: "Oh dear, oh dear～ You're really naive, aren't you, Haruki? It's not like I said I'd dump you or anything～"

findings.highlight: emptiness in my stomach that goes hand in hand with an appetite
findings.evidenceJa: 食欲の伴わない空腹感
findings.explanation: Haruki is left with hunger unaccompanied by appetite, a dangerous symptom of his fever and collapse. The English says the hunger goes hand in hand with an appetite, reversing the symptom immediately before he considers an ambulance.
findings.japanese: 後に残るは更なる疲れと、食欲の伴わない空腹感。
findings.todokanai: What I'm left with is an even greater fatigue and the sensation of emptiness in my stomach that goes hand in hand with an appetite.

findings.highlight: I'm unquestionably hallucinating right now
findings.evidenceJa: 頭がぼうっとしてたからに違いない
findings.explanation: Haruki says his head must have been foggy, explaining why he opened the door without checking the intercom. The English turns ordinary feverish dazedness into an unequivocal hallucination, inventing a much more severe mental symptom.
findings.japanese: 頭がぼうっとしてたからに違いない。
findings.todokanai: I'm unquestionably hallucinating right now.

findings.highlight: blurting out an answer for a question that hasn't even been asked yet
findings.evidenceJa: 質問よりも先に答えを言われてしまうなんて
findings.explanation: Setsuna answers Haruki's 'Why?' before he can formulate the full question, another sign that his feverish mind is slow. The English says Haruki himself blurted out an answer before a question, reversing the speaker and the conversational joke.
findings.japanese:
やっぱり、頭がぼうっとしてたからに違いない。
質問よりも先に答えを言われてしまうなんて。
findings.todokanai: As I thought, I'm unquestionably hallucinating right now. What am I doing, blurting out an answer for a question that hasn't even been asked yet?

findings.highlight: slowly satisfying my intense hunger
findings.evidenceJa: 猛烈な空腹感が、けれどゆっくりとせり上がってきた
findings.explanation: Once his stomach begins working, an intense hunger slowly wells up in Haruki. The English says the food is slowly satisfying that hunger, reversing the physiological recovery which explains why he immediately asks for more.
findings.japanese:
心配していた胃からの猛烈な拒絶反応もなく、
それどころか、きちんと活動を始めてくれたようで、
猛烈な空腹感が、けれどゆっくりとせり上がってきた。
findings.todokanai: My concerns of my stomach's vehement rejection of her food have thankfully been baseless. Contrarily, my stomach's starting to work properly, slowly satisfying my intense hunger.

findings.highlight: it hurts more to hear that the past was more painful and harsh than the present
findings.evidenceJa: あの時辛かった、苦しかったって言われる方が、たった今辛い、苦しいって言われるより、わたしには辛くて、苦しい
findings.explanation: Setsuna says it hurts her more to be told after the fact, 'I was suffering then,' than to be told in the moment, 'I'm suffering now.' The English instead compares whether the past itself was harsher than the present, losing her plea that Haruki ask for help while she can still act.
findings.japanese:
「あの時辛かった、苦しかったって言われる方が、
たった今辛い、苦しいって言われるより、
わたしには辛くて、苦しいんだからね？」
findings.todokanai: "Personally, I think it hurts more to hear that the past was more painful and harsh than the present, you know?"

findings.highlight: the cooking I treated Kazusa to three years prior
findings.evidenceJa: 三年前、初めて俺とかずさに料理を振舞ってくれた時
findings.explanation: Haruki compares Setsuna's present skill with the first meal Setsuna cooked for both him and Kazusa three years earlier. The English makes Haruki the cook who treated Kazusa, reversing the actor and breaking the callback to Setsuna's first attempt to feed the trio.
findings.japanese:
三年前、初めて俺とかずさに料理を振舞ってくれた時と
比べても、きっちりと三年分の進歩が見て取れるくらい、
腕が上がってた。
findings.todokanai: Even if I compare this to the cooking I treated Kazusa to three years prior, there's definitely been enough improvement in these three years that I can grasp it.

findings.highlight: "Then why don't we talk a little more today? Or are you tired of listening to me?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「じゃあ、今日のうちにもう少しだけ話をしたいな。
わたしの話、聞く気ないかな？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether Chiaki would be willing to listen to her story; the English asks whether Chiaki is tired of listening to her.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ、今日のうちにもう少しだけ話をしたいな。
わたしの話、聞く気ないかな？」
findings.todokanai: "Then why don't we talk a little more today? Or are you tired of listening to me?"

findings.highlight: what I've done to him… and how I ended up ruining everything
findings.evidenceJa: あたしが彼に何をしてあげたか…そして、何をしでかしたか
findings.explanation: Chiaki promises to tell Setsuna both what she did for Haruki and what she did to him—the aid and the transgression in deliberate opposition. The English renders both as harm and adds that she ruined everything, prejudging the morally mixed account she is about to perform.
findings.japanese:
「いいよ、教えてあげる。
あたしが彼に何をしてあげたか…
そして、何をしでかしたか、をね」
findings.todokanai: "Fine, I'll tell you all about it. I'll tell you what I've done to him… and how I ended up ruining everything after that."

findings.highlight: the characters in Yuutsuru
findings.evidenceJa: 中学の大会で演じた“つう”
findings.explanation: Tsuu is the crane-wife role in Junji Kinoshita's canonical play The Twilight Crane. The English again leaves the work as unexplained romanization and describes plural characters, obscuring the specific famous role Chiaki places beside her Four Kashiwagi Sisters feat.
findings.japanese:
「中学の大会で演じた“つう”や、
付属祭で演じた“柏木四姉妹”と同じ、
一つの役なんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Much like how I single-handedly played the roles of the characters in Yuutsuru I performed in the middle school competition and The Four Kashiwagi Sisters during the high school festival."

findings.highlight: At the beginning of winter break
findings.evidenceJa: 冬休み明けに会ったとき
findings.explanation: Setsuna noticed Shouko's happiness when they met after winter break, following Chiaki's relationship with Haruki during the holiday. The English moves the meeting to the beginning of winter break, before the experience whose emotional trace Setsuna detected.
findings.japanese:
「冬休み明けに会ったとき…
絶対に、いつもの晶子さんじゃなかった」
findings.todokanai: "At the beginning of winter break… I'm absolutely sure that you weren't the usual Shouko-san."

findings.highlight: I was broken like that three years ago
findings.evidenceJa: わたしも三年前、壊したから
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that when women love the same man such things happen, and that she too broke things three years ago. The English says she was broken, reversing agent and victim and erasing the self-accusation through which Setsuna identifies with and forgives Chiaki.
findings.japanese:
「同じ人を好きになっちゃうと、そういうこともあるよ。
わたしも三年前、壊したから」
findings.todokanai: "For two people to fall in love with the same person… things like that happen. I was broken like that three years ago."

findings.highlight: Embracing a man who you don't even love
findings.evidenceJa: 好きでもない男の人に、簡単に抱かれることなんかできない
findings.explanation: Setsuna says a woman cannot easily let herself be taken or slept with by a man she does not love—some girls cannot do it even with a man they love. The English makes the woman the agent of an ordinary embrace, reversing grammatical direction and stripping the claim of its sexual stakes.
findings.japanese:
「好きでもない男の人に、
簡単に抱かれることなんかできないよ。
…好きでもできない女の子だっているのに」
findings.todokanai: "Embracing a man who you don't even love isn't something you can do. …Especially not when another girl who loves him can't bring herself to do it."

findings.highlight: I'm really sorry for you to have had to come over
findings.evidenceJa: 部屋に上げてしまって、ごめん
findings.explanation: Haruki apologizes for having let Setsuna into his room because accepting her care may lead him to repeat his betrayal. The English apologizes that she had to come over, shifting the burden from his guilty acceptance of intimacy to her inconvenience.
findings.japanese:
「だからさ、ごめん…
部屋に上げてしまって、ごめん…
本当は、優しくしてもらうべきじゃなかった」
findings.todokanai: "That's why I'm sorry… I'm really sorry for you to have had to come over to my apartment… You really shouldn't be treating me so nicely."

findings.highlight: to have been able to treat her as a woman all this time
findings.evidenceJa: これからもずっと女として扱えるのって、世界一ころっと騙された、俺くらいかなぁ
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether he, the world's biggest sucker, may be the only person who can keep treating Chiaki as a woman from now on. The English turns this into a completed past ability, losing the prospective commitment that reveals why he may still choose her.
findings.japanese:
「あいつのこと、
これからもずっと女として扱えるのって、
世界一ころっと騙された、俺くらいかなぁって」
findings.todokanai: "And to have been able to treat her as a woman all this time. I guess I'm the only person in the world that's this gullible."

findings.highlight: I'm not someone indispensable to her
findings.evidenceJa: あいつは俺が必要とするような奴じゃなかったのに
findings.explanation: Haruki says Chiaki was never supposed to be the kind of person he would need, then asks whether he still loves and needs her. The English says he was not indispensable to Chiaki, reversing the direction of need and disrupting the progression to his separate hope that she may need him.
findings.japanese: あいつは俺が必要とするような奴じゃなかったのに。
findings.todokanai: Even though I'm aware that I'm not someone indispensable to her…

findings.highlight: the entrance exams for the new students will start next week
findings.evidenceJa: 再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる
findings.explanation: The university finishes the academic year this weekend, and the business or activity aimed at incoming freshmen begins the week after next. The English turns that into entrance exams beginning next week, changing both the event and its timing.
findings.japanese:
峰城大は、今週末をもって本年度の課程を修了し、
再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる。
findings.todokanai: All of Houjou University's courses for this year will be finished by the end of the week. And the entrance exams for the new students will start next week.

findings.highlight: Whenever I lectured him about women before, he never paid attention to me
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が女のことで説教するたびに、目の前の友がいつも呟いてたっけ
findings.explanation: Haruki recalls that Takeya used to mutter this same 'haven't you learned?' reproach whenever Haruki lectured him about women. The English instead says Takeya ignored Haruki's lectures, erasing the comic callback in which their moral roles have now completely reversed.
findings.japanese:
…って、俺が女のことで説教するたびに、
目の前の友がいつも呟いてたっけ。
findings.todokanai: …Whenever I lectured him about women before, he never paid attention to me.

findings.highlight: "…Glad you failed miserably, then."
findings.evidenceJa: 「………もの凄く納得した」
findings.explanation: Haruki says Takeya's failed week in the theatre club makes complete sense; the English says he is glad Takeya failed miserably.
findings.japanese: 「………もの凄く納得した」
findings.todokanai: "…Glad you failed miserably, then."

findings.highlight: she never cared about it one bit
findings.evidenceJa: あの女はそんなことカケラも覚えてなかった
findings.explanation: Chiaki did not remember Takeya's humiliating rejection at all, exemplifying how she forgets people and events once the performance ends. The English says she never cared, replacing her defining discontinuity of memory with ordinary cruelty.
findings.japanese:
「ところがあの女はそんなことカケラも覚えてなかった。
…そういう奴だよ」
findings.todokanai: "But she never cared about it one bit. …That's the type of person she is."

findings.highlight: "That's why Haruki… I won't speak ill of you. But that woman is just…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「だから春希…
悪いこと言わない。あの女だけは…」
findings.explanation: 悪いこと言わない is an idiom meaning 'take my advice' or 'I say this for your own good'; the English says Takeya will not speak ill of Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「だから春希…
悪いこと言わない。あの女だけは…」
findings.todokanai: "That's why Haruki… I won't speak ill of you. But that woman is just…"

findings.highlight: "That's exactly what I had in mind…"
findings.evidenceJa: 「頭ではわかってるつもりですよ…」
findings.explanation: Yoshida says he understands the danger intellectually; the English says it was exactly what he had in mind.
findings.japanese: 「頭ではわかってるつもりですよ…」
findings.todokanai: "That's exactly what I had in mind…"

findings.highlight: I want to be held
findings.evidenceJa: 抱かれたい
findings.explanation: After explicitly saying carnal desire is rising in her, Chiaki says she wants Haruki to take or sleep with her. 'I want to be held' permits an innocent embrace and blunts the deliberately sexual third item in her list of physical appetites.
findings.japanese: 「あぁ、おなかすいた、眠い…抱かれたい～」
findings.todokanai: "Ahh, I'm hungry, I'm sleepy… I want to be held～"

findings.highlight: I haven't done that with you for three days now
findings.evidenceJa: どれも三日くらい前からしてないんだもん
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she has had none of the three things she just named—food, sleep, and sex—for about three days. The English collapses them into an unspecified act she has not done 'with you,' making the claim nonsensical after Haruki's absence and obscuring her dangerous total exhaustion.
findings.japanese:
「だってさ～。
どれも三日くらい前からしてないんだもん」
findings.todokanai: "I mean, come on～ I haven't done that with you for three days now."

findings.highlight: a sense of pity I'm feeling willingly
findings.evidenceJa: そして自分勝手な憐憫を
findings.explanation: Haruki identifies the last of his unprecedented feelings toward Chiaki as selfish pity, condemning his own compulsion to rescue her. The English calls it pity he feels 'willingly,' which does not convey the moral self-indictment and is barely intelligible.
findings.japanese:
恐怖と、怒りと、焦燥と…
そして自分勝手な憐憫を。
findings.todokanai: There's fear, anger, unease… and a sense of pity I'm feeling willingly.

findings.highlight: Are you trying to predict my future many years from now
findings.evidenceJa: あたしの数年先にいるつもりなの？　春希
findings.explanation: Chiaki asks why Haruki assumes he will witness her ruin—whether he intends to still be there, in her life, several years from now. The English makes this a question about predicting her future, removing the startled romantic implication of his long-term presence.
findings.japanese:
「…どうして、あたしが破滅するところを見るの？
あたしの数年先にいるつもりなの？　春希」
findings.todokanai: "…How do you know you'll see me fail? Are you trying to predict my future many years from now, Haruki?"

findings.highlight: "My appetite has been replaced by an immense lust recently. I get so engrossed in writing the script that I find myself doing it before I know it. …Furiously masturbating, that is…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「あたし最近さぁ、食欲がない代わりに性欲が凄くてさ、
ホン書きに詰まると、ついついしちゃうんだよね。
…激しいオナニー」
findings.explanation: Chiaki masturbates when she gets stuck writing; the English says it happens because she gets engrossed in writing.
findings.japanese:
「あたし最近さぁ、食欲がない代わりに性欲が凄くてさ、
ホン書きに詰まると、ついついしちゃうんだよね。
…激しいオナニー」
findings.todokanai: "My appetite has been replaced by an immense lust recently. I get so engrossed in writing the script that I find myself doing it before I know it. …Furiously masturbating, that is…"

findings.highlight: Well, I'm now stuck in a situation where I can't escape from her little cat charade…
findings.evidenceJa: で、そんな投げっぱなしの猫芝居で逃げられた俺は…
findings.explanation: Chiaki escapes the serious exchange by abandoning it inside an unresolved cat performance; the English says Haruki cannot escape her cat charade.
findings.japanese: で、そんな投げっぱなしの猫芝居で逃げられた俺は…
findings.todokanai: Well, I'm now stuck in a situation where I can't escape from her little cat charade…

findings.highlight: He got into Public Policy
findings.evidenceJa: 政経の補欠合格だった
findings.explanation: Takahiro was admitted from the waitlist to the Politics and Economics program or faculty, the same 政経 field identified elsewhere in the route. The English changes it to Public Policy, creating a different academic program and repeating the earlier systematic misreading of 政治経済.
findings.japanese:
「うん、さっき一緒に発表見てきてね。
政経の補欠合格だった…」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, we just went to check the results together. He got into Public Policy because there was a vacant spot…"

findings.highlight: "If you really want to solve this on your own, then I won't say any more."
findings.evidenceJa:
「雪菜が自分で決着つけるって言ったから、
あたしはもう、何も言わない」
findings.explanation: Io states that because Setsuna said she would settle the matter herself, Io will say no more; the English makes this conditional on whether Setsuna really wants to solve it alone.
findings.japanese:
「雪菜が自分で決着つけるって言ったから、
あたしはもう、何も言わない」
findings.todokanai: "If you really want to solve this on your own, then I won't say any more."

findings.highlight: a portion of the students probably didn't feel like it was spring
findings.evidenceJa: 今日の合格発表も、一部の受験生にしか春を連れてきていない
findings.explanation: The results have brought metaphorical spring only to some examinees—the successful minority—while many remain in winter. The English says merely that a portion did not feel spring, reversing the restrictive population and weakening the passage's insistence that warmth has not yet reached everyone.
findings.japanese:
今日の合格発表も、
一部の受験生にしか春を連れてきていない。
皆に温かい日射しが注がれるのは、何日後のことだろう。
findings.todokanai: The results were posted today as well, and a portion of the students probably didn't feel like it was spring. I wonder how many days it would take before everyone can feel the warmth of the sunlight again?

findings.highlight: It's the year where we don't want any regrets
findings.evidenceJa: 一番後腐れのない年じゃないか
findings.explanation: Takeya calls fourth year the season of departure and therefore the year least likely to leave lingering complications or strings after romances. The English replaces his opportunistic no-strings logic with the wholesome slogan that students do not want regrets, blunting both the joke and Haruki's reply that Takeya says this every year.
findings.japanese:
「大学四年は旅立ちの季節。
…一番後腐れのない年じゃないか」
findings.todokanai: "But the fourth year in university is like a season where the journey begins. …It's the year where we don't want any regrets, right?"

findings.highlight: I can feel the guilt rising in you. Don't say I'm wrong
findings.evidenceJa: なんだか罪悪感湧いてくるだろ。俺、何も悪くないのによ
findings.explanation: Takeya tells the visibly shaken Haruki not to deny remembering so unconvincingly, because it makes Takeya himself start feeling guilty even though he did nothing wrong. The English locates the guilt in Haruki and ends with a different claim about Takeya not being wrong, reversing the comic emotional subject.
findings.japanese:
「思いっきり動揺したまま言うな。
なんだか罪悪感湧いてくるだろ。
俺、何も悪くないのによ」
findings.todokanai: "You really didn't have to say that so unconfidently. I can feel the guilt rising in you. Don't say I'm wrong."

findings.highlight: "Can you please continue from now on? I couldn't do anything for him. Can you please take my place?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「これからもあんなふうに、
今はなにもできないわたしの代わりに
彼をあっためてあげてね？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks Chiaki to warm Haruki in place of Setsuna, who can do nothing now; the English says Setsuna could do nothing, shifting current incapacity into the past.
findings.japanese:
「これからもあんなふうに、
今はなにもできないわたしの代わりに
彼をあっためてあげてね？」
findings.todokanai: "Can you please continue from now on? I couldn't do anything for him. Can you please take my place?"

findings.highlight: "As if I ever had even the slightest control over you! I'd actually appreciate it if you would listen to me for once. My doctor told me that I'm seriously going to get an ulcer at this rate."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ちっとも操られてないだろ！
むしろ少しは俺の思惑通りに動いてくれ。
この前医者で、マジ潰瘍だって言われたんだからな」
findings.explanation: Uehara says a doctor recently diagnosed him with a real ulcer; the English says the doctor warned he would get one at this rate.
findings.japanese:
「ちっとも操られてないだろ！
むしろ少しは俺の思惑通りに動いてくれ。
この前医者で、マジ潰瘍だって言われたんだからな」
findings.todokanai: "As if I ever had even the slightest control over you! I'd actually appreciate it if you would listen to me for once. My doctor told me that I'm seriously going to get an ulcer at this rate."

findings.highlight: I'm taking the last train of the day right now
findings.evidenceJa: 今、俺が乗ってきた終電
findings.explanation: Haruki points out the last train he just arrived on after leaving the station. The translation says he is currently taking it, contradicting both his location and the audible train departing behind him.
findings.japanese:
「ああ、あれ？
今、俺が乗ってきた終電」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, that? I'm taking the last train of the day right now."

findings.highlight: Kaiousha has agreed to hire you
findings.evidenceJa: 開桜社、入れそうなんだ
findings.explanation: Setsuna excitedly says it looks as though Haruki may be able to get into Kaiousha. No hiring decision has been made; the very next line corrects her because he has only been promised a recommendation.
findings.japanese:
「え…本当なの？
開桜社、入れそうなんだ！」
findings.todokanai: "Eh… Really? So Kaiousha has agreed to hire you!"

findings.highlight: This is a really nonsensical conversation
findings.evidenceJa: 本当にとりとめもないことを話した
findings.explanation: Haruki says they talked about genuinely rambling, inconsequential things. Calling the conversation nonsensical makes it irrational rather than tenderly aimless and distorts the point of their prolonged small talk.
findings.japanese: 本当にとりとめもないことを話した。
findings.todokanai: This is a really nonsensical conversation.

findings.highlight: there shouldn't be any issues if you're using it to motivate yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 頭がでかくて何が悪い。支える体だってあることをアピールするまで
findings.explanation: Haruki answers Setsuna's 頭でっかち joke by literalizing the oversized head and boasting that he has the body to support it, then clarifying he does not chiefly mean physical stamina. The translation abandons the head/body mechanism and replaces it with an unrelated claim about motivation.
findings.japanese:
「頭がでかくて何が悪い。
支える体だってあることをアピールするまで。
…主に体力面とは違う意味で」
findings.todokanai: "What's wrong with getting full of myself? At least, there shouldn't be any issues if you're using it to motivate yourself. …Specifically, in a way that's different from keeping yourself physically driven."

findings.highlight: it's already about time this got brought into the conversation
findings.evidenceJa: もう、そうゆうことまで話せるようになっちゃったんだ
findings.explanation: Chiaki realizes Haruki and Setsuna have reconciled enough that they can now talk even about Chiaki's spring deadline. The passive English merely says the subject has entered the conversation, losing who can finally speak to whom.
findings.japanese:
「そっか…そっか…
もう、そうゆうことまで話せるようになっちゃったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I see… I see… so it's already about time this got brought into the conversation…"

findings.highlight: This was always meant to be
findings.evidenceJa: 昔からそうなんだろ
findings.explanation: Haruki says Chiaki has always been this way, leading into Takeya's warning that she discards everything after a performance. The translation turns a claim about her longstanding behavior into a claim of fate or inevitability.
findings.japanese: 「昔からそうなんだろ…」
findings.todokanai: "This was always meant to be, no…?"

findings.highlight: I can grasp the feelings of all of them
findings.evidenceJa: 全部が全部、そのキャラクターになりきることができた
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she could become every character completely, whether adapted, original, or modeled on someone. The translation narrows this to grasping their feelings, weakening the acting claim that sets up Setsuna as the unique failure.
findings.japanese:
「今まで、たくさんの他人を演じてきた。
原作つきも、オリジナルも、誰かをモデルにしたときも、
全部が全部、そのキャラクターになりきることができた」
findings.todokanai: "I've played many different roles up until now. From other people's characters, original characters, to modeled characters. I can grasp the feelings of all of them."

findings.highlight: I can understand her, but I couldn't be like her
findings.evidenceJa: 理解はできたけど、共感はできなかった
findings.explanation: Chiaki's explicit distinction is that she could understand Setsuna but could not empathize with her. 'Couldn't be like her' replaces empathy with resemblance and breaks the conceptual opposition pursued through the next scene.
findings.japanese:
「そこはあたしの負け…
結局、本物の小木曽雪菜にはなれなかった。
理解はできたけど、共感はできなかった」
findings.todokanai: "This is my loss… In the end, I still couldn't become Ogiso Setsuna. I can understand her, but I couldn't be like her."

findings.highlight: what I just said could've started a space-war
findings.evidenceJa: 宇宙戦争を仕掛けようなんて訳じゃないんだけどな。本当は
findings.explanation: Haruki says that, despite attacking Chiaki's interpretation, he is not actually trying to start an interplanetary war. The translation says his words could have started one, replacing denied intention with possible consequence.
findings.japanese:
だからって…
宇宙戦争を仕掛けようなんて訳じゃないんだけどな。
本当は。
findings.todokanai: That's why… what I just said could've started a space-war.

findings.highlight: That's just what you want to believe
findings.evidenceJa: 『思う』ばっかりだね
findings.explanation: Chiaki pointedly observes that Haruki keeps saying 'I think,' challenging the uncertainty in his repeated phrasing. The translation instead accuses him of wishful thinking, changing the specific rhetorical jab.
findings.japanese: 「『思う』ばっかりだね」
findings.todokanai: "That's just what you want to believe."

findings.highlight: the same fear has been ingrained within me
findings.evidenceJa: 俺と同じ恐怖が植えつけられてるんだと『思う』
findings.explanation: Haruki says that because Setsuna underwent the same experience he did, he thinks the same fear has been ingrained in Setsuna. The translation assigns that fear to Haruki, defeating his new recognition that Setsuna shares it.
findings.japanese:
「俺と同じ体験をしてきた雪菜だからさ、
俺と同じ恐怖が植えつけられてるんだと『思う』」
findings.todokanai: "I've shared the same experience Setsuna's had, and that's why I feel that the same fear has been ingrained within me."

findings.highlight: It's not something physical, it's a psychological fear
findings.evidenceJa: かけがえのない人を、物理的にだけじゃなく、精神的に失うことの怖さ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether Chiaki knows the fear of losing an irreplaceable person not only physically but emotionally. The translation contrasts physical and psychological fear instead, deleting the compounded loss and much of the accusation directed at Chiaki.
findings.japanese:
「お前、知らないだろ？
かけがえのない人を、物理的にだけじゃなく、
精神的に失うことの怖さってさ」
findings.todokanai: "You still don't understand? It's not something physical, it's a psychological fear of losing someone important."

findings.highlight: she's actually attentively listening to me talking about my pain
findings.evidenceJa: あからさまに痛いこと聞かれてる
findings.explanation: Haruki says Chiaki is openly asking him painful questions. The translation turns her active probing into compassionate, attentive listening while he volunteers his pain.
findings.japanese:
別にベッドの中で騙されてる訳じゃないのに。
それどころか、あからさまに痛いこと聞かれてるのに。
findings.todokanai: It's not like I was tricked into talking about it on the bed. On the contrary, she's actually attentively listening to me talking about my pain.

findings.highlight: not even let me hold her anymore
findings.evidenceJa: 抱きしめてもくれないこんな奴に
findings.explanation: Haruki laments confiding in someone who will no longer hold him. The translation says Chiaki will not let Haruki hold her, reversing who withholds the embrace.
findings.japanese:
もう、慰めてもくれない、肯定してもくれない、
…抱きしめてもくれないこんな奴に。
findings.todokanai: Why would I tell this to someone who won't comfort me, accept me… and not even let me hold her anymore?

findings.highlight: She's abandoned her acting without knowing it
findings.evidenceJa: 気づかせない演技をかなぐり捨て、はっきりした悪意をわざと剥き出しにさせる
findings.explanation: Chiaki deliberately throws aside the act designed to conceal itself and intentionally lays her malice bare. The translation says she drops the act unknowingly, reversing the calculation Haruki sees in her applause.
findings.japanese:
気づかせない演技をかなぐり捨て、
はっきりした悪意をわざと剥き出しにさせる。
findings.todokanai: She's abandoned her acting without knowing it, laying her spite bare with the gesture.

findings.highlight: you don't have to answer it
findings.evidenceJa: 答え方ってものがあるんじゃない
findings.explanation: Chiaki says that even so, there are ways one ought to answer such a question—she objects to how bluntly Haruki answered. The translation says he need not answer at all.
findings.japanese:
「それにしてもさぁ、
答え方ってものがあるんじゃない？」
findings.todokanai: "Even if that's the case, you don't have to answer it, you know?"

findings.highlight: the sharp, sober remark I mumbled meant for both myself and her
findings.evidenceJa: 精一杯の強がりか、醒めきった捨て台詞か、そんな、自分でもどちらとも取れる台詞
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot tell whether his own line is desperate bravado or a thoroughly disillusioned parting shot. The translation changes this two-way self-interpretation into a remark supposedly meant for both people.
findings.japanese:
でも俺は、精一杯の強がりか、醒めきった捨て台詞か、
そんな、自分でもどちらとも取れる台詞を呟く。
findings.todokanai: But I do my best to steel my senses, the sharp, sober remark I mumbled meant for both myself and her.

findings.highlight: I've said something that I really didn't want to say
findings.evidenceJa: 本気で言って欲しくなかった言葉
findings.explanation: These are words Haruki truly did not want Chiaki to say, although he expected she inevitably would. The translation makes Haruki himself the person who has just said the unwanted words.
findings.japanese:
本気で言って欲しくなかった言葉だけど、
絶対にこいつは言うだろうなぁと覚悟だけはしてた。
findings.todokanai: I've said something that I really didn't want to say, and I can only prepare for the inevitable response she'll have.

findings.highlight: the real Chiaki disapproves of my denial of her
findings.evidenceJa: 演技の千晶を拒絶した俺が、本音の千晶に否定されていく
findings.explanation: Haruki rejected the performed Chiaki and now feels the candid Chiaki rejecting or negating him. The translation instead makes her object to his denial of her, reversing who is being rejected.
findings.japanese:
演技の千晶を拒絶した俺が、
本音の千晶に否定されていく。
findings.todokanai: As I reject Chiaki's masquerade, the real Chiaki disapproves of my denial of her.

findings.highlight: release everything inside my mouth
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと中に出してもらうからね
findings.explanation: Chiaki says that if her mouth makes him hard, his penalty will be to come inside her; the conventional unqualified 中に出す denotes internal ejaculation, not ejaculation into the mouth. The translation adds an oral location absent from and at odds with the sexual proposition.
findings.japanese:
「そんかわり、あたしの口でおっきくなったら
あんたの負け。そんときはペナルティとして、
ちゃんと中に出してもらうからね？」
findings.todokanai: "In exchange, if you happen to get hard when I put it in my mouth, you lose. And as a penalty, I'll have you release everything inside my mouth, alright?"

findings.highlight: You skipped practice the whole day yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 一昨日、稽古抜け出した時
findings.explanation: Uehara says Chiaki slipped out of rehearsal the day before yesterday to see Haruki. The translation moves it to yesterday and expands the absence into the whole day.
findings.japanese:
「結局、彼氏と仲直りできなかったのか？
一昨日、稽古抜け出した時会いに行ったんだろ」
findings.todokanai: "So you didn't make up with your boyfriend in the end, huh? You skipped practice the whole day yesterday just so you could meet him, right?"

findings.highlight: the first day of spring
findings.evidenceJa: 春一番にはほど遠かった
findings.explanation: 春一番 is the season's first strong southerly wind, not the calendar's first day of spring. The piercing wind is far from that herald of spring even though March begins tomorrow.
findings.japanese:
明日から三月だってのに、
肌を突き刺す風は、春一番にはほど遠かった。
findings.todokanai: Although it's going to be March by tomorrow, the way the wind pierces my skin suggests that there's still quite a long time before the first day of spring will arrive.

findings.highlight: there's more than a small trickle of people coming and going no matter the time
findings.evidenceJa: どの時間帯でも人の往来が寂しいことになっていた
findings.explanation: The station has sparse, lonely foot traffic at every time of day. The translation says there is more than a small trickle at all times, reversing the description of the nearly deserted district.
findings.japanese:
もともとあまり栄えていない、
大学から二番目に近いこの駅は、
どの時間帯でも人の往来が寂しいことになっていた。
findings.todokanai: This station is the second nearest to my university, and it was never really a prosperous area to begin with. It feels as if there's more than a small trickle of people coming and going no matter the time.

findings.highlight: please consider letting me join
findings.evidenceJa: 参加は考えさせてください
findings.explanation: Tanaka asks to be allowed to think about whether she would participate in a future professional troupe. The translation asks Uehara to consider allowing her to join, reversing who is making the decision.
findings.japanese: 「えっと、参加は考えさせてください」
findings.todokanai: "Um, please consider letting me join."

findings.highlight: you just look a little giddy
findings.evidenceJa: ふらついてるように見える
findings.explanation: Yoshida says Chiaki looks physically unsteady or as though she is staggering, an early sign of her collapse. 'Giddy' substitutes an emotional state and weakens the medical foreshadowing.
findings.japanese: 「いや、ふらついてるように見えるんで」
findings.todokanai: "Nothing, you just look a little giddy."

findings.highlight: "Please don't joke around like that. I know I'm not fully prepared, but I'm not as nervous as you think I am, either."
findings.evidenceJa:
「冗談やめてください。
そこまで緊張するほど準備不足じゃないです」
findings.explanation: Yoshida says he is not so underprepared that he would be that nervous; the English unnecessarily admits that he is not fully prepared.
findings.japanese:
「冗談やめてください。
そこまで緊張するほど準備不足じゃないです」
findings.todokanai: "Please don't joke around like that. I know I'm not fully prepared, but I'm not as nervous as you think I am, either."

findings.highlight: she's had to change her pastimes and personality so as to not reveal her hobby
findings.evidenceJa: 興じると人格が変わってしまうその趣味を他人に晒すことができずに
findings.explanation: Yukine cannot reveal karaoke because indulging in it transforms her personality, conflicting with the aloof beauty she must perform. The translation says she changed her pastimes and personality, losing the comic split between public persona and hidden hobby.
findings.japanese:
けれど高嶺の花を演じなくてはならない今は、
興じると人格が変わってしまうその趣味を
他人に晒すことができずに、悶々とした日々を送る。
findings.todokanai: Nevertheless, she spends her days in discontent. Placed on such a high pedestal in school, she's had to change her pastimes and personality so as to not reveal her hobby to anyone.

findings.highlight: only has her cuteness going for her
findings.evidenceJa: 歌が上手くて可愛いだけの素人ボーカリスト
findings.explanation: The amateur vocalist has two assets: she sings well and is cute. The translation says cuteness is the only thing she has going for her, erasing the singing ability on which her role in the band depends.
findings.japanese:
歌が上手くて可愛いだけの素人ボーカリストと、
博識だけど技術は凡庸で融通の利かないギタリストは、
練習風景一つ取っても、何かと会話が噛み合わない。
findings.todokanai: The amateur singer who's good at singing but only has her cuteness going for her, and the stubborn guitarist who's knowledgeable but very mediocre. They didn't seem to be on the same wavelength during practice.

findings.highlight: she boasts a dominant presence in the school
findings.evidenceJa: 学園ナンバー１空気。但し不穏な
findings.explanation: Haruna is the school's number-one 'air'—an invisible nonentity, albeit an ominous one. The translation calls her a dominant presence, stating the opposite of the social joke.
findings.japanese:
雪音に負けず劣らずの美貌と、
雪音とは勝負にならない圧倒的不人気を誇る、
学園ナンバー１空気。但し不穏な。
findings.todokanai: With an infamous streak that's a stark contrast to Yukine's popularity despite their rivaling looks, she boasts a dominant presence in the school. Though an unsettling one, at that.

findings.highlight: I've never finished below second place
findings.evidenceJa: 二位に落ちたことすらない
findings.explanation: Haruna says she has never even fallen to second place: she always wins. 'Never below second' allows second-place finishes and materially understates the prodigy's record.
findings.japanese:
「…なんでこのあたしがお前なんかに巻き込まれて
コンテストで笑い者にならなくちゃいけないんだ。
自分のコンクールじゃ二位に落ちたことすらないのに」
findings.todokanai: "…Why did I of all people get involved with you, anyway? It's pretty obvious that this band is going to be nothing more than the laughingstock of the contest. And to think I've never finished below second place in any of my own competitions."

findings.highlight: how innocent the two actors are on stage
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らが演じる二人があまりにも初々しくて
findings.explanation: Haruki is embarrassed by how innocent the two characters portrayed by the actors are. The translation attributes that innocence to the actors themselves, collapsing the play's actor-character distinction.
findings.japanese:
彼らが演じる二人があまりにも初々しくて、
何故か俺の顔から火が出そうだったから。
findings.todokanai: For some reason, I'm feeling incredibly embarrassed about how innocent the two actors are on stage.

findings.highlight: there will be a day where it can be reflected upon your heart
findings.evidenceJa: 届かない恋をしていても、映しだす日がくるかな
findings.explanation: The lyric wonders whether a day will come when this unreachable love can be reflected or made visible. The translation invents 'upon your heart,' supplies a declarative future instead of the question's uncertainty, and leaves the load-bearing title untranslated in the preceding phrase.
findings.japanese:
「『届かない恋をしていても、映しだす日がくるかな』…
すごい、すごいよ和希くん…意外な才能～」
findings.todokanai: "'Even if these feelings can never be conveyed, there will be a day where it can be reflected upon your heart'… Amazing… this is amazing, Kazuki-kun… You have an unexpected talent～"

findings.highlight: I'm going to give you a dose of reality
findings.evidenceJa: わたし今思いっきり落胆してるから
findings.explanation: Yukine says she herself is bitterly disappointed because Kazuki mistook her expectation of a kiss for a lucky charm. The translation instead has her announce that she will give him a dose of reality.
findings.japanese:
「あ、俺今いい話でまとめたな～って
なんか自己満足に浸ってるみたいだけど、
外してるから。わたし今思いっきり落胆してるから！」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, you have this smug look on your face that says 'I just said something cool,' but I'll have you know you're off by a long shot! I'm going to give you a dose of reality!"

findings.highlight: I'm doing this because it's you, Yukine
findings.evidenceJa: 雪音に限って、そんな
findings.explanation: Kazuki protests that surely Yukine of all people could not have expected something sexual or romantic, which is why she accuses him of treating her as an ornament. The translation says he acted especially because it was her, turning his desexualizing assumption into romantic preference.
findings.japanese:
「い、いや、まさか…
雪音に限って、そんな…」
findings.todokanai: "N-No, that can't be… Well, I'm doing this because it's you, Yukine…"

findings.highlight: my right hand that's leaning against the cold wall
findings.evidenceJa: 冷たい床に置かれていた俺の右手
findings.explanation: Haruki's right hand is resting on the cold floor when Setsuna places hers over it. The translation relocates the hand to the wall, making the subsequent physical arrangement difficult to reconstruct.
findings.japanese:
冷たい床に置かれていた俺の右手に、
温かさが重なる。
findings.todokanai: I feel warmth enveloping my right hand that's leaning against the cold wall.

findings.highlight: Is this gonna mess up the whole thing
findings.evidenceJa: 失格になるんじゃないのかなぁ
findings.explanation: The planted spectator wonders whether the band will be disqualified. The translation turns a concrete contest consequence into the vague possibility of messing up the whole thing.
findings.japanese:
「失格になるんじゃないのかなぁ…
なんか勿体ないよな、決して悪くないのに」
findings.todokanai: "Is this gonna mess up the whole thing…? It'd be such a waste. I thought it was going pretty well, too!"

findings.highlight: They became the audience of the competition in the play
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らは、芝居の観客ではなく、コンテストの観衆役
findings.explanation: The nearby troupe members are not ordinary theatergoers becoming absorbed; they are playing the roles of spectators at the fictional competition. The translation conceals that the apparent audience chatter is deliberately staged.
findings.japanese:
彼らは、芝居の観客ではなく、コンテストの観衆役…
こんなところにまで『芝居』が仕込んである。
findings.todokanai: They are no longer the audience here to watch the stage play. They became the audience of the competition in the play… That's how deeply the performance has drawn in its audience.

findings.highlight: they've completely fallen for the illusion
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らが舞台の三人の演奏に聴き入ることで、俺たちまでもが
findings.explanation: By visibly listening to the trio, the planted competition spectators induce the real audience—including Haruki and Setsuna—to experience the scene as a live concert. The translation makes the planted performers themselves victims of the illusion, reversing how the theatrical device works.
findings.japanese:
彼らが舞台の三人の演奏に聴き入ることで、
俺たちまでもが、これが芝居ではなく
ライブだという錯覚を植えつけられていく。
findings.todokanai: While listening to the three performing on stage, they've completely fallen for the illusion that they're watching the competition liveーand so have we.

findings.highlight: if you know it for a fact now, you'll get another chance to make one
findings.evidenceJa: 既成事実ならまた作れば
findings.explanation: 既成事実 is a fait accompli: Uehara awkwardly suggests that if Chiaki wanted pregnancy or sex as an irreversible fact tying Haruki to her, she could make another one. The translation mistakes the idiom for knowing something as fact and becomes incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「残念だったけど…
まぁその、既成事実ならまた作れば」
findings.todokanai: "It's unfortunate, but… if you know it for a fact now, you'll get another chance to make one."

findings.highlight: Yukine will definitely push the story toward a dark ending
findings.evidenceJa: 雪音は、物語の闇に突き落とされていくだろう
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts that the merciless script will cast Yukine down into the story's darkness. The translation makes Yukine the agent who pushes the story toward darkness.
findings.japanese:
きっとあいつは、この先容赦なんかしない。
雪音は、物語の闇に突き落とされていくだろう。
findings.todokanai: She definitely won't show any mercy to me. Yukine will definitely push the story toward a dark ending.

findings.highlight: the two of us will end up having our hearts gouged out
findings.evidenceJa: 抉られた俺が言うんだから間違いない
findings.explanation: Haruki says there can be no mistake because he speaks as someone Chiaki has already gouged emotionally. The translation invents a prediction about both Haruki and Setsuna being wounded instead of grounding the claim in his past experience.
findings.japanese: 何しろ、抉られた俺が言うんだから間違いない。
findings.todokanai: In any case, there's no doubt that the two of us will end up having our hearts gouged out, at least.

findings.highlight: she had to hide her feelings for Kazuki inside her heart
findings.evidenceJa: 和希への募る想いとは裏腹に、二人の時間をじわじわと奪われていく
findings.explanation: As Yukine rises to stardom, time with Kazuki is gradually taken from her despite her growing love for him. The translation invents concealment of her feelings and loses the distance produced by her career.
findings.japanese:
スター街道を駆け上がっていく雪音は、
和希への募る想いとは裏腹に、
二人の時間をじわじわと奪われていく。
findings.todokanai: Since Yukine was a popular star, she had to hide her feelings for Kazuki inside her heart, so the time they spent together drastically decreased.

findings.highlight: the poison that was spreading throughout his entire body
findings.evidenceJa: その毒が全身に回っていくのを抑えられなくなる
findings.explanation: By drawing Kazuki's pain out of him, Haruna finds that its poison spreads through her own body and can no longer suppress it. The translation assigns the poison to Kazuki, eliminating the image of his confidante absorbing his suffering.
findings.japanese:
二人の共通の友人というスタンスを守り続ける榛名は、
和希の悩みや辛さを吸い出してあげているうちに、
その毒が全身に回っていくのを抑えられなくなる。
findings.todokanai: As the friend who watched over them, Haruna tried to help Kazuki vent out his problems. But she couldn't suppress the poison that was spreading throughout his entire body.

findings.highlight: may not have thought of it as a mistake, but it was indeed the gravest mistake of all
findings.evidenceJa: 榛名と和希にとって、それが過ちではなかったことが、最大の過ちだった
findings.explanation: The paradox is that for Haruna and Kazuki their union genuinely was not a mistake—and that very fact was the greatest mistake. The translation reduces this to their possibly failing to recognize an objectively grave mistake.
findings.japanese:
…榛名と和希にとって、それが過ちではなかったことが、
最大の過ちだった。
findings.todokanai: …Haruna and Kazuki may not have thought of it as a mistake, but it was indeed the gravest mistake of all.

findings.highlight: Haruna, who abandoned her piano, stayed by Kazuki's side
findings.evidenceJa: ピアノを捨てた榛名には、和希が側に残り
findings.explanation: Kazuki remains beside Haruna, who abandoned the piano, while Yukine is left only with song. The translation makes Haruna the one who stays beside Kazuki, reversing the result of their sacrifices.
findings.japanese:
ピアノを捨てた榛名には、和希が側に残り、
捨てなかった雪音には、歌だけが残される。
findings.todokanai: Haruna, who abandoned her piano, stayed by Kazuki's side; Yukine, who did not cast aside her singing, only had her singing with her.

findings.highlight: If I keep chasing my love with everything I have, I'll grasp it one day
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の恋を追いかけて、一生懸命やってたら、いつの間にかチャンスを掴んでいた
findings.explanation: Yukine says that while pursuing her love and working with all her might, she found she had already seized a career opportunity before she knew it. The translation changes that accomplished history into a future promise to grasp love someday.
findings.japanese:
「自分の恋を追いかけて、一生懸命やってたら、
いつの間にかチャンスを掴んでいたけれど」
findings.todokanai: "If I keep chasing my love with everything I have, I'll grasp it one day."

findings.highlight: Her love has definitely gone too far and is one that she's forced upon him
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の愛情は、決して行き過ぎず、押しつけず、けれど控えもせず
findings.explanation: The narration says Yukine's love never goes too far and is never imposed, yet is not held back either. The translation states exactly the opposite: that it definitely goes too far and is forced upon Kazuki.
findings.japanese:
彼女の愛情は、決して行き過ぎず、押しつけず、
けれど控えもせず、強く、優しく…
findings.todokanai: Her love has definitely gone too far and is one that she's forced upon him, but it's also boundless, strong, and kind…

findings.highlight: "Abandoning something in order to obtain something else is something I don't like doing."
findings.evidenceJa:
「何か一つを捨てて、他の全てを手に入れるなんて、
そんなバランス感覚、わたしにはないもの」
findings.explanation: Yukine rejects sacrificing one thing to obtain all the rest; the English reduces this to abandoning one thing to obtain another.
findings.japanese:
「何か一つを捨てて、他の全てを手に入れるなんて、
そんなバランス感覚、わたしにはないもの」
findings.todokanai: "Abandoning something in order to obtain something else is something I don't like doing."

findings.highlight: I won't ask you to believe me
findings.evidenceJa: 信じてる、なんて言わない
findings.explanation: Yukine says she will not claim that she trusts Kazuki regardless of whom he chooses. The translation instead says she will not ask Kazuki to believe her, reversing the direction of trust.
findings.japanese:
「信じてる、なんて言わない。
和希くんがわたしと榛名のどっちを選んでも、
それが間違ってるなんて思わない」
findings.todokanai: "I won't ask you to believe me. I don't think it would be wrong for you to choose either me or Haruna, Kazuki-kun."

findings.highlight: locked in a mutual battle of love and hate
findings.evidenceJa: 最後の最後までお互いを愛し合い、そして潰し合った
findings.explanation: Yukine and Haruna continue loving one another even as they destroy one another. The translation replaces this simultaneous mutual love and mutual destruction with a conventional battle of love and hate.
findings.japanese:
雪音も榛名も、
最後の最後までお互いを愛し合い、
そして潰し合った。
findings.todokanai: Yukine and Haruna were locked in a mutual battle of love and hate until the very end.

findings.highlight: we're almost done packing up
findings.evidenceJa: 公演の方もだいぶ押しましたし
findings.explanation: Yoshida explains that it is 1 a.m. because the performance itself ran substantially late. The translation instead says they are almost finished packing up, changing the reason for the time.
findings.japanese:
「ええと…夜中の一時ですね。
ま、公演の方もだいぶ押しましたし」
findings.todokanai: "Let's see… It's 1 AM. Well, we're almost done packing up."

findings.highlight: I'm going to be abandoned without getting a say in it
findings.evidenceJa: 問答無用に捨てられちゃったじゃないかよ
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she has consequently already been dumped without discussion. The translation moves the abandonment into the future even though her breakdown is a reaction to Haruki having rejected her.
findings.japanese:
「おかげであたし…
問答無用に捨てられちゃったじゃないかよ」
findings.todokanai: "But now, I… I'm going to be abandoned without getting a say in it, huh?"

findings.highlight: inflicting wounds upon myself that will never heal
findings.evidenceJa: 自分に癒せない傷が刻まれるから
findings.explanation: Haruki does not want to wound Setsuna because scars he himself cannot heal will be carved into her. The translation relocates those wounds onto Haruki, undermining the stated reason for ending the relationship.
findings.japanese:
「俺はもう、雪菜を傷つけたくない。
だって、自分に癒せない傷が刻まれるから」
findings.todokanai: "I don't want to hurt you anymore, Setsuna. Because I know I'll only keep inflicting wounds upon myself that will never heal if this goes on."

findings.highlight: It's been snowing all along
findings.evidenceJa: 雪が、降っていた
findings.explanation: The narration simply reveals that snow was falling in Chiaki's later-night scene. Adding 'all along' invents continuous duration and conflicts with the parallel earlier scene, where Haruki says the snow has finally begun.
findings.japanese: 雪が、降っていた。
findings.todokanai: It's been snowing all along.

findings.highlight: the perverted behavior you just exhibited
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の行為の変態性に危機感を持ってな
findings.explanation: Haruki says he stopped because he became alarmed at the perversity of his own vacuum-cleaner play. The translation makes him accuse Chiaki of the perverted behavior.
findings.japanese: 「…ちょっと自分の行為の変態性に危機感を持ってな」
findings.todokanai: "…Shouldn't you feel a little concerned about the perverted behavior you just exhibited?"

findings.highlight: she would probably do something horribly wrong with the vacuum cleaner
findings.evidenceJa: 色んな場所を掃除機で責めてしまいそうだった
findings.explanation: Haruki fears that if this continues, he will torment various parts of Chiaki's body with the vacuum while wearing a sadistic smile. The translation again assigns the action to Chiaki and turns Haruki's arousal into hers.
findings.japanese:
このまま放っておくと、
色んな場所を掃除機で責めてしまいそうだった。
…嗜虐心に満ちた笑顔とともに。
findings.todokanai: If I just let her be, she would probably do something horribly wrong with the vacuum cleaner… with an aroused expression as well…

findings.highlight: I'm not bored to the point where I'll believe in dreams like that
findings.evidenceJa: そんなヒモの世迷い言を信じるほど、俺は夢見がちな行き遅れじゃないの
findings.explanation: Haruki jokingly casts Chiaki as a freeloading kept man and himself as a dreamy spinster past marriageable age who should not believe such promises. The translation deletes the inverted gender-role joke and substitutes boredom.
findings.japanese:
「そんなヒモの世迷い言を信じるほど、
俺は夢見がちな行き遅れじゃないの」
findings.todokanai: "I'm not bored to the point where I'll believe in dreams like that."

findings.highlight: if we both agree to it, then the limit can be ignored
findings.evidenceJa: 自分だけじゃなく、相手の両手でもＯＫという規制解除も増えた
findings.explanation: Their truth signal is limited to once per day, but the rule has expanded so that either one's own two hands or the other person's two hands may be pressed in place. The translation invents mutual agreement as a way to ignore the daily limit, losing the physical cue.
findings.japanese:
一日に一度だけって制限を付けたけど。
自分だけじゃなく、相手の両手でもＯＫという
規制解除も増えたけど。
findings.todokanai: We've agreed on a limit of only doing it once per day. But if we both agree to it, then the limit can be ignored.

findings.highlight: she's only saying those words without actually acting on them
findings.evidenceJa: そんな台詞、ただ口に出してないだけで
findings.explanation: Haruki admits internally that he already feels what Chiaki promises to make him say; he simply has not spoken it aloud. The translation instead dismisses Chiaki's words as speech unsupported by action, reversing both speaker and emotional truth.
findings.japanese:
それにそんな台詞、
ただ口に出してないだけで…
findings.todokanai: Moreover, she's only saying those words without actually acting on them…

findings.highlight: Because the cat that I decided to never abandon again confesses her feelings all of a sudden.
findings.evidenceJa:
だから、もう自分は捨てられないと悟った飼い猫は、
そんなふうに、突然自分をさらけ出す。
findings.explanation: The pet cat herself realizes she can no longer be abandoned, while the English makes this chiefly Haruki's decision never to abandon her.
findings.japanese:
だから、もう自分は捨てられないと悟った飼い猫は、
そんなふうに、突然自分をさらけ出す。
findings.todokanai: Because the cat that I decided to never abandon again confesses her feelings all of a sudden.

findings.highlight: It might take some time, but I'll be here for you
findings.evidenceJa: 時間をかけて、春希を染め上げてあげるからね
findings.explanation: Chiaki promises to take her time dyeing or reshaping Haruki in her own colors until the wound of memory closes. The translation replaces that possessive, character-specific intention with generic supportive presence.
findings.japanese:
「時間をかけて、春希を染め上げてあげるからね。
…思い出の傷、塞がるまで」
findings.todokanai: "It might take some time, but I'll be here for you, Haruki. …Until your wounds heal, that is."

findings.highlight: the three people that fell apart
findings.evidenceJa: あたしがぶち壊した三人
findings.explanation: Chiaki explicitly calls them the three people she smashed apart. The translation removes her agency and says only that the trio fell apart, weakening the purpose of her keeping the knife.
findings.japanese:
「あたしが憧れた三人。
あたしがぶち壊した三人を忘れないために。
…二度とこのナイフを使わないために」
findings.todokanai: "For the sake of the three people who I admired. For the sake of never forgetting about the three people that fell apart. …And for the sake of never using this knife again."

findings.highlight: In order for her to remain by my side
findings.evidenceJa: ずっと、俺がこいつの側にいられるように
findings.explanation: Haruki keeps Chiaki dependent so that he can always remain by her side. The translation says he does it so that she remains by his, reversing the dependency he confesses to engineering.
findings.japanese: ずっと、俺がこいつの側にいられるように。
findings.todokanai: In order for her to remain by my side.

findings.highlight: I never plan on changing myself
findings.evidenceJa: これからも演技を続ける
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she has recovered and will continue acting as though she has not changed, forever making Haruki lament that apparent fact. The translation turns the performed unchanged persona into a sincere refusal ever to change.
findings.japanese:
『だけど、これからも演技を続ける。
あたしはちっとも変わってないって、
ずっと春希を嘆かせてやるから』
findings.todokanai: "But even so, I'll keep my act up. I never plan on changing myself, I'll keep making you sigh."

findings.highlight: I've been going to university since yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 今日は、ちゃんと大学には来たよ
findings.explanation: Haruki says he did come to university properly today because he had a class with a report deadline approaching. The translation invents continuous attendance since yesterday.
findings.japanese:
『今日は、ちゃんと大学には来たよ。
レポートの提出期限の迫ってる講義もあったし』
findings.todokanai: "I've been going to university since yesterday. There's a lecture of which the paper submission date is fast approaching, after all."

findings.highlight: will start next week
findings.evidenceJa: 再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる
findings.explanation: The university's business involving incoming students begins the week after next, not next week. The translation advances the admissions schedule by a week.
findings.japanese:
峰城大は、今週末をもって本年度の課程を修了し、
再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる。
findings.todokanai: All of Houjou University's courses for this year will be finished by the end of the week. And the entrance exams for the new students will start next week.

findings.highlight: I'm sure she would understand
findings.evidenceJa: ほんのちょっとの気の迷いじゃないか。もう、忘れろよ
findings.explanation: Takeya dismisses Chiaki as a momentary lapse and tells Haruki to forget it or forget her. The translation instead reassures him that she would understand, replacing advice to move on with an unsupported prediction about Chiaki.
findings.japanese:
「ほんのちょっとの気の迷いじゃないか。
もう、忘れろよ」
findings.todokanai: "You only lost your way a little. I'm sure she would understand."

findings.highlight: you're still so attached to the past
findings.evidenceJa: 相変わらず抱え込みすぎ、自分のせいにしすぎ
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki still takes far too much onto himself and blames himself too much. The translation changes the first criticism into attachment to the past, losing his defining compulsion to shoulder every burden.
findings.japanese:
『ひとことで言ってしまえば、
相変わらず抱え込みすぎ、自分のせいにしすぎ。
…って、ところかな？』
findings.todokanai: "If I'm to sum it up in one sentence, it's that you're still so attached to the past and still blame yourself too much as usual. …Something like that?"

findings.highlight: You're too serious
findings.evidenceJa: 正直すぎ
findings.explanation: Setsuna adds that Haruki is too honest, specifically responding to the exhaustive confession in his letter. The translation calls him too serious, changing the quality she identifies and the reason the truth wounds them.
findings.japanese:
『ああ、もうひとことだけ追加するとね…
正直すぎ』
findings.todokanai: "Ahh, wait, let me add one more thing… You're too serious."

findings.highlight: I neither feel the reason nor the need to be worried
findings.evidenceJa: 焦ってる気配も焦る必要も全くないから
findings.explanation: Haruki says he can speak freely because Mari shows no sign of anxiety about her age and has no need to be anxious. The translation makes Haruki the person who neither feels nor needs worry, losing his compliment about her confidence.
findings.japanese:
「麻理さんだから遠慮なく言えるんです。
焦ってる気配も焦る必要も全くないから」
findings.todokanai: "It's because it's you that I can drop the formalities, Mari-san. I neither feel the reason nor the need to be worried."

findings.highlight: showing up all of a sudden in a place like this on Christmas Eve
findings.evidenceJa: クリスマスの夜中に
findings.explanation: The scene has already crossed midnight into December 25, as Haruki explicitly noted at line 32. Mari says he appeared in the middle of Christmas night; the translation moves the visit back to Christmas Eve.
findings.japanese:
「ま、クリスマスの夜中に、
いきなりこんなところに来ることからして、
何かありますよって言ってるようなものだったし」
findings.todokanai: "Well, showing up all of a sudden in a place like this on Christmas Eve just screams 'something happened.'"

findings.highlight: After hearing my honest response, Mari-san seems ever so slightly shaken up.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺に素直にすがられて、
麻理さんがほんのちょっとだけ慌てる。
findings.explanation: Mari is rattled because Haruki honestly clings to or depends on her, not simply because she hears an honest response.
findings.japanese:
俺に素直にすがられて、
麻理さんがほんのちょっとだけ慌てる。
findings.todokanai: After hearing my honest response, Mari-san seems ever so slightly shaken up.

findings.highlight: Pain from love cannot be healed by love itself
findings.evidenceJa: 恋の傷を、恋で癒せてなかったんです
findings.explanation: Haruki confesses that he had not managed to heal his wound from love with another love. The translation turns his personal failed attempt into a universal claim that love cannot heal love, changing both tense and psychological meaning.
findings.japanese: 「恋の傷を、恋で癒せてなかったんです」
findings.todokanai: "Pain from love cannot be healed by love itself."

findings.highlight: She's a world-class Japanese born in Japan, and after she changed her main site of activity to Europe, she had not come back to her home country even once for years on end.
findings.evidenceJa: 活動拠点をヨーロッパに移してから、数年に一度くらいしか帰国しない、日本が生んだ世界的ピアニスト。
findings.explanation: The source calls Youko a world-famous pianist produced by Japan who, since moving her professional base to Europe, returns home only about once every few years. The translation turns her profession into the nonsensical 'world-class Japanese,' then changes intermittent visits into no return for years on end.
findings.japanese:
活動拠点をヨーロッパに移してから、
数年に一度くらいしか帰国しない、
日本が生んだ世界的ピアニスト。
findings.todokanai: She's a world-class Japanese born in Japan, and after she changed her main site of activity to Europe, she had not come back to her home country even once for years on end.

findings.highlight: They have quite the competition this time.
findings.evidenceJa: なんでもあれに対抗してるんだと
findings.explanation: Hamada says Youko's New Year's concert is apparently intended to compete with artists' overnight New Year's Eve live shows. The translation instead says an unspecified 'they' face strong competition, reversing who is challenging whom.
findings.japanese:
「大晦日に年越しライブやるアーティストいるだろ。
なんでもあれに対抗してるんだと」
findings.todokanai: "Aren't there plenty of artists out there that do cross-year concerts on New Year's Eve? They have quite the competition this time."

findings.highlight: I heard she was going to play Number 9 too. I guess she found some orchestra to perform with her
findings.evidenceJa: 第九も弾くんだとさ。どっかの交響楽団にも張り合ってるんだな
findings.explanation: 第九 is Beethoven's Ninth Symphony, not an item called 'Number 9.' Hamada then jokes that Youko is even taking on some symphony orchestra as a rival; the translation invents an orchestra performing with her and erases the second competitive comparison.
findings.japanese:
「聞いた話だと、第九も弾くんだとさ。
どっかの交響楽団にも張り合ってるんだな…
なんつ～か、若いよなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "I heard she was going to play Number 9 too. I guess she found some orchestra to perform with her… How should I put it, she's still so young and full of life, huh?"

findings.highlight: Apparently, she got a call directly from the chief editor over at Ensemble.
findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜、本人からアンサンブルの編集長に直接連絡があったそうで
findings.explanation: Matsuoka says that last night Youko herself directly contacted Ensemble's editor-in-chief, which is why the special instruction reached Mari and then this office. The translation instead has Mari receiving a call from that editor, omitting Youko's direct intervention and reversing the stated call direction.
findings.japanese:
「さっきの電話、麻理さんからだったんですよ。
昨夜、本人からアンサンブルの編集長に
直接連絡があったそうで」
findings.todokanai: "That call just now was from Mari-san. Apparently, she got a call directly from the chief editor over at Ensemble."

findings.highlight: I've been distancing myself from Takeya, who's been calling me every single day. And every time I hang up, the feeling of guilt envelops me, eating me alive.
findings.evidenceJa: 『あの日』以降、毎日連絡をくれる武也に対して、あしらい気味に扱ってしまいつつ、電話を切ってから詫びるの繰り返し。
findings.explanation: Haruki describes a repeated concrete routine: he brushes off Takeya, who calls daily, then apologizes after ending the call. The translation replaces the apology with invented, highly intensified guilt that 'envelops' and 'eats [him] alive,' turning observed conduct into purple psychological narration.
findings.japanese:
『あの日』以降、毎日連絡をくれる武也に対して、
あしらい気味に扱ってしまいつつ、
電話を切ってから詫びるの繰り返し。
findings.todokanai: Ever since "that day," I've been distancing myself from Takeya, who's been calling me every single day. And every time I hang up, the feeling of guilt envelops me, eating me alive.

findings.highlight: cruel feelings that value nothing of their friendship
findings.evidenceJa: 友達甲斐のない残酷な気持ちだった
findings.explanation: Haruki calls his desire to be left alone cruel and 友達甲斐のない: unworthy of a friend or showing himself to be a poor friend. The translation instead says his feelings place no value on the friendship, changing a self-accusation about what he gives his friends into a denial that he values them.
