findings.japanese:
それが俺の、正直で率直で、
そして、友達甲斐のない残酷な気持ちだった。
findings.todokanai: These are nothing but my frank, direct and cruel feelings that value nothing of their friendship.

findings.highlight: the reason they were so on point with their suspicions was because they already knew the answer to begin with
findings.evidenceJa: きっと、わかっているからこそ的を射た
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that precisely because Io and Takeya understand him and Setsuna so well, whatever they say now will hit the mark. The translation invents prior suspicions and an answer they already know, severing the line from the following prediction that they will force the pair toward a solution.
findings.japanese: きっと、わかっているからこそ的を射た…
findings.todokanai: Chances are, the reason they were so on point with their suspicions was because they already knew the answer to begin with…

findings.highlight: That's exactly why I can't betray their trust. I have to do my utmost to ensure that everything is done on time, carefully, and accurately…
findings.evidenceJa:
だからこそ、その信用を裏切る訳にはいかない。
どの仕事も納期通り、質を下げず、量を削らず、
丁寧に、そして確実にこなしていかないと…
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly vows to meet every deadline without lowering quality or cutting quantity; 'on time, carefully, and accurately' omits the no-compromise pair.
findings.japanese:
だからこそ、その信用を裏切る訳にはいかない。
どの仕事も納期通り、質を下げず、量を削らず、
丁寧に、そして確実にこなしていかないと…
findings.todokanai: That's exactly why I can't betray their trust. I have to do my utmost to ensure that everything is done on time, carefully, and accurately…

findings.highlight: If I recall correctly, printed on that piece of paper is the name "Touma Youko."
findings.evidenceJa: 正確には、その紙面に印刷された『冬馬曜子』の文字が。
findings.explanation: 正確には means 'more precisely': Haruki corrects the preceding sentence to say it is specifically the printed name, not the sheet itself, that catches his eye. 'If I recall correctly' invents uncertainty about what the paper says and removes the deliberate self-correction.
findings.japanese:
正確には、その紙面に印刷された
『冬馬曜子』の文字が。
findings.todokanai: If I recall correctly, printed on that piece of paper is the name "Touma Youko."

findings.highlight: No, what I'd be seeing again are memories pertaining to a certain someone.
findings.evidenceJa: いや、これから集めるであろう“あいつ”のことを。
findings.explanation: The surrounding sentence says Youko's performance would make Haruki remember Kazusa, who inherited her blood and talent. Here he corrects himself: Kazusa is not already commanding audiences abroad but is the one who will do so in the future. The translation instead has him 'seeing ... memories,' eliminating both the career-time correction and the syntax of remembering her.
findings.japanese: いや、これから集めるであろう“あいつ”のことを。
findings.todokanai: No, what I'd be seeing again are memories pertaining to a certain someone.

findings.highlight: Having betrayed Setsuna, I have no business getting involved with anything pertaining to the surname of "Touma."
findings.evidenceJa:
雪菜を裏切ったまま、
“冬馬”という姓を引きずるのは。
findings.explanation: Haruki tells himself to stop dragging the Touma name along while continuing to betray Setsuna; 'no business getting involved with anything pertaining to the surname' makes it a question of external involvement rather than his own attachment.
findings.japanese:
雪菜を裏切ったまま、
“冬馬”という姓を引きずるのは。
findings.todokanai: Having betrayed Setsuna, I have no business getting involved with anything pertaining to the surname of "Touma."

findings.highlight: To the person who'd support me even if I didn't want it.
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌だと言っても支えられようとする人に。
findings.explanation: The paired morphology is deliberate: one person tries to support Haruki without being asked, while another tries to be supported by him even if he says no. The translation makes both people support Haruki, erasing the reversed dependency in the second relationship.
findings.japanese:
頼んでもいないのに支えようとする人に。
嫌だと言っても支えられようとする人に。
findings.todokanai: To the person who's supported me without me asking for it. To the person who'd support me even if I didn't want it.

findings.highlight: "Happy New Year Birthday, Mari～ Another year older."
findings.evidenceJa:
「あけましてお誕生日おめでと～麻理。
また一つ年取ったねぇ」
findings.explanation: Sawako says both Happy New Year and happy birthday because Mari's birthday is January 1; 'Happy New Year Birthday' is malformed English.
findings.japanese:
「あけましてお誕生日おめでと～麻理。
また一つ年取ったねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "Happy New Year Birthday, Mari～ Another year older."

findings.highlight: "What is…? I feel so annoyed and I can't take it anymore…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「どこがよ…
こんなモヤモヤした気持ち、たまんないわよ…」
findings.explanation: もやもや is unresolved, restless uncertainty, while 'annoyed' makes Mari's emotion primarily irritation.
findings.japanese:
「どこがよ…
こんなモヤモヤした気持ち、たまんないわよ…」
findings.todokanai: "What is…? I feel so annoyed and I can't take it anymore…"

findings.highlight: I asked Hamada-san and Suzuki-san for a way to contact the particular venue Mari-san was staying at to make sure she and her partner were safe.
findings.evidenceJa: 浜田さんか鈴木さんに頼んで、麻理さんの滞在先に連絡してもらい、彼女たちの安否を確かめてもらうために。
findings.explanation: This is the purpose for which Haruki changed clothes and rushed to the office: to ask either Hamada or Suzuki to contact Mari's lodging and confirm the women's safety. The translation says he already asked both of them for a way to contact a 'venue,' collapsing intention into completed action and mistranslating the lodging.
findings.japanese:
浜田さんか鈴木さんに頼んで、
麻理さんの滞在先に連絡してもらい、
彼女たちの安否を確かめてもらうために。
findings.todokanai: I asked Hamada-san and Suzuki-san for a way to contact the particular venue Mari-san was staying at to make sure she and her partner were safe.

findings.highlight: nearly 100% of the worst case scenarios that I had pictured were from my absurd fear
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の描いた最悪の状況なんて、ほぼ１００％杞憂で間違いないってわかってた。
findings.explanation: Haruki knew it was virtually certain that the single worst-case scenario he had imagined was a groundless fear. The translation applies 'nearly 100%' to a plurality of scenarios and says that percentage came from fear, garbling the confidence judgment that explains why he feels foolish.
findings.japanese:
俺の描いた最悪の状況なんて、
ほぼ１００％杞憂で間違いないってわかってた。
findings.todokanai: I knew full well that nearly 100% of the worst case scenarios that I had pictured were from my absurd fear.

findings.highlight: You're going to be up to your neck in more than just work if you're not careful.
findings.evidenceJa: いい加減にしないと抜けるよ色々？
findings.explanation: Suzuki warns that if Haruki keeps this up, various things will start falling out or coming loose—an ominously comic bodily consequence of overwork, to which he says 'spare me.' The translation substitutes being 'up to your neck' in unspecified things, an unrelated idiom that makes the reply and joke incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「…年越しの朝まで仕事してて、
この上まだ新しい仕事を探しますか君は。
いい加減にしないと抜けるよ色々？」
findings.todokanai: "…You worked until morning on New Year's and you're still looking for more? You're going to be up to your neck in more than just work if you're not careful."

findings.highlight: Just breaking the rules a little shouldn't be so unforgivable, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 物にあたるくらいなら、許して欲しい。
findings.explanation: After insisting that suicidal thoughts are forbidden, Haruki asks to be forgiven at least for taking his anger out on objects. The translation changes this impending physical displacement into 'breaking the rules,' obscuring both the contrast and what he is about to do.
findings.japanese:
物にあたるくらいなら、
許して欲しい。
findings.todokanai: Just breaking the rules a little shouldn't be so unforgivable, right?

findings.highlight: the director's seat
findings.evidenceJa: 編集長
findings.explanation: Matsuoka says he is aiming to become editor-in-chief. The translation changes this newsroom-specific post into an unspecified director's position.
findings.japanese:
「やっぱ目指すなら編集長ですからね。
今のうちに人使うことにも慣れておかないと」
findings.todokanai: "If you're gonna aim somewhere, it's gotta be the director's seat. Better start getting used to managing people now while we can."

findings.highlight: the manga cafe in the station
findings.evidenceJa: 駅裏の漫画喫茶
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks of a manga cafe behind the station, where other people's presence might let him sleep. The translation relocates it inside the station.
findings.japanese: そうだ、駅裏の漫画喫茶…
findings.todokanai: That's right, the manga cafe in the station…

findings.highlight: With a mentality of do or die, I immediately wanted to take the next step.
findings.evidenceJa: すぐに次のステップを求めてしまい、それが叶えられなかっただけで自滅するくらいに
findings.explanation: Haruki says he demanded the next step so quickly that its mere failure to materialize made him self-destruct. The translation omits both the denied outcome and the self-destruction, replacing them with a generic do-or-die attitude.
findings.japanese:
…すぐに次のステップを求めてしまい、
それが叶えられなかっただけで自滅するくらいに。
findings.todokanai: …With a mentality of do or die, I immediately wanted to take the next step.

findings.highlight: I'm neither of those things in the end, huh…
findings.evidenceJa: その、どっちかでしか、ないんだな
findings.explanation: Mari concludes that she can only be one of the two alternatives she has just imagined: Kazusa's substitute or outside Haruki's romantic notice. The translation says she is neither, reversing the conclusion.
findings.japanese: （その、どっちかでしか、ないんだな…）
findings.todokanai: (I'm neither of those things in the end, huh…)

findings.highlight: That's settled.
findings.evidenceJa: 裁判で
findings.explanation: Mari says she could not win in court. The translation replaces the court qualification with a claim that the matter is settled, obscuring that she is advancing a legal or evidentiary argument.
findings.japanese:
「勝てないから。
裁判で」
findings.todokanai: "It's because I wouldn't win. That's settled."

findings.highlight: Now I definitely feel shocked.
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対に、ショックだったに決まってる
findings.explanation: Haruki insists that Mari must have been shocked by what happened. The translation makes Haruki himself newly feel shocked, reversing whose unspoken injury he is contemplating.
findings.japanese: 絶対に、ショックだったに決まってる。
findings.todokanai: Now I definitely feel shocked.

findings.highlight: piercing countless holes into my physical and mental being
findings.evidenceJa: とんでもない裏切りで、肉体的にも精神的にもボロボロにされた
findings.explanation: Haruki reasons that Mari must have been devastated physically and mentally by his betrayal. The translation assigns that bodily and emotional damage to Haruki instead.
findings.japanese:
飼い犬に手を噛まれるなんてレベルじゃない、
とんでもない裏切りで、肉体的にも精神的にも
ボロボロにされたんだから。
findings.todokanai: It's not the pain of being bitten by a domestic dog; it's a tremendous betrayal piercing countless holes into my physical and mental being.

findings.highlight: I wanted you to become my successor
findings.evidenceJa: 私の後を継ぐのは北原しかいないって思ってたのに
findings.explanation: Mari says she believed no one but Kitahara could succeed her, and immediately reaffirms that belief. The translation reduces this exclusive professional judgment to a past wish that he become her successor.
findings.japanese:
「私の後を継ぐのは北原しかいないって思ってたのに。
…いいや今だって思ってる」
findings.todokanai: "I wanted you to become my successor, Kitahara. …No, I still want that, even now."

findings.highlight: I couldn't completely agree with everything Mari-san had said.
findings.evidenceJa: まるっきり同意なんかしてなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki states that he did not agree at all with Mari's order to forget everything, despite nodding. The translation turns total inner refusal into incomplete agreement, weakening the closing contradiction.
findings.japanese:
けれどその時の俺は、
麻理さんの言葉に、まるっきり同意なんかしてなかった。
findings.todokanai: Yet the way I was then, I couldn't completely agree with everything Mari-san had said.

findings.highlight: Mari-san's… pleasure.
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんの…気持ちよさ
findings.explanation: Haruki is remembering how good Mari felt to him, alongside her scent, softness, and warmth. The translation instead presents the pleasure as Mari's own experience, changing the experiencer of the sexual memory.
findings.japanese: 麻理さんの…気持ちよさ。
findings.todokanai: Mari-san's… pleasure.

findings.highlight: Time began to move once again
findings.evidenceJa: 時間が、ほんの少し戻ってしまってる
findings.explanation: Haruki feels that time has slipped backward a little as he regresses to the abandonment accusation he had just suppressed. The translation says time begins moving again, reversing backward regression into resumed forward motion.
findings.japanese:
時間が、ほんの少し戻ってしまってる。
俺の心の中の声が、漏れてしまっている。
findings.todokanai: Time began to move once again as I spoke my mind.

findings.highlight: I've locked myself in a state of unraveling my disarrayed heart to Mari-san.
findings.evidenceJa: ひねくれた心を解きほぐせないまま、麻理さんに、ぶつけてしまっている
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is hurling his still-unresolved, twisted feelings at Mari. The translation instead describes himself as locked in the act of unraveling them to her, replacing an accusatory emotional outburst with something closer to disclosure or processing.
findings.japanese:
ひねくれた心を解きほぐせないまま、
麻理さんに、ぶつけてしまっている。
findings.todokanai: I've locked myself in a state of unraveling my disarrayed heart to Mari-san.

findings.highlight: came up with the excuse that you were busy
findings.evidenceJa: 用があっても人に言付けたり
findings.explanation: Haruki complains that even when Mari had business with him, she sent messages through other people. The translation invents an excuse that she was busy, changing the conduct he cites as evidence of avoidance.
findings.japanese:
「なのに…用があっても人に言付けたり、
電話を掛けてきておいて、いきなり切ってしまったり…」
findings.todokanai: "But you always… came up with the excuse that you were busy, and when I managed to reach you over the phone, you just hung up…"

findings.highlight: Seeing the fact that Mari-san has slowly relaxed as a good sign
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんが、すっと力を抜いたのをいいことに
findings.explanation: Haruki says he takes advantage of Mari relaxing her resistance after apologizing. The translation calls it a good sign, turning his explicitly opportunistic use of that opening into perceived encouragement.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんが、すっと力を抜いたのをいいことに、
その、女性の曲線豊かな背中にのしかかり、

findings.todokanai: Seeing the fact that Mari-san has slowly relaxed as a good sign, I lean on her feminine and abundantly curvy back, plastering our bodies together.

findings.explanation: Haruki actively hooks his leg around Mari's exposed leg. The translation makes Mari's legs entwine with his, reassigning agency to her during a coercive physical sequence.

スカートからはみ出た足に俺の足を絡め、

findings.explanation: Haruki objects to Mari diminishing herself as 'someone like me'; he says Mari is not a mere 'someone like that' while evading whether he desires her. The translation objects to 'possibly,' destroying the evasive wordplay that Mari immediately calls out.
findings.japanese:
「麻理さんは『なんか』じゃありません…
ん、んぅ…は、ぁぁ、ぁ…」
findings.todokanai: "'Possibly' isn't the right word to describe it, Mari-san… Haah, mmmn…"

findings.highlight: Does that… feel good…? Kitahara

findings.explanation: Mari asks whether this is really acceptable or enough for Haruki after drawing a boundary against penetration. The translation changes that tentative boundary check into a question about whether the rubbing feels good.

「はぁ、はぁ、はぁぁ…
い、いいの…か？
北原…本当に、これで…？」
findings.todokanai: "Haah… haaa… Does that… feel good…? Kitahara… is this really…?"

findings.highlight: I help myself to the tender sensation of her body through the fabric as I thrust on Mari-san, as if I wanted to penetrate her from behind.

findings.japanese:
麻理さんを後ろから突き上げるように、
その、布越しの大ぶりな柔らかさを堪能する。
findings.todokanai: I help myself to the tender sensation of her body through the fabric as I thrust on Mari-san, as if I wanted to penetrate her from behind.

findings.highlight: her buttocks which are squeezing my penis

The translation invents her buttocks squeezing his penis as an actual bodily relation, erasing both the source's deliberate nonnaming and the fact that this part exists in imagination.

触れたり、さすったり、キスしたり、舐めたり。
最初は嫌がっていた麻理さんも、
次第に目がとろんとして、歓喜の声を…
findings.todokanai: I touch her, rub on her, kiss her and lick her. Mari-san, who had initially resisted from the beginning, gradually begins to show an intoxicated gaze, letting out sounds of pleasure…

findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんの悲鳴に近い声が、余計に俺を、余裕のない状態に駆り立ててしまう
findings.explanation: Mari's near-scream drives Haruki further into a state with no composure or restraint. Calling it an exciting situation eroticizes the loss of control and suppresses the source's alarm at her near-scream.

麻理さんの悲鳴に近い声が、

findings.todokanai: Mari-san's voice, close to screaming, only serves to spur me on in this exciting situation.

findings.highlight: I'll work according to my capabilities from now on.
findings.evidenceJa: ここからは体力と相談して悩もうと思ってます
findings.explanation: Haruki says that from here he will continue thinking through his unresolved problems while consulting or respecting his physical stamina. The translation turns that emotional recovery plan into a plan to work within his capabilities, reintroducing work where the source is discussing how safely to agonize and recover.
findings.japanese:
「それでも麻理さんのおかげで、
眠れるようにはなれました。
ここからは体力と相談して悩もうと思ってます」
findings.todokanai: "And of course, it's due to your efforts that I've finally been able to have some sleep. I'll work according to my capabilities from now on."

findings.highlight: apologizing for attempting to check up on you so casually like this
findings.evidenceJa: こうして普通に挨拶しちゃうことの方がごめんなさい、かな
findings.explanation: Setsuna wonders whether she should instead apologize for greeting Haruki normally after what happened. The translation turns the ordinary greeting into casually checking up on him, changing the action for which she feels guilt.
findings.japanese:
『…それとも、
こうして普通に挨拶しちゃうことの方が
ごめんなさい、かな？』
findings.todokanai: "…Though I wonder if I should be apologizing for attempting to check up on you so casually like this."

findings.highlight: the odd fact that she had free time
findings.evidenceJa: その微妙な空き時間
findings.explanation: Haruki reads meaning into the delicate or awkward interval of more than two weeks before Setsuna contacted him. The translation misreads that gap as the odd fact that she had free time.
findings.japanese:
その微妙な空き時間と、その丁寧語が入り混じる口調と、
その他人行儀なサブジェクトに、
今の俺が抱えているのと同じ距離感があった。
findings.todokanai: From the odd fact that she had free time, the fact that she's being more polite than usual, along with the formality of her text's title, I could tell that she was feeling the same sense of distance that I am.

findings.highlight: neither of us would have had the strength to initiate contact of our own accord
findings.evidenceJa: 相手から連絡が来るほど、どこかの誰かは強くないってことが
findings.explanation: Haruki says Setsuna understood that a certain someone—Haruki—was not strong enough to leave contact to the other person after that separation. The translation universalizes his weakness to both of them, erasing why Setsuna mustered the courage to initiate.
findings.japanese:
…ああいう別れ方をした後、相手から連絡が来るほど、
どこかの誰かは強くないってことが。
findings.todokanai: …She knows that after we parted the way we did, neither of us would have had the strength to initiate contact of our own accord.

findings.highlight: It's good that she's recovered.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は戻ってきてる。元気かそうでないかは書いてないからわからないけれど
findings.explanation: Haruki says Setsuna has returned to ordinary social contact but immediately admits that her message does not reveal whether she is well. The translation declares that she has recovered, converting the exact uncertainty he preserves into a health conclusion.
findings.japanese:
雪菜は戻ってきてる。
元気かそうでないかは書いてないからわからないけれど、
それでも普段通り、社会の中で生きている。
findings.todokanai: It's good that she's recovered. She hasn't written anything about it, though, and while I can't tell how she is now, at least she's back to her life in society as she used to.

findings.highlight: More importantly, I need to tell her that I need her help.
findings.evidenceJa: 本当は、助けて欲しかったこと
findings.explanation: Haruki plans to disclose that he had wanted Mari to help him in the past. The translation turns that past unmet wish into a present request for help, contradicting his next recognition that he can no longer ask her for help and can only ask her to listen.
findings.japanese:
ずっと聞いて欲しかったこと。
本当は、助けて欲しかったこと。
findings.todokanai: I need to tell her what I've always wanted her of all people to hear. More importantly, I need to tell her that I need her help.

findings.highlight: Even though I know I'll never be forgiven by you.
findings.evidenceJa: 許してくれるとは、思ってないけど
findings.explanation: Haruki says he does not expect Setsuna to forgive him. The translation turns that pessimistic expectation into certain knowledge that she will never forgive him, making the future permanently closed.
findings.japanese: …許してくれるとは、思ってないけど、な。
findings.todokanai: …Even though I know I'll never be forgiven by you.

findings.highlight: at 1 o'clock on Sunday
findings.evidenceJa: 土曜の１時
findings.explanation: Mari originally said Saturday at one, which Haruki comically interpreted as Saturday afternoon rather than the extended late-night Saturday hour. The translation changes her wording to Sunday at one and removes the ambiguity that caused his mistaken daytime objection.
findings.japanese:
最初、『土曜の１時にこの前三人で飲んだ店』と
言われた時には、『昼間だと開いてないんじゃ？』と、
思いっきり的外れな指摘をしてしまったっけ。
findings.todokanai: At first, when Mari-san initially decided for us to meet up at the bar the three of us went to before, at 1 o'clock on Sunday, I suddenly asked the off-point question of "A bar open during the day?".

findings.highlight: you went all-out last Saturday, as well?
findings.evidenceJa: 先週の土日も全出だった
findings.explanation: Haruki says Mari worked full days on both Saturday and Sunday the previous weekend. The translation reduces both weekend shifts to an undefined all-out effort on Saturday alone.
findings.japanese: 「確か、先週の土日も全出だったんですよね？」
findings.todokanai: "Right, I believe you went all-out last Saturday, as well?"

findings.highlight: You joined us, so working for us is itself your job hunt.
findings.evidenceJa: ウチに入るんだからウチで働くことこそが就職活動だ
findings.explanation: Mari treats Haruki's future entry into the company as a foregone conclusion and argues that his current work there is therefore his job hunt. The translation says he has already joined the company, collapsing the distinction between part-time work and future formal employment.
findings.japanese:
「ウチに入るんだからウチで働くことこそが就職活動だ。
あんまりウダウダ言ってると内定出ても取り消すぞ」
findings.todokanai: "You joined us, so working for us is itself your job hunt. If you keep blabbering on too much, I'll revoke your job offer even if you get one."

findings.highlight: I brought up my intention of resigning and ended up displeasing Mari-san to such an extent, and as paradoxical as it is, I'm admittedly a little embarrassed.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺が辞めるって言い出すことが、
麻理さんをそこまで不機嫌にするって事実が、
逆説的ながら、少しだけ面映ゆいから。
findings.explanation: Haruki feels bashfully pleased that his resignation upsets Mari, while the translation gives only embarrassment.
findings.japanese:
俺が辞めるって言い出すことが、
麻理さんをそこまで不機嫌にするって事実が、
逆説的ながら、少しだけ面映ゆいから。
findings.todokanai: I brought up my intention of resigning and ended up displeasing Mari-san to such an extent, and as paradoxical as it is, I'm admittedly a little embarrassed.

findings.highlight: it means nothing to me for you to be satisfied
findings.evidenceJa: 何もなかったと何度言わせれば気が済むんだ
findings.explanation: Mari asks how many times she must say that nothing happened before Haruki is satisfied. The translation instead says the event means nothing to her for him to be satisfied, scrambling both her minimizing claim and the idiom about repeated reassurance.
findings.japanese: 「…何もなかったと何度言わせれば気が済むんだ？」
findings.todokanai: "How many times do I have to tell you that it means nothing to me for you to be satisfied?"

findings.highlight: Not if you didn't put it in.
findings.evidenceJa: そこは突っ込んでもらわないと
findings.explanation: Mari says Haruki was supposed to play the straight man and call out her deliberately disproportionate tissue-and-dry-cleaning joke. The translation invents a statement about nonpenetration, replacing the comic conversational request with a sexual fact claim.
findings.japanese: 「…そこは突っ込んでもらわないと」
findings.todokanai: "…Not if you didn't put it in."

findings.highlight: She's doing her very best to act cheerful around me, though there's one thing deep down in my heart that I can't ever forgive.
findings.evidenceJa: 努めて明るく振舞ってた態度を思い切りしぼませつつ、でも俺は、心の中で一つだけ承伏していなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki's own deliberately bright demeanor collapses, while inwardly he withholds assent from one part of Mari's explanation. The translation assigns the cheerful act to Mari and turns nonassent into something Haruki can never forgive.
findings.japanese:
努めて明るく振舞ってた態度を思い切りしぼませつつ、
でも俺は、心の中で一つだけ承伏していなかった。
findings.todokanai: She's doing her very best to act cheerful around me, though there's one thing deep down in my heart that I can't ever forgive.

findings.highlight: Please keep this a secret for now.
findings.evidenceJa: 今は、そうっとしておいてください
findings.explanation: Haruki asks Mari to leave him alone for the present while he cools his feelings and prepares to return. The translation asks her to keep something secret, inventing a confidentiality request instead of temporary distance.
findings.japanese:
「今は、そうっとしておいてください。
その代わり一年後、もっと使える奴になってから…
胸を張って、麻理さんの下に戻ってきますから」
findings.todokanai: "Please keep this a secret for now. In exchange for that, I'll become a more useful guy in a year… And then I'll puff out my chest and come back to work under you."

findings.highlight: "This isn't work, but a private matter. Isn't it okay to be just a little irresponsible?"

少しは甘えがあったっていいじゃないですか」
findings.explanation: Haruki says some dependence or self-indulgence is acceptable in private life, but the translation says some irresponsibility is acceptable.
findings.japanese:
「これは仕事じゃなくてプライベートなんですから。
少しは甘えがあったっていいじゃないですか」
findings.todokanai: "This isn't work, but a private matter. Isn't it okay to be just a little irresponsible?"

findings.explanation: Mari has loosened or opened her shirt, removed her belt, and even undone her skirt hook. The translation says she is wearing only her shirt, falsely removing the skirt and making her substantially more undressed than the source describes.

findings.todokanai: Before I noticed it, she's only wearing her shirt. She's unfastened her belt and even the hook on her skirt…
