ただ、麻理さんのその思い詰めた表情と、
一気に燃え上がっていった顔色から、
今、とてつもない告白をしでかしたってことだけ…
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes that Mari has made a momentous confession, but the translation calls it ridiculous.
findings.japanese:
ただ、麻理さんのその思い詰めた表情と、
一気に燃え上がっていった顔色から、
今、とてつもない告白をしでかしたってことだけ…
findings.todokanai: I can only deduce that she was confessing something ridiculous to me from the way she seemed deep in thought and how her complexion flared up instantly…

findings.highlight: a superior who's spoiled by her subordinates
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで部下に甘い上司
findings.explanation: Haruki says he has never known a boss this indulgent toward a subordinate. The translation reverses the direction and calls Mari a boss who is spoiled by her subordinates.
findings.japanese:
俺は、ここまで部下に甘い上司を知らない。
多分、これから一生そんな上司に出会うこともない。
findings.todokanai: I don't know a superior who's spoiled by her subordinates. And I can't imagine myself meeting a superior like her ever again in my whole life.

findings.highlight: "U-Umm… Why are you going out of your way to ask me a question like that? Aren't you someone who goes straight to violating others without a word?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「え、ええと…何でそんなことわざわざ聞くんだ？
何も言わずに犯そうとした奴が」
findings.explanation: Mari refers to Haruki as someone who tried to violate her without asking, but the translation makes the description habitual and plural.
findings.japanese:
「え、ええと…何でそんなことわざわざ聞くんだ？
何も言わずに犯そうとした奴が」
findings.todokanai: "U-Umm… Why are you going out of your way to ask me a question like that? Aren't you someone who goes straight to violating others without a word?"

findings.highlight: I don't want you to hate me anymore, Mari-san.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺、もう、麻理さんの嫌がることはしないから
findings.explanation: Haruki promises that he will no longer do anything Mari dislikes. The translation turns that conduct-based consent commitment into a wish that Mari not hate him, shifting the priority from her boundaries to his desired emotional outcome.
findings.japanese:
「…あの時はごめんなさい。
俺、もう、麻理さんの嫌がることはしないから」
findings.todokanai: "…I'm really sorry for what happened back then. It's just that I don't want you to hate me anymore, Mari-san."

findings.highlight: this is different from the horrible way things transpired back then
findings.evidenceJa: あの時の劣情とは違う
findings.explanation: Haruki distinguishes his present feeling from the base lust that drove him before. The translation compares the present with how events transpired, erasing that his point is a change in motive rather than simply a different sequence of acts.
findings.japanese: だって、あの時の劣情とは違う。
findings.todokanai: After all, this is different from the horrible way things transpired back then.

findings.highlight: I'll do my best to not let that happen.
findings.evidenceJa: 直前で拒まれても、必死で止まってみせる
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even if Mari rejects him at the last instant, he will make himself stop. After describing the rejection, 'not let that happen' reads as preventing the rejection or stop, reversing the explicit commitment to halt.
findings.japanese:
だから、直前で拒まれても、
必死で止まってみせる。
findings.todokanai: That's why even if she rejects me before I can do that, I'll do my best to not let that happen.

findings.highlight: this is something we should really discuss later on
findings.evidenceJa: それは本当に後日談でしかなくて
findings.explanation: Mari says the eventual half-year separation and breakup were merely the epilogue; the damaging cycle had begun much earlier. The translation postpones the topic for later discussion, destroying the chronology that introduces her actual explanation.
findings.japanese: 「とは言っても、それは本当に後日談でしかなくて」
findings.todokanai: "Even so, this is something we should really discuss later on."

findings.highlight: those who should enjoy their work but don't
findings.evidenceJa: 楽しめるくせに楽しまない奴
findings.explanation: After condemning escape into work, Mari says she cannot stand people who are capable of enjoying life or themselves but refuse to do so. The translation makes work the object of enjoyment, undercutting the contrast between work as escape and neglected private life.
findings.japanese:
「私は、仕事に逃げる奴が許せない。
楽しめるくせに楽しまない奴が我慢できない」
findings.todokanai: "I can't forgive those who run away by immersing themselves in work. I also can't stand those who should enjoy their work but don't."

findings.highlight: when we have our lunch break
findings.evidenceJa: 午後から仕事休んで二人で役所に行って
findings.explanation: Mari's example assumes the couple takes the afternoon off work to go to city hall. The translation restricts the errand to a lunch break, changing the planned work absence in her work-versus-private-life test.
findings.japanese:
「…例えばさ、
午後から仕事休んで二人で役所に行って、
婚姻届を出そうって約束したとするよな？」
findings.todokanai: "…For example, would we promise to submit our marriage registration at the city hall when we have our lunch break?"

findings.highlight: a special report just twelve hours ago
findings.evidenceJa: １２時直前に特ダネの連絡が入って
findings.explanation: Mari asks what Haruki would do if a scoop arrived just before noon, immediately before the planned afternoon marriage-registration errand. The translation changes that clock time into twelve hours ago and breaks the collision between the two commitments.
findings.japanese:
「そ、そ、それで、本題はこっちだ。
…１２時直前に特ダネの連絡が入って、
どうしても現場に飛ぶ必要があったらお前はどうする？」
findings.todokanai: "W-W-Well, let's get to the main topic. …What would you do if you were assigned a special report just twelve hours ago and had to fly to the scene no matter what?"

findings.highlight: someone who just can't understand how to work
findings.evidenceJa: 仕事に理解のない相手とは、もう恋愛できない
findings.explanation: Mari says she can no longer date a partner who does not understand or accept her work. The translation instead rejects someone who does not understand how to work, changing compatibility with her career into the partner's general work competence.
findings.japanese:
「…ま、それ以前にそういうことしっかり
話し合っておくのが大事だけどな。
仕事に理解のない相手とは、もう恋愛できないよ、私は」
findings.todokanai: "…Well, this is something we need to discuss beforehand. I can't be in a relationship with someone who just can't understand how to work."

findings.highlight: you're the man I've been looking for
findings.evidenceJa: 私が見込んだ通りの男
findings.explanation: Mari calls Haruki a man just as promising or capable as she judged him to be, then retreats to 'junior.' The translation calls him the man she has been looking for, inflating professional confidence into a romantic search fulfilled.
findings.japanese:
「やっぱりお前は、私が見込んだ通りの男…
いや、後輩だよ」
findings.todokanai: "As I thought, you're the man I've been looking for… Well, I should say underling."

findings.highlight: everything about my world, including myself, has been a lie
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を含めた世界全部に嘘をついてます
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is actively lying to the whole world, including himself, about why he sought Mari. The translation instead says his world itself has been a lie, removing his agency and present confession of deception.
findings.japanese: 俺は今、自分を含めた世界全部に嘘をついてます。
findings.todokanai: With the way I am now, everything about my world, including myself, has been a lie.

findings.highlight: I'm only fooling myself that they're hurting so much.
findings.evidenceJa: とても痛いのに、傷を消してしまうのが怖いから、ただ、痛みだけを誤魔化したかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says the wound truly hurts, but because he fears erasing it he only wanted to mask or numb the pain. The translation says he is fooling himself that the wounds hurt, denying the real pain that makes Mari an anesthetic rather than a cure.
findings.japanese:
とても痛いのに、傷を消してしまうのが怖いから、
ただ、痛みだけを誤魔化したかったんです。
findings.todokanai: After all, I'm scared of losing these wounds despite how painful they are, and I'm only fooling myself that they're hurting so much.

findings.highlight: it'll only raise her heartbeat unnecessarily
findings.evidenceJa: 余計に胸の高鳴りが抑えられなくなってしまう
findings.explanation: Haruki says Mari's shy, turned-away attitude makes his own racing heart even harder to control. The translation assigns the rising heartbeat to Mari instead.
findings.japanese:
そんな態度を取られたら、
余計に胸の高鳴りが抑えられなくなってしまうことが。
findings.todokanai: The fact that if she takes that attitude, it'll only raise her heartbeat unnecessarily.

findings.highlight: Even though I'm at my wit's end
findings.evidenceJa: 俺がこんなに極まってるのに
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is already at an extreme peak of arousal while Mari remains preoccupied with age and skincare. The translation makes him at his wit's end, changing sexual excitement into frustration or exhausted desperation.
findings.japanese: 俺がこんなに極まってるのに…
findings.todokanai: Even though I'm at my wit's end…

findings.highlight: it's still not as great, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 若いコと比べても遜色ない、かな？
findings.explanation: Mari anxiously asks whether her skin compares without inferiority even to women Haruki's age. The translation has her assert that it is not as good, reversing the reassurance she is seeking.
findings.japanese:
「わ、若いコと比べても遜色ない、かな？
その、北原と同じくらいのコたちと…」
findings.todokanai: "I-If you compare it to someone younger, it's still not as great, right? Um, the girls around your age…"

findings.highlight: Taking Mari-san's acting tough as approval
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんの強がりをいいことに
findings.explanation: Haruki says he takes advantage of Mari's brave front as he escalates from kissing to using his tongue. The translation explicitly treats that front as approval, converting opportunistic escalation into a consent signal.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんの強がりをいいことに、
キスの後、舌を這わせ、胸一杯に吸い込む。
findings.todokanai: Taking Mari-san's acting tough as approval, I slither my tongue after a kiss and happily breathe in.

findings.highlight: I slowly reduce my kisses on her back while bringing my hands from the outside of her thighs to the inside
findings.evidenceJa: 口づけを、徐々に、徐々に背中から下げていき、手の方は、太股の外側から裏側にかけて丹念に撫でる
findings.explanation: Haruki gradually moves his kisses downward along Mari's back while carefully stroking from the outside to the back of her thighs. The translation says he reduces the kisses and moves his hands to the inside of her thighs, changing both motions and sexual proximity.
findings.japanese:
口づけを、徐々に、徐々に背中から下げていき、
手の方は、太股の外側から裏側にかけて丹念に撫でる。
findings.todokanai: I slowly reduce my kisses on her back while bringing my hands from the outside of her thighs to the inside, carefully caressing her.

findings.highlight: As though intentionally avoiding her most precious area, I slowly let my affection for Mari-san accumulate elsewhere.
findings.evidenceJa:
麻理さんの、女の中心をわざと避けるように、
じっくりと愛撫を重ねていく。
findings.explanation: Haruki carefully layers physical caresses while avoiding Mari's sexual center, but the translation turns the caresses into affection accumulating elsewhere.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんの、女の中心をわざと避けるように、
じっくりと愛撫を重ねていく。
findings.todokanai: As though intentionally avoiding her most precious area, I slowly let my affection for Mari-san accumulate elsewhere.

findings.highlight: Like that, she slowly melts.
findings.evidenceJa: そうやって、ゆっくりと溶かしていく
findings.explanation: The transitive sentence continues into the next line: Haruki is slowly trying to melt the fear of him and sex that he believes he planted in Mari. The translation makes Mari herself melt and leaves the following fear fragments without their governing action.
findings.japanese: そうやって、ゆっくりと溶かしていく。
findings.todokanai: Like that, she slowly melts.

findings.highlight: she can't run away from me
findings.evidenceJa: 結局俺から逃げなかった
findings.explanation: After hesitating, Mari ultimately does not pull away from Haruki's renewed kiss. The translation says she cannot escape him, replacing her described choice not to retreat with physical or psychological inability.
findings.japanese:
そうすると麻理さんは、
少しだけ躊躇した後、結局俺から逃げなかった。
findings.todokanai: With that, Mari-san hesitates a little bit. But in the end, she can't run away from me.

findings.highlight: I'm… strangling Mari-san's chest.
findings.evidenceJa:
麻理さんの胸が…
俺に、揉みくちゃにされてる。
findings.explanation: Mari's breasts are being mauled or kneaded into disorder, rendered as Haruki strangling her chest.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんの胸が…
俺に、揉みくちゃにされてる。
findings.todokanai: I'm… strangling Mari-san's chest.

findings.highlight: the only sensation I can give her is what she's already used to
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の拙い経験からしても…いや、だからこそ、いつもと同じ感触しかしなかった
findings.explanation: Because Haruki's experience is limited, Mari's entrance feels only the same as the small amount he knows as usual; he cannot confidently infer anything exceptional from it. The translation makes a claim about Haruki giving Mari a familiar sensation, reversing perceiver and recipient and inventing knowledge of what she is used to.
findings.japanese:
その入り口は、俺の拙い経験からしても…
いや、だからこそ、いつもと同じ感触しかしなかった。
findings.todokanai: Because of my lack of experience… or rather, more so because of my lack of skill, the only sensation I can give her is what she's already used to.

findings.highlight: I was completely ready to go inside. The tips of our genitals are still touching.
findings.evidenceJa:
完全に入りかけていた。
性器の先っぽ同士は、今でも触れあってる。
findings.explanation: Haruki has physically begun to enter before Mari stops him, while the translation says only that he was ready to go inside.
findings.japanese:
完全に入りかけていた。
性器の先っぽ同士は、今でも触れあってる。
findings.todokanai: I was completely ready to go inside. The tips of our genitals are still touching.

findings.highlight: The fact that Mari-san had taken a contraceptive to avoid pregnancy just so she could accept me.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺を受け入れるためにも避妊薬を飲むほどに、
ずっと、妊娠するのを避け続けてきた麻理さん。
findings.explanation: Mari's long-standing avoidance of pregnancy is omitted from the observation that she even took contraception to accept Haruki.
findings.japanese:
俺を受け入れるためにも避妊薬を飲むほどに、
ずっと、妊娠するのを避け続けてきた麻理さん。
findings.todokanai: The fact that Mari-san had taken a contraceptive to avoid pregnancy just so she could accept me.

findings.highlight: words that mean the opposite of what she really wants to say
findings.evidenceJa: 苦悶の表情と、泣きそうな声と、そして、意味だけは裏腹な言葉
findings.explanation: Mari's permissive words contrast outwardly with her anguished face, near-tearful voice, and rigid body. The translation concludes that her words oppose what she truly wants to say, turning the bodily-verbal contradiction into an omniscient claim that her actual desire is refusal.
findings.japanese:
その度に麻理さんは顔をしかめ、
苦悶の表情と、泣きそうな声と、
そして、意味だけは裏腹な言葉を漏らす。
findings.todokanai: Every time it happens, Mari-san grimaces. With an expression of anguish and a voice like she's weeping, Mari-san lets out words that mean the opposite of what she really wants to say.

findings.highlight: I'm exploring the hidden depths of Mari-san that not even she herself knows.
findings.evidenceJa: 本人すら意図していないその深淵に、ずるずると引きずり落とされてる
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes he is being dragged helplessly down into an abyss that Mari herself does not intend. The translation makes him an active explorer of hidden depths she does not know, reversing agency and removing the dangerous pull.
findings.japanese:
俺は、本人すら意図していないその深淵に、
ずるずると引きずり落とされてるのを自覚する。
findings.todokanai: I realize that I'm exploring the hidden depths of Mari-san that not even she herself knows.

findings.highlight: she allows me to be assertive toward her
findings.evidenceJa: それでも少しずつ、積極性を出してきてくれている
findings.explanation: Despite being unusually passive relative to their workplace positions, Mari is gradually beginning to show initiative of her own. The translation instead says she permits Haruki to be assertive, assigning the growing activity to him.
findings.japanese:
俺たちの、社会的立場に照らし合わせてみれば、
ほぼ逆の受け身っぷりだけど、
それでも少しずつ、積極性を出してきてくれている。
findings.todokanai: If you compare our social positions, this directional relationship is usually backward. Even then, little by little, she allows me to be assertive toward her.

findings.highlight: A man who just got dumped
findings.evidenceJa: 一つの破局を迎えた男
findings.explanation: Takeya has just brought about a breakup by abandoning the woman at the hotel. The translation instead says that he was dumped, reversing who ended the relationship.
findings.japanese: たった今、一つの破局を迎えた男だった。
findings.todokanai: …A man who just got dumped.

findings.highlight: the truth that I would never have spoken of
findings.evidenceJa: 一番話さなくちゃならない事実
findings.explanation: Haruki calls this the fact he most has to discuss, despite it being hardest to raise. The translation turns that obligation into a categorical refusal or impossibility to speak.
findings.japanese:
かくして、一番話しづらくて、
そして、一番話さなくちゃならない事実は…
findings.todokanai: The truth I tried to hide, the truth that would be the most difficult to talk about, the truth that I would never have spoken of…

findings.highlight: "She's young and really successful, and has an insane work ethic."
findings.evidenceJa:
「若手の中じゃ出世頭で、
とにかくもの凄く仕事のできる人で」
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Mari the fastest-rising young employee and extraordinarily capable at her job; the English substitutes an 'insane work ethic,' changing proven professional ability into diligence.
findings.japanese:
「若手の中じゃ出世頭で、
とにかくもの凄く仕事のできる人で」
findings.todokanai: "She's young and really successful, and has an insane work ethic."

findings.highlight: I told him how I ended up being hurt
findings.evidenceJa: 傷つき、傷つけた俺
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly says that at New Year he was hurt and hurt Mari. The translation preserves only his victimhood and deletes his admission that he harmed her.
findings.japanese:
クリスマスの時の甘え、癒された俺。
年明け早々の傷つき、傷つけた俺。
findings.todokanai: I told him how I was spoiled and healed during Christmas. I told him how I ended up being hurt as soon as the new year began.

findings.highlight: if the other person cheated too and you guys broke up
findings.evidenceJa: 向こうも浮気と割り切ってんなら
findings.explanation: Takeya says matters would be simpler if Mari too understood and compartmentalized their involvement as an affair. The translation invents Mari cheating and a breakup between Haruki and Mari.
findings.japanese:
「かぁ～！
またややこしいことに…
向こうも浮気と割り切ってんならまだ簡単だったのに」
findings.todokanai: "Agh…! You're being complicated again… It would've been so much simpler if the other person cheated too and you guys broke up…"

findings.highlight: the whole time I held her in my arms
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女を抱くその瞬間まで、いつだってそんな機会はあった
findings.explanation: Haruki says he had chances to confess at every point up until the moment he slept with Mari. The translation limits those chances to the time during which he held her, materially narrowing his prolonged culpability.
findings.japanese:
彼女を抱くその瞬間まで、
いつだってそんな機会はあったのに。
それでも俺は、話さなかったんだから。
findings.todokanai: I had the chance to say it the whole time I held her in my arms, and yet, I still did not say it.

findings.highlight: Rather than talking about the truth, I yearned for her instead.
findings.evidenceJa:
本当のことを話すよりも、
彼女を求めることを選んだんだから。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he chose to seek Mari rather than tell her the truth; 'I yearned for her' removes the culpable choice and concrete pursuit.
findings.japanese:
本当のことを話すよりも、
彼女を求めることを選んだんだから。
findings.todokanai: Rather than talking about the truth, I yearned for her instead.

findings.highlight: Don't give me that cliche sentence
findings.evidenceJa: そんな下世話なこと聞くな
findings.explanation: Haruki rebukes Takeya for asking a vulgar or prurient question. The translation calls the preceding speech a cliche sentence, losing both the question and Haruki's privacy boundary.
findings.japanese:
「そんな下世話なこと聞くな…
親友だからって、俺に非があるからって、
それでも言っていいことと悪いことがあるぞ」
findings.todokanai: "Don't give me that cliche sentence… Even though you are a good friend of mine and even though I'm in the wrong here, there are still things you should and shouldn't say."

findings.highlight: he told me that he has no hobbies outside of work
findings.evidenceJa: 仕事以外に趣味がないって嫌よねぇ
findings.explanation: Mari makes a self-directed, general lament that having no hobbies beyond work is awful. The translation fabricates a man who told her that he has no hobbies.
findings.japanese:
「そ、それは…暇だったし、他にやることなかったし。
あ～、仕事以外に趣味がないって嫌よねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "W-Well… I was free, and there was nothing left to do after all. Ah～ he told me that he has no hobbies outside of work, which sucks."

findings.highlight: my crucial error in judgement
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の決断『しなさ』
findings.explanation: Haruki condemns his deliberate failure or refusal to decide, with quotation marks stressing the absence of a decision. The translation turns nondecision into one mistaken judgment.
findings.japanese:
俺の弱さも、俺の選択も、
そして俺の決断『しなさ』も、
自分でさえ反吐が出る汚さに満ちていたから。
findings.todokanai: I myself feel nauseated over the disgusting things I've doneーmy weakness, my choices, and my crucial error in judgement.

findings.highlight: I can't bring myself to want Setsuna
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜を、どうしても自分から求められない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he cannot bring himself to reach for or pursue Setsuna, while he pursued Mari in a cruel way. The translation changes an inability to act on his attachment into an absence of desire for Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
雪菜を、どうしても自分から求められない。
麻理さんには、あんな酷い求め方をしてしまう。
findings.todokanai: No matter what, I can't bring myself to want Setsuna. But as for Mari-san, I end up wanting her, which itself is cruel to Setsuna.

findings.highlight: now just a part of my history
findings.evidenceJa: 一つの歴史のこと
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Touma Kazusa one history in his life. 'Now just a part' adds temporal closure and diminution even as the passage shows her memory still powerfully governing him.
findings.japanese: 冬馬かずさという、一つの歴史のことを。
findings.todokanai: Touma Kazusaーnow just a part of my history.

findings.highlight: She was an excellent student in some ways, and an extremely poor student in others
findings.evidenceJa: 片や超がつくほどの優等生。片や激がつくほどの劣等生
findings.explanation: The paired 'one...the other...' construction contrasts Mari, an exceptional model student, with Kazusa, an extreme poor student. The translation assigns both attributes to one woman.
findings.japanese:
片や超がつくほどの優等生。
片や激がつくほどの劣等生。
findings.todokanai: She was an excellent student in some ways, and an extremely poor student in others.

findings.highlight: She stood above the rest in some ways, though in turn, she always stuck with that aloof air of hers
findings.evidenceJa: 片や常に人の上に立ち、片や何があろうと孤高を貫く
findings.explanation: The source again contrasts Mari's habitual leadership with Kazusa's unwavering isolation. The translation fuses the two women into a single composite character.
findings.japanese:
片や常に人の上に立ち、
片や何があろうと孤高を貫く。
findings.todokanai: She stood above the rest in some ways, though in turn, she always stuck with that aloof air of hers all the time.

findings.highlight: She's far from being a perfect replica of her
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の完成度からして違う
findings.explanation: Haruki says the two women differ even in their degree of completeness or maturity as people. The translation replaces that evaluative difference with the unrelated idea that Mari is an imperfect replica of Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
人間の完成度からして違う、
まったく別個の女性であるはずなのに。
findings.todokanai: She's far from being a perfect replica of her, and she's a completely different woman.

findings.highlight: I'm falling back in love with her
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女に、のめり込ませていく
findings.explanation: Mari's resemblance pulls Haruki into his memories while making him fall ever deeper into Mari. 'Back in love' instead suggests renewed love for the remembered Kazusa and fabricates a prior love cycle for the immediate female referent.
findings.japanese:
否応なく俺を思い出の中に引きずり込む。
彼女に、のめり込ませていく。
findings.todokanai: I'm being pulled back into my memories whether I like it or not. I'm falling back in love with her.

findings.highlight: You used to always reject talking about her
findings.evidenceJa: そんなこと話してよく振られなかったな
findings.explanation: Takeya marvels that Haruki could tell Mari about Kazusa without Mari dumping him. The translation fabricates a history in which Haruki refused to talk about Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
「そいや一緒に冬馬の記事書いたんだっけ？
お前、そんなこと話してよく振られなかったな」
findings.todokanai: "Which reminds me, you two wrote an article on Touma, right? You used to always reject talking about her."

findings.highlight: topic of conversation would not improve even with snacks or alcohol
findings.evidenceJa: 話題が肴では、酒はちっとも進まず
findings.explanation: Haruki says his joyless, irresoluble story makes poor drinking accompaniment, so the alcohol does not go down. The translation instead says snacks and alcohol fail to improve the topic.
findings.japanese:
俺の、楽しくもなく前向きでもなく
解決もしない話題が肴では、酒はちっとも進まず…
findings.todokanai: My neither fun, nor forward-facing, nor resolute topic of conversation would not improve even with snacks or alcohol.

findings.highlight: we said we would redo everythingーa passionate lie that brought us to tears
findings.evidenceJa: あの、クリスマスイブの夜からやり直そうって、魂を込めた嘘の涙を流す
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines a future deception: shedding wholly committed false tears and proposing that he and Setsuna restart from Christmas Eve. The translation presents this as a past joint promise and shared tears.
findings.japanese:
あの、クリスマスイブの夜からやり直そうって、
魂を込めた嘘の涙を流す。
findings.todokanai: That night on Christmas Eve, we said we would redo everythingーa passionate lie that brought us to tears.

findings.highlight: I've not said anything since January arrived. After all, nothing has happened
findings.evidenceJa: ここ一月の間にあったことを何も話さず、全部、なかったことにして
findings.explanation: The imagined lie would conceal everything that happened during the past month and treat it all as though it never occurred. The translation misreads 'the past month' as January and asserts that nothing actually happened.
findings.japanese:
…ここ一月の間にあったことを何も話さず、
全部、なかったことにして。
findings.todokanai: …I've not said anything since January arrived. After all, nothing has happened.

findings.highlight: Didn't you say you understood when I said that I couldn't?
findings.evidenceJa: 俺にできるわけないってわかってて言ってるだろ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether Takeya suggested the lie while knowing Haruki could never carry it out. The translation invents an earlier exchange in which Takeya said he understood Haruki's statement.
findings.japanese: 「…俺にできるわけないってわかってて言ってるだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "…Didn't you say you understood when I said that I couldn't?"

findings.highlight: "close up small wounds," or to make her feel relieved
findings.evidenceJa: 『傷が浅くてすんだ』なんて胸をなで下ろせるほど
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is neither brazen nor untroubled enough to expose everything, decide cleanly, and then reassure himself that the wounds stayed shallow. The translation invents wound-closing and assigns the relief to Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
だからって、全てを白日の下に晒し、
はっきりと結論を出して、『傷が浅くてすんだ』なんて
胸をなで下ろせるほど厚顔でも平気でもない。
findings.todokanai: Even so, I don't have the audacity nor the courage to expose everything to the light of day, to properly come to a conclusion, to "close up small wounds," or to make her feel relieved.

findings.highlight: I won't tell Io about this, either
findings.evidenceJa: 依緒にも言わせない
findings.explanation: Takeya promises that if Haruki reaches a conclusion after suffering it through, he will no longer complain and will not let Io complain either. The translation instead promises to keep the matter secret from Io.
findings.japanese:
「苦しんで、のたうち回って…
それで出した結論なら、俺はもう文句言わない。
依緒にも言わせない」
findings.todokanai: "So you want to suffer and writhe in your own misery… and if you end up making a decision after that, I won't have any more complaints. I won't tell Io about this, either."

findings.highlight: the night where I became alone
findings.evidenceJa: 一つになった夜
findings.explanation: Haruki calls it the night when he and Mari became one. The translation renders this as the night he became alone, the direct opposite of the sexual and emotional union described.
findings.japanese: クリスマスの夜、過ちの夜、そして一つになった夜…
findings.todokanai: About that night on Christmas Eve, the night where I made that grave mistake, the night where I became alone…

findings.highlight: I'll be sure to live my life normally too
findings.evidenceJa: わたしも日々ちゃんと普通に生きてるよ
findings.explanation: Setsuna reassures Haruki that she is already living an ordinary life day by day despite her pain. The translation turns that present fact into a promise about what she will do.
findings.japanese: 『わたしも日々ちゃんと普通に生きてるよ』
findings.todokanai: "I'll be sure to live my life normally too."

findings.highlight: Mari-san, whom I promised to meet, an essential piece of what makes up this crossroad of destiny
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんと会う約束をした、あの、運命の分岐点のうちの、重要な一つ
findings.explanation: The phone call on which Haruki arranged to meet Mari was one important fork in fate. The translation makes Mari herself an appositive 'piece' of a singular crossroads, obscuring the causal event he has just identified.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんと会う約束をした、
あの、運命の分岐点のうちの、重要な一つ。
findings.todokanai: Mari-san, whom I promised to meet, an essential piece of what makes up this crossroad of destiny.

findings.highlight: No matter how you look at it, this deadline is stupid
findings.evidenceJa: どっちも締め切りブッチしてるってのに
findings.explanation: Hamada protests that Mari is only one step ahead even though both of them have blown their deadlines. The translation calls the deadline stupid and deletes the admission that both workers missed it.
findings.japanese:
「なんでことごとく俺の一歩だけ先を行きやがる！
どっちも締め切りブッチしてるってのに！」
findings.todokanai: "How are you always one step ahead of me!? No matter how you look at it, this deadline is stupid!"

findings.highlight: how was there ever a time when I was really so deeply in love with this person?
findings.evidenceJa: このひとに深くのめり込んでいった俺は、果たして存在したんだろうか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether his present self—the self who has fallen deeply into Mari—would exist if Setsuna had spoken to him that Wednesday. The translation instead questions whether such love ever existed in the past.
findings.japanese:
今の俺は…
このひとに深くのめり込んでいった俺は、
果たして存在したんだろうか…
findings.todokanai: With the way I am right now… how was there ever a time when I was really so deeply in love with this person?

findings.highlight: her time of ridiculing others was long over
findings.evidenceJa: 人をからかって遊んでる時間帯はとっくに過ぎ去ってるのに
findings.explanation: Haruki notes that it is already far too late at night for Suzuki to be wasting time teasing people, yet she continues. The translation says her period of teasing was over, implying that the action had stopped.
findings.japanese:
大体、人をからかって遊んでる時間帯は
とっくに過ぎ去ってるのにこの人は…
findings.todokanai: For the most part, her time of ridiculing others was long over.

findings.highlight: To be told to go home this early… This is a warning sign to me that something bad has happened…
findings.evidenceJa:
こんな『早い』時間に帰されるなんて、
何か良くないことが起こる前ぶれとしか…
findings.explanation: Haruki treats the early dismissal as an omen that something bad is about to happen; the English says the bad event has already happened.
findings.japanese:
こんな『早い』時間に帰されるなんて、
何か良くないことが起こる前ぶれとしか…
findings.todokanai: To be told to go home this early… This is a warning sign to me that something bad has happened…

findings.highlight: Stay home for as long as you want. Just calling or emailing is fine
findings.evidenceJa: 会社を一歩出たら好きなだけメールでも電話でもすればいい
findings.explanation: Mari sarcastically permits Haruki to email or call as much as he likes once he steps outside the company. The translation invents an instruction to stay home and restricts him to remote contact.
findings.japanese:
「会社を一歩出たら好きなだけ
メールでも電話でもすればいい。
よい週末を」
findings.todokanai: "Stay home for as long as you want. Just calling or emailing is fine. Have a nice weekend."

findings.highlight: I won't even be able to give Mari-san a follow-up call
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんが帰った頃を見計らって、フォローの電話を入れなければならない
findings.explanation: Haruki decides the situation is serious enough that he must time a conciliatory call for when Mari gets home. The translation says he will be unable to make that call.
findings.japanese:
これは一度、麻理さんが帰った頃を見計らって、
フォローの電話を入れなければならないレベルの…
findings.todokanai: And I imagine I've messed up so horribly this time that I won't even be able to give Mari-san a follow-up call, judging from when she's going to be back…

findings.highlight: Don't get lost
findings.evidenceJa: 寄り道なんかするなよ
findings.explanation: Mari tells Haruki not to make any detours, the final coded direction that sends him straight to her apartment using the key. 'Don't get lost' changes deliberate destination choice into navigation.
findings.japanese:
「さっさと帰れ。
…寄り道なんかするなよ」
findings.todokanai: "You should go home already. …Don't get lost, okay?"

findings.highlight: I've only got the one I gave you earlier
findings.evidenceJa: 私、カギ持ってないんだ。…さっきお前に渡したやつしか
findings.explanation: Mari has no key because her sole key is the one she gave Haruki. The translation says she still has that key, contradicting both her being locked out and Haruki's possession of it.
findings.japanese:
「モニターの下の解錠ボタン押してくれ。
私、カギ持ってないんだ。
…さっきお前に渡したやつしか」
findings.todokanai: "Could you press the unlock button under the screen? I don't have my key on me. …I've only got the one I gave you earlier."

findings.highlight: she was trying to tell me, "your girlfriend is waiting for you"
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に『彼女を待たせて』いたとしたら
findings.explanation: Haruki considers what would have happened if he really had kept a girlfriend waiting and therefore gone to her instead of Mari's room. The translation makes the condition merely whether Mari intended her earlier sarcastic words.
findings.japanese:
いや、そもそも気づいたとしても、
本当に『彼女を待たせて』いたとしたら。
findings.todokanai: No, even if I did realize that she was trying to tell me, "your girlfriend is waiting for you" in the first place…

findings.highlight: And yet, right now, I can't come to grips with the reality that I happily accept these feelings.
findings.evidenceJa:
なのに、今の俺は、
その気持ちを嬉しく受け止めるだけの真実を
持ちきれないなんて…
findings.explanation: Haruki says he lacks enough truth or honesty to receive Mari's feelings with uncomplicated joy; the English instead says he cannot accept the reality that he does receive them happily, producing a different and opaque claim.
findings.japanese:
なのに、今の俺は、
その気持ちを嬉しく受け止めるだけの真実を
持ちきれないなんて…
findings.todokanai: And yet, right now, I can't come to grips with the reality that I happily accept these feelings.

findings.highlight: If I am, your tiredness won't go away
findings.evidenceJa: 強くしないと疲れ取れないですよ
findings.explanation: Haruki says that unless he presses hard, the fatigue will not come out. The translation's malformed conditional states the opposite: if he is forceful, her fatigue will remain.
findings.japanese:
「強くしないと疲れ取れないですよ。
ほら、このくらい我慢してください。大人なんだから」
findings.todokanai: "If I am, your tiredness won't go away. Just bear with it. You're an adult, aren't you?"

findings.highlight: As I thoroughly explored her feet, Mari-san's expression changed from one of ecstasy to one of agony.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺に足の裏をがっちりと極められ、
麻理さんの表情が恍惚から苦痛へと変わる。
findings.explanation: Haruki has Mari's sole firmly locked in a painful pressure-point hold; the English says he merely 'explored her feet,' erasing the action that changes ecstasy to pain.
findings.japanese:
俺に足の裏をがっちりと極められ、
麻理さんの表情が恍惚から苦痛へと変わる。
findings.todokanai: As I thoroughly explored her feet, Mari-san's expression changed from one of ecstasy to one of agony.

findings.highlight: as I lift up her well-toned feet
findings.evidenceJa: その肉付きのいい脚を持ち上げ
findings.explanation: Mari lies back, removes her stockings, and raises her own shapely legs while looking invitingly at Haruki. The translation makes Haruki lift them, altering who initiates the sexualized pose.
findings.japanese:
ベッドに身体を横たえ、ストッキングを脱ぎ、
その肉付きのいい脚を持ち上げ、
俺を誘うような視線を向けて…
findings.todokanai: She's lying on the bed on her back with her stockings pulled off, and as I lift up her well-toned feet, she looks at me with a seductive gaze…

findings.highlight: just to be criticized by you
findings.evidenceJa: 休みになると北原に責められて
findings.explanation: Mari jokes that on her days off Haruki sexually ravishes or relentlessly works her over. The translation reads the erotic seme-ru as ordinary criticism, breaking the stamina joke.
findings.japanese:
「仕事で疲れ果てて帰ってきて、
なのに休みになると北原に責められて、
くたくたのまま、また仕事に出かけて…」
findings.todokanai: "I get tired from work, and then I finally get some time off just to be criticized by you, and then I have to go to work again even though I'm exhausted…"

findings.highlight: "Y…Yeah… It's enough…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「う、うん…
それ、結構…」
findings.explanation: Mari says the massage feels quite good; 'It's enough' instead tells Haruki to stop, reversing the line's practical force.
findings.japanese:
「う、うん…
それ、結構…」
findings.todokanai: "Y…Yeah… It's enough…"

findings.highlight: someone who knows what I want and agrees with it
findings.evidenceJa: 私の意図を正確に汲んでくれること。こちらの会話にきっちり合わせてキャッチボールできること
findings.explanation: Mari values a partner who accurately reads her intent and can sustain a properly matched back-and-forth conversation. The translation replaces reciprocity with agreement or compliance.
findings.japanese:
「私が相手に求めるのは、
私の意図を正確に汲んでくれること。こちらの会話に
きっちり合わせてキャッチボールできること」
findings.todokanai: "What I search for in a partner is someone who knows what I want and agrees with it. Our conversations should always connect like we're playing catch."

findings.highlight: You've returned my warmth to me. And you've done so much more
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の体温を、与えてあげる。そしてもっともっと、あなたを
findings.explanation: Haruki gives Mari his body heat and trails into what more he will do to her. The translation reverses the transfer, saying Mari returned warmth to Haruki and already did more for him.
findings.japanese:
俺の体温を、与えてあげる。
そしてもっともっと、あなたを…
findings.todokanai: You've returned my warmth to me. And you've done so much more…

findings.highlight: my tongue crawled over her leg
findings.evidenceJa: 足の裏に舌を這わせると
findings.explanation: Haruki runs his tongue specifically over the sole of Mari's foot. The translation relocates the action to her leg, losing the fetishized body part that drives her reaction.
findings.japanese:
足の裏に舌を這わせると、
震えが全身に伝播し、
拗ねたような、泣きそうな表情を象っていく。
findings.todokanai: As my tongue crawled over her leg, the shivers spread to her whole body, and she put on a pouting expression that suggested she was about to cry.

findings.highlight: Just confirm what you need to do
findings.evidenceJa: 自分ですべきこと確認しただけよ
findings.explanation: To explain away 'hook my bra' to the caller, Mari claims she was merely checking aloud what she herself needed to do. The translation gives the caller an imperative to confirm their own tasks.
findings.japanese:
「………自分ですべきこと確認しただけよ。
誰もいないってば」
findings.todokanai: "…Just confirm what you need to do. There's no one else."

findings.highlight: the fact that nothing seems to be impossible for her
findings.evidenceJa: 決して無理をしていないふうなのが
findings.explanation: Mari's manner and expression do not look forced despite the abrupt work demand; Haruki reads that composure as strength and kindness. The translation turns the absence of visible strain into limitless capability.
findings.japanese:
その仕草や表情が、
決して無理をしていないふうなのが、
彼女の強さと、優しさなんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: Her actions, her expressions, and the fact that nothing seems to be impossible for her all attest to her strength and kindness.

findings.highlight: I was the one who was played with, in a good way
findings.evidenceJa: またいいように弄ばれただけ
findings.explanation: Mari ruefully says Haruki again toyed with her however he pleased, despite her plan to lead. The translation makes the treatment positively 'in a good way,' muting her complaint about lost control.
findings.japanese:
「お前には物足りなかったんじゃないか？
今日こそは私が導いてやろうと思ってたのに、
結局、またいいように弄ばれただけだったし…」
findings.todokanai: "Aren't you unsatisfied? I thought it would be me taking the lead today, but again I was the one who was played with, in a good way…"

findings.highlight: These are really good. Seriously, people can't live without them
findings.evidenceJa: いざ自分がその立場になると………いいなぁこれ。ホント、人間って都合のいい生き物だよなぁ
findings.explanation: Mari admits that once she occupies the romantic-comic situation herself, it feels wonderful, and wryly calls humans self-serving creatures. The translation turns the scene into plural objects people cannot live without.
findings.japanese:
「いざ自分がその立場になると………いいなぁこれ。
ホント、人間って都合のいい生き物だよなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Come on, once you get to where I… These are really good. Seriously, people can't live without them."

findings.highlight: I promised Takahiro that I'd get him a reference book
findings.evidenceJa: 孝宏の参考書探しにつきあう約束してて
findings.explanation: Setsuna claims she promised to accompany Takahiro while he looked for study guides. The translation says she promised to obtain a single book for him, removing the shared outing that the following sibling scene exposes as a pretext.
findings.japanese:
『日曜日は先約があるの。
孝宏の参考書探しにつきあう約束してて』
findings.todokanai: "I have plans for Sunday. I promised Takahiro that I'd get him a reference book."

findings.highlight: if he even has the intention of studying properly this year
findings.evidenceJa: もしかして、今年は練習のつもりなのかな
findings.explanation: Setsuna jokes that perhaps Takahiro regards this year's actual entrance exam as merely a practice attempt. The translation instead questions whether he intends to study at all.
findings.japanese:
『あと一月もしないうちに入試本番なのに、
相変わらずのんきな弟でしょう？
もしかして、今年は練習のつもりなのかな？』
findings.todokanai: "As usual, he's such a carefree younger brother, even though he has entrance exams in less than a month. I wonder if he even has the intention of studying properly this year?"

findings.highlight: Saturday would have been open for her
findings.evidenceJa: しかも結局土曜が空いて
findings.explanation: Haruki thought he himself could not make Saturday, switched the invitation to Sunday, then unexpectedly became free on Saturday. The translation assigns that newly open Saturday to Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
土曜日は駄目だと思って日曜にしたら、
日曜は向こうがＮＧで、
しかも結局土曜が空いて…
findings.todokanai: I thought I couldn't make it on Saturday so I tried for Sunday, but it's no good for her on that day, and not only that, but Saturday would have been open for her…

findings.highlight: we are going out of our way to avoid one another
findings.evidenceJa: すれ違うことが義務づけられてでもいるんだろうか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether he and Setsuna are somehow fated or condemned to keep missing each other. The translation assigns both of them deliberate effort to avoid one another.
findings.japanese:
にしても…
今の俺と雪菜は、
すれ違うことが義務づけられてでもいるんだろうか。
findings.todokanai: Still… with the way Setsuna and I are right now, I wonder if we are going out of our way to avoid one another.

findings.highlight: One of the top universities?
findings.evidenceJa: 国立狙い？
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether Takahiro is aiming for a national university, contrasted with a university outside the region. The translation changes the public institutional category into a prestige ranking.
findings.japanese:
『どこ受けるって？　国立狙い？
それとも地方の大学とか？』
findings.todokanai: "What university does he want to be accepted to? One of the top universities? Or perhaps a local one?"

findings.highlight: My parents are sighing hopelessly about it
findings.evidenceJa: お父さんたちも、今年は諦めるかってため息ついてる
findings.explanation: Setsuna says their parents are sighing that perhaps Takahiro should give up on this year's attempt. The translation leaves only general hopelessness, deleting the concrete possibility of postponing admission for a year.
findings.japanese:
『しかも、だったら違う大学も受ければいいのに、
今になって峰城大にしか行きたくないなんて駄々こねて…
お父さんたちも、今年は諦めるかってため息ついてる』
findings.todokanai: "That, and we initially thought that it'd be fine if he applied to a different university, but now he's nagging adamantly about wanting to go to Houjou… My parents are sighing hopelessly about it."

findings.highlight: "That's why you should give some suggestions to my lackadaisical younger brother. It'd be great if you could lecture him, as usual."
findings.evidenceJa:
『そんなわけで、ウチのキリギリスな弟に、
何か言ってあげてください。
できればいつもの説教がいいな』
findings.explanation: Calling Takahiro the household's grasshopper invokes The Ant and the Grasshopper and his failure to prepare; 'lackadaisical younger brother' deletes the fable image and its joke.
findings.japanese:
『そんなわけで、ウチのキリギリスな弟に、
何か言ってあげてください。
できればいつもの説教がいいな』
findings.todokanai: "That's why you should give some suggestions to my lackadaisical younger brother. It'd be great if you could lecture him, as usual."

findings.highlight: Between today and yesterday, two days have already passed
findings.evidenceJa: もう、今日か明日、過ぎちゃったね
findings.explanation: By the time Setsuna reads Haruki's message, both of his proposed choices—'today or tomorrow'—have already passed. The translation invents a span 'between today and yesterday' and fails to identify the expired appointment options.
findings.japanese:
『もう、今日か明日、過ぎちゃったね。
わたしのうっかりのせいで、返事できなくてすいません』
findings.todokanai: "Between today and yesterday, two days have already passed. I'm sorry I couldn't reply due to my carelessness."

findings.highlight: Please change the date again
findings.evidenceJa: また、日を改めさせてください
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks Haruki to let her propose or arrange another day, accepting responsibility for the reschedule. The translation commands Haruki to change the date.
findings.japanese:
『また、日を改めさせてください。
それじゃ、おやすみなさい』
findings.todokanai: "Please change the date again. Well then, good night."

findings.highlight: because I've already gained such a reputation
findings.evidenceJa: 今までの蓄積があったから勘違いされてる
findings.explanation: Haruki says people misjudge his festival-term performance because he had accumulated strong academic results beforehand. The translation replaces that concrete accumulated record with a vague reputation.
findings.japanese:
『俺だって、学園祭後の期末はボロボロだったよ。
今までの蓄積があったから勘違いされてるけど』
findings.todokanai: "Actually, I too was in pretty bad shape for the final exams after the festival. I guess I'm misunderstood now because I've already gained such a reputation."

findings.highlight: If you happen to bump into me on campus
findings.evidenceJa: 大学で合流して
findings.explanation: Haruki proposes deliberately meeting up on campus and then talking at a family restaurant. The translation turns their planned rendezvous into a chance encounter.
findings.japanese:
『金曜なら午前中も空けられる。
大学で合流して、どこかファミレスとかで話すのでも
全然ＯＫだから』
findings.todokanai: "I'm also free before noon on Friday. If you happen to bump into me on campus, I'm completely okay with talking with you over lunch at a family restaurant or something."

findings.highlight: After we finished the photocopying
findings.evidenceJa: コピーが終わっても、その後仕分けとかついでに勉強会とか
findings.explanation: Setsuna describes what will still need to happen after the upcoming photocopying, explaining why the end time is unknown. The translation places the copying in the past while the rest of the plan remains future.
findings.japanese:
『コピーが終わっても、
その後仕分けとかついでに勉強会とか（ついでって…）、
何時に終わるかわからないみたい』
findings.todokanai: "After we finished the photocopying, we were thinking about assorting our materials and having a study meeting afterward. We don't really know when we'll finish."

findings.highlight: I shouldn't have been saying those things despite knowing that we're preparing for exams
findings.evidenceJa: 試験前の忙しいときに無理言ってごめん
findings.explanation: Haruki apologizes for making an unreasonable request of Setsuna during her busy pre-exam period. The translation vaguely regrets 'those things' and changes Setsuna's burden into shared exam preparation.
findings.japanese: 『こっちこそ、試験前の忙しいときに無理言ってごめん』
findings.todokanai: "It's just that I shouldn't have been saying those things despite knowing that we're preparing for exams…"

findings.highlight: a life-or-death situation for most people
findings.evidenceJa: 人によっては四年に進級できるかの瀬戸際
findings.explanation: Haruki says that for some students these finals determine whether they can advance to fourth year. The translation inflates 'some' to 'most' and dramatizes the academic threshold as life or death.
findings.japanese:
『そうだよな、期末試験なんだし、
人によっては四年に進級できるかの瀬戸際だもんな』
findings.todokanai: "After all, it's the final exams we're talking about here, so it's a life-or-death situation for most people who want to advance into their fourth year."

findings.highlight: I've been indecisive for more than ten days
findings.evidenceJa: 十日以上もこうして宙に浮いたまま
findings.explanation: Haruki's decision and cruel choice have remained suspended for over ten days because he and Setsuna cannot meet, draining his painfully raised resolve. The translation attributes the delay directly to Haruki's indecision.
findings.japanese:
十日以上もこうして宙に浮いたまま、
必死に持ち上げたテンションを、重く強く殺いでいく。
findings.todokanai: But I've been indecisive for more than ten days, and the resolve that I'd desperately tried to hold onto ended up dwindling heavily.

findings.highlight: Her breakdown on Christmas Eve
findings.evidenceJa: クリスマスイブの決裂
findings.explanation: Haruki lists the rupture or falling-out between him and Setsuna on Christmas Eve. The translation turns the relational break into Setsuna's individual emotional breakdown.
findings.japanese:
クリスマスイブの決裂。
その後の長すぎる冷却期間。
雪菜からのメールに、数日間応えなかった俺。
findings.todokanai: Her breakdown on Christmas Eve. The excessively long cold period that ensued after that. Me taking days to reply to Setsuna's texts.

findings.highlight: because of the other's attitude
findings.evidenceJa: 相手の出方を伺ってばかりで
findings.explanation: Haruki condemns passively waiting to see what the other person will do as another form of flight. The translation makes the lack of progress a consequence of the other person's attitude.
findings.japanese:
相手の出方を伺ってばかりで何の進展もないのは、
逃げているのと同じこと。
findings.todokanai: Not advancing forward because of the other's attitude is ultimately no different from running away.

findings.highlight: at the person who's the most convenient
findings.evidenceJa: 一番ぶつけやすくて、ぶつけたい人
findings.explanation: Haruki directs his bottled-up distress at the person easiest to unload on and the person he actively wants to unload on: Mari. The translation retains convenience but deletes his desire for her as the target.
findings.japanese:
胸に溜まった中途半端で行き場のないもやもやを、
一番ぶつけやすくて、ぶつけたい人に向けてしまう。
findings.todokanai: I'm throwing all my bottled-up, half-baked emotions of confusion and uncertainty at the person who's the most convenient.

findings.highlight: It's so difficult to keep it all in
findings.evidenceJa: なのに、止まらない
findings.explanation: Despite having intended to wait, Haruki states plainly that he does not stop. The translation externalizes that choice as difficulty containing feelings, softening his continued pressure on Mari.
findings.japanese: なのに、止まらない。
findings.todokanai: It's so difficult to keep it all in, though.

findings.highlight: truly lustfully calculating
findings.evidenceJa: 本当は嫌らしいまでに打算的
findings.explanation: Haruki calls himself calculating to a disgusting or repellent degree. The translation reads the evaluative iyarashii as sexual lust and changes cynical manipulation into erotic calculation.
findings.japanese:
あまりにも情けなくて、卑怯で、陰湿で、
けれど本当は嫌らしいまでに打算的で。
findings.todokanai: Am absolutely deplorable, cowardly, and devious… Though I'm also truly lustfully calculating.

findings.highlight: confidently fabricating my miserable state
findings.evidenceJa: 十分な勝算あっての負けたふり
findings.explanation: Haruki knowingly pretends defeat or weakness because he judges the odds of Mari yielding to be good. The translation says he fabricates his miserable state but loses the calculated feint and expected victory that make the tactic explicit.
findings.japanese:
彼女の人の良さと姉御肌なところに付け込んだ、
十分な勝算あっての負けたふり…
findings.todokanai: I'm taking advantage of her kindness and her sisterly demeanor, confidently fabricating my miserable state…

findings.highlight: Fukagawa Yumi from the Public Policy Department
findings.evidenceJa: 同じ政経の深川由美
findings.explanation: Yumi is in the same Politics and Economics program as Setsuna. The English again changes 政経 to Public Policy, repeating the systematic academic-field error found elsewhere in the route.
findings.japanese:
『由美って覚えてる？　同じ政経の深川由美。
彼女の家に四人集まって、コピーの仕分けついでに、
一応、勉強もしておこうって話になってね』
findings.todokanai: "Do you know Yumi? Fukagawa Yumi from the Public Policy Department? The four of us gathered at her place, and after distributing our copied notes, we ended up studying for a bit too."

findings.highlight: You can text me anytime, except for when I'm in the middle of exams, bathing, or before I go to sleep
findings.evidenceJa: 試験中だろうが就寝中だろうが入浴中だろうが、メールしてくれるのは全然構わない
findings.explanation: Haruki says Setsuna may email him regardless of whether he is taking an exam, sleeping, or bathing—there is no inconvenient time. The English turns the emphatic inclusive list into exceptions when she must not text, exactly reversing the reassurance he adds to soften his cold first draft.
findings.japanese:
『試験中だろうが就寝中だろうが入浴中だろうが、
メールしてくれるのは全然構わない』
findings.todokanai: "You can text me anytime, except for when I'm in the middle of exams, bathing, or before I go to sleep."

findings.highlight: I slowly let out a sigh as Mari-san gives no resistance
findings.evidenceJa: 麻理さんは無抵抗なような、だからこそこちらの負荷が高いような、そんな緩慢な動作のまま、ゆっくりため息をつく。
findings.explanation: Mari, moving sluggishly and offering no resistance as Haruki supports her, is the one who slowly sighs. The English assigns the sigh to Haruki, removing one of the bodily signs that her conspicuous cheerfulness is collapsing into exhaustion and anxiety.
findings.japanese:
麻理さんは無抵抗なような、
だからこそこちらの負荷が高いような、
そんな緩慢な動作のまま、ゆっくりため息をつく。
findings.todokanai: I slowly let out a sigh as Mari-san gives no resistance, which only serves to make my efforts more difficult due to how sluggish her movements are.

findings.highlight: Back when I forcibly took Mari-san for myself
findings.evidenceJa: 強引に奪いかけてしまった俺のような行為
findings.explanation: Haruki compares Mari's present aggression to the time he almost forcibly took her as she was leaving. The English says he did forcibly take her, changing an interrupted near-assault into a completed act and materially altering their sexual history.
findings.japanese:
去っていこうとする麻理さんを、
強引に奪いかけてしまった俺のような行為。
findings.todokanai: Back when I forcibly took Mari-san for myself when she was about to leave me.

findings.highlight: I wouldn't let even the slightest changes that she exhibits go unnoticed
findings.evidenceJa: 相手の、そんなちょっとした変化に目くじらなんか立てていられない
findings.explanation: Because Haruki himself has maintained an ambiguous attitude, he says he is in no position to make an issue of Mari's slight change in behavior. The English says he refuses to let even the slightest change escape notice, reversing humility and restraint into vigilance.
findings.japanese:
俺だって、ずっと曖昧な態度を取り続けてるのに、
相手の、そんなちょっとした変化に
目くじらなんか立てていられない。
findings.todokanai: Even if I've been acting rather ambiguously around her all this time, I wouldn't let even the slightest changes that she exhibits go unnoticed.

findings.highlight: So reliable, so dignified, and most of all, so delicately charming…
findings.evidenceJa:
なんて頼もしくて、なんて凛々しくて、
そして、なんて弱く、可愛いんだ…
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Mari strong, dignified, weak, and cute; the English drops 'weak' into the vaguer 'delicately charming.'
findings.japanese:
なんて頼もしくて、なんて凛々しくて、
そして、なんて弱く、可愛いんだ…
findings.todokanai: So reliable, so dignified, and most of all, so delicately charming…

findings.highlight: As I rub the area up and down, the movements of Mari-san's mouth suddenly stop and she promptly inquires about the uncomfortable teasing.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺が上下にこするたびに、
麻理さんの口の動きがぴたりと止まり、
早速違和感に苛まれていることを伺わせる。
findings.explanation: Mari's mouth stopping shows that the unfamiliar sensation is already tormenting her; the English says she 'inquires' about the teasing despite no speech.
findings.japanese:
俺が上下にこするたびに、
麻理さんの口の動きがぴたりと止まり、
早速違和感に苛まれていることを伺わせる。
findings.todokanai: As I rub the area up and down, the movements of Mari-san's mouth suddenly stop and she promptly inquires about the uncomfortable teasing.

findings.highlight: it gets caught by the folds of red flesh
findings.evidenceJa: その白い布すらも横にずらすと、その中に隠れていた赤い肉ひだにむしゃぶりつく。
findings.explanation: After moving the white underwear aside, Haruki devours or fastens his mouth on the exposed red folds. The English instead says the cloth 'gets caught' by them, reversing the actor and removing the oral act that directly causes Mari's climax in the following lines.
findings.japanese:
その白い布すらも横にずらすと、
その中に隠れていた赤い肉ひだにむしゃぶりつく。
findings.todokanai: When I slide that white cloth off to the side as well, it gets caught by the folds of red flesh hidden beneath it.

findings.highlight: Saying such utter vulgarities to someone
findings.evidenceJa: 人に散々はしたないとか言っておいて、自分がこれじゃ…あ、あぁ…やぁぁ…だ、駄目…忘れてくれ
findings.explanation: Mari is ashamed because after repeatedly calling other people indecent, she herself is now behaving this way. The English says she has spoken vulgarities to someone, losing the self-directed hypocrisy that makes her beg Haruki not to be disillusioned with her.
findings.japanese:
「人に散々はしたないとか言っておいて、
自分がこれじゃ…あ、あぁ…やぁぁ…
だ、駄目…忘れてくれ」
findings.todokanai: "Saying such utter vulgarities to someone… makes me… ahh, ah… nooo… I-I can't… please forget it!"

findings.highlight: I'll… I'll… go crazy
findings.evidenceJa: こんなことじゃ…困る。私、私…迷ってしまうじゃないか…っ
findings.explanation: Mari says Haruki treating her this way is a problem because it will make her waver or become uncertain—about leaving and about their relationship. The English says she will go crazy, replacing the decision-level conflict that explains her unusual desperation with generic sexual overwhelm.
findings.japanese:
「こんなことじゃ…困る。
私、私…迷ってしまうじゃないか…っ」
findings.todokanai: "If you keep going… I'll be in trouble. I'll… I'll… go crazy…"

findings.highlight: …For how long… have we been making love?
findings.evidenceJa: …どれだけの時間、抱きあってるんだろう。
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders how long they have been holding one another; the English says how long they have been making love.
findings.japanese: …どれだけの時間、抱きあってるんだろう。
findings.todokanai: …For how long… have we been making love?

findings.highlight: I indulge myself in her body and her reactions over and over like I'm trying to break her
findings.evidenceJa: 抱えていたはずの迷いを取り上げられ、麻理さんに粉砕されてしまったように、その身体と反応に溺れまくっている。
findings.explanation: Haruki feels as though Mari has seized and shattered the hesitation he had been carrying, leaving him to drown in her body and responses. The English makes Haruki try to break Mari, reversing both the agent and object of the passage's emotional destruction.
findings.japanese:
抱えていたはずの迷いを取り上げられ、
麻理さんに粉砕されてしまったように、
その身体と反応に溺れまくっている。
findings.todokanai: The hesitation and confusion I was shouldering are stripped away, as I indulge myself in her body and her reactions over and over like I'm trying to break her.

findings.highlight: I said, "What'll you do if you carelessly call me by my name at work?"
findings.evidenceJa: 前に一度、その話をしたことがあったけれど、『職場でうっかり名前で呼んでしまったらどうする？』と、少しだけ頬を膨らませ、拗ねたことがあった。
findings.explanation: Mari herself once pouted and explained that she avoids 'Haruki' because she might accidentally use his first name at work. The English assigns the quoted warning to Haruki, reversing who established this intimate surname rule and why her 'Kitahara' now carries special affection.
findings.japanese:
前に一度、その話をしたことがあったけれど、
『職場でうっかり名前で呼んでしまったらどうする？』と、
少しだけ頬を膨らませ、拗ねたことがあった。
findings.todokanai: We had this talk once before but… I said, "What'll you do if you carelessly call me by my name at work?" and with slightly pouted cheeks, she sulked.

findings.highlight: will start next week
findings.evidenceJa: 峰城大は、今週末をもって本年度の課程を修了し、再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる。
findings.explanation: 再来週 means the week after next, not next week. The English advances the university's incoming-student business by a full week in a scene whose calendar culminates in the February 14 scheduling conflict.
findings.japanese:
峰城大は、今週末をもって本年度の課程を修了し、
再来週からは、とうとう新入生相手の商売が始まる。
findings.todokanai: All of Houjou University's courses for this year will be finished by the end of the week. And the entrance exams for the new students will start next week.

findings.highlight: I'm finally done with my exams.
findings.evidenceJa: 『試験お疲れさま』
findings.explanation: The message says 'Good work on your exams,' not that the sender has finished hers. The following message separately says that Setsuna has just finished her last subject, so the English collapses two sides of the exchange and assigns the wrong content to this message.
findings.japanese: 『試験お疲れさま』
findings.todokanai: "I'm finally done with my exams."

findings.highlight: two whole months
findings.evidenceJa: ん～、全部の仕事が終わるまでには２月いっぱいかかるかなぁ
findings.explanation: 二月いっぱい means through the end of February. The scene is already in mid-February, so Mari expects roughly the rest of the month, not two whole months.
findings.japanese:
「ん～、全部の仕事が終わるまでには
２月いっぱいかかるかなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Hmm～ Wrapping up all my work is going to take two whole months, it seems."

findings.highlight: during her lunch break while she's at work on-site
findings.evidenceJa: 最近、麻理さんからは毎日『現地の』昼休みに電話がかかってくる。
findings.explanation: Quoted 現地の means Mari calls during the lunch hour in her local time abroad. The English reads 現地 as an on-site workplace, losing the time-zone contrast that establishes the daily international-call routine.
findings.japanese:
最近、麻理さんからは毎日
『現地の』昼休みに電話がかかってくる。
findings.todokanai: Nowadays, Mari-san calls me every day during her lunch break while she's at work on-site.

findings.highlight: She'll be continuing her business trip to America in December after that.
findings.evidenceJa: １２月に引き続きのアメリカ出張。しかも今度は、ほぼ一月間という長期滞在。
findings.explanation: Mari is on another American business trip following the one in December, and this time it is a nearly month-long stay. The English moves the trip into a future December and obscures that the present call is already coming from America.
findings.japanese:
１２月に引き続きのアメリカ出張。
しかも今度は、ほぼ一月間という長期滞在。
findings.todokanai: She'll be continuing her business trip to America in December after that. And I believe she's going to be staying there for about a month this time.

findings.highlight: I love you, Mari-san.
findings.evidenceJa: 「…好きですよ、麻理さんのこと」
findings.explanation: Mari asks whether Haruki 愛してくれてるか—whether he loves her—and he answers only 好きですよ, 'I do like/care for you.' The next narration explicitly says he still never reaches the words she truly wants. Translating his reply as 'I love you' erases the deliberate evasion on which the exchange turns.
findings.japanese: 「…好きですよ、麻理さんのこと」
findings.todokanai: "…I love you, Mari-san."

findings.highlight: we're in a state where we still haven't come to the conclusion we want, and when we're just one step away from it, too
findings.evidenceJa: だって、そこに辿り着きたいという結論にすら、まだ辿り着いていないという、さらに一歩手前の状態なんだから。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he has not even reached the conclusion that he wants to arrive at those words—he is one stage earlier than that. The English instead makes the couple sound one step away from a mutually desired conclusion, reversing how far Haruki remains from commitment.
findings.japanese:
だって、そこに辿り着きたいという結論にすら、
まだ辿り着いていないという、
さらに一歩手前の状態なんだから。
findings.todokanai: After all, we're in a state where we still haven't come to the conclusion we want, and when we're just one step away from it, too.

findings.highlight: she did sound exceptionally cheerful today
findings.evidenceJa: でも今日は、いつもと比べると格段に嬉しい言葉があったから、差し引きでも大幅プラスに傾いていた。
findings.explanation: Haruki says there was something Mari said today that made him far happier than usual, enough to leave the emotional balance strongly positive. The English instead describes Mari herself as sounding exceptionally cheerful, reassigning the emotion and losing why the promised return matters to him.
findings.japanese:
でも今日は、いつもと比べると
格段に嬉しい言葉があったから、
差し引きでも大幅プラスに傾いていた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, she did sound exceptionally cheerful today, so if you consider the good and the bad, I'd say it definitely leaned toward the good.

findings.highlight: My ignorance led me to the doorstep of this store once more.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はまた、馬鹿の一つ覚えみたいに、この店へと辿り着く。
findings.explanation: 馬鹿の一つ覚え means doing the same one thing like a fool who knows no other trick. Haruki has reflexively returned to the same gift shop; his ignorance does not lead him there. The English replaces self-mocking repetition with an invented causal character flaw.
findings.japanese:
俺はまた、馬鹿の一つ覚えみたいに、
この店へと辿り着く。
findings.todokanai: My ignorance led me to the doorstep of this store once more.

findings.highlight: Sorry for replying to you so late.
findings.evidenceJa: 『すいません、遅れます』
findings.explanation: Haruki's message says 'I'm sorry, I'll be late.' It does not apologize for a delayed reply. This is the notice that he will miss Mari's arrival and meet her only after seeing Setsuna, so the English changes the practical content of the message.
findings.japanese: 『すいません、遅れます』
findings.todokanai: "Sorry for replying to you so late."

findings.highlight: I can't repeat the mistake I made three years ago.
findings.evidenceJa: 三年前の非道を繰り返すわけにはいかないんです。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls his act three years ago 非道, inhuman cruelty; the English reduces it to a mistake.
findings.japanese: 三年前の非道を繰り返すわけにはいかないんです。
findings.todokanai: I can't repeat the mistake I made three years ago.

findings.highlight: If only I had rushed to give her my present immediately after buying it, just like what I've just done…
findings.evidenceJa: もしもあの日、プレゼントを買ったのが、今日みたいに時間ギリギリだったなら。
findings.explanation: Haruki wishes that three years earlier he had bought the present at the last possible moment, as he did today. The English instead says he wishes he had rushed to give it to Setsuna after buying it, altering the first condition in his chain of alternate-history causes.
findings.japanese:
もしもあの日、プレゼントを買ったのが、
今日みたいに時間ギリギリだったなら。
findings.todokanai: If only I had rushed to give her my present immediately after buying it, just like what I've just done…

findings.highlight: Regardless of my intention for seeking Kazusa out back then
findings.evidenceJa: 求める理由にどんな裏があろうとも、その想いだけは誰が何と言おうと本気だった。
findings.explanation: The omitted object is Setsuna from the preceding line: Haruki wanted Setsuna, and whatever ulterior motives lay behind wanting her, that feeling was real. The English substitutes Kazusa, reversing the woman whose sincerity this counterfactual is meant to establish.
findings.japanese:
求める理由にどんな裏があろうとも、
その想いだけは誰が何と言おうと本気だった。
findings.todokanai: Regardless of my intention for seeking Kazusa out back then, that feeling I had was real, no matter what anyone says.

findings.highlight: she'll continue telling me that she doesn't know anything until I spell it out to her
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんとわかってるのに、俺がはっきり口に出すまでは、自分は何もわかってないって言ってもいい。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that under the social rule Setsuna clings to, she is entitled to say she does not know until he states the breakup explicitly. The English says she will actively keep telling him she knows nothing, turning a fragile procedural refuge into a planned lie.
findings.japanese:
ちゃんとわかってるのに、
俺がはっきり口に出すまでは、
自分は何もわかってないって言ってもいい。
findings.todokanai: Despite knowing full well about those facts, she'll continue telling me that she doesn't know anything until I spell it out to her.

findings.highlight: under the haze of alcohol
findings.evidenceJa: 酒が見せた哀しい幻影だって、そう、思い込むしかない。
findings.explanation: Haruki decides to treat the self-destructive Setsuna before him as a sad apparition produced by her drinking. The English locates the alcohol haze in Haruki's own act of seeing, even though he declined alcohol and Setsuna is the one who drank herself into this state.
findings.japanese:
酒が見せた哀しい幻影だって、
そう、思い込むしかない。
findings.todokanai: …And she's merely a sorrowful illusion I'm seeing under the haze of alcohol.

findings.highlight: It's snowing, just like it did back then three years ago.
findings.evidenceJa: 三年前のあの時は、雪だった。ぬかるんだ心に足をとられ、つまづいた。
findings.explanation: The present sky is cold and clear with stars. Haruki says that three years earlier it was snowing, then metaphorically says his feet were caught in his muddied heart and he stumbled. The English falsely makes it snow now and turns the inner mud into a current physical slip, breaking both chronology and image.
findings.japanese:
三年前のあの時は、雪だった。
ぬかるんだ心に足をとられ、つまづいた。
findings.todokanai: It's snowing, just like it did back then three years ago. My wavering heart causes my feet to slip and stumble forward.

findings.highlight: I've spent almost 100000 yen just for this
findings.evidenceJa: 会社の金じゃないんだぞ、自費で帰ってきたんだぞ…今度は１０万どころの騒ぎじゃなかったんだぞ…っ
findings.explanation: Mari says the self-funded emergency return was not remotely a mere 100,000-yen matter—it cost far more. The English says she spent almost 100,000 yen, inverting the stated scale of her sacrifice.
findings.japanese:
「会社の金じゃないんだぞ、
自費で帰ってきたんだぞ…
今度は１０万どころの騒ぎじゃなかったんだぞ…っ」
findings.todokanai: "I wasn't paid by the company for this, you know. I paid to come back here on my own… You know that I've spent almost 100000 yen just for this, right…?"

findings.highlight: almost as important as you are
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺にとって、麻理さんと同じくらい大切な人の」
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Setsuna someone as important to him as Mari, 同じくらい. 'Almost as important' creates a hierarchy absent from the confession and softens precisely the equality that makes the disclosure devastating.
findings.japanese: 「俺にとって、麻理さんと同じくらい大切な人の」
findings.todokanai: "She's someone important to me, almost as important as you are, Mari-san…"

findings.highlight: forced myself to look their way
findings.evidenceJa: 心の行き場をなくし、近くの優しさにすがりつき、無理やり俺に向けさせようとした。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his stranded heart clung to nearby kindness and tried to force that kindness—Mari's feelings—to turn toward him. The English instead says he forced himself to look toward her, reversing the coercive direction in his self-indictment.
findings.japanese:
心の行き場をなくし、近くの優しさにすがりつき、
無理やり俺に向けさせようとした。
findings.todokanai: There was no place for my heart to go, so I chose to tightly cling onto the closest act of kindness and forced myself to look their way.

findings.highlight: as if to blow a gust of fresh air to bequeath my flustered self
findings.evidenceJa: そんな、俺の焦燥なんか何処吹く風みたいに、麻理さんがゆっくり立ち上がる。
findings.explanation: 何処吹く風 means acting as though another person's agitation is no concern of yours. Mari slowly stands as if Haruki's panic means nothing to her. The English decomposes the idiom into an incoherent literal gust of air that she somehow 'bequeaths' him.
findings.japanese:
そんな、俺の焦燥なんか何処吹く風みたいに、
麻理さんがゆっくり立ち上がる。
findings.todokanai: Mari-san slowly stood up, as if to blow a gust of fresh air to bequeath my flustered self.

findings.evidenceJa: 「メールの件、正気じゃないよな？」
findings.explanation: The editor asks whether Mari is sane—正気. She replies that she had hoped he would ask whether she was serious—本気. Rendering both words as 'serious' erases the one-character contrast and the joke that he treats her decision as insanity rather than mere bluffing.
findings.japanese: 「メールの件、正気じゃないよな？」
findings.todokanai: "About the email you sent me, you weren't serious, now, were you?"

おっしゃる通り、のびのびやらせてもらってます」
findings.todokanai: "Thank you very much. Just as you said, please allow me to do it."

findings.highlight: "In any case, I can't really refuse this arrangement given it's something that's decided by the company, and I have no reason to decline it at all since it's what I wished for in the first place. …And the truth is, it's something that I've decided on quite a while ago."

findings.explanation: The fourth blow stops just before landing because Haruki stops it. The English first says Mari stopped herself, then immediately says Haruki stopped her, producing an internally contradictory action and briefly assigning the decisive resistance to the wrong person.
findings.japanese:
四発目は、直前で止まった。
俺が、止めた。
findings.todokanai: She stopped before she could slap me for the fourth time. And I was the one who stopped her.

そんな俺の現実逃避を、

findings.explanation: Mari begins 'I, you… about you…' and cannot complete what is plainly tending toward a confession before retreating in line 698. The English supplies past tense and a possessive construction ('You were my…'), making Haruki answer 'I was your?' and forcing a specific utterance that the Japanese deliberately leaves broken.

私はお前が…お前のこと…」
findings.todokanai: "Goodbye, Kitahara. You… were my…"

findings.todokanai: "I… I'm… to me… even though you're the only one for me… even though you're… the only one!"

findings.explanation: Mari says that if Haruki had given her one word—just one word—the result could have changed. The English twice makes it 'a few words,' erasing the emphasis on a single decisive declaration.

findings.todokanai: "I… I, you… hah! You, with a few words… just a few words… u-uwaaah! Hah, aahn!"

俺にとっては、
最初から、あなたは剥き出しの女性だったのに…
findings.todokanai: From the very beginning, I had regarded you as a frank woman…

裏切り者、裏切りもの…うらぎりものぉ…っ」

findings.todokanai: "I'm just kidding. I know that if I'm truly going to apologize, I shouldn't be apologizing for this in particular."
