findings.highlight: Please don't put it that way…
findings.evidenceJa: 「そう言っていただけると…」
findings.explanation: Haruki says that hearing Hamada put it that way is a relief or something he appreciates. The English makes him ask Hamada not to say it, reversing his response to being released from guilt over resigning.
findings.japanese: 「そう言っていただけると…」
findings.todokanai: "Please don't put it that way…"

findings.highlight: I doubt I'll choose this path again.
findings.evidenceJa:
それは多分、
もう選ばれるはずのない進路だったけど。
findings.explanation: Kaiousha is a career path that is probably no longer available to Haruki; the English says he doubts he will choose it again.
findings.japanese:
それは多分、
もう選ばれるはずのない進路だったけど。
findings.todokanai: I doubt I'll choose this path again.

findings.highlight: it's amplifying the tortuous, anxious feeling that's festering within me
findings.evidenceJa: その痛みの思った以上の激しさは、自分の中にわだかまる、焦りにも似た感情によって増幅されているせいかもしれない。
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks his festering anxiety may be amplifying the physical pain of the cold wind. The English says the pain is amplifying the anxiety, reversing cause and effect in the body/feeling comparison.
findings.japanese:
その痛みの思った以上の激しさは、
自分の中にわだかまる、焦りにも似た感情によって
増幅されているせいかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: The pain feels more extreme than I expected it to be, perhaps because it's amplifying the tortuous, anxious feeling that's festering within me.

findings.highlight: I never asked anyone to do it with me.
findings.evidenceJa: 『本当は昔から一度はやってみたかったんだ。ただ、わたしってインドア派のイメージあったし、実際そうだったから今まで声かからなかったんだよね』
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that because everyone correctly saw her as indoorsy, nobody had ever invited her. The English says she never invited anyone herself, reversing the social agency and losing why Io's invitation matters to her.
findings.japanese:
『本当は昔から一度はやってみたかったんだ。
ただ、わたしってインドア派のイメージあったし、
実際そうだったから今まで声かからなかったんだよね』
findings.todokanai: "The truth is, I've been meaning to try something like this for a long time. It's just that everyone's had the perception of me being an indoorsy person, and it wasn't exactly wrong either, so I never asked anyone to do it with me."

findings.highlight: The moment I heard you weren't going, I found myself at a loss.
findings.evidenceJa: 『…春希くんが行かないって言ったとき、どうしようか、迷ってる』
findings.explanation: Setsuna is wondering what she will do if Haruki says he is not going. The English says she has already heard that he will not go, contradicting Haruki's later reply that he has not decided and erasing her indirect attempt to learn his choice.
findings.japanese:
『…春希くんが行かないって言ったとき、
どうしようか、迷ってる』
findings.todokanai: "…The moment I heard you weren't going, I found myself at a loss."

findings.highlight: Setsuna also knowing that she's wavering because my feelings are no longer directed at her
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は、俺の気持ちが自分じゃない方に揺れたのを感じ取っているのに。
findings.explanation: Setsuna has sensed that Haruki's feelings wavered toward someone other than her. The English makes Setsuna herself the one wavering, reversing the subject of the emotional movement she has detected.
findings.japanese:
雪菜は、俺の気持ちが自分じゃない方に揺れたのを
感じ取っているのに。
findings.todokanai: And this is despite Setsuna also knowing that she's wavering because my feelings are no longer directed at her.

findings.highlight: the event coordinator shot that idea down pretty quickly
findings.evidenceJa: 『俺も、スキーもスノボもやったことない。研究室でスキー合宿って話が出たけど、幹事権限で潰したくらいだし』
findings.explanation: Haruki says he used his own authority as organizer to kill his seminar's ski-camp proposal, proof of how little he wanted to ski. The English invents a separate event coordinator who killed it, removing Haruki's joke and agency.
findings.japanese:
『俺も、スキーもスノボもやったことない。
研究室でスキー合宿って話が出たけど、
幹事権限で潰したくらいだし』
findings.todokanai: "I've never gone skiing or snowboarding before either. Someone did throw around the idea for a group overnight skiing trip in one of my seminars, but the event coordinator shot that idea down pretty quickly."

findings.highlight: Whoever survives can worry about what to do next.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ま、今日はそんな古いことは忘れて、とりあえず潰れるまで飲みましょう？生き残った方が既成事実を作る方向で」
findings.explanation: Sawako jokes that they should drink until one collapses and the survivor can create a 既成事実—a sexual or romantic fait accompli. The English replaces the punch line with the survivor generically worrying about what to do next.
findings.japanese:
「ま、今日はそんな古いことは忘れて、
とりあえず潰れるまで飲みましょう？
生き残った方が既成事実を作る方向で」
findings.todokanai: "Well, how about we just let bygones be bygones today, and drink until we drop? Whoever survives can worry about what to do next."

findings.highlight: I don't think that simply hitting you a couple times will be nearly enough of a retribution
findings.evidenceJa: 「二、三発殴っても罰あたらないんじゃないかって、そのくらいは思ってるのよ？」
findings.explanation: Sawako says she thinks divine punishment would not strike her even if she hit Haruki two or three times—she would be justified in doing that much. The English says a couple of hits would not be enough punishment, escalating the number and changing her calibrated anger into a demand for more violence.
findings.japanese:
「二、三発殴っても罰あたらないんじゃないかって、
そのくらいは思ってるのよ？」
findings.todokanai: "And do you know that I don't think that simply hitting you a couple times will be nearly enough of a retribution?"

findings.highlight: there's still hope for you if you're ready to face the consequences
findings.evidenceJa: 「わたしが殴っても、麻理の傷は癒えないのよ？…あなたは罰を受けた気になって、少しは救われるのかもしれないけど」
findings.explanation: Sawako refuses because hitting Haruki would not heal Mari; it would only let him feel punished and therefore a little absolved. The English turns this critique of self-serving penance into hopeful approval that he is ready to face consequences.
findings.japanese:
「わたしが殴っても、麻理の傷は癒えないのよ？
…あなたは罰を受けた気になって、
少しは救われるのかもしれないけど」
findings.todokanai: "You know Mari's wounds won't heal even if I do hit you, right? …Though I suppose there's still hope for you if you're ready to face the consequences."

findings.highlight: It's just impossible to persuade her.
findings.evidenceJa: 「特にあいつは、今の段階で圧倒的に不利だからね。…ちっとも駆け引きしてやがらないんだもの」
findings.explanation: Mari is overwhelmingly disadvantaged because she is not playing any romantic game or strategy at all—she has exposed herself completely. The English says she is impossible to persuade, replacing the reason for her vulnerability with stubborn resistance.
findings.japanese:
「特にあいつは、今の段階で圧倒的に不利だからね。
…ちっとも駆け引きしてやがらないんだもの」
findings.todokanai: "Especially considering how severely disadvantaged she is right now. …It's just impossible to persuade her."

findings.highlight: It's a matter of who I could tell that I loved them…
findings.evidenceJa: 「誰に対しても好きって言えないんじゃなくて、誰に対しても好きって言ってしまっただけなんです…」
findings.explanation: Haruki's self-indictment is not that he cannot tell anyone he loves them, but that he has ended up saying it to everyone. The English reduces this to an opaque question of whom he could tell, deleting the serial confession that explains why even a sincere 'I love her' cannot exonerate him.
findings.japanese:
「誰に対しても好きって言えないんじゃなくて、
誰に対しても好きって言ってしまっただけなんです…」
findings.todokanai: "This isn't about me being unable to tell someone I love them. It's a matter of who I could tell that I loved them…"

findings.highlight: even though I'm still in love with Mari-san right now
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺は麻理さんに、昔好きだった人の面影を見てた。麻理さんを、今でも好きな人と同時に好きになった」
findings.explanation: Haruki says he saw in Mari the traces of someone he once loved, and fell for Mari while simultaneously loving a person he still loves now. 今でも好きな人 modifies the other person, not Mari. The English attaches the continuing love to Mari and reverses the temporal/referential structure of his divided heart.
findings.japanese:
「俺は麻理さんに、昔好きだった人の面影を見てた。
麻理さんを、今でも好きな人と同時に好きになった」
findings.todokanai: "I see someone I used to be in love with in Mari-san. And I'm in love with someone else simultaneously, even though I'm still in love with Mari-san right now."

findings.highlight: She's made up her mind not to even look for another man for the next five years!
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつ、この調子じゃ、ものすっごい引きずるよ？５年は新しい男見つけられないの確定よ！」
findings.explanation: Sawako predicts that Mari will certainly be unable to find another man for five years because she will take this breakup so badly. The English says Mari has consciously decided not to look, replacing emotional incapacity with a deliberate plan.
findings.japanese:
「あいつ、この調子じゃ、ものすっごい引きずるよ？
５年は新しい男見つけられないの確定よ！」
findings.todokanai: "Do you have any idea how long this'll keep dragging her down if she keeps this up? She's made up her mind not to even look for another man for the next five years!"

findings.highlight: you can't let her give up on falling in love for the rest of her life!
findings.evidenceJa: 「そうするしかないの！すぐ次の恋に走らせるか、一生恋を諦めさせるかしないと駄目なの！」
findings.explanation: Sawako says Haruki must force a decisive outcome: either send Mari running into a new love immediately or make her give up love for life. The English changes the second explicit alternative into something he must not allow, reversing one branch of the either/or construction.
findings.japanese:
「そうするしかないの！
すぐ次の恋に走らせるか、
一生恋を諦めさせるかしないと駄目なの！」
findings.todokanai: "Well, that's the only way you can do it! You need to push her toward her next love; you can't let her give up on falling in love for the rest of her life!"

findings.highlight: I wouldn't have expected the opportunity to work overseas if I didn't have the confidence.
findings.evidenceJa: 「自信がなきゃ海外赴任なんて希望しないわよ。３０前にせめてデスクにはなっておかないとね」
findings.explanation: Mari says she would not have requested an overseas posting without confidence; the transfer was her active longstanding ambition. The English says she would not have expected the opportunity, making her a passive recipient rather than the person who pursued it.
findings.japanese:
「自信がなきゃ海外赴任なんて希望しないわよ。
３０前にせめてデスクにはなっておかないとね」
findings.todokanai: "I wouldn't have expected the opportunity to work overseas if I didn't have the confidence. I want to at least be promoted to managing editor before I turn 30."

findings.highlight: I guess it's possible that that's the sort of relationship we had…
findings.evidenceJa: 「………冷静に考えてみると、私って、あっち関係では本当にそうかもしれない」
findings.explanation: After Sawako asks whether she is an M, Mari admits that when she thinks calmly, she really may be masochistic in sexual matters. The English says only that theirs may have been that sort of relationship, shifting the discovery from Mari's sexuality to a vague relationship dynamic.
findings.japanese:
「………冷静に考えてみると、
私って、あっち関係では本当にそうかもしれない」
findings.todokanai: "…If I calm down and think about it, I guess it's possible that that's the sort of relationship we had…"

findings.highlight: our barely budding relationship is now on the brink of collapse
findings.evidenceJa: けれど、その時深刻な話をしなかったせいで、始まったばかりの関係が、あっさりと破局を迎えた。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that because he and Mari failed to have the serious talk, their newly begun relationship readily reached a breakup. The English leaves them only on the brink of collapse, withholding the completed rupture that defines the route's present state.
findings.japanese:
けれど、その時深刻な話をしなかったせいで、
始まったばかりの関係が、あっさりと破局を迎えた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, it's exactly because we didn't manage to have that serious talk that our barely budding relationship is now on the brink of collapse.

findings.highlight: I'm alright with whatever time you decide.
findings.evidenceJa: 「いつならＯＫなんだよ？もうすぐ３月だぞ？」
findings.explanation: Takeya asks Haruki when Haruki will be available, pressing him to commit to a date before March. The English instead has Takeya offer unrestricted availability, reversing who must answer the scheduling question.
findings.japanese:
「いつならＯＫなんだよ？
もうすぐ３月だぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "I'm alright with whatever time you decide. It's almost March, you know?"

findings.highlight: they only work on the last days before the deadline, so nobody has come
findings.evidenceJa: …さすがに奴らは締め切り明けの日曜なんで、誰も来てないが
findings.explanation: The office is empty because this is the Sunday after the deadline, when the exhausted staff are finally absent. The English says they work only immediately before deadlines, losing the post-deadline timing and the workplace joke.
findings.japanese:
「で、今からこっちに顔出すか？　俺はいるぞ。
…さすがに奴らは締め切り明けの日曜なんで、
誰も来てないが」
findings.todokanai: "So are you going to show up here? I'm here. …As you'd expect, they only work on the last days before the deadline, so nobody has come."

findings.highlight: the memory of a certain someone inevitably popped into my mind
findings.evidenceJa: それでもなんとか無事故で切り抜けて、だから、いつかの誰かを思い出さずには済んだ。
findings.explanation: Because Haruki gets through the drive without an accident, he is spared having to remember a certain earlier driver. The English says the safe arrival inevitably makes him remember her, exactly reversing the negated result; the next line then jokes that articulating this has made him remember after all.
findings.japanese:
それでもなんとか無事故で切り抜けて、
だから、いつかの誰かを思い出さずには済んだ。
findings.todokanai: With the way we ended up reaching our venue without accident, the memory of a certain someone inevitably popped into my mind.

findings.highlight: "I see you still have that rigid way of thinking, huh, Haruki?"
findings.evidenceJa: 「相変わらず春希らしい堅実な考え方だねぇ」
findings.explanation: Takeya's career choice is called prudent or steady; the English calls it rigid.
findings.japanese: 「相変わらず春希らしい堅実な考え方だねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "I see you still have that rigid way of thinking, huh, Haruki?"

findings.highlight: I guess I just think I should still be working.
findings.evidenceJa: 一応、セミナーにはもう何度か参加してるけど、イマイチピンとこないって言うか…まだ働くんだっていう実感がね～
findings.explanation: Io has attended several recruiting seminars but still cannot quite feel that she is actually about to enter the workforce. The English says she thinks she should still be working, producing the wrong career state and an incoherent reply.
findings.japanese:
「一応、セミナーにはもう何度か参加してるけど、
イマイチピンとこないって言うか…
まだ働くんだっていう実感がね～」
findings.todokanai: "I attend seminars every now and then, but maybe I think it doesn't really help me or… I guess I just think I should still be working."

findings.highlight: Up until the point where he has to help a client, that is.
findings.evidenceJa: 「顧客に手を出したことが発覚するまではね」
findings.explanation: Io jokes that Takeya will prosper in insurance only until it is discovered that he has made a pass at or slept with a client. 手を出す is the punch line; the English turns the misconduct into the ordinary act of helping a client.
findings.japanese: 「顧客に手を出したことが発覚するまではね」
findings.todokanai: "Up until the point where he has to help a client, that is."

findings.highlight: "Before this, when I called him, he started babbling on in Kansai dialect."
findings.evidenceJa:
「この前電話かかってきたとき、
いきなり関西弁でまくしたてられてさ…」
findings.explanation: Hayasaka called Haruki to ask for Setsuna's contact details; the English suggests Haruki called Hayasaka.
findings.japanese:
「この前電話かかってきたとき、
いきなり関西弁でまくしたてられてさ…」
findings.todokanai: "Before this, when I called him, he started babbling on in Kansai dialect."

findings.highlight: Katou-san and I weren't even in the same class. We were farthest apart on attendance numbers
findings.evidenceJa: 「わたし、加藤さんとは同じクラスどころか、出席番号も一番違いだったのに…」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that she and Tomo were not merely in the same class: their attendance numbers were one apart. The English reverses both facts, putting them in different classes and at opposite ends of the roll.
findings.japanese:
「わたし、加藤さんとは同じクラスどころか、
出席番号も一番違いだったのに…」
findings.todokanai: "Katou-san and I weren't even in the same class. We were farthest apart on attendance numbers…"

findings.highlight: So I guess you could say it's not your fault.
findings.evidenceJa: …だから難攻不落だったとも言えるが
findings.explanation: Takeya says Setsuna's lifelong obliviousness to romance is precisely why she was an impregnable fortress. The English replaces the comic explanation for her legendary unattainability with generic reassurance that it was not her fault.
findings.japanese:
「ま、雪菜ちゃん、
昔っからそういうこと疎かったもんなぁ。
…だから難攻不落だったとも言えるが」
findings.todokanai: "Well, Setsuna-chan, you've been ill informed on this stuff for a long time. So I guess you could say it's not your fault."

findings.highlight: "But Nagisa got into a vocational school here, right? I wonder if she broke up with Hayasaka… At that time, did he say anything?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「でも渚ってこっちの短大進んだよね？
早坂とは切れちゃったのかなぁ…
その辺りのこと、なんか言ってた？」
findings.explanation: Tomo attends a junior college; the English calls it a vocational school.
findings.japanese:
「でも渚ってこっちの短大進んだよね？
早坂とは切れちゃったのかなぁ…
その辺りのこと、なんか言ってた？」
findings.todokanai: "But Nagisa got into a vocational school here, right? I wonder if she broke up with Hayasaka… At that time, did he say anything?"

findings.highlight: We talk excitedly about our relatives in a way no other group can imitate
findings.evidenceJa: 六年間も同じ場所で過ごした俺たちだからこそ、誰にも真似できない、身内の話で盛り上がる。
findings.explanation: 身内の話 here means in-group or insider talk available to friends who shared the same place for six years. The English makes them talk about their relatives, severing the sentence from the group's shared school history.
findings.japanese:
六年間も同じ場所で過ごした俺たちだからこそ、
誰にも真似できない、身内の話で盛り上がる。
findings.todokanai: We talk excitedly about our relatives in a way no other group can imitate, for the four of us have spent the past six years living in the same place.

findings.highlight: While I understand that they're drunk
findings.evidenceJa: 酒とつまみが心許ないからと言って、二人が外に買い出しに出かけてから３０分以上…
findings.explanation: Io and Takeya went shopping because their alcohol and snack supplies looked inadequate. The English reads 酒 as their being drunk, drops the snacks, and no longer explains why they went out.
findings.japanese:
酒とつまみが心許ないからと言って、
二人が外に買い出しに出かけてから３０分以上…
findings.todokanai: While I understand that they're drunk, it's been over 30 minutes since they went out to do some shopping…

findings.highlight: Or perhaps this is something they've set up…
findings.evidenceJa:
しかもそれは、
果たしてあいつらのことなんだろうかというのか…
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether the issue concerns Io and Takeya or himself and Setsuna; the English recasts it as something the friends arranged.
findings.japanese:
しかもそれは、
果たしてあいつらのことなんだろうかというのか…
findings.todokanai: Or perhaps this is something they've set up…

findings.highlight: one that's well-deserved for the two of them
findings.evidenceJa: あいつらに付け込まれるにふさわしい、とてつもない優しさに満ちていた。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's words are so extraordinarily kind that they are ripe for Io and Takeya to take advantage of. The English says the two friends deserve the kindness, reversing the exploitative dynamic Setsuna is forgiving.
findings.japanese:
あいつらに付け込まれるにふさわしい、
とてつもない優しさに満ちていた。
findings.todokanai: …Her words were filled with an unbelievable kindness, one that's well-deserved for the two of them.

findings.highlight: they just couldn't keep it to themselves anymore
findings.evidenceJa: けど、あそこまで“親友”になっちゃったから、もう引っ込みがつかなくなってるだけなんだ
findings.explanation: Takeya says Io has gone so far into the role of Setsuna's 'best friend' that she can no longer back out or change course. The English invents an inability to keep something secret, losing the explanation of why Io remains trapped in the relationship.
findings.japanese:
「けど、あそこまで“親友”になっちゃったから、
もう引っ込みがつかなくなってるだけなんだ」
findings.todokanai: "But they've come this far as 'good friends,' so maybe they just couldn't keep it to themselves anymore."

findings.highlight: No one made Setsuna-chan leave Haruki back thenーshe did it of her own volition.
findings.evidenceJa: 「あの時の春希から離れていかなかったのは、誰でもない、雪菜ちゃんの意志だったんだ」
findings.explanation: Takeya insists that it was Setsuna's own choice not to leave Haruki after the original crisis. The English says leaving him was her choice, reversing the defining decision on which his defense of her rests.
findings.japanese:
「あの時の春希から離れていかなかったのは、
誰でもない、雪菜ちゃんの意志だったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "No one made Setsuna-chan leave Haruki back thenーshe did it of her own volition."

findings.highlight: I was relieved by something
findings.evidenceJa: それでも彼女が、その瞬間何に安心したのか、それだけは、はっきり理解できたと思ってる。
findings.explanation: Haruki believes he understood exactly what Setsuna felt relieved about at that moment. The English makes Haruki himself the person who was relieved, reversing the emotional subject of his observation.
findings.japanese:
それでも彼女が、その瞬間何に安心したのか、
それだけは、はっきり理解できたと思ってる。
findings.todokanai: Even so, at that moment, the only thing that I think I clearly understood was that I was relieved by something.

findings.highlight: I'm making sure that I'm currently the same person
findings.evidenceJa: 今日の俺は、数日前の、パーティの時の俺と同じだって、そう、見極めたんだ。
findings.explanation: The continuing subject is Setsuna: she has assessed that today's Haruki is the same gentle Haruki she saw at the party. The English makes Haruki verify his own identity, erasing Setsuna's cautious test and the basis of her renewed approach.
findings.japanese:
今日の俺は、
数日前の、パーティの時の俺と同じだって、
そう、見極めたんだ。
findings.todokanai: I'm making sure that I'm currently the same person who attended Setsuna's birthday party just a few days ago.

findings.highlight: the number of courses we're taking haven't gone down at all
findings.evidenceJa: 「受ける講義も全然重ならなくなったし、顔合わせてる時間、だいぶ減っただろ？」
findings.explanation: Haruki says their classes no longer overlap at all, so they see much less of each other. The English says the number of courses has not decreased, confusing overlap with quantity and breaking the stated causal connection.
findings.japanese:
「受ける講義も全然重ならなくなったし、
顔合わせてる時間、だいぶ減っただろ？」
findings.todokanai: "Well, the number of courses we're taking haven't gone down at all, so the amount of time we've had to see each other has also lessened quite a lot, huh?"

findings.highlight: Only for today, the preparations for my move are all done.
findings.evidenceJa: 『今日までで、赴任の準備は全部終わった。あとは明日１３時発の飛行機で飛んでいくだけだ』
findings.explanation: Mari says all preparations for her posting were completed by today and that only tomorrow's 1 p.m. flight remains. The English's 'only for today' is not the temporal construction and obscures the countdown established by the message.
findings.japanese:
『今日までで、赴任の準備は全部終わった。
あとは明日１３時発の飛行機で飛んでいくだけだ』

findings.explanation: Haruki repeatedly sins, is repeatedly forgiven, cannot bear having been forgiven, and therefore sins again. The English assigns the unbearable burden to Setsuna, losing Haruki's self-destructive response to grace and the mechanism of the three-year cycle.

findings.evidenceJa: また俺、雪菜とセックスしてる
findings.explanation: Haruki's internal line bluntly and almost incredulously says, 'I'm having sex with Setsuna again.' 'Making love' prettifies the deliberately plain セックス and smooths away the boyish immediacy of his realization.
findings.japanese: また俺、雪菜とセックスしてる…
findings.todokanai: I'm once again making love to Setsuna…

findings.highlight: With my penis going in and out of her at its own leisure, Setsuna is left with a tearful expression, heaving out an even more tearful voice.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺の欲望の赴くままに激しく出し入れされ、
雪菜は泣きそうな表情で、泣きそうな声を振り絞る。
findings.explanation: Haruki thrusts her violently as his desire dictates; giving his penis movement 'at its own leisure' is odd agency and the opposite of urgency.
findings.japanese:
俺の欲望の赴くままに激しく出し入れされ、
雪菜は泣きそうな表情で、泣きそうな声を振り絞る。
findings.todokanai: With my penis going in and out of her at its own leisure, Setsuna is left with a tearful expression, heaving out an even more tearful voice.

findings.highlight: she will accept anything with both body and soul
findings.evidenceJa: もう、俺がどんなに激しくしても、心と身体の奥底から受け入れて
findings.explanation: Within this consensual act, Setsuna accepts Haruki from the depths of body and heart however intensely he moves. 'She will accept anything' generalizes that sexual trust into unlimited acceptance, materially widening its scope.
findings.japanese:
もう、俺がどんなに激しくしても、
心と身体の奥底から受け入れて、
それを大きくうねる快感として表現してくれる。
findings.todokanai: It doesn't matter how rough I am anymore, she will accept anything with both body and soul, turning it into pure pleasure.

findings.highlight: Setsuna's shameless confession
findings.evidenceJa: そんな雪菜の恥を忍んだ告白に
findings.explanation: Setsuna makes the confession despite or at the cost of her embarrassment. Calling it 'shameless' reverses the characterization from overcoming shame to lacking it.
findings.japanese:
そんな雪菜の恥を忍んだ告白に、
俺は、限界を突破することで応える。
findings.todokanai: In response to Setsuna's shameless confession, I surpass my own limit.

findings.highlight: puts me at my wits end
findings.evidenceJa: 今、果てたばかりの俺を、すぐにいたたまれなくさせる
findings.explanation: Setsuna's exhausted expression and breathing immediately make the just-climaxed Haruki unable to contain himself—overwhelmed by her cuteness and arousal again. 'At my wits' end' instead suggests frustration or desperation at her condition.
findings.japanese:
その表情も、その息遣いも、
今、果てたばかりの俺を、すぐにいたたまれなくさせる。
findings.todokanai: Her expression, her breathing… all of it puts me at my wits end, especially because I've just climaxed.

findings.highlight: Fourth-year Economics Department student
findings.evidenceJa: 峰城大学商学部四回生
findings.explanation: Tomo is a fourth-year student in Houjou University's Faculty of Commerce or business school, not an economics-department student.
findings.japanese:
柳原朋。
峰城大学商学部四回生。
findings.todokanai: Yanagihara Tomo. Fourth-year Economics Department student at Houjou University.

findings.highlight: the stuff we spent all day studying in university really is completely useless in the business world
findings.evidenceJa: 大学で勉強ばっかしてた奴らは結局会社じゃ役に立たないんだよ
findings.explanation: Takeya claims that people who did nothing but study in university end up useless in a company; his argument praises social experience over bookish students. The translation instead claims university subject matter itself is useless, changing the target of his provocation.
findings.japanese:
「だからな、大学で勉強ばっかしてた奴らは
結局会社じゃ役に立たないんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Anyway, the stuff we spent all day studying in university really is completely useless in the business world."

findings.highlight: you know he can't refute you
findings.evidenceJa: それ言われたら論破のしようがないじゃないか
findings.explanation: Io says Takeya's point is unfair because she has no way to refute it. The translation makes an unspecified male—most naturally Haruki—the person unable to answer him.
findings.japanese:
「卑怯だぞ武也…
それ言われたら論破のしようがないじゃないか」
findings.todokanai: "That's a low-blow, Takeya… you know he can't refute you when you say something like that."

findings.highlight: I just hated how you were back then more than anything else
findings.evidenceJa: その時その時の武也の性格が一番嫌いって言うか
findings.explanation: Cornered between disliking Takeya when he was flashy and disliking him now that he is lame, Io says whatever personality he has at any given moment is the one she hates most. The translation confines the dislike to his past self and loses the flirtatiously impossible standard.
findings.japanese:
「え？　あ、あぁ…ええと…
あたしは…その時その時の武也の性格が
一番嫌いって言うか…」
findings.todokanai: "Huh? A-Aah… ehm… you could say I just… I just hated how you were back then more than anything else, Takeya…"

findings.highlight: Setsuna managed to become the center of attention at her new company.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は会社でも、やっぱり看板背負ってる
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna already carries the company's signboard—she is a public face or representative asset in PR. 'Center of attention' reduces that professional representational burden to popularity.
findings.japanese:
「雪菜は会社でも、やっぱり看板背負ってる。
春希は最初から期待値が高くて、しかもそれに応えてる。
武也だって、大学時代からは信じられない高評価」
findings.todokanai: "Setsuna managed to become the center of attention at her new company. Haruki has always had high expectations placed on him, and he even manages to live up to them. Even Takeya has been doing unbelievably well since graduating."

findings.highlight: She wanted to work as a designer
findings.evidenceJa: 企画職を希望してたけど
findings.explanation: As in the preceding career summary, Io wanted planning or product-development work, not design. The repeated mistranslation obscures the exact career frustration motivating her confession.
findings.japanese:
企画職を希望してたけど、なかなか競争率が高いらしく、
今は人事部で事務仕事に忙殺される毎日だとか。
findings.todokanai: She wanted to work as a designer, but since it's too competitive, she's now busy working in the HR department.

findings.highlight: Who do you think you are?
findings.evidenceJa: 誰だよお前
findings.explanation: Takeya's 誰だよお前 means 'Who are you?'—this passive, complaining Io is unrecognizable to him. 'Who do you think you are?' instead makes him accuse her of arrogance, the opposite of his attempt to provoke her out of defeatism.
findings.japanese:
「自分から変えてやろうとかもしないくせに、
与えられたことに不満持ってぶちぶち…誰だよお前」
findings.todokanai: "You don't even try to make any changes yourself, yet you whine about everything handed to you… Who do you think you are?"

findings.highlight: You've really turned into a drunkard, Iizuka-san.
findings.evidenceJa: ほんっとおっさんくさくなったなぁ飯塚さん
findings.explanation: Tomo says Takeya has become thoroughly middle-aged-man-like, then completes the stock salaryman image with a necktie around his head. 'Drunkard' deletes the age/status stereotype that makes the second sentence land.
findings.japanese:
「…ほんっとおっさんくさくなったなぁ飯塚さん。
これでネクタイ頭に巻いてたら完璧」
findings.todokanai: "You've really turned into a drunkard, Iizuka-san. All you have to do now is tie a necktie around your head and you'll fit the bill perfectly."

findings.highlight: would never allow the players to get heated up any more
findings.evidenceJa: 厳格な審判は、決してピッチを上げることを許さず
findings.explanation: Haruki, the strict referee of their drinking match, refuses to let either contestant increase her drinking pace. The translation treats it as emotional escalation, missing the alcohol/competition mechanics.
findings.japanese:
厳格な審判は、決してピッチを上げることを許さず、
そして１時間にもわたる勝負の末…
findings.todokanai: This strict referee would never allow the players to get heated up any more. As a result, one hour into the match…

findings.highlight: Both players ended up being supported on the shoulders of the referee
findings.evidenceJa: 両者の腕が審判によって掲げられ
findings.explanation: The referee raises both contestants' arms, declaring the drinking match a draw. The translation has Haruki physically support them on his shoulders and misses the boxing-style result image.
findings.japanese:
結局、両者の腕が審判によって掲げられ、
そこで一次会はお開きになった。
findings.todokanai: …Both players ended up being supported on the shoulders of the referee, and the first party thus concluded.

findings.highlight: What's your vote?
findings.evidenceJa: そっちの二票はどうかなぁ？
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly asks how the two votes on Haruki and Io's side will go. The translation reduces them to one vote, which makes the supposed majority and Haruki's turn to Io less coherent.
findings.japanese:
「あのさぁ、
こっち多数決でカラオケって流れになってるんだけど、
そっちの二票はどうかなぁ？」
findings.todokanai: "We have a majority vote for karaoke so far. What's your vote?"

findings.highlight: She's my superior when it comes to things like that.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつ、俺のそっち方面の師匠でもあるんだから
findings.explanation: Haruki says Takeya is also his mentor in that department—romance, sex, and hotel choices. The translation calls the referent 'she,' obscuring that Haruki and Io chose the same hotel because both learned this sort of thing from Takeya.
findings.japanese:
「しょうがないだろ。
あいつ、俺のそっち方面の師匠でもあるんだから」
findings.todokanai: "There's nothing I can do about it. She's my superior when it comes to things like that."

findings.highlight: the estimated profit for a concert has jumped to twice the usual amount
findings.evidenceJa: 来日公演の提示額がいきなり倍に跳ね上がる
findings.explanation: The amount being offered for a Japanese performance has doubled. The translation turns a concrete offer made to Youko's office into an internally estimated profit, changing both the payer/payee relation and the certainty of the money.
findings.japanese:
「おかげで来日公演の提示額が
いきなり倍に跳ね上がるし…
今日本に行かないテはないのよ」
findings.todokanai: "Thanks to that, the estimated profit for a concert has jumped to twice the usual amount… There's just no way we can miss out on going to Japan right now."

findings.highlight: If I start looking for another route now, I might be late
findings.evidenceJa: 今から乗り継ぎだから、わたしの方が遅くなるかな
findings.explanation: Setsuna is waiting for the connecting bus and still has a transfer ahead of her, so she may arrive later. She is not searching for an alternate route.
findings.japanese:
「そっか…こっちは今、連絡バス待ち。
今から乗り継ぎだから、わたしの方が遅くなるかな…」
findings.todokanai: "Is that so… I'm still waiting for my bus. If I start looking for another route now, I might be late…"

findings.highlight: It's snowing really hard here in Paris.
findings.evidenceJa: パリがもう凄い雪でさ、今日中に着かないかと思ったよ
findings.explanation: Haruki has reached the station at his destination and says the snow in Paris was so severe he feared he would not arrive that day. 'Here in Paris' leaves him in the wrong city during the phone call.
findings.japanese:
「パリがもう凄い雪でさ、
今日中に着かないかと思ったよ」
findings.todokanai: "It's snowing really hard here in Paris. I didn't think I'd make it by today."

findings.highlight: The detailed information will be sent to you
findings.evidenceJa: 詳細はＰＣのメアドに添付ファイルで送ってある
findings.explanation: The attachment has already been sent to Haruki's computer email address, and he is instructed to read it carefully. The translation makes the delivery future and replaces the instruction with a summary statement.
findings.japanese:
『詳細はＰＣのメアドに添付ファイルで送ってあるから、
そっちをしっかり見ておくように。
とりあえずこちらは概要だけ』
findings.todokanai: "The detailed information will be sent to you in an attached file via email. I just want to summarize the most important points."

findings.highlight: what interaction will take place
findings.evidenceJa: どんな接点があったとしても
findings.explanation: Haruki resolves that whatever connection may already exist between pianist Kazusa and Kaiousha's Kitahara Haruki must not matter professionally. The future wording erases the dangerous shared past he is trying to bracket.
findings.japanese:
ピアニスト冬馬かずさと、開桜社北原春希の間に
どんな接点があったとしても…
findings.todokanai: No matter what interaction will take place between the pianist Touma Kazusa and Kitahara Haruki of Kaiousha…

findings.highlight: play the piano with such emotion
findings.evidenceJa: あんな色ボケたピアノが弾ける
findings.explanation: Youko marvels that her ascetic daughter can play such a lovesick or erotically infatuated piano. Generic 'emotion' sanitizes the pointed contradiction between Kazusa's outward severity and the desire exposed in her playing.
findings.japanese:
「ほんと、我が娘ながらストイックなコ…
それでよくもまぁあんな色ボケたピアノが弾けるわね」
findings.todokanai: "Oh dear, my daughter is a stoic… I'm amazed you can play the piano with such emotion when this is what you're like."

findings.highlight: the back of her feet
findings.evidenceJa: 足の裏や指の間まで念入りにぬぐう
findings.explanation: Haruki carefully wipes the soles of Kazusa's feet and between her toes. 足の裏 is the sole, not the top or back of the foot.
findings.japanese:
傷の回りの汚れを落とし、
それから足の裏や指の間まで念入りにぬぐう。
findings.todokanai: After cleaning away the dirt around her wound, I wipe the back of her feet and between her toes.

findings.highlight: bruised and scratched at the same time
findings.evidenceJa: 擦り傷と打ち身としもやけを一気にこさえる
findings.explanation: Haruki lists three simultaneous injuries: an abrasion, a bruise, and chilblains. The translation omits the cold injury, even though the following extended treatment is specifically about restoring warmth and circulation.
findings.japanese:
「擦り傷と打ち身としもやけを一気にこさえるからだ。
ほら、足こっち向けて。
しみると思うけど我慢しろよ」
findings.todokanai: "Only because you got yourself bruised and scratched at the same time. Come on, hold your leg out. This might sting a bit, but try to bear it."

findings.highlight: Once Kazusa finally calms down, I grab her foot and clean the wounded area with cotton containing disinfectant.
findings.evidenceJa:
ふてくされたようにやっと黙ったかずさの足を取り、
脱脂綿に含めた消毒薬を、
かかとの傷口につける。
findings.explanation: Kazusa has begun sulking after the alcohol stings; 'she's calmed down' reverses the emotional coloring.
findings.japanese:
ふてくされたようにやっと黙ったかずさの足を取り、
脱脂綿に含めた消毒薬を、
かかとの傷口につける。
findings.todokanai: Once Kazusa finally calms down, I grab her foot and clean the wounded area with cotton containing disinfectant.

findings.highlight: The courage to finally face the lingering feeling from my past.
findings.evidenceJa:
過去からの因縁に連なる思い出の魔女に、
最後の戦いを挑む勇気を。
findings.explanation: The memory-witch bound to fate from the past becomes an abstract lingering feeling, dropping Haruki's fantasy-adventure metaphor.
findings.japanese:
過去からの因縁に連なる思い出の魔女に、
最後の戦いを挑む勇気を。
findings.todokanai: The courage to finally face the lingering feeling from my past.

findings.highlight: I'm sure it won't be what Kazusa wants to hear
findings.evidenceJa: 何を答えても、それは多分かずさの聞きたかったことであり
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that whatever of the two possible questions he answers, it probably is something Kazusa wanted to ask—and also something he did not want to discuss. The translation negates the first proposition and substitutes 'want to hear' for 'wanted to ask.'
findings.japanese:
けど、何を答えても、それは多分
かずさの聞きたかったことであり…
findings.todokanai: But no matter what I answer, I'm sure it won't be what Kazusa wants to hear…

findings.highlight: I'm sure that this "a lot" includes Kazusa herself
findings.evidenceJa: かずさ自身は登場していたんだろうか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether Kazusa herself appeared in the 'various things' she imagined behind his delayed relationship with Setsuna. The English asserts certainty where the Japanese sustains his uncertainty about her self-awareness.
findings.japanese:
その時、かずさが思い浮かべた『色々』に、
かずさ自身は登場していたんだろうか。
findings.todokanai: I'm sure that this "a lot" includes Kazusa herself in Kazusa's mind.

findings.highlight: She's even forgiven all that you've… All that I've done…
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に、本当にいいコだもんな、雪菜
findings.explanation: Kazusa only says that Setsuna is a truly, truly good girl. The English adds a complete self-correcting confession about what Haruki and Kazusa did, making implicit guilt explicit dialogue.
findings.japanese: 「本当に、本当にいいコだもんな、雪菜」
findings.todokanai: "Setsuna is a really, really good girl, after all. She's even forgiven all that you've… All that I've done…"

findings.highlight: And she won't run away… like I did…
findings.evidenceJa: 可愛くて、優しくて、心が綺麗で、一途で…
findings.explanation: Kazusa praises Setsuna as cute, kind, pure-hearted, and devoted, then trails off. The translation writes a new explicit comparison to Kazusa running away, again converting subtext into authored confession.
findings.japanese:
「世界中探しても、あんな素敵な恋人はいないぞ。
可愛くて、優しくて、心が綺麗で、一途で…」
findings.todokanai: "You couldn't find a better lover than her if you searched the whole world. She's adorable, kind, pure-hearted, and devoted… And she won't run away… like I did…"

findings.highlight: a languid feeling of uncertainty
findings.evidenceJa: 気怠い無常感みたいなのがじわじわと全身を覆う
findings.explanation: 無常感 here is a languid sense of impermanence, futility, or transience as the meeting ends, not uncertainty about what will happen. The mistranslation weakens the scene's terminal emotional atmosphere.
findings.japanese:
ただ、さっきのかずさの態度と同じように、
気怠い無常感みたいなのがじわじわと全身を覆う。
findings.todokanai: Instead, just like in Kazusa's case a short while ago, a languid feeling of uncertainty slowly permeates my body.

findings.highlight: My uncertainty flies away in an instant
findings.evidenceJa: 無常感は一瞬で吹き飛び
findings.explanation: This explicitly recalls the preceding sense of impermanence, which vanishes when Haruki learns there will be a tomorrow. Repeating 'uncertainty' breaks that emotional callback.
findings.japanese:
無常感は一瞬で吹き飛び、
様々な思いが頭の中をかき回すように飛び交った。
findings.todokanai: My uncertainty flies away in an instant, and various thoughts float around in my head.

findings.highlight: served to increase my persuasiveness
findings.evidenceJa: 俺のこの態度に、説得力を持たせてしまっていた
findings.explanation: The obvious wrong Haruki did Setsuna makes his excessive apologetic behavior look convincingly explained, thereby camouflaging the deeper betrayal. He is not becoming more persuasive in an argument.
findings.japanese:
雪菜にそんなに酷いことをしてしまった事実が、
俺のこの態度に、説得力を持たせてしまっていた。
findings.todokanai: The fact that I've done something so horrible to Setsuna only served to increase my persuasiveness.

findings.highlight: I'd consider her declaration a bit selfish
findings.evidenceJa: いつもなら、もう少しワガママを言ったかもしれない
findings.explanation: Haruki observes that under ordinary circumstances Setsuna herself might have made a slightly more selfish demand. The translation instead has Haruki judge her present, conspicuously considerate words as selfish.
findings.japanese: いつもなら、もう少しワガママを言ったかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: Normally, I'd consider her declaration a bit selfish.

findings.highlight: a parent who can cheer you up just by being around you
findings.evidenceJa: 一緒にいてもいいって気にさせてくれる親なんだぞ
findings.explanation: Haruki says Youko is a parent who makes Kazusa feel that it is all right for them to be together. 'Cheer you up just by being around' replaces the hard-won permission for continued family intimacy with a generic mood benefit.
findings.japanese:
「それでも一緒にいること、お前全然嫌がってないだろ。
一緒にいてもいいって気にさせてくれる親なんだぞ？
お前、その価値全然認めないつもりか？」
findings.todokanai: "Yet you don't mind being with her at all, do you? She's a parent who can cheer you up just by being around you. You don't plan on recognizing the value in that?"

findings.highlight: as if attempting to persuade her
findings.evidenceJa: まるで口説いているかのようにかずさをカメラのレンズ越しに視姦してる
findings.explanation: The photographer is talking as though trying to seduce Kazusa while visually undressing or violating her through the lens. 'Persuade' strips the explicitly sexual register from both 口説く and 視姦.
findings.japanese:
そして今は、こちらも３０分遅れて到着した
現地のカメラマンが、まるで口説いているかのように
かずさをカメラのレンズ越しに視姦してる。
findings.todokanai: And now the cameraman, who himself arrived 30 minutes late, is ogling at Kazusa through the camera lens, as if attempting to persuade her.

findings.highlight: it seems you rejected her
findings.evidenceJa: わたしのコンサートチケット送ったのに、結局、ふられちゃったわね
findings.explanation: Youko says that although she sent Haruki a ticket to her concert, he ultimately stood her up; his was the sole empty front-row seat. 'Rejected her' falsely points the action toward Kazusa and obscures Youko's own invitation.
findings.japanese:
「だからわたしのコンサートチケット送ったのに、
結局、ふられちゃったわね。
…最前列で空いてたのはあなたの席だけだったわよ」
findings.todokanai: "That's why I sent you a concert ticket, but in the end, it seems you rejected her… After all, your seat was the only one that was empty in the front row."

findings.highlight: win time after time in famous competitions
findings.evidenceJa: 世界中の権威あるコンクールを勝ち抜く腕
findings.explanation: Kazusa has acquired the skill to fight her way through prestigious competitions worldwide, not a record of repeatedly winning them. The overstatement conflicts with her much-discussed fourth-place finish.
findings.japanese:
だから、五年間頑張ってきたかずさは、
世界中の権威あるコンクールを勝ち抜く腕と、
強い意志を手に入れた。
findings.todokanai: That's why Kazusa's been able to win time after time in famous competitions after working so hard for five years. She's gained a strong will.

findings.highlight: She had the talent from the start.
findings.evidenceJa: 富は、もともとあった
findings.explanation: Kazusa originally had wealth; she later acquired fame herself. Translating 富 as talent erases the wealth/fame pair and repeats an artistic endowment already established elsewhere.
findings.japanese:
富は、もともとあった。
名声は、自分で手に入れた。
findings.todokanai: She had the talent from the start. She gained renown with her own hands.

findings.highlight: No matter what happens… and no matter what the reason…
findings.evidenceJa: だからどうだって訳でも…どうしようって訳でも、ないんだけど
findings.explanation: Haruki tells himself that their final separation does not mean anything in particular and that he does not intend to do anything about it. The English does not express either proposition and is incoherent with the sentence fragment that follows.
findings.japanese:
だからどうだって訳でも…
どうしようって訳でも、ないんだけど…
findings.todokanai: No matter what happens… and no matter what the reason…

findings.highlight: Kazusa's outstretched right foot
findings.evidenceJa: かずさが軽く右足を引きずってみせた
findings.explanation: Kazusa demonstrates by lightly dragging or limping on her injured right foot. She does not merely stretch it out; the visible limp is what reminds Haruki why she cannot use the piano pedal.
findings.japanese:
かずさが軽く右足を引きずってみせたのと同時に、
何もかも吹っ飛んでた記憶が一気に蘇る。
findings.todokanai: At the sight of Kazusa's outstretched right foot, all the memories that had left me return in an instant.

findings.highlight: who couldn't even choose her in the end
findings.evidenceJa: 結果としてしか雪菜を選べなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki condemns himself because he could choose Setsuna only as the eventual result—after remaining with Kazusa until time forced his return. The English says he did not choose Setsuna even in the end, reversing the tortured distinction on which his self-indictment rests.
findings.japanese:
結果としてしか雪菜を選べなかった、
こんな、最低な…
findings.todokanai: This horrible person, who couldn't even choose her in the end…

findings.highlight: …I hate my outstanding ex-superior who set up this kind of culture.
findings.evidenceJa: …優秀な元上司が作り上げたこの文化が恨めしい。
findings.explanation: Haruki resents the workplace culture established by his excellent former superior, while the English directly says he hates the former superior.
findings.japanese: …優秀な元上司が作り上げたこの文化が恨めしい。
findings.todokanai: …I hate my outstanding ex-superior who set up this kind of culture.

findings.highlight: spent the whole night making love to Setsuna
findings.evidenceJa: 一晩中、雪菜と抱き合ったまま眠らずに
findings.explanation: Haruki stayed awake all night holding Setsuna in his arms. 抱き合ったまま means they remained in an embrace; it does not state that they had sex. 'Making love' invents a sexual act at a psychologically precise point in his accounting of sleepless nights.
findings.japanese:
そして、そのさらに前日は、
一晩中、雪菜と抱き合ったまま眠らずに…
findings.todokanai: And the day before that I spent the whole night making love to Setsuna, so I couldn't sleep then either…

findings.highlight: "Yeah, we can call it a celebration of your hard work. You even helped him out during this trip, so Kizaki-san's paying."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ほら、北原のお疲れ会ってことで。
今回の出張の事情のこともあるし、
全部木崎さん持ちで」
findings.explanation: Kizaki pays because of the circumstances surrounding this assignment; 'you even helped him out during this trip' invents a favor Haruki did Kizaki.
findings.japanese:
「ほら、北原のお疲れ会ってことで。
今回の出張の事情のこともあるし、
全部木崎さん持ちで」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, we can call it a celebration of your hard work. You even helped him out during this trip, so Kizaki-san's paying."

findings.highlight: If they make me tell them about back then with alcohol involved, the regrets I've shut in the recesses of my mind will reappear.
findings.evidenceJa:
酒が入って、しかもあの時のことを語らされたら、
せっかく記憶の底に押し込めた後ろめたさが、
また蘇ってきてしまうから。
findings.explanation: 後ろめたさ is guilt, not regret; Haruki fears alcohol will revive his guilty conscience over choosing Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
酒が入って、しかもあの時のことを語らされたら、
せっかく記憶の底に押し込めた後ろめたさが、
また蘇ってきてしまうから。
findings.todokanai: If they make me tell them about back then with alcohol involved, the regrets I've shut in the recesses of my mind will reappear.

findings.highlight: neither a guardian angel nor a demon
findings.evidenceJa: 救いの神でも、地獄の仏でもなかった
findings.explanation: Both Japanese images are rescuers: a saving god and the proverbial Buddha encountered in hell. Hamada is neither kind of salvation from the drinking party. Turning the second into a demon changes the sentence to 'neither good nor evil' and loses the joke that Haruki has not been rescued at all.
findings.japanese:
そこに現れたのは、
どうやら救いの神でも、地獄の仏でもなかった。
findings.todokanai: The person who appeared was neither a guardian angel nor a demon.

findings.highlight: our big moment on the stage back in high school
findings.evidenceJa: 部活仲間の晴れ舞台に
findings.explanation: Setsuna is excited about the present grand stage awaiting her former clubmate Kazusa. The translation moves the stage back to the trio's own high-school performance, changing both whose stage it is and when it occurs.
findings.japanese:
同級生の華々しい活躍に。
部活仲間の晴れ舞台に。
findings.todokanai: Talking about how amazing her classmate was, and about our big moment on the stage back in high school.

findings.highlight: How many times do you have to tell me that
findings.evidenceJa: さっきから何度確かめれば気が済むんだよ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks how many times Takeya and Io need to check or confirm his promise before they are satisfied. The English makes them the ones repeatedly telling Haruki the answer, reversing the question's direction.
findings.japanese:
「さっきから何度確かめれば気が済むんだよ…
行く予定なんかないって言ってるだろ」
findings.todokanai: "How many times do you have to tell me that…? I've already told you I have no intention of going."

findings.highlight: a certain famous idol that came before her
findings.evidenceJa: かつて一世を風靡したアーティストのように
findings.explanation: Kazusa is being treated almost exactly like the artist who once swept the age—her mother Youko. Calling that comparator a 'certain famous idol' changes Youko's profession and obscures the mother-daughter media-cycle parallel.
findings.japanese:
そんな、かつて一世を風靡したアーティストのように…
というか、ほぼそのままの扱いをされていた。
findings.todokanai: Just like a certain famous idol that came before her… In fact, people are already looking at her with the same eyes.

findings.highlight: Like how they didn't want to let the popularity from their success in the Giovanni International Competition escape them, or like how they were pressured by some big advertising corporation.
findings.evidenceJa:
ジェバンニ国際コンクール入賞という旬を逃さないよう、
大手広告代理店が強引に押し込んだとか。
findings.explanation: The speculation is that a major ad agency forcibly crammed the Japan performance into the schedule to exploit the prize's timeliness; the English vaguely says they were pressured by a corporation.
findings.japanese:
ジェバンニ国際コンクール入賞という旬を逃さないよう、
大手広告代理店が強引に押し込んだとか。
findings.todokanai: Like how they didn't want to let the popularity from their success in the Giovanni International Competition escape them, or like how they were pressured by some big advertising corporation.

findings.highlight: Normally, it'd be rude to be imposing on them for the whole day
findings.evidenceJa: 一日は一応そこで失礼するけれど、二日の早朝には、すぐに雪菜が俺の部屋に来て
findings.explanation: Haruki plans to take his leave from the Ogiso home on January 1, after which Setsuna will come to his room early on January 2. The translation invents a general etiquette judgment and fails to state the actual first-day departure.
findings.japanese:
一日は一応そこで失礼するけれど、
二日の早朝には、すぐに雪菜が俺の部屋に来て。
findings.todokanai: Normally, it'd be rude to be imposing on them for the whole day, but in the morning of the second day, Setsuna will come over to my place again.

findings.highlight: Setsuna peers at me thoughtlessly
findings.evidenceJa: 気づかわしげに俺の顔を覗き込む
findings.explanation: Setsuna peers into Haruki's face with concern or solicitude. 'Thoughtlessly' states the opposite attitude at the moment she cautiously asks whether he wants to see Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
いつの間にか神妙な態度に戻っていた雪菜が、
気づかわしげに俺の顔を覗き込む。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna peers at me thoughtlessly, now that she has finally regained her calm demeanor.

findings.highlight: hardly a satisfactory answer
findings.evidenceJa: 全然答えになっていない答えだった
findings.explanation: Haruki calls his promise an answer that is not an answer at all: it evades Setsuna's request that he remain himself. 'Hardly satisfactory' makes it sound like a merely weak answer rather than a deliberate non-answer both recognize.
findings.japanese:
それは、全然答えになっていない答えだった。
お互い、そんなことはわかってた。
findings.todokanai: It was hardly a satisfactory answer. We both know that.

findings.highlight: the final nail in the coffin for the sin I've committed
findings.evidenceJa: 何よりの俺の罪にして、十字架だった
findings.explanation: Keeping the reunion secret is above all Haruki's sin and his cross to bear. The translation replaces the paired Christian confession images with a 'final nail in the coffin,' which denotes conclusive ruin rather than an enduring burden.
findings.japanese:
その事実を今まで雪菜に黙っていたことが、
何よりの俺の罪にして、十字架だった。
findings.todokanai: The fact that I've hid this from Setsuna all this time is the final nail in the coffin for the sin I've committed.

findings.highlight: The three of us could've met up together. We could've talked all night
findings.evidenceJa: 三人で会いたかったのに。夜通し思い出を語り合いたかったのに
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly says she wanted the three of them to meet and wanted to reminisce all night. The English recasts her painful, frustrated desire as a neutral statement of what could have happened.
findings.japanese:
「三人で会いたかったのに。
夜通し思い出を語り合いたかったのに」
findings.todokanai: "The three of us could've met up together. We could've talked all night about our memories…"

findings.highlight: "No, perhaps… I thought so myself too."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ううん、そもそも…
わたしだって、本当にそう思ってたのかな？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether even she truly wanted the imagined reunion; 'perhaps I thought so myself too' tilts the uncertainty toward affirmation.
findings.japanese:
「ううん、そもそも…
わたしだって、本当にそう思ってたのかな？」
findings.todokanai: "No, perhaps… I thought so myself too."

findings.highlight: "I got my license during university… though it's only a certification."
findings.evidenceJa:
「免許なら大学の時取りましたけど…
でも、ペーパーですよ？」
findings.explanation: ペーパードライバー means Haruki has a license but no real driving practice; 'it's only a certification' is not idiomatic English and does not convey that fact.
findings.japanese:
「免許なら大学の時取りましたけど…
でも、ペーパーですよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I got my license during university… though it's only a certification."

findings.highlight: "Well, things like that happen, and I actually owed one of their guys a favor."
findings.evidenceJa:
「まぁそのこともあって、
向こうさんにも恩返しの必要があってな」
findings.explanation: Hamada says their editorial side owes Ensemble a favor for yielding the scoop; the English makes it Hamada's personal debt to an unspecified individual.
findings.japanese:
「まぁそのこともあって、
向こうさんにも恩返しの必要があってな」
findings.todokanai: "Well, things like that happen, and I actually owed one of their guys a favor."

findings.highlight: I uncomfortably wonder whether my blunt rejection didn't come across as all too unnatural
findings.evidenceJa: そんないやらしい計算をしながら
findings.explanation: Haruki deliberately calculates whether the others noticed how obstinately and unnaturally he refused the Touma assignment. The translation retains discomfort and suspicion but deletes his admission that he is making a self-serving calculation.
findings.japanese:
実は頑なに拒絶していたことを、
不自然に思われなかったかなって…
そんないやらしい計算をしながら。
findings.todokanai: And I uncomfortably wonder whether my blunt rejection didn't come across as all too unnatural.

findings.highlight: has been unsuitable for living in for over three years
findings.evidenceJa: 三年ほど前から、人の住む場所じゃなくなっていた
findings.explanation: The old Touma residence has ceased to be anyone's home and has stood unoccupied for about three years. The translation asserts that the building became physically unsuitable for habitation.
findings.japanese:
やっと辿り着いた場所は…
もう三年ほど前から、人の住む場所じゃなくなっていた。
findings.todokanai: And the place I reach… is a place that has been unsuitable for living in for over three years.

findings.highlight: I don't get it at all
findings.evidenceJa: 本当、ついてない
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls herself truly unlucky for fleeing one unwanted meeting only to encounter Haruki at the ruined house. The translation changes bad luck into incomprehension.
findings.japanese:
「そしたら、こんな…
本当、ついてない」
findings.todokanai: "And yet, when I came here… I don't get it at all."

findings.highlight: the memories left by the three of us are long gone
findings.evidenceJa: 三人の思い出を残すものはもう跡形もなくなってて
findings.explanation: What has vanished are the physical traces and objects that preserve the three friends' memories, not the memories themselves; both characters are vividly remembering them in this scene.
findings.japanese:
けれどそこに、三人の思い出を残すものは
もう跡形もなくなってて…
findings.todokanai: But the memories left by the three of us are long gone, without any trace being left behind…

findings.highlight: "There are Japanese artists working harder than me overseas, yet no one even bats an eye at them…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「向こうであたしより活躍してる
日本人のアーティストなんてごまんといる。
なのに、その人たちには目も向けないで…」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says many Japanese artists are more active or successful than she is overseas; 'working harder than me' changes professional achievement into moralized effort.
findings.japanese:
「向こうであたしより活躍してる
日本人のアーティストなんてごまんといる。
なのに、その人たちには目も向けないで…」
findings.todokanai: "There are Japanese artists working harder than me overseas, yet no one even bats an eye at them…"

findings.highlight: She did take offense in the end
findings.evidenceJa: 結局、買ってしまったけど
findings.explanation: Continuing the stock pairing of selling and buying words, Haruki says he ultimately took Kazusa's bait and answered her provocation. The translation assigns the reaction to Kazusa instead.
findings.japanese: …結局、買ってしまったけど。
findings.todokanai: …She did take offense in the end.

findings.highlight: What an awful celebrity you are. Or perhaps that kind of attitude is par for the course in the celebrity world?
findings.evidenceJa: 最低の芸人だな。あ、それとも芸術家ならそういうのＯＫなんだっけ
findings.explanation: Haruki needles Kazusa by contrasting geinin, an entertainer, with geijutsuka, an artist: perhaps ignoring fans is unacceptable for the former but permitted for the latter. The translation calls both roles celebrities and erases the distinction driving the jab.
findings.japanese:
「ファンの声は無視かよ…最低の芸人だな。
あ、それとも芸術家ならそういうのＯＫなんだっけ？」
findings.todokanai: "You're going to ignore the voices of your fans? What an awful celebrity you are. Or perhaps that kind of attitude is par for the course in the celebrity world?"

findings.highlight: You haven't changed at all
findings.explanation: Kazusa makes only a choked, nonverbal reaction after Haruki's apology. The translation invents an explicit judgment that he has not changed.
findings.todokanai: "You haven't changed at all."

findings.highlight: we may never find out
findings.evidenceJa: 結論が出てないのかもしれない
findings.explanation: Haruki says they may not yet have reached a conclusion about whether these concerns are truly unnecessary. The translation adds permanent unknowability.
findings.japanese:
…余計なことなのかどうかは
結論が出てないのかもしれないけど。
findings.todokanai: …Though whether those things truly are unnecessary or not, we may never find out.

findings.highlight: I haven't met any of my friends from work since New Year's yet
findings.evidenceJa: 年明けてまだ誰も友達に会えてない
findings.explanation: Setsuna says work has been so busy since New Year that she has not seen any of her friends. The translation invents that the friends are coworkers.
findings.japanese:
「仕事は順調。
…順調すぎて、年明けてまだ誰も友達に会えてない」
findings.todokanai: "Work is going well… Too well, because I haven't met any of my friends from work since New Year's yet."

findings.highlight: the work bag laid on my bed
findings.evidenceJa: 床の上に置かれた通勤鞄
findings.explanation: Haruki looks at the work bag placed on the floor, specifically at the magazine inside it. The translation relocates the bag to his bed.
findings.japanese:
俺の視線が、床の上に置かれた通勤鞄に向けられる。
正確には、その中に収められた…
findings.todokanai: My eyes dart toward the work bag laid on my bed. Specifically, my eyes dart toward the contents of the bag…

findings.highlight: I would still have been able to make a cowardly excuse to get out of trouble, such as "I wasn't allowed to tell you."
findings.evidenceJa: 俺にはまだ、卑怯者から逃れるチャンスはあった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even after failing to tell Setsuna before the interview, he still had later opportunities to escape being a coward by confessing. The translation turns that moral opportunity into an opportunity to remain cowardly by fabricating an excuse.
findings.japanese:
それに、あの時話せなかったからと言って、
俺にはまだ、卑怯者から逃れるチャンスはあった。
findings.todokanai: Moreover, I would still have been able to make a cowardly excuse to get out of trouble, such as "I wasn't allowed to tell you."

findings.highlight: "…That's the reason it took so much effort to make him look at me again. That's the reason it was so hard for him to overcome the past."
findings.evidenceJa:
「…そのせいでもう一度振り向かせるのに苦労したけどね。
昔のこと乗り越えるの、大変だったけどね」
findings.explanation: Setsuna describes her own difficulty in making Haruki turn back toward her and overcoming their past; the English assigns the second struggle solely to Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「…そのせいでもう一度振り向かせるのに苦労したけどね。
昔のこと乗り越えるの、大変だったけどね」
findings.todokanai: "…That's the reason it took so much effort to make him look at me again. That's the reason it was so hard for him to overcome the past."

findings.highlight: "Though, I wouldn't put it past him to cheat on you in secret."
findings.evidenceJa: 「まぁ、隠れて浮気くらいならアリかもしんないけど」
findings.explanation: Tomo says a secret affair might at least be possible or conceivable; 'I wouldn't put it past him' instead characterizes Haruki as the sort of man expected to cheat.
findings.japanese: 「まぁ、隠れて浮気くらいならアリかもしんないけど」
findings.todokanai: "Though, I wouldn't put it past him to cheat on you in secret."

findings.highlight: My friend from five years ago has returned
findings.evidenceJa: 親友が五年ぶりに帰国してきた
findings.explanation: Setsuna calls Kazusa her best friend, who has returned to Japan after five years. The translation instead calls her a friend from five years ago, weakening the relationship into a past association.
findings.japanese:
「親友が五年ぶりに帰国してきたっていうのに、
連絡も取ろうとしない。素直に喜べない。
そんな、嫌な女の子ですよ～だ」
findings.todokanai: "My friend from five years ago has returned, and I haven't even tried to contact her. I can't even feel happy about her return. I'm that kind of an unpleasant girl."

findings.highlight: end up giving Kazusa unpleasant memories
findings.evidenceJa: かずさにだって…もしかしたら嫌な思いさせてるかも
findings.explanation: Setsuna fears that her current avoidance and jealousy may also be causing Kazusa painful feelings. The translation turns the ongoing emotional harm into the creation of unpleasant memories.
findings.japanese:
「やだもう、自己嫌悪…
こんなことじゃ、余計に春希くんに愛想尽かされる。
かずさにだって…もしかしたら嫌な思いさせてるかも」
findings.todokanai: "Oh jeez, I'm self-loathing now… Haruki-kun will just get sick of me like this. I might even… end up giving Kazusa unpleasant memories."

findings.highlight: she's been kicked from the band
findings.evidenceJa: もめた末に結局飛び出しちゃって
findings.explanation: After conflict over dating both the drummer and bassist, the singer ultimately stormed out or left the band herself. The translation says the band expelled her.
findings.japanese:
「ところがその子がとんでもないタマで…
ドラムとベースを二股かけちゃって、
もめた末に結局飛び出しちゃってさぁ」
findings.todokanai: "But the girl was absolutely unbelievable… She two-timed both the drummer and the bassist, so she's been kicked from the band."

findings.highlight: I have no room to hesitate right now
findings.evidenceJa: 今回の申し出ばかりは躊躇せざるを得ない
findings.explanation: Whatever pressure Hamada applies, Haruki cannot help hesitating over this particular offer. The translation says he has no room to hesitate, reversing compelled hesitation into compelled action.
findings.japanese:
けど、押されようが引かれようが、
今の俺にとって今回の申し出ばかりは躊躇せざるを得ない。
findings.todokanai: But whether he plans on forcing me or luring me into this job, I have no room to hesitate right now.

findings.highlight: The first issue of this year was better than any issues we had last year
findings.evidenceJa: 今年一発目で去年のどの号よりも出た
findings.explanation: Hamada says the first issue of the year sold more copies than every issue released the previous year. The translation turns an objective circulation result into a vague claim of qualitative superiority.
findings.japanese:
「先週出た最新号のインタビュー記事が評判良くてな。
何しろ今年一発目で去年のどの号よりも出たんだよ。
…ほら、社長賞の金一封だ」
findings.todokanai: "The interview article on last week's issue received an amazing response. The first issue of this year was better than any issues we had last year… Here, it's the reward money from our president."

findings.highlight: it contains Hamada-san's own pocket change
findings.evidenceJa: 浜田さんのポケットマネーなんじゃ
findings.explanation: Haruki jokes that the suspiciously informal president's award may actually have been funded from Hamada's personal money. The translation instead says the envelope contains a trivial amount of loose change.
findings.japanese: …実は浜田さんのポケットマネーなんじゃ？
findings.todokanai: …I imagine that it contains Hamada-san's own pocket change.

findings.highlight: I'm pretty sure she did
findings.evidenceJa: 本人の希望じゃないのか？
findings.explanation: Hamada asks whether it might be Kazusa's own request and why Haruki believes otherwise. The translation hardens his uninformed question into near-certainty, despite the parallel scene showing Kazusa had not been consulted.
findings.japanese:
「いや、本人の希望じゃないのか？
どうして違うなんて思うんだ？」
findings.todokanai: "No, I'm pretty sure she did. Why do you think otherwise?"

findings.highlight: she said something rude during the interview
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女に何か失礼なことでもしたのか
findings.explanation: Hamada asks whether Haruki did something rude or offensive to Kazusa during the interview. The translation reverses the direction and asks whether Kazusa said something rude.
findings.japanese:
「そういえば、この前の出迎えも嫌がってたな。
ひょっとしてインタビューの時、
彼女に何か失礼なことでもしたのか？」
findings.todokanai: "By the way, you were against picking her up before too. Could it be that she said something rude during the interview?"

findings.highlight: your piano is getting more clumsy
findings.evidenceJa: ピアノも荒れてる
findings.explanation: Youko says Kazusa's playing has become rough, unsettled, or emotionally wild because of her instability. The translation describes the piano itself or her technique as increasingly clumsy.
findings.japanese:
「そのせいでピアノも荒れてる。
正直、今のままの状態じゃコンサートも心許ないわね」
findings.todokanai: "Thanks to that, your piano is getting more clumsy. To be honest, I feel a bit uneasy about holding a concert at this rate."

findings.highlight: if you mess up even slightly
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっとでも腑抜けた演奏したら
findings.explanation: Youko warns that even a slightly spiritless, gutless performance will make the press turn on Kazusa after such hype. The translation changes the artistic failure into any minor technical mistake.
findings.japanese:
「前評判が高い分、ちょっとでも腑抜けた演奏したら、
あっという間に手のひらを返されるわよ？
…あなたの大嫌いなマスコミに」
findings.todokanai: "The interest in your concert is high, so if you mess up even slightly, everything will be turned on its head… by the mass media you hate so much."

findings.highlight: A lot of work in the afternoon?
findings.evidenceJa: どこ行くんだ？午後いっぱいって、何時くらいまで
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks where Youko is going and what time 'the whole afternoon' means. The destination and purpose are unstated; the translation invents that Youko has work.
findings.japanese:
「どこ行くんだ？
午後いっぱいって、何時くらいまで…」
findings.todokanai: "Where are you going? A lot of work in the afternoon? Until when…?"

findings.highlight: your third appearance in Studio Troy
findings.evidenceJa: 三丁目のスタジオトロイ
findings.explanation: The source locates Studio Troy in the third chome. The translation turns that address element into Setsuna's third appearance at the venue.
findings.japanese:
「三丁目のスタジオトロイで。
来週末にライブなんでしょ？」
findings.todokanai: "I'm talking about your third appearance in Studio Troy. You're having a live concert next weekend, aren't you?"

findings.highlight: her true calling is in expressing her feelings
findings.evidenceJa: 基本は感性で生きてる
findings.explanation: The speaker says Setsuna fundamentally lives by intuition or sensibility despite seeming intellectual. The translation changes this way of moving through life into a vocational calling to express feelings.
findings.japanese:
「あれだよね、小木曽ちゃんって
峰城出ててインテリっぽいけど、
基本は感性で生きてるよね」
findings.todokanai: "I know what this is. Ogiso-chan's looked like an intellectual ever since she left Houjou, but her true calling is in expressing her feelings."

findings.highlight: I don't have feelings for them
findings.evidenceJa: あなたと違って割り切れるからね
findings.explanation: Youko says she can compartmentalize or keep the relationship cleanly separated, unlike Kazusa. The translation instead denies that she has feelings at all, changing the distinction she draws between feeling and conduct.
findings.japanese: 「あなたと違って割り切れるからね」
findings.todokanai: "Unlike you, I don't have feelings for them."

findings.highlight: Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine
findings.evidenceJa: 東邦出版、シャンディ編集部
findings.explanation: Itakura identifies Touhou Publishing and the Shandy editorial department. The translation invents a magazine titled 'The Orient' and treats Shandy Editing as a unit within it.
findings.japanese:
「あの～、すいません。
東邦出版、シャンディ編集部の板倉と申しますが」
findings.todokanai: "Um, excuse me? I'm Itakura from Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine."

findings.highlight: We're going to have you on our front page
findings.evidenceJa: 来月号の表紙は冬馬さんで行きますから
findings.explanation: Itakura promises Kazusa the cover of next month's issue. A magazine cover is not a newspaper-style front page, and the issue timing is also omitted.
findings.japanese:
「あ、それと後日正式に依頼に上がりますが、
写真撮影の方もよろしくお願いしますね。
来月号の表紙は冬馬さんで行きますから！」
findings.todokanai: "Oh and also, we'll send a request at a later date, but we look forward to doing a photoshoot with you too. We're going to have you on our front page!"

findings.highlight: Tell me everything
findings.evidenceJa: 何でも聞いてください
findings.explanation: The reporter invites Youko to ask her anything. The translation reverses the flow of information and tells Youko to disclose everything instead.
findings.japanese:
「はい？　なんでしょうか？
本当、もうざっくばらんで行きましょう！
何でも聞いてください」
findings.todokanai: "Yes? What is it? Let's not keep anything hidden! Tell me everything."

findings.highlight: countless places nearby
findings.evidenceJa: この近く、何軒か案内できますよ
findings.explanation: The reporter says she can show them a few nearby restaurants. 'Countless' inflates a small, concrete number into an unlimited range.
findings.japanese:
「あ、それともお食事がまだでしたら、
何か食べられるお店の方がいいかしら。
この近く、何軒か案内できますよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Ah! Or if you haven't eaten yet, we could go to a place that serves food. I can guide you to countless places nearby."

findings.highlight: doing its best to contradict that
findings.evidenceJa: その予報を一度に再現しようと
findings.explanation: The weather seems to be trying to reproduce both sides of the forecast at once by producing rain and snow together. The translation says it is contradicting the forecast, reversing the image.
findings.japanese:
天気予報では、今夜は『雨、または雪』って言ってたけど、
実際の天気は、どうやらその予報を一度に再現しようと、
無理やり頑張っているみたいだった。
findings.todokanai: According to the weather forecast, it will either rain or snow tonight, but it seems like the weather itself is doing its best to contradict that.

findings.highlight: Since I have a history with you
findings.evidenceJa: 昔のお前を知ってる俺には、もう…っ
findings.explanation: Haruki breaks off after saying that, as someone who knew the old Kazusa, he can no longer... The translation supplies a completed causal statement about merely having a history together.
findings.japanese:
「近づかないんじゃなかったのかよ…
昔のお前を知ってる俺には、もう…っ」
findings.todokanai: "Weren't you never going to come near me ever again…? Since I have a history with you…!?"

findings.highlight: I'm only helping her out a little
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっと世間話をするだけだ
findings.explanation: Haruki tells himself he is only making a little small talk. The translation recasts that rationalization as helping Kazusa, giving him an altruistic purpose absent from the source.
findings.japanese:
俺は、ただ事務的に話してるだけだ。
ちょっと世間話をするだけだ。
findings.todokanai: I'm simply answering her in a professional way. I'm only helping her out a little.

findings.highlight: It's reasonable to say I'd die if I fell asleep
findings.evidenceJa: だから『眠ったら死ぬぞ』とか言われても大丈夫だ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says the stock warning is harmless or inapplicable because she cannot fall asleep. The translation instead endorses the warning as reasonable.
findings.japanese:
「寒い、寒いよ、春希…
けど眠れない。
だから『眠ったら死ぬぞ』とか言われても大丈夫だ」
findings.todokanai: "I'm cold, I'm cold, Haruki… but I can't fall asleep. It's reasonable to say I'd die if I fell asleep."

findings.highlight: glues herself to my back
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の後ろについて、ゆっくりと
findings.explanation: Kazusa slowly follows behind Haruki; the following line then begins her attempt to climb onto him. The translation makes her adhere to his back one beat too early and collapses the staged action.
findings.japanese: そして、俺の後ろについて、ゆっくりと…
findings.todokanai: And then she slowly glues herself to my back…

findings.highlight: that night in Strasbourg
findings.evidenceJa: ストラスブールのイブの夜
findings.explanation: The explicit callback is to Christmas Eve night in Strasbourg. Omitting 'Eve' strips the temporal marker that identifies the remembered scene.
findings.japanese: …あの、ストラスブールのイブの夜みたいに。
findings.todokanai: …Just like that night in Strasbourg.

findings.highlight: I show Kazusa a thumbs up
findings.evidenceJa: 指で丸印を作り
findings.explanation: Haruki makes a circle or OK sign with his fingers. The translation substitutes a thumbs-up, and the same substitution recurs when Kazusa returns the signal.
findings.japanese:
指で丸印を作りかずさの方に示すと、
向こうは結構無感動で軽く頷いた。
findings.todokanai: I show Kazusa a thumbs up, but she only nods apathetically.

findings.highlight: I'll call you back myself. I think I'll do so tomorrow or the day after that
findings.evidenceJa: こちらから連絡しておきます。明日か明後日にでもそちらに伺うと思います
findings.explanation: Haruki says they will contact the other party and that Kazusa will probably visit tomorrow or the next day. The translation turns the projected visit into Haruki calling back himself.
findings.japanese:
「ああ、いや！　大丈夫！
こちらから連絡しておきます。
明日か明後日にでもそちらに伺うと思います」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, no! It's okay! I'll call you back myself. I think I'll do so tomorrow or the day after that."

findings.highlight: holds the warm bowl firmly in her hands
findings.evidenceJa: 熱いはずの土鍋をしっかり抱え込む
findings.explanation: Kazusa hugs the earthenware hot pot that ought still to be hot. The translation substitutes a merely warm bowl held in her hands, losing both the prop and the dangerous physical closeness.
findings.japanese:
文句を言いながら、
かずさが熱いはずの土鍋をしっかり抱え込む。
findings.todokanai: Kazusa holds the warm bowl firmly in her hands, complaining all the while.

findings.highlight: Being a celebrity is part of being an artist
findings.evidenceJa: 芸術家って言ったところで芸人の一種だろ
findings.explanation: Haruki argues that even an artist is one kind of entertainer and therefore needs an interested audience. The translation reverses the containment relation and substitutes 'celebrity' for entertainer.
findings.japanese:
「芸術家って言ったところで芸人の一種だろ。
自分に興味持ってくれる人がいなくちゃ、
話が始まらないんだぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "Being a celebrity is part of being an artist. You wouldn't be able to get anywhere if people didn't take an interest in you."

findings.highlight: Are you going after me now?
findings.evidenceJa: 今度は開き直りか
findings.explanation: Haruki accuses Youko of brazenly owning or doubling down on her position. The translation instead asks whether she is attacking him, changing the target and nature of his retort.
findings.japanese: 「今度は開き直りか？」
findings.todokanai: "Are you going after me now?"

findings.highlight: climb the ranks of a company like that
findings.evidenceJa: その社会の中で上の方には行ける
findings.explanation: Youko speaks about rising within whatever society, field, or community one enters. The translation narrows the principle to corporate promotion inside a company.
findings.japanese:
「その社会の中で上の方には行けるけど、
トップに上り詰めることはできそうにないな」
findings.todokanai: "You might be able to climb the ranks of a company like that, but you'll never reach the top."

findings.highlight: You have changed less in these five years than me
findings.evidenceJa: 五年前から少しも変わってない
findings.explanation: Haruki says Kazusa has not changed at all since five years ago. The translation invents a comparison with himself and allows that she may have changed somewhat.
findings.japanese:
「なぁ、かずさ…
お前こそ、五年前から少しも変わってないじゃないか」
findings.todokanai: "Hey, Kazusa… You have changed less in these five years than me, don't you think?"

findings.highlight: Kazusa would have gotten sick of me
findings.evidenceJa: ずっとそうしていたら、いつかかずさは俺のこと呆れて
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines a future consequence if he keeps acting this way: someday Kazusa will tire of him. The translation turns it into an unreal past counterfactual.
findings.japanese:
ずっとそうしていたら、
いつかかずさは俺のこと呆れて、苦笑して、
何もかも馬鹿馬鹿しくなったって言い出して。
findings.todokanai: If I kept this up, Kazusa would have gotten sick of me, given me a bitter laugh and exclaimed that everything has become ridiculous.

findings.highlight: I woke her up when I saw you were coming
findings.evidenceJa: 来るとわかってたら起こしたんですけど
findings.explanation: Haruki says he would have woken Kazusa if he had known Youko was coming, implying he did not. The translation asserts that he did wake her when he learned of the visit.
findings.japanese:
「すいません。
来るとわかってたら起こしたんですけど」
findings.todokanai: "I'm sorry. I woke her up when I saw you were coming but…"

findings.highlight: "And you dare say you don't belong in Japanーthat this is outside of your territory? Your mother is utterly embarrassed."
findings.evidenceJa:
「何が日本には居場所がない、よ。
ここだけ治外法権？
親の面目丸つぶれ」
findings.explanation: Youko jokes that Kazusa's apartment is an enclave of extraterritorial jurisdiction inside Japan; 'outside of your territory' mistranslates the mock-legal metaphor.
findings.japanese:
「何が日本には居場所がない、よ。
ここだけ治外法権？
親の面目丸つぶれ」
findings.todokanai: "And you dare say you don't belong in Japanーthat this is outside of your territory? Your mother is utterly embarrassed."

findings.highlight: five years ago and also half a year ago
findings.evidenceJa: 五年と半年前
findings.explanation: The source gives one point in time, five and a half years ago. The translation splits it into two separate times, five years ago and half a year ago.
findings.japanese:
俺がこれを始めた五年と半年前、
とある不良っぽい同級生に腕前の差を思い知らされた
屈辱的なエピソードがあったけど…
findings.todokanai: When I started playing the guitar five years ago and also half a year ago, I became painfully aware of the skill difference between me and a certain delinquent classmate, and it was a rather humiliating experience…

findings.highlight: there is actually another feeling existing alongside
findings.evidenceJa: 方向性の違う二つの気持ちが混在してる
findings.explanation: Haruki says two feelings pointing in different directions coexist within his self-interest, and the following lines enumerate them. The translation reduces the pair to one additional feeling.
findings.japanese:
けれど、そんな自己都合の中にも、
本当は、さらに方向性の違う二つの気持ちが混在してる。
findings.todokanai: But inside that self-interest, there is actually another feeling existing alongside, coming from a different direction.

findings.highlight: talking with sincerity
findings.evidenceJa: 感性で話してるように見える
findings.explanation: Youko appears to speak by intuition or sensibility while accurately probing Haruki's weak spots. 'Sincerity' assigns her a moral quality rather than the instinctive mode of thought under discussion.
findings.japanese:
…感性で話してるように見えるのに、
的確にこっちの穴を突いてくるんだもんなぁ。
findings.todokanai: …She makes it look like she's talking with sincerity, but she never misses an opportunity to put me in a bind.

findings.highlight: "That's why I want you to show everyone. Show them the expressions she only shows you."
findings.evidenceJa:
「だから、みんなに見せてあげて欲しいのよ。
この子が、あなたにだけ見せる素顔を」
findings.explanation: Youko wants Haruki to show the public Kazusa's unguarded, true self—the self she reveals only to him; 'the expressions she only shows you' narrows that motive to facial expressions.
findings.japanese:
「だから、みんなに見せてあげて欲しいのよ。
この子が、あなたにだけ見せる素顔を」
findings.todokanai: "That's why I want you to show everyone. Show them the expressions she only shows you."

findings.highlight: at the end of the week
findings.evidenceJa: 週明けにもう一度編集部に連絡する
findings.explanation: Youko will contact the editorial department again at the beginning of the coming week. The translation moves the call to the end of the week.
findings.japanese:
「とにかく、考えておいて。
週明けにもう一度編集部に連絡する」
findings.todokanai: "At any rate, think about it. I'll contact the editing department once again at the end of the week."

findings.highlight: whom I brought home on Friday
findings.evidenceJa: 金曜の夜に部屋に来たかずさ
