findings.explanation: The source only says Kazusa came to Haruki's room Friday night. The translation asserts that Haruki brought her home, inventing his agency in her arrival.
findings.japanese:
金曜の夜に部屋に来たかずさが再び目覚めたのは、
結局、日曜の朝だった…
findings.todokanai: Kazusa, whom I brought home on Friday, didn't wake up until Sunday morning…

findings.highlight: To accept my exclusive coverage of Kazusa
findings.evidenceJa: かずさの独占取材権を勝ち取れ
findings.explanation: Youko told Haruki to win the right to exclusive coverage of Kazusa. The translation makes him accept coverage rather than obtain the reporting rights.
findings.japanese:
かずさの独占取材権を勝ち取れって。
来日期間中、ずっとあいつに張りつけって。
findings.todokanai: To accept my exclusive coverage of Kazusa. To be on her tail during her stay in Japan.

findings.highlight: didn't materialize
findings.evidenceJa: 約束違反は結局通じなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki's needy breach of his promise—placing the call so Setsuna could decide for him—ultimately did not connect or get through. The translation says only that his desire failed to materialize, obscuring the actual failed call.
findings.japanese:
そんな、雪菜に決断を委ねようとした、
俺の甘えた約束違反は結局通じなかった。
findings.todokanai: In the end, my childish desire to push the decision onto Setsuna didn't materialize.

findings.highlight: It's an overbearing result
findings.evidenceJa: しごく当然で、そして重い結果
findings.explanation: The result is utterly natural or only to be expected, yet heavy: Haruki must bear responsibility himself. 'Overbearing' instead presents that demand as oppressive or presumptuous.
findings.japanese:
自分で責任を負えという、
しごく当然で、そして重い結果が。
findings.todokanai: It's an overbearing result telling me to bear the responsibility by myself.

findings.highlight: All my family around the same age have gathered
findings.evidenceJa: 同期の家族とか集まってて
findings.explanation: Hamada is at a barbecue with peers from his cohort and their families. The translation turns them into members of his own family who happen to be around the same age.
findings.japanese:
「そうなのか？
こっちは今、バーベキューの最中でな。
同期の家族とか集まってて」
findings.todokanai: "Is that so? I'm actually in the middle of a barbecue right now. All my family around the same age have gathered."

findings.highlight: I've left those articles to a pro
findings.evidenceJa: そっちの記事は編プロに任せてある
findings.explanation: Hamada says the music-focused articles have been entrusted to an editorial production company. The translation reads 編プロ as an individual professional and erases the separate contractor.
findings.japanese:
「いいよ、そっちの記事は編プロに任せてある。
お前が担当するのはあくまでも、
神秘のベールに包まれた冬馬かずさの『私』の部分だ」
findings.todokanai: "That's fine. I've left those articles to a pro. Your job is purely to unveil the mysterious character behind the veil of Touma Kazusa."

findings.highlight: I don't think this'll be a meager job
findings.evidenceJa: 『こんな芸能ネタで』と思わないでもないけど
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot entirely suppress the dismissive thought 'over entertainment gossip like this.' The translation instead says he does not think the assignment will be meager, reversing his opening evaluation before the line reaches its own contrary conclusion.
findings.japanese:
『こんな芸能ネタで』と思わないでもないけど、
ま、入社一年目の新人社員に全面的に任せるんだから、
その程度の仕事ってことなんだろう…多分。
findings.todokanai: I don't think this'll be a meager job, but if it's something they're willing to completely hand over to a newcomer in his first year, it can't be much more than that… I think.

findings.highlight: make sure to show up twice a week
findings.evidenceJa: 週に二度、月曜と金曜に進捗報告とそこまでの成果物を提出すること
findings.explanation: The requirement is to submit progress reports and completed material twice a week, on Monday and Friday. The source does not require physical attendance, which matters because the assignment explicitly permits remote and flexible work.
findings.japanese:
「ただ、週に二度、月曜と金曜に進捗報告と
そこまでの成果物を提出すること」
findings.todokanai: "Just make sure to show up twice a week. I'll want your progress reports on Mondays and Fridays, including everything you've finished so far."

findings.highlight: They never mentioned that, did they, Hamada-san
findings.evidenceJa: 言ってませんでしたよねぇ浜田さん
findings.explanation: Haruki abruptly redirects Hamada's question by accusing Hamada himself of not having told him. The translation makes the Toumas the people who failed to mention it, weakening the deliberate conversational dodge that hides Haruki's prior contact.
findings.japanese: 「言ってませんでしたよねぇ浜田さん！」
findings.todokanai: "They never mentioned that, did they, Hamada-san!?"

findings.highlight: I've heard rumors
findings.evidenceJa: ええ、そうなんです………か
findings.explanation: Haruki almost says 'yes, that's right' from firsthand knowledge and then changes the final particle into 'is that so?' The translation invents rumors as an explicit source of knowledge and replaces the source's one-syllable near-slip.
findings.japanese: 「ええ、そうなんです………か」
findings.todokanai: "Yes, that's right… I've heard rumors."

findings.highlight: the location for her recitals
findings.evidenceJa: 練習場所も変える
findings.explanation: They will also change Kazusa's practice location. The translation turns private rehearsal space into a venue for recitals.
findings.japanese:
「今後は他社の目をくらますという意味もあって、
二人は別々に都内に部屋を借りたらしい。
ついでに練習場所も変えるそうだ」
findings.todokanai: "From now on, it appears they'll live separately in different apartments to avoid other magazines. This includes the location for her recitals."

findings.highlight: leads only in a worse direction
findings.evidenceJa: その特別が悪い方向に働くことだってある
findings.explanation: Haruki says their special history can also work in a bad direction. The translation says it leads only in a worse direction, changing a dangerous possibility into an exclusive certainty.
findings.japanese:
…ということにしないとやってられない。
だって、その特別が悪い方向に働くことだってある。
findings.todokanai: …I can't do this job without that mindset. After all, that special circumstance leads only in a worse direction.

findings.highlight: Hamada-san opens a brown envelope
findings.evidenceJa: 浜田さんから渡された茶封筒を開くと
findings.explanation: Haruki opens the brown envelope Hamada handed him. The translation makes Hamada open it, shifting the discovery action away from the focal character.
findings.japanese:
と、浜田さんから渡された茶封筒を開くと、
中から軽い金属音とともにこぼれてきたのは…
findings.todokanai: Hamada-san opens a brown envelope, and something falls out of it with a clang.

findings.highlight: responsible for all of Touma Kazusa's privileges
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬かずさの権利を管理してる
findings.explanation: The company manages Kazusa's rights, which Haruki uses to argue that its permission makes the coverage authorized. 'Privileges' is a different legal and ethical concept and obscures the management-versus-personal-consent conflict.
findings.japanese:
「冬馬かずさの権利を管理してるのは、
株式会社冬馬曜子オフィスだよ。
…そこがいいと言えば、それはもうＯＫなんだ」
findings.todokanai: "It's Touma Youko Office PLC that's responsible for all of Touma Kazusa's privileges. …Everything will be alright so long as they give the word."

findings.highlight: set in stone since hundreds of years ago
findings.evidenceJa: そんな前提、数年前から骨身に染みてるはず
findings.explanation: Kazusa should have internalized that corporate premise over the past several years. The translation expands a few years of personal experience into hundreds of years of historical custom.
findings.japanese:
そんな前提、数年前から骨身に染みてるはずなのに、
かずさは今さら子供みたいな理屈で拗ねてみせる。
findings.todokanai: Those rules regarding contracts have been set in stone since hundreds of years ago, but Kazusa sulks like a child over it.

findings.highlight: your recitals and concerts
findings.evidenceJa: 練習とかコンサートとか
findings.explanation: Haruki expected to follow official practice sessions and concerts. Replacing practice with recitals turns the private working process into an additional public performance category.
findings.japanese:
「けどそれは練習とかコンサートとか、
一応、オフィシャルの場だけのつもりだった。
こんな、プライベートにまで侵食するなんて…」
findings.todokanai: "But I only meant it to be about your recitals and concerts. At the very least, only about official topics. I never thought it would encroach on your privacy too…"

findings.highlight: She threw out all my luggage in the freezing winter
findings.evidenceJa: トランク一つで、冬の寒空の中に放り出されて
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she herself was cast out into the winter cold with only one trunk. The translation makes the luggage the thing Youko threw out and inflates the single trunk to all of Kazusa's luggage.
findings.japanese:
「ホテルだって、チェックアウトさせられて、
トランク一つで、冬の寒空の中に放り出されて…」
findings.todokanai: "She even forced me to check out of the hotel. She threw out all my luggage in the freezing winter…"

findings.highlight: is indulgent the other
findings.evidenceJa: ワガママを言ってみたり
findings.explanation: Kazusa alternates between being considerate and making selfish demands. 'Is indulgent' normally means she indulges someone else, reversing the interpersonal direction of her demanding behavior.
findings.japanese:
気を使ってみたり、ワガママを言ってみたり、
雪菜のことを気にしてみたり、
雪菜を気にする俺を気にしてみたり。
findings.todokanai: She tries to be considerate one second, and is indulgent the other. She worries about Setsuna one second, and worries about me worrying about Setsuna the other.

findings.highlight: white noodles
findings.evidenceJa: しらたきまで
findings.explanation: The ingredient is shirataki, translucent konjac noodles with a specific hot-pot role, not generic white wheat noodles.
findings.japanese:
「あ、こら！　お前のより入ってるじゃないか！
ああっ、しらたきまでっ！」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, hey! You're putting in even more than before! Aah, you're even putting in white noodles now!"

findings.highlight: my very own creation, consisting of a random assortment of ingredients
findings.evidenceJa: 適当に食材をぶち込み“自称”寄せ鍋の完成
findings.explanation: Haruki mockingly declares the result a self-proclaimed yose-nabe after throwing ingredients together. The translation omits the named hot-pot dish and replaces it with a generic personal creation.
findings.japanese:
近くのスーパーで、急いで食材を買い込み、
テーブルと電気鍋と食器を持ち込んで、
適当に食材をぶち込み“自称”寄せ鍋の完成。
findings.todokanai: I rushed to the supermarket and bought ingredients, then brought a table, an electric cooking pot, and some tableware. Now my very own creation, consisting of a random assortment of ingredients, is done.

findings.highlight: Once someone relieves you of a certain affliction, it's easy to forget about that affliction along with any sense of gratitude
findings.evidenceJa: 喉元過ぎればというか、衣食足りてなお文句を言うというか
findings.explanation: Haruki juxtaposes one shortened proverb with a comic reversal of another: once the heat passes one forgets it, and even with food and clothing satisfied she still complains. The translation expands only the first idea and drops the second punch line.
findings.japanese:
…喉元過ぎればというか、
衣食足りてなお文句を言うというか。
findings.todokanai: …Once someone relieves you of a certain affliction, it's easy to forget about that affliction along with any sense of gratitude.

findings.highlight: I brought with me some noodles
findings.evidenceJa: 引っ越し蕎麦がある
findings.explanation: The item is explicitly hikkoshi soba, invoking the Japanese moving custom and Youko's earlier joke about greeting neighbors. The translation reduces it to unspecified noodles Haruki happened to bring.
findings.japanese:
「そういえば、引っ越し蕎麦があるんだけど、
鍋に入れれば良かったかな？」
findings.todokanai: "By the way, I brought with me some noodles. Should I have put it in the pot?"

findings.highlight: going on the front page
findings.evidenceJa: 表紙用の撮影
findings.explanation: The earlier professional shoot was for a magazine cover, not a newspaper-like front page.
findings.japanese:
「あれは表紙用の撮影だからな。
それだって昔はスタジオ借りてやってたんだぞ」
findings.todokanai: "That was because the pictures were going on the front page. Even those used to be done in rented studios."

findings.highlight: I'm the only employee in an independent studio
findings.evidenceJa: まるで同人誌作りの勢いだ
findings.explanation: Haruki likens handling interviews, photography, writing, and editing himself to making a doujinshi. The translation invents a one-employee independent studio and loses the self-publishing comparison.
findings.japanese:
もともと最近の雑誌編集の仕事の範囲は広いけど、
今度はインタビューから写真撮影、記事の執筆、
編集までって、まるで同人誌作りの勢いだ。
findings.todokanai: The job of a magazine editor has always been broad, but this time it's interviewing, taking pictures, writing articles, and even editing. It's almost like I'm the only employee in an independent studio.

findings.highlight: Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine
findings.evidenceJa: 東邦出版のシャンディ
findings.explanation: Shandy is one of the major women's fashion magazines published by Touhou Publishing. The translation again invents an 'Orient Magazine' and makes Shandy Editing a subordinate unit.
findings.japanese:
「東邦出版のシャンディって名乗ったんだろ？
それ、三大女性ファッション誌の一つだぞ？
表紙に載ると電車の中吊りにまでお前が出てくる」
findings.todokanai: "She said she was part of Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine, right? That's one of the big three women's fashion magazines. If you're on their front page, you'll definitely end up on advertising posters on trains."

findings.highlight: As long as my output meets their expectations
findings.evidenceJa: アウトプットさえ期限通りに出せれば
findings.explanation: Haruki's freedom is conditional on delivering output on time. The translation replaces the explicit deadline with an undefined quality expectation.
findings.japanese: …アウトプットさえ期限通りに出せればだけど。
findings.todokanai: …As long as my output meets their expectations.

findings.highlight: had this been right before a concert or a competition
findings.evidenceJa: これがコンサートやコンクールの直前だと
findings.explanation: Kazusa describes her habitual schedule whenever a concert or competition is imminent: she plays during every waking, non-eating hour. The translation turns it into an unreal past counterfactual.
findings.japanese:
「で、これがコンサートやコンクールの直前だと、
寝て食べる以外の時間は全部弾いてる」
findings.todokanai: "Well, had this been right before a concert or a competition, I'd be practicing every second I'm not eating or sleeping."

findings.highlight: "It sure is. That's why it's only natural that I don't know anything about doing chores or having a private life. I simply don't have the time."
findings.evidenceJa:
「そうだよ。だから家事とか私生活のことなんか
何もできなくて当然なんだ。
する暇がないからな」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she cannot handle household and private-life matters, while Todokanai TL says she knows nothing about chores or having a private life.
findings.japanese:
「そうだよ。だから家事とか私生活のことなんか
何もできなくて当然なんだ。
する暇がないからな」
findings.todokanai: "It sure is. That's why it's only natural that I don't know anything about doing chores or having a private life. I simply don't have the time."

findings.highlight: when you weren't a professional pianist
findings.evidenceJa: ピアノやってなかった頃だって
findings.explanation: Haruki refers to the period when Kazusa was not playing piano, not a period when she played but lacked professional status. The translation invents a career-stage distinction.
findings.japanese:
「お前は単に物臭なだけだろ。
ピアノやってなかった頃だって全然…」
findings.todokanai: "No, that's just because you're lazy. Even when you weren't a professional pianist, you weren't at all…"

findings.highlight: making me feel even more uncertain
findings.evidenceJa: 余計にヤバい気持ちになってしまう
findings.explanation: Seeing Kazusa's hidden side makes Haruki's feelings more dangerous or alarming to him, feeding the vicious cycle. 'Uncertain' reduces an explicit sense of emotional peril to indecision.
findings.japanese:
…そのせいで、
かずさが普段見せない一面を引き出してしまい、
余計にヤバい気持ちになってしまう。
findings.todokanai: …Thanks to that, Kazusa shows a side of herself she usually keeps hidden, making me feel even more uncertain.

findings.highlight: an advertisement belonging to a familiar magazine
findings.evidenceJa: お馴染みの写真週刊誌の中吊り広告
findings.explanation: Haruki sees the hanging train advertisement for a familiar photo weekly. The translation loses both the photo-weekly format and the fact that the ad is suspended inside the train, weakening the spatial reveal that makes Kazusa immediately recognizable.
findings.japanese:
かずさに説教を垂れつつふと見上げた先の、
お馴染みの写真週刊誌の中吊り広告。
findings.todokanai: As I was lecturing Kazusa, I happened to look up to see an advertisement belonging to a familiar magazine.

findings.highlight: Homecoming of the second generation genius pianist Touma Kazusa
findings.evidenceJa: 初来日・天才二世ピアニスト冬馬かずさ
findings.explanation: The sensational headline calls this Kazusa's first visit to Japan. The translation instead calls it a homecoming, reversing the tabloid's stated arrival status.
findings.japanese:
『初来日・天才二世ピアニスト冬馬かずさ
母親譲りの唯我独尊』
findings.todokanai: "Homecoming of the second generation genius pianist Touma Kazusa. Inherited self-centeredness from mother."

findings.highlight: I don't want to show you to anyone
findings.evidenceJa: 『見せたくない』気持ちの方が強かった
findings.explanation: Haruki admits that his stronger feeling is not wanting to show the hurtful advertisement to Kazusa. The translation instead says he does not want to show Kazusa to other people, making both contrasted motives about concealing her identity and erasing his protective concern for what she reads.
findings.japanese:
本当は『気づかれたくない』より
『見せたくない』気持ちの方が強かったけど、
いちいちそんな心情を説明する必要なんかない。
findings.todokanai: In truth, rather than "I don't want anyone to recognize you," my feelings lean closer to "I don't want to show you to anyone." But there's no reason to explain every single sentiment like that to her.

findings.highlight: a cushion for Kazusa while she's in Japan
findings.evidenceJa: かずさと日本との間の、緩衝材
findings.explanation: Haruki casts himself as a buffer between Kazusa and Japan, mediating their harmful contact. The translation makes him a generic cushion for her during her stay and removes the two-sided relationship.
findings.japanese:
ただ、俺がこうしないと。
かずさと日本との間の、緩衝材にならないと…
findings.todokanai: All that matters is that I become a cushion for Kazusa while she's in Japan.

findings.highlight: she's beginning to allow herself to touch my body
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の体が触れるのを許し始めた
findings.explanation: Haruki interprets Kazusa's relaxation as beginning to allow his body to touch hers. The translation makes Kazusa the person actively allowing herself to touch Haruki, reversing agency inside an already focalized consent reading.
findings.japanese:
だって、全身の緊張が解けたから。
少しだけ、俺の体が触れるのを許し始めたから。
findings.todokanai: I can tell because her whole body doesn't feel tense anymore. And she's beginning to allow herself to touch my body, even if only a little.

findings.highlight: I'm not sure if my judgement was correct
findings.evidenceJa: その事実に俺の判断が効いたのかどうかは正直よくわからなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki is unsure whether his intervention actually contributed to the passengers failing to recognize Kazusa. The translation instead questions whether his judgment was correct, changing causal efficacy into moral or practical correctness.
findings.japanese:
その事実に俺の判断が効いたのかどうかは
正直よくわからなかったけど、
でも、今後もこういう判断が発生することだけは実感した。
findings.todokanai: Facing that fact, I'm not sure if my judgement was correct, but I do realize now that I'll have to make this kind of judgement many times in the future.

findings.highlight: a beauty salon
findings.evidenceJa: アクセサリショップだった
findings.explanation: Their first stop is an accessory shop, where they buy a comb ornament and disguise items. The translation relocates the scene to a beauty salon.
findings.japanese:
電車から降りて俺たちが最初に目指したのは、
家電量販店でも家具店でもなく、
アクセサリショップだった。
findings.todokanai: Our first destination after we got off the train was not an electronic store or a furniture store, but rather a beauty salon.

findings.highlight: the beautiful spectacled young lady next door
findings.evidenceJa: その辺にいる眼鏡の綺麗なお姉さん
findings.explanation: The phrase means an ordinary beautiful woman with glasses one might see around town. 'Next door' is not present and is especially misleading here because Kazusa has literally just moved into the apartment beside Haruki.
findings.japanese:
これで『ただ今話題沸騰のピアニスト冬馬かずさ』改め、
『その辺にいる眼鏡の綺麗なお姉さん』の出来上がり。
findings.todokanai: With this, she's no longer "the talk of the town pianist Touma Kazusa," but rather "the beautiful spectacled young lady next door."

findings.highlight: Indeed
findings.evidenceJa: ねぇ？
findings.explanation: Haruki turns to the clerk and solicits agreement that the disguise suits Kazusa. The translation makes him provide an affirmative answer himself, reversing question and confirmation.
findings.japanese: 「ねぇ？」
findings.todokanai: "Indeed."

findings.highlight: I'll calculate the total later
findings.evidenceJa: 後でまとめて精算するから
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will settle up or reimburse the purchases together later. The translation says only that she will calculate a total, omitting the payment that prompts Haruki's refusal.
findings.japanese:
「後でまとめて精算するから、
とりあえず渡しておいて…」
findings.todokanai: "I'll calculate the total later, so give it to me for now…"

findings.highlight: from telephone providers to furniture stores
findings.evidenceJa: 家電売り場と家具売り場を縦横無尽に走り回り
findings.explanation: They race through home-appliance and furniture departments to buy a refrigerator, table, and bed. The translation substitutes telephone service providers for the appliance section.
findings.japanese:
冷蔵庫、テーブル、ベッド、その他諸々。
家電売り場と家具売り場を縦横無尽に走り回り、
たった数時間で１０万以上も散財してしまった。
findings.todokanai: A fridge, a table, a bed etc. We went through everywhere from telephone providers to furniture stores, spending over 100000 yen in just a few hours.

findings.highlight: three months worth of fees for just a single month at their hotel, including deposits and key money
findings.evidenceJa: 敷金礼金合わせて三か月分を払う
findings.explanation: The Toumas pay three months' rent-equivalent in apartment deposit and key money for a roughly one-month stay. The translation moves these apartment-specific charges to a hotel and describes the stay itself as a month of hotel fees.
findings.japanese:
…なにしろたった一月程度の滞在のために、
敷金礼金合わせて三か月分を払う気前のいい一家だ。
findings.todokanai: …After all, this generous family has paid three months worth of fees for just a single month at their hotel, including deposits and key money.

findings.highlight: is the reason I came back to Japan
findings.evidenceJa: お前に最高の冬馬かずさを見せるためだけに、あたしは日本まで来た
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she came all the way to Japan only to show Haruki the very best Touma Kazusa. The translation preserves the motive but omits the exclusive 'only,' weakening the climactic declaration of singular purpose.
findings.japanese:
「だってさ…
お前に最高の冬馬かずさを見せるためだけに、
あたしは日本まで来たんだぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "After all… Showing you the absolute best of Touma Kazusa is the reason I came back to Japan."

findings.highlight: to drink coffee with plenty of sugar and milk
findings.evidenceJa: それを砂糖とミルクたっぷりのコーヒーで流し込む
findings.explanation: The Touma household habit was to wash the entire spread of sweets down with heavily sweetened, milky coffee. The translation mentions only drinking the coffee and drops the excess dessert consumption it accompanies.
findings.japanese:
「それを砂糖とミルクたっぷりのコーヒーで流し込むのが
子供の頃のウチの習慣で…」
findings.todokanai: "It was our habit back when I was a kid to drink coffee with plenty of sugar and milk…"

findings.highlight: That's how much strength and willpower she must've had
findings.evidenceJa: それだけ体力と精神力を使ってたんだろうな
findings.explanation: Kazusa supposes Youko must have expended that much physical and mental energy, explaining the calories. The translation says the feat proves how much strength and willpower she possessed, reversing consumption into capacity.
findings.japanese:
「あの人はそれをこともなげに平らげてた。
…それだけ体力と精神力を使ってたんだろうな」
findings.todokanai: "She was able to eat it all without a care… That's how much strength and willpower she must've had."

findings.highlight: The cake-addicted pianist
findings.evidenceJa: ケーキをぱくつくピアニスト
findings.explanation: Haruki suggests the image or headline 'a pianist gobbling cake.' The translation diagnoses addiction, escalating a visual human-interest detail into a dependency claim.
findings.japanese: 「ケーキをぱくつくピアニスト？」
findings.todokanai: "The cake-addicted pianist?"

findings.highlight: Despite the sound of the shutter, Kazusa still puts the fork in her mouth, softly forgiving me
findings.evidenceJa: 突然のフラッシュにもかかわらず、かずさはフォークを口に入れたまま、ちょっと照れただけで俺を許してくれた
findings.explanation: The flash interrupts Kazusa while the fork is already in her mouth; Haruki interprets her mere embarrassment as forgiveness. The translation substitutes shutter sound, makes her put the fork in afterward, and narrates forgiveness as an observable action rather than his reading.
findings.japanese:
突然のフラッシュにもかかわらず、
かずさはフォークを口に入れたまま、
ちょっと照れただけで俺を許してくれた。
findings.todokanai: Despite the sound of the shutter, Kazusa still puts the fork in her mouth, softly forgiving me with an embarrassed look.

findings.highlight: made the usual breakfast, I went over to Kazusa's apartment
findings.evidenceJa: 隣に朝食を作りに行ったら、かずさは昨日届いたベッドと見事に一体化していた
findings.explanation: Haruki goes next door to make breakfast and discovers Kazusa fused with the bed. The translation has him make breakfast first and only then go to her apartment, relocating the cooking and reversing the discovery sequence.
findings.japanese:
いつもの時間に起床した俺が、
そのままの勢いで隣に朝食を作りに行ったら、
かずさは昨日届いたベッドと見事に一体化していた…
findings.todokanai: After I had woken up at my usual time and made the usual breakfast, I went over to Kazusa's apartment only to see her spectacularly glued to the bed…

findings.highlight: inside a metropolis
findings.evidenceJa: 都内にしては綺麗な川
findings.explanation: The river is unusually clean specifically for one within Tokyo. 'A metropolis' removes the established city and turns the comparison generic.
findings.japanese:
都内にしては綺麗な川が流れ、草木も多く、
だからこそ、寒さも余計身に染みて…
findings.todokanai: The river is beautiful for being something inside a metropolis. There's even a lot of vegetation. That's precisely why the cold permeates this area that much more…

findings.highlight: any place that has a history with me
findings.evidenceJa: 昔のあたしを知っている場所
findings.explanation: Kazusa reverses the prior grammar: first places her old self knew, then places that know and can bear witness to her old self. 'Has a history with me' flattens that deliberate personification and parallel inversion.
findings.japanese:
『昔のあたしが知っている場所には…
昔のあたしを知っている場所には、近づかない』
findings.todokanai: "I won't ever come near any place that I used to know… or any place that has a history with me."

findings.highlight: I'm so indecisive
findings.evidenceJa: なんて朝令暮改
findings.explanation: Kazusa condemns herself with 朝令暮改, changing an order by evening after issuing it in the morning—fickle inconsistency and immediate reversal. 'Indecisive' instead suggests failure to decide at all.
findings.japanese:
「なんて意志薄弱。
なんて朝令暮改。
あたしって、馬鹿じゃないのか…」
findings.todokanai: "I'm so weak-willed. I'm so indecisive. Am I an idiot or something…?"

findings.highlight: colored paper
findings.evidenceJa: 勝手に色紙を預かってくる
findings.explanation: The objects are shikishi autograph boards collected for Kazusa's signature, not ordinary sheets of colored paper. The same mistranslation obscures why they later form a valuable stack.
findings.japanese:
「そんなの知るか！
勝手に色紙を預かってくるなんて
どういうつもりだ！？」
findings.todokanai: "I don't give a crap about that! You say they gave you colored paper for me to sign without asking for permission!?"

findings.highlight: while compiling the work sent to me as miscellaneous work
findings.evidenceJa: 在宅勤務中に受けた仕事について、各所を回って打ち合わせをしているうちに
findings.explanation: Haruki spends the day visiting various parties for meetings about assignments received during remote work. The translation turns that field coordination into compiling miscellaneous work and loses how the autograph requests accumulated.
findings.japanese:
その後、在宅勤務中に受けた仕事について、
各所を回って打ち合わせをしているうちに、
何故か手元に色紙が山積みになっていた。
findings.todokanai: After that, while compiling the work sent to me as miscellaneous work, for some reason there was a mountain of colored paper in front of me.

findings.highlight: "Then what is it? There is no more dessert. You need to worry about your nutritional balance after eating…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「じゃあなんだよ？
デザートの追加はなしだぞ。
俺の飯を食うからには栄養バランスを…」
findings.explanation: after eating — Haruki says that so long as Kazusa eats his cooking, he controls its nutritional balance. 'After' makes the concern merely temporal.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあなんだよ？
デザートの追加はなしだぞ。
俺の飯を食うからには栄養バランスを…」
findings.todokanai: "Then what is it? There is no more dessert. You need to worry about your nutritional balance after eating…"

findings.highlight: Little by little, Kazusa crosses over the line
findings.evidenceJa: とうとう、かずさが踏み込んだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa finally steps into the avoided topic in a decisive moment. The translation makes the crossing gradual and ongoing.
findings.japanese: とうとう、かずさが踏み込んだ。
findings.todokanai: Little by little, Kazusa crosses over the line.

findings.highlight: Tell me that you're sick of me
findings.evidenceJa: だったらのろけてみせろよ？あたしに『やってられるか』って言わせてみろよ
findings.explanation: Kazusa challenges Haruki to gush about Setsuna until Kazusa herself says she cannot stand listening. The translation makes Haruki tell Kazusa that he is sick of her, reversing speaker, object, and the relationship being discussed.
findings.japanese:
「だったらのろけてみせろよ？
あたしに『やってられるか』って言わせてみろよ」
findings.todokanai: "Then go ahead and tell me. Tell me that you're sick of me."

findings.highlight: which reason is the true one
findings.evidenceJa: どんな理由も本当なんだ
findings.explanation: Haruki understands that every offered reason is a pretext and, simultaneously, every one expresses part of Kazusa's truth. The translation turns that coexistence into selecting which single reason is true.
findings.japanese:
もとからどんな理由だって嘘だって。
そして、どんな理由も本当なんだって。
findings.todokanai: That all her reasons were lies to begin with, and which reason is the true one.

findings.highlight: memorized my methods of interviewing
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の取材道具の使い方を覚えてしまっていた
findings.explanation: Kazusa has learned how to operate Haruki's interview equipment, enabling her to stop recordings, delete images, and turn the recorder on him. The translation changes concrete device literacy into abstract interviewing method.
findings.japanese:
ここ数日の取材攻勢で、かずさはすっかり
俺の取材道具の使い方を覚えてしまっていた。
findings.todokanai: After these past days of aggressive interviewing from me, Kazusa has completely memorized my methods of interviewing.

findings.highlight: our job hunting
findings.evidenceJa: お互いの卒業とか、就職とか
findings.explanation: Haruki lists their graduations and starting employment during the first year. The translation moves them backward to job hunting.
findings.japanese:
「一年目はお互いの卒業とか、就職とか。
友達のこととか家族のこととか雪菜の歌のこととか…」
findings.todokanai: "The first year was about our graduation, our job hunting, our friends, our family, and Setsuna's singing…"

findings.highlight: both Kazusa and Setsuna
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜とかずさを『平等にひいき』してた
findings.explanation: Haruki's quoted paradox is that he favored both girls equally. The translation keeps special treatment but drops equality, the element that makes the earlier innocent balance possible.
findings.japanese:
怖いもの知らずだった。
雪菜とかずさを『平等にひいき』してた。
findings.todokanai: I was reckless. I was giving both Kazusa and Setsuna "special treatment."

findings.highlight: We two cannot be allowed to like each other
findings.evidenceJa: 二人のことを好きでいることは許されない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is no longer permitted to love both Setsuna and Kazusa. The translation instead says Haruki and one other person are forbidden to like each other, replacing a triangular moral problem with reciprocal prohibition.
findings.japanese: 二人のことを好きでいることは許されない。
findings.todokanai: We two cannot be allowed to like each other.

findings.highlight: she has been on stage countless times
findings.evidenceJa: 何度かステージに上がってた
findings.explanation: Setsuna appeared onstage several times after the Valentine's live. 'Countless' radically inflates a limited number central to the five-year summary.
findings.japanese:
就職してからはずっとご無沙汰だったけど、
あのバレンタインライブ以降、
何度かステージに上がってた。
findings.todokanai: She has been on a hiatus ever since she got employed, but ever since that Valentine's Day concert, she has been on stage countless times.

findings.highlight: due to my poor conversational abilities, and my unstable feelings
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の話術の未熟さか、俺の気持ちの不安定さか
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot tell whether his concealment fails because his speaking technique is immature or because his feelings are unstable. The translation makes both definite cumulative causes.
findings.japanese:
隠そうとしても、結局そこに行き着いてしまうのは、
俺の話術の未熟さか、俺の気持ちの不安定さか。
findings.todokanai: Even when I tried to hide it, this is the destination I've arrived at due to my poor conversational abilities, and my unstable feelings.

findings.highlight: ten whole days
findings.evidenceJa: 十数日も会っていない
findings.explanation: Haruki and Setsuna have not met for more than ten days—some number in the teens. The translation fixes it at exactly ten.
findings.japanese:
もう、十数日も会っていないこと。
声すら、聞けていないこと。
findings.todokanai: Now we haven't met for ten whole days. I haven't even heard her voice.

findings.highlight: But of course I can't tell her that
findings.evidenceJa: なんて、言うわけないだろ
findings.explanation: The rejected utterance is Haruki's preceding internal admission that he could not leave Kazusa suffering and wanted to help her, not the reassurance about feelings he has just spoken aloud. The English attaches 'that' to the voiced reassurance and creates an immediate contradiction.
findings.japanese: なんて、言うわけないだろ。
findings.todokanai: But of course I can't tell her that.

findings.highlight: perhaps I'll be able to return in my second year
findings.evidenceJa: さすがに二年目にもなったら、少しは余裕が
findings.explanation: Setsuna thought that by her second year as an employee she might gain a little breathing room, then jokes that work may instead grow busier. The translation says she hoped she could return, changing the expected resource from spare capacity to a comeback.
findings.japanese:
「でも、さすがに二年目にもなったら、
少しは余裕が…なんて、
かえって忙しくなりそうな気配がアリアリですけど」
findings.todokanai: "But I thought that perhaps I'll be able to return in my second year… or so I hoped. It actually looks like I'm only going to get more busy from now on."

findings.highlight: one of those famous industry people
findings.evidenceJa: 噂を聞きつけた業界の人
findings.explanation: They speculate that the disguised woman may be an industry person who heard the buzz about Setsuna. The translation makes the industry person herself famous.
findings.japanese:
「なるほど、そういう考え方もあるのか…
てことは噂を聞きつけた業界の人かなぁ？」
findings.todokanai: "I see, that's one way of looking at it… Does that mean she's one of those famous industry people?"

findings.highlight: that's how much ability Setsuna has
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜にはそれだけの華がある
findings.explanation: Tomo argues that Setsuna has star presence or glamour warranting discovery. Generic ability removes the public charisma under discussion and makes the next line about ambition less coherent.
findings.japanese:
「だって雪菜にはそれだけの華があるんだもん。
眠らせておくのもったいないって！」
findings.todokanai: "But that's how much ability Setsuna has. It's a crime to let her talent go to waste!"

findings.highlight: Setsuna was there
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜だった
findings.explanation: Kazusa says the performer truly was the Setsuna she knew—recognition of enduring Setsuna-ness, not merely confirmation that Setsuna was physically present. The translation reduces the emotional identification to attendance.
findings.japanese: 「雪菜だった…」
findings.todokanai: "Setsuna was there…"

findings.highlight: the concert hall
findings.evidenceJa: ライブハウスに赴いた
findings.explanation: Kazusa goes to a live house, the small club venue central to Routes and Setsuna's scene. 'Concert hall' implies a larger, formal performance space.
findings.japanese:
そう言って、
いつもの変装でライブハウスに赴いたかずさは…
findings.todokanai: With those words, Kazusa went toward the concert hall with her usual disguise…

findings.highlight: we couldn't become friends
findings.evidenceJa: 親友にはなれなかった
findings.explanation: Kazusa says they failed to become best friends, recalling the earlier extreme of lifelong best friendship. The translation lowers the failed possibility to ordinary friendship.
findings.japanese:
「結局、親友にはなれなかったけど…
そうしてしまったのはあたしだけど」
findings.todokanai: "In the end, we couldn't become friends… but that was my fault."

findings.highlight: a bitter, resigned breakdown in resolve
findings.evidenceJa: 諦めにも似た決裂
findings.explanation: The narration calls this a rupture or break resembling resignation, contrasting the former agreement. The translation says Kazusa's resolve breaks down, when the resolve to avoid becoming Setsuna's enemy is precisely what she has reached.
findings.japanese:
あの時の、苦笑混じりの合意とは違う、
ただ苦いだけの、諦めにも似た決裂。
findings.todokanai: Unlike her bitter smile of agreement back then, she shows nothing but a bitter, resigned breakdown in resolve.

findings.highlight: I think that Setsuna… still thinks of you as a friend
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は…今でもかずさのこと、親友だと思ってる
findings.explanation: Haruki asserts that Setsuna still regards Kazusa as her best friend. The translation both hedges the statement with 'I think' and downgrades best friend to friend.
findings.japanese:
「雪菜は…
今でもかずさのこと、親友だと思ってる」
findings.todokanai: "I think that Setsuna… still thinks of you as a friend, Kazusa."

findings.highlight: So you can remain employed
findings.evidenceJa: 春希は社会人であるために、開桜社の編集部の北原社員であるために
findings.explanation: Kazusa builds a normative role argument: as a working adult and Kaiousha editorial employee, Haruki cannot disclose a subject's privacy. The translation invents a threat that disclosure would cost his employment.
findings.japanese:
「だから、春希は社会人であるために、
開桜社の編集部の北原社員であるために、
雪菜にあたしのことを言うことができないんだ」
findings.todokanai: "So you can remain employed, Haruki; so you can remain as Mr. Kitahara of the editing department of Kaiousha, you can't tell Setsuna anything about me."

findings.highlight: when I try to sound smart
findings.evidenceJa: 理論武装したときの俺そのもの
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes Kazusa as himself when armored in logic—using airtight reasoning to defend an emotionally unacceptable act. 'Try to sound smart' reduces the shared defense mechanism to intellectual vanity.
findings.japanese: 今のお前は、理論武装したときの俺そのものだ。
findings.todokanai: Right now, you're just like me when I try to sound smart.

findings.highlight: how the opponent feels when they use it
findings.evidenceJa: その戦法を使ったときの、敵の心情
findings.explanation: Haruki knows how his opponent feels when he himself uses this argumentative strategy against them. The translation says the opponent is the one employing the strategy, reversing the combat roles.
findings.japanese:
だから俺は、その戦法の弱点を知っている。
その戦法を使ったときの、敵の心情を知っている。
findings.todokanai: That's why I know the weakness of that strategy. I know how the opponent feels when they use it.

findings.highlight: trembles in fear on my chest
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の胸の中でむずがってみせる
findings.explanation: Kazusa fusses, squirms, or protests restlessly in Haruki's arms after explicitly saying no. The translation invents fear as her emotional state, which the source does not establish.
findings.japanese: かずさが、俺の胸の中でむずがってみせる。
findings.todokanai: Kazusa trembles in fear on my chest.

findings.highlight: Is everyone outside now?
findings.evidenceJa: みんなもう外に出てるよ？
findings.explanation: Tomo tells Setsuna that everyone is already outside, using a prompting final particle. The translation makes Tomo ask Setsuna for information she has come to provide.
findings.japanese: 「みんなもう外に出てるよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Is everyone outside now?"

findings.highlight: found my determination to meet him
findings.evidenceJa: やっとぶつかってみる決心がついた
findings.explanation: Setsuna resolves to try confronting or colliding with Haruki directly after remembering everything. 'Meet him' removes the difficult conflict that her planned tears and mutual forgiveness are meant to initiate.
findings.japanese:
「ステージに立って、何もかも忘れて思いっきり歌って、
ステージから降りて何もかも思い出したら、
やっとぶつかってみる決心がついた」
findings.todokanai: "When I stood on the stage singing my heart out, I forgot about everything. When I got off the stage, I remembered everything and found my determination to meet him."

findings.highlight: wasn't something I could see, but something I could smell
findings.evidenceJa: 見えるものと言うよりは染みるものだった
findings.explanation: The smoke is less something Haruki can see than something that stings or smartingly gets into his eyes, as the tears on the next line confirm. The translation changes that physical eye irritation into smell.
findings.japanese:
俺が部屋に飛び込んだとき真っ先に目に入ったのは、
見えるものと言うよりは染みるものだったりした。
findings.todokanai: The first sensation that came to me the moment I bolted into the room wasn't something I could see, but something I could smell.

findings.highlight: finish the first and second movements today
findings.evidenceJa: 今日中に、二曲目までは完成させる
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will finish through the second piece today. 曲 refers to separate pieces in the concert program, not the first and second movements of one work.
findings.japanese:
「今日中に、二曲目までは完成させる。
三日前までには完璧にしておくよ」
findings.todokanai: "I'll finish the first and second movements today. I'll have everything done completely three days before the concert."

findings.highlight: for that in itself was part of her ability
findings.evidenceJa: それでいて実力も一流だったから
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that despite promoting herself beyond what her ability alone warranted, Youko's actual ability was also first-rate. The English redefines promotion as part of her ability and deletes the concession that she truly was a first-rate pianist.
findings.japanese:
「実力以上に人気を獲得する手段をよく知ってた。
一応、それでいて実力も一流だったから、
誰も文句は言えなかった」
findings.todokanai: "She was very good at getting popularity above what her actual ability warranted. Though I suppose no one could complain, for that in itself was part of her ability."

findings.highlight: she crushed them all with shady tactics
findings.evidenceJa: 全部実力と裏工作で叩き潰してきた
findings.explanation: Youko crushed her complainers and rivals with both genuine skill and backstage maneuvering. Omitting 実力 makes her success rest entirely on dirty tricks, contradicting Kazusa's deliberately mixed respect and contempt.
findings.japanese:
「…いいや、文句を言ったり、
妬んだりする人間はたくさんいたけど、
全部実力と裏工作で叩き潰してきた」
findings.todokanai: "…No, there were plenty of people who complained about her and envied her, but she crushed them all with shady tactics."

findings.highlight: I can't reach that castle of hers.
findings.evidenceJa: あの域に達するのは不可能だ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she cannot reach that level—the extreme domain of Youko's sexual and promotional tactics. 域 is a level or realm, not a castle.
findings.japanese:
「あたしにはできない…
あの域に達するのは不可能だ」
findings.todokanai: "It's something I'm incapable of… I can't reach that castle of hers."

findings.highlight: I haven't lost my way yet.
findings.evidenceJa: 少なくとも軸はぶれてないからな
findings.explanation: Haruki defends Youko by saying that at least her underlying axis or guiding purpose has never wavered. The translation makes Haruki claim that he himself has not lost his way.
findings.japanese:
「少なくとも軸はぶれてないからな。
それに俺だって本人には言いたいこと言ってる」
findings.todokanai: "I haven't lost my way yet. And besides, I'm only saying what I want to tell her myself."

findings.highlight: with the help of a single female worker
findings.evidenceJa: 女手一つでこんなワガママ娘を育てた
findings.explanation: 女手一つで means Youko raised her daughter single-handedly as a woman or single mother. The translation invents a separate female employee who helped her raise Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
「当たり前だ。
そうやって女手一つでこんなワガママ娘を育てたんだ。
どこに嫌われる理由があるんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Of course not. She raised such a spoiled daughter with the help of a single female worker. Why would you ever hate her?"

findings.highlight: converting this to a book or a movie script
findings.evidenceJa: 書籍化した方がいいかもしれないな
findings.explanation: Hamada suggests turning the material into a book. A movie script is entirely absent and changes his publishing-industry proposal into an additional adaptation plan.
findings.japanese:
「………書籍化した方がいいかもしれないな。
今出せば『今週のベストセラー』くらいなら
余裕で狙える」
findings.todokanai: "…We might be better off converting this to a book or a movie script. I'm sure we'd be able to produce the bestseller of the week with this."

findings.highlight: It's not like I can just say no
findings.evidenceJa: 断ることもできたんだけどね
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly says she could have refused the business trip, but accepted because it was the opportunity she had long requested and refusal might cost future work. The translation says she could not simply refuse, removing her active career choice.
findings.japanese:
「断ることもできたんだけどね…
でも、ずっと希望してたし、なのに断っちゃうと、
二度とこういう仕事回ってこないかもって」
findings.todokanai: "It's not like I can just say no… but I always hoped for something like this. If I said no now, I might never get a chance for a job like this again."

findings.highlight: there was this independent conductor
findings.evidenceJa: 一人傑作なのがいてさ。フランス人の、３０半ばの指揮者で
findings.explanation: Kazusa says there was one especially outrageous or hilarious specimen, a French conductor in his mid-thirties. 一人 counts the person and 傑作 marks him as a piece of work; it does not mean an independent conductor.
findings.japanese:
「で、一人傑作なのがいてさ。
フランス人の、３０半ばの指揮者で…
そいつ、若い頃母さんの愛人やってたらしいんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Anyway, there was this independent conductor. A Frenchman in his mid thirties… Apparently he was mom's lover when he was young."

findings.highlight: she looks sorrowful as if hit with a painful realization
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱり痛快でどうしようもないみたいに
findings.explanation: Kazusa finds Haruki's visible relief irresistibly satisfying or exhilarating because she is teasing his jealousy. The translation reverses her delight into sorrow and a painful realization.
findings.japanese:
俺が、ほっとした表情を浮かべるのも、
やっぱり痛快でどうしようもないみたいに。
findings.todokanai: And when I breathe a sigh of relief in the end, she looks sorrowful as if hit with a painful realization.

findings.highlight: a standing member of the Paris orchestra
findings.evidenceJa: 今でもパリのオケの常任だよ
findings.explanation: The man is still a permanent or resident conductor of a Paris orchestra. He is not merely a standing rank-and-file orchestra member.
findings.japanese:
「そいつ、今でもパリのオケの常任だよ。
なんなら名前も教えようか？
もしかしたらあたしの父親かも」
findings.todokanai: "He's still a standing member of the Paris orchestra. Should I tell you his name? He might even be my father."

findings.highlight: tons of men who had as little talent as they had money
findings.evidenceJa: 金の代わりに才能って置き換えても、当てはまる奴らばっかりだった
findings.explanation: Kazusa says the same two categories apply if 'money' is replaced with 'talent': men too talented to care about her and untalented men whose pride cannot bear her. The translation collapses that mirrored binary into uniformly poor, untalented men.
findings.japanese:
「ああ、そうだ…
金の代わりに才能って置き換えても、
当てはまる奴らばっかりだった」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, right… there were tons of men who had as little talent as they had money."

findings.highlight: platonic physical intimacy
findings.evidenceJa: ただスキンシップを重ねただけ。俺の欲求を一方的に満たしただけ
findings.explanation: Haruki says he merely accumulated physical contact and one-sidedly satisfied his desire. Adding 'platonic' sanitizes contact that the surrounding narration explicitly frames as taboo, self-gratifying, and escalating sexual desire.
findings.japanese:
ただスキンシップを重ねただけ。
俺の欲求を一方的に満たしただけ。
findings.todokanai: All I did was initiate some platonic physical intimacy. I only managed to gratify my own desires one-sidedly.

findings.highlight: turn 30 and suddenly kick the bucket
findings.evidenceJa: ３０過ぎていきなりキたら嫌だなぁ
findings.explanation: Haruki fears that the consequences of this workload will suddenly hit or catch up with him after thirty. The translation escalates delayed burnout or bodily collapse into sudden death.
findings.japanese: …３０過ぎていきなりキたら嫌だなぁ。
findings.todokanai: …I wouldn't want to turn 30 and suddenly kick the bucket.

findings.highlight: It's not commendable, but I won't be able to do any interviews today.
findings.evidenceJa: とてもじゃないけど、今日は取材はできない
findings.explanation: とてもじゃないけど means there is simply no way he can conduct an interview this late. It is not a moral judgment that interviewing would be uncommendable.
findings.japanese:
時計を見ると、午前０時をとっくに過ぎてる。
とてもじゃないけど、今日は取材はできない。
findings.todokanai: Looking at the clock I see that it's long past midnight. It's not commendable, but I won't be able to do any interviews today.

findings.highlight: my dishonesty in skipping our interview without calling her
findings.evidenceJa: 不誠実を働いた『ことになってる』昨夜
findings.explanation: The scare-quoted ことになってる says last night is being treated as though Haruki dishonestly skipped an interview without notice; Haruki disputes that premise because he only promised to call when coming. The English states the dishonesty as fact and drops the scene's argumentative frame.
findings.japanese:
俺が連絡もせずに取材をすっぽかすという、
不誠実を働いた『ことになってる』昨夜についての…
findings.todokanai: She's been babbling about my dishonesty in skipping our interview without calling her about it last night…

findings.highlight: All the articles must be published by Friday
findings.evidenceJa: 記事の提出期限は金曜朝まで
findings.explanation: Friday morning is the deadline for Haruki to submit the article, not the publication date for multiple articles. The distinction matters to Kazusa's argument that he still had one or two days of scheduling slack.
findings.japanese:
「…記事の提出期限は金曜朝までだから、
まぁ、１、２日は余裕あったけど」
findings.todokanai: "…All the articles must be published by Friday, though I suppose I had a day or two to spare."

findings.highlight: Those two hours reminiscing about some family-centered soap opera
findings.evidenceJa: そんな、ホームドラマというかフィクションみたいな二時間
findings.explanation: The warm two-hour visit itself felt like a family drama or fiction. They were not spending the two hours reminiscing about a soap opera; the genre label is Haruki's metaphor for the improbable reunion.
findings.japanese:
そんな、ホームドラマというか
フィクションみたいな二時間は、
あっという間に過ぎ去った。
findings.todokanai: Those two hours reminiscing about some family-centered soap opera felt like they went by in a flash.

findings.highlight: eventually from even herself
findings.evidenceJa: とうとう自分からも距離を置いてしまったとき
findings.explanation: Within the indirect account of Mrs. Shibata's apology, 自分 is Mrs. Shibata: Kazusa eventually distanced herself even from her. The translation instead says Kazusa distanced herself from herself, inventing psychological self-alienation and removing Shibata from her own regret.
findings.japanese:
かずさが世間からドロップアウトして、
ピアノも捨てて、周囲からどんどん距離を置き、
とうとう自分からも距離を置いてしまったとき…
findings.todokanai: Back when Kazusa shut herself off from society, abandoning even the piano. When she distanced herself more and more from her surroundings, and eventually from even herself…

findings.highlight: her happy memories and her painful memories might have just been mixed up
findings.evidenceJa: 楽しかった思い出や、辛かった記憶が余計にデフォルメされただけ
findings.explanation: Haruki considers whether five years have further exaggerated or distorted Shibata's happy and painful memories. He does not suggest that the two categories became confused or mixed together.
findings.japanese:
旦那さんも、最近涙もろくなってきたと言っていた。
あれから五年経って、楽しかった思い出や、
辛かった記憶が余計にデフォルメされただけかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: Her husband told me she's been tearing up quite a lot recently. After five years, her happy memories and her painful memories might have just been mixed up.

findings.highlight: I don't think she's wrong in doing so.
findings.evidenceJa: そのことを間違ってるなんて思っていない
findings.explanation: Haruki believes his own ambush was worthy of criticism but does not believe that doing it was wrong. The translation instead says Kazusa is not wrong to criticize him, replacing his moral defense of the act with agreement about her response.
findings.japanese:
俺は非難されるにふさわしい騙し討ちをしたし、
そしてそのことを間違ってるなんて思っていないから。
findings.todokanai: I did plan a surprise attack worthy of criticism, and I don't think she's wrong in doing so.

findings.highlight: before it was just our fingers that were intertwined
findings.evidenceJa: さっきまで指が触れていただけだったのに
findings.explanation: Until that moment their fingers had merely been touching; now their palms meet, and only on the following lines do all their fingers interlace. The translation moves interlacing earlier and breaks the staged escalation of contact.
findings.japanese:
だって、さっきまで指が触れていただけだったのに、
今は、手のひらを合わせてる。
findings.todokanai: Because before it was just our fingers that were intertwined, but now I can feel her entire palm.

findings.highlight: …That question, along with the warmth and sweat of Kazusa's palm, dissipates into nothingness.
findings.evidenceJa:
…そんな問いかけは、
かずさの手のひらの、あまりの熱さと汗に、
かき消されてしまった。
findings.explanation: Haruki's questions are drowned out by the extraordinary heat and sweat of Kazusa's palm; the English says the physical sensations dissipate along with the question — Their contact still overwhelms his moral reasoning.
findings.japanese:
…そんな問いかけは、
かずさの手のひらの、あまりの熱さと汗に、
かき消されてしまった。
findings.todokanai: …That question, along with the warmth and sweat of Kazusa's palm, dissipates into nothingness.

findings.highlight: When I saw that they put Touma Kazusa's image on the advertisements for the school
findings.evidenceJa: 発売後、『我が校』の写真に冬馬かずさ本人が写り込んでるのを見たら
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines Suwa, after the publication goes on sale, discovering Kazusa herself in a photograph of 'our school.' The English makes Haruki the past-tense viewer and turns the future magazine photo into school advertising.
findings.japanese:
発売後、『我が校』の写真に
冬馬かずさ本人が写り込んでるのを見たら…
ま、クレームがないことを祈ろう。
findings.todokanai: When I saw that they put Touma Kazusa's image on the advertisements for the school… I can only pray she doesn't file charges.

findings.highlight: I'm savoring the experience until the concert.
findings.evidenceJa: コンサートまで、お預けだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa tells Haruki that hearing her play is withheld from him until the concert—he must wait. The English makes Kazusa herself voluntarily savor an experience, reversing who is being denied.
findings.japanese:
「この前も言っただろ？
コンサートまで、お預けだ」
findings.todokanai: "Didn't I tell you earlier? I'm savoring the experience until the concert."

findings.highlight: our memories after this point diverge
findings.evidenceJa: ここから俺の記憶は途切れる
findings.explanation: Haruki's memory simply cuts out from this point because he fell asleep. The translation invents a divergence between two people's memories, obscuring why only Kazusa can narrate the unseen interval.
findings.japanese: だから、ここから俺の記憶は途切れる。
findings.todokanai: Because of that, our memories after this point diverge.

findings.highlight: making love to him
findings.evidenceJa: キスしたのも、抱きあったのも。…そいつのこと好きになったのも
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she was first to kiss him, embrace him, and fall in love with him. 抱きあった is mutual embracing, not sex; 'making love' invents an impossible sexual encounter while Haruki was asleep and corrupts the revelation's exact hierarchy of firsts.
findings.japanese:
「キスしたのも、抱きあったのも。
…そいつのこと好きになったのも」
findings.todokanai: "Kissing him, making love to him… and falling in love with him."

findings.highlight: Even if it's only spam mail
findings.evidenceJa: それがスパムメールだったとしても
findings.explanation: Haruki says even if the interruption had been spam, its timing would have been uncannily exact; the next line reveals it is from Setsuna. 'It's only spam mail' falsely identifies the actual message as spam.
findings.japanese:
それがスパムメールだったとしても、
あまりにも絶妙で、ピンポイントで、
最高にして最悪のタイミングだったけれど。
findings.todokanai: Even if it's only spam mail, the timing of which it was sent was far too miraculous and precise, and it was both great and awful at the same time.

findings.highlight: You really don't know how to spot a joke.
findings.evidenceJa: お前、本当に融通利かないのな
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Haruki rigid, inflexible, or impossible to negotiate with after he refuses her attempted final transgression. She does not claim he lacks the ability to recognize humor; her 'joke' is an admitted cover story no one believes.
findings.japanese:
「結局、最後の最後まで失敗続きだったけどな。
…お前、本当に融通利かないのな」
findings.todokanai: "Although, it failed completely until the very end… You really don't know how to spot a joke."

findings.highlight: making love to him
findings.evidenceJa: キスしたのも、抱きあったのも。…そいつのこと好きになったのも
findings.explanation: The later verbatim recollection repeats the same embrace, and the translation repeats the same invented claim that Kazusa and Haruki had sex.
findings.japanese:
『キスしたのも、抱きあったのも。
…そいつのこと好きになったのも』
findings.todokanai: "Kissing him, making love to him… and falling in love with him."

findings.highlight: One moment I prepare the tea cold, and then I prepare it hot the other.
findings.evidenceJa: 熱くしたり冷たくしたり、自分でもやってることがぶれてる
findings.explanation: Haruki alternately heats and cools himself—alcohol inflames him, then cold tea attempts to cool him. The tea itself is not alternately prepared hot and cold.
findings.japanese:
熱くしたり冷たくしたり、
自分でもやってることがぶれてるとは思うけど。
findings.todokanai: One moment I prepare the tea cold, and then I prepare it hot the other. Even I think my actions are not making sense.

findings.highlight: My wavering heart despises the actions I take against my instincts.
findings.evidenceJa: 揺れる心が本能に及ぼす作用が恨めしい
findings.explanation: Haruki resents the effect his wavering heart has on his bodily instincts—the arousal and masturbation made explicit by the following lines. The English makes the heart itself the experiencer of hatred and invents actions taken against instinct.
findings.japanese:
自分に起きた、心と体の反応が恐ろしい。
揺れる心が本能に及ぼす作用が恨めしい。
findings.todokanai: The response from my mind and body is terrifying. My wavering heart despises the actions I take against my instincts.

findings.highlight: why Knights-san was so beautiful at first
findings.evidenceJa: 急に華やいじゃったなぁナイツさん
findings.explanation: The venue contact jokes that Knights Records has suddenly become more glamorous now that Setsuna is handling the account. He is not wondering why a person called 'Knights-san' looked beautiful at first.
findings.japanese:
「そうですかぁ。こちらこそよろしく。
いや、急に華やいじゃったなぁナイツさん。
小木曽さんだっけ？　ステージの方も出たりするの？」
findings.todokanai: "I see. Likewise, then. I was wondering why Knights-san was so beautiful at first. You were Ogiso-san, right? Do you appear on stage too?"

findings.highlight: pay for my daughter's education
findings.evidenceJa: 娘の養育費も稼がないと
findings.explanation: 養育費 is the cost of raising or supporting her daughter, not specifically tuition or educational expenses. Youko is joking about having to earn Kazusa's keep.
findings.japanese:
「社長ですもの。
社員を食べさせる義務があるの。
ついでに娘の養育費も稼がないと」
findings.todokanai: "I'm your company president. I have a duty to make sure my workers can eat, not to mention that I have to earn enough money to pay for my daughter's education."

findings.highlight: since 5 AM
findings.evidenceJa: 朝から五時間ぶっ続け
findings.explanation: Kazusa has been playing continuously for five hours since the morning. The translation turns the duration into a 5 a.m. start time.
findings.japanese: 「…これで朝から五時間ぶっ続けよ？」
findings.todokanai: "…You've been at it since 5 AM, you know?"

findings.highlight: Try to keep the pace, would you?
findings.evidenceJa: なんとか、もってよね
findings.explanation: Youko is privately urging herself or her body to hold out for one more day. This is about endurance under her illness, not maintaining Kazusa's rehearsal pace.
findings.japanese: 「なんとか、もってよね…」
findings.todokanai: "Try to keep the pace, would you?"

findings.highlight: done with all the magazines before noon. The only job remaining was the compiling of the interviews
findings.evidenceJa: 雑務の方は午前中で終わってしまい、後はインタビューの起こしだけが残った
findings.explanation: Haruki finishes his miscellaneous work by noon and has only interview transcription left. The English invents magazines and weakens 起こし from transcribing recorded interviews to vaguely compiling them.
findings.japanese:
気を紛らすために仕事をしようとしても、
雑務の方は午前中で終わってしまい、
後はインタビューの起こしだけが残った。
findings.todokanai: I tried distracting myself with work, but I was done with all the magazines before noon. The only job remaining was the compiling of the interviews.

findings.highlight: lying down on the bed
findings.evidenceJa: 部屋の床に寝転がってしまった
findings.explanation: Haruki lies down on the floor of the room, not on a bed. The physical self-neglect in the scene is erased.
findings.japanese:
けれど、今はとてもあいつの声を聞く気になれず、
結局、そのまま部屋の床に寝転がってしまった。
findings.todokanai: But I couldn't bring myself to listen to her voice. In the end, I found myself just lying down on the bed like this.

findings.highlight: She would've done so earlier if she had forgiven me. And she would've done so much later if she began to trust me again.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺を許していたなら、もっと前に。
俺を信じ切っていたなら、もっと後になるはずだった。
findings.explanation: 信じ切っていた is complete ongoing trust, while 'began to trust me again' introduces a recovery process — The earlier-versus-later timing contrast is preserved.
findings.japanese:
俺を許していたなら、もっと前に。
俺を信じ切っていたなら、もっと後になるはずだった。
findings.todokanai: She would've done so earlier if she had forgiven me. And she would've done so much later if she began to trust me again.

findings.highlight: That's why, this time… is our final farewell.
findings.evidenceJa: 今度こそ、今度こそ…これで、さよならだ
findings.explanation: The remembered line emphatically repeats 'this time' twice: 'This time, this time... this is goodbye.' The translation invents 'That's why' and removes the deliberate repetition.
findings.japanese:
『今度こそ、今度こそ…
これで、さよならだ』
findings.todokanai: "That's why, this time… is our final farewell."

findings.highlight: Nothing good would come from being with you.
findings.evidenceJa: あんたと一緒だと時間がもたないから
findings.explanation: Io says she cannot fill or sustain the time when she is with Takeya—the conversation drags. She does not say that being with him produces bad consequences.
findings.japanese:
「嫌よ。
あんたと一緒だと時間がもたないから」
findings.todokanai: "No way. Nothing good would come from being with you."

findings.highlight: If only they could resolve it by themselves, with just the two of them
findings.evidenceJa: 二人で済んでればいいんだけどな
findings.explanation: Takeya hopes the problem involves only Haruki and Setsuna. He is worried a third person is involved; he is not saying the couple should resolve it without help.
findings.japanese: 「二人で済んでればいいんだけどな…」
findings.todokanai: "If only they could resolve it by themselves, with just the two of them…"

findings.highlight: be with him throughout the whole concert
findings.evidenceJa: 開演までずっと一緒にいて
findings.explanation: Takeya proposes staying with Haruki until the concert begins, then arranging to go home together afterward. The English instead has them accompany him throughout the performance.
findings.japanese:
「そんなの簡単だ。
偶然だなって声かけて、開演までずっと一緒にいて、
コンサートが終わったら一緒に帰る約束をすればいい」
findings.todokanai: "That's simple. We'll greet him and say 'fancy seeing you here,' then we'll be with him throughout the whole concert and make plans to all go home together once it's over."

findings.highlight: wrap things up for now
findings.evidenceJa: とにかく早く切り替えることだ
findings.explanation: Her manager tells her to reset mentally and move on quickly so she can handle tomorrow's work. He is not telling her to finish or wrap up the current task.
findings.japanese:
「次に活かしてくれればいい。
まだ明日もそちらでの仕事が残ってるんだから、
とにかく早く切り替えることだ」
findings.todokanai: "Just make sure it goes well next time and everything will work out. You still have work left to do over there tomorrow, so wrap things up for now."

findings.highlight: I just felt like I had to see you in person
findings.evidenceJa: ただ、雪菜に直接連絡しなければって
findings.explanation: Haruki rationalizes that it might remain within their rules so long as he did not contact Setsuna directly; he obtained her whereabouts through her family. The English reverses that into a need for direct personal contact.
findings.japanese:
「ルール違反気味ってのはわかってる。
ただ、雪菜に直接連絡しなければって…」
findings.todokanai: "I'm aware that that's breaking the rules. I just felt like I had to see you in person, Setsuna…"

findings.highlight: waiting to receive her with a smile on my face
findings.evidenceJa: あいつが満面の笑顔で応えてきたら
findings.explanation: Kazusa is the one who might respond to Haruki and his bouquet with a radiant smile. The translation transfers the smile to Haruki and turns Kazusa's response into his act of waiting.
findings.japanese:
全てが終わったあとの控え室で、花束を抱えた俺に、
あいつが満面の笑顔で応えてきたら…
findings.todokanai: Had I stood in the waiting room once the concert was over with a bouquet in my hands, waiting to receive her with a smile on my face…

findings.highlight: hold back my own feelings
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の気持ちを強く保てるかどうか
findings.explanation: Haruki doubts whether he could keep his feelings firm or remain steadfast after Kazusa smiled at him. 'Hold back' recasts the problem as suppressing desire rather than maintaining his chosen resolve.
findings.japanese:
その時俺は、
自分の気持ちを強く保てるかどうかがわからない。
findings.todokanai: Then I can't be sure if I'd be able to hold back my own feelings.

findings.highlight: it didn't end up stopping because it froze over
findings.evidenceJa: 冷たく凍った訳じゃなかった。凍ったまま、乾いてしまったようだった
findings.explanation: Time has frozen, but not with coldness; it feels frozen and dried out. The English introduces an unrelated causal denial about why time stopped and breaks the dry-freeze metaphor.
findings.japanese:
けど、冷たく凍った訳じゃなかった。
凍ったまま、乾いてしまったようだった。
findings.todokanai: But it didn't end up stopping because it froze over. It was more so as if it dried up.

findings.highlight: under the pretense that someone had asked her to pass it to me
findings.evidenceJa: 『人から預かった』と俺に差し出した
findings.explanation: Kazusa handed him the ticket saying she had received it from someone. The Japanese does not call this a pretense; that word adds an unsupported judgment that the explanation was false.
findings.japanese:
かずさが『人から預かった』と俺に差し出した、
雪菜の参加してたライブチケット。
findings.todokanai: Kazusa had offered me a ticket to attend Setsuna's live performance under the pretense that someone had asked her to pass it to me.

findings.highlight: forgotten about public appearances
findings.evidenceJa: 自身の恥も省みず俺を責めた
findings.explanation: Setsuna condemns him without regard for her own embarrassment, despite the surrounding customers watching. 'Public appearances' is not the meaning and sounds as if she has forgotten scheduled performances.
findings.japanese:
それほどまでに雪菜が、
自身の恥も省みず俺を責めたのは…
findings.todokanai: Setsuna had forgotten about public appearances and condemned me…

findings.highlight: no matter what happens to you
findings.evidenceJa: 今日だけは何があっても、あなただけは何があっても
findings.explanation: Setsuna says 'today of all days, no matter what—and you of all people, no matter what.' The second phrase emphatically singles Haruki out as the person who must hear Kazusa; it does not mean regardless of what happens to him.
findings.japanese:
「どうしてそんなことするの？
今日だけは何があっても、あなただけは何があっても、
かずさのピアノを聴かなくちゃならないはずだよね？」
findings.todokanai: "Why would you do such a thing? No matter what happens today, and no matter what happens to you, you have to listen to her play the piano, don't you?"

findings.highlight: doesn't mean she has the confidence to do it
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜の方には自信があるって訳じゃ、なかった
findings.explanation: Although Setsuna can rebuke Haruki, that does not mean she herself feels secure or confident about their relationship. The English narrowly makes the confidence concern her ability to lash out.
findings.japanese:
俺を叱咤できるからと言って、
雪菜の方には自信があるって訳じゃ、なかった。
findings.todokanai: Just because Setsuna says she's capable of lashing out at me, doesn't mean she has the confidence to do it.

findings.highlight: let me pretend that I'm angry at you
findings.evidenceJa: 今は建前で怒らせて
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks to be allowed, for now, to speak from the principled or publicly defensible position and say only what is right. 建前 does not mean her anger is feigned.
findings.japanese:
「だけど、今は建前で怒らせて。
すごく原則的なこと言わせて。
正しいことだけ、言わせて」
findings.todokanai: "But right now, let me pretend that I'm angry at you. Let me admonish you with my principles. Let me say only the right things."

findings.highlight: I might actually remember her saying them back then rather than today
findings.evidenceJa: 未来から思い返したら、本当にそんな日として記憶されるかもしれない
findings.explanation: Haruki fears that when he looks back from the future, today may truly be remembered as the day they parted. The translation invents a competition between remembering the words as spoken 'back then' and today.
findings.japanese:
いや、未来から思い返したら、
本当にそんな日として記憶されるかもしれないって
思わせる、雪菜の台詞だった。
findings.todokanai: No, I could even say that if I were to recall them in the future, I might actually remember her saying them back then rather than today.

findings.highlight: a misguided, yet utterly virtuous woman
findings.evidenceJa: 聖女過ぎる悪女
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Setsuna a 'villainess far too saintly': her excessive goodness enables his moral collapse. 'Misguided, yet virtuous' removes the deliberately accusatory saint/villain paradox and substitutes a different fault.
findings.japanese:
俺を甘えるだけの情けない男へと、
言い訳ばかりのずるい男へと堕落させてしまう、
聖女過ぎる悪女。
findings.todokanai: She's a misguided, yet utterly virtuous woman who's degrading me into a miserable man who only wants to take advantage of her. She's turning me into someone who will give her nothing but excuses.

findings.highlight: I've never wanted to tell her
findings.evidenceJa: 今ほど強く思ったことはなかったから
findings.explanation: Haruki says he has never more strongly felt or wished that she would remain this awful man's girlfriend. The Japanese does not say he wanted to voice that thought to her.
findings.japanese:
『ずっと、その最低男の彼女でいて欲しい』って、
今ほど強く思ったことはなかったから。
findings.todokanai: Because I've never wanted to tell her "I want you to remain as the girlfriend of this despicable man" more than now either.

findings.highlight: won't ever be able to repeat those resolute words ever again
findings.evidenceJa: 二度も口に出す勇気なんかないから
findings.explanation: Haruki lacks the courage to say such a momentous line twice now, so he saves it for the next opportunity. 'Ever again' contradicts the explicit plan on the following line to say it later.
findings.japanese:
だって、こんなもの凄い決意を込めた台詞、
二度も口に出す勇気なんかないから。
findings.todokanai: Because I won't ever be able to repeat those resolute words ever again.

findings.highlight: The further away I get, the less clear Setsuna's expression becomes.
findings.evidenceJa: 離れるにつれ、雪菜の表情が段々と歪んでいく。
findings.explanation: Her expression grows distorted as distance increases; 'less clear' makes it only a loss of visual resolution — The next line restores the ambiguity between smiling, crying, and Haruki's own distorted vision.
findings.japanese: 離れるにつれ、雪菜の表情が段々と歪んでいく。
findings.todokanai: The further away I get, the less clear Setsuna's expression becomes.

findings.highlight: a situation where she doesn't feel like she belongs
findings.evidenceJa: この場と状況にそぐわないものだった
findings.explanation: Setsuna's sad, enduring expression is incongruous with the post-sex and post-reconciliation situation. The Japanese does not say Setsuna herself feels that she does not belong there.
findings.japanese:
どちらかと言えば、悲しそうな…
何かに耐えているような、
この場と状況にそぐわないものだった。
findings.todokanai: If I had to put it into words, she looks sad… as if trying to endure something in a situation where she doesn't feel like she belongs.

findings.highlight: My legs are completely stuck together.
findings.evidenceJa: 脚、パンパンに張っちゃってるから
findings.explanation: Setsuna says her legs are swollen, tight, or painfully stiff after the night's exertion. They are not stuck together.
findings.japanese:
「明日、外回り辛いなぁって。
脚、パンパンに張っちゃってるから」
findings.todokanai: "Tomorrow is going to be rough. My legs are completely stuck together."

findings.highlight: how I'm doing this with Setsuna while hiding something from her
findings.evidenceJa: 今の俺が雪菜に隠れてするもののように
findings.explanation: Setsuna's unguarded expression, which she did not mean Haruki to see, is likened to the expression Haruki is now making out of her sight. The English turns this mirrored hidden-face image into an unspecified act he is doing 'with Setsuna' while concealing something.
findings.japanese: …まるで、今の俺が雪菜に隠れてするもののように。
findings.todokanai: …Just like how I'm doing this with Setsuna while hiding something from her.

findings.highlight: proof that I dragged her along for an entire month
findings.evidenceJa: 一月近くも引きずってしまうって証明された
findings.explanation: The earlier tiny encounter and failure to disclose it proved that the conflict or hurt could drag on for nearly a month. Haruki did not literally drag Setsuna along for that month.
findings.japanese:
偶然ほんの少し会っただけで、
そのことを話さなかっただけで、
一月近くも引きずってしまうって証明されたのに？
findings.todokanai: That I met Kazusa by pure coincidence for a short while, and I simply neglected to tell her about it? Even though there is proof that I dragged her along for an entire month?

findings.highlight: I wasn't nervous back then.
findings.evidenceJa: あの時は、緊張しかなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that on the previous occasion he felt nothing but nervousness. The English states the exact opposite.
findings.japanese:
あの時は、緊張しかなかった。
額から噴き出した汗が、やけに冷たかった。
findings.todokanai: I wasn't nervous back then. Rather, the sweat pouring from my forehead was awfully cold.

findings.highlight: tons of men who had as little talent as they had money
findings.evidenceJa: 金の代わりに才能って置き換えても、当てはまる奴らばっかりだった
findings.explanation: Kazusa says the same two categories still fit if 'money' is replaced with 'talent': men above her who have no interest in her, and men below her whose pride cannot bear her. The translation collapses that binary into people low in both money and talent.
findings.japanese:
『ああ、そうだ…
金の代わりに才能って置き換えても、
当てはまる奴らばっかりだった』
findings.todokanai: "Ah, right… There were tons of men who had as little talent as they had money."

findings.highlight: We're going to the high school together.
findings.evidenceJa: 今から付属に向かうところだよ
findings.explanation: Kazusa records this before joining Haruki and says she is now on her way to their old high school. 'We're going together' wrongly puts Haruki with her already and changes the recorded timeline.
findings.japanese:
『現在、１月２５日、金曜の午後２時。
お前と合流する少し前。
…今から付属に向かうところだよ』
findings.todokanai: "It's currently January 25th, 2 PM on Friday. A short while before I meet up with you… We're going to the high school together."

findings.highlight: a normal guy like you would come to love a defective person like me
findings.evidenceJa: 欠陥品が、お前みたいな普通の男、好きになるなんてさ
findings.explanation: Kazusa marvels bitterly that a defective article like her could fall in love with an ordinary man like Haruki. The English reverses the direction and says Haruki came to love her.
findings.japanese:
『あたしみたいな、ピアノしか能がない、
他にはなにもできない欠陥品が、
お前みたいな普通の男、好きになるなんてさ…』
findings.todokanai: "The fact that a normal guy like you would come to love a defective person like me, who's so incompetent that she can't do anything other than play the piano…"

findings.highlight: erase my feelings for you
findings.evidenceJa: お前への想いを昇華する
findings.explanation: Kazusa intends to sublimate or transform her feelings for Haruki through the concert, not simply erase them. 昇華 is load-bearing because the performance becomes the form in which the love is preserved and transcended.
findings.japanese:
『来てくれる、だけでいい。
そしたらあたしはもう、お前のこと諦めるから。
その日限りで、お前への想いを昇華するから』
findings.todokanai: "All you need to do is to come. If you do that, I'll give up on you. I'll make sure to erase my feelings for you on that day."

findings.highlight: forcefully pushing the door to the room shut
findings.evidenceJa: 強くドアに押しつけたまま
findings.explanation: Haruki keeps Setsuna pressed hard against the door while embracing her from behind. He is not pushing the door shut; it was already closed after they entered.
findings.japanese:
そうして、強くドアに押しつけたまま、
背中から抱きしめ強くのしかかり、
二度と離れないよう全身を密着させる。
findings.todokanai: Then, after forcefully pushing the door to the room shut, I embrace Setsuna from behind and lean into her, pressing my body against hers so tightly that we'd never part again.

findings.highlight: Without even taking the time to take my shoes, or let alone my clothes off
findings.evidenceJa: 服どころか、靴を脱ぐ余裕すら与えずに
findings.explanation: Haruki gives Setsuna no time to remove even her shoes, much less her clothes. The English assigns the undressing to Haruki and tangles the 'even shoes, let alone clothes' escalation.
findings.japanese: 服どころか、靴を脱ぐ余裕すら与えずに…
findings.todokanai: Without even taking the time to take my shoes, or let alone my clothes off…

findings.highlight: pull up Setsuna's shirt all the way to her shoulders
findings.evidenceJa: シャツを肩まではだけさせ
findings.explanation: Haruki pulls the unbuttoned shirt open and down/off around her shoulders, exposing her upper body. Pulling a shirt up to the shoulders describes the wrong movement and exposed area.
findings.japanese:
シャツを肩まではだけさせ、
剥き出しになったそこに唇と舌と、歯を当てる。
findings.todokanai: I pull up Setsuna's shirt all the way to her shoulders, and attack her exposed skin with my lips, tongue, and teeth.

findings.highlight: both of her legs tremble, and her high-heels rise higher
findings.evidenceJa: 両脚はぴぃんと突っ張り、パンプスのかかとが今まで以上に持ち上がる
findings.explanation: Setsuna's legs snap taut and the heels of her pumps lift farther off the floor as she rises onto her toes. The English replaces the tautening with trembling and makes the shoes themselves rise.
findings.japanese:
ただそれだけの愛撫で、雪菜の両脚はぴぃんと突っ張り、
パンプスのかかとが今まで以上に持ち上がる。
findings.todokanai: With just a single caress, both of her legs tremble, and her high-heels rise higher than any other time so far.

findings.highlight: slowly exposing her butt
findings.evidenceJa: ゆっくりと雪菜の太股が露わになっていく
findings.explanation: As Haruki's fingers catch and raise the skirt, Setsuna's thighs are gradually exposed. The translation changes thighs to buttocks.
findings.japanese:
そのまま、股の内側を撫で上げていくと、
指先がスカートを巻き込み、
ゆっくりと雪菜の太股が露わになっていく。

「あれぇ？　おかしいなぁ…
つい先ほど滞在先に伺ってきたばかりなんですが」
findings.todokanai: "Huh? That's strange… I swear she just came back to her residence."

findings.highlight: Do you take me for someone who's self-employed…?
findings.evidenceJa: 「どこの同人誌ですか…」
findings.explanation: After Suzuki claims Haruki will write, photograph, edit, print, and sell the issue alone, he asks what kind of doujinshi operation she thinks this is. The English replaces the specific self-published-zine production joke with the unrelated employment category 'self-employed.'
findings.japanese: 「どこの同人誌ですか…」
findings.todokanai: "Do you take me for someone who's self-employed…?"

findings.highlight: It'll fester, and pus will gush out of your wrist.
findings.evidenceJa: 「化膿するぞ？腐りきって、手首からぽとっと落ちるぞ？」
findings.explanation: Haruki grotesquely jokes that Kazusa's hand will suppurate, rot through, and drop off at the wrist with a plop. The English instead has pus gush out of the wrist, changing the threatened loss of her pianist's hand into discharge from it.
findings.japanese:
「化膿するぞ？
腐りきって、手首からぽとっと落ちるぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "The wound will become infected, you know? It'll fester, and pus will gush out of your wrist."

findings.highlight: Because her attitude is so half-assed, I have no choice but to accept any fastballs she throws at me.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな中途半端な態度だから、ど真ん中の剛速球を受け止めることなんかできない。
findings.explanation: Because Haruki's own attitude is so half-hearted, he cannot catch Kazusa's blazing fastball straight down the middle—her declaration that he matters more than her hands. The English assigns the half-heartedness to Kazusa and says Haruki has no choice but to accept the pitches, reversing both subject and result.
findings.japanese:
そんな中途半端な態度だから、
ど真ん中の剛速球を受け止めることなんかできない。
findings.todokanai: Because her attitude is so half-assed, I have no choice but to accept any fastballs she throws at me.

findings.highlight: "My new project has been decided on. They're going to let me write an entire issue."
findings.evidenceJa:
『新しいプロジェクトが決まった。
雑誌を一冊、任せてもらえることになった』
findings.explanation: Haruki has been entrusted with an entire magazine issue, which includes editing; the English says he will write an entire issue — The larger conversation repeatedly states his editorial role and broad production duties.
findings.japanese:
『新しいプロジェクトが決まった。
雑誌を一冊、任せてもらえることになった』
findings.todokanai: "My new project has been decided on. They're going to let me write an entire issue."

findings.highlight: I was ready to look down on her and give her a lecture or two.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分のことを棚に上げ、説教の一つでもかますつもりで気合いを入れていた。
