findings.explanation: Haruki was steeling himself to lecture Youko while setting aside his own failings—an explicit acknowledgment of hypocrisy. The English instead says he intended to look down on her, replacing self-reproach with contempt for Youko.
findings.japanese:
自分のことを棚に上げ、説教の一つでもかますつもりで
気合いを入れていた。
findings.todokanai: I was ready to look down on her and give her a lecture or two.

findings.highlight: "The fatality rate for this disease has gone down considerably in recent years. And I've been using plenty of both medications and money. I'll make it to a hundred at the very least."
findings.evidenceJa:
「最近はだいぶこの病気の致死率も下がってきてるし、
薬打ちまくって、金使いまくって、
少なくとも１００までは生き延びるわよ？」
findings.explanation: Youko vows that she will use drugs and money in the future, while the English says she has already been using them — Her defiant commitment to aggressive treatment is still intelligible from the surrounding lines.
findings.japanese:
「最近はだいぶこの病気の致死率も下がってきてるし、
薬打ちまくって、金使いまくって、
少なくとも１００までは生き延びるわよ？」
findings.todokanai: "The fatality rate for this disease has gone down considerably in recent years. And I've been using plenty of both medications and money. I'll make it to a hundred at the very least."

findings.highlight: During our commemorations… or even whenever I feel like it, I can call Kazusa to join our gatherings.
findings.evidenceJa:
お互いや、仲間たちの記念日に…
それどころか、単に思い立っただけでも、
すぐに集まれるメンバーの中にかずさがいる。
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines Kazusa among friends who can gather for one another's anniversaries or on a whim; the English makes Haruki the person who calls her to 'our gatherings.' — The essential fantasy of Kazusa becoming readily present in the old social circle remains.
findings.japanese:
お互いや、仲間たちの記念日に…
それどころか、単に思い立っただけでも、
すぐに集まれるメンバーの中にかずさがいる。
findings.todokanai: During our commemorations… or even whenever I feel like it, I can call Kazusa to join our gatherings.

findings.highlight: It really is… a mockery of art.
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱり芸術って………馬鹿みたいだ。
findings.explanation: Haruki concludes that art itself is absurd or stupid: Kazusa's narrow, childish fixation is precisely what made her art shine. 'A mockery of art' instead implies a debasement of art, reversing the object and direction of his judgment.
findings.japanese: やっぱり芸術って………馬鹿みたいだ。
findings.todokanai: It really is… a mockery of art.

findings.highlight: Being with someone so troublesome is impossible for you, just as I suspected.
findings.evidenceJa: 「だってギター君、普通の人だもの。そんなハードルの高い相手、やっぱりあの子には無理だったのよ」
findings.explanation: Youko says that an ordinary man is too high a hurdle for Kazusa: Kazusa cannot live normally without destroying the world around him. The English reverses the relationship, calling Kazusa troublesome and saying she is impossible for Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「だってギター君、普通の人だもの。
そんなハードルの高い相手、
やっぱりあの子には無理だったのよ」
findings.todokanai: "Because you're an ordinary person, Guitar-kun. Being with someone so troublesome is impossible for you, just as I suspected."

findings.highlight: To other people, that would be a very brutal, heartless and terrible thing.
findings.evidenceJa: 「それは、別のある人にとっては、とても残酷で、無情で、本当に酷いこと」
findings.explanation: Youko refers to one particular other person—Setsuna—for whom Kazusa taking Haruki would be cruel. The English pluralizes her into generic 'other people,' erasing the pointed third member of the triangle.
findings.japanese:
「それは、別のある人にとっては、
とても残酷で、無情で、本当に酷いこと」
findings.todokanai: "To other people, that would be a very brutal, heartless and terrible thing."

findings.highlight: what about the people who were around me when I lived an ordinary life…?
findings.evidenceJa: そして、もしリスクを覚悟で飛び込んだとしても、その時、普通の俺の側にいようとしてくれていた人は…
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks of the single person who had been trying to stay by ordinary Haruki's side—Setsuna. The English turns her into plural people who merely happened to be around him, losing both the referent and her sustained effort.
findings.japanese:
そして、もしリスクを覚悟で飛び込んだとしても、
その時、普通の俺の側にいようとしてくれていた人は…
findings.todokanai: Even if I jumped into it with full awareness of the risks, what about the people who were around me when I lived an ordinary life…?

findings.highlight: So make sure you don't forget that.
findings.evidenceJa: 「だから、これからも忘れない。下手をしたら…いえ、今のままじゃ確実に、一生、新しい恋なんてできるわけがない」
findings.explanation: Youko says Kazusa will continue not to forget Haruki and, at this rate, will certainly never love anyone new. The English changes the first sentence into an instruction for Haruki to remember Youko's warning.
findings.japanese:
「だから、これからも忘れない。
下手をしたら…いえ、今のままじゃ確実に、
一生、新しい恋なんてできるわけがない」
findings.todokanai: "So make sure you don't forget that. If she's unlucky… No, it's almost certain that she'll never fall in love again her whole life at this rate."

findings.highlight: I can manage to stay in Setsuna's room overnight all the time.
findings.evidenceJa: …まぁ、逆にこういう一家だからこそ、雪菜を大っぴらに部屋に泊めることもできるんだけど。
findings.explanation: Haruki says this family's openness is what lets him openly have Setsuna stay overnight in his room. The English reverses both the guest and the room, saying Haruki repeatedly stays in Setsuna's room.
findings.japanese:
…まぁ、逆にこういう一家だからこそ、
雪菜を大っぴらに部屋に泊めることもできるんだけど。
findings.todokanai: …Well, on the other hand, it's precisely because this family is the way it is that I can manage to stay in Setsuna's room overnight all the time.

findings.highlight: Amidst this heavy atmosphere
findings.evidenceJa: この、軽くて浮き足立った雰囲気の中でも。一世一代の決め所かもしれなかった場面でも…
findings.explanation: The family is in a light, excited, almost giddy mood as they anticipate a marriage. Calling the atmosphere 'heavy' reverses the contrast: Haruki is sinking internally despite everyone else's buoyancy.
findings.japanese:
この、軽くて浮き足立った雰囲気の中でも。
一世一代の決め所かもしれなかった場面でも…
findings.todokanai: Amidst this heavy atmosphere, and in this place where my once in a lifetime choice could be made…

findings.highlight: In fact, it was probably the best way to go about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 気が早すぎても、問題ないはずだった。それどころか、正式に申し込むべき話の流れだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that, far from the family merely being premature, the conversation had reached the point where he should formally propose/ask for Setsuna's hand. The English reduces this decisive missed act to a vague 'best way to go about it.'
findings.japanese:
気が早すぎても、問題ないはずだった。
それどころか、正式に申し込むべき話の流れだった。
findings.todokanai: There shouldn't be anything wrong with being eager. In fact, it was probably the best way to go about it.

findings.highlight: Setsuna's mother started talking about the future of the household, putting her in direct opposition to the children who insisted on talking about that with only the family around.
findings.evidenceJa: お母さんは、もう親戚の予定を気にしだして、『内輪で』を多用する若手組と真っ向から対立し。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's mother is already worrying about relatives' schedules, while the younger group repeatedly insists on keeping the wedding intimate or within the family. The English invents a discussion about the household's future and mistakes 内輪で for privately discussing it with family present.
findings.japanese:
お母さんは、もう親戚の予定を気にしだして、
『内輪で』を多用する若手組と真っ向から対立し。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna's mother started talking about the future of the household, putting her in direct opposition to the children who insisted on talking about that with only the family around.

findings.highlight: I feel like I'm at the edge of a violent passion. One that is trying to make me forget about everything…
findings.evidenceJa: まるで何もかも忘れようとしているかのような、激しい情欲のぶつけあいの果てに…
findings.explanation: Haruki is looking back on what came at the end of their violent mutual collision of lust, as if both were trying to forget everything. The English turns the aftermath into a present feeling 'at the edge' of an abstract passion and loses the mutual sexual act.
findings.japanese:
まるで何もかも忘れようとしているかのような、
激しい情欲のぶつけあいの果てに…
findings.todokanai: I feel like I'm at the edge of a violent passion. One that is trying to make me forget about everything…

findings.highlight: we should give our undivided attention to Kazusa's additional concert
findings.evidenceJa: 「今は、かずさを追加公演に専念させることが第一だと言うことで、彼女とも一致しました」
findings.explanation: Haruki and Miyoko agree that their first priority is keeping Kazusa focused on the additional concert. The English instead says they themselves should devote their undivided attention to it, shifting both the subject and the management plan.
findings.japanese:
「今は、かずさを追加公演に専念させることが
第一だと言うことで、彼女とも一致しました」
findings.todokanai: "I told her that we should give our undivided attention to Kazusa's additional concert, and she agreed."

findings.highlight: I'll give that girl a happy life no matter what it takes…
findings.evidenceJa: 二人じゃ、文殊の知恵は出ないかもしれないけれど、なんとしても、あいつが笑って暮らせる一生を…
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even if two heads may not produce wisdom, he and Youko must somehow find a whole life in which Kazusa can live smiling. The English turns that tentative collaborative search into Haruki's unilateral promise to give Kazusa a happy life.
findings.japanese:
二人じゃ、文殊の知恵は出ないかもしれないけれど、
なんとしても、あいつが笑って暮らせる一生を…
findings.todokanai: The two of us might not be able to come up with anything wise, but I'll give that girl a happy life no matter what it takes…

findings.highlight: "Decide after you've asked yourself if you value him or Kazusa more."
findings.evidenceJa: 「かずさとどっちを取るか考えた上で決めてください」
findings.explanation: Youko asks about men in general; the English's singular 'him' invents a specific current partner — Haruki's answer still communicates that she must choose Kazusa over romantic indulgence.
findings.japanese: 「かずさとどっちを取るか考えた上で決めてください」
findings.todokanai: "Decide after you've asked yourself if you value him or Kazusa more."

findings.highlight: I can't think of any other reason…
findings.evidenceJa: それが、熱気のこもった練習のせいなのか、治りきっていない患部が熱を持ってしまったのか、それ以外の理由なのかはわからなかったけど…
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot tell whether Kazusa's hot hands come from practice, inflammation, or some other reason—the final possibility quietly allows for emotional arousal. The English says he cannot think of any other reason, explicitly excluding the implication the source leaves open.
findings.japanese:
それが、熱気のこもった練習のせいなのか、
治りきっていない患部が熱を持ってしまったのか、
それ以外の理由なのかはわからなかったけど…
findings.todokanai: Perhaps it was due to her passionate practice up until now, or perhaps the result of an inflammation in her injured hands. I can't think of any other reason…

findings.highlight: I wanted to do it directly…
findings.evidenceJa: 「実は記事の最終チェック、事務所通してると時間かかるから、直接やってもらいたくてさ…」
findings.explanation: Haruki wants Kazusa to check the article directly because routing it through her office takes too long. The English says Haruki himself wants to do the check directly, reversing who is being asked to perform the work.
findings.japanese:
「実は記事の最終チェック、
事務所通してると時間かかるから、
直接やってもらいたくてさ…」
findings.todokanai: "The truth is, the final checking of the articles will take a while if I do it at the office, so I wanted to do it directly…"

findings.highlight: Kazusa just refuses to get a clue.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺がどれだけはぐらかしても、かずさは遠慮という名の拒絶をやめようとしなかった。
findings.explanation: Kazusa persists in a refusal she calls consideration or restraint: she knowingly tries to withdraw for Haruki's sake. 'Refuses to get a clue' instead portrays her as failing to understand his hints, reversing her awareness and motive.
findings.japanese:
俺がどれだけはぐらかしても、
かずさは遠慮という名の拒絶をやめようとしなかった。
findings.todokanai: No matter how much I try to change the topic, Kazusa just refuses to get a clue.

findings.highlight: The amount of damage she would receive really makes me not want to resort to this tactic.
findings.evidenceJa: 威力はともかく、あまりにダメージが大きいから、あまり使いたくはなかった作戦だったけど。
findings.explanation: Haruki's tactic is to move closer so Kazusa's refusal loses force, but doing so inflicts too much emotional damage on Haruki himself. The English assigns that damage to Kazusa, reversing the reason he hates using the tactic.
findings.japanese:
威力はともかく、あまりにダメージが大きいから、
あまり使いたくはなかった作戦だったけど。
findings.todokanai: Unfortunately, I wouldn't just be toning down the tension. The amount of damage she would receive really makes me not want to resort to this tactic.

findings.highlight: As long as you want me to, I'll do my very best for you, Kazusa…
findings.evidenceJa: 「かずさがそう言う限り、俺は俺の万全を尽くす。…今度こそ、お前の側にいる」
findings.explanation: Haruki means that as long as Kazusa keeps saying her concert failed because he did not come, he will do everything in his power and stay by her this time. The English changes that revealing dependence into a generic condition that she wants his help.
findings.japanese:
「かずさがそう言う限り、
俺は俺の万全を尽くす。
…今度こそ、お前の側にいる」
findings.todokanai: "As long as you want me to, I'll do my very best for you, Kazusa… This time, I'll be by your side."

findings.highlight: you should probably avoid cake
findings.evidenceJa: 「そっか、ステーキか。うん、そんなの朝飯前だ。…いや、そんな時間に食うものじゃないけど」
findings.explanation: Haruki literalizes his own easy-task idiom and immediately corrects himself. Todokanai TL begins an English ‘piece of cake’ recreation but turns the payoff into unexplained dietary advice, so the self-correction does not land as intentional wordplay. An English recreation need not preserve the source's exact breakfast-hour mechanism; it does need a coherent literalized-idiom punchline.
findings.japanese:
「そっか、ステーキか。
うん、そんなの朝飯前だ。
…いや、そんな時間に食うものじゃないけど」
findings.todokanai: "I see, you want steak. Yes, making that should be a piece of cake… no, you should probably avoid cake."

findings.highlight: her classmates who heard rumors about her treated her like a pest
findings.evidenceJa: 事情を知っていた教師は路傍の石のように、そして噂を聞いていたクラスメイトは腫れ物のように扱い、そこに血の通ったコミュニケーションは存在しなかった。
findings.explanation: Kazusa's teachers ignored her like a roadside stone, while classmates who knew the rumors treated her like a sore spot—warily, as though walking on eggshells around something that must not be touched. 'Like a pest' instead says they regarded her as vermin or a nuisance, changing the form of her isolation.
findings.japanese:
事情を知っていた教師は路傍の石のように、
そして噂を聞いていたクラスメイトは腫れ物のように扱い、
そこに血の通ったコミュニケーションは存在しなかった。
findings.todokanai: The teachers who knew of her circumstances treated her like a stone on the roadside, and her classmates who heard rumors about her treated her like a pest. No authentic communication existed between them.

findings.highlight: I'll make Setsuna upset if I make you do this.
findings.evidenceJa: 「いいんだって…そんなことさせたら、雪菜に悪いよ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says allowing Haruki to stay and hold her hand would be wrong or unfair to Setsuna. The English reduces that moral recognition to the possibility that Setsuna will become upset, changing an ethical boundary into reaction management.
findings.japanese:
「いいんだって…
そんなことさせたら、雪菜に悪いよ」
findings.todokanai: "I said it's okay… I'll make Setsuna upset if I make you do this."

findings.highlight: my own emptied lunch plate
findings.evidenceJa: 目の前の、綺麗に平らげたランチプレート
findings.explanation: Haruki is looking at Youko's completely cleared lunch plate as evidence of her forced performance. The translation makes the plate his own, reversing the observed eater and breaking the setup for her condition.
findings.japanese:
目の前の、綺麗に平らげたランチプレートを見ながら、
俺も少しだけ、彼と同じ表情をしてみせる。
findings.todokanai: Looking at my own emptied lunch plate in front of me, I make the same expression as him.

findings.highlight: only had to take out the IV from her hand
findings.evidenceJa: 腕から点滴の管を引き抜いたところだった
findings.explanation: The IV tube had just been pulled from Youko's arm when Haruki arrived. The translation relocates it to her hand and makes removal a remaining task rather than a just-completed action.
findings.japanese:
俺が病院に迎えに行ったとき、
曜子さんはちょうど午前の診察を終え、
腕から点滴の管を引き抜いたところだった。
findings.todokanai: When I went to pick Youko-san up from the hospital, she was just about done with her medical checkup, and only had to take out the IV from her hand.

findings.highlight: just discovered a bottle of morphine
findings.evidenceJa: 末期ガンの患者がとうとうモルヒネに手を出した感じ
findings.explanation: Youko likens herself to a terminal patient who has finally resorted to morphine: a deliberate last-resort act in a dependency metaphor. Merely discovering a bottle removes that choice and the sense of crossing a threshold.
findings.japanese:
「正直で、面白くて、そして危険なコね。
…ちょっと自分のしたことにビビったかも。
末期ガンの患者がとうとうモルヒネに手を出した感じ」
findings.todokanai: "You're an honest, funny and dangerous child… I might even feel a bit scared of what I just did. I feel like a patient with terminal cancer who just discovered a bottle of morphine."

findings.highlight: you have courage
findings.evidenceJa: あなたは勇気がありすぎる
findings.explanation: Youko says Haruki has too much courage, continuing her warning that his persistence is dangerous. The translation turns excessive courage into unqualified praise.
findings.japanese:
「わたしには全然そうは思えない。
だって、あなたは勇気がありすぎる」
findings.todokanai: "I don't think so at all. After all, you have courage."

findings.highlight: If you've hesitated many times before reaching the top of the cliff. If you've been pushed forward
findings.evidenceJa: 何度も逡巡して呼び出した崖の上だからこそ。葛藤に葛藤を重ねて押した背中だからこそ
findings.explanation: The omitted subject is Youko: she hesitated repeatedly before calling Haruki to the cliff, then pushed his back only after conflict upon conflict. The translation makes Haruki reach the top and be pushed there, reversing both agency and action.
findings.japanese:
何度も逡巡して呼び出した崖の上だからこそ。
葛藤に葛藤を重ねて押した背中だからこそ。
findings.todokanai: If you've hesitated many times before reaching the top of the cliff. If you've been pushed forward toward the top through conflict after conflict…

findings.highlight: it's that very trouble that reaches out its hand toward you
findings.evidenceJa: 崖下に落ちていく俺に手を差し伸べようとする葛藤は、押したときの何倍も抱えているに違いない
findings.explanation: Haruki infers that Youko must now feel many times more conflict trying to reach toward the falling man than she felt when pushing him. The translation turns abstract 'trouble' into the acting hand and loses Youko, the comparison, and the magnitude of her conflict.
findings.japanese:
崖下に落ちていく俺に手を差し伸べようとする葛藤は、
押したときの何倍も抱えているに違いない。
findings.todokanai: Then it's that very trouble that reaches out its hand toward you when you fall off, with much more strength than it had when it pushed you forward.

findings.highlight: as if we're both guilty parties in some war crime
findings.evidenceJa: 一緒に悪事を働いた戦友にして戦犯同士のような
findings.explanation: Their solidarity is deliberately double-edged: comrades-in-arms who committed the wrongdoing together and fellow war criminals. The translation retains only shared guilt and drops the comradely half of the bond.
findings.japanese:
俺たちには、
一緒に悪事を働いた戦友にして戦犯同士のような、
奇妙な連帯感が生まれていた。
findings.todokanai: A weird feeling of solidarity grows between us, as if we're both guilty parties in some war crime.

findings.highlight: I'm full.
findings.evidenceJa: ごちそうさま
findings.explanation: Youko ends the meal with the conventional ごちそうさま, not a claim that she is satiated. This matters because more than half remains and the scene has established that nausea, not fullness, stopped her.
findings.japanese:
「…もういい。
ごちそうさま」
findings.todokanai: "…That's enough. I'm full."

findings.highlight: No one ever trusts me.
findings.evidenceJa: 信用ないんだな、あたし
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that she has no credibility with Haruki in this exchange. The translation turns that relational complaint into an absolute claim that nobody ever trusts her.
findings.japanese: 「信用ないんだな、あたし」
findings.todokanai: "No one ever trusts me."

findings.highlight: thanks to you not worrying about it
findings.evidenceJa: 特別に心配しなかったせいでお前は
findings.explanation: Haruki blames himself: because he did not worry especially last time, Kazusa ended up harmed. The translation blames Kazusa for not worrying, reversing the subject of his guilt.
findings.japanese: けどあの時、特別に心配しなかったせいでお前は…
findings.todokanai: But thanks to you not worrying about it back then, the result was…

findings.highlight: yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 一昨日
findings.explanation: Kazusa would not let Haruki go the day before yesterday, not yesterday. The one-day shift alters the already tightly specified sequence around her return and recovery.
findings.japanese:
一昨日は離してくれなかったのに、
今日はあまりにも素っ気なく突き放そうとする。
findings.todokanai: She wouldn't let go of me yesterday, yet today she's being uncomfortably blunt about throwing me out.

findings.highlight: Having you around against my will
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌々側にいられても迷惑なだけだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says it is no help if Haruki stays beside her unwillingly; the reluctance she imagines is his. The translation makes his presence violate her will, reversing whose unwillingness motivates the complaint.
findings.japanese:
「それが余計なお世話だって言うんだ。
こっちだって、嫌々側にいられても迷惑なだけだ。
さっさと雪菜のもとに帰れよ！」
findings.todokanai: "I'm telling you that I don't want that. Having you around against my will is a nuisance for me too. Go to where Setsuna is already!"

findings.highlight: You were talking to Setsuna
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜と、繋がってたんだろ
findings.explanation: Kazusa accuses Haruki of remaining connected to Setsuna before her eyes, even through unanswered emails. 'Talking to Setsuna' makes the contact sound reciprocal and conversational when the next lines stress that no replies came.
findings.japanese:
「いつもいつも、ここで打ってただろ？
雪菜と、繋がってたんだろ？
…あたしの、目の前で」
findings.todokanai: "You were typing them all the time here, weren't you? You were talking to Setsuna… right in front of me."

findings.highlight: my only friend in the whole world
findings.evidenceJa: 世界で一人きりの、あたしの肉親
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Youko her only blood relative in the world. The translation replaces this unique family bond with friendship, obscuring why being kept from her mother is intolerable.
findings.japanese:
「どうして駄目なんだよ…
あの人は、世界で一人きりの、あたしの肉親なんだぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "Why can't I…? She's my only friend in the whole world, you know?"

findings.highlight: these upcoming days
findings.evidenceJa: ここ数日ものすごく忙しい
findings.explanation: Haruki says Youko has been extremely busy over the past or recent few days. The translation shifts the workload into the future, weakening his improvised explanation for her present absence.
findings.japanese:
「曜子さん、ここ数日ものすごく忙しいんだよ！
だからさ、今だけは手を患わせたりするなよ」
findings.todokanai: "Youko-san is really busy these upcoming days! That's why you shouldn't cause her trouble."

findings.highlight: holding Youko-san down
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が曜子さんを抑え込んでる。彼女の反対を押し切って
findings.explanation: Haruki means that he is overruling or restraining Youko's opposition, as the next sentence explicitly clarifies. 'Holding Youko-san down' physicalizes the control and can falsely suggest bodily force.
findings.japanese:
本当は、俺が曜子さんを抑え込んでる。
彼女の反対を押し切って、かずさの側にいる。
findings.todokanai: The truth is, I'm the one holding Youko-san down. I'm by Kazusa's side despite her objections.

findings.highlight: tricked her with lukewarm crocodile tears
findings.evidenceJa: 生温い憂いと猫なで声で欺き続ける
findings.explanation: Haruki condemns himself for deceiving Setsuna with lukewarm concern or melancholy and a coaxing voice. The translation invents crocodile tears, drops the vocal tactic, and changes how his false tenderness operates.
findings.japanese:
生温い憂いと猫なで声で欺き続ける悪魔の俺に、
また騙され、裏切られているというのに…
findings.todokanai: Even when she was being deceived and betrayed again, by the devil who tricked her with lukewarm crocodile tears.

findings.highlight: work at home to do
findings.evidenceJa: 特命業務で外回りばかり
findings.explanation: Haruki says special assignments have kept him continually out making rounds or field visits. The translation gives him work at home, the opposite location and working pattern.
findings.japanese:
「そうだな…まぁ、
色々と特命業務で外回りばかり…
あ、全部食うなよ？　半分だけだからな？」
findings.todokanai: "I am… Well, I've had tons of special assignments and work at home to do… Ah, don't eat it all. Only half of it, okay?"

findings.highlight: gave Takahiro any hush money
findings.evidenceJa: 孝宏に口止めしてなかったろ
findings.explanation: Takeya says Haruki did not tell Takahiro to keep quiet, then jokes that asking would have been futile. The translation invents a bribe and turns a failed secrecy instruction into payment.
findings.japanese:
「なんてな～。
お前、孝宏に口止めしてなかったろ？
…って、止めたところで無駄なんだけどな」
findings.todokanai: "Just kidding. You never gave Takahiro any hush money… Not that it would stop him from spilling the beans."

findings.highlight: she has done the right thing
findings.evidenceJa: それどころか、正しいことだ
findings.explanation: Haruki says the friends' celebration and the engagement they believe in are not wrong but right. The translation assigns a completed righteous act to Setsuna, changing the subject and action of his self-persuasion.
findings.japanese: それどころか、正しいことだ。
findings.todokanai: Not only that, she has done the right thing.

findings.highlight: desperately running away from me
findings.evidenceJa: 必死で掛け出そうとしていたその背中
findings.explanation: Kazusa is desperately trying or preparing to break into a run when Haruki's call makes her back twitch. The translation makes her already running away, collapsing the hesitation and start of flight.
findings.japanese:
必死で掛け出そうとしていたその背中が、
少しだけ決心が揺るいだように、びくっと震えた。
findings.todokanai: The back of the person desperately running away from me starts to tremble, as if there is a crack in her determination.

findings.highlight: my only two friends in the world
findings.evidenceJa: 世界で二人だけの親友
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Haruki and Setsuna her only two best friends in the world. The translation downgrades 親友 to ordinary friends at the climax of her forced congratulations.
findings.japanese:
「世界で二人だけの親友が、一緒になってさぁ…
最初から、ずっと決まってたことが
とうとう本当に決まっちゃってさぁ…っ」
findings.todokanai: "To see my only two friends in the world get together… To see the thing that was bound to happen from the start finally happen…!"

findings.highlight: tearing off the chains of her anchor
findings.evidenceJa: 自ら防波堤を決壊させる方向へ波を追い込んだ
findings.explanation: Haruki calls himself the breakwater meant to protect Kazusa, then says he drove the waves toward making that very breakwater collapse. The translation replaces the structure with an anchor and invents chains being torn off, losing his image of actively worsening the pressure he was meant to block.
findings.japanese:
それどころか、かずさの感情を強く刺激して、
自ら防波堤を決壊させる方向へ波を追い込んだ。
findings.todokanai: If anything, I fiercely provoked Kazusa's feelings. I was the one responsible for tearing off the chains of her anchor.

findings.highlight: a crime of conscience
findings.evidenceJa: そこで謝るのも確信犯よね
findings.explanation: Youko calls Haruki a 確信犯: he apologizes while knowingly persisting and accepting that the apology will not make him withdraw. 'Crime of conscience' is not the idiom and obscures her criticism of deliberate, unrepentant conduct.
findings.japanese:
「…そこで謝るのも確信犯よね。
わたしが巻き込んだことに文句一つ言わずに」
findings.todokanai: "…Apologizing there is a crime of conscience too. Never once complaining about how I dragged you into this mess."

findings.highlight: I'll administer the same medicine
findings.evidenceJa: 前回と同じ薬を投与しといて。で、目覚めたら僕に直接連絡して
findings.explanation: The doctor instructs another medical worker to administer the same medicine as last time and contact him when Youko wakes. The translation makes him the person who will administer it, contradicting the following request to contact him.
findings.japanese:
「…とりあえず、前回と同じ薬を投与しといて。
で、目覚めたら僕に直接連絡して」
findings.todokanai: "…I'll administer the same medicine as last time for now. Contact me directly once she wakes up."

findings.highlight: You weren't even like this when you were a baby
findings.evidenceJa: あなたが赤ん坊の時だって、こんなことしなかったわよ
findings.explanation: Youko says that even when Kazusa was a baby, she herself never soothed and embraced her like this. The translation says baby Kazusa did not behave like this, reversing the caregiver and destroying Youko's next-line admission that this neglect helped make Kazusa who she is.
findings.japanese:
「まったく…
あなたが赤ん坊の時だって、
こんなことしなかったわよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Jeez… You weren't even like this when you were a baby, you know?"

findings.highlight: deadlines for bachelor's and master's theses
findings.evidenceJa: 卒論発表や修論発表も間近に迫っている
findings.explanation: What is approaching is the undergraduate- and master's-thesis presentation period, explaining activity in the university buildings at night. The translation changes public presentations into manuscript deadlines.
findings.japanese:
それでも、学部棟の窓からいくつか明かりが漏れていて、
試験だけでなく、卒論発表や修論発表も
間近に迫っていることを伺わせる。
findings.todokanai: Despite that, there are still some illuminated windows in the school buildings. They indicate that more than just exams are closing in, but also the deadlines for bachelor's and master's theses.

findings.highlight: once she comes out to the world. That's why I can't knock on her door
findings.evidenceJa: 天照大神の出てきた後の世界を自分の中にイメージできていない。だから今、その扉の前で踊る訳には行かない
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly continues the Heavenly Rock Cave myth: he cannot imagine the world after Amaterasu emerges, so he cannot yet dance before the cave door to entice her out. The translation removes Amaterasu and replaces ritual dance with knocking, erasing the source's sustained mythic analogy.
findings.japanese:
だって俺はまだ、天照大神の出てきた後の世界を
自分の中にイメージできていない。
だから今、その扉の前で踊る訳には行かない。
findings.todokanai: Because I still don't know what will happen once she comes out to the world. That's why I can't knock on her door just yet.

findings.highlight: it might be accurate to call it her final goal as a pianist
findings.evidenceJa: その日がピアニストとしての最終到達点となっても構わないほどに
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines Kazusa pursued the day she surpassed Youko so exclusively that she might not mind even if it became her final destination as a pianist. The translation merely classifies the goal as possibly final, losing her inferred willingness to let everything culminate there.
findings.japanese:
もしかしたら、その日がピアニストとしての
最終到達点となっても構わないほどに、
そこだけ目指してたんだと思う。
findings.todokanai: Her aim was so focused on that specific goal that it might be accurate to call it her final goal as a pianist.

findings.highlight: begged her to stay after she graduated
findings.evidenceJa: 大学に進学してからも泣きつかれるままバイトを続け
findings.explanation: Koharu continued the job after advancing to university because the restaurant pleaded with her. The translation has her continue only after graduating, moving the episode several years and removing the high-school-to-university transition.
findings.japanese:
結局、大学に進学してからも泣きつかれるまま
バイトを続け、いつの間にやら数十人の常連を生み出す
看板娘になっていたっけ。
findings.todokanai: Eventually, the other employees begged her to stay after she graduated, which she did. And soon after, she became the poster girl for the restaurant, attracting dozens of repeat customers.

findings.highlight: I don't want to know someone I can't understand
findings.evidenceJa: 自分にとって、わからない人でいて欲しくないから
findings.explanation: Koharu says she does not want Haruki to remain someone she cannot understand, which is why she wants to know him. The translation says she does not want to know such a person, reversing the desire that motivates her intervention.
findings.japanese:
『先輩のことを知るためです。
自分にとって、わからない人でいて欲しくないから』
findings.todokanai: "Because I want to know more about you. I don't want to know someone I can't understand."

findings.highlight: I feel bothered when you act like that
findings.evidenceJa: そういう態度は改めてもらわないと困ります
findings.explanation: Koharu tells Haruki that if he is going to remain near her, she needs him to correct that attitude. The translation turns a characteristic demand that he change into a statement of personal annoyance.
findings.japanese:
『わたしの近くにいる以上、
そういう態度は改めてもらわないと困ります』
findings.todokanai: "Well, I feel bothered when you act like that around me."

findings.highlight: effort, independent of her talent and painful fantasies
findings.evidenceJa: その才能と、夢想混じりの苦しみを伴わない努力だけで上がってきた
findings.explanation: Haruki says Kazusa rose on her talent and effort mixed with fantasy that did not involve suffering. The translation makes the effort independent of her talent and attaches pain to the fantasies, reversing both components of his critical characterization.
findings.japanese:
しかも、そんな普通じゃない現実の中ですら、その才能と、
夢想混じりの苦しみを伴わない努力だけで上がってきた、
正真正銘、純粋培養の天才なんだから。
findings.todokanai: Not only that, even in the unnatural reality she lives in, she still is a true genius who managed to improve through effort, independent of her talent and painful fantasies.

findings.highlight: will depart shortly
findings.evidenceJa: まもなく、一番線御宿行きが参ります
findings.explanation: The Onjuku-bound train is about to arrive at platform one. The translation announces that it will depart, changing the stage of the station sequence before the later platform-two departure.
findings.japanese:
「まもなく、一番線御宿行きが参ります。
白線の内側までお下がりください」
findings.todokanai: "The train on Line 1 toward Onjuku will depart shortly. Please stay within the white lines."

findings.highlight: All because of a nobody like me.
findings.evidenceJa: 誰でもない、俺のせいで
findings.explanation: 誰でもない means nobody else: Haruki assigns himself sole responsibility for Kazusa's collapse. The translation misreads it as Haruki calling himself an insignificant nobody, losing the all-exclusive causal claim.
findings.japanese:
あいつは、積み上げてきたものを全て失って、
根元からぽきりと折れてしまったんだから。
…誰でもない、俺のせいで。
findings.todokanai: She has broken down at her very foundation, losing everything she built up… All because of a nobody like me.

findings.highlight: feign strength despite her weak heart
findings.evidenceJa: 弱い心のまま、強い力を振り回し
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines Kazusa retaining a weak heart while wielding her genuinely great power recklessly enough to destroy an ordinary world. The translation says she only pretends to be strong, removing the dangerous mismatch between real ability and emotional weakness.
findings.japanese:
そうして、周囲の期待や家族の思いを全て捨て去り、
弱い心のまま、強い力を振り回し、
普通の世界を壊してしまうという未来は…
findings.todokanai: Will she turn her back on the expectations her surroundings have for her, as well as the feelings of her family? Will she feign strength despite her weak heart and approach a future where any semblance of a normal world would be ruined?

findings.highlight: the same as determining her life for her
findings.evidenceJa: そいつ自身の人生を決断するってことでも
findings.explanation: If someone commands Kazusa's choice, that person must also decide his or her own life. The translation repeats deciding Kazusa's life, losing the reciprocal stake that leads Haruki to become that someone.
findings.japanese:
でもそれって、
そいつ自身の人生を決断するってことでも…
あるんじゃないのか？
findings.todokanai: But wouldn't that be the same as determining her life for her…?

findings.highlight: pretty naive
findings.evidenceJa: 北原って結構ナイーブだよな。傷つきやすくて
findings.explanation: Mari calls Haruki emotionally sensitive or delicate, immediately glossed as easily hurt. Rendering ナイーブ as English 'naive' falsely characterizes him as inexperienced or gullible.
findings.japanese:
『北原って結構ナイーブだよな。
傷つきやすくて、自分で自分を責めてばかりで』
findings.todokanai: "You're pretty naive, aren't you, Kitahara? You're quite fragile, and you always seem to only put the blame on yourself."

findings.highlight: nobody you could ask for forgiveness afterward
findings.evidenceJa: 叱った後、許してくれないから
findings.explanation: Mari asks whether Haruki sinks further because no one scolds him and then forgives him. The translation instead says he lacks someone from whom he can request forgiveness, reversing who performs the absolution and weakening her refusal in the next line.
findings.japanese:
『だから余計落ち込むのか？
誰も、自分を叱ってくれないから。
…叱った後、許してくれないから』
findings.todokanai: "Is that why you got so depressed? Because there was nobody to reprimand you for it? Because there was nobody you could ask for forgiveness afterward…?"

findings.highlight: I'm thoroughly connected to every corner of it
findings.evidenceJa: その世界の隅々まで繋がろうと手を伸ばしてる
findings.explanation: Haruki is reaching outward, trying to connect with every corner of his small social world. The translation declares him already thoroughly connected, turning ongoing effort and openness into completed social mastery.
findings.japanese:
かずさのそれとは似ても似つかない小さな世界だけど、
その世界の隅々まで繋がろうと手を伸ばしてる。
findings.todokanai: My world may be a small one that bears no resemblance to Kazusa's world, but I'm thoroughly connected to every corner of it.

findings.highlight: pass the night walking around in circles
findings.evidenceJa: いつまでも堂々巡りを繰り返し、今日という日をやり過ごそうとしていた
findings.explanation: Haruki was repeating the same circular reasoning and trying to ride out this decisive day without choosing. The translation turns the mental loop into literal walking and narrows the evaded day to the night.
findings.japanese:
そうやって、いつまでも堂々巡りを繰り返し、
今日という日をやり過ごそうとしていた俺を…
findings.todokanai: As I was trying to pass the night walking around in circles as I was…

findings.highlight: The snow seeps through me.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪が、滲む
findings.explanation: The snow blurs in Haruki's vision as pain reaches the corners of his eyes. The translation treats 滲む as the snow physically seeping through him and loses the onset of tears.
findings.japanese: 雪が、滲む。
findings.todokanai: The snow seeps through me.

findings.highlight: assaults me from within
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の目頭までも襲ってきたから
findings.explanation: The pain attacks even the inner corners of Haruki's eyes, explaining why the snow blurs through tears. The translation omits the eyes and substitutes an unspecific internal assault.
findings.japanese:
体も心も掻き毟らんばかりの痛みが、
俺の目頭までも襲ってきたから。
findings.todokanai: A pain intense enough to tear off my heart and tear my body apart assaults me from within.

findings.highlight: And now, half a year later
findings.evidenceJa: 今、俺達は半年後のジューンブライドに向けて
findings.explanation: Haruki and Setsuna are now preparing for a June wedding six months in the future. The translation says they are already half a year later, reversing the planning horizon and confusing the one-year epilogue chronology.
findings.japanese:
そして今、俺達は半年後のジューンブライドに向けて、
様々な準備や契約や打ち合わせに追われている。
findings.todokanai: And now, half a year later, we're signing contracts and making lots of different arrangements in regards to the June bride.

findings.highlight: Kazusa's fame came to an abrupt end among the Japanese mass media
findings.evidenceJa: かずさは日本のマスコミから忽然とその姿を消した
findings.explanation: Kazusa abruptly disappeared from Japanese media coverage after the night of separation. The source does not say her fame ended; converting absence from domestic press into loss of fame overstates what is known about her career and status.
findings.japanese:
あの、俺達の決別の夜以来、
かずさは日本のマスコミから忽然とその姿を消した。
findings.todokanai: Ever since that night when we bade each other farewell, Kazusa's fame came to an abrupt end among the Japanese mass media.

findings.highlight: you can just have me removed on the spot
findings.evidenceJa: もし嘘だったらそのまま俺を突き出せばいい
findings.explanation: Haruki offers to have the hotel hand him directly over to the police if he is lying. 'Removed on the spot' reduces this acceptance of arrest and criminal consequences to ordinary ejection from the hotel.
findings.japanese:
「ああもう…いいです、俺が勝手にやります！
あなたは警察でも何でも呼んでてください。
もし嘘だったらそのまま俺を突き出せばいいでしょ！」
findings.todokanai: "Fine, then! I'll do it on my own. You can go ahead and call the police. If it turns out I'm lying, you can just have me removed on the spot."

findings.highlight: dozens of minutes
findings.evidenceJa: 不毛な交渉をすること十数分
findings.explanation: Haruki has argued with the front desk for more than ten minutes, a duration in the teens. 'Dozens of minutes' requires at least twenty and inflates the tightly timed emergency negotiation.
findings.japanese:
規則を盾に、電話取り次ぎ以上をしてくれないフロントと
不毛な交渉をすること十数分…
findings.todokanai: I spent dozens of minutes having a fruitless exchange with the front desk employee, who told me that the rules meant that giving her a phone call on my behalf was the best they could do.

findings.highlight: their doubts were still very strong
findings.evidenceJa: まだ、９対１くらいで疑惑の方が強かった
findings.explanation: The staff's mental balance is explicitly about nine parts suspicion to one part belief, establishing how slightly cooperation has begun. The translation removes the ratio and with it the measurable starting point for the later change.
findings.japanese: それでもまだ、９対１くらいで疑惑の方が強かった。
findings.todokanai: However, their doubts were still very strong.

findings.highlight: Her "farewell" wasn't as profound in meaning as I had thought.
findings.evidenceJa: 『さよなら』なんて意味深な電話は、もちろん、かかってきてない
findings.explanation: Haruki admits that no ominous 'farewell' phone call came at all; he invented it to force hotel cooperation. The translation says a farewell occurred but was less profound than he thought, erasing the reveal that his specific evidence was a lie.
findings.japanese:
『さよなら』なんて意味深な電話は、
もちろん、かかってきてないけどな。
findings.todokanai: Her "farewell" wasn't as profound in meaning as I had thought.

findings.highlight: It's not like we… have nothing to talk about.
findings.evidenceJa: 別に…話すことなんかない
findings.explanation: Kazusa says they have nothing in particular to talk about while continuing to follow him. The English double negative means that they do have something to discuss, reversing her verbal refusal and weakening the word-action contrast.
findings.japanese: 「別に…話すことなんかない」
findings.todokanai: "It's not like we… have nothing to talk about."

findings.highlight: she lines up perfectly next to me
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の隣にぴったりと身体を寄せて
findings.explanation: Kazusa finally presses her body snugly against Haruki's side for warmth. Merely lining up beside him removes the physical contact that contradicts her rejection and marks escalating proximity.
findings.japanese: ついには、俺の隣にぴったりと身体を寄せて。
findings.todokanai: At last, she lines up perfectly next to me.

findings.highlight: how I forced you out here tonight
findings.evidenceJa: さっきみたいに、無茶な手を使って押しかけて
findings.explanation: Haruki says he barged in on Youko using reckless methods, just as he has forced his way to Kazusa's hotel door. He did not force Kazusa outside; she opened the door and then followed him, so the translation invents coercion and assigns the wrong target.
findings.japanese:
「俺が強引に聞き出したんだよ。
さっきみたいに、無茶な手を使って押しかけて…」
findings.todokanai: "I practically forced it out of her. Just like how I forced you out here tonight."

findings.highlight: That one unbelievable delusion that could never come true.
findings.evidenceJa: 一番ありえないはずの妄想が
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Kazusa's enduring love the delusion that should have been the least possible, before saying Kazusa herself affirmed it. 'Could never come true' asserts ongoing impossibility even though the next line says the proposition has just been confirmed.
findings.japanese:
そんな、俺にとって夢みたいな、
一番ありえないはずの妄想が…
findings.todokanai: That dream-like reality. That one unbelievable delusion that could never come true.

findings.highlight: Even if nothing happens to cause her harm
findings.evidenceJa: 自分で自分に手を下すことはなくても
findings.explanation: Haruki distinguishes Kazusa not actively laying hands on herself from still decaying into the same outcome through helplessness. The translation removes her agency and self-harm reference, turning it into the much broader condition that no harmful event occurs.
findings.japanese:
自分で自分に手を下すことはなくても、
結果として、そうなってしまってもおかしくない、
そんな、弱すぎる奴。
findings.todokanai: Even if nothing happens to cause her harm, it wouldn't surprise me if she still ended up that way. That's how weak she is.

findings.highlight: your inability to see anything through
findings.evidenceJa: 性格も、態度も、そして諦めも
findings.explanation: 悪い distributes across personality, attitude, and 諦め: Kazusa is bad at giving up, with a pointed implication that she has not relinquished Haruki. The translation makes her unable to see things through, the opposite persistence trait.
findings.japanese:
「しかも悪い女だ。性格も、態度も、そして諦めも。
お前のいいところなんて
見た目とピアノの腕だけじゃないか！」
findings.todokanai: "And you're a bad person too. Your personality, your attitude, and your inability to see anything through. The only things you have going for you are your looks and your piano!"

findings.highlight: On top of being talented, you stubbornly refuse to fit in with the rest of society. You're left with almost no social skills whatsoever
findings.evidenceJa: 才能の上にあぐらをかいて、社会と馴染もうとしない、人としては、本当に未熟な奴
findings.explanation: Haruki accuses Kazusa of resting complacently on her talent, making no attempt to fit into society, and being truly immature as a person. The translation removes complacency and reduces broad personal immaturity to a lack of social skills.
findings.japanese:
「だから、お前みたいな奴は世界に弾かれて当然なんだ。
才能の上にあぐらをかいて、社会と馴染もうとしない、
人としては、本当に未熟な奴だから…」
findings.todokanai: "That's why people like you struggle so much! On top of being talented, you stubbornly refuse to fit in with the rest of society. You're left with almost no social skills whatsoever…"

findings.highlight: I can't bear seeing you unhappy!
findings.evidenceJa: お前が幸せに生きてくれないと嫌なんだ
findings.explanation: Haruki says he needs Kazusa to live a happy life, a future-oriented wish that motivates his decision to sustain her. The translation makes it only an inability to witness her present unhappiness and drops the crucial verb 'live.'
findings.japanese: 「お前が幸せに生きてくれないと嫌なんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I can't bear seeing you unhappy!"

findings.highlight: cast doubt on any future performance being held
findings.evidenceJa: 次回公演の開催が危ぶまれている
findings.explanation: The report says Kazusa's next performance, the scheduled additional concert, is in jeopardy. 'Any future performance' expands one endangered event into doubt about her entire future performing career.
findings.japanese:
「実は現在、深刻な体調不良ということで
次回公演の開催が危ぶまれていることが、
関係者の話で明らかになりました」
findings.todokanai: "However, recent statements made by related sources have cast doubt on any future performance being held, due to poor health."

findings.highlight: Thus, it is likely that her health has indeed deteriorated
findings.evidenceJa: 前回のコンサートの後に体調不良を訴え、現在は都内の病院で療養していると言うんですね
findings.explanation: The broadcaster relays the story that Kazusa complained of poor health after the concert and is recuperating in a Tokyo hospital. The translation converts the manufactured report into the announcer's evidential conclusion that her health likely did deteriorate, while dropping her reported complaint.
findings.japanese:
「実は、前回のコンサートの後に体調不良を訴え、
現在は都内の病院で療養していると言うんですね」
findings.todokanai: "Thus, it is likely that her health has indeed deteriorated since the previous concert, and that she is currently recuperating in a hospital somewhere within the Metropolitan Area."

findings.highlight: She's still not focusing on her piano practice
findings.evidenceJa: 相変わらずピアノに向かおうとしません
findings.explanation: Kazusa still will not even go to or face the piano, behavior that supports the possibility of abandoning her artistic identity. 'Not focusing on practice' reduces active avoidance to poor concentration.
findings.japanese:
「相変わらずピアノに向かおうとしません。
時々外出はしてるみたいですけど、
周囲を散歩する程度みたいで…」
findings.todokanai: "She's still not focusing on her piano practice. Sometimes I see her walking outside, but it never seems like she's doing anything more than just wandering aimlessly."

findings.highlight: in a bad mood
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱり落ち込んでる？
findings.explanation: Youko asks whether Kazusa is depressed or deeply dejected. 'In a bad mood' suggests irritability and trivializes the emotional-risk assessment that follows.
findings.japanese: 「やっぱり落ち込んでる？」
findings.todokanai: "You think she's in a bad mood?"

findings.highlight: feeling a bit overwhelmed
findings.evidenceJa: まさか変なふうに思い詰めたりとか
findings.explanation: Miyoko worries that Kazusa may brood herself into a dangerous extreme, euphemistically raising possible self-harm. 'A bit overwhelmed' removes both the intensity and the safety concern answered by Youko's statement that Kazusa will not stop being human.
findings.japanese:
「社長、かずささん、本当に大丈夫でしょうか？
まさか変なふうに思い詰めたりとか…」
findings.todokanai: "President, do you really think she's okay? You don't think she's feeling a bit overwhelmed?"

findings.highlight: Being famous can come with a lot of hardships
findings.evidenceJa: けど芸術家って色々と
findings.explanation: Miyoko worries specifically about artists and their propensity for extremes, not the burden of fame. The substitution breaks Youko's coming distinction between remaining a person and ceasing to be an artist.
findings.japanese:
「ほ、本当にそうでしょうか？
けど芸術家って色々と…」
findings.todokanai: "A-Are you sure? Being famous can come with a lot of hardships…"

findings.highlight: giving up on being famous
findings.evidenceJa: 芸術家ってのの方をやめる可能性
findings.explanation: Youko allows that Kazusa may cease being an artist, a possible abandonment of vocation and artistic self. The translation makes it merely relinquishing fame, which could happen while she continued as a musician.
findings.japanese:
「だから、何があっても人であることはやめないわよ。
ただ、芸術家ってのの方をやめる可能性は…」
findings.todokanai: "So you shouldn't worry about her giving up on life. I can't say the same about her giving up on being famous, however."

findings.highlight: The moment you made your decision, I started working
findings.evidenceJa: 社長が決断した瞬間に、すぐに各方面が動けるように手配しています
findings.explanation: Miyoko has made advance arrangements so every party can move the instant Youko decides. The translation says the decision already happened and Miyoko only then began work, reversing preparedness into reaction and prematurely resolving the concert choice.
findings.japanese:
「社長が決断した瞬間に、
すぐに各方面が動けるように手配しています。
損害も最小限に抑えられるように手を打ちました」
findings.todokanai: "The moment you made your decision, I started working on everything on all sides, minimizing the possible damage."

findings.highlight: I'm… not that famous.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな有名人なんかじゃない
findings.explanation: Kazusa rejects the category of celebrity altogether, leading to her insistence that Touma Kazusa is an ordinary Japanese person. 'Not that famous' accepts celebrity as a matter of lesser degree and weakens the identity refusal.
findings.japanese:
「あたし…
そんな有名人なんかじゃない」
findings.todokanai: "I'm… not that famous."

findings.highlight: I'll get the first draft finished today
findings.evidenceJa: 今日中に初校上がります
findings.explanation: The first proofs will be ready today, meaning the manuscript has already progressed through composition into proofing. Calling this a first draft moves the special issue much earlier in production and undercuts why coworkers find his speed abnormal.
findings.japanese:
「今日中に初校上がります。
週末にはこっちの作業は全部終わる予定です」
findings.todokanai: "I'll get the first draft finished today. As things stand right now, everything should be done by the weekend."

findings.highlight: wait for the revision and compilation work to finish… as well as the supervisors' and editors' post-scripts
findings.evidenceJa: あとは修正作業と、編プロの方の原稿待ちと監修と…それに編集後記だけ
findings.explanation: The remaining items are correction work, waiting for manuscripts from the editorial production company, supervision or fact-checking, and the editor's afterword. The translation turns tasks into things merely awaited and combines supervisors and editors into authors of multiple postscripts.
findings.japanese:
「あとは修正作業と、編プロの方の原稿待ちと監修と
…それに編集後記だけです」
findings.todokanai: "All that's left now is to wait for the revision and compilation work to finish… as well as the supervisors' and editors' post-scripts."

findings.highlight: I feel like I might wake up from this dream
findings.evidenceJa: すぐに夢から覚めてしまうから
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will immediately wake from the dream and be forced to realize it cannot happen. 'Might' weakens the certainty that makes Haruki's impossible promise cruel.
findings.japanese:
「すぐに夢から覚めてしまうからだよ…
そんなことできるわけないって、
思い知らされてしまうからだよ」
findings.todokanai: "It's because I feel like I might wake up from this dream… I'll wake up and be reminded that this could never happen."

findings.highlight: await us on this path
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちを襲い、覆い、のしかかっていく
findings.explanation: Despair, dark clouds, and pressure are already attacking, covering, and weighing down on them as their promises intensify. The translation relocates these forces into what awaits in the future, losing the immediate emotional freezing of the scene.
findings.japanese:
ただ、絶望と、暗雲と、重圧が、
俺たちを襲い、覆い、のしかかっていく。
findings.todokanai: Only despair, enveloping dark clouds, and unimaginable pressure await us on this path.

findings.highlight: for a short while, but then immediately understands
findings.evidenceJa: ほんの少しだけ思い違いをしてた。そして、そのことに今、やっと気がついた
findings.explanation: Kazusa was mistaken only in one small respect and has only now finally realized it. The translation makes the misunderstanding brief in duration and the realization immediate, reversing both modifiers.
findings.japanese:
かずさは、ほんの少しだけ思い違いをしてた。
そして、そのことに今、やっと気がついた。
findings.todokanai: Kazusa got the wrong idea for a short while, but then immediately understands.

findings.highlight: the person who has loved you so earnestly for five years
findings.evidenceJa: 五年間もずっと愛してきた相手を捨ててしまったら
findings.explanation: Kazusa warns Haruki about abandoning the person he has loved continuously for five years: Setsuna. The translation makes Setsuna the one who has loved Haruki, reversing the subject and weakening Kazusa's insistence that his own love remains.
findings.japanese:
「だから、そんなことしてしまったら…
五年間もずっと愛してきた相手を捨ててしまったら…
お前、一生後悔して生きていくことになるんだぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "If you do this… If you abandon the person who has loved you so earnestly for five years, you'll regret it for the rest of your life."

findings.highlight: when you betray those you love
findings.evidenceJa: 好きな人を裏切るなら
findings.explanation: Haruki says that if Kazusa betrays the person she loves, she must remember it. The singular retains a pressured ambiguity between rejecting Haruki and accepting him at Setsuna's expense; plural 'those' dissolves that focused choice.
findings.japanese:
「だからせめて…
自分の選択で後悔するんだ。
好きな人を裏切るなら、そのことを覚えておくんだ」
findings.todokanai: "That's why at least… Your regret should be of your own choice. That when you betray those you love, you'll remember that."

findings.highlight: one filled with greater happiness
findings.evidenceJa: 今よりもう少しだけ、幸せになるか
findings.explanation: Accepting Haruki means suffering more than now in exchange for becoming only a little happier than now. The translation promises broadly 'greater happiness,' losing the deliberately meager, asymmetrical gain.
findings.japanese:
「今のまま、辛いまま必死で生きていくか…
今よりもっと辛い思いをして、
そして、今よりもう少しだけ、幸せになるか…」
findings.todokanai: "Will you decide to continue living in despair as you are now? Or will you choose to live a life filled with greater pain, but also one filled with greater happiness?"

findings.highlight: My bad, let's go.
findings.evidenceJa: 悪いな、それじゃ行ってくる
findings.explanation: Oda apologizes and says 'I'm off; I'll be back,' setting up the other traveler's question about whether he can really return. The translation changes the singular departure into a group suggestion and drops the return implication.
findings.japanese: 「悪いな、それじゃ行ってくる」
findings.todokanai: "My bad, let's go."

findings.highlight: why do you keep saying that you can't make it? At least say that you might be late
findings.evidenceJa: 行けないかもとか、遅刻するかもとか
findings.explanation: Takeya complains that Haruki keeps hedging both that he may be unable to come and that he may be late. The translation turns the second hedge into advice Takeya prefers, reversing the list of excuses.
findings.japanese:
「なのに、何さっきからグダグダ言ってんだよ？
行けないかもとか、遅刻するかもとか…」
findings.todokanai: "So why do you keep saying that you can't make it? At least say that you might be late…"

findings.highlight: entrusted me with the front page
findings.evidenceJa: メインで任されたの今回が初めて
findings.explanation: This is Haruki's first time being entrusted with primary responsibility for the project or issue. The source says nothing about a front page; the translation invents a specific page assignment.
findings.japanese:
「そうも行かないんだよ…
メインで任されたの今回が初めてなんだし」
findings.todokanai: "I can't do that either… This is the first time they've entrusted me with the front page."

findings.highlight: your voice is getting drowned out
findings.evidenceJa: お前の声が消え入りそうなだけか？周りの音はよく聞こえるしな
findings.explanation: Takeya observes that Haruki's voice itself sounds ready to fade away, especially because surrounding sounds are audible clearly. 'Drowned out' blames the surroundings that the source uses to rule out a bad connection and diagnose Haruki's weakness.
findings.japanese:
「それとも、お前の声が消え入りそうなだけか？
周りの音はよく聞こえるしな」
findings.todokanai: "Or perhaps it's just that your voice is getting drowned out. I can hear your surroundings."

findings.highlight: I have to get off the train.
findings.evidenceJa: 電車出るから、切るな
findings.explanation: Haruki says the train is departing, so he is ending the call; the next narration has him jump through the doors before they close. The translation says he must get off, the opposite movement.
findings.japanese: 「あ、悪い…電車出るから、切るな」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, sorry… I have to get off the train. I'm hanging up."

findings.highlight: normally I wouldn't even go home today
findings.evidenceJa: 予定通りならそのまま帰るわけにはいかない
findings.explanation: This is his first pre-midnight return of the week, but if tonight proceeds according to plan he cannot go straight home because he must attend Setsuna's party. The translation turns that one planned detour into a general norm of not going home.
findings.japanese:
今週初めての、日付が変わる前の帰宅。
…いや、予定通りならそのまま帰るわけにはいかない。
findings.todokanai: This week is the first time I'm able to go home before midnight… No, normally I wouldn't even go home today.

findings.highlight: It would usually take me a station's travel from Minami-Suetsugu to Suetsugu-chou
findings.evidenceJa: いつもの南末次から一駅乗り越して、末次町で降りて
findings.explanation: Haruki rides one station past his usual stop, Minami-Suetsugu, gets off at Suetsugucho, then walks fifteen minutes. The translation makes travel between the two stations his usual route and loses the meaningful act of passing his normal stop.
findings.japanese:
いつもの南末次から一駅乗り越して、
末次町で降りてそこから徒歩１５分。
findings.todokanai: It would usually take me a station's travel from Minami-Suetsugu to Suetsugu-chou, after which I'd need to take a fifteen-minute walk.

findings.highlight: I head toward Setsuna's house
findings.evidenceJa: 結論の出ないまま雪菜と逢瀬を重ねる日
findings.explanation: This is the day Haruki will add another romantic rendezvous with Setsuna while his decision with Kazusa remains unresolved. The translation reduces that ethically charged repetition to the destination of Setsuna's house.
findings.japanese:
追加公演まで、あと二週間。
そして今日は、結論の出ないまま雪菜と逢瀬を重ねる日。
findings.todokanai: Her next concert is in two weeks. And today, having still not heard any decision from Kazusa, I head toward Setsuna's house.

findings.highlight: regretting your choice, like I said you would
findings.evidenceJa: この前あたしに言ったこと、後悔してるみたいだぞ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki looks as though he regrets what he told her the other day. The translation makes the relevant prior speech Kazusa's prediction and labels Haruki's statement a choice, reversing who said what.
findings.japanese:
「なんだよ、その顔…
まるでこの前あたしに言ったこと、
後悔してるみたいだぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "Why are you looking at me like that? It's almost like you're regretting your choice, like I said you would."

findings.highlight: the pain everyone else would feel from my foolish choice
findings.evidenceJa: 周りがみんな壊れてしまうときの辛さ
findings.explanation: Kazusa compares her own separation pain with the pain she would feel when everyone around her is destroyed by her foolish decision. The translation assigns the latter pain to everyone else, changing the emotional comparison she made at the airport.
findings.japanese:
「そして、比べてみたんだ。
あたしの馬鹿な決断で、
周りがみんな壊れてしまうときの辛さとさ」
findings.todokanai: "And I tried to compare it to the pain everyone else would feel from my foolish choice."

findings.highlight: signed a contract in the depths of hell
findings.evidenceJa: 悪魔との騙しあいに。地獄の裏取引に
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks he has won at mutual deception with a devil and at an under-the-table bargain in hell. The translation says a contract has already been signed, preempting the actual blood contract that occurs only after the finger bite.
findings.japanese:
悪魔との騙しあいに。
地獄の裏取引に。
findings.todokanai: I've won this game of deception with the devil, and signed a contract in the depths of hell.

findings.highlight: we exchanged our vows in each other's embrace
findings.evidenceJa: 抱き合い、この場で唇を重ねてもおかしくないほどの誓いを交わした
findings.explanation: They exchanged vows intense enough that embracing and kissing on the spot would not have been surprising. The translation says they exchanged them while already embracing, contradicting the next line's insistence that they do not move closer and only finger and lips meet.
findings.japanese:
瞬間…
抱き合い、この場で唇を重ねてもおかしくないほどの
誓いを交わした俺たちは…
findings.todokanai: At that moment… we exchanged our vows in each other's embrace, and the natural next step would have been to share a passionate kiss…

findings.highlight: From now on… you belong to me.
findings.evidenceJa: これでお前は………あたしのものだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says 'with this'—the bite and swallowed blood make Haruki hers in her ritual logic. 'From now on' gives only a temporal boundary and loses the act's causal function in the blood contract.
findings.japanese: 「これでお前は………あたしのものだ」
findings.todokanai: "From now on… you belong to me."

findings.highlight: once I reached the transit station, I just collapsed
findings.evidenceJa: この乗り継ぎ駅でほとんど潰してしまった
findings.explanation: Haruki used up nearly all of the more-than-thirty-minute margin he had allowed at the transfer station by missing three trains. The translation says he physically collapsed there, replacing elapsed-time loss with an event that the scene does not report.
findings.japanese:
せっかく待ち合わせ場所に着く時間を逆算して、
３０分以上余裕を持って家を出たのに、
この乗り継ぎ駅でほとんど潰してしまった。
findings.todokanai: I even decided to leave home 30 minutes early to make sure I had time to spare, but once I reached the transit station, I just collapsed.

findings.highlight: entrusted you with the front page
findings.evidenceJa: 今度の雑誌、メインで任されてるんだって
findings.explanation: Setsuna heard that Haruki was given primary responsibility for the coming magazine or special issue. The translation again invents a front-page assignment rather than project leadership.
findings.japanese:
『それに、武也君から聞いたよ？
今度の雑誌、メインで任されてるんだって？』
findings.todokanai: "I also heard from Takeya-kun. Is it really true that they entrusted you with the front page?"

findings.highlight: feel guilty about her, I remember what I am hiding from her
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜に罪悪感を抱くと。雪菜への秘密を思い出すと
findings.explanation: Thinking of Setsuna, caring about her, feeling guilt toward her, and remembering his secret from her are four parallel triggers of Haruki's bodily reaction. The translation makes remembering the secret a result of feeling guilty and removes one branch of the cumulative construction.
findings.japanese:
雪菜を想うと。雪菜を気遣うと。
雪菜に罪悪感を抱くと。
雪菜への秘密を思い出すと…
findings.todokanai: Whenever I think about her, worry about her, feel guilty about her, I remember what I am hiding from her.

findings.highlight: I feel a restlessness in my body and heart.
findings.evidenceJa: 体と心が暴れ出す。肉体と精神の均衡が保てなくなる
findings.explanation: Haruki's body and heart run wild and he can no longer maintain equilibrium between body and mind. 'Restlessness' sharply understates a full functional breakdown that includes severe physical symptoms.
findings.japanese:
体と心が暴れ出す。
肉体と精神の均衡が保てなくなる。
findings.todokanai: I feel a restlessness in my body and heart.

findings.highlight: focus my weary eyes
findings.evidenceJa: かすむ目を必死に凝らして
findings.explanation: Haruki strains to focus eyes whose vision is blurring, another concrete symptom of his attack. 'Weary' changes impaired vision into generic fatigue.
findings.japanese:
それでも俺は、かすむ目を必死に凝らして、
携帯のキーを打ち続ける。
findings.todokanai: Despite that, I focus my weary eyes on the cell phone, and continue typing.

findings.highlight: get my first draft checked
findings.evidenceJa: 初校のチェックを進めて
findings.explanation: Haruki plans to continue checking the first proofs on Monday. The translation again calls 初校 a first draft, moving the project backward from proofing to authoring.
findings.japanese:
そして、できれば月曜からちゃんと出勤して、
初校のチェックを進めて…
findings.todokanai: And if possible, I'll be back to work on Monday, and get my first draft checked…

findings.highlight: we'll be able to continue as a couple for the winter
findings.evidenceJa: この冬の間は恋人同士を続けられるんだろうか
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether postponement might let them remain lovers through the winter, exposing the temptation as uncertain self-questioning. The translation states that they will be able to do so.
findings.japanese:
そして俺たちは何も決断を下さないまま、
この冬の間は恋人同士を続けられるんだろうか…
findings.todokanai: And without settling any matters, we'll be able to continue as a couple for the winter…

findings.highlight: let such a mild punishment make me give up
findings.evidenceJa: こんな甘い罠に負けてどうする
findings.explanation: The sweet or tempting trap is the chance to use illness as an excuse and postpone the breakup. The translation calls his symptoms a mild punishment, losing the seductive escape route he is resisting.
findings.japanese:
こんなことでどうする…
こんな甘い罠に負けてどうする…
findings.todokanai: What purpose would that serve… How can I let such a mild punishment make me give up?

findings.highlight: develop a habit of turning away from that which I need to face
findings.evidenceJa: 立ち向かおうとするたびに拒絶反応なんか起こしてたら
findings.explanation: Haruki fears that every attempt to confront pain will trigger another involuntary rejection reaction like the current bodily attack. The translation makes avoidance a chosen habit and omits the psychosomatic reaction.
findings.japanese:
そうやって辛いことから逃げてたら、
立ち向かおうとするたびに拒絶反応なんか起こしてたら…
findings.todokanai: If I run away from painful encounters now, if I develop a habit of turning away from that which I need to face…

findings.highlight: I'm really not smart enough to understand
findings.evidenceJa: 天才の言うことは難しくてよくわかんないな
findings.explanation: The source presents 天才 with the spoken ruby かあさん: Kazusa mockingly says that what 'Mother/the genius' says is difficult to understand, dodging Youko's professional judgment. The translation instead calls Kazusa unintelligent and loses the expert-mother double role.
findings.japanese: 「天才の言うことは難しくてよくわかんないな」
findings.todokanai: "I'm really not smart enough to understand what that means."

findings.highlight: I suppose the difference is paper thin. I only wanted to try bragging about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 一応、紙一重の方だと自負してるけどね
findings.explanation: After being called an idiot, Youko boasts that she considers herself on the favorable side of the paper-thin line between genius and fool. The translation notes only a thin difference and does not identify the side on which she proudly places herself.
findings.japanese: 「一応、紙一重の方だと自負してるけどね」
findings.todokanai: "I suppose the difference is paper thin. I only wanted to try bragging about it."

findings.highlight: congratulations to you for your first magazine
findings.evidenceJa: 春希くんこそ入稿おめでとう
findings.explanation: Setsuna congratulates Haruki on reaching manuscript submission for the project. She does not call the magazine itself his first magazine; the next phrase separately identifies it as his first major assignment.
findings.japanese:
「春希くんこそ入稿おめでとう。
初めての大仕事、たくさん売れるといいね」
findings.todokanai: "And congratulations to you for your first magazine, Haruki-kun. I hope your first big project sells well."

findings.highlight: I don't want to be reminded of who's paying for it.
findings.evidenceJa: その差額が誰の懐に行くのか考えたくない
findings.explanation: Haruki does not want to think about whose pocket receives the markup between ingredient cost and menu price. The translation asks who pays, reversing the direction of the money and missing the restaurant-margin joke.
findings.japanese:
「今日は食材の原価を推理するのはやめてくれよ。
その差額が誰の懐に行くのか考えたくない」
findings.todokanai: "Stop worrying about the cost of food today. I don't want to be reminded of who's paying for it."

findings.highlight: I forced it out of my body
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の体の変調を無理やり押さえつけた
findings.explanation: Haruki forcibly suppresses the bodily abnormality within thirty minutes so he can proceed. The translation says he expelled it from his body, implying cure rather than controlled containment.
findings.japanese: ３０分で、自分の体の変調を無理やり押さえつけた。
findings.todokanai: In 30 minutes, I forced it out of my body.

findings.highlight: Because I closed it all off in my mind.
findings.evidenceJa: 心に置き場所を作ったから
findings.explanation: Haruki recovers because he creates a place in his heart where Kazusa's expressions can remain and be recalled at will. 'Closed it all off' describes repression, the opposite mechanism, and the translation also drops the explicit absence of nausea from his symptom inventory.
findings.japanese:
今は、頭痛も吐き気も寒気もない。
心に置き場所を作ったから。
findings.todokanai: Right now, I don't have a headache, nor do I feel cold. Because I closed it all off in my mind.

findings.highlight: I naturally accept that she isn't doing any of those things.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺がそうしないことも自然に受け入れる
findings.explanation: Setsuna naturally accepts that Haruki does not initiate handholding, linked arms, or kisses either. The translation makes Haruki accept her restraint, reversing whose accommodating behavior he is observing.
findings.japanese: そして、俺がそうしないことも自然に受け入れる。
findings.todokanai: And I naturally accept that she isn't doing any of those things.

findings.highlight: Is it because it's evening?
findings.evidenceJa: 今が昼間だからなのか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether their physical distance is because it is daytime. The translation says evening, directly contradicting the lunch and shopping chronology before sunset.
findings.japanese:
今が昼間だからなのか、
久しぶりの逢瀬で距離を測りかねてるのか。
findings.todokanai: Is it because it's evening? Is it because we haven't seen each other for so long she doesn't know how to gauge the appropriate distance?

findings.highlight: I can now say with certainty that I love her
findings.evidenceJa: 今でも掛け値なしに、心の底から愛してる
findings.explanation: Haruki says he still loves Setsuna genuinely from the bottom of his heart. 'Can now say' recasts enduring love as a newly acquired certainty and weakens the painful coexistence with his choice of Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
今でも掛け値なしに、
心の底から愛してる。
findings.todokanai: I can now say with certainty that I love her from the bottom of my heart.

findings.highlight: brave enough to pretend to be all those things
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の前ではそうであるよう努力してくれるくらい健気
findings.explanation: Haruki praises Setsuna as devoted and admirable enough to make an effort to remain cheerful and well in front of him. 'Pretend' frames that care as false performance and 'brave' misses the tender self-sacrifice of 健気.
findings.japanese:
いつも明るくて、健やかで。
少なくとも、俺の前ではそうであるよう
努力してくれるくらい健気で。
findings.todokanai: She's always so cheerful, always so energetic. At the very least, she's brave enough to pretend to be all those things when I'm around.

findings.highlight: makes absolutely no attempt to better herself
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を取り繕うことすらしようとしなくて
findings.explanation: Haruki says Kazusa does not even try to put on appearances or smooth over how she presents herself. The translation says she makes no effort to improve as a person, a broader moral judgment already treated separately in the next line.
findings.japanese:
だってあいつは、いつも怒ってて、偏食で、
礼儀知らずで、他人に興味がなくて、
自分を取り繕うことすらしようとしなくて。
findings.todokanai: After all, she's always angry, picky about her food, lacks manners, is unconcerned about others, and makes absolutely no attempt to better herself.

findings.highlight: something you absolutely have to hear
findings.evidenceJa: どうしても言わなくちゃならない、大事な
findings.explanation: Haruki says it is an important thing he absolutely must tell Setsuna. The translation puts the obligation on Setsuna to hear it, changing his moral duty into a demand on the person he is about to hurt.
findings.japanese:
「話があるんだ。
どうしても言わなくちゃならない、大事な…」
findings.todokanai: "I have something to tell you. It's something important, something you absolutely have to hear…"

findings.highlight: She probably had her suspicions of what was happening, she just never had any positive proof
findings.evidenceJa: その可能性に、まるで思い至らない訳じゃなかった。ただ、ずっと確証が持てなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says he had considered the possibility that Setsuna already knew but lacked confirmation until seconds ago. The translation assigns the suspicions and lack of proof to Setsuna, reversing the focalized knower.
findings.japanese:
その可能性に、まるで思い至らない訳じゃなかった。
ただ、ずっと確証が持てなかった。
………ほんの数秒前までは。
findings.todokanai: She probably had her suspicions of what was happening, she just never had any positive proof… up until these last few seconds.

findings.highlight: cut myself off from the one thing we both considered so precious
findings.evidenceJa: 二人にとって一番大事なものを、刃で断ち切ってしまおうとしている
findings.explanation: Haruki is about to cut apart the thing most important to both of them—their bond—with his hidden blade. The translation makes him cut himself off from an object, narrowing mutual destruction into personal separation and making the attempted act sound completed as a choice.
findings.japanese:
俺が、かずさを嵐から護るために、
二人にとって一番大事なものを、
刃で断ち切ってしまおうとしていることが。
findings.todokanai: And she knew that in order to protect Kazusa from this storm, I had chosen to use that dagger to cut myself off from the one thing we both considered so precious.

findings.highlight: the moment we reached the station
findings.evidenceJa: 駅へと急ぐ雪菜の足が止まってしまってから
findings.explanation: Haruki's words stop Setsuna's feet while she is hurrying toward the station. The translation says they reached the station, inventing arrival and altering the midnight return route.
findings.japanese:
俺の容赦ない言葉に、
駅へと急ぐ雪菜の足が止まってしまってから。
findings.todokanai: My heartless words caused Setsuna's feet to halt the moment we reached the station.

findings.highlight: does her utmost to prevent herself from losing her voice
findings.evidenceJa: か細い声をそれでも必死に抑え
findings.explanation: Setsuna desperately suppresses her thin voice while her feelings overflow. The translation says she tries to prevent the voice from being lost, reversing restraint into preservation.
findings.japanese:
肩を震わせ、か細い声をそれでも必死に抑え、
けれど湧き出る感情を抑えきれずに、
小さく、けれど激しく泣き出してしまってから。
findings.todokanai: Her shoulders shudder, and she does her utmost to prevent herself from losing her voice. But she is unable to control her feelings, as she cries quietly, yet intensely.

findings.highlight: I slept with you knowing how much you desired me.
findings.evidenceJa: あなたに求められるままに、身体で繋ぎとめようとした
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that instead of talking, she responded to Haruki's desire by trying to hold him in place with her body. The translation reports sex but removes her active purpose of using bodily intimacy to keep him from Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
「なのにわたし、あなたと話し合わなかった。
それどころか、あなたに求められるままに、
身体で繋ぎとめようとした」
findings.todokanai: "Yet I didn't talk to you about it. Even worse, I slept with you knowing how much you desired me."

findings.highlight: turn into the girl you'll like
findings.evidenceJa: あなたがまた、振り向いてくれる女の子になれない
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she cannot become a girl who will make Haruki turn and look back toward her again. 'You'll like' drops the lost relationship and her plea to regain his attention.
findings.japanese:
「あなたのために、変われないよ…
あなたがまた、振り向いてくれる女の子になれないよ」
findings.todokanai: "…I won't be able to change for your sake… I won't be able to turn into the girl you'll like."

findings.highlight: There's nothing you can do
findings.evidenceJa: 何も、ない
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats that there is nothing wrong with Setsuna—no defect for her to fix. The translation says there is no action she can take, which validates her helplessness rather than answering her question about what she did wrong.
findings.japanese:
「もう一度言う。
何も、ない…」
findings.todokanai: "I'll say it again. There's nothing you can do…"

findings.highlight: the coats of passers-by
findings.evidenceJa: 旅人のコートも
findings.explanation: The image invokes the single traveler's coat from the North Wind fable, with Setsuna's storm unable to dislodge Haruki's decision. Plural passers-by turns the specific fable structure into a generic street scene.
findings.japanese:
旅人のコートも。
そして、俺の決断も。
findings.todokanai: Not the coats of passers-by, nor my determination.

findings.highlight: I have a strong desire to make sure, but what right do I have
findings.evidenceJa: 確かめる術も、その欲求もありながら、俺にはもう、その資格がない
findings.explanation: Haruki has both the means to check on Setsuna—phone, home, Takahiro—and the desire, but judges himself unqualified. The translation drops the available means, making his silence sound practically constrained rather than entirely self-imposed.
findings.japanese:
…確かめる術も、その欲求もありながら、
俺にはもう、その資格がない。
findings.todokanai: …I have a strong desire to make sure, but what right do I have to do that now?

findings.highlight: the path in which very few people have found happiness going down
findings.evidenceJa: 幸せになる人よりも、不幸になる人の方が圧倒的に多い
findings.explanation: Haruki chose an unthinkable outcome that will make overwhelmingly more people unhappy than happy. The translation turns that comparative future consequence into a claim that few past travelers found happiness on a path and never states the number harmed.
findings.japanese:
幸せになる人よりも、
不幸になる人の方が圧倒的に多い、
普通じゃ考えられない、選択を。
findings.todokanai: I finally did the unthinkable. I chose the path in which very few people have found happiness going down.

findings.highlight: exhales on our intertwined hands, rubbing them together
findings.evidenceJa: かずさの手は、息を吹きかけたり、こすり合わせたりして温められていた
findings.explanation: Kazusa's hand has already been warmed by blowing on it and rubbing it before she takes Haruki's hand. The translation makes her perform those actions now on intertwined hands, inventing mutual hand-rubbing and changing her preparation into contact.
findings.japanese:
けれど、頬に触れた俺の手を握り返すかずさの手は、
息を吹きかけたり、こすり合わせたりして温められていた。
findings.todokanai: However, Kazusa grabs my hand that's touching her cheeks and exhales on our intertwined hands, rubbing them together to give me warmth.

findings.highlight: brushes herself against my body
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の体を撫で、さすり、包み込んで温め返しながら
findings.explanation: Kazusa strokes, rubs, and wraps Haruki's body to warm him in return. The translation makes her rub her own body against his, sexualizing a sequence described as reciprocal caregiving and changing the acting body.
findings.japanese: 俺の体を撫で、さすり、包み込んで温め返しながら。
findings.todokanai: She wraps around me, and brushes herself against my body, warming me up in return.

findings.highlight: she's the person this is all for
findings.evidenceJa: まぎれもない当事者なんだから
findings.explanation: Haruki hides nothing because Kazusa is indisputably a direct party to what happened and shares responsibility for Setsuna's pain. The translation makes her the beneficiary for whom it was all done, replacing accountability with motive.
findings.japanese:
かずさには、何も隠さない。
だって、まぎれもない当事者なんだから。
findings.todokanai: I won't hide anything from Kazusa. After all, she's the person this is all for.

findings.highlight: not getting even a glimpse of punishment
findings.evidenceJa: ほんのわずかも、罪を償えなかった
findings.explanation: They hurt because they were unable to atone for even the slightest portion of their guilt. The translation says they did not receive punishment, substituting suffering imposed on them for reparation owed to Setsuna.
findings.japanese: …ほんのわずかも、罪を償えなかったことに。
findings.todokanai: …For not getting even a glimpse of punishment.

findings.highlight: I decided to conclude the subject.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はただ、わざとらしく結論をぼかすだけ
findings.explanation: Haruki could refute Kazusa endlessly but only makes a conspicuous show of blurring the conclusion, avoiding a direct declaration of her role. The translation says he concludes the subject, the opposite discourse action.
findings.japanese:
…そうやっていくらでも論破できるけど、
俺はただ、わざとらしく結論をぼかすだけ。
findings.todokanai: …We can go back and forth for as long as it takes, but I decided to conclude the subject.

findings.highlight: The story will just follow the direction that the director stubbornly decided on.
