findings.evidenceJa: 制作者の独りよがりの主人公とヒロインなんだって
findings.explanation: Haruki would have to admit that he and Kazusa are a protagonist and heroine self-indulgently imposed by the creator who make no audience member happy. The translation drops their protagonist-and-heroine identities and turns authorial self-indulgence into simple directorial stubbornness.
findings.japanese:
観客を誰一人幸せにしない、
制作者の独りよがりの主人公とヒロインなんだって。
findings.todokanai: It won't make a single member of the audience happy. The story will just follow the direction that the director stubbornly decided on.

findings.highlight: caused by more reasons than I can name
findings.evidenceJa: 原因のわかりすぎていた体調不良
findings.explanation: Haruki considers the cause of his illness all too clear: his conflict over Setsuna, relieved by Kazusa's presence. The translation says there are more causes than he can identify, the exact opposite epistemic state.
findings.japanese:
原因のわかりすぎていた体調不良は、
これからはもう、襲ってこないと思う。
findings.todokanai: I think that my illness, caused by more reasons than I can name, won't be bothering me anymore.

findings.highlight: That's exactly what I mean when I say you two are inseparable!
findings.evidenceJa: それがらぶらぶでなくてなんだっつ～の。こりゃ、マジで秒読みかな
findings.explanation: Takahiro not only insists the bento proves they are lovey-dovey but jokes that the marriage countdown may truly have begun. The translation omits 秒読み and therefore his innocent belief that the wedding is imminent.
findings.japanese:
「それがらぶらぶでなくてなんだっつ～の。
こりゃ、マジで秒読みかな」
findings.todokanai: "That's exactly what I mean when I say you two are inseparable!"

findings.highlight: You'll only cause me more worry
findings.evidenceJa: あなたは食べたら駄目。…余計な心配することになるから
findings.explanation: Setsuna's mother forbids Takahiro from eating the leftovers because he would end up worrying unnecessarily after discovering something wrong. The translation says his eating will cause the mother more worry, reversing the experiencer and obscuring that she is shielding him from knowledge.
findings.japanese:
「いいから。
あなたは食べたら駄目。
…余計な心配することになるから」
findings.todokanai: "Listen to me, don't eat that… You'll only cause me more worry…"

findings.highlight: make things easier for Kazusa
findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜の俺が少しでもかずさを満たしたのなら
findings.explanation: Haruki hopes that what he did the previous night satisfied or fulfilled Kazusa even a little, a charged emotional and bodily formulation. 'Made things easier' reduces that intimacy to relief from difficulty.
findings.japanese:
もし、昨夜の俺が少しでもかずさを満たしたのなら、
それに勝る喜びはない。
findings.todokanai: If I managed to make things easier for Kazusa yesterday, then there is no greater happiness for me.

findings.highlight: I didn't think so though
findings.evidenceJa: わ、わたしは、そんなつもりなかったんだけど
findings.explanation: In Setsuna's rehearsed excuse, she denies that she personally intended to bring Haruki food or show affection; her mother supposedly made her. The translation says she disagreed with the mother's assessment that he was not eating properly, changing the protective lie she is constructing.
findings.japanese:
「春希くん、最近忙しそうだったから。
きちんとした食事してないだろうからって。
わ、わたしは、そんなつもりなかったんだけど…」
findings.todokanai: "She said that you probably haven't been eating properly, with how busy you are all the time. I didn't think so though…"

findings.highlight: half the clothes I have are work clothes
findings.evidenceJa: 持ってる服は、大半が仕事用のスーツやワイシャツ
findings.explanation: The great majority of Haruki's clothes are work suits and dress shirts. The translation reduces that dominant professional uniform to only half his wardrobe.
findings.japanese:
最低限の家具と家電。
持ってる服は、大半が仕事用のスーツやワイシャツ。
findings.todokanai: The bare minimum for any home. And half the clothes I have are work clothes and dress shirts.

findings.highlight: the other tenant staying here
findings.evidenceJa: 俺以外の、『二人目の住人』が持ち込んだもの
findings.explanation: The quoted 'second resident' is Haruki's domestic recognition of the person who frequently used the room and brought cookware, not a legal tenant or confirmed cohabitant. The translation turns the metaphor into actual tenancy.
findings.japanese: ………俺以外の、『二人目の住人』が持ち込んだもの。
findings.todokanai: …Items that the other tenant staying here had brought into the room.

findings.highlight: The current contract runs out at the end of next month. You'll have to pay that month's rent too before the end of this month.
findings.evidenceJa: 今の契約期限が３末までですから、来月末には引き払っていただくことになりますが
findings.explanation: The lease expires at the end of March, so Haruki will need to vacate by the end of next month. The translation changes the expiration date and invents a rent-payment deadline that does not appear in the source.
findings.japanese:
「今の契約期限が３末までですから、
来月末には引き払っていただくことになりますが」
findings.todokanai: "The current contract runs out at the end of next month. You'll have to pay that month's rent too before the end of this month."

findings.highlight: the history I've shared with that apartment
findings.evidenceJa: あの部屋の、味わいのある光景
findings.explanation: Alongside five years of memories, Haruki separately mourns the room's characterful view or scene—the visible mixture of their possessions. The translation repeats an abstract shared history and loses the physical domestic arrangement that will vanish in days.
findings.japanese:
五年かかって築き上げた思い出も、
あの部屋の、味わいのある光景も…
findings.todokanai: Both the memories that I've built up for the past five years as well as the history I've shared with that apartment I've lived in…

findings.highlight: You haven't accomplished anything yet
findings.evidenceJa: お前、まだ何も返しちゃいないだろ
findings.explanation: Hamada says Haruki has not yet repaid or given anything back to the company that trained him. This is not a judgment that Haruki has accomplished nothing; the debt-to-company motif is repeated at lines 49 and 52.
findings.japanese:
「これからだろ…
お前、まだ何も返しちゃいないだろ…」
findings.todokanai: "You have so much potential… You haven't accomplished anything yet, right…?"

findings.highlight: How should I know?
findings.explanation: The source contains only a startled or choked exclamation. The English invents a fully articulated defensive reply.
findings.todokanai: "How should I know?"

findings.highlight: letter of resignation for your editor position
findings.evidenceJa: 編集長に辞表出したって
findings.explanation: Haruki submitted his resignation letter to the editor-in-chief. The English instead implies he is resigning from an editor position, changing the grammatical role of 編集長.
findings.japanese: 「編集長に辞表出したって…どういうことだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Submitting a letter of resignation for your editor position… why would you do that?"

findings.highlight: But you live alone, don't you?
findings.evidenceJa: でもお前、独身だよな
findings.explanation: Hamada says Haruki is unmarried, making 'family circumstances' an odd resignation formula before asking about his parents. Living alone is a different fact.
findings.japanese:
「家庭の事情とか？
でもお前、独身だよな？
もしかして、親御さんが何か？」
findings.todokanai: "Family matters? But you live alone, don't you? Did you hear something from your parents?"

findings.highlight: skills I have learned from both seniors and juniors
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩から後輩に脈々と受け継がれてゆくスキル
findings.explanation: These are skills handed continuously down from seniors to juniors. The English instead has Haruki learning from both groups and erases the intergenerational transmission he is abandoning.
findings.japanese:
先輩から後輩に脈々と受け継がれてゆくスキル、人脈、
そして、絆。
findings.todokanai: The skills I have learned from both seniors and juniors, the connections, and the bonds I have formed.

findings.highlight: you're still a rookie around here
findings.evidenceJa: まだ会社的には全然赤字なんだぞ
findings.explanation: Hamada says the company is still deeply in the red on its investment in Haruki. Rookie status is only the context; the explicit financial loss and unpaid obligation disappear.
findings.japanese:
「いくらお前でも、まだ会社的には全然赤字なんだぞ？
なんの恩返しもできてないんだぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "Even as you are now, you're still a rookie around here. You haven't given back anything yet!"

findings.highlight: not in a way that took too much initiative from yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 決して個人主義ってんじゃなくて
findings.explanation: Although Haruki sometimes charges ahead alone, Hamada says he is never an individualist. The English is nonsensical and does not preserve the distinction between solitary initiative and selfish individualism.
findings.japanese:
「たまに一人で突っ走ることもあるけど、
決して個人主義ってんじゃなくて、
何より、仕事と真剣に向き合ってた」
findings.todokanai: "There were times you did too much on your own, but not in a way that took too much initiative from yourself. Rather, you were very serious about your job."

findings.highlight: I'm supposed to get the boot
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が飛ばされんのが先だろ
findings.explanation: Matsuoka jokes that he should be transferred or banished to an undesirable post before Haruki disappears. 飛ばされる does not mean being fired outright.
findings.japanese:
「な………んだよそれ。
なんでお前が先にいなくなるんだよ？
どう考えても俺が飛ばされんのが先だろ！」
findings.todokanai: "What… the hell is this? Why are you leaving before me? Shouldn't it be a given that I'm supposed to get the boot before you do!?"

findings.highlight: it's unfortunate
findings.evidenceJa: けれど…最悪ね
findings.explanation: Youko calls the situation the worst: it is Kazusa's desired result but not Youko's desired ending. 'Unfortunate' substantially softens her categorical moral judgment.
findings.japanese:
「けれど…最悪ね。
あの子の望んだ結果だけど、
わたしの望んだ結末とは違う」
findings.todokanai: "But… it's unfortunate. The resolution she wished for is different from mine."

findings.highlight: I would accept any divine punishment awaiting me. However, I couldn't bear seeing that happening to my daughter.
findings.evidenceJa: 天罰も地獄行きも覚悟してる。…けれど、我が娘が地獄に落ちるのは見るに忍びない
findings.explanation: Youko is prepared both for divine punishment and to go to hell herself, but cannot bear watching her daughter fall into hell. The English drops hell from both halves and reduces the daughter's fate to vague 'that happening.'
findings.japanese:
「わたしが直接壊したなら、天罰も地獄行きも覚悟してる。
…けれど、我が娘が地獄に落ちるのは見るに忍びない」
findings.todokanai: "Had I been the one directly responsible, I would accept any divine punishment awaiting me. However, I couldn't bear seeing that happening to my daughter."

findings.highlight: You won't be any less free than in Japan. No, I'll make sure you have even more freedom.
findings.evidenceJa: あなたに不自由はさせません
findings.explanation: Haruki promises Youko will want for nothing and suffer no inconvenience or lack in his care abroad. 不自由 here is not political or personal freedom, much less a promise of greater freedom than Japan.
findings.japanese:
「あなたのケアについては、俺が絶対に何とかします。
日本じゃなくても…ううん、日本以上に、
あなたに不自由はさせません」
findings.todokanai: "I'll make sure your medical needs are looked after. You won't be any less free than in Japan. No, I'll make sure you have even more freedom."

findings.highlight: the three of us will bear it all together
findings.evidenceJa: 二人…いや、三人だって抱えてみせます
findings.explanation: Haruki vows that he himself will support/carry two people—no, all three lives including Youko. The English redistributes the burden equally among the three, undoing Youko's warning that no one will support him.
findings.japanese:
「ちゃんと現地で仕事を探して、言葉も勉強して、
二人…いや、三人だって抱えてみせます」
findings.todokanai: "I'll make sure to find employment over there, I'll learn the necessary language, and the two of us… no, the three of us will bear it all together."

findings.highlight: Even though I have been adamant about this since the beginning, she has diverted the thread of the conversation to the bitter end.
findings.evidenceJa: 今まで散々煽っておきながら、最後の最後に梯子を外されてしまったことに対して
findings.explanation: Youko had repeatedly egged Haruki on, only to pull the ladder out from under him at the very end; his bravado may be retaliation for that. The English makes Haruki the previously adamant one and reduces Youko's reversal to conversation drift.
findings.japanese:
今まで散々煽っておきながら、
最後の最後に梯子を外されてしまったことに対して、
意趣返しをしたかっただけかもしれなかった。
findings.todokanai: Even though I have been adamant about this since the beginning, she has diverted the thread of the conversation to the bitter end. This is my tiny form of revenge for that.

findings.highlight: While the fact was obvious to Kazusa, I was unable to hide my shock
findings.evidenceJa: かずさは当然として、俺も、ショックを隠しきれていなかった
findings.explanation: Kazusa naturally cannot hide her shock, and neither can Haruki. The English turns Kazusa's visible shock into the verdict being obvious to her and leaves the emotion only with Haruki.
findings.japanese:
かずさは当然として、
俺も、ショックを隠しきれていなかった。
findings.todokanai: While the fact was obvious to Kazusa, I was unable to hide my shock when I learned her verdict.

findings.highlight: isn't feeling very well right now
findings.evidenceJa: 今はちょっと気弱になってるだけ
findings.explanation: Haruki argues that Youko is merely feeling timid, vulnerable, or fainthearted now and may think differently when her spirits recover. The English makes this her physical illness, obscuring his denial of her stated resolve.
findings.japanese:
「曜子さん、今はちょっと気弱になってるだけだって。
もっと元気になれば考え方も変わってくるって」
findings.todokanai: "Youko-san isn't feeling very well right now, but her point of view might change when she feels better."

findings.highlight: Then Kazusa won't be there during her final moments
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の最期に立ち会えないことも
findings.explanation: Haruki fears that Kazusa might be unable to attend Youko's final moments. The English converts the feared possibility into a certainty.
findings.japanese:
もしかしたらかずさは、
彼女の最期に立ち会えないことも…
findings.todokanai: Then Kazusa won't be there during her final moments…

findings.highlight: that possibility is too cruel to even come to her mind
findings.evidenceJa: 敢えて思いつかないかのように振舞う
findings.explanation: Kazusa deliberately behaves as though she has not thought of that worst possibility. The English says it genuinely cannot enter her mind, erasing her conscious performance of denial.
findings.japanese:
けれどかずさは、その最悪の想像を
敢えて思いつかないかのように振舞う。
findings.todokanai: Yet to Kazusa, that possibility is too cruel to even come to her mind.

findings.highlight: you were the one who made me swear that stupid oath
findings.evidenceJa: そもそも勝手に誓いを立ててるのはお前だ
findings.explanation: Kazusa tells Haruki that he is the one arbitrarily imposing the vow on himself. The English says he made Kazusa swear it and adds that the oath is stupid.
findings.japanese:
「それこそ心配したって仕方ないだろ。
お前の意志がそんなに弱いわけがないし、
そもそも勝手に誓いを立ててるのはお前だ」
findings.todokanai: "Even less reason to worry then. You're not that weak-willed, and you were the one who made me swear that stupid oath in the first place."

findings.highlight: We cannot consummate our love
findings.evidenceJa: 愛を育むことなんか、できるわけが
findings.explanation: Haruki says they cannot nurture or cultivate their love in the same place as Setsuna. 'Consummate' narrows this to sex, especially damaging here because the couple is explicitly discussing a promise not to sleep together.
findings.japanese: 愛を育むことなんか、できるわけが…
findings.todokanai: We cannot consummate our love…

findings.highlight: their disposition toward Yanagihara-san's personality
findings.evidenceJa: 柳原朋の、元々の性格に起因するものだったり
findings.explanation: The gap in how quickly the friends understand is attributed partly to Tomo Yanagihara's own original personality. The English instead invents a disposition that the others have toward her personality.
findings.japanese:
それは、俺と過ごした時間の差だったり、
柳原朋の、元々の性格に起因するものだったり、
そんな様々な要因が絡んでのことだと思うけど…
findings.todokanai: It may be due to the difference in time spent with me, or merely their disposition toward Yanagihara-san's personality…

findings.highlight: improvise an answer
findings.evidenceJa: もし俺が口から出任せを言っても
findings.explanation: 口から出任せ means making up a convenient lie on the spot, not merely improvising an answer. This begins Haruki's imagined attempt to deceive his friends about the breakup.
findings.japanese: 今、もし俺が口から出任せを言っても…
findings.todokanai: Let's say I were to improvise an answer…

findings.highlight: we got into a little fight
findings.evidenceJa: 悪い、ちょっとやっちゃってさ
findings.explanation: Haruki's hypothetical lie remains deliberately vague: roughly, 'Sorry, I kind of screwed up.' The English specifies a fight, supplying a concrete explanation the source withholds.
findings.japanese:
『悪い、ちょっとやっちゃってさ…』なんて、
頭を掻きながら白々しく反省の表情を見せたとしても…
findings.todokanai: Scratch my head with a half regretful look on my face, and say "Sorry, we got into a little fight."

findings.highlight: Neither Takeya nor Io tried reinterpreting it to make me look better, even though I'm sure they could.
findings.evidenceJa: すぐに思いつきながらも、必死で思い描こうとしなかった最悪の事実
findings.explanation: Takeya and Io immediately thought of the worst possibility but had desperately resisted picturing it. The English replaces that denial with a nonexistent opportunity to reinterpret Haruki's confession favorably.
findings.japanese:
武也と依緒が、すぐに思いつきながらも、
必死で思い描こうとしなかった最悪の事実が、
俺の口から語られてしまったから。
findings.todokanai: I told the truth in its terrible entirety. Neither Takeya nor Io tried reinterpreting it to make me look better, even though I'm sure they could.

findings.highlight: and looks at Takeya and Io from the side
findings.evidenceJa: 柳原朋は俺を睨みつけ、武也は依緒の横顔を見つめ
findings.explanation: Tomo glares at Haruki, while Takeya looks at Io's profile. The English makes Tomo perform both actions and turns Io's profile into a side view of both Takeya and Io.
findings.japanese:
柳原朋は俺を睨みつけ、
武也は依緒の横顔を見つめ。
findings.todokanai: Yanagihara Tomo glares at me, and looks at Takeya and Io from the side.

findings.highlight: the true lie had been everything I had told her up until today
findings.evidenceJa: 今までの俺が嘘をついていたこと
findings.explanation: Tomo finally believes that Haruki had been lying or maintaining a lie until now. The English says everything he had ever told her was a lie, a much broader and materially different accusation.
findings.japanese:
今の俺が嘘をついていないって…
今までの俺が嘘をついていたことを、やっと信じた。
findings.todokanai: She finally understood that I'm not lying… That the true lie had been everything I had told her up until today.

findings.highlight: She desired the artist SETSUNA more than the actual Ogiso Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜が、小木曽雪菜であるよりも、ＳＥＴＳＵＮＡである時間をもっと求めてた
findings.explanation: Tomo wanted Setsuna to spend more time being the performer SETSUNA than being ordinary Ogiso Setsuna. The English instead says that Setsuna herself desired the stage persona more than the real person, reversing both subject and motivation.
findings.japanese:
雪菜が、小木曽雪菜であるよりも、
ＳＥＴＳＵＮＡである時間をもっと求めてた。
findings.todokanai: She desired the artist SETSUNA more than the actual Ogiso Setsuna.

findings.highlight: Did she find all your weak spots?
findings.evidenceJa: 身体の相性、抜群だった？
findings.explanation: Tomo asks whether Haruki and Kazusa were exceptionally sexually compatible. 'Find all your weak spots' is a different sexual idea and loses the comparison of bodily compatibility.
findings.japanese:
「そんなに彼女は良かった？
身体の相性、抜群だった？」
findings.todokanai: "Was she that good in bed? Did she find all your weak spots?"

findings.highlight: What a poor excuse for love.
findings.evidenceJa: 最低の純愛だね
findings.explanation: Tomo calls it 'the worst kind of pure love,' a pointed oxymoron that concedes the purity of Haruki and Kazusa's devotion while condemning its effects. 'Poor excuse for love' denies that central paradox.
findings.japanese: 「最低の純愛だね。吐き気がする」
findings.todokanai: "What a poor excuse for love. I feel like vomiting."

findings.highlight: my love for her isn't reaching them
findings.evidenceJa: 本当の心が通じないのが痛い。相手を好きな気持ちがもう二度と伝わらないのが痛い
findings.explanation: The narration describes the pain of two true hearts no longer communicating and one's love for the other never being conveyed again. The English collapses this into Haruki's unilateral feelings and ends with an incoherent her/them referent.
findings.japanese:
本当の心が通じないのが痛い。
相手を好きな気持ちがもう二度と伝わらないのが痛い。
findings.todokanai: It hurts that my feelings aren't being conveyed. It hurts that my love for her isn't reaching them.

findings.highlight: this is what Setsuna looks like after being abandoned by you
findings.evidenceJa: あんたに捨てられた雪菜はこんなもんじゃ
findings.explanation: Io says that what Setsuna suffered after Haruki abandoned her was nothing like this—implicitly far worse. The English instead identifies the present scene as what abandoned Setsuna looks like.
findings.japanese:
「でもな、春希…
雪菜は…あんたに捨てられた雪菜はこんなもんじゃ…」
findings.todokanai: "But you know, Haruki… this is what Setsuna looks like after being abandoned by you…"

findings.highlight: retribution for switching partners overnight
findings.evidenceJa: ただ、日を変え相手を変え、俺に返ってきた報い
findings.explanation: The same cruelty has returned to Haruki on another day and from another person: Io is now confronting him as he once confronted Setsuna. The English invents Haruki switching romantic partners overnight.
findings.japanese:
ただ、日を変え相手を変え、
俺に返ってきた報い。
findings.todokanai: This is my retribution for switching partners overnight.

findings.highlight: take on the responsibility for all my actions
findings.evidenceJa: いつもは俺がやってたことを、これからは自分の役目だと覚悟した
findings.explanation: Takeya appears resolved to take over the role Haruki had always played: shouldering responsibility for failing to persuade someone. The English vastly broadens this into responsibility for all of Haruki's actions.
findings.japanese:
それはまるで、いつもは俺がやってたことを、
これからは自分の役目だと覚悟したかのようで…
findings.todokanai: It's almost as though he's ready to take on the responsibility for all my actions…

findings.highlight: feeling cold because of the loneliness
findings.evidenceJa: そんな寒さが、俺の孤独感を呼び覚ましたのか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether the cold awakened his loneliness. The English reverses the causal direction and makes loneliness the cause of his feeling cold.
findings.japanese:
そんな寒さが、俺の孤独感を呼び覚ましたのか、
それとも他の理由なのかはわからないけど。
findings.todokanai: I'm not sure if I'm feeling cold because of the loneliness that's welling up within me, or if it's because of another reason.

findings.highlight: That's pretty under wraps.
findings.evidenceJa: なんつ～灯台の真下だよ。マスコミ全然気づいてないじゃん
findings.explanation: Takeya riffs on 灯台下暗し: Youko was hidden in plain sight, right under the media's nose. 'Under wraps' implies deliberate secrecy and loses the joke linking her location to the blind spot beneath a lighthouse.
findings.japanese:
「峰城大病院って…なんつ～灯台の真下だよ。
マスコミ全然気づいてないじゃん」
findings.todokanai: "Houjou University Hospital… That's pretty under wraps. The mass media doesn't know a thing, huh?"

findings.highlight: I might be unable to pick Kazusa anymore.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はもう、二人のうちからかずさを選べなくなる
findings.explanation: Haruki says that sharing the burden among all three would leave him no longer able to choose Kazusa over Setsuna. This is the categorical selfish motive for rejecting the proposed solution; 'might' improperly hedges it.
findings.japanese:
「………もし三人で背負ったら、
俺はもう、二人のうちからかずさを選べなくなる」
findings.todokanai: "…If we shared the burden among the three of us, then… I might be unable to pick Kazusa anymore."

findings.highlight: until I started believing them myself
findings.evidenceJa: 二年間、自分でも気づかないうちに嘘を重ねてたんだ
findings.explanation: Haruki says he had unknowingly piled up lies for two years. The English invents a progression in which he eventually came to believe those lies himself.
findings.japanese:
「二年前、吹っ切ったと思ってたけど違ってた。
ずっと昔から、何も変わってなかった。
二年間、自分でも気づかないうちに嘘を重ねてたんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I thought I was over her two years ago, but I was wrong. Even after all this time, nothing has changed. I only piled up lie over lie for these two years until I started believing them myself."

findings.highlight: I may not have any desire to be
findings.evidenceJa: 望みがないってわかってるけど、それでも、まだお前の親友だからさ
findings.explanation: Takeya knows there is no hope of changing Haruki's mind, but pleads because he is still Haruki's best friend. The English says Takeya may have no desire to remain his friend, reversing the force of his last appeal.
findings.japanese:
「けど俺、お前の親友だから。
望みがないってわかってるけど、
それでも、まだお前の親友だからさ…」
findings.todokanai: "But I'm still your friend. I may not have any desire to be, but even then, I'm still your friend…"

findings.highlight: I'll probably never be able to see him again
findings.evidenceJa: もう、二度と出会えないかもしれない存在
findings.explanation: Takeya was a singular kind of person Haruki might never encounter again, not merely someone he might never physically see again after this rupture. The English turns irreplaceability into future access.
findings.japanese:
俺にとって、唯一の…
もう、二度と出会えないかもしれない存在、だったんだ…
findings.todokanai: The only one I had… and I'll probably never be able to see him again…

findings.highlight: nostalgia that I once shared with him are brought to my mind
findings.evidenceJa: 新しい発見は、嬉しさと、悔しさと、切なさと。そして、懐かしさを俺の心に運んでくれる
findings.explanation: The new realization brings Haruki happiness, regret, heartache, and nostalgia. The English grammatically recasts the feelings as things Haruki once shared with Takeya, then makes them the subject of an incoherent sentence.
findings.japanese:
新しい発見は、嬉しさと、悔しさと、切なさと。
そして、懐かしさを俺の心に運んでくれる。
findings.todokanai: New discoveries, happiness, frustration, pain, and nostalgia that I once shared with him are brought to my mind.

findings.highlight: overwhelmed by all the things that had happened up until now
findings.evidenceJa: 今までこらえていたものが溢れそうになり
findings.explanation: What Haruki has been holding back—his tears or emotion—threatens to overflow when the crowd brings relief. The English substitutes the external events that happened, breaking the physical-emotional sequence that makes him look upward.
findings.japanese:
そんな、駅前の人の群れにほっとしてしまったのか、
今までこらえていたものが溢れそうになり、
思わず空を見上げるしかなくなる。
findings.todokanai: Perhaps I felt relieved by seeing the big crowd of people in front of the station, or perhaps I felt overwhelmed by all the things that had happened up until now, and before I knew it, I was looking up at the sky.

findings.highlight: the center of all my relationship problems
findings.evidenceJa: いつも、俺の人間関係の中心にいやがった
findings.explanation: Takeya was always at the center of Haruki's human relationships or social world. The source does not call those relationships problems; the insertion makes Takeya sound like their cause.
findings.japanese:
付属に入って、一番最初にできた友達だった。
いつも、俺の人間関係の中心にいやがった。
findings.todokanai: He was the first friend I ever made after I enrolled in high school. He was always at the center of all my relationship problems.

findings.highlight: the bicycle passing by me stopped to make way for me
findings.evidenceJa: 道を譲ろうとした自転車が急に止まったかと思うと
findings.explanation: Haruki tries to yield to the bicycle, which then stops suddenly. The English reverses the direction of courtesy and says the bicycle stops to make way for Haruki.
findings.japanese:
道を譲ろうとした自転車が急に止まったかと思うと、
聞き覚えのある声が俺を呼んだ。
findings.todokanai: I thought the bicycle passing by me stopped to make way for me, yet its rider spoke with a voice I recognized.

findings.highlight: this is something they don't want their children to see
findings.evidenceJa: 聞かせたくない話も辞さないという意志
findings.explanation: Haruki infers that the parents are resolved not to shrink from scenes or conversation they would never want their children to witness. The English merely says the matter is something they do not want the children to see or hear, omitting the parents' deliberate readiness to proceed.
findings.japanese:
つまりそれは、自分たちの子供には見せたくない場面も…
聞かせたくない話も辞さないという意志なのかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: In other words, this is something they don't want their children to see… and a conversation they don't want them to hear.

findings.highlight: we ran into some obstacles
findings.evidenceJa: 少しヘコむことがあったのは本当だけど、でも今までだって、何度もこういうことあった
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she personally suffered a discouraging blow, but has faced this kind of thing many times before and survived it. The English turns her recurring emotional collapses into obstacles jointly encountered by the relationship.
findings.japanese:
「確かに、少しヘコむことがあったのは本当だけど、
でも今までだって、何度もこういうことあった。
…何度も切り抜けてきたんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "True, we ran into some obstacles, but we've had plenty of those before… and we've always overcome them."

findings.highlight: unwarranted trust
findings.evidenceJa: その、無償の信頼が
findings.explanation: 無償の信頼 is the mother's unconditional, freely given trust in Haruki. 'Unwarranted trust' calls it unjustified or foolish, replacing the source's emphasis on generosity with retrospective judgment.
findings.japanese: その、無償の信頼が…
findings.todokanai: That unwarranted trust…

findings.highlight: you loved Setsuna from the bottom of your heart
findings.evidenceJa: 心の底から雪菜を一番に考えてくれている、嫌になるくらい信頼できる男
findings.explanation: Setsuna's father trusted Haruki as a man who, from the bottom of his heart, always put Setsuna first. The English reduces this to loving her, omitting the precise priority Haruki has now betrayed.
findings.japanese:
「そういう言葉では、絶対に娘を諭せない…
心の底から雪菜を一番に考えてくれている、
嫌になるくらい信頼できる男だと思っていたから…っ」
findings.todokanai: "But those weren't words I could tell my daughter… because I thought that you loved Setsuna from the bottom of your heart. I thought you were a man I could trust…!"

findings.highlight: "I'm going to… Vienna. I'm sorry for all the trouble I've caused you."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ウィーンに…行きます。
今まで色々と、お世話になりました」
findings.explanation: 今まで色々と、お世話になりました is a formal expression of gratitude for all the family's past care, not an apology for trouble caused — The line still functions as Haruki's final farewell.
findings.japanese:
「ウィーンに…行きます。
今まで色々と、お世話になりました」
findings.todokanai: "I'm going to… Vienna. I'm sorry for all the trouble I've caused you."

findings.highlight: didn't allow me to speak about what happened
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は、有無を言わせてくれなかった
findings.explanation: Setsuna brooks no objection while treating Haruki's injury. The English invents a refusal to let him discuss what happened, changing determined first aid into active suppression of the confrontation.
findings.japanese: 雪菜は、有無を言わせてくれなかった。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna didn't allow me to speak about what happened.

findings.highlight: replace it with a different kind of happiness
findings.evidenceJa: 同じ大きさの、違う幸せを積み上げていくことになる
findings.explanation: Setsuna believed she and Haruki would accumulate a different happiness of the same magnitude as the lost happiness of the trio. 'Replace it' omits both gradual accumulation and the crucial claim of equal scale.
findings.japanese:
「だから春希くんと二人で、同じ大きさの、
違う幸せを積み上げていくことになるんだって。
一緒に、生きていくんだって、そう信じてた…」
findings.todokanai: "That's why I thought I could replace it with a different kind of happiness with just the two of us. I believed we could live together…"

findings.highlight: even greater than what we had five years ago
findings.evidenceJa: 今と同じくらい、ううん、それ以上の大きな幸せに包まれるだけだよ
findings.explanation: Setsuna says the happiness of the trio five years ago was as great as her present happiness with Haruki—no, even greater. The English instead makes the proposed happiness greater than what they had five years ago, reversing which state is the benchmark.
findings.japanese:
「ただ、５年前の…
今と同じくらい、ううん、
それ以上の大きな幸せに包まれるだけだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Because all we have to do is… wrap ourselves in a happiness that's even greater than what we had five years ago."

findings.highlight: yet also indecisive at the same time
findings.evidenceJa: どっちつかずでもない、どっちとも深く繋がってしまう人生
findings.explanation: Haruki says this would not be a life of mere indecision; it would be a life deeply bound to both women. The English calls him indecisive, erasing the distinction that explains why the arrangement would injure both.
findings.japanese:
そんな、どっちつかずでもない、
どっちとも深く繋がってしまう人生は、
俺の世界で一番大切な二人を不幸にしてしまう。
findings.todokanai: I'd only end up making the two people I care about more than anyone else in the world completely miserable, chaining them to myself in a limbo where I'm closely tied to the both of them, yet also indecisive at the same time.

findings.highlight: use different means
findings.evidenceJa: たとえ目的と手段を入れ替えてでも
findings.explanation: Haruki is prepared to invert purpose and means—to make his exclusion of Setsuna serve the choice of a future with Kazusa. The English reduces this morally perverse inversion to using different means.
findings.japanese:
…たとえ目的と手段を入れ替えてでも、
雪菜まで、先の見えない未来に巻き込むわけにはいかない。
findings.todokanai: …Even if it means I have to use different means… I cannot involve Setsuna in a future without light at the end of the tunnel.

findings.highlight: She's giving me up to Kazusa.
findings.evidenceJa: どこまでも、俺に、かずさに譲歩する
findings.explanation: Setsuna keeps conceding to both Haruki and Kazusa by offering to join them on their terms. She is not simply surrendering Haruki to Kazusa; her proposed three-person life still includes herself.
findings.japanese: どこまでも、俺に、かずさに譲歩する。
findings.todokanai: She's giving me up to Kazusa.

findings.highlight: "I don't need any of them!"
findings.evidenceJa: 「そんなのなくしたっていい！」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she would be willing to lose family and friends, rather than that she presently needs none of them — Her readiness to sacrifice every external bond for the trio remains.
findings.japanese: 「そんなのなくしたっていい！」
findings.todokanai: "I don't need any of them!"

findings.highlight: Kazusa is a tumbleweed
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜が樹木なら、かずさは浮き草だ
findings.explanation: Kazusa is 浮き草, a floating aquatic plant or duckweed, contrasted with Setsuna as a rooted tree. 'Tumbleweed' breaks the next lines' water-and-nutrient logic and substitutes an arid image for the source's aquatic dependence.
findings.japanese:
雪菜が樹木なら、かずさは浮き草だ。
地面に根を張って強く生きていくことはできないんだ。
findings.todokanai: If Setsuna is a tree that plants roots, then Kazusa is a tumbleweed. It's just not possible for her to extend her roots and live firmly.

findings.highlight: find water to sustain herself little by little as she goes
findings.evidenceJa: 水から少しずつ栄養をもらって生きていくしかない
findings.explanation: As floating weed, Kazusa can only live by taking nourishment little by little from the water itself while cut off from earth and world. The English makes her travel in search of water, continuing the erroneous tumbleweed metaphor.
findings.japanese:
地面と、世界と隔絶したところで、
水から少しずつ栄養をもらって生きていくしかないんだ。
findings.todokanai: She must find water to sustain herself little by little as she goes, separated both from the ground and the world.

findings.highlight: 'my body' doesn't belong to 'only' myself anymore
findings.evidenceJa: お前『の体』はもう、お前『だけ』のものじゃない
findings.explanation: Haruki corrects Kazusa by saying, 'Your body isn't yours alone anymore.' The English changes both possessors to Haruki and has him talk about his own body.
findings.japanese:
「お前『の体』はもう、
お前『だけ』のものじゃない、だろ。
必要な部分まで省略するな」
findings.todokanai: "You mean to say that 'my body' doesn't belong to 'only' myself anymore. Don't neglect the important parts."

findings.highlight: I could push her down
findings.evidenceJa: 強く押し倒し、全身でのしかかって拘束し、激しくその身体をまさぐっても
findings.explanation: The ても sequence describes concrete acts Haruki performs—forcing Kazusa down, pinning her with his body, and groping her—before the apodosis at line 567 says she still relaxes and accepts him. Repeated 'I could' wording turns the enacted assaultive contact into a hypothetical possibility.
findings.japanese:
強く押し倒し、全身でのしかかって拘束し、
激しくその身体をまさぐっても。
findings.todokanai: I could push her down with all my force and lean my body over her. I could experience the sensation of her body.

findings.highlight: call me out on it
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が迷うたびに、何度も振り回して
findings.explanation: Haruki apologizes for jerking Kazusa around over and over whenever he wavers. The English instead asks Kazusa to call him out, turning his admission of harm into an instruction for her future behavior.
findings.japanese:
「ごめんな、かずさ。
俺が迷うたびに、何度も振り回して」
findings.todokanai: "I'm sorry, Kazusa… Every time I lose my way, call me out on it."

findings.highlight: Let me be of some use.
findings.evidenceJa: 少しでも、あたしを必要としてくれよ
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks Haruki to need her, even a little. 'Let me be of some use' changes her plea for emotional necessity into utility, precisely the reduction her painkiller metaphor has made painful.
findings.japanese:
「だから、せめてあたしの胸で泣いてくれ。
少しでも、あたしを必要としてくれよ」
findings.todokanai: "Then at least cry in my arms. Let me be of some use."

findings.highlight: The amount of suffering we've caused to so many people
findings.evidenceJa: あれだけ多くの人を踏み台にした意味がない
findings.explanation: Haruki says that otherwise there would have been no point in using so many people as stepping stones. The English replaces his ruthless, self-aware instrumentalization of others with the more passive suffering they caused.
findings.japanese: でないと、あれだけ多くの人を踏み台にした意味がない。
findings.todokanai: The amount of suffering we've caused to so many people would have been for nothing otherwise.

findings.highlight: For a while, I listened in drowsiness
findings.evidenceJa: しばらく後、かずさが呟いたその言葉を、俺は夢うつつで聞いていた
findings.explanation: Kazusa murmurs the words some time later, and Haruki hears them half-asleep. The English attaches しばらく to how long he listened rather than when she spoke.
findings.japanese:
しばらく後、かずさが呟いたその言葉を、
俺は夢うつつで聞いていた。
findings.todokanai: For a while, I listened in drowsiness to Kazusa's whispers.

findings.highlight: the tour documents
findings.evidenceJa: ツール関係はこのフォルダに入ってますから
findings.explanation: Haruki says the work-related tools or utilities are in the folder and their use is covered by the procedure manual. The English turns ツール into tour documents, inventing travel material.
findings.japanese:
「それで、ツール関係はこのフォルダに入ってますから。
使い方は手順書を見ればわかるようになってます」
findings.todokanai: "…And the tour documents are in this folder. I've set it up so you can find the instructions in these documents."

findings.highlight: thinking that no one else would accept such an assignment
findings.evidenceJa: 誰もが激しく拒否すると思ってた当の本人は、少し考え込む仕草を見せると、あっさり首を縦に振った
findings.explanation: Matsuoka is the very person everyone expected to reject the assignment fiercely; after a moment's thought, he simply nods. The English instead makes him think no one else would accept and then volunteer, inventing his motive.
findings.japanese:
その措置が決まった瞬間、
誰もが激しく拒否すると思ってた当の本人は、
少し考え込む仕草を見せると、あっさり首を縦に振った。
findings.todokanai: Once this measure was decided on, thinking that no one else would accept such an assignment, Matsuoka-san looked a bit deep in thought and eventually stepped forward.

findings.highlight: increasing the workload
findings.evidenceJa: しばらくはバイト増やして乗り切るしかない
findings.explanation: Hamada's temporary plan is to increase the number of part-time workers. The English says the department will increase the workload, the opposite of the proposed staffing relief.
findings.japanese:
「今、浜田さんが一生懸命人事と交渉してるけど、
しばらくはバイト増やして乗り切るしかないだろうって」
findings.todokanai: "Hamada-san is doing his best to come to a solution with HR, but for now, we'll have to live with increasing the workload."

findings.highlight: exclusively focused on work
findings.evidenceJa: 木崎さんはますます出先ばかり
findings.explanation: Kizaki is spending more and more of his time out of the office on assignments. The English turns his physical absence into the generic virtue of focusing exclusively on work.
findings.japanese:
浜田さんは部下に当たり散らすことが多くなり、
鈴木さんの雑談は消え、木崎さんはますます出先ばかり。
findings.todokanai: Hamada-san has become more irritable with his subordinates. Suzuki-san has stopped chatting, and Kizaki-san has been exclusively focused on work.

findings.highlight: the deadline for the Air Pocket
findings.evidenceJa: 締め切り後のエアポケットと相まって
findings.explanation: エアポケット is the lull or vacuum after a deadline, combining with the disappearance of conversation to make the office unnaturally quiet. The English parses Air Pocket as a publication whose deadline has passed.
findings.japanese:
そうやって編集部からどんどん会話が消えていき、
締め切り後のエアポケットと相まって、
ここが出版社とは思えない静けさに包まれている。
findings.todokanai: Couple the disappearance of chatter from the editing department with the passing of the deadline for the Air Pocket, and you would find the office so quiet that you could wonder whether this is a publishing office at all.

findings.highlight: I am the guest of honor at your farewell party
findings.evidenceJa: 一応、送別会の主賓だし
findings.explanation: Matsuoka says he will pay for Haruki's share because Haruki is the guest of honor. The English makes Matsuoka call himself the guest of honor at Haruki's farewell party.
findings.japanese:
「その代わり、お前の分は俺が出すから。
…一応、送別会の主賓だし」
findings.todokanai: "In exchange, I'll pay for your drink. I am the guest of honor at your farewell party, after all."

findings.highlight: when can I enter the venue tomorrow?
findings.evidenceJa: 明日、何時に会場入りだっけ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks what time Kazusa is due to enter the venue. The English has him ask when he is allowed to enter it.
findings.japanese:
「あ、それでさ…
明日、何時に会場入りだっけ？」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, by the way… when can I enter the venue tomorrow?"

findings.highlight: I'll begin by afternoon.
findings.evidenceJa: 昼過ぎには出るよ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will leave after noon, which may cause her and Haruki to miss each other. 'I'll begin' does not state the departure that creates that possibility.
findings.japanese:
「昼過ぎには出るよ。
もしかしたら、すれ違いになるかもな」
findings.todokanai: "I'll begin by afternoon. We may end up passing each other."

findings.highlight: He's accepting my selfishness
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の身勝手のとばっちりを受けて、ずっと俺に厳しく当たっていた先輩とともに
findings.explanation: The sentence identifies Matsuoka as the senior who bore collateral damage from Haruki's selfishness and therefore treated him harshly. The English invents someone accepting Haruki's selfishness and leaves the relation to the senior incoherent.
findings.japanese:
俺の身勝手のとばっちりを受けて、
ずっと俺に厳しく当たっていた先輩とともに。
findings.todokanai: He's accepting my selfishness, along with the senior who was always so strict with me.

findings.highlight: It's my jealousy that ruined everything
findings.evidenceJa: 全部、あたしの独占欲がいけないんだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa first identifies her possessiveness—her need to have Haruki exclusively—as the cause, then names jealousy of Setsuna in the following line. The English collapses the first cause into jealousy and erases the deliberate progression.
findings.japanese: 「全部、あたしの独占欲がいけないんだ…」
findings.todokanai: "It's my jealousy that ruined everything…"

findings.highlight: he has been focused on nothing but his work
findings.evidenceJa: たまに顔を合わせても一言も会話がなくて、あからさまに避けられてたはずの先輩
findings.explanation: Haruki believed Kizaki had been openly avoiding him, saying nothing even when they happened to meet. The English reframes that social rejection as dedication to work and omits the explicit avoidance that makes Kizaki's arrival moving.
findings.japanese:
最近、ずっと出先ばかりで、
たまに顔を合わせても一言も会話がなくて、
あからさまに避けられてたはずの先輩が…
findings.todokanai: Recently, he has been focused on nothing but his work, and even when we passed each other by, he never said a word.

findings.highlight: the perfect person
findings.evidenceJa: 初めて会ったときから正しい人間だった
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Setsuna a righteous or morally correct person from the moment they met. 'Perfect person' changes the specific moral quality that frightened and dazzled Kazusa into general flawlessness.
findings.japanese:
「お前は、初めて会ったときから正しい人間だった。
春希と同じ…ううん、
あいつ以上にまっすぐで、強かった」
findings.todokanai: "You were the perfect person from the moment we met. You were strong and straightforward, just like… no, even more than Haruki."

findings.highlight: "I know it's not the right thing to do. I know no one will accept it. But I can't help myself from betraying you."
findings.evidenceJa:
「悪いことだってわかってる。
許されないって知ってる。
けど、裏切らずにはいられないんだ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she knows the betrayal cannot be forgiven; 'no one will accept it' changes forgiveness into social acceptance — Her moral recognition that the act is wrong and her inability to stop are explicit.
findings.japanese:
「悪いことだってわかってる。
許されないって知ってる。
けど、裏切らずにはいられないんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I know it's not the right thing to do. I know no one will accept it. But I can't help myself from betraying you."

findings.highlight: I think.
findings.evidenceJa: 持ってる。どっちの部屋のも
findings.explanation: Kazusa states that she has the keys to both apartments. The English adds uncertainty, misleadingly suggesting she may be unsure whether she has them when the scene's question is why she chose to wait outside despite certainly having access.
findings.japanese:
「あ、ええと…持ってる。
どっちの部屋のも」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, I have the keys for both apartments… I think."

findings.highlight: I grab onto her hands and let out an anguished expression
findings.evidenceJa: とうとう俺に、手のひらを掴まれ、苦悶の表情を浮かべ
findings.explanation: Kazusa has her palms seized by Haruki and shows an anguished expression. The English assigns that expression to Haruki.
findings.japanese:
とうとう俺に、手のひらを掴まれ、
苦悶の表情を浮かべ…
findings.todokanai: Eventually, I grab onto her hands and let out an anguished expression…

findings.highlight: I was holding on to your hand before I even realized it.
findings.evidenceJa: 気がついたら振り払ってた。あなたの愚かな真似を、必死で止めてた
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that before she knew it she had knocked or swept away Kazusa's attempted act and was desperately stopping the foolish self-injury. The English invents her holding Kazusa's hand, obscuring the physical interruption that caused the glass to fall.
findings.japanese:
「だからわからないんだよ！
気がついたら振り払ってた。
あなたの愚かな真似を、必死で止めてた」
findings.todokanai: "I just said I don't know! I was holding on to your hand before I even realized it. I was desperately trying to stop your idiotic act."

findings.highlight: including the smell of alcohol
findings.evidenceJa: むせ返るようなアルコール臭の中、ほんのわずかな俺の匂いを逃すまいとするように
findings.explanation: Amid Haruki's overpowering reek of alcohol, Kazusa presses close as if determined not to miss the faint trace of his own scent. The English says the alcohol smell is included among the scents she is trying to preserve, reversing the contrast.
findings.japanese:
むせ返るようなアルコール臭の中、
ほんのわずかな俺の匂いを逃すまいとするように。
findings.todokanai: Almost as if trying to keep the smell of me from escaping, including the smell of alcohol.

findings.highlight: Setsuna would completely break down
findings.evidenceJa: それがますます雪菜を追い込み、どうしようもなく決裂してしまう
findings.explanation: Kazusa's intervention would drive Setsuna further into a corner and make an irreparable rupture between the two women inevitable. The English replaces the rupture of their relationship with Setsuna personally breaking down.
findings.japanese:
それがますます雪菜を追い込み、
どうしようもなく決裂してしまうなんて、
火を見るより明らかだったのに。
findings.todokanai: In the end, she only made things worse for Setsuna. It was plain as day from the start that Setsuna would completely break down.

findings.highlight: her overestimating herself
findings.evidenceJa: 自分に対しての過大評価…というか、あまりの想いの深さ
findings.explanation: The narrator Haruki leaves unmentioned Kazusa's excessive valuation of him—or rather, the overwhelming depth of her feelings for him. The English instead says Kazusa overestimates herself, reversing the object of valuation.
findings.japanese:
この際、自分に対しての過大評価…というか、
あまりの想いの深さには触れないままにしておく。
findings.todokanai: I have some words about her overestimating herself… but right now, I won't touch on any subject heavy in emotion.

findings.highlight: allow myself to be restrained
findings.evidenceJa: 余計にかずさの温もりを感じてしまうという甘い制裁を俺に科す
findings.explanation: By loosening his grip and embracing Kazusa gently, Haruki imposes on himself the sweet punishment of feeling her warmth even more intensely. The English invents restraint and omits both punishment and heightened warmth.
findings.japanese:
余計にかずさの温もりを感じてしまうという
甘い制裁を俺に科す。
findings.todokanai: I feel her warmth. And allow myself to be restrained.

findings.highlight: She refused to admit I was wrong
findings.evidenceJa: 最後の最後でどうしようもなく優しくて、見誤って、手を離して、足を止めて
findings.explanation: Kazusa lists Setsuna's terminal kindness and the actions born of her misjudgment: letting go and stopping. The English invents Setsuna refusing to admit Kazusa was wrong, assigning an object and moral claim absent from 見誤って.
findings.japanese:
「でもあいつ、最後の最後でどうしようもなく優しくて、
見誤って、手を離して、足を止めて…」
findings.todokanai: "But she was hopelessly kind to me, even up until the very end. She refused to admit I was wrong, she let go of my hand, and she stopped me in my tracks…"

findings.highlight: quarrel, and get sick of each other
findings.evidenceJa: 傷ついて、傷つけられて、疲れてもまだ、息ができないほどの恋に、落ちていこう
findings.explanation: Haruki proposes that even after hurting and being hurt, even when exhausted, they keep falling into a love so intense they cannot breathe. The English changes reciprocal wounds into quarrelling and changes exhaustion into becoming sick of each other.
findings.japanese:
傷ついて、傷つけられて、疲れてもまだ、
息ができないほどの恋に、落ちていこう…
findings.todokanai: Let's overwhelm ourselves in a love so powerful that we can get hurt, quarrel, and get sick of each other, and still go on despite that.

findings.highlight: will it one day reflect back to me
findings.evidenceJa: 届かない恋をしていても
findings.explanation: The lyric asks whether, even while loving beyond reach, a day will come when that love can be shown or brought into view. 'Reflect back to me' invents a reflexive return and obscures the load-bearing song phrase 届かない恋.
findings.japanese:
「届かない恋をしていても…
映し出す日が来るかな…」
findings.todokanai: "Even if my love can't reach you… will it one day reflect back to me…?"

findings.highlight: I'll force you down on my bed.
findings.evidenceJa: 容赦なく病院に連れ帰るからね
findings.explanation: Takayanagi warns that if Youko shows any sign of illness, he will take her straight back to the hospital without mercy. The English invents a sexual threat to force her onto his bed.
findings.japanese:
「とにかく今日は大人しくしてなさい。
少しでも具合が悪そうに見えたら、
容赦なく病院に連れ帰るからね」
findings.todokanai: "Either way, be good today. If I see even a hint of your health failing, I'll force you down on my bed."

findings.highlight: I doubt the beginning of the concert will be a quiet one.
findings.evidenceJa: 今のところ落ち着いた滑り出しに見えないでもなかった
findings.explanation: Despite the tickets selling instantly, the currently only seventy-percent-full hall could be seen as a calm start. The English says Haruki doubts the opening will be quiet, reversing his provisional assessment.
findings.japanese:
それでも、チケット販売時の瞬殺ぶりから考えると、
今のところ落ち着いた滑り出しに見えないでもなかった。
findings.todokanai: But considering all the noise that was made when the tickets were still on sale, I doubt the beginning of the concert will be a quiet one.

findings.highlight: being forced to sit by and watch these two restless adults go after each other
findings.evidenceJa: 意地を張ったり逡巡したりして、かえって悪辣な大人たちを楽しませるのも癪だった
findings.explanation: Haruki leaves because stubbornly refusing or hesitating would only entertain the two wicked adults teasing him. The English says he cannot bear watching the adults attack each other.
findings.japanese:
意地を張ったり逡巡したりして、
かえって悪辣な大人たちを楽しませるのも癪だったので、
俺はそそくさと席を立った。
findings.todokanai: Remaining stubborn with her, or being forced to sit by and watch these two restless adults go after each other was far too unbearable to me, so I got off my seat and left.

findings.highlight: we kept ignoring each other
findings.evidenceJa: すれ違いを繰り返してた二年前
findings.explanation: Two years earlier Haruki and Setsuna repeatedly missed or misunderstood each other while trapped in an unresolved relationship. 'Kept ignoring each other' turns crossed signals into deliberate mutual avoidance.
findings.japanese:
俺たちが中途半端な関係のまま、
すれ違いを繰り返してた二年前…
雪菜は、二度ほど俺たちの前から姿を消した。
findings.todokanai: Two years ago when our relationship was uncertain, we kept ignoring each other… Setsuna disappeared twice.

findings.highlight: in an attempt to find her
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜を力ずくで見つけ出してきた
findings.explanation: On each prior disappearance, Haruki mobilized a large search and forcibly succeeded in finding Setsuna. The English reduces the achieved result to an attempt.
findings.japanese:
その度ごとに、俺は周囲の人たちを巻き込んで
大規模な捜査網を引き、
雪菜を力ずくで見つけ出してきた。
findings.todokanai: Each time I involved everyone around me, and organized a search on a large scale in an attempt to find her.

findings.highlight: would usually be forced to join in
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の無茶に乗っかって、一緒に無茶をしてくれた
findings.explanation: Io and Takeya willingly bought into Haruki's recklessness and acted recklessly alongside him. The English says they were forced to participate, reversing the loyalty being mourned.
findings.japanese:
そして、そういう時いつも、
俺の無茶に乗っかって、
一緒に無茶をしてくれた…
findings.todokanai: And they would usually be forced to join in on my absurd efforts during times like those…

findings.highlight: she has told me as little as she could get away with, but now I have to force it out of her
findings.evidenceJa: 今までは、一を語るだけだった意志の疎通も、十も二十も語って聞かせるしかない
findings.explanation: Their former mutual understanding needed only one part spoken; now Haruki must explain ten or twenty parts to make himself understood. The English instead accuses Io of withholding information and makes Haruki force it out of her.
findings.japanese:
今までは、一を語るだけだった意志の疎通も、
十も二十も語って聞かせるしかない。
findings.todokanai: Up until now, she has told me as little as she could get away with, but now I have to force it out of her.

findings.highlight: My five calls earlier got transferred to voicemail
findings.evidenceJa: さっきまでは、５コールくらいで留守番電話に移行してた
findings.explanation: Earlier each call transferred to voicemail after about five rings. The English says five separate calls were transferred, obscuring why the presently continuing ring count proves Setsuna's phone is on.
findings.japanese:
さっきまでは、５コールくらいで
留守番電話に移行してたのに、
今はずっとコールが続いている。
findings.todokanai: My five calls earlier got transferred to voicemail, but now my call is continuing.

findings.highlight: I won't sleep in peace.
findings.evidenceJa: 困るよ、俺
findings.explanation: Haruki says simply and personally that if Setsuna does not go home, he will be troubled. The English invents sleeplessness and turns the direct admission of emotional stake into a practical consequence.
findings.japanese: 「雪菜が帰らなかったら…困るよ、俺」
findings.todokanai: "If you don't go home, Setsuna… I won't sleep in peace."

findings.highlight: where I went on a date with a boy for the first time
findings.evidenceJa: わたしが、初めて男の子をデートに誘った場所
findings.explanation: Setsuna identifies the karaoke bar as the first place where she invited a boy on a date. The English instead calls it her first date with a boy, erasing her initiative and changing her romantic history.
findings.japanese:
「南末次の、カラオケ屋…
わたしが、初めて男の子をデートに誘った場所」
findings.todokanai: "The karaoke bar in Minami-Suetsugu… where I went on a date with a boy for the first time."

findings.highlight: picking a song right before the time was up just to sing for a few extra minutes
findings.evidenceJa: 終了時間までぎっしり予約で埋めてあって、しかも店内電話が鳴ったとき、ぴったりと最後の曲の後奏に入って
findings.explanation: Setsuna had packed the reservation through closing time and timed the set so the final song entered its outro exactly when the room phone rang. The English invents an attempt to steal extra minutes and loses the joke about her meticulous selfishness.
findings.japanese:
終了時間までぎっしり予約で埋めてあって、
しかも店内電話が鳴ったとき、
ぴったりと最後の曲の後奏に入って。
findings.todokanai: Singing for as long as the reserved time would allow, and even picking a song right before the time was up just to sing for a few extra minutes.

findings.highlight: "For three years, we kept missing one another. For two years, we were in each other's arms."
findings.evidenceJa:
「三年間、ずっとあなたとすれ違って、
二年間、ずっとあなたと触れあってきたんだよ？」
findings.explanation: For two years Haruki and Setsuna kept in contact/touched one another; 'were in each other's arms' makes the whole span exclusively physical-romantic — Their bodily and emotional entanglement is explicit in the following lines.
findings.japanese:
「三年間、ずっとあなたとすれ違って、
二年間、ずっとあなたと触れあってきたんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "For three years, we kept missing one another. For two years, we were in each other's arms."

findings.highlight: ineffective at leaving an impression on you
findings.evidenceJa: わたし、そんなにあなたに影響を与えられてなかった
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether she truly had so little influence on the person Haruki became. 'Leaving an impression' suggests memorability rather than the formative interpenetration of their five-year history.
findings.japanese:
「わたし、そんなにあなたに影響を与えられてなかった？
そんなに…あなたと絡み合うことはできなかったの！？」
findings.todokanai: "Was I that ineffective at leaving an impression on you? Was our bond… so fragile that you could just tear it off like that?"

findings.highlight: but just barely
findings.evidenceJa: 震えてはいたけれど、儚さは取り払われていた
findings.explanation: Setsuna's voice still trembles, but its fragility has been stripped away. 'But just barely' says the voice itself barely persists, nearly the opposite of its recovered firmness.
findings.japanese: 震えてはいたけれど、儚さは取り払われていた。
findings.todokanai: Her voice was shaking, but just barely.

findings.highlight: let out my thoughts, only to have her watch as I try to stop myself from saying too much
findings.evidenceJa: ただ一方的に自分の思いを募らせ、そして必死で思い留まるくらいは許して欲しかった
findings.explanation: Haruki wants permission only to let his feelings accumulate unilaterally inside him and desperately restrain himself from acting on them. The English invents him voicing those thoughts and Setsuna watching his attempted self-censorship.
findings.japanese:
ただ一方的に自分の思いを募らせ、
そして必死で思い留まるくらいは許して欲しかった。
findings.todokanai: I only wanted to one-sidedly let out my thoughts, only to have her watch as I try to stop myself from saying too much.

findings.highlight: her words enter my head, and one after another, they wreak havoc
findings.evidenceJa: 否定の言葉が、次から次へと頭の中に浮かび、そして、次から次へと頭の中で潰していく
findings.explanation: Words denying Setsuna's self-condemnation rise one after another in Haruki's mind, and he crushes each one before speaking it. The English makes Setsuna's words invade and damage him, erasing his deliberate silence.
findings.japanese:
否定の言葉が、次から次へと頭の中に浮かび、
そして、次から次へと頭の中で潰していく。
findings.todokanai: One after another, her words enter my head, and one after another, they wreak havoc.

findings.highlight: one that is exactly like her to make
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に雪菜らしい、偽悪の言葉だった
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes Setsuna's apology as characteristically 偽悪: language that falsely casts herself as the villain. The English calls the interpretation merely like her, omitting the explicit mechanism of self-villainization.
findings.japanese:
その雪菜の謝罪は、
あまりにも一方的な解釈に囚われた、
本当に雪菜らしい、偽悪の言葉だったけど。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna's apology came from a one-sided interpretation, one that is exactly like her to make.

findings.highlight: with a complete lie
findings.evidenceJa: 最低の偽善で応えた
findings.explanation: Haruki answers Setsuna's false self-condemnation with what he calls the worst hypocrisy: assuring her Kazusa will play while seeing evidence that she needed him present. A lie is not the same moral category as self-serving hypocritical consolation.
findings.japanese:
それでも、敢えて俺は、
その言葉に、最低の偽善で応えた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, I answer her words with a complete lie.

findings.highlight: to never do anything that would get in the way
findings.evidenceJa: 護るための障害となるようなことは、一切約束しないって、新しい誓い
findings.explanation: Haruki vows never to make any promise that could become an obstacle to protecting Kazusa. The English says he will never perform an obstructive action, losing the passage's recursive distinction between vows and the freedom to break expectations.
findings.japanese:
そして、護るための障害となるようなことは、
一切約束しないって、新しい誓いを立てた。
findings.todokanai: And so I made another vow, to never do anything that would get in the way of protecting her.

findings.highlight: Be my reason to work as hard as I can.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が頑張れるように、一生、俺の負担になってくれ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks Kazusa to remain his burden for life so that carrying her will give him strength to strive. The English keeps the motivation but omits the deliberately paradoxical request that she burden him.
findings.japanese:
「俺のために、ずっと役立たずでいてくれ。
俺が頑張れるように、一生、俺の負担になってくれ」
findings.todokanai: "Be useless, for my sake. Be my reason to work as hard as I can."

findings.highlight: Something that is of absolutely no use to Kazusa
findings.evidenceJa: かずさは自分の中に何も生み出さない。けれど、俺の中に強いエネルギーを灯してくれる
findings.explanation: Kazusa produces nothing within herself, but lights a powerful energy within Haruki. The English changes internal production into usefulness to Kazusa and drops the contrast between emptiness in her and generation in him.
findings.japanese:
かずさは自分の中に何も生み出さない。
けれど、俺の中に強いエネルギーを灯してくれる。
findings.todokanai: Something that is of absolutely no use to Kazusa, yet gives me a powerful energy.

findings.highlight: keep saying things like that and I actually might
findings.evidenceJa: 今からそんな縁起でもないこと考えてたって
findings.explanation: Haruki protests that there is no point thinking such ill-omened thoughts already. The English has him say Kazusa's words might actually cause his early death.
findings.japanese:
「お前なぁ…
今からそんな縁起でもないこと考えてたって」
findings.todokanai: "Hey… keep saying things like that and I actually might."

findings.highlight: I'll do everything I can to make something of myself
findings.evidenceJa: あたしは絶対やり遂げてみせるからな
findings.explanation: Kazusa defiantly vows she will absolutely follow through on killing herself after Haruki dies and challenges him to stop her if he can. The English turns this into the life-affirming promise to make something of herself.
findings.japanese:
「それこそ、何とでも言え、だ。
あたしは絶対やり遂げてみせるからな。
…止められるものなら止めてみろ」
findings.todokanai: "And you can say whatever you want. I'll do everything I can to make something of myself… and if you think you can stop me, I dare you to try."

findings.highlight: if we could have managed to keep the balance between us
findings.evidenceJa: 三人の平均を取れば、だけどな
findings.explanation: Kazusa jokes that the wedding future was happiest only when the three people's happiness is averaged: Setsuna and Haruki gain much, while Kazusa suffers at the organ. The English replaces this explicit arithmetic joke with maintaining relationship balance.
findings.japanese:
「そんな未来が、三人にとって一番幸せだったんだ。
………三人の平均を取れば、だけどな」
findings.todokanai: "That future would have been the happiest future for the three of us… only if we could have managed to keep the balance between us."

findings.highlight: a smile that could tear herself apart
findings.evidenceJa: 俺にとっては、とんでもなく身勝手だけど、身を引き裂かれる笑顔
findings.explanation: To Haruki, Setsuna's withdrawal is outrageously selfish and her smile tears him apart. The English makes the smile tear Setsuna herself apart and omits Haruki's pained accusation of selfishness.
findings.japanese:
そして俺にとっては、
とんでもなく身勝手だけど、身を引き裂かれる笑顔。
findings.todokanai: And in my eyes, she wore a smile that could tear herself apart.

findings.highlight: our check-out from this place
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちの精算
findings.explanation: Setsuna begins the final settling of accounts between herself and Haruki. The English literalizes 精算 as checking out of a location, erasing the emotional reckoning.
findings.japanese: 俺たちの精算を…始める。
findings.todokanai: She begins our check-out from this place.

findings.highlight: Snow that only ever fell during times of hardship and sorrow.
findings.evidenceJa: 辛いこと、悲しいことを時期限定で埋め尽くす、白い幕
findings.explanation: Snow is the white curtain that appears at their crossroads and blankets painful and sad things only temporarily. The English says it falls only during hardship and sorrow, moving 時期限定 from the duration of concealment to the occasions of snowfall and losing the warning that the cover will melt.
findings.japanese:
いつも俺たちの分岐点に現れ、
辛いこと、悲しいことを時期限定で埋め尽くす、白い幕。
findings.todokanai: The curtain of white that always appeared during the crossroads of our lives. Snow that only ever fell during times of hardship and sorrow.

findings.highlight: I can no longer be with Setsuna. That's what she herself has said to me.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺は、もう、
雪菜の側に寄り添えない。
自分で、そして雪菜に言ってもらったじゃないか。
findings.explanation: Haruki says both he himself and Setsuna have told him he can no longer stay beside her; the English credits only Setsuna — His self-imposed separation is explicit throughout the scene.
findings.japanese:
俺は、もう、
雪菜の側に寄り添えない。
自分で、そして雪菜に言ってもらったじゃないか。
findings.todokanai: I can no longer be with Setsuna. That's what she herself has said to me.

findings.highlight: Touma Kazusa confirmed to settle down in Japan.
findings.evidenceJa: スポーツ紙や大衆週刊誌はこぞって『冬馬かずさ　今後は日本を拠点に活動』と報道し、誤解はとうとう世間にまで浸透した。
findings.explanation: The mistaken reports say Kazusa will henceforth base her professional activities in Japan. The English upgrades that to a confirmed permanent personal settlement, conflating the media's inference with Youko's separate permanent-residence announcement.
findings.japanese:
スポーツ紙や大衆週刊誌はこぞって
『冬馬かずさ　今後は日本を拠点に活動』と報道し、
誤解はとうとう世間にまで浸透した。
findings.todokanai: From sports weeklys to gossip magazines, it was reported as "Touma Kazusa confirmed to settle down in Japan." And this misunderstanding has already spread to the general public.

findings.highlight: Kazusa's popularity in Japan experienced another boom
findings.evidenceJa: その流れは、コンサートのブルーレイ発売発表と絡み、日本に、新たな冬馬家ブームを巻き起こした。
findings.explanation: The announcement and Blu-ray news create a new boom around the Touma family as a public phenomenon—mother and daughter together. The English narrows this to another rise in Kazusa's individual popularity.
findings.japanese:
その流れは、コンサートのブルーレイ発売発表と絡み、
日本に、新たな冬馬家ブームを巻き起こした。
findings.todokanai: And thanks to that, Kazusa's popularity in Japan experienced another boom, with blu-ray recordings of her concert being announced.

findings.highlight: By being with me, she'll be happy. She'll smile for me just by being next to me…
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつが俺の側にいることで幸せになってくれるなら。隣にいるときだけでも笑ってくれるなら…」
findings.explanation: Haruki offers a conditional justification: if being beside him makes Kazusa happy, if she can smile at least while she is beside him. The English turns that fragile hope into confident statements that she will be happy and smile for him.
findings.japanese:
「あいつが俺の側にいることで
幸せになってくれるなら。
隣にいるときだけでも笑ってくれるなら…」
findings.todokanai: "By being with me, she'll be happy. She'll smile for me just by being next to me…"

findings.highlight: "Well, I do plan on living moderately long."
findings.evidenceJa: 「ま、ほどほどに生きるつもり」
findings.explanation: ほどほどに生きる means Youko plans to live with moderation; 'living moderately long' converts manner into lifespan — Kazusa's pleas for treatment compliance and Youko's promise to keep living remain.
findings.japanese: 「ま、ほどほどに生きるつもり」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I do plan on living moderately long."

findings.highlight: "You left the Vienna office to me. I won't be able to do anything useful for it, but Haruki will be able to do anything."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ウィーンの事務所の方は任せといて。
あたしは役に立たないけど、
春希が何もかもやってくれるから」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says to leave the Vienna office to her; the English changes this into a past action by Youko — Haruki's future operational role and Kazusa's self-deprecation remain explicit.
findings.japanese:
「ウィーンの事務所の方は任せといて。
あたしは役に立たないけど、
春希が何もかもやってくれるから」
findings.todokanai: "You left the Vienna office to me. I won't be able to do anything useful for it, but Haruki will be able to do anything."

findings.highlight: If you're going to play, make sure you enjoy it… and make him happy.
findings.evidenceJa: 「贖罪のための演奏なんてつまんない。やるならとことん色っぽく楽しみなさい。…そうやって彼を幸せにしてあげなさい」
findings.explanation: Youko tells Kazusa not merely to enjoy playing, but to enjoy it thoroughly and sensually/sexily, and thereby make Haruki happy. Dropping 色っぽく erases the route-long identification of Kazusa's erotic feeling with the mature color of her piano.
findings.japanese:
「贖罪のための演奏なんてつまんない。
やるならとことん色っぽく楽しみなさい。
…そうやって彼を幸せにしてあげなさい」
findings.todokanai: "No one wants to hear a musical performance born from a desire for atonement. If you're going to play, make sure you enjoy it… and make him happy."

findings.highlight: it was the only thing I wanted to keep, only so I could give it back to the manufacturer.
findings.evidenceJa: 荷物を運び出し、鍵を返したとき、それだけは捨てるつもりで手に持っていたのを、業者に渡し忘れていただけ。
findings.explanation: Haruki had the guitar in his hand intending to throw it away and simply forgot to hand it to the removal contractor. The English reverses disposal into wanting to keep it and misreads the contractor as the guitar's manufacturer.
findings.japanese:
荷物を運び出し、鍵を返したとき、
それだけは捨てるつもりで手に持っていたのを、
業者に渡し忘れていただけ。
findings.todokanai: When I had carried out all my luggage and handed over the key, it was the only thing I wanted to keep, only so I could give it back to the manufacturer.

findings.highlight: I also trust they'll handle it appropriately.
findings.evidenceJa: 多分今ごろは管理会社が見つけて、ちょっと迷惑そうな態度で、適当に処分してるはず。
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines the management company finding the abandoned guitar and disposing of it casually, with some annoyance. The English instead says he trusts them to handle it appropriately, reversing the contemptuous finality of the image.
findings.japanese:
多分今ごろは管理会社が見つけて、
ちょっと迷惑そうな態度で、適当に処分してるはず。
findings.todokanai: I imagine the management company is handling it with a rather troubled attitude, though I also trust they'll handle it appropriately.

findings.highlight: I feel something running down my cheeks.
findings.evidenceJa: かずさの優しい声と温かい息が耳にかかり、そして、目元に柔らかい布が押しつけられる。
findings.explanation: Kazusa leans close and presses a soft cloth to Haruki's eyes, gently wiping tears he has not noticed. The English replaces her consoling physical action with liquid running down his cheeks.
findings.japanese:
かずさの優しい声と温かい息が耳にかかり、
そして、目元に柔らかい布が押しつけられる。
findings.todokanai: The sensation of Kazusa's warm, gentle breath touches my ears, and I feel something running down my cheeks.

findings.highlight: She wants to hold me tight, but she can't bring herself to…
findings.evidenceJa: 抱きしめたいけれど、抱きしめられない…
findings.explanation: Kazusa wants to embrace Haruki but physically cannot because both are strapped into airplane seats; she reaches as far as she can. 'Can't bring herself to' instead attributes emotional hesitation to her at the moment of wholehearted consolation.
findings.japanese: 抱きしめたいけれど、抱きしめられない…
findings.todokanai: She wants to hold me tight, but she can't bring herself to…

findings.highlight: The conversation was with a newspaper company we've known for a long time, but it seems that their management has changed, so I had to spend the whole day explaining things.
findings.evidenceJa: いつも付き合いのある雑誌社からだったけど、担当が替わったらしく、色々と話が通らず、つい長電話になってしまった。
findings.explanation: A familiar magazine publisher calls, but its individual contact person has changed, so mutual understanding is poor and the call runs long. The English turns the publisher into a newspaper company, the contact into management, and a long late-night call into a whole day of explanation.
findings.japanese:
いつも付き合いのある雑誌社からだったけど、
担当が替わったらしく、色々と話が通らず、
つい長電話になってしまった。
findings.todokanai: The conversation was with a newspaper company we've known for a long time, but it seems that their management has changed, so I had to spend the whole day explaining things.

findings.highlight: Not that I don't do that in my free time anyway.
findings.evidenceJa: それこそ下着を穿くのだって、下手すりゃマネージャーにやらせようとするくらい。…いや、脱がす方なら普通にやるんだけど。
findings.explanation: Haruki says Kazusa might even make her manager put her underwear on, then corrects himself: taking it off is something he routinely does. The English leaves 'that' directionless and loses the reversal from caretaking to sex that makes the punchline.
findings.japanese:
それこそ下着を穿くのだって、
下手すりゃマネージャーにやらせようとするくらい。
…いや、脱がす方なら普通にやるんだけど。
findings.todokanai: Sometimes she even makes her manager put on her underwear for her… Not that I don't do that in my free time anyway.

findings.highlight: You already know I'm the most clingy person in the world.
findings.evidenceJa: 「答えのわかってる質問をするな。あたしが世界一の甘党だってこと、世界一知ってるくせに」
findings.explanation: After Haruki asks whether she dislikes being spoiled (甘やかす), Kazusa says he knows better than anyone that she is the world's greatest 甘党—literally sweet tooth, figuratively addicted to his sweetness/indulgence. 'Most clingy person' removes the lexical joke and changes liking to be spoiled into initiating attachment.
findings.japanese:
「答えのわかってる質問をするな。
あたしが世界一の甘党だってこと、
世界一知ってるくせに」
findings.todokanai: "Don't ask questions you know the answer to. You already know I'm the most clingy person in the world."

findings.highlight: the only people the European branch consists of is the pianist herself, and her sole manager, just like in Japan.
findings.evidenceJa: それ以来、株式会社冬馬曜子オフィス欧州支部は、一人の所属アーティストと一人のマネージャーという、日本人のみの最小構成で稼動してる。
findings.explanation: The European branch operates in the smallest possible all-Japanese configuration: one represented artist and one manager. The English invents a comparison 'just like in Japan' and omits both the nationality point and deliberate minimality.
findings.japanese:
それ以来、株式会社冬馬曜子オフィス欧州支部は、
一人の所属アーティストと一人のマネージャーという、
日本人のみの最小構成で稼動してる。
findings.todokanai: Since then, the only people the European branch consists of is the pianist herself, and her sole manager, just like in Japan.

findings.highlight: By the way, that sole pianist with the household name "Touma Kazusa" attempted to replace it with her new real name.
findings.evidenceJa:
ちなみに昨年、その唯一の所属アーティストは、
冬馬かずさという“芸名”を、
“新しい本名”に合わせようとした。
findings.explanation: Touma Kazusa is explicitly her stage name, which she tried to align with her new legal name; 'household name' is an unsuitable rendering — The next line's business insistence on retaining Touma makes the surname conflict recoverable.
findings.japanese:
ちなみに昨年、その唯一の所属アーティストは、
冬馬かずさという“芸名”を、
“新しい本名”に合わせようとした。
findings.todokanai: By the way, that sole pianist with the household name "Touma Kazusa" attempted to replace it with her new real name.

findings.highlight: she attended a lecture in Hokkaido just last month… One about sea urchins, salmon roe, crabs and scallops apparently.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ああ、元気いっぱいみたいだぞ。先月北海道に講演に行ってきたんだってさ。…ウニとイクラとカニとホタテの話ばかりだけど」
findings.explanation: Youko went to Hokkaido to give a lecture; her message to them merely talks incessantly about the seafood she ate. The English makes her an attendee at a seafood lecture, reversing her professional role and missing the cover-story joke later exposed at the hospital.
findings.japanese:
「ああ、元気いっぱいみたいだぞ。
先月北海道に講演に行ってきたんだってさ。
…ウニとイクラとカニとホタテの話ばかりだけど」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, she seems to be doing just fine. She says she attended a lecture in Hokkaido just last month… One about sea urchins, salmon roe, crabs and scallops apparently."

findings.highlight: we reach out our fingers and wipe off each other's tears, and heal our invisible wounds.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちは、お互いそのことを何も話したりしない。ただ、相手の涙を指で拭いたり、舌先で舐め取ったり、そうやって、見えない傷を舐めて癒しあう。
findings.explanation: Haruki and Kazusa silently wipe one another's tears with their fingers or lick them away with the tips of their tongues, literally enacting the idiom of licking each other's wounds. The English deletes the tongue contact and therefore the physicalized wordplay.
findings.japanese:
俺たちは、お互いそのことを何も話したりしない。
ただ、相手の涙を指で拭いたり、舌先で舐め取ったり、
そうやって、見えない傷を舐めて癒しあう。
findings.todokanai: The two of us never talk about it. Instead, we reach out our fingers and wipe off each other's tears, and heal our invisible wounds.

findings.highlight: We still refuse to talk about that country.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちはまだ、あの国のことを口に出せずにいる。
findings.explanation: Two years later they remain unable to bring themselves to speak about Japan. 'Refuse' gives them a deliberate, controlled choice where the source describes traumatic incapacity.
findings.japanese: 俺たちはまだ、あの国のことを口に出せずにいる。
findings.todokanai: We still refuse to talk about that country.

findings.highlight: A few dozen files appear on my download bar.
findings.evidenceJa: 数十メガのファイルがディスクのアクセスランプとともに流れ込んでいく。
findings.explanation: A single file tens of megabytes in size streams onto the disk as its access light flickers. The English invents several dozen files and a download bar.
findings.japanese:
数十メガのファイルが
ディスクのアクセスランプとともに流れ込んでいく。
findings.todokanai: A few dozen files appear on my download bar.

findings.highlight: The girl who makes me repress her in my heart so that my words don't leak from my mouth
findings.evidenceJa: 口から漏れない分、心の中に溜まり込み、今でも鮮明に、二年前の姿形を思い起こせる、彼女。
findings.explanation: Because Haruki never lets Setsuna's name escape his mouth, thoughts of her accumulate inside his heart. The English reverses the causal direction and makes Setsuna the agent forcing him to repress her so that he will not speak.
findings.japanese:
口から漏れない分、心の中に溜まり込み、
今でも鮮明に、二年前の姿形を思い起こせる、彼女。
findings.todokanai: The girl who makes me repress her in my heart so that my words don't leak from my mouth, the girl whose figure is still vivid in my mind two years later.

findings.highlight: You've breathed your last, Ogiso Setsuna
findings.evidenceJa: 「そうそう。何かと言えば『打倒、小木曽雪菜！』ってさ。そのためなら誰を陥れても構わないみたいな」
findings.explanation: Tomo's old slogan was 'Defeat Ogiso Setsuna!' or 'Down with Ogiso Setsuna!'—a melodramatic rivalry cry. 'You've breathed your last' converts it into a death threat and wildly escalates the recalled school hostility.
findings.japanese:
「そうそう。
何かと言えば『打倒、小木曽雪菜！』ってさ。
そのためなら誰を陥れても構わないみたいな」
findings.todokanai: "Right, right! She'd say things like, 'You've breathed your last, Ogiso Setsuna' and wouldn't mind tricking anyone to put her down."

findings.highlight: cast doubt on any future performance being held
findings.evidenceJa: 「実は現在、深刻な体調不良ということで次回公演の開催が危ぶまれていることが、関係者の話で明らかになりました」
findings.explanation: The report casts doubt on the next scheduled performance—the additional concert—because of serious ill health. 'Any future performance' broadens the rumor into possible permanent cessation.
findings.japanese:
「実は現在、深刻な体調不良ということで
次回公演の開催が危ぶまれていることが、
関係者の話で明らかになりました」
findings.todokanai: "However, recent statements made by related sources have cast doubt on any future performance being held, due to poor health."

findings.highlight: Wasn't that all already decided in the plan from the very beginning?
findings.evidenceJa: 「ええ、ええ………何ですって？　そんな…それ、初っ端に向こうにハねられた企画じゃないですか」
findings.explanation: Hamada says the other party rejected that proposal at the outset. The English says it had already been decided in the plan from the beginning, reversing rejection into prior approval.
findings.japanese:
「ええ、ええ………何ですって？　そんな…
それ、初っ端に向こうにハねられた企画じゃないですか」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, yeah… What did you just say? But that's… Wasn't that all already decided in the plan from the very beginning?"

findings.highlight: Did Yoshimatsu-san tell you about all that?
findings.evidenceJa: 「吉松さんが通したんですか？　それ。え、だから俺じゃ…」
findings.explanation: Hamada asks whether Yoshimatsu got the proposal approved. The English asks whether Yoshimatsu merely told the other person about it, losing the approval maneuver that reveals Haruki played both superiors.
findings.japanese:
「吉松さんが通したんですか？　それ。
え、だから俺じゃ…」
findings.todokanai: "Did Yoshimatsu-san tell you about all that? No, like I said, it wasn't me…"

findings.highlight: "If you're looking for Kitahara, he went home immediately after the briefing earlier. He did show his face before you came to work, though."
findings.evidenceJa:
「北原なら打ち合わせで直帰になってますよ。
浜田さんが出社する前に顔出してましたけどね」
findings.explanation: 直帰 means Haruki will go straight home after an outside meeting, not that he already went home after an earlier briefing — The essential fact that he is absent from the office is preserved.
findings.japanese:
「北原なら打ち合わせで直帰になってますよ。
浜田さんが出社する前に顔出してましたけどね」
findings.todokanai: "If you're looking for Kitahara, he went home immediately after the briefing earlier. He did show his face before you came to work, though."

findings.highlight: It seems that they're wary about meeting us
findings.evidenceJa: 「なんか会ってる気配なかったし、雪菜ちゃんに聞いても、どことなくぎこちなかったし」
findings.explanation: Takeya says there has been no sign Haruki and Setsuna are seeing each other, and Setsuna acted awkward when asked. The English instead says the couple are wary of meeting Takeya and Io, replacing the suspected romantic separation with social avoidance of the speakers.
findings.japanese:
「なんか会ってる気配なかったし、
雪菜ちゃんに聞いても、どことなくぎこちなかったし」
findings.todokanai: "It seems that they're wary about meeting us, and Setsuna-chan didn't really give me anything to work with when I inquired about things on her end."
