findings.highlight: Could he have gotten himself involved in Touma's affairs again?
findings.evidenceJa: 「…まさかあいつ、まだ冬馬のこと引きずってるんじゃないだろうな」
findings.explanation: Takeya fears Haruki may still be emotionally hung up on Touma. The English reduces this to renewed involvement in her affairs, erasing the romantic suspicion driving Io's panic.
findings.japanese:
「…まさかあいつ、
まだ冬馬のこと引きずってるんじゃないだろうな」
findings.todokanai: "…Could he have gotten himself involved in Touma's affairs again?"

findings.highlight: "…And you can't even reassure yourself properly despite causing me to worry."
findings.evidenceJa:
「…しかも人の不安煽っておいて
自己解決しないでよね」
findings.explanation: Io objects that Takeya stirred up her anxiety and then resolved the issue only for himself; the English says he cannot reassure himself properly — Her frustration at being left anxious remains evident.
findings.japanese:
「…しかも人の不安煽っておいて
自己解決しないでよね」
findings.todokanai: "…And you can't even reassure yourself properly despite causing me to worry."

findings.highlight: people will be less skeptical when my illness is reported on.
findings.evidenceJa: 「…なるほど、かずさの件がガセとわかったら、今度は冬馬曜子だと言っても誰も信用しない、か」
findings.explanation: Youko realizes that once the Kazusa illness story is exposed as false, nobody will believe a later report that the patient was actually Youko. The English says people will become less skeptical—more likely to believe her illness—the exact opposite of Miyoko's diversion.
findings.japanese:
「…なるほど、かずさの件がガセとわかったら、
今度は冬馬曜子だと言っても誰も信用しない、か」
findings.todokanai: "…I see. Once it is made known Kazusa was fine all along, people will be less skeptical when my illness is reported on."

findings.highlight: The moment you made your decision, I started working on everything
findings.evidenceJa: 「社長が決断した瞬間に、すぐに各方面が動けるように手配しています。損害も最小限に抑えられるように手を打ちました」
findings.explanation: Miyoko has arranged matters so every party can move the instant Youko makes her still-pending decision. The English says Youko already decided and Miyoko only then began work, contradicting the prepared-options discussion.
findings.japanese:
「社長が決断した瞬間に、
すぐに各方面が動けるように手配しています。
損害も最小限に抑えられるように手を打ちました」
findings.todokanai: "The moment you made your decision, I started working on everything on all sides, minimizing the possible damage."

findings.highlight: I feel tired enough to want to call a taxi.
findings.evidenceJa: 始発が動き出すまでにはまだ時間があり、タクシーを使ってまで動こうという気力も湧かず。
findings.explanation: Haruki has no energy or will to move even if it means taking a taxi. The English says his fatigue makes him want to call one, reversing his paralysis into a desire for transport.
findings.japanese:
始発が動き出すまでにはまだ時間があり、
タクシーを使ってまで動こうという気力も湧かず。
findings.todokanai: There's still some time before the first train departs, and I feel tired enough to want to call a taxi.

findings.highlight: Put it in your pocket and you'll feel nice and warm… oh, what am I saying?
findings.evidenceJa: 「これ、使い捨てカイロ。懐に入れて温めておきました…なんてね」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she kept the disposable warmer inside her clothes to warm it for Haruki, then playfully retracts the intimate claim. The English tells Haruki to put it in his own pocket and makes her embarrassment causeless.
findings.japanese:
「これ、使い捨てカイロ。
懐に入れて温めておきました…なんてね」
findings.todokanai: "Here, take this disposable heat pack. Put it in your pocket and you'll feel nice and warm… oh, what am I saying?"

findings.highlight: That I'd stay by Kazusa's side from now on.
findings.evidenceJa: かずさから逃げないって。今はかずさの側にいるって。
findings.explanation: Haruki promised not to flee Kazusa and to remain beside her for now, until she was reassured. 'From now on' extends the bounded crisis commitment into an indefinite future and conflicts with the condition stated two lines later.
findings.japanese:
かずさから逃げないって。
今はかずさの側にいるって。
findings.todokanai: That I wouldn't run away from Kazusa. That I'd stay by Kazusa's side from now on.

findings.highlight: "No, perhaps it was a mistake to even suggest that I would be able to support her in the first place… In the end, it was all pointless."
findings.evidenceJa:
「いや、俺が支えようとすることそのものが
間違ってたのかも。
…やっぱり俺じゃ、駄目だったんだ」
findings.explanation: Haruki concludes that he himself is no good for Kazusa; 'it was all pointless' relocates the judgment to the effort — His self-condemnation and Setsuna's denial remain emotionally aligned.
findings.japanese:
「いや、俺が支えようとすることそのものが
間違ってたのかも。
…やっぱり俺じゃ、駄目だったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "No, perhaps it was a mistake to even suggest that I would be able to support her in the first place… In the end, it was all pointless."

findings.highlight: how much you've been held down as well
findings.evidenceJa: 「この二週間のこと。春希くんがどう頑張って、どう挫折したのかを」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks how Haruki tried and how he failed or broke down. The English says he was 'held down,' shifting his acknowledged failure into something externally done to him.
findings.japanese:
「この二週間のこと。
春希くんがどう頑張って、どう挫折したのかを」
findings.todokanai: "Tell me everything that's happened these two weeks. How much you've worked hard, Haruki-kun, and how much you've been held down as well…"

findings.highlight: you didn't even want to take the initiative to contact me at all.
findings.evidenceJa: 「あ～あ、連絡欲しかったな。かずさ、昔の携帯番号繋がらないし。何より、わたしから連絡入れても嫌だろうし」
findings.explanation: Setsuna wanted contact, but Kazusa's old number no longer worked and Setsuna assumed Kazusa would hate being contacted by her. The English instead says Kazusa did not want to initiate contact, reversing who contemplated calling whom.
findings.japanese:
「あ～あ、連絡欲しかったな。
かずさ、昔の携帯番号繋がらないし。
何より、わたしから連絡入れても嫌だろうし」
findings.todokanai: "Aa-ah, I really wanted to get in touch with you. Your old phone number doesn't work anymore, after all, and more importantly, you didn't even want to take the initiative to contact me at all."

findings.highlight: She had her doubts, of course.
findings.evidenceJa: 「もちろん、コネはあったよ。春希くんが直接曜子さんに口利きしたから、理屈抜きでウチが仕事を取れた」
findings.explanation: Setsuna admits they had connections: Haruki directly put in a word with Youko, letting Knights obtain the work outside normal logic. The English translates コネ as doubts, making the next sentence disconnected.
findings.japanese:
「もちろん、コネはあったよ。
春希くんが直接曜子さんに口利きしたから、
理屈抜きでウチが仕事を取れた」
findings.todokanai: "She had her doubts, of course. It was Haruki-kun who managed to persuade Youko-san and make her give this job over to us."

findings.highlight: You'd be happy as long as Haruki-kun reciprocated your feelings?
findings.evidenceJa: 「ただ、好きな人を振り向かせられたら良かった？…春希くんにさえ、届けば良かった？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether Kazusa wanted only to make her beloved turn toward her—if only she could reach Haruki. The English converts 届く, the work's load-bearing reach/unreachable motif, into explicit reciprocation.
findings.japanese:
「ただ、好きな人を振り向かせられたら良かった？
…春希くんにさえ、届けば良かった？」
findings.todokanai: "You'd be happy by simply having the person you love look at you? …You'd be happy as long as Haruki-kun reciprocated your feelings?"

findings.highlight: I do remember something like that happening in the past.
findings.evidenceJa: 「あと二週間かぁ…昔も、そんなやっつけ仕事があったね」
findings.explanation: Setsuna pointedly recalls another two-week rush job: the improvised school-festival performance that formed the trio. The vague English loses both やっつけ仕事 ('rush/slapdash job') and the callback binding this recording project to that origin.
findings.japanese:
「あと二週間かぁ…
昔も、そんなやっつけ仕事があったね」
findings.todokanai: "Two weeks left… I do remember something like that happening in the past."

findings.highlight: I can't do this anymore…
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺じゃ、駄目だった」
findings.explanation: Haruki says that he was no good for Kazusa—he was not enough and could not save her. The English instead says he can no longer continue, turning a judgment of his inadequacy into a decision to stop.
findings.japanese: 「俺じゃ、駄目だった」
findings.todokanai: "I can't do this anymore…"

findings.highlight: So many things happened, and now I have no choice but to rely on her
findings.evidenceJa: 色々あって、あいつが頼れなくなってしまった…けれど一度は、永遠の友情を誓い合った相手だから。
findings.explanation: Setsuna is the friend Kazusa became unable to rely on after everything that happened, even though they once swore eternal friendship. The English instead says Haruki now has no choice but to rely on Setsuna, reversing both subject and direction.
findings.japanese:
色々あって、あいつが頼れなくなってしまった…
けれど一度は、永遠の友情を誓い合った相手だから。
findings.todokanai: So many things happened, and now I have no choice but to rely on her… but they did once swear eternal friendship to each other.

findings.highlight: the beautiful descendant of a pianist who won a prize at the Giovanni Competition
findings.evidenceJa: 「それで、次の手を模索してたところに出てきたのが、美人二世ピアニストのジェバンニコンクール入賞…」
findings.explanation: The drawcard that appears is Kazusa: a beautiful second-generation pianist who herself placed in the Giovanni Competition. The English grammatically makes her an attractive descendant of some pianist who won the prize.
findings.japanese:
「それで、次の手を模索してたところに出てきたのが、
美人二世ピアニストのジェバンニコンクール入賞…」
findings.todokanai: "And from there, after searching, we ended up chancing upon the beautiful descendant of a pianist who won a prize at the Giovanni Competition…"

findings.highlight: Getting money off fame without doing anything is no different from scamming others.
findings.evidenceJa: 「どこがだよ…腕もないのに人気だけで金を稼ぐなんて、そんなの、詐欺みたいなもんだ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says earning money from popularity despite lacking ability would be fraudulent, exposing her professional insecurity. 'Without doing anything' instead accuses the hypothetical star of laziness rather than insufficient skill.
findings.japanese:
「どこがだよ…
腕もないのに人気だけで金を稼ぐなんて、
そんなの、詐欺みたいなもんだ」
findings.todokanai: "How exactly…? Getting money off fame without doing anything is no different from scamming others."

findings.highlight: I was simply trying to lighten the mood, you know?
findings.evidenceJa: 「どうかな？ただのウサ晴らしかもしれないよ？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna suggests she may simply be venting her own frustration on Kazusa. The English says she is trying to lighten the mood, reversing a hostile cathartic motive into a benevolent social one.
findings.japanese:
「どうかな？
ただのウサ晴らしかもしれないよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Who knows? I was simply trying to lighten the mood, you know?"

findings.highlight: given that everything Youko-san's done has been for Kazusa's sake, she doesn't really know much about Setsuna at all.
findings.evidenceJa: 何しろ、今まで彼女がかずさのためにしてきたことは、雪菜をよく知らないからこそできたとも言える訳で。
findings.explanation: The point is causal and morally damning: Youko could do everything she did for Kazusa precisely because she did not know Setsuna well. The English states two disconnected facts and erases the implication that ignorance enabled her cruelty.
findings.japanese:
何しろ、今まで彼女がかずさのためにしてきたことは、
雪菜をよく知らないからこそできたとも言える訳で。
findings.todokanai: In any case, given that everything Youko-san's done has been for Kazusa's sake, she doesn't really know much about Setsuna at all.

findings.highlight: She feels that she's worth fighting for.
findings.evidenceJa: 目の前にいる人が、かずさと同じだって気づいたから。戦うに値する相手だって、感じ取ったから。
findings.explanation: Setsuna recognizes Youko as like Kazusa—an opponent worthy of fighting. 'Worth fighting for' makes Youko a beneficiary whom Setsuna wishes to defend, reversing the combative relationship.
findings.japanese:
目の前にいる人が、かずさと同じだって気づいたから。
戦うに値する相手だって、感じ取ったから。
findings.todokanai: She's realized that the person before her is very similar to Kazusa. She feels that she's worth fighting for.

findings.highlight: I like you, Kazusa! Is me liking you not a good enough reason, Kazusa!?
findings.evidenceJa: 「好きだから！かずさのこと、大好きだからじゃいけないの！？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna escalates from 好き to 大好き: she loves Kazusa dearly and asks why that cannot justify staying. The English flattens both to 'like,' repeating the same weakening at line 284 despite the scene's explicit like/love/hate vocabulary.
findings.japanese:
「好きだから！
かずさのこと、大好きだからじゃいけないの！？」
findings.todokanai: "I like you, Kazusa! Is me liking you not a good enough reason, Kazusa!?"

findings.highlight: Who ever decided that it's impossible to like horrible people?
findings.evidenceJa: 「最低な人を好きになっちゃいけないなんて、一体誰が決めたのよ！？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks who decided one must not love a terrible person—a challenge to moral prohibition. The English asks who decided it is impossible, collapsing her ethical defense into a factual argument about capacity.
findings.japanese:
「最低な人を好きになっちゃいけないなんて、
一体誰が決めたのよ！？」
findings.todokanai: "Who ever decided that it's impossible to like horrible people?"

findings.highlight: As Setsuna momentarily left to plant the flower she'd brought
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜が花を生けるために席を外すと、曜子さんは、なんだか呆れたような視線で俺を見上げた。
findings.explanation: Setsuna steps away to arrange the cut flowers in a vase. The English says she leaves to plant the moth orchid inside a hospital, producing a physically and culturally wrong action.
findings.japanese:
雪菜が花を生けるために席を外すと、
曜子さんは、なんだか呆れたような視線で俺を見上げた。
findings.todokanai: As Setsuna momentarily left to plant the flower she'd brought, Youko-san suddenly stared at me with a bewildered expression for some reason.

findings.highlight: The client which we're giving our proposal to is currently in the hospital. And the person who's giving that proposal hasn't really gone through any of the official procedures required; instead, he simply rode on the fact that Youko-san's the mother of her friend to push it upon her.
findings.evidenceJa:
売り込むべきクライアントは入院中。
しかも、何一つ正式な段取りを踏まずに、
ただ、友達の母親というコネを利用しただけのゴリ押し。
findings.explanation: The source describes the proposal as a brute-force use of a friend's-mother connection; the English assigns the presentation to a male 'he,' despite Setsuna delivering it and the pair devising it — Their joint authorship and Haruki's role in obtaining access are both established.
findings.japanese:
売り込むべきクライアントは入院中。
しかも、何一つ正式な段取りを踏まずに、
ただ、友達の母親というコネを利用しただけのゴリ押し。
findings.todokanai: The client which we're giving our proposal to is currently in the hospital. And the person who's giving that proposal hasn't really gone through any of the official procedures required; instead, he simply rode on the fact that Youko-san's the mother of her friend to push it upon her.

findings.highlight: for a girl who's trying to take back the man she loves?
findings.evidenceJa: 「普通、ここまでする？ふった女のために。自分の彼にコナかけてくる女のために」
findings.explanation: Youko asks whether anyone would go this far for a woman her boyfriend rejected who is now making a pass at that boyfriend. The English says Kazusa is trying to 'take back' the man she loves, granting her prior ownership and removing Setsuna's relationship boundary.
findings.japanese:
「普通、ここまでする？
ふった女のために。
自分の彼にコナかけてくる女のために」
findings.todokanai: "Would someone usually go so far? For a girl you rejected… for a girl who's trying to take back the man she loves?"

findings.highlight: She's important to us…
findings.evidenceJa: 「大事な奴なんです…」
findings.explanation: Haruki answers personally: Kazusa is someone important to him. The English pluralizes this into 'important to us,' diffusing his continuing individual attachment into the joint rescue project.
findings.japanese: 「大事な奴なんです…」
findings.todokanai: "She's important to us…"

findings.highlight: I imagine only Kazusa would forgive me in such a scenario…
findings.evidenceJa: かずさだけは、許すって…
findings.explanation: In context Haruki recognizes that Setsuna, unlike Youko or Haruki, would forgive Kazusa alone. The English instead says Kazusa alone would forgive Haruki, reversing both forgiver and forgiven at the pivot that demonstrates Setsuna's exceptional choice.
findings.japanese: かずさだけは、許すって…
findings.todokanai: I imagine only Kazusa would forgive me in such a scenario…

findings.highlight: now the president of the company Setsuna's working at.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ええ、知ってました。その時の担当が、今の彼女の部署の部長です」
findings.explanation: The former contact is now head of Setsuna's department, not president of Knights Records. The English inflates a departmental manager into the company's chief executive and distorts the internal approval route.
findings.japanese:
「ええ、知ってました。
その時の担当が、今の彼女の部署の部長です」
findings.todokanai: "Yes, I know about that. The person responsible for that arrangement is now the president of the company Setsuna's working at."

findings.highlight: you've even looked up on how you'd manage to persuade me
findings.evidenceJa: 「既に話を通すルートまで見つけてあるんだ…抜け目ないわね」
findings.explanation: Youko notes that Haruki has already found a channel through which to get the proposal approved inside Knights. The English says he researched how to persuade Youko herself, even though he is already negotiating directly with her.
findings.japanese:
「既に話を通すルートまで見つけてあるんだ…
抜け目ないわね」
findings.todokanai: "I see you've even looked up on how you'd manage to persuade me… you let nothing slip by you, now, do you?"

findings.highlight: I suppose I can buy some time and… that's it!
findings.evidenceJa: 「じゃあ間を取って………これで！今約束できるギリギリの線です！」
findings.explanation: Haruki proposes splitting the difference between their circulation numbers and names the maximum he can presently promise. The English turns 間を取って into buying time, breaking the numerical bargaining joke.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ間を取って………これで！
今約束できるギリギリの線です！」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I suppose I can buy some time and… that's it! That's the most I can promise you right now!"

findings.highlight: is our relationship not simple enough to be described with words like that?
findings.evidenceJa: 「好きとか、嫌いとか、愛してるとか、憎いとか…そんなふうに、十文字以内で答えられるほど、わたしたちの関係、単純じゃないのかな…？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna wonders whether their relationship is too complex to answer in ten Japanese characters or fewer with labels like like, hate, love, loathe. The English retains generic complexity but drops the precise ten-character conceit that foregrounds language's insufficiency.
findings.japanese:
「好きとか、嫌いとか、愛してるとか、憎いとか…
そんなふうに、十文字以内で答えられるほど、
わたしたちの関係、単純じゃないのかな…？」
findings.todokanai: "Like, dislike, love, hate… is our relationship not simple enough to be described with words like that?"

findings.highlight: That means it's our sake as well.
findings.evidenceJa: 「かずさのためなんだよ？…それって、わたしたちのためじゃない」
findings.explanation: Setsuna insists the mission is for Kazusa and explicitly not for Haruki and Setsuna. The English says the exact opposite: that Kazusa's sake therefore equals their own sake.
findings.japanese:
「かずさのためなんだよ？
…それって、わたしたちのためじゃない」
findings.todokanai: "This is all for Kazusa's sake, you know? …That means it's our sake as well."

findings.highlight: Despite the fact that she willingly volunteered for the role
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が求めたこととは言え、雪菜に、ここまで残酷な役目を負わせることを。
findings.explanation: Haruki acknowledges that he himself asked for this and imposed the cruel role on Setsuna. The English shifts responsibility to Setsuna by saying she volunteered.
findings.japanese:
自分が求めたこととは言え、
雪菜に、ここまで残酷な役目を負わせることを。
findings.todokanai: Despite the fact that she willingly volunteered for the role, the fact remains that I'm imposing an extremely cruel task on her.

findings.highlight: I want to put my full concentration into thinking about what I can do for her.
findings.evidenceJa: 「今はかずさのことだけ考えていたい。かずさとぶつかることに集中していたいの」
findings.explanation: Setsuna wants to focus on colliding/clashing directly with Kazusa, not benevolently contemplating what she can do for her. The English removes the conflict she sees as necessary.
findings.japanese:
「今はかずさのことだけ考えていたい。
かずさとぶつかることに集中していたいの」
findings.todokanai: "I want to only think about Kazusa right now. I want to put my full concentration into thinking about what I can do for her."

findings.highlight: Still, maybe we will end up quarrelling a little.
findings.evidenceJa: 「そう、そんな感じ。まぁ面白くはないけど…でも、ちょっとだけほぐれてきたかな？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki's awkward joking response is the right idea and asks whether he has loosened up a little. The English instead predicts that Setsuna and Kazusa may quarrel, changing both subject and event.
findings.japanese:
「そう、そんな感じ。まぁ面白くはないけど…
でも、ちょっとだけほぐれてきたかな？」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, that's how it feels. Well, I suppose it wouldn't be particularly interesting this way… Still, maybe we will end up quarrelling a little."

findings.highlight: I decided to focus on getting better by familiarizing myself with the work
findings.evidenceJa: 「それでも、自分にできることは少なかったから、とにかくその場をうまく回すことだけ考えて、言われたこと一生懸命、とにかく笑顔でやってみた」
findings.explanation: Setsuna had little authority, so she focused on keeping the troubled worksite running smoothly, doing every instruction earnestly and smiling. The English turns crisis coordination into personal familiarization and improvement.
findings.japanese:
「それでも、自分にできることは少なかったから、
とにかくその場をうまく回すことだけ考えて、
言われたこと一生懸命、とにかく笑顔でやってみた」
findings.todokanai: "Even so, I couldn't really get very much done by myself, so I decided to focus on getting better by familiarizing myself with the work, and to follow my instructions with the utmost effort, or at the very least a smile."

findings.highlight: She's really, really done her best, all while she's trying to feel encouraged by words I'd said to deceive her, and all while knowing that there's a possibility that I might've betrayed her.
findings.evidenceJa:
そんな俺の誤魔化しでしかない言葉で自分を奮い立たせ、
俺に裏切られていたかも知れないその同じ時、
本当に、本当に、頑張って。
findings.explanation: Setsuna worked while Haruki might at that same time have been betraying her; 'knowing there was a possibility' makes her contemporaneously aware — The brutal coincidence between his words and possible betrayal remains.
findings.japanese:
そんな俺の誤魔化しでしかない言葉で自分を奮い立たせ、
俺に裏切られていたかも知れないその同じ時、
本当に、本当に、頑張って。
findings.todokanai: She's really, really done her best, all while she's trying to feel encouraged by words I'd said to deceive her, and all while knowing that there's a possibility that I might've betrayed her.

findings.highlight: the three of us will cross that final hurdle together
findings.evidenceJa: 「だから、その時は…三人でゴールしようね？」
findings.explanation: Within the explicit baton-and-anchor relay metaphor, Setsuna promises that all three will finish together. The English replaces the finish line with a 'final hurdle,' mixing sports metaphors and weakening the promise's endpoint.
findings.japanese: 「だから、その時は…三人でゴールしようね？」
findings.todokanai: "That's why when the time comes… the three of us will cross that final hurdle together, alright?"

findings.highlight: I suppose I need to think about how I'm going to spend the rest of my life making up for everything I've done to her.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女は…これから一生かかって償わせてくれるだろうか。
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether Setsuna will allow him to spend the rest of his life atoning to her. The English turns her future permission into his private planning, removing Setsuna's agency over whether she accepts that life.
findings.japanese:
彼女は…
これから一生かかって償わせてくれるだろうか。
findings.todokanai: I suppose I need to think about how I'm going to spend the rest of my life making up for everything I've done to her.

findings.highlight: Perhaps I was never needed by her in the first place.
findings.evidenceJa: もう、多分俺を必要としないはずの彼女は。
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks the newly strong Setsuna probably no longer needs him. The English says she never needed him in the first place, erasing the relationship history and reversing the temporal claim.
findings.japanese: もう、多分俺を必要としないはずの彼女は。
findings.todokanai: Perhaps I was never needed by her in the first place.

findings.highlight: "I'm sorry, Haruki-kun… I'm so sorry! If only I'd kept close watch on her… no, it's because I've been so pushy with her that this ended up happening!"
findings.evidenceJa:
「ごめん春希くん…ごめんなさいっ！
わたしがついていながら…
ううん、わたしがついてたせいでこんなことにっ」
findings.explanation: Setsuna corrects 'despite being with her' to 'because I was with her'; the English changes this into insufficient watchfulness versus pushiness — Her self-blame for worsening Kazusa's state remains.
findings.japanese:
「ごめん春希くん…ごめんなさいっ！
わたしがついていながら…
ううん、わたしがついてたせいでこんなことにっ」
findings.todokanai: "I'm sorry, Haruki-kun… I'm so sorry! If only I'd kept close watch on her… no, it's because I've been so pushy with her that this ended up happening!"

findings.highlight: No reason, really, I just didn't want you to bother me, Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: 「別に、雪菜がウザくなっただけじゃないよ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says it is not merely that Setsuna became annoying; she also missed the piano. The English says annoyance is the sole reason, reversing the setup for her more vulnerable admission.
findings.japanese: 「別に、雪菜がウザくなっただけじゃないよ」
findings.todokanai: "No reason, really, I just didn't want you to bother me, Setsuna."

findings.highlight: It's amazing anyone can bear him… that coward.
findings.evidenceJa: 「本当、やられちゃうよね…あの卑怯者」
findings.explanation: Setsuna quietly agrees that the underhanded Haruki really gets/defeats you—he makes both women succumb to him. The English says it is remarkable anyone can tolerate him, replacing rueful shared romantic defeat with repulsion.
findings.japanese: 「本当、やられちゃうよね…あの卑怯者」
findings.todokanai: "It's amazing anyone can bear him… that coward."

findings.highlight: After all, I am her yes-man here.
findings.evidenceJa: なんて、それも当然だ。何しろあの人の受け売りなんだから。
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes that Hamada's noble declaration is naturally reminiscent of Mari because Hamada has just repeated words borrowed from her after her international call. The English instead calls Haruki Mari's yes-man, changing both the person being described and the point of the reveal.
findings.japanese:
なんて、それも当然だ。
何しろあの人の受け売りなんだから。
findings.todokanai: Who am I kidding, that's only natural. After all, I am her yes-man here.

findings.highlight: He's been sitting on the fence for the past five years!
findings.evidenceJa: 「ほんっと酷い人だよね春希くんって。五年間もずっとふたまたかけ続けてさぁ！」
findings.explanation: Setsuna accuses Haruki of two-timing Kazusa and her continuously for five years. 'Sitting on the fence' turns sustained romantic betrayal into mere indecision and strips the accusation of its sexual and relational force.
findings.japanese:
「ほんっと酷い人だよね春希くんって。
五年間もずっとふたまたかけ続けてさぁ！」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki-kun really is a cruel person, isn't he? He's been sitting on the fence for the past five years!"

findings.highlight: you think you're winning his favor by trying to help me up on my feet again
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前があたしに構うのは、あいつがそうするからだろ？あたしを立ち直らせることが、あいつに尽くすことだって思ってるんだろ？」
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks whether Setsuna believes restoring her is a way of devoting herself to Haruki—doing for him what he would do. 'Winning his favor' instead imputes a calculated attempt to ingratiate herself with him, materially changing Setsuna's motive and Kazusa's accusation.
findings.japanese:
「お前があたしに構うのは、あいつがそうするからだろ？
あたしを立ち直らせることが、
あいつに尽くすことだって思ってるんだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "The reason that you're concerned about me is because he himself is concerned about me, right? And you think you're winning his favor by trying to help me up on my feet again, don't you?"

findings.highlight: when you're the one lacking in skill
findings.evidenceJa: 「居眠りしてる客を目覚めさせてこそプロだろ？認めてくれないのは相手が悪いなんて、努力不足の言い訳でしかないな」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says blaming an unreceptive audience is merely an excuse for insufficient effort. The English changes 努力不足 into lack of skill, contradicting the scene's sustained argument about effort, understanding, and professional responsibility.
findings.japanese:
「居眠りしてる客を目覚めさせてこそプロだろ？
認めてくれないのは相手が悪いなんて、
努力不足の言い訳でしかないな」
findings.todokanai: "A true pro would be able to awaken the audience from their sleep, no? It's nothing but an excuse to blame the people who won't give you the light of day when you're the one lacking in skill."

findings.highlight: This time, I'll capture the hearts of your audience.
findings.evidenceJa: 「追加公演を見てなさい。今度こそかずさの…観客の心、掴んでみせるから」
findings.explanation: Setsuna starts to say that this time she will capture Kazusa's heart, then corrects herself to the audience's heart. The English smooths the broken syntax into 'your audience' and erases the revealing romantic slip that makes Kazusa invite her upstairs for an encore.
findings.japanese:
「追加公演を見てなさい。
今度こそかずさの…
観客の心、掴んでみせるから」
findings.todokanai: "Just wait until the additional concert. This time, I'll capture the hearts of your audience."

findings.highlight: If you're going to rile me up, I won't be heading back until morning.
findings.evidenceJa: 「っ！…一度上がり込んだら朝まで帰らないに決まってるから、せっかく遠慮してたのになぁ」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she had been holding back out of consideration because, once she went up to Kazusa's room, she knew she would not leave until morning. The English invents retaliation for being riled up and loses the admission that her apparent retreat was deliberate restraint.
findings.japanese:
「っ！
…一度上がり込んだら朝まで帰らないに決まってるから、
せっかく遠慮してたのになぁ」
findings.todokanai: "…! If you're going to rile me up, I won't be heading back until morning. And here I was actually being considerate of you."

findings.highlight: An electric heater. I'm not allowed to use a gas heater according to the front desk.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ああこれ？　電熱器。フロントに聞いたらガス使えないって」
findings.explanation: Setsuna is holding an electric hotplate because the hotel will not allow gas; she has brought it with pots, pans, and ingredients to cook for Kazusa. The English turns both appliances into room heaters, making the physical comedy and the next inventory incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「ああこれ？　電熱器。
フロントに聞いたらガス使えないって」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, this? An electric heater. I'm not allowed to use a gas heater according to the front desk."

findings.highlight: You're the one he's truly loved since five years ago, Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつは五年前から雪菜のことが好きだったよ。ずっとあいつを見てたあたしだからわかるんだよ…」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki liked Setsuna five years ago; she can tell because she was watching him. 'Truly loved' adds exclusivity and contradicts the surrounding argument that Kazusa remained his first and foremost love while Setsuna's effort eventually brought her level with or beyond Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
「あいつは五年前から雪菜のことが好きだったよ。
ずっとあいつを見てたあたしだからわかるんだよ…」
findings.todokanai: "You're the one he's truly loved since five years ago, Setsuna. I know that full well because I've been watching him all that time…"

findings.highlight: Even so, I'll never be able to become the one he loves most.
findings.evidenceJa: 「それでも、彼の中の一番はずっと変わらなかった。…途中からだけど、ずっと彼を見てるわたしならわかる」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki's number one had remained unchanged throughout that period. The English turns this retrospective observation into a permanent prediction that she will never become number one, immediately clashing with her next statement that her best was to draw level and Kazusa's answer that Setsuna ultimately did become the woman he loves most.
findings.japanese:
「それでも、彼の中の一番はずっと変わらなかった。
…途中からだけど、ずっと彼を見てるわたしならわかる」
findings.todokanai: "Even so, I'll never be able to become the one he loves most. …I know because I've always watched him, even if not for as long as you."

findings.highlight: You worked really hard while I couldn't.
findings.evidenceJa: 「でも雪菜は努力した。…あたしのしなかった努力をさ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Setsuna made the effort that she herself did not make. The English changes self-reproach for not acting into inability, mitigating the agency and responsibility on which Kazusa bases her concession of defeat.
findings.japanese:
「でも雪菜は努力した。
…あたしのしなかった努力をさ」
findings.todokanai: "But you worked really hard, Setsuna. …You worked really hard while I couldn't."

findings.highlight: There's no need for me to go out of my way to admit that, is there?
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前の勝ちだよ。もう勝負はついてる。…わざわざ、あたしに負けを認めさせなくてもいいだろ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa tells Setsuna there is no need for Setsuna to go out of her way to make Kazusa admit defeat. The English says Kazusa herself need not go out of her way to admit it, reversing the agency in her accusation that Setsuna is pressing the victory upon her.
findings.japanese:
「お前の勝ちだよ。もう勝負はついてる。
…わざわざ、あたしに負けを認めさせなくてもいいだろ」
findings.todokanai: "You win. The game is over. …There's no need for me to go out of my way to admit that, is there?"

findings.highlight: I like you, and you're already so close to me!
findings.evidenceJa: 「でも、でも…わたし、かずさに対して無関心じゃいられない。…好きと、ものすごく近いところにいるんだよ！」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she cannot be indifferent to Kazusa and that what she feels lies extremely close to love. The English instead says Kazusa is physically or emotionally close to Setsuna, changing the subject of 'close' and flattening Setsuna's difficult attempt to name her own feeling.
findings.japanese:
「でも、でも…
わたし、かずさに対して無関心じゃいられない。
…好きと、ものすごく近いところにいるんだよ！」
findings.todokanai: "Still, still… I just can't bring myself to not worry about you, Kazusa. …I like you, and you're already so close to me!"

findings.highlight: that guy lacks common sense
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつの言ってることは全部間違いだ。だってあいつは、人としてのセンスがないから」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki has no sense or talent for being a human being. She deliberately casts moral judgment as innate artistic センス, then extends the conceit through talent, artists, and Japanese people. 'Lacks common sense' turns this into conventional social judgment and breaks the sustained analogy.
findings.japanese:
「あいつの言ってることは全部間違いだ。
だってあいつは、人としてのセンスがないから」
findings.todokanai: "Everything that comes out of his mouth is wrong. After all, that guy lacks common sense."

findings.highlight: "Still, I don't think his mistakes can be attributed to his lack of sense. It's just that nothing was really ever fair from the very beginning."
findings.evidenceJa:
「でも、彼が間違いを犯すのは、
彼にセンスがないからじゃない。
ただ、最初から公平じゃないんだよ」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki is not impartial from the outset when reaching conclusions; 'nothing was ever fair' externalizes the bias into circumstances — Her explanation that he always favors Kazusa follows directly.
findings.japanese:
「でも、彼が間違いを犯すのは、
彼にセンスがないからじゃない。
ただ、最初から公平じゃないんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Still, I don't think his mistakes can be attributed to his lack of sense. It's just that nothing was really ever fair from the very beginning."

findings.highlight: the world of those five years past
findings.evidenceJa: 「けれど日本に来て、五年後の世界に来て…幸せな空想が、現実に壊された」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that by coming to Japan she entered the world five years later—the present from which Vienna had insulated her—and reality destroyed her happy fantasy. The English calls it the world of five years past, reversing the temporal movement central to the scene.
findings.japanese:
「けれど日本に来て、五年後の世界に来て…
幸せな空想が、現実に壊された」
findings.todokanai: "But the moment I came to Japan, the world of those five years past… my fantasies of happiness had been destroyed by reality."

findings.highlight: The one person that I've always gone for has disappeared… the one person who's always supported me all this time is no more.
findings.evidenceJa: 「目指してた人が、あたしの先にいなくなった…ずっと支えてくれていた人が、消えてしまった」
findings.explanation: Kazusa distinguishes two losses: Youko, the person she aimed toward, is no longer ahead of her as a guiding goal; Haruki, the person who supported her, has disappeared from her life. The English describes both as simple disappearance and obscures why Setsuna immediately answers first about Youko and then about Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「目指してた人が、あたしの先にいなくなった…
ずっと支えてくれていた人が、消えてしまった」
findings.todokanai: "The one person that I've always gone for has disappeared… the one person who's always supported me all this time is no more."

findings.highlight: Even though I've known full well that they could never be a reality…
findings.evidenceJa: 「でも現実には、あたしの望みは何一つ叶わない。わかってたことだけど、永遠に知りたくなかった…っ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she knew none of her wishes would come true but wanted never, for all eternity, to know or confront that fact. The English omits the refusal to know and replaces it with the flatter claim that she knew the wishes could not become reality, losing the distinction between abstract knowledge and forced recognition.
findings.japanese:
「でも現実には、
あたしの望みは何一つ叶わない。
わかってたことだけど、永遠に知りたくなかった…っ」
findings.todokanai: "But the reality is that not even one of my wishes has come true. Even though I've known full well that they could never be a reality…"

findings.highlight: Stay by my side tonight, too.
findings.evidenceJa: 「もう、寝るよ。ありがと、雪菜。今夜も、側にいてくれて」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she is going to sleep and thanks Setsuna for having stayed beside her again tonight. The English changes completed companionship and gratitude into a fresh imperative that Setsuna remain, altering both tense and Kazusa's emotional gesture.
findings.japanese:
「もう、寝るよ。
ありがと、雪菜。
今夜も、側にいてくれて」
findings.todokanai: "Let's just go to sleep. Thank you, Setsuna. Stay by my side tonight, too."

findings.highlight: The narrative of her triumphant return to Japan would also be erased
findings.evidenceJa: 凱旋帰国の空気は一変し、冬馬家を取り巻く環境は、曜子さんが日本を追われた頃のように厳しくなるだろう。
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts that the atmosphere of triumph will reverse and the actual environment surrounding the Touma family will become as harsh as when Youko was driven out of Japan. The English reduces renewed public and professional hostility to the erasure of a favorable 'narrative.'
findings.japanese:
凱旋帰国の空気は一変し、冬馬家を取り巻く環境は、
曜子さんが日本を追われた頃のように厳しくなるだろう。
findings.todokanai: The narrative of her triumphant return to Japan would also be erased, much like the time when Youko-san was ousted from Japan.

findings.highlight: Because she believes that Kazusa would be able to rise once more? Because she believes that Kazusa isn't someone so half-hearted that she would crumble over a scandal like this?
findings.evidenceJa:
必ず再起できるって。
この程度のスキャンダルで潰されるような
半端な実力ではないって。
findings.explanation: Youko trusts Kazusa's skill is not half-baked enough to be destroyed by this scandal; 'someone so half-hearted' shifts from ability to temperament — The claim that Kazusa's professional substance can survive the scandal remains.
findings.japanese:
必ず再起できるって。
この程度のスキャンダルで潰されるような
半端な実力ではないって。
findings.todokanai: Because she believes that Kazusa would be able to rise once more? Because she believes that Kazusa isn't someone so half-hearted that she would crumble over a scandal like this?

findings.highlight: "Just a little longer… please, just wait for one more day. I'm sure something's bound to happen."
findings.evidenceJa:
「もう少し…あと一日だけ待ってください。
絶対に何とかなりますから」
findings.explanation: Haruki promises they will definitely make something work; 'something's bound to happen' sounds passive and providential — His request for one more day and confidence are still explicit.
findings.japanese:
「もう少し…あと一日だけ待ってください。
絶対に何とかなりますから」
findings.todokanai: "Just a little longer… please, just wait for one more day. I'm sure something's bound to happen."

findings.highlight: This time… we will cast our final die.
findings.evidenceJa: 今度こそ…最後の賽が投げられた。
findings.explanation: The final die has just been cast: Youko has accepted Haruki's midnight deadline. The English moves the decisive act into the future, weakening the narration's explicit recognition that there is now no retreat.
findings.japanese:
今度こそ…
最後の賽が投げられた。
findings.todokanai: This time… we will cast our final die.

findings.highlight: after you decide whether or not you'll be going through with it
findings.evidenceJa: 「それを心配するのは、かずさがやるって決めた後だよ」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says they will worry about the impossible production schedule after Kazusa decides that she will do it. The English changes the assumed affirmative decision into an open choice of whether or not, softening Setsuna's deliberate confidence and pressure.
findings.japanese:
「それを心配するのは、
かずさがやるって決めた後だよ」
findings.todokanai: "If I'm going to worry about that, it'll be only after you decide whether or not you'll be going through with it, Kazusa."

findings.highlight: You'll be able to enjoy yourself with many more people who will love you in this world
findings.evidenceJa: 「お母さんだけじゃなく、春希くんだけじゃない…もっとたくさんの、あなたを好きな人たちを、あなたの世界の中で、遊ばせてあげようよ？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna urges Kazusa to let many more people who love her come and play inside Kazusa's world. The English makes Kazusa the one enjoying herself with them, losing the proposed act of opening her formerly tiny world to others—the premise for Setsuna asking to be admitted again.
findings.japanese:
「お母さんだけじゃなく、春希くんだけじゃない…
もっとたくさんの、あなたを好きな人たちを、
あなたの世界の中で、遊ばせてあげようよ？」
findings.todokanai: "It won't be just your mother, and not just Haruki-kun either… You'll be able to enjoy yourself with many more people who will love you in this world, you know?"

findings.highlight: "After all, I, I… as long as Haruki stays by my side, I won't be able to give up on him! And as long as you stay by my side, Setsuna, I won't be able to stop envying you!"
findings.evidenceJa:
「だって、あたしは、あたしは…
春希の側にいる限り、あいつを諦めきれないよ！
雪菜の側にいる限り、お前を妬んじゃうんだよ！」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she cannot give Haruki up as long as she remains beside him; 'as long as Haruki stays by my side' reverses who maintains the proximity — The impossible coexistence of the three remains.
findings.japanese:
「だって、あたしは、あたしは…
春希の側にいる限り、あいつを諦めきれないよ！
雪菜の側にいる限り、お前を妬んじゃうんだよ！」
findings.todokanai: "After all, I, I… as long as Haruki stays by my side, I won't be able to give up on him! And as long as you stay by my side, Setsuna, I won't be able to stop envying you!"

findings.highlight: You won't be able to get into my world.
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前なんか、あたしの世界に入れてやらない。たとえ世界にお前とあたししかいなくても…」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will not let Setsuna into her world even if only the two of them remain. The English turns an intentionally cruel refusal into Setsuna's inability to enter, removing Kazusa's agency immediately before she begs not to be excluded herself.
findings.japanese:
「お前なんか、あたしの世界に入れてやらない。
たとえ世界にお前とあたししかいなくても…」
findings.todokanai: "You won't be able to get into my world. Even if you and I are the only ones left in the world…"

findings.highlight: But now they're no longer with me… why were the two of them taken away from me!?
findings.evidenceJa: 「母さんとだって離れたくないよ…嫌だよ。たった二人しかいらないのに…どうして二人とも取り上げようとするんだよ！」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she needs only two people—Haruki and her mother—and asks why the world is trying to take both away. The English says simply that the two are already gone, omitting the stark 'only those two' confession that answers Setsuna's invitation to fill her world with many people.
findings.japanese:
「母さんとだって離れたくないよ…嫌だよ。
たった二人しかいらないのに…
どうして二人とも取り上げようとするんだよ！」
findings.todokanai: "I don't want to be separated from mom, either… I don't want that! But now they're no longer with me… why were the two of them taken away from me!?"

findings.highlight: I then proceed to slowly strum my fingers on the guitar, playing a melody I haven't listened to in a very long time.
findings.evidenceJa:
それからゆっくりと弦に指をかけて、
久しぶりの旋律を奏で始める。
findings.explanation: Haruki places his fingers on the strings and plays a melody he has not played in a long time; the English says he strums his fingers and has not listened to it — The next line explicitly identifies the two-year gap since he played this way.
findings.japanese:
それからゆっくりと弦に指をかけて、
久しぶりの旋律を奏で始める。
findings.todokanai: I then proceed to slowly strum my fingers on the guitar, playing a melody I haven't listened to in a very long time.

findings.highlight: With him playing outside like that, one could feel too embarrassed to even look.
findings.evidenceJa: 「…ちょっと、痛いでしょ？外からだと、恥ずかしくて見てられないかもね」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki's grand romantic guitar gesture is a little cringeworthy and may be too embarrassing to watch from an outsider's perspective. The English misreads 外から as Haruki physically playing outdoors, inventing a location and losing Setsuna's self-aware comment on how the scene looks to other people.
findings.japanese:
「…ちょっと、痛いでしょ？
外からだと、恥ずかしくて見てられないかもね」
findings.todokanai: "…It's a little awkward, isn't it? With him playing outside like that, one could feel too embarrassed to even look."

findings.highlight: The way I put it makes it sound like something made up
findings.evidenceJa: 「彼に凍らされた心を、彼が無理やり溶かしてくれた。…なんか、自作自演みたいな言い方だけど、それが実際、二年前にあったこと」
findings.explanation: Setsuna jokes that Haruki freezing her heart and then forcibly thawing it sounds like 自作自演—creating the crisis and staging its solution himself. The English says only that it sounds fictitious, discarding the pointed joke about Haruki being both culprit and rescuer.
findings.japanese:
「彼に凍らされた心を、彼が無理やり溶かしてくれた。
…なんか、自作自演みたいな言い方だけど、
それが実際、二年前にあったこと」
findings.todokanai: "My heart was frozen by him, but he also forcibly melted it… The way I put it makes it sound like something made up, but it actually happened two years ago."

findings.highlight: Perhaps you think that the best way to save you would be to not get involved with you.
findings.evidenceJa: 「本当なら、わたしがいないことが、あなたにとって一番の救いなのかもしれない」
findings.explanation: Setsuna admits that, in truth, her complete absence may be the greatest salvation for Kazusa. The English instead attributes the idea to Kazusa and reduces absence to Setsuna merely not getting involved, weakening the sacrifice that Setsuna immediately says she cannot make.
findings.japanese:
「本当なら、わたしがいないことが、
あなたにとって一番の救いなのかもしれない」
findings.todokanai: "Perhaps you think that the best way to save you would be to not get involved with you."

findings.highlight: We'll be staying there together.
findings.evidenceJa: 「合宿」
findings.explanation: Kazusa names the plan a 合宿: an intensive live-in training or rehearsal camp. The English conveys only that the trio will stay together, omitting the established Japanese institutional concept that explains the booked studio, round-the-clock schedule, cooking gear, and comic severity of their week.
findings.japanese: 「合宿」
findings.todokanai: "We'll be staying there together."

findings.highlight: "Well, that's how it is, so I have to rush over to the studio now. If there's anything that either of you need me for, you know where to find me."
findings.evidenceJa:
「そんなわけだから、
あたしもすぐにスタジオ入りしないと。
あと何かあったらまた現地で相談させて」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will consult Miyo and Youko on-site if anything else arises; 'you know where to find me' reverses who initiates later contact — Her immediate departure for the studio remains.
findings.japanese:
「そんなわけだから、
あたしもすぐにスタジオ入りしないと。
あと何かあったらまた現地で相談させて」
findings.todokanai: "Well, that's how it is, so I have to rush over to the studio now. If there's anything that either of you need me for, you know where to find me."

findings.highlight: Our stamina will be just as important as our health
findings.evidenceJa: 「この期に及んでジャンクフードとかなに考えてんだお前。これからは時間と同じくらい体力が大事だって時に」
findings.explanation: Haruki says that from now on stamina is as important as time. The English replaces time with health, producing a near-tautology—stamina versus health—and discarding the point of their 150-hour countdown.
findings.japanese:
「この期に及んでジャンクフードとかなに考えてんだお前。
これからは時間と同じくらい体力が大事だって時に」
findings.todokanai: "And what do you think you're doing, thinking about junk food during such a tight period? Our stamina will be just as important as our health in the days to come."

findings.highlight: we're only pretending to be as lax as we are
findings.evidenceJa: みんな、本当はわかってる。誰もが空元気を振り絞ってるって。
findings.explanation: All three know they are squeezing out false or forced cheer while desperately holding back tears. The English says they are pretending to be lax, replacing a brave emotional performance with casual looseness and misdescribing the banter that follows their reunion.
findings.japanese:
みんな、本当はわかってる。
誰もが空元気を振り絞ってるって。
findings.todokanai: Every one of us truly understands. We understand that we're only pretending to be as lax as we are.

findings.highlight: I understand that I'm imposing a very tough schedule. I would understand if they snapped at me for this arrangement.
findings.evidenceJa:
過酷なスケジュールだってのはわかってる。
絶対に噛みつかれるってわかってる。
findings.explanation: Haruki knows with certainty that Kazusa will bite at the schedule; 'would understand if they snapped' turns prediction into magnanimity — Her immediate objections fulfill the expected reaction.
findings.japanese:
過酷なスケジュールだってのはわかってる。
絶対に噛みつかれるってわかってる。
findings.todokanai: I understand that I'm imposing a very tough schedule. I would understand if they snapped at me for this arrangement.

findings.highlight: And it's factored into our leisure time, as well!
findings.evidenceJa: 「って、おいちょっと待て！入浴が一時間しか取ってないじゃないか！しかも移動時間込みで！」
findings.explanation: Kazusa protests that the single allotted hour for bathing even includes travel time to and from the bath. The English says bathing is factored into leisure time, inventing a schedule category and losing why one hour is especially impossible.
findings.japanese:
「って、おいちょっと待て！
入浴が一時間しか取ってないじゃないか！
しかも移動時間込みで！」
findings.todokanai: "Hey, wait, hold on a second! That means I won't even have an hour to take a bath, doesn't it! And it's factored into our leisure time, as well!"

findings.highlight: allows us 30 minutes to bathe every day
findings.evidenceJa: 入浴時間を毎日、しかも３０分延長する代わりに、睡眠時間が更に３０分短縮された…
findings.explanation: The compromise makes bathing daily and extends the originally allotted bath period by thirty minutes, in exchange for shortening sleep by another thirty. The English changes the new bath allowance itself to only thirty minutes, losing both the extension and the arithmetic of the negotiation.
findings.japanese:
入浴時間を毎日、しかも３０分延長する代わりに、
睡眠時間が更に３０分短縮された…
findings.todokanai: Our schedule now allows us 30 minutes to bathe every day, and in exchange, our time for sleep had to be cut down by the same duration…

findings.highlight: This song's been excluded since it's meant for the CD recording
findings.evidenceJa: 「ほら、この三曲目。これだけはＣＤの収録曲から外れてるだろ？」
findings.explanation: Haruki points out that the third concert piece is the sole item excluded from the CD track list. The English says it is excluded because it is meant for the CD, giving the exact opposite relationship between the two lists.
findings.japanese:
「ほら、この三曲目。
これだけはＣＤの収録曲から外れてるだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "Here, this third song. This song's been excluded since it's meant for the CD recording, right?"

findings.highlight: The album I've thought of won't include songs you'll play in the additional concert
findings.evidenceJa: 「手を抜いてるわけじゃない。効率化だ！アルバムはもちろん、追加公演での新曲はなし。いや、どれだけ譲ってもせめて１曲…」
findings.explanation: Haruki's efficiency rule is no new pieces for the album and none for the additional concert—at the absolute most, one new piece if he yields. The English instead forbids overlap between album and concert, nearly the reverse of his actual plan to maximize overlap.
findings.japanese:
「手を抜いてるわけじゃない。効率化だ！
アルバムはもちろん、追加公演での新曲はなし。
いや、どれだけ譲ってもせめて１曲…」
findings.todokanai: "We're not cutting corners, we're making things efficient! The album I've thought of won't include songs you'll play in the additional concert, of course. Well, I suppose if you absolutely insist, we could at least include one new song…"

findings.highlight: "No, we need to work with a completely new selection of songs. Including the song that resulted in my massive failure in my previous concert is a bad omen. I am not playing it again."
findings.evidenceJa:
「いいや全部新曲やる。
大失敗した前のコンサートの曲なんて縁起悪い。
二度と弾きたくないね」
findings.explanation: Kazusa rejects all pieces from the previous disastrous concert as bad luck; the English narrows this to a single song that caused her failure — Her demand for an entirely new selection remains explicit.
findings.japanese:
「いいや全部新曲やる。
大失敗した前のコンサートの曲なんて縁起悪い。
二度と弾きたくないね」
findings.todokanai: "No, we need to work with a completely new selection of songs. Including the song that resulted in my massive failure in my previous concert is a bad omen. I am not playing it again."

findings.highlight: "This is going to be my welcoming performance… one that will welcome my new world…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「歓迎の曲なんだ…
あたしの、新しい世界への…」
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls them welcoming songs directed into her new world; the English calls the performance something that welcomes the world itself — Her expression of a new self and the later audience invitation preserve the motif.
findings.japanese:
「歓迎の曲なんだ…
あたしの、新しい世界への…」
findings.todokanai: "This is going to be my welcoming performance… one that will welcome my new world…"

findings.highlight: it's just impossible for us to prepare for something that's very unlikely to be complete in time
findings.evidenceJa: 「だからって完成度の低いものを出したらどうしようもないじゃないかよ…」
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even so, putting out a low-quality or poorly polished work would be indefensible. The English makes the objection merely that the work is unlikely to be finished in time, erasing the quality threshold at the heart of his conservative program.
findings.japanese:
「だからって完成度の低いものを出したら
どうしようもないじゃないかよ…」
findings.todokanai: "Like I said, it's just impossible for us to prepare for something that's very unlikely to be complete in time…"

findings.highlight: It's frustrating to say, but I worship her too.
findings.evidenceJa: 「永遠の女神、だよね…悔しいくらい、崇拝してるもんね」
findings.explanation: Setsuna addresses Haruki: Kazusa is his eternal goddess, and he worships her enough to make Setsuna jealous. The English changes the omitted subject to Setsuna and says she too worships Kazusa, replacing romantic jealousy with shared devotion.
findings.japanese:
「永遠の女神、だよね…
悔しいくらい、崇拝してるもんね」
findings.todokanai: "Your eternal goddess, right…? It's frustrating to say, but I worship her too."

findings.highlight: she will have to be proactive and reactive
findings.evidenceJa: 全ての負荷は…衝動も反動も、かずさ一人へと収束する。
findings.explanation: Haruki says every load—both impulse and recoil, action and reaction—will converge on Kazusa alone. The English turns the paired physical forces into personality or work-style adjectives, 'proactive and reactive,' producing nonsense and obscuring why he wants a safety margin.
findings.japanese:
全ての負荷は…
衝動も反動も、かずさ一人へと収束する。
findings.todokanai: Kazusa will have to shoulder everything by herself… she will have to be proactive and reactive.

findings.highlight: our plan just underwent a disastrous rehaul
findings.evidenceJa: というか企画そのものが、青天の霹靂と呼ぶにふさわしい超企画に変貌していた…
findings.explanation: The project has transformed into an extraordinary super-project worthy of being called a bolt from the blue. The English labels the overhaul disastrous before its contents are revealed, changing surprise and scale into failure and preempting the comic reunion proposal.
findings.japanese:
というか企画そのものが、
青天の霹靂と呼ぶにふさわしい超企画に変貌していた…
findings.todokanai: I think it's better to say that our plan just underwent a disastrous rehaul…

findings.highlight: Leaving Setsuna's responsibilities aside
findings.evidenceJa: 「無理だって今さら！まだ現役の雪菜はともかく、それ俺の負荷高すぎるだろ！？」
findings.explanation: Haruki says Setsuna is one thing because she is still an active singer, but asking the long-retired guitarist to join imposes far too much on him. The English changes her continuing musical status into unspecified 'responsibilities,' obscuring the practical contrast behind his panic.
findings.japanese:
「無理だって今さら！
まだ現役の雪菜はともかく、
それ俺の負荷高すぎるだろ！？」
findings.todokanai: "With the way things are now, it's impossible! Leaving Setsuna's responsibilities aside, wouldn't that be an excessively tall task you're putting on me!?"

findings.highlight: working members of society working in different branches
findings.evidenceJa: 「あ、あのさ…俺たち、もう分別のある社会人だよな…？」
findings.explanation: Haruki appeals to the fact that he and Setsuna are now sensible, responsible working adults. The English invents their employment in different branches and omits 分別のある, destroying the setup for the narration's joke that Setsuna's fundamental irresponsibility has not changed since high school.
findings.japanese:
「あ、あのさ…
俺たち、もう分別のある社会人だよな…？」
findings.todokanai: "H-Hey, you know… the two of us are both working members of society working in different branches, aren't we…?"

findings.highlight: Let's become the three happy fools we were back then again!
findings.evidenceJa: 「ね、やろうよ！………また三人で笑い者になっちゃおうよ！」
findings.explanation: Setsuna proposes that the three of them become laughingstocks together again, directly answering Haruki's fear that Kazusa alone would bear public ridicule. 'Happy fools' turns external humiliation into private silliness and breaks the callback that persuades him.
findings.japanese:
「ね、やろうよ！
………また三人で笑い者になっちゃおうよ！」
findings.todokanai: "Hey, let's go for it! …Let's become the three happy fools we were back then again!"

findings.highlight: tens of thousands of first editions
findings.evidenceJa: 「待て、待て、待て！全国の書店で売るんだぞ！？初版○万部だぞ！？」
findings.explanation: Haruki says the initial print run is a censored number of ten-thousands of copies. The English says there will be tens of thousands of 'first editions,' confusing copies with editions and making the publishing-scale objection nonsensical.
findings.japanese:
「待て、待て、待て！
全国の書店で売るんだぞ！？
初版○万部だぞ！？」
findings.todokanai: "Wait, wait, wait! This is going to be selling in bookstores all over the country, you know!? And tens of thousands of first editions, at that!"

findings.highlight: We'll be doing a complete reenactment this time.
findings.evidenceJa: 「今度こそ完全再結成だ。………峰城大付属軽音楽同好会の」
findings.explanation: Kazusa declares that this time the light-music club will reunite in its complete three-person form. 'Reenactment' treats the performance as an imitation of a past event rather than the actual reunion whose missing third member she has just reproached them for excluding.
findings.japanese:
「今度こそ完全再結成だ。
………峰城大付属軽音楽同好会の」
findings.todokanai: "We'll be doing a complete reenactment this time. …A reenactment of Houjou High School's Light Music Club, that is."

findings.highlight: I suppose they wanted to prepare early.
findings.evidenceJa: 前が押してんのかな。
findings.explanation: 前が押す means the preceding booking or session is running late, not that the occupants wanted to prepare early.
findings.japanese:
「前が押してんのかな。
それより何でブースの中に寝袋が？」
findings.todokanai: "I suppose they wanted to prepare early. That aside, though, why is there a sleeping bag in the booth?"

findings.highlight: Which means that what we're working on is…
findings.evidenceJa: それだと、俺たちの担当じゃ…
findings.explanation: The director says classical recording would not be their department; the translation turns that disqualification into an unfinished statement about their current work.
findings.japanese:
「え、でもあれどう聴いてもクラシックだろ？
それだと、俺たちの担当じゃ…」
findings.todokanai: "Eh? There is no doubt that it's classical music. Which means that what we're working on is…"

findings.highlight: We're actually working with…
findings.evidenceJa: ですからまず打ち合わせを…
findings.explanation: Setsuna is proposing that they first hold the planning meeting; the translation invents an explanation of whom they are working with.
findings.japanese: 「ええ、ですからまず打ち合わせを…」
findings.todokanai: "Of course. We're actually working with…"

findings.highlight: most amateur performers
findings.evidenceJa: 下手な芸能人より話題になってる
findings.explanation: 下手な芸能人 means many or run-of-the-mill celebrities, not amateur performers; the contrast is Kazusa's extraordinary publicity despite not being a conventional celebrity.
findings.japanese:
「今、下手な芸能人より話題になってるでしょ彼女？
これまで営業がどれだけ声かけても反応しなかったのに、
それが突然向こうから売り込んできたって…」
findings.todokanai: "She's more popular than most amateur performers nowadays, isn't she? To think that she'd suddenly decide to promote herself despite not responding to any of the attempts of our sales department to reach out to her…"

findings.highlight: They'd at least perform better than when I heard you play for the first time.
findings.evidenceJa: 少なくとも初めて聴いたお前の音の方が上だった
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki himself sounded better the first time she heard him. The translation instead makes an imagined amateur better than that first performance.
findings.japanese:
「素人だってもっと上手く弾くぞ。
少なくとも初めて聴いたお前の音の方が上だった」
findings.todokanai: "Even an amateur would be able to play well, you know? They'd at least perform better than when I heard you play for the first time."

findings.highlight: the dismantled Light Music Club
findings.evidenceJa: 体裁すら整っていなかった同好会
findings.explanation: The club had not even acquired a proper organizational form; it had not been dismantled.
findings.japanese:
何より、体裁すら整っていなかった同好会で、
無理やり学園祭のステージにエントリーしたのだって、
全ての元凶は俺で。
findings.todokanai: And above all, I had forced the dismantled Light Music Club onto the stage of the school festival.

findings.highlight: She kept laughing everything off
findings.evidenceJa: 適当なことばっかり言っててさ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Setsuna kept tossing out glib or irresponsible suggestions, not that she laughed everything off. The error weakens the teasing callback to Setsuna's reckless enthusiasm.
findings.japanese:
「ふふ、そうだったな。
あいつ、あの時も適当なことばっかり言っててさ、
一人だけなんの苦労もしてなかったもんなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Hehe, you're right. She kept laughing everything off, and was the only one who didn't have to work hard among us."

findings.highlight: I would have never even thought about something so self-serving as that up until three months ago.
findings.evidenceJa: 三か月前までは、そんな都合のいいこと考えてたんだっけ。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that until three months ago he had entertained that convenient hope. The translation explicitly says he never had.
findings.japanese:
三か月前までは、
そんな都合のいいこと考えてたんだっけ。
findings.todokanai: I would have never even thought about something so self-serving as that up until three months ago.

findings.highlight: you've had the guts to ignore all my warnings in the status reports.
findings.evidenceJa: 事前に相談もなしに全部事後報告で、あげくの果てにこっちの忠告まで無視しやがって
findings.explanation: Hamada says Haruki consulted him about nothing, reported everything only after the fact, and even ignored his advice. The translation relocates the advice into nonexistent status reports and loses the after-the-fact reporting charge.
findings.japanese:
「事前に相談もなしに全部事後報告で、
あげくの果てにこっちの忠告まで無視しやがって」
findings.todokanai: "You haven't discussed anything with me and you've had the guts to ignore all my warnings in the status reports."

findings.highlight: So she was right about Mari-san…
findings.evidenceJa: 言ってきたってのは当たりだったんだ…
findings.explanation: Matsuoka realizes Suzuki correctly guessed that Mari had contacted Hamada. The translation supplies no coherent referent and says an unidentified woman was right about Mari.
findings.japanese: 「言ってきたってのは当たりだったんだ…」
findings.todokanai: "So she was right about Mari-san…"

findings.highlight: packages of multi-function printing paper and ink
findings.evidenceJa: まだ梱包されたままの複合機にプリンタ用紙にインク
findings.explanation: The list contains a still-boxed multifunction printer, printer paper, and ink. The translation collapses the machine and paper into the nonexistent product 'multi-function printing paper.'
findings.japanese:
傍らには、山と積まれた家電製品。
まだ梱包されたままの複合機にプリンタ用紙にインク。
それに、デザインソフトのパッケージ。
findings.todokanai: There's a pile of miscellaneous items beside me. They include still-wrapped packages of multi-function printing paper and ink, as well as a graphics software package.

findings.highlight: I barely managed to keep these expenses within the company's allocated budget.
findings.evidenceJa: 会社の経費で落ちるかは思い切り微妙な線
findings.explanation: Haruki doubts whether the company will reimburse the purchases at all; he is not saying they barely fit an allocated budget.
findings.japanese:
…全部でいくらかかったかは思い出したくない。
何しろ会社の経費で落ちるかは思い切り微妙な線だし。
findings.todokanai: …I don't even want to think about how much all that cost. After all, I barely managed to keep these expenses within the company's allocated budget.

findings.highlight: until the concert
findings.evidenceJa: もう本番まで時間ないんだよ
findings.explanation: In this studio sequence 本番 is the imminent recording proper, not Kazusa's separate concert.
findings.japanese:
「…わかったら早くセッティングしろ。
もう本番まで時間ないんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "…If you understand, then hurry and get things set up, already. We don't have much time left until the concert."

findings.highlight: Why wouldn't he help me himself?
findings.evidenceJa: なんで、助けがいるんだよ
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks why help was needed at all, exposing her hurt that Haruki could not keep their secret self-contained. The translation invents a complaint that Haruki personally refused to help her.
findings.japanese:
「どうして他の女に助けを求めるんだよ。
…なんで、助けがいるんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Why would he ask another woman for help? …Why wouldn't he help me himself?"

findings.highlight: That's because there's no need for words in this case.
findings.evidenceJa: ピンと来なかったってことだよね
findings.explanation: Setsuna interprets their silence as proof the design failed to click with them. The translation romanticizes the silence as communication beyond words, reversing the evaluative point.
findings.japanese:
「うん、かずさも春希くんも一言もなかった。
…ピンと来なかったってことだよね」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, neither you or Kazusa actually said anything, Haruki-kun. …That's because there's no need for words in this case."

findings.highlight: I'm sure he has a backup plan prepared in advance, and will definitely have some solution ready
findings.evidenceJa: 実はもう手を回してくれていて、明日会社に行ったら何もかも解決してたりとか…
findings.explanation: Haruki is desperately entertaining a possibility: perhaps Hamada has arranged something and everything might be solved tomorrow. 'I'm sure' and 'definitely' erase the uncertainty that drives his temptation to compromise.
findings.japanese:
浜田さんはああやって大げさに言ったけど、
実はもう手を回してくれていて、
明日会社に行ったら何もかも解決してたりとか…
findings.todokanai: As harsh as Hamada-san was earlier, I'm sure he has a backup plan prepared in advance, and will definitely have some solution ready when I arrive at the company tomorrow…

findings.highlight: Let's not make it too flashy… no, let's actually just not go for that at all…
findings.evidenceJa: あんまり色使わなくてさ…いや、全然使わなくてさ…
findings.explanation: Kazusa specifically proposes using few colors, then no color at all. The translation replaces the concrete path to a white jacket with generic flashiness and an unclear rejection.
findings.japanese:
「あんまり色使わなくてさ…
いや、全然使わなくてさ…」
findings.todokanai: "Let's not make it too flashy… no, let's actually just not go for that at all…"

findings.highlight: Three heads are better than one, after all, so I see nothing but positives from us pooling our wisdom together.
findings.evidenceJa: 三人寄れば知恵も出るし矢も折れないし姦しいし
findings.explanation: Setsuna comically piles together three separate three-person sayings: three heads produce wisdom, three arrows do not break, and three women are noisy. Todokanai TL keeps only the first, deleting both the escalating joke and Haruki's response to 'the last one.'
findings.japanese:
「そうだよね。
三人寄れば知恵も出るし矢も折れないし姦しいし
いいこと尽くめだよ」
findings.todokanai: "That's right. Three heads are better than one, after all, so I see nothing but positives from us pooling our wisdom together."

findings.highlight: This is quite the tight schedule…
findings.evidenceJa: なんというタイトロープスケジュール…
findings.explanation: The coined 'tightrope schedule' continues the chapter's repeated tightrope imagery. Reducing it to a merely tight schedule deletes the callback.
findings.japanese: なんというタイトロープスケジュール…
findings.todokanai: This is quite the tight schedule…

findings.highlight: I'd probably end up getting chased away by her in a rage.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしがあの子なら怒鳴り散らすわね
findings.explanation: Youko says that if she were Kazusa, she herself would yell at an interrupter. The translation instead has Kazusa angrily chase Youko away.
findings.japanese:
「わたしがあの子なら怒鳴り散らすわね。
『今いいところなんだから邪魔するな』って…」
findings.todokanai: "I'd probably end up getting chased away by her in a rage. She'd probably say something like, 'don't bother me at a time like this'…"

findings.highlight: I suppose I wouldn't want to break the deadline I've established.
findings.evidenceJa: まぁ、とっくにデッドライン破ってるからなぁ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says their deadline has already been blown. Todokanai TL changes this into her desire not to break a deadline she established.
findings.japanese:
「まぁ、とっくにデッドライン破ってるからなぁ。
今さら頑張ったところで間に合うのやら…」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I suppose I wouldn't want to break the deadline I've established. I'm not sure if he'll make it in time even if he works hard at this point…"

findings.highlight: Todokanai Koi
findings.evidenceJa: 『届かない恋』の時も
findings.explanation: The load-bearing song title is left as untranslated romaji rather than translated as Love Beyond Reach, breaking English-edition title continuity.
findings.japanese:
「『届かない恋』の時も、
そうだったこと、知ってるもん」
findings.todokanai: "I knew this even when we worked on Todokanai Koi back then."

findings.highlight: I sought to become two amongst the three of us… I wanted to become two with him.
findings.evidenceJa: 三人でいることを二人に求めておきながら、自分は彼と二人になることを求めた。
findings.explanation: Setsuna confesses the contradiction plainly: while asking the other two to preserve the trio, she herself sought to be alone with Haruki. The first translated sentence is nonsensical and duplicates the second instead of stating what she demanded of Haruki and Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
「三人でいることを二人に求めておきながら、
自分は彼と二人になることを求めた。
…かずさのこと、出し抜いた」
findings.todokanai: "I sought to become two amongst the three of us… I wanted to become two with him. …And I ended up stealing the march on you, Kazusa."

findings.highlight: the lyrics I poured my heart and soul into for a day and a half
findings.evidenceJa: 一日と半日遅れた北原春希入魂…かもしれない新曲の詞
findings.explanation: 一日と半日遅れた means the lyrics are a day and a half late. Todokanai TL instead treats that duration as the time Haruki spent pouring himself into them.
findings.japanese:
一日と半日遅れた北原春希入魂…
かもしれない新曲の詞を書き連ねたノートを抱え、
スタジオの中に飛び込んだ瞬間…
findings.todokanai: The moment I bolted into the studio while carrying a notebook filled with the lyrics I poured my heart and soul into for a day and a half…

findings.highlight: despite my mentions of "although" and "however."
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の『けど』や『ですが』以前までの台詞に満面の笑みを見せた
findings.explanation: Hamada smiles at only the portion of Haruki's report before each 'but' or 'however,' deliberately ignoring the caveats. Todokanai TL says he smiles despite hearing them.
findings.japanese:
最近、俺のせいで色々と胃を痛めていただろう浜田さんは、
俺の『けど』や『ですが』以前までの台詞に
満面の笑みを見せた。
findings.todokanai: Hamada-san, who I imagine was put under a lot of stress because of me, responds to my explanation with a wide smile on his face despite my mentions of "although" and "however."

findings.highlight: I have to work on site for the entire month.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺、今月そんな現場ばっかり
findings.explanation: The staffer complains that all his recording jobs this month have been troubled like this one, not that he has been assigned to one site for the whole month.
findings.japanese:
「嘘ぉ、勘弁してよ…
俺、今月そんな現場ばっかり」
findings.todokanai: "You're kidding, spare me already… I have to work on site for the entire month."

findings.highlight: what, did Ogata Eiji suddenly decide to get involved in this?
findings.evidenceJa: どこの緒方英二だよ
findings.explanation: The director jokes 'Who do they think they are, Eiji Ogata?' about composing during the recording session, a White Album callback. The translation invents Ogata personally becoming involved in their project.
findings.japanese:
「収録中にスタジオの中で作曲とか…
どこの緒方英二だよ」
findings.todokanai: "Having to make a song in the studio in the middle of a recording session… what, did Ogata Eiji suddenly decide to get involved in this?"

findings.highlight: I've taken out countless days off this month
findings.evidenceJa: 私たちは今月いっぱい予定取ってあるからいいけど
findings.explanation: The staff are booked or have held their schedules open through the end of the month. The woman has not taken countless vacation days.
findings.japanese:
「そりゃ、私たちは
今月いっぱい予定取ってあるからいいけど…」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I've taken out countless days off this month, so that's actually fine, but…"

findings.highlight: Let's change the tempo here…
findings.evidenceJa: ここで転調入れるか…
findings.explanation: 転調 is a modulation or key change, not a tempo change.
findings.japanese:
「ん～んん～…と。
ここで転調入れるか…」
findings.todokanai: "Hmm～ mmm～… Alright. Let's change the tempo here…"

findings.highlight: Entry hours begin at 3 PM
findings.evidenceJa: １５時に会場入りだから
findings.explanation: Kazusa is due to arrive at the venue at 3 p.m.; this is not a statement that public entry hours begin then.
findings.japanese:
「１５時に会場入りだから…
それまでには曲を仕上げてもらう。
できるよね、かずさ？」
findings.todokanai: "Entry hours begin at 3 PM… so we should try to have the song finished before that time. You can do that, right, Kazusa?"

findings.highlight: There's a more practical appeal to being formulaic.
findings.evidenceJa: 数式はもっと機能的で美しいんだぞ
findings.explanation: Haruki pedantically answers the charge that his lyrics resemble equations by saying equations are much more functional and beautiful. Todokanai TL turns 数式 into the adjective 'formulaic' and deletes both halves of the joke.
findings.japanese:
「馬鹿言うな。
…数式はもっと機能的で美しいんだぞ」
findings.todokanai: "Don't be silly. …There's a more practical appeal to being formulaic."

findings.highlight: Why did I have to be assigned photography work today of all days!?
findings.evidenceJa: どうして今日に限って撮影が押すかなぁっ！
findings.explanation: Tomo complains that the shoot ran late today, not that she was assigned photography work that day.
findings.japanese: 「どうして今日に限って撮影が押すかなぁっ！」
findings.todokanai: "Why did I have to be assigned photography work today of all days!?"

findings.highlight: It's getting hard to breathe…
findings.evidenceJa: なんか息もつかせぬって感じなんだもん
findings.explanation: 息もつかせぬ describes the concert's breathtaking, unrelenting intensity. Todokanai TL literalizes it as Io suffering respiratory difficulty.
findings.japanese:
「どうしよ…鳥肌立ってる。
なんか息もつかせぬって感じなんだもん」
findings.todokanai: "What's wrong with me…? I'm getting goosebumps all over. It's getting hard to breathe…"

findings.highlight: the pain and numbness in them have finally subsided.
findings.evidenceJa: 指先の痛みと痺れが、そろそろ気持ちいい段階にまで突入してる
findings.explanation: Haruki says the pain and numbness have crossed into the perversely pleasant stage; they have not subsided.
findings.japanese:
しかも、指先の痛みと痺れが、
そろそろ気持ちいい段階にまで突入してるけど。
findings.todokanai: Plus, my fingers are just about starting to feel good again, given that the pain and numbness in them have finally subsided.

findings.highlight: I've made myself clear.
findings.evidenceJa: 言ってろ。
findings.explanation: 言ってろ dismisses Youko's boast as 'say what you like' or 'keep talking.' Todokanai TL reverses the speaking party and makes Kazusa claim she has made herself clear.
findings.japanese:
「言ってろ。
本当なら共演して叩き潰してやりたいところだけど、
あんたの名誉と健康のために自重しとく」
findings.todokanai: "I've made myself clear. I could've crushed you if we ended up performing together, but I decided against it in consideration of both your reputation and your health."

findings.highlight: to wow guests of a higher caliber, to be endorsed by fellow performers of a higher level
findings.evidenceJa: レベルの高い観客に揉まれて、レベルの高い共演者に恵まれて
findings.explanation: Youko asks whether Kazusa wants to be tested and tempered by discerning audiences and blessed with high-level collaborators. The translation changes those developmental pressures into impressing guests and receiving endorsements.
findings.japanese:
「レベルの高い観客に揉まれて、
レベルの高い共演者に恵まれて、
ずっと世界で戦っていたい？」
findings.todokanai: "You wish to wow guests of a higher caliber, to be endorsed by fellow performers of a higher level, and to fight against the world forever?"

findings.highlight: It's actually quite flashy…
findings.evidenceJa: 実は結構重いんだけどさ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says the concert dress is quite heavy, not flashy.
findings.japanese:
「どうだこれ？
実は結構重いんだけどさ」
findings.todokanai: "What do you think? It's actually quite flashy…"

findings.highlight: I can't really hear you.
findings.evidenceJa: 聞くな聞くな。
findings.explanation: Kazusa says 'Don't ask, don't ask'; she is not claiming she cannot hear Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「あ～、聞くな聞くな。
そのことに関しては、今は何も話したくない」
findings.todokanai: "Huh? I can't really hear you. I really don't wanna talk about anything related to that right now."

findings.highlight: A guitarist who was lambasted for his lack of skill over and over again. A pianist who was forced to play along time after time despite doing nothing wrong. A singer who kept comfortably singing, without thinking of anything else.
findings.evidenceJa:
ダメ出しを食らいまくってたギター。
何も悪くないのに何度も付き合わされていたピアノ。
諸事情関係なしに気持ちよく歌い続けてたボーカル。
findings.explanation: 諸事情関係なしに says Setsuna kept singing happily regardless of every circumstance; 'without thinking of anything else' makes her oblivious rather than irrepressible — The three contrasting rehearsal roles remain recognizable.
findings.japanese:
ダメ出しを食らいまくってたギター。
何も悪くないのに何度も付き合わされていたピアノ。
諸事情関係なしに気持ちよく歌い続けてたボーカル。
findings.todokanai: A guitarist who was lambasted for his lack of skill over and over again. A pianist who was forced to play along time after time despite doing nothing wrong. A singer who kept comfortably singing, without thinking of anything else.

findings.highlight: the slightest feeling of loneliness.
findings.evidenceJa: 少なからぬ寂寥感。
findings.explanation: 少なからぬ means a not inconsiderable measure of loneliness. 'The slightest' minimizes exactly what the Japanese emphasizes.
findings.japanese: そして、少なからぬ寂寥感。
findings.todokanai: As well as the slightest feeling of loneliness.

findings.highlight: I owe everything that I've been capable of doing up until now to you
findings.evidenceJa: あたしが今ここにいられるのは、全部、雪菜のおかげだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says her being here now is entirely thanks to Setsuna. Todokanai TL expands this into owing every accomplishment up to the present to her.
findings.japanese:
「あたしが今ここにいられるのは、
全部、雪菜のおかげだ」
findings.todokanai: "I owe everything that I've been capable of doing up until now to you, Setsuna."

findings.highlight: will never be able to love her again.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を愛さなかった俺を。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls himself the man who did not love Kazusa. The translation changes his past moral failure into a future inability to love her.
findings.japanese:
自分を見捨てた俺を。
自分を愛さなかった俺を。
findings.todokanai: She intends to separate from meーthe person who's abandoned her and will never be able to love her again.

findings.highlight: You don't need to give me a place I can aim for. I only ask that you give me a place I can return to.
findings.evidenceJa: あたしの目指す場所じゃなくていい。ただ、あたしの帰る場所でいてくれればいい
findings.explanation: Kazusa tells Youko she need not remain the destination Kazusa strives toward; she need only be the place Kazusa returns to. Todokanai TL makes Youko the giver of both places, weakening the mother-as-home contrast.
findings.japanese:
「あたしの目指す場所じゃなくていい。
ただ、あたしの帰る場所でいてくれればいい」
findings.todokanai: "You don't need to give me a place I can aim for. I only ask that you give me a place I can return to."

findings.highlight: Nor does Kazusa herself cause a stir.
findings.evidenceJa: そしてかずさだって、それどころの騒ぎじゃなかった。
findings.explanation: Kazusa is in no position to cry or react sentimentally because Setsuna's breakdown is now the emergency. The translation instead states, incoherently, that Kazusa does not cause a stir.
findings.japanese: そしてかずさだって、それどころの騒ぎじゃなかった。
findings.todokanai: Nor does Kazusa herself cause a stir.

findings.highlight: Don't take me for another girl.
findings.evidenceJa: あたし相手に、作んな
findings.explanation: Io tells Takeya not to put on an act with her. The translation turns 作る into treating her as another woman and obscures the setup for Takeya admitting that he is performing.
findings.japanese: 「あたし相手に、作んな」
findings.todokanai: "Don't take me for another girl."

findings.highlight: It's natural that I'd make my move, no? After all, you're so meek the way you are now.
findings.evidenceJa: 作るに決まってるだろ。だって素だといけそうじゃん、今のお前
findings.explanation: Takeya says of course he is putting on an act: if he were his unvarnished self, the present Io seems attainable. Todokanai TL changes acting into making a sexual move and invents that Io is meek.
findings.japanese:
「作るに決まってるだろ。
だって素だといけそうじゃん、今のお前」
findings.todokanai: "It's natural that I'd make my move, no? After all, you're so meek the way you are now."

findings.highlight: I wouldn't want to discover that I've been under nothing but a delusion after that.
findings.evidenceJa: 後で気の迷いだったとか思われそうな状況はヤなの
findings.explanation: Takeya rejects a situation in which Io might later decide her consent was only a momentary lapse. Todokanai TL makes Takeya the person who might discover he was deluded.
