findings.todokanai: The boundless kindness Setsuna has is deceiving Setsuna herself, and is bringing forth my dark heart that's trying to betray her.

findings.highlight: "Before I knew it, I couldn't even bring myself to separate myself from my feelings."
findings.evidenceJa:
「自分の気持ちと折り合いをつけることが、
いつの間にか、できなくなってたんだ」
findings.explanation: Haruki can no longer reconcile himself with or come to terms with his feelings; 'separate myself from my feelings' suggests dissociation instead — His inability to manage divided love remains in the surrounding confession.
findings.japanese:
「自分の気持ちと折り合いをつけることが、
いつの間にか、できなくなってたんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Before I knew it, I couldn't even bring myself to separate myself from my feelings."

findings.highlight: remained truthful to Setsuna to the very last detail.
findings.evidenceJa: 結局俺は、そんなかずさの妥協案さえも踏みにじり、雪菜に対して、最後の最後だけ正直で、そしてもっとも最悪かもしれない態度を取った。
findings.explanation: Haruki tramples Kazusa's compromise by being honest with Setsuna only at the very, very end, after sustained deception; that belated honesty may be his worst act. The English says he is truthful down to every last detail, turning temporal limitation into completeness and overstating what he disclosed.
findings.japanese:
結局俺は、そんなかずさの妥協案さえも踏みにじり、
雪菜に対して、最後の最後だけ正直で、
そしてもっとも最悪かもしれない態度を取った。
findings.todokanai: But in the end, I even stomped on that last desire of hers, and remained truthful to Setsuna to the very last detail. In doing so, I might have done something even more despicable.

findings.highlight: Of course I can't bring myself to say that. It would be nothing else but the remark of a defeated man.
findings.evidenceJa: …なんて、そんなこと言ったってしょうがない。それは度し難い男の勝手な妄言だ。
findings.explanation: Haruki has just said aloud that he forgot Setsuna and betrayed her from the bottom of his heart; the narration judges that saying so is useless, merely the self-serving nonsense of an incorrigible man. The English claims he cannot say what he demonstrably just said and mistranslates 度し難い, irredeemable or incorrigible, as defeated.
findings.japanese:
…なんて、そんなこと言ったってしょうがない。
それは度し難い男の勝手な妄言だ。
findings.todokanai: …Of course I can't bring myself to say that. It would be nothing else but the remark of a defeated man.

findings.highlight: That's why I can't force the burden of giving me hope upon Setsuna. I can't force the burden of giving me compassion onto her.
findings.evidenceJa:
だから、雪菜に
希望という名の重荷を背負わせたらいけない。
憐憫という名の責任感を抱かせたらいけない。
findings.explanation: Haruki must not make Setsuna carry a burden called hope or a sense of responsibility called pity; the English recasts both as burdens of giving him things — His refusal to exploit her hope and compassion remains.
findings.japanese:
だから、雪菜に
希望という名の重荷を背負わせたらいけない。
憐憫という名の責任感を抱かせたらいけない。
findings.todokanai: That's why I can't force the burden of giving me hope upon Setsuna. I can't force the burden of giving me compassion onto her.

findings.highlight: the Haruki that used to love me
findings.evidenceJa: 「強い人間のままで…あたしが愛した、出逢ったときの春希のままで…ずっと生きていって欲しいんだよ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa wants Haruki to remain the strong Haruki she loved—the person he was when they met. The English reverses the subject of 愛した and says Haruki used to love Kazusa, changing her definition of his authentic self into a claim that his love for her belongs to the past.
findings.japanese:
「強い人間のままで…
あたしが愛した、出逢ったときの春希のままで…
ずっと生きていって欲しいんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "I want you to remain strong… to live on as the Haruki that used to love me, and to remain the way you were when we first met."

findings.highlight: Rather than his looks, it's his weaknesses…
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつの、見た目よりも弱っちいところが…あたしなんかに引っ張られる愚かなところが…本当に、本当に、愛おしくてしょうがないんだ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa loves that Haruki is weaker than he looks, and foolish enough to be dragged along by someone like her. The English makes weakness something she prefers over his appearance, replacing the comparative characterization of a deceptively fragile man with a contrast between two objects of attraction.
findings.japanese:
「あいつの、見た目よりも弱っちいところが…
あたしなんかに引っ張られる愚かなところが…
本当に、本当に、愛おしくてしょうがないんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Rather than his looks, it's his weaknesses… The way he'll let himself be dragged along by someone like me like a fool, is so dear to me."

findings.highlight: yet you never told anyone…
findings.evidenceJa: 「ま、あんたにはバレバレだったと思うけど、それでも、誰かに話しておきたかった。…あたしの恋は、こんなに素敵なんだぞって」
findings.explanation: Although Youko surely saw through her, Kazusa still wanted to tell somebody how wonderful her love was. The English says Youko never told anyone, transferring the action to her mother and erasing Kazusa's need to confess and commemorate her love before leaving Japan.
findings.japanese:
「ま、あんたにはバレバレだったと思うけど、
それでも、誰かに話しておきたかった。
…あたしの恋は、こんなに素敵なんだぞって」
findings.todokanai: "Though I'm sure you knew everything anyway, yet you never told anyone… That's how amazing my love is."

findings.highlight: "It looks like I've still got something to live for for quite a long time."
findings.evidenceJa: 「どうやら、まだまだ長生きする必要があるみたいね」
findings.explanation: Youko now appears to need to live much longer; 'still got something to live for' changes longevity under illness into purpose — Her renewed will to live for Kazusa remains.
findings.japanese: 「どうやら、まだまだ長生きする必要があるみたいね」
findings.todokanai: "It looks like I've still got something to live for for quite a long time."

findings.highlight: Everything will be solved if you just pull your hand away.
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前が手を引けば、すぐに解ける。お前は、どこへでも行ける」
findings.explanation: Haruki is not gripping Kazusa; if she draws her hand back, their interlaced fingers will immediately come loose and she can go anywhere. The English reads 解ける as all their problems being solved, replacing the literal last physical bond that Kazusa is asking him to release.
findings.japanese:
「お前が手を引けば、すぐに解ける。
お前は、どこへでも行ける」
findings.todokanai: "Everything will be solved if you just pull your hand away. You'll be able to go anywhere."

findings.highlight: One year ago, I stopped having to rely on medicine anymore to treat my "mental damage as a result of overworking," as the doctors decided to interpret my symptoms as.
findings.evidenceJa: 一年前『身に余る仕事量とプレッシャーの大きさによるメンタルダメージ』と随分好意的に解釈された例の症状は、もう、薬に頼る必要もなくなるほどに落ち着いてきた。
findings.explanation: The symptoms were charitably diagnosed a year ago as damage from overwork and pressure; only now have they subsided enough that Haruki no longer needs medication. Todokanai TL moves stopping medication back one year and leaves the present recovery without a predicate.
findings.japanese:
一年前『身に余る仕事量とプレッシャーの大きさによる
メンタルダメージ』と随分好意的に解釈された例の症状は、
もう、薬に頼る必要もなくなるほどに落ち着いてきた。
findings.todokanai: One year ago, I stopped having to rely on medicine anymore to treat my "mental damage as a result of overworking," as the doctors decided to interpret my symptoms as.

findings.highlight: certain things would cause my nerves to stop listening to me
findings.evidenceJa: 何かきっかけがあるとすぐに自律神経が言うことを聞かなくなり
findings.explanation: Haruki says that for about six months any trigger could immediately throw his autonomic nervous system out of regulation. Generic 'nerves' suggests anxiety or disobedient body sensations and erases the concrete physiological aftermath of his breakdown.
findings.japanese:
とはいえ半年間くらいは、何かきっかけがあると
すぐに自律神経が言うことを聞かなくなり、
随分と周囲に迷惑を掛けたものだった。
findings.todokanai: But even then, for half a year, certain things would cause my nerves to stop listening to me, which caused those around me considerable trouble.

findings.highlight: It's not strong enough to leave a mark in their hearts.
findings.evidenceJa: 心をガツンと殴るほど強くない。けれど、優しく包み込む。なのに、華がある。
findings.explanation: Haruki contrasts Setsuna's non-punching vocal style with its enveloping gentleness and glamour. Todokanai TL turns 'not forceful enough to punch you in the heart' into the disparaging claim that her singing cannot leave an emotional mark, undercutting the praise that structures the passage.
findings.japanese:
心をガツンと殴るほど強くない。
けれど、優しく包み込む。
なのに、華がある。
findings.todokanai: It's not strong enough to leave a mark in their hearts. Rather, her voice gently envelops us, though there's also a brilliant quality to it.

findings.highlight: the scattering powder snow
findings.evidenceJa: 空から降りてくる粉雪は、ますますその数を増やしていく。
findings.explanation: This is ordinary fine, powdery snow in the reprise of the opening image, not the separately load-bearing English song title 'Powder Snow.' Using the exact song title here collapses an intentional distinction between the weather motif and the named song.
findings.japanese:
まだ耳に残る雪菜の歌をかき消すように、
空から降りてくる粉雪は、
ますますその数を増やしていく。
findings.todokanai: And now, as if to drown out the sound of Setsuna's singing, the scattering powder snow descending from the heavens grows ever more dense.

findings.highlight: I'm giving Setsuna no choice but to protect me.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜に、護ってもらうしかなくなる。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he will again be reduced to having no choice but to rely on Setsuna to protect him. Todokanai TL transfers the lack of choice to Setsuna, making him compel her instead of confessing his dependency.
findings.japanese:
だって俺は、また雪菜に迷惑をかける。
雪菜に、護ってもらうしかなくなる。
findings.todokanai: Because I'm causing Setsuna trouble again. I'm giving Setsuna no choice but to protect me.

findings.highlight: The time we decided on was 6 o'clock, wasn't it?
findings.evidenceJa: 春希くんとこの定時って６時だったよね？
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki's official quitting time at work is six, so proposing an eight-o'clock start already assumes two hours of overtime. Todokanai TL invents a previously agreed six-o'clock appointment and loses the workplace joke.
findings.japanese:
「８時ぃ？
春希くんとこの定時って６時だったよね？
そりゃ、普段は忙しいのはわかるけどさぁ」
findings.todokanai: "8 o'clock? The time we decided on was 6 o'clock, wasn't it? I get that you're busy, though."

findings.highlight: you really have become stubborn.
findings.evidenceJa: お前、結構したたかになったなぁ
findings.explanation: したたか here means shrewd, formidable, or calculating: Setsuna has learned how to bargain with Haruki. 'Stubborn' misidentifies the trait and misses her deliberately canny demand.
findings.japanese:
「雪菜…
お前、結構したたかになったなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Setsuna… you really have become stubborn."

findings.highlight: I've begun to talk to this foolish girl who's so dear to me.
findings.evidenceJa: いつの間にか『お前』って呼び捨てられるくらい、愚かで、愛しい女が。
findings.explanation: The narration explicitly marks that Haruki has grown close enough to call Setsuna お前 without a name or title. Todokanai TL deletes the quoted address form and the relationship milestone, replacing it with the contentless statement that he has begun to talk to her.
findings.japanese:
いつの間にか『お前』って呼び捨てられるくらい、
愚かで、愛しい女が。
findings.todokanai: Before I even realized it, I've begun to talk to this foolish girl who's so dear to me.

findings.highlight: You really have become good-natured.
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に、いい性格になったよ
findings.explanation: いい性格 is sarcastic here: after Setsuna's barb about being loved second-most, Haruki says she has developed quite a nasty or formidable personality. 'Good-natured' reverses the joke into sincere praise.
findings.japanese: 「…本当に、いい性格になったよ」
findings.todokanai: "…You really have become good-natured."

findings.highlight: leaving us there in its wake.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ白く、綺麗なだけの世界を目の前に広げ、俺たちを、そこに閉じこめようとする。
findings.explanation: The snow spreads a merely white and beautiful world before them and tries to imprison them inside it. Todokanai TL deletes the active attempt at confinement, the central danger in Haruki's fantasy of a purified two-person world, and substitutes the semantically unrelated 'in its wake.'
findings.japanese:
ただ白く、綺麗なだけの世界を目の前に広げ、
俺たちを、そこに閉じこめようとする。
findings.todokanai: A white world abundant only in beauty expands before our eyes, leaving us there in its wake.

findings.highlight: all of the hidden truths and forgotten emotions it had been hiding will once again be brought into daylight for all to see.
findings.evidenceJa: 一度解けたら、のたうち回って生き抜いた過去を、二度と忘れたらいけない思い出を、もう一度、俺たちの心に呼び戻す。
findings.explanation: When snow melts, it summons back into their hearts the past they writhed through and survived, and the memories they must never again forget. Todokanai TL invents hidden truths, already-forgotten emotions, daylight, and public exposure, erasing both survival and the moral duty to remember.
findings.japanese:
一度解けたら、のたうち回って生き抜いた過去を、
二度と忘れたらいけない思い出を、
もう一度、俺たちの心に呼び戻す。
findings.todokanai: Once it melts, all of the hidden truths and forgotten emotions it had been hiding will once again be brought into daylight for all to see.

findings.highlight: showed us to our suite despite looking completely taken aback,
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちを、ドン引きしつつ部屋まで案内してくれた先輩、というか、冬馬曜子オフィス日本支部の工藤美代子さんが、ものすっごい気まずそうな目で俺を覗き込んでいる。
findings.explanation: The sentence says Miyoko, their senior and the Japanese-branch staffer who showed them to the room while recoiling at the quarrel, is now peering at Haruki with intense awkwardness. Todokanai TL leaves the English as an incomplete subordinate clause ending in a comma, omits her present look entirely, and never supplies a main predicate.
findings.japanese:
俺たちを、ドン引きしつつ部屋まで案内してくれた先輩、
というか、冬馬曜子オフィス日本支部の工藤美代子さんが、
ものすっごい気まずそうな目で俺を覗き込んでいる。
findings.todokanai: This person, or more specifically Kudou Miyoko of the Japanese branch of Touma Youko Office, showed us to our suite despite looking completely taken aback,

findings.highlight: kept glaring at me with a grim expression until it was no longer visible behind the closing door.
findings.evidenceJa: 工藤さんは扉を閉める最後の最後まで、悲壮な表情で俺を見つめ、帰っていった。
findings.explanation: Miyoko fixes Haruki with a desperate, almost tragic look until the very last instant she closes the door, then leaves. Todokanai TL changes anxious concern into hostile glaring and invents the physically confused image of an expression becoming hidden behind a door.
findings.japanese:
工藤さんは扉を閉める最後の最後まで、
悲壮な表情で俺を見つめ、帰っていった。
findings.todokanai: Walking away, Kudou-san kept glaring at me with a grim expression until it was no longer visible behind the closing door.

findings.highlight: she didn't seem to mind at the time.
findings.evidenceJa: でもまだその時までは、あいつもいつも通りだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that up to that point Kazusa had still been her usual self. The text does not say she was unbothered; her 'usual self' can include irritation, and the distinction matters because he is locating when her behavior became abnormal.
findings.japanese:
でもまだその時までは、あいつもいつも通りだった。
問題なのは飛行機に乗ってからというか、
その後の乗り継ぎを含めてやたらと色々あったことだ。
findings.todokanai: But she didn't seem to mind at the time. The problems only started after we boarded the next flight, and the transit that followed.

findings.highlight: After years of running away, we've finally returned to the place we once called home.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺と二人で逃げ出してから数年。やっと帰ってきた故郷なんだ。
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly recalls that Kazusa ran away with him alone several years ago and has now finally returned to her homeland. Todokanai TL turns the completed joint elopement into years spent running away and blurs Kazusa's personal homecoming into a generic place 'we once called home.'
findings.japanese:
……俺と二人で逃げ出してから数年。
やっと帰ってきた故郷なんだ。
findings.todokanai: …After years of running away, we've finally returned to the place we once called home.

findings.highlight: spending yet another day flirting with your husband takes priority over reuniting with your own mother…
findings.evidenceJa: 久しぶりに会う母親ほったらかして、一緒に住んでる旦那といつも通りイチャつくのを優先するなんて……とんでもない親不孝娘ね
findings.explanation: Youko completes the complaint by calling Kazusa an outrageous unfilial daughter. Todokanai TL drops the accusation that gives the line its punchline and leaves the quotation syntactically unclosed.
findings.japanese:
「久しぶりに会う母親ほったらかして、
一緒に住んでる旦那といつも通りイチャつくのを
優先するなんて……とんでもない親不孝娘ね」
findings.todokanai: "So according to you, spending yet another day flirting with your husband takes priority over reuniting with your own mother…

findings.highlight: You mean to say that you couldn't care less if your mother died alone in some barren corner of the world?
findings.evidenceJa: あなたは私が社会の片隅でひっそりと孤独死してもいいっていうのね。ああ……育て方を間違えたわ
findings.explanation: Youko follows the lonely-death melodrama with 'Ah… I raised you wrong.' Todokanai TL omits that conclusion and leaves the quote open, so Haruki's immediate 'You sure did' has no translated referent.
findings.japanese:
「か、かずさ……なんて容赦のない。
あなたは私が社会の片隅でひっそりと孤独死しても
いいっていうのね。ああ……育て方を間違えたわ」
findings.todokanai: "K-Kazusa… how cold of you. You mean to say that you couldn't care less if your mother died alone in some barren corner of the world?

findings.highlight: These two have always found themselves separated for one reason or another,
findings.evidenceJa: 普段は遠く離れ離れの二人だけれど、最近では、かずさもＩＴツールをそこそこ使いこなし、曜子さんとのコミュニケーションに余念がない。
findings.explanation: The sentence says that although mother and daughter normally live far apart, Kazusa has recently learned to handle online tools and communicates with Youko assiduously. Todokanai TL keeps only the subordinate setup, omits the entire present reconciliation, and ends on a comma.
findings.japanese:
普段は遠く離れ離れの二人だけれど、
最近では、かずさもＩＴツールをそこそこ使いこなし、
曜子さんとのコミュニケーションに余念がない。
findings.todokanai: These two have always found themselves separated for one reason or another,

findings.highlight: Just as Youko-san herself said back then, not even tomorrow was a certainty for her.
findings.evidenceJa: 最初は、曜子さんが自身で言う通り、『明日をも知れぬ』という症状だったけれど、粘り強い治療を続け、今も何とか小康状態を保っている。
findings.explanation: The original contrasts Youko's initially critical condition with the relative stability she has maintained through persistent treatment. Todokanai TL translates only the initial danger and entirely omits her continuing treatment and present remission-like plateau.
findings.japanese:
最初は、曜子さんが自身で言う通り、
『明日をも知れぬ』という症状だったけれど、
粘り強い治療を続け、今も何とか小康状態を保っている。
findings.todokanai: Just as Youko-san herself said back then, not even tomorrow was a certainty for her.

findings.highlight: see her reach adulthood,
findings.evidenceJa: 成人式の晴れ姿をこの目に収めて、お葬式で弔辞を読むくらいには生き永らえてみせるわ
findings.explanation: Youko vows not only to see the grandchild come of age but to live long enough to deliver the eulogy at the child's funeral. Todokanai TL cuts the line before that grotesque escalation, leaves the quotation unfinished, and makes Haruki's next protest about killing their unborn child appear unmotivated.
findings.japanese:
「そうね、少なくとも、初孫に名前を付けて、
入学式に立ち会って、成人式の晴れ姿をこの目に収めて、
お葬式で弔辞を読むくらいには生き永らえてみせるわ」
findings.todokanai: "At the very least, I can see myself living long enough to name my first grandchild, attend her entrance ceremony, see her reach adulthood,

findings.highlight: In fact, she's always like this when she talks to Youko-san.
findings.evidenceJa: 軽口はいくらでも叩くけれど、少しでも病状のことになると、急に口をつぐむ。
findings.explanation: The defining contrast is omitted: Kazusa trades endless jokes with her mother, then falls abruptly silent at the slightest mention of her illness. 'Always like this' neither states what she normally does nor explains the emotionally loaded change the scene is analyzing.
findings.japanese:
実は今でも、曜子さんと話すときはいつもそんな感じで、
軽口はいくらでも叩くけれど、
少しでも病状のことになると、急に口をつぐむ。
findings.todokanai: In fact, she's always like this when she talks to Youko-san.

findings.highlight: It came in the form of a visit to Vienna by Youko-san, who took the trip despite her illness.
findings.evidenceJa: 病をおしてウィーンにやってきた曜子さんと、そして……
findings.explanation: The Japanese deliberately leaves a second catalyst hanging after Youko—'Youko, who came to Vienna despite her illness, and then…' Todokanai TL closes the sentence as though Youko alone were the answer, deleting the suspenseful second term in the thaw that later points beyond this dinner.
findings.japanese: 病をおしてウィーンにやってきた曜子さんと、そして……
findings.todokanai: It came in the form of a visit to Vienna by Youko-san, who took the trip despite her illness.

findings.highlight: The adoration we feel for the country we were raised in.
findings.evidenceJa: 生まれ育った国への消えない憧憬。少しでも許してもらいたいという淡い期待。
findings.explanation: The list culminates in the couple's faint hope of receiving even a little forgiveness from the people they hurt. Todokanai TL omits that motive entirely, yet the next line refers to plural 'naive hopes,' weakening the reason they finally accepted the return.
findings.japanese:
かつて愛した人たちとふたたび同じ場所に立つ喜び。
生まれ育った国への消えない憧憬。
少しでも許してもらいたいという淡い期待。
findings.todokanai: The joy of being in the same place as those we once loved. The adoration we feel for the country we were raised in.

findings.highlight: I'm starting to get bored of looking at her sleep…
findings.evidenceJa: いい加減、ずっとこいつの寝顔見てるのも……いや、飽きないけど、空腹に耐えられないのも本当で。
findings.explanation: Haruki starts to say he has had enough of watching her sleep, immediately corrects himself—no, he never gets tired of that—and admits only that he cannot bear the hunger. Todokanai TL cuts before the self-correction and states as fact the very feeling he retracts.
findings.japanese:
何しろこっちは起きてからもう５時間くらい経ってる。
いい加減、ずっとこいつの寝顔見てるのも……
いや、飽きないけど、空腹に耐えられないのも本当で。
findings.todokanai: In any case, it's been five hours since I woke up. I'm starting to get bored of looking at her sleep…

findings.highlight: she managed to love someone like me, and yet I…
findings.evidenceJa: だって、俺なんか、愛してた。なのに、あんな……
findings.explanation: In the middle of Kazusa's guilt over Setsuna, Haruki reflects that Setsuna loved even someone like him, and yet Kazusa or the two of them did what they did. Todokanai TL's added final 'I' reallocates the suspended reproach solely to Haruki and makes the sentence sound as though Setsuna merely 'managed' the feat of loving him.
findings.japanese:
だって、俺なんか、愛してた。
なのに、あんな……
findings.todokanai: After all, she managed to love someone like me, and yet I…

findings.highlight: This is a city of over ten million people in the heart of world-famous Tokyo!
findings.evidenceJa: そんな偶然が起こるとでも思ってるのか？
findings.explanation: Haruki's argument culminates in the rhetorical question 'Do you really think a coincidence like that could happen?' Todokanai TL drops it and leaves the quotation open, removing the exact claim Kazusa's anxious rebuttal answers.
findings.japanese:
「お前、ここをどこだと思ってる？
一千万都市だぞ？　花の都大東京だぞ？
そんな偶然が起こるとでも思ってるのか？」
findings.todokanai: "Just where do you think we are? This is a city of over ten million people in the heart of world-famous Tokyo!

findings.highlight: Don't try to rile me up, you bastard!
findings.evidenceJa: 今さら歯の浮くようなこと言うな馬鹿野郎
findings.explanation: Kazusa tells Haruki not to say such embarrassingly sappy or cheesy things now. Todokanai TL turns romantic embarrassment into an accusation that he is provoking her, breaking the setup for his reply about a hackneyed pickup line.
findings.japanese:
「お互い様だろ馬鹿野郎……
今さら歯の浮くようなこと言うな馬鹿野郎」
findings.todokanai: "I could say the same, you bastard…! Don't try to rile me up, you bastard!"

findings.highlight: the same old cliched provocations.
findings.evidenceJa: こんな陳腐な口説き文句に引っかかる馬鹿がいるからだ
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly calls what he said a clichéd seduction or pickup line and says he uses it because one particular fool always falls for it. 'Provocations' removes the flirtation and makes Kazusa's answer—because it is you—lose its romantic force.
findings.japanese:
「そりゃ、いつまで経っても、
こんな陳腐な口説き文句に引っかかる馬鹿がいるからだ」
findings.todokanai: "I'm only doing it because a certain idiot keeps falling for the same old cliched provocations."

findings.highlight: No matter how many punches we have to take, and no matter how hard it is, we'll live in harmony with the outside world.
findings.evidenceJa:
どれだけ叩かれても、辛くても
外と触れ合って生きていくって……
findings.explanation: They resolve to live in contact with the outside world however much it attacks them or hurts; 'live in harmony' promises a concord the Japanese explicitly does not — The following line restores the expectation of pain.
findings.japanese:
どれだけ叩かれても、辛くても
外と触れ合って生きていくって……
findings.todokanai: No matter how many punches we have to take, and no matter how hard it is, we'll live in harmony with the outside world.

findings.highlight: I've decided to move forward with my life, even if it means I have to get hurt, whether because of myself or because of others.
findings.evidenceJa: 傷ついて、傷つけられて、これからも生きていくって、決めたんだから。
findings.explanation: The couple have decided to keep living while hurting others and being hurt themselves. Todokanai TL makes the decision Haruki's alone and converts the active moral admission that they will hurt people into the passive idea that his own actions may hurt him.
findings.japanese:
傷ついて、傷つけられて、
これからも生きていくって、決めたんだから。
findings.todokanai: I've decided to move forward with my life, even if it means I have to get hurt, whether because of myself or because of others.

findings.highlight: but it's not the only thing I gave her in this place.
findings.evidenceJa: それが三年前、俺がかずさに与えたもの。そしてここが、その中でも偽名以外を与えた場所。
findings.explanation: Haruki lists the comb, glasses, scarf, hat, and false name as what he gave Kazusa three years earlier, then identifies this mall as where he gave her all of those except the alias. Todokanai TL instead vaguely says he gave her additional unidentified things here and loses the precise physical callback.
findings.japanese:
それが三年前、俺がかずさに与えたもの。
そしてここが、その中でも偽名以外を与えた場所。
findings.todokanai: That's what I gave to Kazusa three years ago, but it's not the only thing I gave her in this place.

findings.highlight: only walking around the streets of Onjuku with nothing but our memories to guide us.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ記憶を頼りにさまよい、懐かしがり、はしゃぎ、そして笑いあった。
findings.explanation: The day is summarized not merely as wandering by memory, but as reminiscing, romping excitedly, and laughing together. Todokanai TL drops the entire sequence of recovered joy that makes their subsequent silence at the final location emotionally legible.
findings.japanese:
一度も電車やバスに乗らず、
ただ御宿の街を、ただ記憶を頼りにさまよい、
懐かしがり、はしゃぎ、そして笑いあった。
findings.todokanai: Not once getting on a bus or a train, only walking around the streets of Onjuku with nothing but our memories to guide us.

findings.highlight: I'd only figured that out much later after the fact.
findings.evidenceJa: いや、本当は二回目だったって、後から聞いたっけ。
findings.explanation: Haruki remembers being told afterward that this had actually been their second kiss—Kazusa kissed him first while he slept. Todokanai TL changes a later revelation from another person into something he independently figured out, obscuring the callback and who possessed the secret.
findings.japanese: いや、本当は二回目だったって、後から聞いたっけ。
findings.todokanai: Actually, that was the second time, though I'd only figured that out much later after the fact.

findings.highlight: As always, we spend our time together without any idea of what the future holds in store for us, even on this sudden vacation.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちは相変わらず、突然訪れた、宙に浮いたような先の見えない休暇の中にいた。
findings.explanation: The couple are still suspended inside an unexpected, unmoored vacation whose next step they cannot see. Todokanai TL turns 相変わらず into habitual 'as always,' invents a general statement about spending time together, and loses the image of a temporary holiday hanging in midair.
findings.japanese:
俺たちは相変わらず、突然訪れた、
宙に浮いたような先の見えない休暇の中にいた。
findings.todokanai: As always, we spend our time together without any idea of what the future holds in store for us, even on this sudden vacation.

findings.highlight: but you should've said that when we were in Onjuku.
findings.evidenceJa: ここら辺だとコンビニくらいしかないぞ
findings.explanation: Haruki adds that around Iwazucho a convenience store is about their only option. Todokanai TL drops that clause and leaves the quotation open, removing the direct setup for Kazusa's defense of convenience-store sweets.
findings.japanese:
「そういう気遣いができるようになったのは評価するが、
御宿にいる時に言ってくれ。
ここら辺だとコンビニくらいしかないぞ」
findings.todokanai: "I admire that you've become considerate enough to think about that, but you should've said that when we were in Onjuku.

findings.highlight: that was just business, a mere rite of passage, a teeny little appointment.
findings.evidenceJa: 社交辞令じゃない、通過儀礼じゃない、お約束じゃない～
findings.explanation: Youko calls her greeting a social nicety, a ritual, a conventional bit everyone is expected to perform. Todokanai TL mistranslates 社交辞令 as business and お約束 as an appointment, producing a list whose first and third items do not make sense in the exchange.
findings.japanese:
「やぁねかずさ、社交辞令じゃない、通過儀礼じゃない、
お約束じゃない～」
findings.todokanai: "Come now, Kazusa, that was just business, a mere rite of passage, a teeny little appointment."

findings.highlight: Normally, Kudou-san and I would have been strongly opposed to a plan like this, writing it off as a "waste of money."
findings.evidenceJa: いつもなら、『経費の無駄遣い』とか言って猛反対するはずの俺も工藤さんも、このワガママだけは、見過ごさない訳にはいかなかった。
findings.explanation: The point is the exception: Haruki and Miyoko would normally oppose such spending, but this was the one selfish wish they could not simply overlook or dismiss. Todokanai TL stops after the habitual opposition and omits the approval that explains why the restoration happened.
findings.japanese:
いつもなら、『経費の無駄遣い』とか言って
猛反対するはずの俺も工藤さんも、
このワガママだけは、見過ごさない訳にはいかなかった。
findings.todokanai: Normally, Kudou-san and I would have been strongly opposed to a plan like this, writing it off as a "waste of money."

findings.highlight: cheerfully passing the time by watching a lame variety TV show,
findings.evidenceJa: くっだらないバラエティを文句言いながら見て、くっだらない話に花を咲かせて。
findings.explanation: The family watch the stupid variety show while complaining about it and let equally stupid conversation blossom. Todokanai TL drops both the affectionate complaining and the lively talk, then leaves the line grammatically hanging on a comma.
findings.japanese:
冬馬家のリビングで、三人で食卓を囲み、
くっだらないバラエティを文句言いながら見て、
くっだらない話に花を咲かせて。
findings.todokanai: Three people sitting around the dinner table of the Touma household, cheerfully passing the time by watching a lame variety TV show,

findings.highlight: in a way that seemed impossible just a few months prior.
findings.evidenceJa: 穏やかで無駄な時間を過ごすなんて、かつては想像もできなかったけれど……
findings.explanation: Haruki says that once, in their former lives and relationships, he could not have imagined peacefully wasting time with these people. Todokanai TL invents a timeframe of only a few months, sharply minimizing the years of estrangement the restored household resolves.
findings.japanese:
こんなふうに、この人たちと、
穏やかで無駄な時間を過ごすなんて、
かつては想像もできなかったけれど……
findings.todokanai: Just like that, these three were able to waste their time in happiness and quiet, in a way that seemed impossible just a few months prior.

findings.highlight: raising sheep or something.
findings.evidenceJa: 鵜飼いでもして稼いでもらいなさいな
findings.explanation: Youko tells Kazusa to make her manager husband earn the tax money by practicing 'cormorant fishing'—managing lucrative performers as cormorants who bring the catch to their handler. Todokanai TL turns the specific 鵜飼い metaphor into raising sheep, so Kazusa's next question about who exactly the 'cormorants' are becomes a nonsensical question about sheep.
findings.japanese:
「そのくらいは、あなたの愛する旦那に、
鵜飼いでもして稼いでもらいなさいな」
findings.todokanai: "And to solve that issue, you have a beloved husband who will earn back that money by raising sheep or something."

findings.highlight: eventually their daughter helped me to convince them as well.
findings.evidenceJa: でも、向こうの娘さんも一緒に説得してくれてね。それで、今は……
findings.explanation: Youko says the other family's daughter joined her in persuading the parents, and then deliberately trails into the present result: 'and now…' Todokanai TL closes the sentence before that suspended resolution, dropping the cue that reconciliation has progressed to a new current state.
findings.japanese:
「それからも、何度会ったか覚えてないけれど……
でも、向こうの娘さんも一緒に説得してくれてね。
それで、今は……」
findings.todokanai: "I don't remember how many times I met them after that, but eventually their daughter helped me to convince them as well."

findings.highlight: "Mom…"
findings.evidenceJa: 「お母さん……」
findings.explanation: Kazusa has called Youko the rougher 母さん throughout the scene, then switches here to the childlike and ceremonially appropriate お母さん before kneeling and formally thanking her. Todokanai TL renders both forms identically as 'Mom,' leaving the emotional regression and the setup for Youko's astonishment completely unmarked.
findings.japanese: 「お母さん……」
findings.todokanai: "Mom…"

findings.highlight: we had already lost eight precious hours of it.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちに残された時間は、すでに八時間を切っていた。
findings.explanation: Fewer than eight hours remain before the memorial day and year end. Todokanai TL says they have lost eight hours, which would leave roughly sixteen; it reverses the quantity at the center of Haruki's urgency.
findings.japanese:
今年最後のメモリアルデーにもかかわらず、
俺たちに残された時間は、すでに八時間を切っていた。
findings.todokanai: Despite being the last commemorative day of the year, we had already lost eight precious hours of it.

findings.highlight: Unable to bring myself to break apart such an endearing spectacle,
findings.evidenceJa: そんな訳で俺は近くの喫茶店でモーニングを頼みつつ時間を潰して、二人が起きるのを待った。
findings.explanation: Haruki therefore kills time over a breakfast set at a nearby café while waiting for mother and daughter to wake. Todokanai TL keeps only the subordinate emotional setup, omits his entire action, and ends on a comma; the next line's forced lunch order consequently lacks its location and cause.
findings.japanese:
その微笑ましい光景を壊してしまうのは忍びなく、
そんな訳で俺は近くの喫茶店でモーニングを頼みつつ
時間を潰して、二人が起きるのを待った。
findings.todokanai: Unable to bring myself to break apart such an endearing spectacle,

findings.highlight: Houjou High School.
findings.evidenceJa: 峰城大学付属学園。
findings.explanation: The full institution is Houjou University's affiliated academy or high school, not simply Houjou High School. Dropping 大学付属 erases the university affiliation that governs the campus description and carries the recurring 付属祭 wordplay; an English edition needs the standardized University High School name.
findings.japanese: 峰城大学付属学園。
findings.todokanai: Houjou High School.

findings.highlight: either her pride as a delinquent, or her desire to spite the class rep triumphed over her wariness.
findings.evidenceJa: 意を決して、強い足取りで俺を追い抜いていく。
findings.explanation: Kazusa makes up her mind, strides forcefully past Haruki, and leads into the school. Todokanai TL stops at the possible motives and omits the decisive action, leaving the next standalone 'Toward the school building' as a fragment without a subject.
findings.japanese:
けれど最後には、不良の矜持なのか、
委員長に意地を張ったのか、
意を決して、強い足取りで俺を追い抜いていく。
findings.todokanai: In the end though, either her pride as a delinquent, or her desire to spite the class rep triumphed over her wariness.

findings.highlight: we bring back long forgotten memories to the light.
findings.evidenceJa: ずっと忘れていた、封印していた淡い記憶を、その陽光よりも明るい白日の下にさらけ出す。
findings.explanation: The empty sunset classroom itself exposes their long-forgotten, sealed-away pale memories beneath a daylight brighter than the sun entering it. Todokanai TL makes the couple voluntarily 'bring back' generic memories and drops the sealed-memory paradox and the room's active revelatory force.
findings.japanese:
そんな、俺たち以外に誰もいない夕暮れの教室は、
ずっと忘れていた、封印していた淡い記憶を、
その陽光よりも明るい白日の下にさらけ出す。
findings.todokanai: Under the evening sun, in a classroom empty save the two of us, we bring back long forgotten memories to the light.

findings.highlight: someone who keeps making me want to say embarrassing things.
findings.evidenceJa: 恥ずかしいことばかり言わせたがる奴と一緒に暮らしてるせいでな
findings.explanation: Haruki lives with someone who is always trying to make him say embarrassing things—Kazusa actively solicits declarations from him. Todokanai TL changes this to her inspiring his own desire to say them, reversing the married-couple dynamic he is teasing her about.
findings.japanese:
「恥ずかしいことばかり言わせたがる奴と
一緒に暮らしてるせいでな」
findings.todokanai: "That's because I live with someone who keeps making me want to say embarrassing things."

findings.highlight: during the school festival.
findings.evidenceJa: 付属祭の時よりも、寒い
findings.explanation: Haruki uses the coined 付属祭, the trio's quoted private name for their University High School festival and its later reprise, not the generic 学園祭. Todokanai TL normalizes it to 'school festival,' deleting the deliberately repeated coinage and the callback it signals.
findings.japanese:
「うん、寒いな。
付属祭の時よりも、寒い」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, it's cold. Even colder than during the school festival."

findings.highlight: "This is the last time, okay?"
findings.evidenceJa: 最終的には『今回だけだぞ』と応えてくれて
findings.explanation: Kazusa relents with 'just this once,' the familiar pretense that each indulgence is a one-off. Todokanai TL changes it to 'the last time,' an explicit promise of finality that she does not make.
findings.japanese:
けれど、これもいつも通り、
最終的には『今回だけだぞ』と応えてくれて、
かずさは、静かに弾き始めた。
findings.todokanai: And of course, also as always, she relents by saying "This is the last time, okay?" before quietly beginning her performance.

findings.highlight: The solitary performance she held every day for three years, using this piano.
findings.evidenceJa: 付属に通った三年間、ずっと弾いていたピアノ。
findings.explanation: This is the piano Kazusa played throughout three school years; the English invents a solitary performance held every day — The piano's sustained place in her school life is preserved and elaborated next.
findings.japanese: 付属に通った三年間、ずっと弾いていたピアノ。
findings.todokanai: The solitary performance she held every day for three years, using this piano.

findings.highlight: which also worsened the friction between her and her classmates.
findings.evidenceJa: けれどその存在のせいで、かずさから友達を遠ざけた、祝福の、そして呪いのピアノ。
findings.explanation: The piano is explicitly both blessing and curse: it stayed beside Kazusa yet helped keep friends away from her. Todokanai TL reduces this dual symbol to ordinary classroom friction and omits the named blessing/curse opposition.
findings.japanese:
三年間、ずっとかずさと共にあり、
けれどその存在のせいで、かずさから友達を遠ざけた、
祝福の、そして呪いのピアノ。
findings.todokanai: The piano that stood by Kazusa for those three years, and which also worsened the friction between her and her classmates.

findings.highlight: The piano that guided our amateur band to greatness.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の拙いギターを導き、俺たちの素人バンドを導き、学園祭ライブを成功に導いてくれたピアノ。
findings.explanation: The sentence's three-step anaphora says the piano guided Haruki's poor guitar, guided their amateur band, and guided the school-festival concert to success. Todokanai TL repeats 'to greatness' twice and entirely omits the culminating successful live performance.
findings.japanese:
八年前、俺の拙いギターを導き、
俺たちの素人バンドを導き、
学園祭ライブを成功に導いてくれたピアノ。
findings.todokanai: The piano that guided my clumsy guitar to greatness. The piano that guided our amateur band to greatness.

findings.highlight: the Kitahara and Touma family banquet.
findings.evidenceJa: それが北原家、冬馬家披露宴の日程
findings.explanation: Youko identifies the date for the Kitahara–Touma wedding reception, 披露宴. 'Family banquet' removes the public wedding function and makes Haruki's subsequent questions about ceremony permission and venue sound disconnected.
findings.japanese:
「そ。
それが北原家、冬馬家披露宴の日程」
findings.todokanai: "That's right. That is the plan for the Kitahara and Touma family banquet."

findings.highlight: "I-I-I didn't… I didn't agree to…!"
findings.evidenceJa:
「あ、あ……あたしが……
あたしがっ、こんな……っ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa's fragment is simply 'Me… me, like this…'; 'I didn't agree to' invents a consent objection rather than speechless self-consciousness — Her resistance to the bridal costume is established before and after.
findings.japanese:
「あ、あ……あたしが……
あたしがっ、こんな……っ」
findings.todokanai: "I-I-I didn't… I didn't agree to…!"

findings.highlight: I feel like a lone traveler marching against the north wind.
findings.evidenceJa: こうなったときの彼女は、まさに北風に抗う旅人。生半可な強制じゃ、てこでも動かない。
findings.explanation: The line invokes 'The North Wind and the Sun': Setsuna is the traveler resisting the north wind, immovable by half-hearted force. Todokanai TL makes Haruki the traveler and turns the domestic persuasion problem into his own march against weather, breaking both agency and the fable setup.
findings.japanese:
こうなったときの彼女は、まさに北風に抗う旅人。
生半可な強制じゃ、てこでも動かない。
findings.todokanai: When she's like this, I feel like a lone traveler marching against the north wind. Ordinary means simply will not work.

findings.highlight: the only thing capable of stopping the north wind is the sun.
findings.evidenceJa: そう、太陽の光を浴びせるまでだ。
findings.explanation: Continuing the fable, Haruki decides to bathe the resistant traveler Setsuna in sunlight—use warmth and temptation where force fails. Todokanai TL says the sun stops the north wind, which is not what happens in the fable and compounds the preceding reassignment of traveler and wind.
findings.japanese: そう、太陽の光を浴びせるまでだ。
findings.todokanai: Of course, the only thing capable of stopping the north wind is the sun.

findings.highlight: you already do the laundry and clean the house whenever I look away.
findings.evidenceJa: 料理くらい守っておかないとカッコつかないよ～
findings.explanation: Setsuna concludes that if she does not at least defend cooking as her domain, she cannot preserve any pride as a wife. Todokanai TL drops the conclusion and leaves the quotation open, so Haruki's immediate ultimatum that she get up and cook lacks the stated stake he is answering.
findings.japanese:
「でも春希くん、洗濯も掃除も
隙あらばわたしから奪うじゃない。
料理くらい守っておかないとカッコつかないよ～」
findings.todokanai: "But Haruki-kun, you already do the laundry and clean the house whenever I look away.

findings.highlight: The CEO of the underworld!
findings.evidenceJa: 鬼、悪魔、裏の実行委員長～
findings.explanation: Setsuna caps 'ogre, demon' by calling Haruki the shadow or behind-the-scenes executive committee chairman, an in-character school-festival callback to his controlling organizer role. Todokanai TL converts 裏 into the underworld and 実行委員長 into CEO, deleting the callback and inventing a different fantasy title.
findings.japanese: 「うう、鬼、悪魔、裏の実行委員長～」
findings.todokanai: "Ohh, you're a demon! Satan himself! The CEO of the underworld!"

findings.highlight: This is the story of that winter we spent together, in this apartment.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな冬の、こんな部屋での、残り数日間の物語。
findings.explanation: The narration explicitly frames the story as the final few days of that winter in this apartment, immediately before the couple move. Todokanai TL expands it into the whole winter they spent together and removes the countdown that gives the domestic reminiscence its shape.
findings.japanese:
そんな冬の、こんな部屋での、
残り数日間の物語。
findings.todokanai: This is the story of that winter we spent together, in this apartment.

findings.highlight: it'll also be more efficient for our new neighbors.
findings.evidenceJa: 引っ越し蕎麦がそのまま年越し蕎麦に使えますから、隣近所としても効率的かなって
findings.explanation: Haruki jokes that the soba traditionally given to neighbors when moving can double as New Year's Eve soba, making the timing efficient for the neighborhood too. Todokanai TL omits the entire moving-soba/year-crossing-soba pun, retains only its conclusion, and leaves the quotation unclosed.
findings.japanese:
「それに、引っ越し蕎麦が
そのまま年越し蕎麦に使えますから、
隣近所としても効率的かなって」
findings.todokanai: "Besides, it'll also be more efficient for our new neighbors.

findings.highlight: but to the Ogiso household, they were akin to heresy.
findings.evidenceJa: 発言の後、雪菜含めた皆にめっちゃ怒られた。
findings.explanation: After Haruki reflexively declined their help, everyone—including Setsuna—became extremely angry with him. Todokanai TL substitutes the metaphor 'akin to heresy' and omits the concrete collective rebuke that demonstrates his continuing difficulty accepting family participation.
findings.japanese:
そんな、当然のように俺の口から出た辞退の言葉は、
小木曽家の人々にいたく反感を買ったらしく、
発言の後、雪菜含めた皆にめっちゃ怒られた。
findings.todokanai: Those words had left my mouth the day before as if it was the most natural thing in the world… but to the Ogiso household, they were akin to heresy.

findings.highlight: we should stay here until
findings.evidenceJa: 『貯金がある程度貯まるまではここでいいよ』って強硬に主張してたのは、どちらかと言えばお宅の娘さんだったんですけどね
findings.explanation: Haruki notes that it was primarily the mother's own daughter who adamantly insisted the apartment was fine until they had built up some savings. Todokanai TL cuts the embedded quotation after 'until,' omits the savings threshold and the attribution to Setsuna, and leaves the narration syntactically unfinished.
findings.japanese:
『貯金がある程度貯まるまではここでいいよ』
って強硬に主張してたのは、
どちらかと言えばお宅の娘さんだったんですけどね……
findings.todokanai: If I remember correctly, it was her daughter ーnot meーwho adamantly stated we should stay here until

findings.highlight: don't go running off to cover it.
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩とか編集長に押し付けてでも帰ってくるんだよ？
findings.explanation: Setsuna orders Haruki to come home even if he has to dump a late scoop on his seniors or editor-in-chief. Todokanai TL drops that absolute and professionally outrageous condition, leaves the quotation open, and weakens the exact promise the emergency will test.
findings.japanese:
「夜遅く特ダネが入って来ても
取材に行っちゃ駄目だからね？
先輩とか編集長に押し付けてでも帰ってくるんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Even if some special scoop pops up late tonight, don't go running off to cover it.

findings.highlight: The second time is during my birthday in April.
findings.evidenceJa: 別に、俺としてはどうということもないただの日だけど、多分、一年で一番のご馳走が用意されているのはこの日だ。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls his own birthday an ordinary day to him, while noting that Setsuna probably prepares the year's greatest feast for it. Todokanai TL omits both his self-effacement and her lavish care, reducing the second annual occasion to a date on a list.
findings.japanese:
二つめは、４月の俺の誕生日。
別に、俺としてはどうということもないただの日だけど、
多分、一年で一番のご馳走が用意されているのはこの日だ。
findings.todokanai: The second time is during my birthday in April.

findings.highlight: the day we faced our greatest crisis at a seaside hotel;
findings.evidenceJa: 欧州の小都市で、ふたたびすれ違いが始まってしまったり。
findings.explanation: The Christmas Eve history has a third episode: in a small European city the couple began missing each other again. Todokanai TL cuts the list after the seaside hotel and leaves the sentence on a semicolon, erasing the later repetition that makes the date an enduring cycle rather than two old incidents.
findings.japanese:
北の温泉で、永遠の友情を誓ったり、
海沿いのホテルで、決定的な危機を迎えたり、
欧州の小都市で、ふたたびすれ違いが始まってしまったり。
findings.todokanai: It's the day we once swore eternal friendship in a hot spring up north; the day we faced our greatest crisis at a seaside hotel;

findings.highlight: If I'm to keep my promise with Setsuna to see her before 10 PM, I'll have to finish things up rather quickly.
findings.evidenceJa:
雪菜と約束した『２２時までに自宅』を守るには、
そろそろ仕事を収束させていかなくちゃならない時間帯だ。
findings.explanation: The promise is specifically to be home by 22:00, not merely to see Setsuna before ten — The deadline still governs his attempt to leave.
findings.japanese:
雪菜と約束した『２２時までに自宅』を守るには、
そろそろ仕事を収束させていかなくちゃならない時間帯だ。
findings.todokanai: If I'm to keep my promise with Setsuna to see her before 10 PM, I'll have to finish things up rather quickly.

findings.highlight: my two seniors seem to have a lot going on during Christmas Eve…
findings.evidenceJa: 今年のクリスマスはどうやら色々とある……というか、今年に関しては色々とないみたいだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki starts to say the seniors have various things going on, then corrects himself: this year they conspicuously have nothing going on. Todokanai TL cuts before the reversal and states the rejected positive premise, obscuring why both resent his married Christmas.
findings.japanese:
……なのだが、二人の先輩方は、
今年のクリスマスはどうやら色々とある……というか、
今年に関しては色々とないみたいだった。
findings.todokanai: …Is what I'd like to say, but my two seniors seem to have a lot going on during Christmas Eve…

findings.highlight: She's famous in the industry as the public relations beauty of Knights Records.
findings.evidenceJa: なんでこんな堅物に引っかかっちゃったかなぁ
findings.explanation: Suzuki wonders how a famous beauty like Setsuna ever got caught by such a stiff, straitlaced man. Todokanai TL omits the insult and leaves the quote open, so Matsuoka's sexual answer that Haruki was probably 'stiff in various ways' loses the word it is punning on.
findings.japanese:
「ちょっと洒落になんないもんね～北原君の奥さん。
ナイツレコードの美人広報って業界でも有名なんだよね？
なんでこんな堅物に引っかかっちゃったかなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Your wife is something else, isn't she? She's famous in the industry as the public relations beauty of Knights Records.

findings.highlight: why don't you just go home?
findings.evidenceJa: だいたい松岡さんだって彼女との約束ないんですか？
findings.explanation: Haruki specifically asks whether Matsuoka has plans with his girlfriend. Todokanai TL drops the question and leaves the quotation open, so Matsuoka's 'That's precisely the thing' has no translated referent.
findings.japanese:
「……二人とも、そんな無駄話してる暇があったら、
さっさと帰ったらどうですか？
だいたい松岡さんだって彼女との約束ないんですか？」
findings.todokanai: "…You two, if you can afford to waste time rambling on like that, why don't you just go home?

findings.highlight: if you're going to be in a long-term relationship,
findings.evidenceJa: 断り続けて悪印象持たれるのも……
findings.explanation: Haruki advises visiting because the relationship may continue and repeatedly refusing would make a bad impression on her family. Todokanai TL cuts the conditional advice mid-clause, omits the concrete social consequence, and leaves the quotation unfinished.
findings.japanese:
「いや、実家くらい行けばいいでしょう。
もしかしたら、ずっと付き合っていくかもしれないし、
断り続けて悪印象持たれるのも……」
findings.todokanai: "No, I don't see the problem with visiting her family. Besides, if you're going to be in a long-term relationship,

findings.highlight: half-baked men like this are a dime a dozen.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はまだ自分に自信が持てないんだ～とか、けど、決してお前に飽きたわけじゃないんだ～とか
findings.explanation: Suzuki quotes the stock excuses of an indecisive man—he still lacks confidence, but definitely has not tired of his girlfriend. Todokanai TL omits both quoted lines, so Matsuoka's next suspicion that she has bugged him loses the uncannily exact words it answers.
findings.japanese:
「……あ～いるいるこういう煮え切らない男。
俺はまだ自分に自信が持てないんだ～とか、
けど、決してお前に飽きたわけじゃないんだ～とか」
findings.todokanai: "…Oh dear, half-baked men like this are a dime a dozen.

findings.highlight: Since you two have all this time to sit around chit-chatting,
findings.evidenceJa: 今年いっぱい、一度も家に帰れないくらいの仕事あげようか？
findings.explanation: Suzuki threatens to give both men enough work that they will not make it home once for the rest of the year. Todokanai TL drops the entire threat and leaves the line on a comma, removing the immediate cause of their panicked refusals and attempted escape.
findings.japanese:
「……二人とも、こんな無駄話してる暇があったら、
今年いっぱい、一度も家に帰れないくらいの
仕事あげようか？」
findings.todokanai: "…Since you two have all this time to sit around chit-chatting,

findings.highlight: This always happens to me.
findings.evidenceJa: 大事な用があって絶対に帰らなくちゃならないときに限って、狙ったように新しい仕事が舞い込んできて
findings.explanation: Matsuoka defines his 'law': precisely when he has important plans and absolutely must leave, new work arrives as though aiming for him. Todokanai TL omits the entire rule after its generic opening, leaving no explanation of the named law that the ensuing ministerial scoop fulfills.
findings.japanese:
「俺、いっつもそうなんだよ。大事な用があって
絶対に帰らなくちゃならないときに限って、
狙ったように新しい仕事が舞い込んできて……」
findings.todokanai: "This always happens to me.

findings.highlight: nearly at midnight.
findings.evidenceJa: 日付をまたぐ、その瞬間だった。
findings.explanation: Haruki reaches Setsuna at the exact instant the date crosses midnight, too late to keep the Christmas Eve promise; the next sentence marks the day vanishing. 'Nearly at midnight' places the call before the deadline and contradicts that symbolic loss.
findings.japanese:
目の回る忙しさがほんの一段落つき、
やっと雪菜への連絡が取れたのは、
日付をまたぐ、その瞬間だった。
findings.todokanai: It was only after the bustle had settled down a bit that I was able to get in touch with Setsuna, nearly at midnight.

findings.highlight: The moment I was about to give up, an exasperated voice reached me from the receiver.
findings.evidenceJa:
と、途方に暮れそうになったその瞬間、
電話口から、ようやく待ち焦がれた声が聞こえてきた。
findings.explanation: The voice is one Haruki has longed desperately to hear; 'an exasperated voice' adds an emotional judgment before her words — His relief and her dry response remain.
findings.japanese:
と、途方に暮れそうになったその瞬間、
電話口から、ようやく待ち焦がれた声が聞こえてきた。
findings.todokanai: The moment I was about to give up, an exasperated voice reached me from the receiver.

findings.highlight: "Were you really at work?"
findings.evidenceJa: 「……本当に仕事だったんだな」
findings.explanation: Haruki says 'So it really was work,' registering surprise and relief; 'Were you really at work?' sounds like a continuing accusation — His next line explains the charitable lie he had imagined.
findings.japanese: 「……本当に仕事だったんだな」
findings.todokanai: "Were you really at work?"

findings.highlight: A long, long time ago…
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちの絆が弱く、脆く、お互いに、間違った気遣いをしてしまっていたあの頃。
findings.explanation: The line defines the past as a time when their bond was weak and fragile and both practiced mistaken forms of consideration. Todokanai TL retains only 'long ago,' omitting the diagnosis that the following lies, vows, and corrected marriage are structured against.
findings.japanese:
ずっとずっと昔……
俺たちの絆が弱く、脆く、
お互いに、間違った気遣いをしてしまっていたあの頃。
findings.todokanai: A long, long time ago…

findings.highlight: Nothing happens. We remain ourselves, just like we swore to… No, it's more like something that kind of just happened on its own.
findings.evidenceJa:
やっぱり、俺たちは俺たちのままだって、
そんなふうに誓いあい……いや、適当に決めあった。
findings.explanation: They loosely agreed that even after a broken promise they remain themselves; 'something that kind of just happened on its own' removes their mutual decision — The resilient-marriage principle is still stated.
findings.japanese:
やっぱり、俺たちは俺たちのままだって、
そんなふうに誓いあい……いや、適当に決めあった。
findings.todokanai: Nothing happens. We remain ourselves, just like we swore to… No, it's more like something that kind of just happened on its own.

findings.highlight: I was having a perfectly good time up until now…
findings.evidenceJa: 引っ越し前のクソ忙しいときに、いきなり空気読まない招かれざる客が来るまではな！
findings.explanation: Haruki says he was in a fine mood until socially oblivious uninvited guests suddenly arrived during the insanely busy period before the move. Todokanai TL cuts the whole accusation after 'until,' omits the punchline that answers their complaint about his mood, and leaves the quotation unfinished.
findings.japanese:
「さっきまでは悪くなかったよ。
……引っ越し前のクソ忙しいときに、
いきなり空気読まない招かれざる客が来るまではな！」
findings.todokanai: "I was having a perfectly good time up until now…

findings.highlight: and yesterday was Christmas Eve…
findings.evidenceJa: どうせお前らも昨日はベッタベタしてたんだろ？
findings.explanation: Takeya adds that Haruki and Setsuna were surely glued all over each other yesterday too. Todokanai TL omits the tease and leaves the quotation open; more importantly, it deletes the 'too' that Haruki later identifies as Takeya's revealing narrative trick.
findings.japanese:
「いや、来るなら今日しかないかなって。
明日は引越し前日だし、昨夜はイブだし。
……どうせお前らも昨日はベッタベタしてたんだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "I felt today would be our only chance to drop by, ya know? Tomorrow will be the day before moving day, and yesterday was Christmas Eve…

findings.highlight: "Hmmm? What about you back then? What are you saying you felt about me back then?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「ん～？　あの頃のあんたはどうだったって？
……あの頃のあたしは、どうだったって～？」
findings.explanation: Io presses what Takeya was like then and what she herself was like then; 'what you felt about me' turns the second prompt into a direct romantic confession — The almost-confession and embarrassed stop remain.
findings.japanese:
「ん～？　あの頃のあんたはどうだったって？
……あの頃のあたしは、どうだったって～？」
findings.todokanai: "Hmmm? What about you back then? What are you saying you felt about me back then?"

findings.highlight: The smile on her face no longer bears the sense of sadness and loneliness that I saw back then,
findings.evidenceJa: 無理めに感情を盛り上げた、テンションの高い笑顔でもない。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's smile is neither the sad lonely smile of that period nor the artificially high-energy smile she used to force her emotions upward. Todokanai TL omits the second false smile, leaves the sentence on a comma, and weakens the contrast that establishes her present laughter as genuine.
findings.japanese:
あの頃の、悲しげで寂しげな笑顔じゃない。
無理めに感情を盛り上げた、
テンションの高い笑顔でもない。
findings.todokanai: The smile on her face no longer bears the sense of sadness and loneliness that I saw back then,

findings.highlight: Did he have any lame hero's journey stories?
findings.evidenceJa: なんか嫌な武勇伝とかないかな？
findings.explanation: 武勇伝 means boast-worthy exploits or legendary anecdotes; Setsuna asks for some awful, embarrassing 'legend' from Haruki's unpleasant past. 'Hero's journey stories' is a different literary concept and produces unnatural dialogue that does not describe the requested dirt.
findings.japanese:
「ねぇねぇ、あの頃の春希くんの話、もっと聞かせてよ。
すっごく性格悪かったはずだよね？
なんか嫌な武勇伝とかないかな？」
findings.todokanai: "Come on, lemme hear all about Haruki-kun back then. His personality must've been awful. Did he have any lame hero's journey stories?"

findings.highlight: I bet you got a promotion to a supervisory role
findings.evidenceJa: お局になって実権を手に入れただけじゃないの？
findings.explanation: Tomo jokes that Io has become the office battle-axe or entrenched senior woman and merely acquired de facto power. Todokanai TL converts the gendered workplace insult and informal clout into a literal promotion, flattening why Io immediately rejects the label rather than discussing a new job title.
findings.japanese: 「お局になって実権を手に入れただけじゃないの？」
findings.todokanai: "I bet you got a promotion to a supervisory role, and now you enjoy toying with those under you."

findings.highlight: all the escapades of your youth…
findings.evidenceJa: そこまで青臭い話を俺に喋っちまったこと。
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether Takeya will regret telling him such painfully earnest, idealistic talk about marriage, children, and parental leave. Todokanai TL calls it 'escapades of your youth,' relocating the content into past adventures that Takeya never narrated.
findings.japanese:
「いや、そこまで青臭い話を俺に喋っちまったこと。
……俺なら明日頭抱えてるレベル」
findings.todokanai: "No, I meant how you just told me about all the escapades of your youth… If I were you, I'd be burying my head in embarrassment."

findings.highlight: Time will inevitably cause our own affairs and the affairs of others around us to converge.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちの事情も、その近くで起こっていた事情も、いつか時間と共に収束していく。
findings.explanation: With time, each situation—the couple's and the nearby couple's—will settle or reach its own resolution. Todokanai TL says the affairs converge with one another, replacing the theme of individual conflicts resolving over time with a claim that their stories merge.
findings.japanese:
俺たちの事情も、
その近くで起こっていた事情も、
いつか時間と共に収束していく。
findings.todokanai: Time will inevitably cause our own affairs and the affairs of others around us to converge.

findings.highlight: On an early morning like this, when normally only the sound of the newspaper delivery bike can be heard,
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜の、まるで一曲ノーミスで弾ききったような歓声が響く。
findings.explanation: The sentence ends after establishing the otherwise silent dawn and omits its predicate: Setsuna's cheer rings out as if she has just played an entire song without one mistake. The missing musical simile is the joke that Haruki immediately deflates by noting that they only finished packing.
findings.japanese:
そんな、新聞配達員のバイク音以外は聞こえることのない
早朝に、雪菜の、まるで一曲ノーミスで弾ききったような
歓声が響く。
findings.todokanai: On an early morning like this, when normally only the sound of the newspaper delivery bike can be heard,

findings.highlight: Then on Wednesday we were tied down all day at work, and on Thursday we were forced to participate in a hot pot party,
findings.evidenceJa: 二日分の作業が停滞した。
findings.explanation: The line is left hanging after the two interruptions and omits their consequence: two full days of moving work stalled. That missing tally explains why the couple is still packing at six in the morning.
findings.japanese:
なのに水曜にはトラブルで帰れず、
木曜には鍋パーティの来襲を受け、
二日分の作業が停滞した。
findings.todokanai: Then on Wednesday we were tied down all day at work, and on Thursday we were forced to participate in a hot pot party,

findings.highlight: At this rate, the two of us won't be able to enjoy the weekend at our new home.
findings.evidenceJa: 多分、荷物を解くこともなく二人して倒れてるんだろうな。……月曜の朝まで。
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts something much more concrete and comic: they will collapse without even unpacking and stay down until Monday morning. The generic loss of an enjoyable weekend removes both the physical exhaustion and the setup for unpacking being postponed into New Year.
findings.japanese:
このままじゃ、せっかく新居に移って週末を過ごそうにも、
多分、荷物を解くこともなく二人して倒れてるんだろうな。
……月曜の朝まで。
findings.todokanai: At this rate, the two of us won't be able to enjoy the weekend at our new home.

findings.highlight: This is the coldest time of the year, after all.
findings.evidenceJa: だいたい今くらいが一番寒い時間帯だからな
findings.explanation: 時間帯 is a period of the day: Haruki says this pre-dawn hour is about the coldest part of the day. The translation changes that immediate observation into a claim about the season.
findings.japanese: 「だいたい今くらいが一番寒い時間帯だからな」
findings.todokanai: "This is the coldest time of the year, after all."

findings.highlight: During what is practically moments before New Year's,
findings.evidenceJa: まさに夜明け前の一瞬。
findings.explanation: The narration says it is the brief moment just before dawn, continuing the preceding line about the coldest hour. Todokanai TL mistakes 夜明け for the turn of the year and moves the scene's temporal focus from sunrise to New Year's.
findings.japanese:
まさに夜明け前の一瞬。
雲一つない空の下を、凍えるような冷気が支配していた。
findings.todokanai: During what is practically moments before New Year's, the icy cold wind dominates everything under the cloudless sky.

findings.highlight: Her hand isーas she herself puts itーlow in blood pressure
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっとだけ（自称）低血圧気味の彼女の手は、俺のより若干冷たく感じたけれど。
findings.explanation: Setsuna, self-described as tending toward low blood pressure, has a hand that feels slightly colder than Haruki's. A hand cannot itself be 'low in blood pressure'; the modifier has been attached to the wrong noun and the resulting English is nonsensical.
findings.japanese:
ちょっとだけ（自称）低血圧気味の彼女の手は、
俺のより若干冷たく感じたけれど。
findings.todokanai: Her hand isーas she herself puts itーlow in blood pressure, so it feels a decent bit colder than mine.

findings.highlight: And for Setsuna, this walkway is a path she went down nearly every day on her way to school.
findings.evidenceJa: 付属、大学の７年間、毎日のように通ったはずの道。
findings.explanation: The source specifies the full seven years of affiliated high school and university. Replacing that span with the generic 'on her way to school' erases the precise duration that makes her sudden nostalgia seem initially absurd and connects both stages of their shared history.
findings.japanese:
しかも雪菜にとって、付属、大学の７年間、
毎日のように通ったはずの道。
findings.todokanai: And for Setsuna, this walkway is a path she went down nearly every day on her way to school.

findings.highlight: That's why looking for ourselves is important, to touch…
findings.evidenceJa: だから、自分から見ること、触れることが必要
findings.explanation: 自分から means taking the initiative oneself: one has to choose to look at and touch what is nearby. 'Looking for ourselves' instead suggests self-discovery, while the stranded infinitive 'to touch' does not form intelligible English.
findings.japanese:
だから、自分から見ること、触れることが必要……
いや、何に対してそう思ったのかは置いといて。
findings.todokanai: That's why looking for ourselves is important, to touch… Let's set aside what specifically I'm referring to.

findings.highlight: nor that her department's building was right next to mine.
findings.evidenceJa: すぐ隣の、同じ大学に通っていたにも関わらず。
findings.explanation: The university itself was right next door, and both attended that same university despite Haruki fleeing this road after graduation. The source says nothing about their departments or adjacent faculty buildings; Todokanai TL invents a campus geography and changes what 'right next door' modifies.
findings.japanese: すぐ隣の、同じ大学に通っていたにも関わらず。
findings.todokanai: It didn't matter that we were in the same university, nor that her department's building was right next to mine.

findings.highlight: and the memories of her absence.
findings.evidenceJa: それ以外の、ほんの少しの思い出を
findings.explanation: Haruki sinks into memory his many recollections with Setsuna and the small number of other memories associated with the place. The Japanese deliberately leaves those other memories unnamed; defining them as memories of Setsuna's absence imposes a specific emotional interpretation not stated here.
findings.japanese:
雪菜とのたくさんの思い出と、
それ以外の、ほんの少しの思い出を……
findings.todokanai: The endless memories I share with Setsuna here, and the memories of her absence.

findings.highlight: in second grade
findings.evidenceJa: ２年の頃の雪菜って、評判の学園アイドルじゃん。
findings.explanation: This is Setsuna's second year of high school, not second grade. In English, 'second grade' places the famous school idol in elementary school and makes the ensuing Miss Houjou High history temporally absurd.
findings.japanese:
「だって２年の頃の雪菜って、評判の学園アイドルじゃん。
俺と接点ができるなんて夢にも思わないって」
findings.todokanai: "But in second grade you were the famous school idol, Setsuna. I never even imagined I'd ever get a chance to talk to you."

findings.highlight: Thinking about it now, it doesn't make any sense how a guy like you could've been popular with girls.
findings.evidenceJa: それも、わたしはともかく、あんな凄い美人に
findings.explanation: Setsuna continues by specifying the astonishingly beautiful woman who wanted Haruki, while ostentatiously setting herself aside. Todokanai TL cuts that jealous, self-flattering qualification and leaves the quotation open, so Haruki's rebuke about transparent self-deprecation loses the words that provoked it.
findings.japanese:
「今から考えても、あの頃の春希くんがモテるのって
納得いかないよね～。
それも、わたしはともかく、あんな凄い美人に」
findings.todokanai: "Thinking about it now, it doesn't make any sense how a guy like you could've been popular with girls.

findings.highlight: We walked the Houjou University grounds and the area around the main gate of the high school,
findings.evidenceJa: 学生時代の思い出を（ちょっと不穏なものも含め）語りつつ
findings.explanation: The sentence omits the action governing the walk: they talk through their student memories, including some slightly disturbing ones. That parenthetical is part of the mature couple's ability to revisit their entire past, and the translated line simply stops at a comma.
findings.japanese:
峰城大学や、付属の正門あたりを歩き、
学生時代の思い出を（ちょっと不穏なものも含め）
語りつつ……
findings.todokanai: We walked the Houjou University grounds and the area around the main gate of the high school,

findings.highlight: I lost touch with her again,
findings.evidenceJa: 愛して、迷って、愛して、揺れて、そして愛して
findings.explanation: More than half of Haruki's cumulative history is missing after the second estrangement: loving, wavering, loving, faltering, and finally loving again. The omitted crescendo is what carries the sentence from betrayal and flight to the settled love of this ending.
findings.japanese:
憧れて、結ばれたと思い込んで、裏切って、逃げて、
すれ違って、近づこうとして、またすれ違って、
愛して、迷って、愛して、揺れて、そして愛して……
findings.todokanai: I adored her, I thought she was mine, I betrayed her, I ran away from her, I lost touch with her, I tried getting closer to her, I lost touch with her again,

findings.highlight: that after her anger and lecturing, she'll forgive me.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らは俺に怒り、さんざん説教をした後、許してくれるって
findings.explanation: 彼ら is Setsuna's family collectively: Haruki now trusts that they will be angry, lecture him thoroughly, and then forgive him. Todokanai TL twice turns the plural family into a singular woman, weakening the point that he has finally learned to accept the Ogisos as a forgiving family unit.
findings.japanese:
だって多分、彼らは俺に怒り、
さんざん説教をした後、許してくれるって……
今の俺には、そう信じられるから。
findings.todokanai: Because after all this time, I've learnt to believe… that after her anger and lecturing, she'll forgive me.

findings.highlight: you insist on lecturing others, but you can't stand getting lectured yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 他人にはあんなにお節介なのに、自分がお節介されるの嫌がるもんね
findings.explanation: お節介 is Haruki's defining tendency to meddle, fuss over people, and help without being asked. Setsuna observes that he does it constantly to others but hates receiving it himself; reducing both sides to 'lecturing' discards the established character motif and misreads the family's intrusive care.
findings.japanese:
「春希くんって、他人にはあんなにお節介なのに、
自分がお節介されるの嫌がるもんね」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki-kun, you insist on lecturing others, but you can't stand getting lectured yourself, can you?"

findings.highlight: instead opting to show
findings.evidenceJa: 反発とも共感とも違う、素直な態度で受け止める。
findings.explanation: The English stops in mid-sentence. Setsuna receives words that could deny her family with an unaffected, honest attitude distinct from either resistance or agreement; that quiet mode of acceptance is never stated.
findings.japanese:
そして雪菜は、その、
自分の家族を否定されたとも取れる俺の言葉を、
反発とも共感とも違う、素直な態度で受け止める。
findings.todokanai: But Setsuna, in response to my statement that could very well be seen as a rejection of her family, neither agrees nor disagrees, instead opting to show

findings.highlight: the two had promised not to do it outside.
findings.evidenceJa: けれど外でやるなよっていう約束を交わしている。
findings.explanation: They are exchanging an ordinary, natural marital promise of the sort that makes the narrator interject, 'but don't do that outside.' Todokanai TL turns the aside into a pre-existing agreement not to perform the ceremony outdoors, directly contradicting the fact that they are doing it in a deserted park.
findings.japanese:
すごくありきたりで、とても自然で、
けれど外でやるなよっていう約束を交わしている。
findings.todokanai: It was a perfectly ordinary ceremony, and perfectly natural. However, the two had promised not to do it outside.

findings.highlight: The woman I will soon be calling "mom" in front of our child.
findings.evidenceJa: もうしばらくしたら『お母さん』って呼ぶようになる女性を
findings.explanation: The implied future subject is their baby: Haruki embraces the woman whom someone will soon call 'Mom.' Todokanai TL instead makes Haruki himself begin calling his wife 'mom' in front of the child, reversing the family relation at the emotional peak of the pregnancy revelation.
findings.japanese:
もうしばらくしたら
『お母さん』って呼ぶようになる女性を……
findings.todokanai: The woman I will soon be calling "mom" in front of our child.

findings.highlight: to the apartment where she used to…
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の、この場所での最後の日に、あの、思い出の部屋に送ってくるなんて
findings.explanation: Haruki marvels that on his last day there Kazusa sent the postcard to that particular room laden with memories. Todokanai TL trails off after 'where she used to,' never names the room as the remembered place, and supplies an unfinished relative clause with no source predicate.
findings.japanese:
俺の、この場所での最後の日に、
あの、思い出の部屋に送ってくるなんて……
findings.todokanai: And she knowingly made sure it'd arrive today, to the apartment where she used to…

findings.highlight: you've risen so far up the ranks
findings.evidenceJa: 飯塚君が担当になってからかなり上がってるのよ。ここの売り場の成績
findings.explanation: The sales performance of this store has risen considerably since Iizuka took charge. Todokanai TL instead says Iizuka himself rose through the corporate ranks, changing both subject and business context immediately before the celebration proposal.
findings.japanese:
「飯塚君が担当になってからかなり上がってるのよ。
ここの売り場の成績」
findings.todokanai: "Iizuka-kun, ever since they put you in charge, you've risen so far up the ranks."

findings.highlight: underclassmen to high school graduates
findings.evidenceJa: 短大出や高卒のコもよりどりみどり
findings.explanation: The prospective mixer includes a choice of junior-college graduates and high-school graduates. Todokanai TL turns 短大出 into underclassmen, replacing an educational background with a relative school-year status.
findings.japanese:
「今年入ったコたち、結構可愛いよ？
短大出や高卒のコもよりどりみどり」
findings.todokanai: "The girls in this one are quite cute, you know? You can pick and choose from underclassmen to high school graduates!"

findings.highlight: we've gathered around five or six people
findings.evidenceJa: だからさ、そっちも５、６人揃えてさ
findings.explanation: The woman asks Iizuka to assemble five or six men on his side, even if they are friends rather than coworkers. Todokanai TL says her side has already gathered the group, reversing the request that makes his Houjou connections relevant.
findings.japanese:
「だからさ、そっちも５、６人揃えてさ…
会社絡みじゃなくて友達関係でもいいから」
findings.todokanai: "So we've gathered around five or six people. You can just see the whole thing as a friendly outing, rather than a corporate thing."

findings.highlight: Especially not when the welcoming ceremony is already finished…
findings.evidenceJa: こっちはもう三か月も前から準備してるんですよ？
findings.explanation: Mizusawa finishes by protesting that her group has been preparing the retail-training program for three months. Todokanai TL drops that entire investment and leaves the quotation open, weakening the concrete basis of her anger.
findings.japanese:
「新人教育から販売店研修を削るなんて！
それも入社式が終わってからそんなこと…
こっちはもう三か月も前から準備してるんですよ？」
findings.todokanai: "You can't just remove the sales course from the employee training! Especially not when the welcoming ceremony is already finished…

findings.highlight: The other departments are demanding I send them more manpower ASAP.
findings.evidenceJa: 君らの努力が無駄になったことは済まなく思っているが
findings.explanation: The manager acknowledges and apologizes that the group's effort has been wasted before Mizusawa dismisses that as mere venting. Todokanai TL omits the apology, leaves the quotation unfinished, and removes the premise of her reply.
findings.japanese:
「いや、今期は全社的に負荷が高くて、
新人を早くよこせという他部署の意見が強くてね。
君らの努力が無駄になったことは済まなく思っているが」
findings.todokanai: "Like I said, the company is short on staff this season. The other departments are demanding I send them more manpower ASAP.

findings.highlight: all employees, including the managers
findings.evidenceJa: リーダー含め、全員の意見をまとめて持って来てます
findings.explanation: Mizusawa has brought the unified opinion of everyone in her particular group, including its leader. Todokanai TL expands this into all employees and plural managers, materially inflating the constituency she claims to represent.
findings.japanese:
「もちろんです。
リーダー含め、全員の意見をまとめて持って来てます」
findings.todokanai: "Of course. I've gathered the opinions of all employees, including the managers."

findings.highlight: convey some rawness in your reporting
findings.evidenceJa: 雑誌ってのは人が作ってんだ。もっとこう、血の通ったコミュニケーションってもんが
findings.explanation: Hamada argues that magazines are made by people and therefore require warm, human communication. Todokanai TL changes that interpersonal principle into conveying rawness in reporting, shifting the object from working relationships to prose style.
findings.japanese:
「しかしだな、それじゃあまりにもビジネスライクだろ。
雑誌ってのは人が作ってんだ。
もっとこう、血の通ったコミュニケーションってもんが」
findings.todokanai: "But it becomes too businesslike otherwise. Magazines are written by people, so you need to convey some rawness in your reporting."

findings.highlight: going out of one's way is good
findings.evidenceJa: 浜田さんが前から言ってる『必要な無駄』って奴でしょ
findings.explanation: Matsuoka names Hamada's established principle of 'necessary waste': apparently inefficient human contact that still has value. Todokanai TL paraphrases it as going out of one's way being good, deleting the quoted oxymoron and its callback function.
findings.japanese:
「浜田さんが前から言ってる『必要な無駄』って奴でしょ。
そりゃ、俺だってそういうの嫌いじゃないですよ。
けど今は、優先順位ってもんがあるんですよ」
findings.todokanai: "I know, you're telling me that going out of one's way is good. I don't disagree with that. But right now I have other priorities that take precedence."

findings.highlight: forcing your junior to listen
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩にノロケ話聞かせておいて
findings.explanation: The senior jokes that Setsuna has made her senior listen to romantic bragging and is now refusing weekend work as an advanced tactic. Todokanai TL calls the listener Setsuna's junior, reversing their workplace relationship.
findings.japanese:
「つまりあれよね～。
先輩にノロケ話聞かせておいて、
ついでに休日出勤も断るという高等戦術」
findings.todokanai: "In other words, on top of always forcing your junior to listen to you ramble on about your boyfriend, you're also going to refuse working on the weekends."

findings.highlight: Two springs ago I graduated university
findings.evidenceJa: 大学を卒業して、二度目の四月。社会に出て、二年目の春
findings.explanation: This is the second April since graduation and Setsuna's second spring in working life. Todokanai TL says she graduated two springs ago, moving the graduation itself back an extra year and blurring the carefully parallel calendar markers.
findings.japanese:
わたしにとっては、
大学を卒業して、二度目の四月。
社会に出て、二年目の春。
findings.todokanai: Two springs ago I graduated university, and for two springs I have worked for my current company.

findings.highlight: A friend who never broke the oath that we swore last spring.
findings.evidenceJa: かつて自分が持っていた輝きを、やっと取り戻した友
findings.explanation: The spring inventory contains three friends: one aflame with hope in a new place, one keeping last spring's vow, and one who has finally regained her former radiance. Todokanai TL omits the third friend and breaks the route-wide portrait of everyone advancing separately.
findings.japanese:
新しい自分の居場所で、希望に燃える友。
去年の春に建てた誓いをずっと守り続けてる友。
かつて自分が持っていた輝きを、やっと取り戻した友。
findings.todokanai: A friend burning with hope, in a new place to belong. A friend who never broke the oath that we swore last spring.

findings.highlight: I screamed at my own failure, so much worse than anything I did five years ago.
findings.evidenceJa: そして、五年前よりも強い気持ちを思い出し
findings.explanation: Setsuna weeps with the same regret as five years ago, screams at a more complete defeat, and then remembers feelings stronger than five years ago. Todokanai TL omits the third movement—the renewed strength that explains her return to Haruki's room.
findings.japanese:
五年前と同じ後悔に泣き。
五年前よりも完全な敗北に叫び。
そして、五年前よりも強い気持ちを思い出し。
findings.todokanai: I weeped with the same regret as five years ago. I screamed at my own failure, so much worse than anything I did five years ago.

findings.highlight: stress from unjust overwork
findings.evidenceJa: 『過分な仕事を任されたことによるプレッシャー』に原因の一端があると認定し、休職扱いにしてくれた
findings.explanation: The occupational physician attributes part of Haruki's condition to pressure from being entrusted with excessive work, and the company consequently places him on leave. Todokanai TL invents 'unjust overwork' and stops before the crucial employment outcome.
findings.japanese:
産業医との面談で、
『過分な仕事を任されたことによるプレッシャー』
に原因の一端があると認定し、休職扱いにしてくれた。
findings.todokanai: After an interview with an occupational health physician, they determined that his condition was partly due to "stress from unjust overwork"

findings.highlight: Because he never got any decent sleep since his graduation from university.
findings.evidenceJa: あの頃足りてなかった睡眠時間をやっと取り戻してると思えば全然問題ない
findings.explanation: Setsuna rationalizes his hypersomnia as finally recovering the sleep he lacked during university, and therefore no problem at all. Todokanai TL omits that conclusion and shifts the deprivation to the period after graduation.
findings.japanese:
だって、大学の時から全然眠っていなかったんだから。
あの頃足りてなかった睡眠時間を
やっと取り戻してると思えば全然問題ない。
findings.todokanai: Because he never got any decent sleep since his graduation from university.

findings.highlight: I can finally admit this, now that I feel so fulfilled.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が満たされてからやっと、こんなこと言い出してる
findings.explanation: Haruki condemns himself for only starting to tell Setsuna to leave after she has washed, cooked, embraced him, and filled his needs. Todokanai TL makes it sound like fulfillment has finally enabled an honest admission, softening the selfish timing he is indicting.
findings.japanese:
「洗濯してもらって、料理してもらって、
抱きしめてもらって…
自分が満たされてからやっと、こんなこと言い出してる」
findings.todokanai: "You did my laundry, you cooked for me, you embraced me… I can finally admit this, now that I feel so fulfilled."

findings.highlight: Not so I can save him, but to satisfy my own desires.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼を救いたいから、だけじゃない。自分の欲望も満足させたかったから
findings.explanation: Setsuna says saving Haruki was not her only motive; she also wanted to satisfy her own desire. Todokanai TL turns the additive confession into an exclusive contrast—she did not act to save him, only for herself—making her self-accusation much harsher than the source.
findings.japanese:
彼を救いたいから、だけじゃない。
自分の欲望も満足させたかったから。
findings.todokanai: Not so I can save him, but to satisfy my own desires.

findings.highlight: All I want to do… is to convince myself that the past two years weren't for nothing
